items.quote: we are hopeful that by December end, we should have some trial production happening there . T he galvanizing plant is also being put up . T he material is reaching us and by March , we are hopeful that we will start doing some trials for galvanizing

items.statement: PEB facility at Bhachau 100,000 tonnes; trials by Mar-Apr 2027
items.quote: We are looking to start with 100,000 tonnes of capacity in our Bhachau plant and the team, our business head has already joined and so is the design team.

items.statement: Total sellable capacity ~1.4 million tonnes after all capex and Saudi ramp-up
items.quote: So, with all the CAPEX in place and once our Saudi is also up and running, and the capacity which we have said that which is going to come up in our Kutch area, this will become like 1.4 million tons, around 1.4 million tons of the sellable capacity.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.9% (+100 bps QoQ); freight cost pass-through to aid H2 margins
items.quote: EBITDA was Rs. 196 crores at a margin of 11.9%, a growth of 46% year-on-year basis. Of course, freight continued to remain high during the quarter.

items.statement: Freight cost pass-through in large US contracts; Middle East contracts partially absorbed
items.quote: Freight becomes a pass - through. In large contracts in North America, it's pass - through . Some contracts in the Middle East have been on actual s . Some places we have been able to pass through part of it, some we have had to absorb

items.statement: Raw material risk mitigated via back-to-back booking; commodity price risk contained
items.quote: As a policy, we mitigat e the risk of raw material fluctuations by booking material on a back - to - back basis. This discipline approach enables us to protect margins and keep commodity price risk contained

items.statement: Global renewable energy and power transmission supercycle; India 500 GW by 2030, $400 bn investment
items.quote: Currently, India has committed to Karamtara Engineering Limited November 06, 2026 3 achieving 500 gigawatts of non - fossil fuel capacity by 2030 and around 800 gigawatts by 2035 with incremental investments estimated at $ 400 billion by

items.statement: US demand robust driven by data centers, chips, aging transmission grids; Rs 550 crore order received yesterday
items.quote: We incidentally just one very large 550 crore order yesterday in the US, the order has just come in yesterday and we believe that it's going to be a large transmission market for us.

items.statement: International revenue 73% in Q2 FY27 (70% H1); US ~57% of order book; forex hedged via PCFC and natural hedge
items.quote: In Q2 '27 revenue from operations was Rs. 1,647 crores, a growth of 62% year-on-year basis. The international revenue stood at 73%.

items.statement: Tariffs pass-through; 30% price advantage vs US manufacturers even at 50% tariff
items.quote: tariffs , it really doesn't matter where the tariffs go because it's all a pass through to us . A s I have spoken in our last call , last quarter's call that the difference between our product that we are supplying out of I ndia and what is being sold by the US manufacturers , there's still a 30 % upside on that in the selling price and the tariffs get factored in

items.statement: Working capital cycle 37 days in H1 FY27; debtor days down QoQ from 100 to 94
items.quote: During H1, FY27 our working capital cycle reduced to 37 days.

items.statement: Debtor days increased YoY due to higher international mix (73% vs 45%) and Middle East transit delays
items.quote: Last year in the same quarter if you see our international sales were 45%, but in this quarter we have done 73% as international sales. So, in international sales, there is a longer working capital cycle as compared to the debtor days in the domestic market.

items.statement: Capex funded from internal accruals, IPO proceeds (Rs 200 cr in FD), and term debt if needed
items.quote: From the internal accruals, and to some extent from debt if required, then we will go for the term debt. But as of now, it looks like that we have sufficient cash flow available within the system because we haven't utilized the IPO money as of now ful ly. So, that is also there in the system. You have seen that in our balance sheet, Rs. 200 crores has already been parked in FD

items.statement: Historical revenue seasonality: 42-45% in H1, 55-58% in H2
items.quote: Historically we have been at about 42% to 58% revenue, that's how the revenue has been casted for us historically.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues (Middle East) impacting freight costs and dispatch; margins to improve if situation settles
items.quote: the freight impact if it continues , that will continue to impact us , but if things settle down completely that margin will also get passed back to profitability

items.statement: Defense/aerospace subsidiary under discussion; no guidance yet; team building in progress
items.quote: We have three or four possible scenarios that are playing out for us right now and we are trying to see which is the best way forward. So, it's all under discussion and deliberation. We are also trying to build out the team which is the core for building this business, so we are not wanting to give any guidance as of right now.

items.statement: US customers repeat orders due to quality, delivery reliability, backward integration; replacement cost high
items.quote: There's a lot of customer belief in us over the years. It's a very sensitive market where you need to have quality product, which you've delivered consistently over the years for people to have confidence in giving you those orders.

items.statement: Compete with Indian and Turkish firms; Chinese limited by national security and quality requirements in US/Europe
items.quote: Yes, so China is very limited in terms of because let's say in the US or in some of the countries in Europe, they don't want Chinese products because of national security. Some of them have regulations against and the kind of quality products that are required in some of the European countries, the Chinese manufacturers cannot match up to those.

items.statement: Saudi local content mandate requires in-kingdom manufacturing; cannot serve via exports
items.quote: Local manufacturing is a must in the kingdom of Saudi Arabia due to the preconditions of local content in all energy infrastructure projects. Therefore, the local requirements cannot be served through exports from India or other country.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 4 per equity share declared by board
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the board of directors in its meeting has declared an interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.

items.statement: PLA project on track, targeting November commissioning with INR 2,400 crore spent by mid-October
items.quote: On our strategic initiative, the 80,000 PLA project continues to remain on track, and we are hoping to commence operations in November itself. Construction activities are in full swing, and we have already spent INR2,400 crores approximately by 15th October.

items.statement: Sugar segment PBIT increased 166% to INR 140 crore in Q2 FY27 vs year-ago quarter
items.quote: Strong volume coupled with improved realization resulted in sugar segment PBIT to increase by 166% to INR140 crores during Q2 2027 as compared to corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Distillery margins compressed due to no ethanol price revision in three years despite 16% FRP increase
items.quote: Distillery segment was affected by compressed margin due to non -revision of procurement prices of ethanol over the last three years. Despite increase in sugarcane prices, that is the FRP, again over three years. FRP is increased by 16%, ethanol price has not gone up.

items.statement: 2025-26 sugar season tighter than expected with 3.6 MT closing stock; 2026-27 production expected to decline further
items.quote: The 2025 -2026 sugar season has turned out to be tighter than expected, with lower -than-expected production, resulting in a drawdown in inventory. The closing stock for the season is 3.6 million tonnes, providing an initial cushion for domestic availability.

items.statement: Company projects 2.5-3.5 million tonnes of sugar imports needed for 2026-27 season
items.quote: The long story short, there will be a requirement. It can be 2.5 million tonnes, it can be 3.5 million tonnes. So we're taking a basic average of 3 million tonnes or 30 lakh tonnes, as would be needed from the import market.

items.statement: Ethanol production estimated at 18-20 crore litres for ESY 2027 including C-heavy and grain
items.quote: We are expecting total production to be in the region of around 18 crores- 20 crores litre.

items.statement: Maizapur distillery to run fully on grain targeting 8-9 crore litres subject to feedstock availability
items.quote: Our Maizapur distillery is expected to run fully on grain, which can be maize as well as rice. Intention is to run that distillery for 8 crores- 9 crores litre, subject to availability of feedstock.

items.statement: Every INR 10 increase in cane price adds INR 100 crore incremental raw material cost
items.quote: Let's assume last year we crushed around 10.4 crores quintal of cane. Let's assume we are able to do 10 crores this year. INR10 increase will have a variable cost impact of INR100 crores on the company.

items.statement: PLA prices increased ~10% in last six months; sugar price rise is global phenomenon keeping PLA competitive
items.quote: PLA prices have also increased in the last six months at a 10% level already. That is also there.

items.statement: PLA plant passed all testing protocols for pan masala application; government mandate nearing completion
items.quote: We've also passed all the testing protocols which are there for this application. As Mr. Saraogi is pointing out, it will be sort of closing in soon. Yes, I think significant part of PLA can go into this application.

items.statement: Management requests 6 months patience for PLA plant to stabilize; will provide cost and yield data on next call
items.quote: My humble request to the investor, watch and, you know, let's not look to guide this business every quarter, for the next two quarters. Having said that, post that, we are very confident that this will turn out to be a new business with great potential.

items.statement: Future PLA capacity expansion capex expected to be much lower than initial project
items.quote: Logically, physically understood with the supplier, much lower.

items.statement: Cane crushing estimated 2% lower at ~10 crore quintals; recovery initially lower but may recover
items.quote: We crushed 10 crores 40 lakh quintals of cane. Maybe we will go a couple of percentage points lower. And recovery initially would be lower because of the soil being a little affected by rain. Thereafter, we hope the recovery will also pick up.

items.statement: Maize-based ethanol currently leaving margin on the table at prevailing prices
items.quote: At current prices, maize is leaving something on the table.

items.statement: U.P. government yet to announce State Advised Price for current sugar season
items.quote: U.P. government is yet to announce the State Advised Price for the current season.

items.statement: Government allowed TRQ of 10 lakh tonnes sugar imports to contain price rise
items.quote: Government has taken various measures to ensure adequate availability to contain the sharp rise in prices. And currently, the first step is to allow TRQ of 10 lakh tons.

items.statement: Cane crushing to start in central U.P. after Diwali, east U.P. around 20th November
items.quote: Maybe central U.P. we will start after Deepavali, and east U.P. around the 20th November.

items.statement: Sugar prices expected to remain firm; management positive within realms of reality (INR 50-60/kg range implied)
items.quote: We remain positively inclined. Giving numbers is impossible. But, what should I say? Everybody should feel pleasantly surprised within the realms of reality.

items.statement: PLA business requires 3-6 months for production trials and marketing maturity; costs currently on drawing board
items.quote: In six months, therefore, there will be trials, where you have to achieve quality. You might have to market to some people to get them in. All this requires a bit of patience. Thereafter, I am seeing or we are seeing a runway where we will be on the take -off stage.

items.statement: Normalized Titan Jewellery margin for Q2 FY27 is 11.1% after adjusting for ₹490 cr customs duty gain and ₹46 cr CaratLane gain; further normalizing for 60 bps MTM reversal gives 11.7%.
items.quote: Normalized margin, once you do adjustment for this, on Titan Jewellery business would be 11.1%.

items.statement: Management anchors FY27 jewellery margin target around 11% despite mix shifts and gold price volatility.
items.quote: I think we still, Mihir, would like to anchor our margin target at around 11%.

items.statement: CaratLane H1 margin remains healthy; EBIT margin expected to gradually inch up from 8% to 9% over next couple of years.
items.quote: But if you look at the entire H1 margin profile of CaratLane, still remains healthy, still remains as per our plan that gradually their EBIT margin should start inching up from 8% to 9%, and then further from there in next couple of years.

items.statement: Watch division margin improved in Q2 FY27 driven by Edge collection, Made in India campaign, and strong sales in ₹25,000–₹1 lakh price points.
items.quote: This quarter, we've had a really good story on Edge, driven partly by the Made in India: A Titan Story piece, as well as the launch of a good set of products that took price points up and therefore margins up.

items.statement: Festive season saw strong start during Navratri, mid-season softness due to gold price volatility, and strong recovery from Oct 31; studded jewellery sustained growth, investment buying soft.
items.quote: The first phase of Navratri, we saw good consumers, positive consumer sentiments and good traffic to our stores. Pretty much from the day of Vijayadashami for the next few days, there was some softness owing to gold rate volatility, which kept customers away. But pretty much from the last weekend, which was October 31, we have seen customers come back as we saw an al l- time low perhaps of the las

items.statement: CaratLane saw healthy revenue and buyer growth during 24-day festive period barring one weak week.
items.quote: During the 24 days of festive season, we, barring for one week, I think we have seen a very healthy growth in terms of both revenue as well as buyer growth.

items.statement: Watches posted better-than-Q2 growth in October, particularly in ₹25,000–₹1 lakh price points where share gains continue.
items.quote: Watches, generally festive doesn't really do that well, but this time around, in October, we had pretty good growth, better than Q2. The momentum looks good, and particularly in the price points of ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh, which is an area that we have been gaining share, we have done really well.

items.statement: Studded jewellery growth is industry-wide, driven by secular trend toward natural diamonds since January; Diamond Expertise Centres at 250+ stores will play out longer term.
items.quote: It is a month-on-month sustainable kind of track. But we think it is an industry-wide thing. As far as the benefits of Diamond Expertise Centre, it will play out over time. We have now reached about 250+ stores.

items.statement: Lower caratage (18K, 14K, 9K) and lightweight jewellery gaining fast adoption, especially in North and West; strategy is long-term, not tied to short-term gold price moves.
items.quote: We have been working on 18-carat gold for core gold jewellery, both in wedding and daily wears, and also 14-carat in Tanishq studded jewellery and up to nine-carat in Mia. And so far, it has built a good catalogue and a good availability across stores in the last 9 to 10 months, and it is growing at a very fast clip, and we are seeing good adoption by customers.

items.statement: Buyer growth flat in Q2 due to festive shift and weak coin demand; recovery seen in late festive period but final outcome depends on last few days.
items.quote: Both of that, Nihal. Both the festive shift as well as the gold coin and investment buying, both have contributed.

items.statement: New buyers entering at sub-₹1 lakh price points across Mia, CaratLane, Tanishq; gold exchange programme, store upgrades and network expansion are key levers.
items.quote: For buyer growth to happen, we need buyer growth sub ₹1 lakh, and therefore, a lot of our efforts are to make jewellery accessible, give a lot of product choice, sub ₹1 lakh, sub ₹50,000.

items.statement: Domestic gold prices trading at discount to international since customs duty hike, creating realization pressure; customs duty gain of ₹490 cr (Titan Jewellery) and ₹46 cr (CaratLane) in Q2 fully normalized.
items.quote: Since increase in customs duty, the domestic market has been operating at a discount compared to international. I am talking about gold prices. That leads to the gold price realization pressure.

items.statement: Management expects government may reduce customs duty eventually, which would eliminate grey-channel attractiveness and improve operating environment.
items.quote: Our expectation is that at some point of time, government would also perhaps take a view on customs duty, and again, the way they have done, and they will hopefully reduce that, so that that grey channel attractiveness completely diminishes.

items.statement: Competitive intensity rising structurally as organized players expand geographies and smaller jewellers discount; management braces for continued increase and keeps margin guidance anchored at 11%.
items.quote: Competitive intensity, please expect it to continue to improve and increase all the time. More players will come, more people get capital, more people want to expand.

items.statement: Damas acquisition second-tranche liability revalued down by ₹671 cr to ₹1,668 cr under Ind AS 109; fair-value assessment each quarter may cause further pluses/minuses; long-term opportunity unchanged.
items.quote: This amount is ₹671 crores. As per Ind AS 109, any financial liability has to be fair val ued at every accounting period. And with the current environment, when we looked at our liability at the end of four years, which was accounted for in our books of accounts at ₹1,668 crores, the reassessed liability is less by ₹671 crores

items.statement: Board approved ₹2,500 cr fund raise to replenish existing borrowings, not additional debt.
items.quote: This is a replenishment of some of the existing borrowing. It is not additional borrowing.

items.statement: Non-jewellery businesses (Watches, EyeCare, Fragrances, Fashion Accessories, Taneira, TEAL, North America jewellery) delivered strong growth and higher operating leverage in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Watch division, EyeCare division, our newer businesses, fragrances, fashion accessories, even Taneira has started showing some promising green shoots. TEAL on the other side, and international jewellery business on North America, they have been doing extremely well, and we believe that they will continue their growth trajectory, making a meaningful contribution to Titan consolidated performance.

items.statement: MTM volatility of 40-60 bps per quarter on gold forwards/futures is now a recurring P&L feature; management advises not to overreact to quarterly swings.
items.quote: With the current, the way gold price behaves, the way our volume and forwards, futures, etcetera, valuation happens, it has become part and parcel of our P&L that 40-50 basis point of MTM pluses, minuses will keep happening, and we need to live with this.

items.statement: FY27 jewellery margin guidance anchored at ~11%; no change despite gold price correction or competitive pressure.
items.quote: We would not, as far as FY27 is concerned, change our stance on margins.

items.statement: Retained near-term guidance of revenue growth in high teens and underlying EBITDA margins of 20% plus
items.value: high teens revenue growth; 20%+ underlying EBITDA margin
items.quote: We are retaining our near -term guidance of revenue growth in high teens and underlying margins of 20%.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 capex guided at INR 625-700 crores
items.quote: So, our capex for the full year will be in the range of about INR625 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex was INR 3,150 million, nearly 90% increase YoY
items.quote: Capex investments in H1 2027 was INR 3,150 million, which is almost 90% increase over the same period of last year.

items.statement: Capex focused on B&C growth: extruded tube capabilities in China, India, Europe, US and advanced printing decoration
items.quote: We've invested in extruded tube capabilities in China. We've also made those investments in India and Europe. We've invested in U.S., which is a very significant B&C market where our business in B&C was relatively small.

items.statement: Normal utilization around 60-65% of rated capacity; most capex is brownfield expansion
items.quote: Normal utilization will be around 60%, 65% on the rated capacity because what happens in the market is capacity comes in bulk, but the growth happens linearly, right?

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY, highest ever; underlying revenue growth 20.3%
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter grew by 30%. This is the highest ever growth that EPL has ever declared.

items.statement: Beauty & Cosmetics grew 42.9%, Oral Care grew 19.2%; B&C became largest category in September
items.quote: Beauty & Cosmetics delivered exceptional performance at 42.9% growth, while Oral Care continued its strong performance with a growth of 19.2%.

items.statement: All regions grew strongly: EAP 40%, Europe 30%, AMESA 28%, Americas 25%, India 30%
items.quote: Regionally, we delivered strong performance across all markets. EAP led with revenue growth of 40%, followed by Europe at 30%, AMESA at 28% and Americas at 25%. India stand-alone also delivered robust growth of 30%.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 18.9%; underlying EBITDA margin 20.4% after full pass-through of raw material cost inflation
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 17.6%, with reported EBITDA margins at 18.9%. On an underlying basis, excluding the pass -through impact of higher raw material prices, revenue grew by 20.3%, with underlying EBITDA margins at 20.4%.

items.statement: Gross contribution underlying 60.5% after excluding inflationary cost pass-through
items.quote: But if you look at it underlying, our gross margin or gross contribution after excluding the inflationary cost is 60.5%.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margins temporarily depressed due to Poland centralization delays; expect 2-3 quarters to stabilize
items.quote: Overall, we feel that it will take us another 2 to 3 quarters to fully stabilize operations and get margins back to the levels at which we want them to be.

items.statement: Fully recovered elevated raw material costs through pricing actions; built pricing muscle and proactive price discussions
items.quote: Despite continued cost pressures, we have successfully recovered the full impact of cost increases through pricing actions.

items.statement: Sustainable tubes account for 41% of product mix; B&C and Oral Care each ~44% of revenue
items.quote: We have also advanced our sustainable packaging portfolio, with sustainable tubes accounting for 41% of our product mix.

items.statement: B&C growth driven by existing customers in strong markets (India) and new customer acquisition in white-space markets (China extruded)
items.quote: Bulk of our growth is being driven by our existing customers. While we continue to acquire new customers, a large proportion of our growth is coming from existing customers.

items.statement: Gained 130 bps global market share in B&C over last year; superior service and air freight deliveries driving wallet share gains
items.quote: And in the last 1 year, we've gained 130 basis points of market share, which at a global level is a very significant achievement.

items.statement: Merger with Indovida progressing: CCI, foreign antitrust, stock exchange approvals received; NCLT application filed; expect completion by Q4 FY27
items.quote: We have now filed our application with the National Company Law Tribunal, bringing us a s tep closer to the important milestone for EPL, with the process advancing as planned

items.statement: Merger synergies guided at US$35-50 million over 3 years post-merger, mostly growth-related from geographic expansion
items.quote: Total synergy benefit on account of the merger will be US$35 million to US$50 million.

items.statement: Indovida Q1 FY27 (public): revenue +25%, EBITDA +62%, EBITDA margin 27% (614 bps improvement), EBITDA INR 383 crores
items.quote: For the most recent quarter, which is available publicly, the results of Indovida have been absolutely fantastic. Their revenue grew 25%, EBITDA grew 62%, and there was a 614 basis points improvement in the EBITDA margin. EBITDA is equivalent to INR 383 crores and EBITDA margin stands at 27%.

items.statement: 16th consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth
items.quote: Our EBITDA continued its strong momentum, growing by 17.6% and marking our 16th consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth.

items.statement: PAT grew 5.6% impacted by higher depreciation, tax rate, and adverse forex
items.quote: PAT during this quarter grew by 5.6% due to higher depreciation, higher effec tive tax rate as a result of country mix and adverse forex movements

items.statement: Adverse forex movements impacted PAT; Middle East conflict keeping commodity prices elevated and disrupting supply chains
items.quote: The ongoing conflict in Middle East is keeping commodity prices elevated and disrupting supply chains.

items.statement: Increased inventory levels to maintain superior OTIF and customer service
items.quote: We have also invested in superior customer service. We have incurred additional freight costs. We have increased our inventory levels just to make sure that our OTIFs and customer service remains at a superior level.

items.statement: Post-merger debt-to-EBITDA expected at 0.2-0.25x; Indovida has no debt, EPL debt very low
items.quote: Post the merger, our debt-to-EBITDA ratio will be about 0.2, 0.25, and that will enable with a very strong balance sheet for us to look at inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: Operations in seven countries certified as Great Place to Work
items.quote: We are proud that our operations in seven countries are certified as Great Place to Work, reflecting our commitment to building a positive, engaging and thriving workplace.

items.statement: Poland printing site regulatory approvals took 6-9 months longer than anticipated, causing higher outsourcing costs
items.quote: And in our printing site, which we had found in Poland, it took us much longer to get regulatory approvals than what we had anticipated. It took us at least 6 to 9 months longer.

items.statement: Divisionalized front-end sales: separate teams for Oral Care and B&C to avoid cannibalization
items.quote: One significant decision we took recently was to completely divisionalize our front end. So, our sales people now for ora l and B&C are distinct

items.statement: Expects revenue of INR550-600 crore next year after expansion, with INR80 crore annual free cash flow post-July
items.quote: next year itself, we are expecting to do a realization of at least INR550 crores. That's primarily going to come from the expansion in soda. And going forward within this, because we're up and running with our new plant by July, we'll only have 9 months of sales. And possibly within the same capacity, about INR550 crores to INR600 crores is the revenue that we expect with the current capex plan th

items.statement: Targets 70-80% renewable energy share within 2-3 years, subject to Rajasthan policy
items.quote: The intent is to be in the next 2 years at about 70% to 80% renewable. So we have those target as well and when those contracts are finalized, we'll be obviously giving it to BSE & NSE once those contracts are finalized. But within 2 to 3 years at most, we'll be at about 70 to 80% renewable.

items.statement: INR315 crore capex plan: INR150 crore completed last year, remaining INR165 crore by July next year
items.quote: And as you are aware we are having an INR315 crores capex plan, of which approximately INR150 crores was completed last year. Another INR165 crores will be completed by July of next year, at the latest.

items.statement: Next expansion of 120-140 tons caustic soda requires INR140-150 crore; timeline undecided
items.quote: The timeline I can't commit to at the moment. It would be forward-looking for me to commit, but the investment required for another 140 tons would be another INR140 crores to INR150 crores.

items.statement: Caustic soda capacity to rise from 300 to 360 tons/day by July next year; targets 500 tons eventually
items.quote: So from 300 tons will be at 360 tons, by July of next year. As I mentioned, between March and July of next year will be from 300 tons to 360. Subsequent to that, only one very large electrolyzer, about 120 tons to 140 tons will take us directly to 500 tons.

items.statement: Commissioned 21 MW DC solar captive with BESS; total renewable capacity now 47 MW DC (40% of power)
items.quote: One of the more later developments during this quarter was that we have also sanctioned and commissioned 21 MW DC solar captive power with BESS. In total, our captive, and group captive renewable energy has now increased to 47 MW DC. That constitutes around 40% of our total power is now coming from renewable sources

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA grew 10.36% YoY despite lower caustic soda realizations
items.quote: Our EBITDA of H1 FY26 has registered a growth of about 10.36%, which is, also significant.

items.statement: Power cost dropped INR5 crore QoQ to INR37.79 crore due to renewable commissioning
items.quote: if you see power and fuel expenses declined to INR37.79 crores despite the increase in sales of caustic soda and the production of caustic soda from INR42 crores in just the previous quarter. So, quarter-on-quarter, INR5 crores reduction in power cost.

items.statement: Raw material cost rose INR6 crore QoQ due to higher paraffin oil and sulfuric acid prices from war impact
items.quote: cost of raw material consumed has gone up by about INR6 crores. If you see last quarter, INR30 crores versus INR36 crores, that has been the biggest issue. And that is primarily because of chlorinated paraffin wax. In that basically paraffin oil is put. And because of the war, paraffin oil, sulfuric acid, and these kind of chemicals have gone up significantly.

items.statement: Grid power at INR8.3/unit vs captive solar at INR2 and group captive at INR4.50
items.quote: our power grid rate has reduced significantly, which the grid rate is at about INR8.3, whereas captive power comes at about INR2 and group captive power comes at about INR4.50.

items.statement: Plans to diversify into specialty chemicals using post-July free cash flow of INR80 crore annually
items.quote: we'll have at least a free cash flow of INR80 odd crores annually to invest in other, chemicals that we may seem appropriate at that time. What that means is that the growth will only grow much significantly quicker subsequent to the expansion plants being completed. Where we see ourselves in 5 years is that we are not just a commodity chemical player.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisitions in specialty chemicals; can leverage INR80 crore FCF for INR250-300 crore deal at 30% equity
items.quote: We are very much looking into, expansions through strategic expansions and acquisitions. Actually, what I mentioned earlier is that because we are going to have about INR80 odd crores of free cash flow annually, any expansion or acquisition is open to us because let's say if I have INR80 crores of free cash flow available, I can take, at least on a 30% equity basis, a INR200 crores loan and acquir

items.statement: Comfortable debt-to-equity and debt-to-EBITDA; banks supportive; can raise debt for acquisitions
items.quote: We are in a fairly good debt-to-equity level. We are well serviceable. Debt-to-EBITDA is also strong. The banks are very supportive to us, so we are able to get more debt, but we may not necessarily choose to be overleveraged either.

items.statement: Rajasthan allows 2x contract demand in renewable; targets 70-80% renewable subject to policy continuity
items.quote: Rajasthan, 2x of contract demand is allowed in renewable. And so this is a forward-looking statement I have to mention. If the laws allow for us to do this, they do at the moment, we'll be at 70% to 80% in the next 2 to 3 years unless there is any other change in law in Rajasthan

items.statement: 10 MW wind-solar hybrid project already online and contributing to results since last year
items.quote: Second, you asked about the, 10 MW wind-solar project that is online. We are already receiving power from last year and very much part of our results already.

items.statement: CPW initially for captive chlorine use (100 tons) but now selling well; 150 tons chlorine sold in open market
items.quote: Roughly about 150 tons open market, and 100 tons in our own consumption. And CPW was put actually for a captive chlorine use case. And of late, CPW is actually doing really well for us because of this paraffin oil cost increase, even the price of CPW has increased significantly.

items.statement: Chlorine realizations in Alwar at negative INR1,000 to 0 vs negative INR2,000 in Gujarat; fewer competitors advantage
items.quote: So right now we are still at about between negative 2000 to 0 in terms of chlorine in Alwar, which is significantly better than the Gujarat region. That's primarily because you mentioned Since we have fewer competitors here, we are able to achieve better realizations for chlorine. Now, negative 1,000 to 0 is actually significantly better than what it has been in the past. Gujarat is still relative

items.statement: Chlorine market to improve when Reliance/Adani commission PVC plants absorbing chlorine
items.quote: Reliance and Adani come in, they are going to be making PVC. What would happen invariably is that all their chlorine will go into PVC, and it would mean that the chlorine market over time will improve

items.statement: Caustic soda pricing at import parity plus INR4,000-5,000 freight to North India from Gujarat
items.quote: For example, if at the port or in Gujarat caustic soda costs INR32,000-INR33,000, in Alwar or in the north it will cost roughly about INR36,000-INR37,000. That is the difference between the freight from Gujarat to northern India. As the competition is less, so our pricing strategy is always whatever the rate is in the world or whatever the rate is in Gujarat plus around INR4,000-INR5,000, the cost

items.statement: Employee benefits up due to half-yearly incentives and Diwali bonus; variable component linked to EBITDA
items.quote: Employee benefits, basically, we have our incentives given not on a quarterly basis, but on a half-yearly basis. If we convert to a quarterly basis, it will reach there to there only. And it's only variable on EBITDA. So that's where INR1.20 crores has gone there.

items.statement: Expects INR80 crore annual free cash flow from July after capex completion
items.quote: we'll have at least a free cash flow of INR80 odd crores annually to invest in other, chemicals that we may seem appropriate at that time.

items.statement: BESS of 1.45 MW mandated by law; not significant for operations; will not invest heavily until pricing falls and use case emerges
items.quote: for the moment, we only have about 1.45 MW of battery. It is very small and actually quite insignificant, and that's primarily because the law mandates for us to have this. Besides that, we don't have much battery, and this battery will not have any real consequential meaningful difference on our results or our consumption of renewable power.

items.statement: Doubling capacity from current levels with new plant at Nagpur and supplier park land acquisition
items.quote: We are now going ahead with a very large plant at Nagpur , and we have actually committed to buy close to 1,500 to 2,000 acres of land. So, the ability to expand quickly will be very fast as well beyond that. So, we are effectively doubling capacity from where we stand right now, and have the potential to increase a lot more very quickly.

items.statement: Targeting 27% growth this year to reach 82 then 92
items.quote: So, at this point, as I mentioned, 27% growth this year to go to 82 and then to 92.

items.statement: Order book is robust with longest waiting period of 9S and 7XO models
items.quote: Order book is robust. The longest order book by way of waiting period is 9S as , Velu said, 7XO, both of these are on the longest waiting period.

items.statement: All products on very strong demand with order intake trending well
items.quote: All products are on very strong demand.

items.statement: Auto margin could be one of the highest globally this quarter; EV margins around 9% with PLI contribution
items.quote: In fact, I think your auto margin could be one of the highest globally in this quarter.

items.statement: Less than 4 metre portfolio contributes 45% and is positioned aspirationally for pricing leverage
items.quote: About 45% of our portfolio, at least 40% is less than 4 metre because all Boleros, all Thars, 3-door and 3XO are all part of their weighted margin.
We've been most aggressive in taking prices in the last four months; not reckless, I think, but most aggressive.

items.statement: Large plant at Nagpur with 1500-2000 acres land committed; supplier park land also bought
items.quote: We are now going ahead with a very large plant at Nagpur , and we have actually committed to buy close to 1,500 to 2,000 acres of land.

items.statement: Doubling capacity from current levels with potential to increase more quickly
items.quote: So, we are effectively doubling capacity from where we stand right now, and have the potential to increase a lot more very quickly.

items.statement: EV business margins closer to 9% with PLI contribution; path to ICE-like margins over time
items.quote: The EV business has to be treated like a startup. It's got volume that will come in, which will allow us to spread a lot of the depreciation amortization costs over a much larger revenue base.

items.statement: Adding short-term capacity for next financial year and scouting for large-scale expansion to double footprint
items.quote: We are again adding some short-term capacity for the next financial year. But fundamentally, we are also looking at a large-scale capacity expansion.

items.statement: Expects modest second half FY27 due to high base, inflation, weak monsoon, and rate tightening
items.quote: We've already stated that the second half is going to be a bit modest. The primary reasons are what you already described. There is a lot of effect, inflation effect in the system. Monsoons have been weak. The interest rates are getting tightened.

items.statement: Expects flat to modest growth in Q3 FY27 relative to high prior-year base
items.quote: We expect flat to modest growth in Q3 FY27 relative to a high prior-year base.

items.statement: RBIC EBITDA margin declined due to raw material prices, forex, depreciation change, and capacity investments; expects recovery in subsequent quarters
items.quote: are some effects that we currently have in the short term, which is the forex effect, the increased investments that we've been doing to enhance capacities. So there's a lot of investment going in. There is a change of depreciation method and, of course, significant increase in raw material

items.statement: Bosch Limited margins on upward track despite transient forex and raw material impacts; endeavor to maintain and improve margins
items.quote: See, our endeavor is to maintain and even improve on the margin. Quarter-on-quarter, there could be some effects which we may encounter like currently we just talked about the forex impact or the raw material prices going up suddenly or some costs which have not yet been passed on to the OEMs or to our customers.

items.statement: Cost pass-through to customers has contractual time lag; may not recover 100% due to customer pushback
items.quote: There is a certain time lag in this as we are passing on to our customers, if we have a contractual base for this passing on. We have a time lag because of the occurrence of the increased cost and the point in time as this has been contractually agreed for recomposition or reimbursement by our customers.

items.statement: FX pass-through is contract-based for most customers, negotiation-based for some
items.quote: For most of the customers, it is contract based, but there is single customers where it is negotiation based.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR350 crores; annual spend focused on upgrading production lines for volume output
items.quote: Was a very high spend in the third quarter of the financial year. So most of the spending goes into plant and machinery, that's the lion's share of it. And in this year, it especially is the upgrading of existing production lines to facilitate the volume output so that we can deliver to our customers.

items.statement: RBIC Chakan plant surpassed 20 million active safety units cumulative across ESP, ABS, and two-wheeler ABS platforms
items.quote: During the quarter under review, our Chakan ma nufacturing facility scaled new milestone, officially surpassing a cumulative milestone of over 20 million active safety units manufactured across each of our four-wheeler ESP, ABS, and two-wheeler ABS platforms

items.statement: Chennai power tools plant surpassed 20 million power tools production milestone
items.quote: Our Chennai power tools plant surpassed a production milestone of 20 million power tools this quarter.

items.statement: RBIC commissioning additional line for ABS10M two-wheeler ABS capacity increase and new-generation ESP10 start of production
items.quote: The decline is again attributed mainly to increase in raw material prices and one-time costs incurred for start of production of new-generation ESPs like ESP10 and commissioning of additional line for increase in capacity of ABS, which is ABS10M for two-wheelers.

items.statement: Validated CNG direct injection on engine and vehicle benches for passenger car and LCV segments, achieving diesel-par performance
items.quote: In a world's first, Bosch Limited has successfully validated CNG direct injection on engine and vehicle benches for passenger car and light commercial vehicle segments, achieving performance and fuel efficiency on par with diesel, confirming technological leadership in alternate fuels.

items.statement: Launched first PPE safety helmets range, diversifying Power Tools beyond hand tools
items.quote: In a major strategic milestone, the division successfully diversified beyond hand tools into an adjacent market with the launch of our first ever range of PPE safety helmets.

items.statement: Launched PRO360 digital platform for professionals simplifying tool management, services, inventory, and rewards
items.quote: Also launched PRO360 platform for users and sub-dealers. PRO360 is Bosch's all-in-one digital platform that helps professionals work smarter by simplifying tool management, services, inventory, and rewards.

items.statement: Surpassed 5,000 Bosch Workshops benchmark in Mobility Aftermarket
items.quote: In a major milestone, we have surpassed the landmark 5,000 Bosch Workshops benchmark.

items.statement: Received Innovation and Technology Excellence Award at annual supplier conference; Bidadi plant honored with Automation and Operational Excellence; Jaipur plant awarded Customer-Centric Approach Award
items.quote: Recently, at the annual supplier conference, the company was recognized with Innovation and Technology Excellence Award. Further, our Bidadi plant was honored with Automation and Operational Excellence. Another OEM awarded our Jaipur plant with the Customer-Centric Approach and Looking Through the Lens of the Customer Award.

items.statement: RBIC received Super Platinum Quality Award from marquee OEM partner
items.quote: RBIC's relentless focus on operational excellence directly translates into deep customer trust, recently consolidated by the prestigious Super Platinum Quality Award conferred by one of our marquee OEM partners.

items.statement: CAFE Phase 3 effective April 2027; Bosch well positioned as core system and calibration partner with super credits for hybrids
items.quote: Following the final gazette notification for CAFE Phase 3 effe ctive April 2027, OEMs are actively aligning their platform road maps. With strong regulatory incentives for alternative fuels like ethanol blends and CNG, alongside 1.6 to 2.5 times super credits for hybrids, Bosc h is well positioned as the core system and calibration partner

items.statement: Technical regulations for retrofit emission control devices mandate 60% NOx or 97% particulate matter reduction for legacy fleet
items.quote: The technical regulations for retrofit emission control devices, addressing the legacy in-use fleet, includi ng commercial vehicles and off-highway diesel engines, mandates a minimum 60% reduction in NOx or 97% reduction in particulate matter or both

items.statement: Bosch TACO JV at Nashik to start production mid-next year; TSF JV in Chennai towards end of next year; both cleared merger control worldwide
items.quote: The TACO joint venture will get into production mid-next year, and the TSF – the joint venture with TSF towards the end of next year. So, things are on track. Everything is going well, and we are making very good progress.

items.statement: EV joint venture in process of being set up; acquired several projects to run through JV; RBIC also supplies components to EVs
items.quote: We have, as already indicated, acquired several projects which will be run through the joint venture, and we'll certainly share more information about this as we go forward. We do also supply some other components from Bosch Limited and other Bosch companies, including RBIC, into the EV space as such.

items.statement: Board approved 3:1 bonus shares and share subdivision from INR10 to INR2 face value, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: The Board of Directors has at its meeting held on November 6, 2026, approved the utilization of retained earnings to issue three fully paid bonus equity shares for every one fully paid-up equity share held, and a subdivision of each INR10 equity share, including the proposed bonus shares, into shares of INR2 face value as on the record date to be determined, and the consequential increase in autho

items.statement: Discontinued employee long-term service award for managerial staff effective 1 Jan 2027; reversed provision of INR1,304 million (consolidated) and INR1,240 million (standalone) as exceptional item
items.quote: During July-September '26 quarter, the company decided to discontinue employee benefits towards service recognition for long-term service for managerial staff with effect from 1st Jan 2027 and, accordingly, reassessed the service award liability and has reversed the provision amounting to INR1,304 million, which is shown as an exceptional item.

items.statement: Steep increase in raw material prices, mainly aluminum, and adverse forex from INR depreciation versus euro impacted EBITDA
items.quote: The improvement in absolute EBITDA was mainly driven by strong growth in revenue, which was partly offset by steep increase in raw material prices, mainly aluminum, and adverse forex development due to depreciation of INR versus euro.

items.statement: RBIC EBITDA impacted by steep increase in raw material prices, particularly aluminum and ECUs, and INR depreciation versus euro
items.quote: The growth in EBITDA was less pronounced due to adverse impacts of steep increase in raw material prices, particularly aluminum, and ECUs, which drove higher material costs. This was additionally compounded by the depreciation of the INR versus euro, which further added to the increased material costs of imported components.

items.statement: Two-wheeler electronic control modules production milestone surpassed 10 million units shipped
items.quote: The company reached a production milestone with over 10 million units of electronic control modules, electronic product modules shipped to date, reinforcing our commitment to operational excellence.

items.statement: RBIC FY26 revenue INR48,935 million, EBITDA INR9,045 million, PAT INR5,891 million
items.quote: RBIC closed FY25-'26 with INR48,935 million in revenue, delivering an EBITDA of INR9,045 million and a PAT of INR5,891 million.

items.statement: Bosch Limited standalone Q2 FY27 revenue INR61,641 million, up 28.6% YoY; H1 FY27 revenue up 25.3% YoY
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, revenue from operations in July-September 2026 stood at INR61,641 million, which grew by 28.6% over July-September 2025. The growth was mainly driven by sale of products, as seen in the previous slide. Likewise, revenue for the six months period, April-September '26, grew by 25.3% over April-September '25

items.statement: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue INR76,551 million, up 28.2% YoY; H1 FY27 revenue up 25% YoY
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, revenue from operations in July-September 2026 stood at INR76,551 million, which grew by 28.2% over July-September 2025, mainly resulting from strong growth in product sales, as seen in the previous slide. Likewise, revenue for six months period, April-September '26, grew by 25% over April-September 2025.

items.statement: Global restructuring of Bosch mobility division into independent company in Germany has no impact on Bosch Limited India
items.quote: Earlier, Bosch mobility division was housed within the corporate at Bosch in Germany. And now there are two separa te I mean, the Bosch mobility division has been spun off as an independent company. All other companies in the Bosch Group are independent companies, and only Bosch mobility was housed within corporate. And that's a lot of historical reasons there, and that has been now corrected or c

items.statement: Export share from India currently 8-9% on average; future export opportunity uncertain due to geopolitical shifts and regional localization trends
items.quote: So, the current situation, for your information, is that we also have an export number of maybe 8 percent or 9 percent on an average from India. Now, to answer your question, what is the likely future situation, it's very hard to predict at this point of time.

items.statement: RBIC depreciation method changed from straight-line to written-down value in H1 FY26; one-time cumulative impact of INR775 million charged to P&L
items.quote: During the previous year, RBIC revised its method of depreciation from straight-line to written-down value method. Due to the change, a one-time cumulative impact of INR775 milli on was charged to P&L and is reflected in the results for the half-year period, April-September 2025, of the previous financial year

items.statement: RBIC depreciation alignment with Bosch Group is a timing effect expected to recover in subsequent quarters
items.quote: Yes, to align the depreciation between the mother world, Bosch India, and RBIC, we aligned. And this has an effect because it is a pull-forward of the depreciation. It's a timing effect. It ties back also to the question asked earlier about th e margin development. So since this is a timing effect, we expect this portion of the of the effect to recover in subsequent quarters

items.statement: Soda ash demand outlook challenging due to persistent oversupply, subdued industrial demand in China, and intense export competition
items.quote: the near- to medium-term outlookfor the global soda ash industry continues to remain challenging. Market conditions are characterized by persistent oversupply, subdued industrial demand, especially in China, and intense competition across export markets

items.statement: India soda ash demand growing above global average driven by solar glass capacity expansion and infrastructure investments
items.quote: India continues to outperform most global markets. Demand growth remains healthy, supported by strong activity right across segments. Capacity expansion by solar glass manufacturers and continued infrastructure investments are expected to continue to provide above-average global demand growth.

items.statement: Living Essentials demand supported by premiumization across food, feed, pharma, beverage; salt and bicarbonate stable, prebiotics long-term opportunity
items.quote: In the Living Essentials, which is mainly bicarbonate, salt, and FOS, the demand outlook remains supported by premiumization, increasing consumption across food, feed, pharma, and beverage applications.

items.statement: Farm Essentials demand affected by uneven rainfall and delayed sowing; broader agriculture outlook cautious but supported by crop coverage, irrigation, policy, technology, rural demand
items.quote: In terms of Farm Essentials, uneven rainfall and delayed sowing affected demand during parts of the quarter. Although Kharif acreage subsequently recovered, the broader agriculture outlook remains cautious, supported by crop coverage, improving irrigation, policy support, technology adoption, and resilient rural demand.

items.statement: Soda ash pricing expected to remain range-bound due to elevated inventory levels; sustained improvement depends on supply rationalization and strong demand growth
items.quote: Looking ahead, pricing is expected to remain range bound as market participantscontinue to contend with elevated inventory level. Any sustained improvement in prices is likely to depend on a combination of supply rationalizationand strong demand growth in the applications and in the geographies

items.statement: Indian domestic soda ash pricing softened in later part of year due to improved import availability and increased domestic supply
items.quote: The Indian domestic pricing softened towards the later part of the year following improved import availability and increased domestic supply.

items.statement: UK salt and bicarbonate operations impacted by sharp spike in gas and energy costs in Q2; expected to normalize as energy and logistics costs moderate
items.quote: The impact on salt is mainly coming in from, I would say, the higher gas and energy cost. In terms of bicarbonate, it also is coming in from the higher cost of getting the feedstock soda ash into the business, in addition to the energy cost.

items.statement: Capex budget around INR 1,000 crore for FY27 and similar level for FY28, includes growth projects
items.quote: Around INR 1,000 crores, Abhijit, for the current year. Next year, it should remain around the same level, without much change.

items.statement: TCNA acquired Searles Valley Minerals customer contracts representing half a million tonnes to be serviced over two years via Chapter 11 bankruptcy bid
items.quote: During the quarter, TCNA was declared the successful bidder for Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings of Searles Valley Minerals, and this led to acquisition of customer contracts representing half a million tonnes to be serviced over two years.

items.statement: Searles Valley contracts provide logistical advantage for overland sales to California and Mexico markets with positive netbacks vs export routes
items.quote: We get the benefit of being able to service customers who are in geographical proximity, which obviously enables us to also have much greater control on logistic costs, which is one of the issues which is impacting the business today.

items.statement: Sold listed shares in group companies worth INR 796 crore in July; proceeds used to repay US and UK debt; hold ~INR 8,000 crore market value of group company shares
items.quote: We sold some of those shares in July, and that came to us, and we again used it to pay off debt in U.S. and U.K. It is part of our strategy to bring down debt. That is all the shares we are holding in group companies. If you look at, we hold around 8,000 crores of shares, which are at market value in the group company.

items.statement: DGTR recommended quantity restrictions on soda ash imports for two years after finding 89% import surge in FY24 causing serious injury to domestic industry
items.quote: DGTR has recommended quantity restrictions on soda ash imports for two years after concluding that imports have surged and are causing serious injury to domestic industry. Imports increased by 89% in FY202 4 and have remained at elevated levels

items.statement: Kenya operations suspended after Ministry of Mining notice; engaging administratively and legally; lease valid until 2053, approved mining licenses paid but not issued; court hearings in November
items.quote: Kenya operations, as you know, are fairly resilient and it is a debt-free operation, and the unit has continued to generate a positive margin even in this challenging environment. It is unfortunate that the operations were suspended post notice from the Ministry of Mining.

items.statement: Operation covered under UK-Kenya Bilateral Investment Treaty protecting the investment; evaluating legal remedies including compensation beyond Kenyan courts
items.quote: Fundamentally, I think this operation is covered under UK -Kenya Bilateral Investment Treaty, because this is a UK investment into Kenya, and t he BIT actually protects the

items.statement: Kenya expansion plans included doubling capacity, adding bicarbonate unit, and partnering for container glass; all highlighted in submissions to authorities
items.quote: we were in the midst of our expansion to doubling the capacity. We were also in the midst ofadding a bicarbonate unit there, and also getting a partner to set up container glass because we ourselves are not in the business

items.statement: US peer announced 1.5 million ton production reduction at Wyoming and exit of uneconomic export volumes; confirms industry cost competitiveness focus
items.quote: Recent announcement by a U.S. producer to reduce production at Wyoming by 1.5 million tons and exit uneconomic export volume underscores the severity of current market conditions.

items.statement: TCNA exited unremunerative Southeast Asia export markets ahead of peers; focusing on Western world (North and South America) and positive netback markets
items.quote: We are in the last leg of servicing whatever was left over. Most of them would have been done. We had taken this intent not to serve Southeast Asian market much, much before, much ahead of everybody else.

items.statement: China soda ash producer inventory reached nearly 1.89 million metric tons by end September; Berun phase one 5mt maintenance in October, Qinghai Salt Lake reducing rates, Jinjing closing soda ash and bicarbonate lines
items.quote: By the end of September, producer inventory had reached nearly 1.89 million metric tons. Inner Mongolia Berun's phase one, 5 million tons, underwent maintenance outages in October. This capacity is expected to return to full operating rates at the end of the month. Meanwhile, Qinghai Salt Lake, a Solvay - based soda ash producer, will reduce operating rates at the end of October. The magnitude and

items.statement: Prolonged Middle East conflict driving input cost increases in CO2, freight and logistics; elevated energy and logistics costs weighed on results
items.quote: The prolonged Middle East conflict continued to drive input costs both in CO2as well as in freight and logistics. These were additionally weighed down by temporary suspension of operations in Kenya on the consolidated performance

items.statement: Strategy to increase contribution of non-cyclical specialty and value-added businesses, reduce earnings volatility, strengthen portfolio quality and resilience via LIFE framework
items.quote: We continue to advance our strategy of increasing contribution of non-cyclical specialty and value-added business, reducing earnings volatility, and strengthening quality and resilience of our portfolio.

items.statement: Near-term market conditions expected to remain range-bound due to China capacity additions and sustained export activity; demand supported by solar glass, lithium, food, pharma applications
items.quote: Near-term market conditions are expected to remain range-bound, especially due to the impact of capacity addition in China and sustained export activity. The demand is going to be supported by several segments, including solar glass, lithium, food, pharma applications.

items.statement: Priorities include protecting cash flows, preserving balance sheet strength, ensuring financial flexibility, optimizing working capital, maintaining disciplined capital allocation
items.quote: our priorities remain clear: strengthening cost competitiveness, enhancing supply chain resilience, driving operational excellence, optimizing working capital, and maintaining disciplined capital allocation. We remain focused on protec ting cash flows, preserving balance sheet strength, and ensuring financial flexibility amidst this uncertainty

items.statement: Searles Valley acquisition: $22 million paid treated as intangible amortized over five years; contract pricing substantially better than export option
items.quote: On that accounting treatment for this, it's an intangible treatment here. What we have paid them, $22 million, is over intangible over five years' time as an amortization part. And on the pricing part, it's much more than the export option we have. Exact pricing we can't disclose, but I think it's substantially more than the export option which we currently have.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain EBITDA margin between 20% and 25% over the long term
items.quote: our endeavor is to maintain an EBITDA margin between 20% and 25% is what we are envisaging, and that is what our endeavor is to.

items.statement: Pirelli Phase 1 production and sales expected to start next calendar year, ramping to 8 lakh tires by year four (2030)
items.quote: in Phase 1, the production and sales is expected to start in the next calendar year, and we look forward to gradually ramping up the sales volume to 8 lakh tires - in year four, that is year 2030.

items.statement: Vision 2030 targets 5% market share and 20% turnover from on-road vertical by 2030
items.quote: we have said that we would like 5% of the market share to come by 2030 and 20% of our turnover to come by this new vertical.

items.statement: Capex spend for H1 FY27 was approximately INR 1,850 crores; full year target INR 3,000 crores remains on track
items.quote: Our capex spend for H1 FY27 was approximately INR 1,850 crores.

items.statement: Remaining capex to be spent over next two years; loans preponed to speed up project completion
items.quote: Remaining we will do in next two years.

items.statement: New Carbon Black capacity online; old capacity fully utilized; new line mainly for third-party external sales
items.quote: our new capacity has come online. So, we are working towards getting that new capacity fully utilized. The old capacity was completely utilized.

items.statement: PCR tire launch scheduled for January 2027; distributor network set up for all categories including PCR
items.quote: we are looking forward to the launch of PCR tires in the month of January '27.

items.statement: OHT sales volume growth in Q2 led by uptick in end markets; India outperformed across micro markets despite erratic monsoons
items.quote: Our OHT business delivered good sales volume growth in Q2. The sales momentum was led by uptick in our end markets and segments.

items.statement: Channel inventory at normal levels; management confident of sustaining recent run rate despite headwinds
items.quote: the channel, the inventory is at normal levels, so that is what it is. And as far as the demand is there, as I mentioned, there are headwinds.

items.statement: Q2 standalone EBITDA margin 18.24%, impacted by raw material inflation, freight costs, and higher India volume share (40%)
items.quote: The standalone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR 629 crores with margin of 18.24%. The margin was particularly impacted on account of raw material prices due to global geopolitical situation and its impact on supply chain.

items.statement: H1 standalone EBITDA margin 19.42%
items.quote: For H1, EBITDA stood at INR 1,332 crores with a margin of 19.42%.

items.statement: Price hikes of 2%-3% taken mainly in Indian market; could not fully pass through cost inflation; tactical mix of price and volume to continue
items.quote: we have tried to pass on a price increase of about 2%-3%, mainly from Indian market. Globally, we are looking into the current environment, and we use a judicious mix of price and volume, which we are playing, and we are making a tactical play in this.

items.statement: Freight cost at 6.5% of total sales value; sea freight expected to remain at elevated levels with marginal increase
items.quote: it is around 6.5% of the total sales value.

items.statement: Raw material inflation and freight cost headwinds to continue for coming quarters; Carbon Black sees raw material volatility from higher crude prices
items.quote: Going forward, we believe these headwinds will continue in the coming few quarters.

items.statement: On-road portfolio (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR) contributed low single-digit volume in Q2; strong acceptance from channel and end users
items.quote: Of this, the on-road portfolio contributed early single digit to the Q2 sales volume.

items.statement: All-Steel Radial mining tires gaining acceptance in major mining markets globally
items.quote: One of the emerging growth levers for us in the OHT segment is the positive response from our end markets for the All-Steel Radial mining - range of tires.

items.statement: Strategic offtake agreement with Pirelli for premium car tires at Bhuj facility; Phase 2 envisages 50-50 JV for dedicated high-value PCR plant
items.quote: recently announced tie-up with Pirelli for a strategic offtake agreement for the production of Pirelli-branded premium car tires in our facility in Bhuj.

items.statement: Carbon Black third-party sales at around 10% of overall business; endeavor to increase third-party sales via new capacity
items.quote: third-party sales at around 10% of overall business.

items.statement: Working capital outflow significant in H1 due to 35% revenue growth (INR ~1,800 crores); inventory up due to supply chain disruption and EUDR regulation prep
items.quote: this is in line with our revenue increase for H1, which is 35%, close to INR 1,800 crores. Yes, there was a slightly increase in the inventory levels and that is mainly from the supply chain disruption

items.statement: Inventory built up for EUDR regulation compliance; expected to ease as supply chain settles
items.quote: we were also building up for the EUDR regulation, which kicks in. So we had to doubly add some inventory to cater to the regulation there so that should also start easing up.

items.statement: Gross debt INR 5,985 crores, cash INR 3,100 crores, net debt INR 2,887 crores as of Sep 30, 2026; loans preponed for capex acceleration
items.quote: As on September 30, 2026, the gross debt and cash and cash equivalents were approximately INR 5,985 crores and INR 3,100 crores respectively. Accordingly, we have a net debt of approximately INR 2,887 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended second interim dividend of INR 4 per equity share in addition to INR 4 paid for Q1 FY27
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a second interim dividend of INR 4 per equity share in addition to INR 4 paid for Q1 FY27.

items.statement: EUDR regulation kicking in required additional inventory build-up
items.quote: we were also building up for the EUDR regulation, which kicks in.

items.statement: Tire sales volume 185,167 metric tons in H1 FY27; on-road portfolio early single digit of Q2 volume
items.quote: For H1, tire sales volume stood at 185,167 metric tons. Of this, the on-road portfolio contributed early single digit to the Q2 sales volume.

items.statement: Standalone revenue Q2 INR 3,450 crores (+49% YoY) including INR 41 crores realized FX loss; H1 INR 6,859 crores (+35% YoY) including INR 76 crores FX loss
items.quote: Our standalone revenue for the quarter stood at INR3,450 crores, registering a growth of 49% year-on-year.This includes realized loss on foreign exchange pertaining to sales of INR 41 crores.

items.statement: PAT Q2 INR 291 crores; H1 INR 723 crores
items.quote: Profit after tax stood for the quarter was recorded at INR 291 crores, while for H1 PAT was INR 723 crores.

items.statement: Euro rate for Q2 FY27 around INR 103; realized FX loss on sales INR 41 crores in Q2, INR 76 crores in H1
items.quote: The euro rate for Q2 FY27 is around INR 103.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility causing raw material and freight cost inflation; headwinds expected to continue for coming quarters
items.quote: End markets across the globe were extremely volatile due to evolving geopolitical situation. Despite this backdrop, we have delivered good sales volumes growth in quarter two. The profitability was impacted due to the headwinds caused by inflation in raw materials and freight costs.

items.statement: Other expenses declined QoQ due to IPL promotion expenses booked in Q1; seasonal pattern expected
items.quote: it is the promotion expenses. We are heavily investing in the Indian domestic T20 league, and during that quarter, all the expenses for that had been booked in.

items.statement: Board approved acquisition of Adani Group's 60% stake in Monte South for INR335 crores; INR200 crores already paid; completion likely this quarter, raising ownership from 40% to 100%
items.quote: As announced on October 31, our Board has approved the acquisition of Adani Group's 60% stake in the project for INR335 crores. An amount of INR200 crores has already been paid. Upon completion, which is likely in this quarter, our ownership will increase from 40% to 100%, giving Marathon sole ownership of the landmark project Monte South in Byculla.

items.statement: Monte South has estimated future gross development value of INR6,500 crores on 100% basis; remaining unsold area 15 lakh sq ft with INR7,000 crores future sales receivable
items.quote: Friends, Monte South has approximately INR6,500 crores of estimated future gross development value remaining on a 100% project basis.

items.statement: Monte South expected to sell INR600 crores in FY27; company anticipates better than INR1,000 crores total sales this year; INR7,000 crores bookings over 4-year period post full ownership
items.quote: Assuming at this rate, Monte South will sell around INR600 crores this year. But again, I'm just extrapolating, rest is future-looking. But like I said, from the demand of rainy season, we see at least the next few festive seasons and the other good times are yet to come.

items.statement: Remaining construction spend for Monte South Tower B is around INR200 crores; project operates at 30-35% EBITDA margins
items.quote: So yes, Tower B in terms of balance cost is around INR200 crores. That being said, in this specific project, we are working between 30% to 35% EBITDA margins. So that's the typical cost.

items.statement: Monte South commercial tower launch in FY28, completion in 4-5 years; Tower D launch in FY29 with GDV INR1,800 crores; commercial GDV INR3,400 crores
items.quote: Monte South, commercial will be launched in the next financial year. Again, the GDV of that is around INR3,400 crores. And Tower D, which is something that we're going to launch in FY29, the GDV of that will be around INR1,800 crores.

items.statement: Q2 pre-sales INR154 crores vs INR86 crores in Q1; area sold nearly doubled to 71,000 sq ft; affordable and mid-income portfolio led with INR80 crores bookings vs INR31 crores in Q1
items.quote: Compared with quarter 1, FY27, booking value on our existing portfolio increased to INR154 crores from INR86 crores. Area sold nearly doubled to 71,000 square feet as compared to 38,000 square feet.

items.statement: Monte South prices increased ~10% over last 12 months across Tower A, B, C; ready-to-move Tower A commands premium over nearing-ready Tower B and under-construction Tower C
items.quote: Yes, definitely, Ashish, we have already seen that happening over the last 12 months, if you see the prices have firmed up. And even in our own project, Tower A commands a much higher value, which is ready, compared to Tower B is nearing ready, and Tower C is still away from possessions.

items.statement: Added three new projects in Versova, Sewri, Kanjur with combined estimated GDV INR1,740 crores; selective approach to well-connected Mumbai locations
items.quote: We have added three new projects, one in Versova, another in Sewri, and third is in Kanjur, with a combined estimated GDV of INR1,740 crores. These additions reflect our selective approach to well connect Mumbai locations.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR145 crores, EBITDA INR61 crores, PAT INR45 crores; H1 FY27 revenue INR362 crores, EBITDA INR127 crores, PAT INR98 crores
items.quote: Total revenue for quarter 2 FY27, INR145 crores; and for the half year H1 FY27, INR362 crores. EBITDA for quarter 2 FY27, INR61 crores and INR127 crores for half year FY27. Profit after tax is INR45 crores for quarter 2 and INR98 crores for H1 FY27.

items.statement: Company ended September with net debt-free balance sheet and positive net cash position; judicious capital allocation to continue with Monte South acquisition and wider portfolio
items.quote: We ended September with a net debt-free balance sheet and a positive net cash position. As we pursue the Monte South acquisition and developed a wider portfolio, judicious capital allocation will remain central to our approach.

items.statement: NSE/BSE 'No Adverse Observation' letter submitted to NCLT; secured and unsecured stakeholder meetings completed with positive reports; NCLT hearings scheduled this month for merger
items.quote: Friends, on the merger front, we have had NSE/BSE "No Adverse Observation" letter submitted to NCLT. As a next step, all unsecured and secured equity stakeholders meeting, as convened by NCLT, is over with positive reports filed with NCLT. Hearings of NCLT is scheduled this month.

items.statement: Marathon Futurex: leading financial services group expanded by ~45,000 sq ft; Q2 commercial sales 21,700 sq ft vs 4,000 sq ft in Q1; booking value INR107 crores vs INR19 crores; collections INR91 crores
items.quote: At Marathon's Futurex, on a combined basis, including the merged portfolio, we sold about 21,700 square feet during the quarter compared with 4,000 square feet in quarter 1. Booking value rose to INR107 crores from INR19 crores, and collections were INR91 crores.

items.statement: Bhandup launches in FY28-29 with GDV ~INR1,000 crores; Panvel Phase 3 launched with GDV ~INR600 crores; Versova and Sewri projects (combined GDV ~INR900 crores) to launch in next 2 financial years
items.quote: In the next 2 years, FY28 and '29, we are thinking of launching a couple of projects in Bhandup, which all in all, the GDV of that would be around INR1,000 crores or above. And Panvel, we have already launched the Phase 3, the estimated GDV of that is around INR600 crores.

items.statement: Redevelopment project approvals and tenant vacation process takes 8-12 months for environmental clearance and government approvals; society member inputs cause plan changes; Versova and Sewri follow this process
items.quote: Now comes the process of environmental clearance and government approval so that typically takes around 8 to 12 months, the process of getting the approval. And because even in that, the finalization of plan, the society members do have their few says, and so that the drawing slightly keeps changing.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 50% to 60% for FY27
items.quote: In terms of our growth what we have given guidance is of 50% to 60% of AUM growth.

items.statement: Branch expansion guidance of 50 to 60 branches for FY27
items.quote: In terms of the branch expansion guidance, we had given a guidance of 50 to 60 branches for this year.

items.statement: Off-book AUM target of 30% to 35% of overall portfolio in next 3 years
items.quote: Our target is to take this share to a reasonable one-third kind of an overall book number, which is roughly 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Plan to add ~28 branches by December end from current 122
items.quote: If you see by December end we would be anywhere around 150 kind of a branch number, which means from 122 to almost adding about 28 more branches by December end.

items.statement: AUM grew ~95% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our AUM has grown about 95% YoY, and profitability is again up.

items.statement: Off-book AUM nearly doubled to ~Rs 78 crores in Q2, now ~6% of total AUM
items.quote: Our AUM proportion of on-book and off-book has changed until Q2, Q1 we were at almost 1%, 2%, 3% kind of proposition which we have taken it to 6%.

items.statement: Yield on gold loans rose from 20% to 20.8% QoQ
items.quote: Our yield on gold loans have risen from 20% to 20.8% also.

items.statement: ROA at 3%, ROE crossed 10% with leverage >2.5x
items.quote: Our ROA is at 3% and ROE has crossed 10%, first time after a couple of quarters, despite of having a leverage of more than 2.5x.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 28.7%
items.quote: Our capital adequacy today is at 28.7%.

items.statement: NCD borrowings capped at 40-45% of overall borrowing; bank sanctions received
items.quote: Internally, what we have done is we have capped that t oo not more than 40 % to 45% of our overall borrowing

items.statement: NCD cost now on par with institutional borrowings due to fixed cost vs repo-linked
items.quote: NCD borrowings today are on par with the institutions' borrowings maybe sometimes cheaper, because again, these NCDs are coming at a fixed cost, whereas borrowing from institutions are rising because of the rising repo rates.

items.statement: Personal loan portfolio steady at Rs 45-50 crores QoQ, yields higher but net hurdle rate retained
items.quote: The personal loan portfolio is again, where the yields are a little higher there, and that portfolio has been at an average of about Rs. 45 crores to 50 crores QoQ.

items.statement: Target portfolio mix 90% secured gold loans, 10% personal loans
items.quote: In terms of personal loans, the portfolio mix what we are trying today is about a 90-10, wherein 90% has to be our secured portfolio, which is currently gold, and 10% is what we aspire for the personal loans.

items.statement: Focus on Tier 2/3 cities, customers with no access to banks/large NBFCs
items.quote: Our branch network is currently in Tier 2, Tier 3 cities. If you see our customer segment also, we lend to customers who have absolutely no access or maybe very little access to official banking and large banking channels and with large NBFCs.

items.statement: Competition from banks/large NBFCs acknowledged; differentiation via underserved segments and faster turnaround
