items.quote: It's a mixture of both. It's not only pricing. Pricing is always probably one of the factors, but a more important approach would be that how fast am I able to serve to the customers, which is our turnaround times.

items.statement: RBI revised framework causing transition to monthly/quarterly repayments, impacting NPA classification
items.quote: Now, as the industry transitions towards new repayment frameworks like paying monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, it's becoming a little difficult for them to regularize their accounts.

items.statement: RBI allows up to 85% LTV for consumption loans; no ceiling for income-generating loans with proper assessment
items.quote: RBI has allowed you to go up to 85% in consumption loans. But in loans wherein you can properly assess the income of the borrower, which becomes income-generating loans, that RBI technically has no ceiling.

items.statement: GNPA increased sharply to ~2.6%, NNPA at 2.4%; attributed to regulatory repayment transition and gold price correction
items.quote: The increases that you are seeing in terms of our NPAs is primarily due to one or two reasons. One is, of course, the recent changes in the regulatory framework.

items.statement: Collection efficiency declined to ~90% from ~98% QoQ, driving higher NPA
items.quote: Because of the declining collection efficiency, the delinquencies have increased and that's why you see a higher NPA as compared to the previous quarters.

items.statement: Auctions last resort; most NPA accounts regularized via reminders and customer engagement
items.quote: auction is our last resort. First , we speak to customers, we understand the intent of the customer. Historically, all NP A accounts have been regularized because customers, like I mentioned, have a lot of equity plus they have margins

items.statement: Chief Compliance Officer appointed; investing in risk, technology, operations, governance framework
items.quote: We have further strengthened our leadership team with the appointment of our Chief Compliance Officer and continue to invest in a risk, technology, operational, and governance framework.

items.statement: No fresh NCD issuance in Q2; existing NCDs committed in Q1; increasing bank borrowings and co-lending to diversify
items.quote: We have not raised anything fresh from an NCD. Whatever we had raised was already committed by Q1 itself, and there are no further fresh borrowings.

items.statement: Positive cumulative ALM mismatches across all buckets; adequate liquidity maintained
items.quote: We have maintained adequate liquidity in terms of ALM. We have positive cumulative mismatches across all our buckets.

items.statement: Gold price correction defers customer loan demand; competition intensity rising but manageable
items.quote: When gold prices usually go down, customers usually tend to defer taking a loan because, for example, if the requirement is of Rs. 10,000 and when gold prices go down, he is only able to realize Rs. 7,000 out of it.

items.statement: Transitioning to unified Augmont brand for gold loan business to reduce customer confusion
items.quote: Another important milestone is our transition towards adopting the Augmont brand across our gold loan business. Historically, operating under different brand identities created some confusion among customers.

items.statement: Loan against digital gold not permitted regulatorily; open to adjacent synergistic opportunities
items.quote: Loan against digital gold is not possible as of now. We have tried, we have understood the protocol, but as of now you can't in terms of regulatorily you can't do that.

items.statement: Management expects minimum 15% growth in publication revenue next year driven by higher-grade curriculum changes
items.quote: So with these grades changing, minimum 15% growth we are expecting.

items.statement: Management guides for around INR250 crores export stationery revenue and INR200 crores domestic stationery revenue for remaining part of FY27
items.value: INR250 crores export, INR200 crores domestic
items.quote: Yes, so around INR250 odd crores will come from exports of stationery. And in domestic, and around INR200 crores will come from domestic stationery.

items.statement: Management expects full-year stationery EBIT margin around 2% lower than last year
items.quote: Around 2% lower it will be.

items.statement: Curriculum change cycle began in FY26 and will continue over next two financial years, moving into higher grades which command larger revenue share per student
items.quote: This cycle began i n FY26 and is fully expe cted to continue over the next two financial years. Having successfully adopted to change in the lower grades during FY26 and FY27, we will now move into the higher grades

items.statement: Global stationery export markets showing signs of revival with U-shape recovery anticipated in near term
items.quote: Global markets are showing clear signs of revival. While global supply chain geopolitical tensions and shifting macro demand remain d ynamic, we anticipate a U -shape recovery in exports in the near

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA grew 150% to INR20 crores, margins expanded from 3.3% to 6.2% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So first, if I talk about standalone EBITDA, went up by 150% to INR20 crores, lifting our margins from 3.3% to 6.2%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA was INR11 crores, margins expanded from 0.4% to 3.4% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: And on consolidated, EBITDA was INR11 crores, expanding margins from 0.4% to 3.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Domestic stationery margins dragged down by branding activities, one-time GST reversal, and additional manpower costs for non-paper stationery
items.quote: So though there was a sizable growth in publication and stationery both, the margins in domestic stationery were dragged down on account of various branding activities. The re was a one-time GST reversal which you all may know that earlier we had GST on our stationery products, and since last November or so it got cancelled

items.statement: Export stationery profitability impacted by reversal of additional discounts given last year due to tariffs; discounts discontinued from H2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: However, the most of the additional discounts is discontinued. Which will result in better profitability from H2 FY27 onwards.

items.statement: New plastic products plant depreciation and fixed costs pressured stationery margins due to delayed orders from raw material price spikes
items.quote: And lastly, we have put up one new plant for plastic products. Now that also was put up with confidence of getting larger orders from our present market, but with these ta riffs, with this war, the raw material prices shot up so much, that even customers were not ready to place orders on, and that delayed our, supply, or rather sales

items.statement: Publication segment revenue grew 53.8% YoY to INR140 crores in Q2 FY27; H1 publication revenue grew 6.7% to INR544 crores
items.quote: Our Publication segment delivered an impressive perfor mance with revenue growing from -- by around 53.8% year on year to INR140 crores

items.statement: Total stationery revenue grew 18.7% YoY to INR184 crores in Q2 FY27; domestic stationery INR52 crores (34% growth), exports INR132 crores
items.quote: And on stationery, our total stationery revenue grew to INR184 crores, making an overall year-on-year growth of 18.7%.

items.statement: Indiannica revenue ~INR1 crore with loss of ~INR9.5 crores in Q2 FY27 (revenue reduced by returns of earlier year)
items.quote: So revenue is about INR1 crores and losses is about INR9.5 crores.

items.statement: Introduced 70+ new items in domestic stationery (paper and non-paper categories) in last six months
items.quote: So at present in India, we have not introduced new category, but within the same category of paper and non-paper both, we would have introduced not less than 70-odd new items in the market.

items.statement: Paper prices increased ~INR2,000 per ton (3%) in last month; mills indicating 5-10% incremental pricing over next year
items.quote: So in last 1 month, paper prices have increased by around INR2 or INR2,000 per ton. And as per the market news and the feelers, paper prices are likely to increase further from here on.

items.statement: Aggressive strategy focused on high-margin branding and non-paper stationery verticals driving domestic stationery growth
items.quote: Which was INR52 crores. It grew by 34% almost, and this continuous success is the direct outcome of our aggressive strategy focused on high-margin branding and non-paper stationery verticals.

items.statement: Expanding export stationery categories beyond existing ones to drive revenue growth despite flat category growth
items.quote: So as a strategy, what we have done now, that not only focusing the existing categories that we have, but simultaneously introducing more and more categories. items.statement: Target Apollo standalone EBITDA spread of INR 8,000-12,000 per ton over next 3-4 years
items.quote: we are confident that, I mean, without being too much aggressive in the pricing war, we can sustain INR8,000 to INR12,000 per ton kind of spreads, this journey.

items.statement: Consolidated sales volume grew 13% YoY to 24,501 tons in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Apollo Pipes Q2 FY27 consol sales volume grew 13% Y-o-Y to 24,501 tons and revenue grew 31% Y-o-Y to INR309.6 crores.

items.statement: Quarterly volume run rate of 25,000 tons, targeting 30,000 tons in Q4 FY27 for full year ~105,000 tons
items.quote: if you look at Q1, Q2, Q3 run rate, we are at 25,000 tons per quarter. So in 9 months, we'll be like 75,000 tons. And then in quarter 4, we could do like 30,000 tons for the quarter 4, so which will take full year numbers to around 105,000 tons.

items.statement: UPVC 45%, CPVC 15-20%, PPR <5%, balance from water tanks, window profiles, OPVC, HDPE pipes
items.quote: UPVC is 45% of our sales. CPVC is 15% to 20% of our sales and PPR is less than 5%. Rishab: Okay. And the balance comes from? Anubhav Gupta: Balance comes from, we have products like water tanks, window profiles, OPVC pipes, HDPE pipes

items.statement: CPVC volumes grew double-digit in H1 FY27
items.quote: CPVC has performed much better than this. Karan: Double-digit? Anubhav Gupta: Yes, double-digit

items.statement: Window profile business at INR 70-80 crore annualized run rate, targeting INR 250-300 crore
items.quote: window profile, which already is at run rate of INR70 crores, INR80 crores annualized, it will reach INR250 crores, INR300 crores number.

items.statement: Apollo maintains highest market share in North India (70% of sales) with pricing at par with top 2-3 players
items.quote: We have the highest market share in North India. 70% of our sales come from North India, and we are at par with all the top 5 -- top 2, 3 players in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Current market share ~4% pan-India, matched industry growth in last 2-3 years
items.quote: From 0, we could reach 4% market share. After that, now we are matching industry run rate.

items.statement: PVC price volatility moderated in Q2 vs Q1, government measures including minimum import price on suspension grades PVC resin supported domestic market
items.quote: Q2 FY27 saw a gradual improvement in market conditions as polymer price volatility moderated from the levels witnessed in Q1. Geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia continued to influence raw material prices, but government measures, including the minimum import price on suspension grades PVC resin and the withdrawal of customs duty exemptions supported the domestic market.

items.statement: Channel inventory soft but restocking began as prices rose in recent weeks
items.quote: channel inventory was a bit soft. It's just that in last few weeks, prices went up. So now people have started stocking up.

items.statement: Kisan operating with minimal inventory levels but PVC price fluctuations still impact profitability
items.quote: Although Kisan, we are operating with very minimal inventory levels, but then whatever inventory levels are there, it does impact the profitability, right?

items.statement: Plan to sell 2-3 owned land parcels in next 6-12 months to raise ~INR 130 crore for South India capex
items.quote: we have identified 2, 3 land parcels also, which we might sell in the next 6 to 12 months, and it could help us raise almost INR130 crores, which will help us fund our South India capex also.

items.statement: Announced INR 200 crore equity raise for ceramics business entry
items.quote: we have already announced equity raise of INR200 crores, right, when we entered the ceramic business a month back.

items.statement: Target ceramics acquisitions at 4-7x EV/EBITDA for profitable units with long-term contracts to organized brands
items.quote: our target valuation multiple is 4 to 7x EBITDA multiple basis product categories in which they are present, EBITDA margins what they are making and the type of clientele they are having.

items.statement: Kisan turnaround dependent on favorable industry dynamics and macro conditions beyond management control
items.quote: we believe that for Kisan to come out of like the challenges, we need favorable industry dynamics, right? At the same time, we are not waiting for that to happen because it is in no one's hands, no one control.

items.statement: Target consolidated plumbing EBITDA of INR 10,000 per ton with INR 3,000 crore revenue by 2030
items.quote: overall, plumbing business on a consolidated basis, we should be like INR10,000 per ton EBITDA with INR3,000 crores kind of revenue.

items.statement: Ceramics business targeting 80% domestic / 20% export mix for INR 1,000 crore revenue target
items.quote: for INR1,000 crores target, I mean, it will be like 80% domestic and maybe 20% exports.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 better than H1 as monsoon impact over and PVC prices stabilizing
items.quote: Looking at the current scenario, I believe the second half will be better than first half as monsoon impact is over, the PVC prices are stabilizing.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 volumes expected flattish QoQ due to festival labor shortage and Delhi NCR pollution ban
items.quote: December quarter should remain flattish Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR2,300-2,400 crore and standalone revenue of INR1,900-1,950 crore with domestic 20% and international 15% growth
items.value: INR2,300-2,400 crore consolidated; INR1,900-1,950 crore standalone
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we maintain revenue guidance of INR2,300 crore-INR2,400 crores. On a standalone basis, INR1,900 crore -INR1,950 crores, with domestic growing 20% and international growing 15%.

items.statement: Increased standalone EBITDA margin guidance from 25-27% to 26-27.5% for FY27; maintained consolidated EBITDA margin guidance of 23-25%
items.quote: We are increasing our standalone EBITDA margin guidance from 25%-27% to 26%-27.5% for FY27 on improved performance. For consolidated business, we are maintaining our EBITDA guidance of 23% -25%.

items.statement: Maintained capex guidance of INR200-225 crore for FY27
items.quote: Our capex guidance also remains the same between INR200 crores-225 crores.

items.statement: Domestic business growing at 22% in Q2 and over 19% in H1, broadly in line with 20% guidance
items.quote: Our domestic business continues a strong growth trajectory with a growth of 22% in quarter and more than 19% for the half year, broadly in the lines of our guidance of around 20% given in the beginning of the year.

items.statement: International revenue grew 15% in Q2 vs 10% in Q1, reflecting improving trajectory; H1 export revenue grew 12.5%
items.quote: International revenue grew by 15% in quarter 2 versus 10% in quarter 1, reflecting improving growth trajectory. Export revenue grew by 12.5% for the half year.

items.statement: Europe organic growth at 40% in Q2 and 29% in H1; ROW markets down 7% in Q2 and 1.8% in H1 due to West Asia challenges
items.quote: Our Q2 European business has grown at close to 40%, which is on the back of Q1, which has also grown quite well, but Q2 has really come back strongly. Our ROW market is down 7% in quarter 2, reflecting the consistent geopolitical challenge that we are seeing because of West Asia war.

items.statement: Added 30 new customers internationally in last six months; deepened relationships with existing customers through cross-selling
items.quote: In international markets, we have added 30 new customers in last six months, deepened relationship with existing customers by increasing our share of revenue and cross-selling new products to them.

items.statement: Mitigated guided 200-300 bps gross margin impact from raw material inflation via inventory management, price hikes, and high-value product focus
items.quote: As you may recall that in the beginning of the year, we had guided for an impact of 200 to 300 basis points in gross margin due to increase in raw material prices on account of ongoing West Asia crisis. We have effectively mitigated that risk by proactivel y managing inventory, taking calibrated price hikes, and focusing on selling high -value

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 27.4% in Q2, up 20% absolute; consolidated EBITDA margin maintained at 23-25% guidance
items.quote: Operating EBITDA was INR134 crores with EBITDA margin of 27.4% with an absolute growth of 20%.

items.statement: Spent INR124 crore on capex in H1 against annual guidance of INR200-225 crore; INR124 crore in India and INR15 crore overseas
items.quote: We spent INR124 crores on capex in first half of our annual guidance of INR200 crore-INR225 crores. Out of this, INR124 crores in India business and INR15 crores in overseas businesses.

items.statement: Established direct presence in UK to capture India-UK FTA opportunities; three projects lined up with first in Q1, second in Q4 FY27, third in Q3 FY28
items.quote: We also established a direct presence in the U.K. This ha s been done to capture new opportunities under the India-UK FTA agreement. We are already working on three important projects. Hopefully, the first project will go live in quarter 1, the second one, the quarter 4 of this current financial year, the next one in quarter 1, and then the third one is anticipated in quarter 3 of the next financi

items.statement: Started dispatching first shipments to Brazil subsidiary in October; Renato Rocha joined as CEO of Polymed Brazil
items.quote: We have also started dispatching our goods, first shipments to Brazil, the new subsidiary in October. This is a vital step for us to service our customers in Brazil, which is one of our key markets.

items.statement: Cardiology revenue INR56 crore H1, INR27 crore Q2 led by PendraCare acquisition; implanted ~18,000 drug-eluting stents by October; PACIFIER DES registry enrolled 1,150 of 2,000 patients
items.quote: Cardiology revenue was INR56 crores in H1 and INR27 crores in Q2, led by PendraCare acquisition. Clinical deployment is improving month on month. As in October, we have implanted close to 18,000 drug-eluting stents. Our 2,000 patient PACIFIER DES clinical registry has enrolled 1,150 patients, with full enrollment targeted by end of FY27.

items.statement: Launched IVL (intravascular lithotripsy) technology in August for heavily calcified arteries; expect revenue contribution shortly
items.quote: We have also launched the IVL, a minimally invasive technology that uses sonic pressure waves to break up calcium in heavily calcified arteries. This new product launch was done in August in current financial year, and hopefully we will see the revenue taking up from this business also shortly.

items.statement: Other segments grew 23% to INR317 crore in H1 and 26% to INR173 crore in Q2 with broad-based growth across critical care, transfusion systems
items.quote: The other segments grew 23% to INR317 crores in H1 and 26% to INR173 crores in Q2, with broad-based growth across critical care, transfusion system, et cetera.

items.statement: Added 28-29 new customers in Europe in H1; gained share in existing customer base as inventory normalizes
items.quote: As Himanshu also mentioned, we have been working on many projects in the larger European region, which some of them are starting to pl ay out, and some will play out in the next year. In fact, quarter 4 and next financial year. I think the fact that we have been able to gain share in our existing customer base as inventory situation normalizes, the new projects that we are doing, plus the new cust

items.statement: PendraCare's large OEM relationship (15+ years) grew 40% this year, partially offsetting Middle East revenue loss
items.quote: In fact, we are gaining more customers, including, we have grown the one of the large OEMs where we have a relationship for over 15 years, has grown at about 40% this year, right?

items.statement: Chinese dumping continues in dialysis machines; anti-dumping case filed end of June, government may take action in few months
items.value: Case filed June; action expected in months
items.quote: We are still waiting for the results of the anti-dumping case which we have filed, which was filed in end of June. It has been four months we have been pursuing with the government, and I think we are seeing some movement there. Hopefully, in few months, we should be able to see some action from the government on this issue.

items.statement: DGHS issued notification in late October mandating single-use of dialyzers (previously reused 4-5 times), effective immediately; expected to increase long-term demand
items.quote: There is a recent notification from Government of India, DGHS, to use medical devices only one time. I think this is a very big thing which has happened because currently, dialyzers were used four to five times. So now with this notification, I think most of these dialysis chains will be now forced to use it only one time.

items.statement: ROW markets down due to West Asia war: container availability issues, Hormuz Strait challenges, higher freight costs causing order delays despite strong underlying demand
items.quote: The biggest challenge is the fact that logistically to fulfill that demand is becoming very, very difficult for two reasons. One, availability of containers has been a challenge. Secondly, obviously, with all the issues going around Hormuz, getting products to the ports is a challenge. And thirdly, the freight costs have also gone up, right?

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased due to working capital growth proportional to business growth; no change in trend expected
items.quote: The working capital debt or the short-term debt is primarily increasing because of the increase in working capital, right? As the business has grown and the working capital has increased, the short-term debt has increased in proportion, right? I do not see any difference in the trend there.

items.statement: Consolidated liquidity strong at INR839 crore vs debt of INR377 crore; net cash position INR460 crore as of Sept 30
items.value: INR839 crore cash; INR377 crore debt; INR460 crore net cash
items.quote: Turning to our balance sheet, our liquidity remains strong at INR839 crores as on September 30 against consolidated debt of INR377 crores, net cash position of INR460 crores.

items.statement: Italian subsidiary has long-term debt of ~USD6-7 million with repayment of EUR1.5-2 million annually over 5 years
items.quote: One of our subsidiary in Italy has long-term debt, and that has a repayment plan agreed. That amount in total is, I think, about USD6 million-USD7 million max. That is getting repaid over next five years, so it should be between, yearly repayment is between EUR1.5 million-EUR2 million.

items.statement: PendraCare earnout milestone missed: one contract development project failed regulatory/clinical trials; reversed INR96 million contingent consideration
items.quote: One of the projects did not pass the regulatory and clinical trials, and hence that project was shelved. Because of that, we reversed the contingent consideration which we had included in our financials.

items.statement: Target to take acquired businesses to ~20% EBITDA margin in 3-5 years via procurement, supply chain, distribution, and product development synergies (1-3 year lead time for regulatory approvals)
items.quote: Our even three to five-year target is to take these companies to close to 20% EBITDA margin, and which is what we are working on, which will come through the synergy projects that we are running with them, as well as the benefit of operating leverage as th e business scales up from the current levels

items.statement: Infusion therapy expected to remain 45-50% of revenue over next 4-5 years; US expansion is infusion-driven
items.quote: I think we will be happy if the infusion contribution remains between 45%-50% over the next four to five years.

items.statement: 30 new product registrations pending in Europe; expected to become productive next year
items.quote: A lot of these will become more productive in next year, where we see almost 30 new products getting added in European markets through new registrations, which we are going through.

items.statement: Raised FY27 EBITDA floor to at least INR 310 crores from earlier INR 300 crores
items.quote: We began the year expecting to comfortably cross INR 300 crores of EBITDA. We are now raising the floor, and we expect FY'27 EBITDA to be at least INR 310 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 34.3%, highest in recent history; Q2 margin 34.3% second quarter in a row above 34%
items.quote: The first half of FY'27 was the most profitable half -year in the history of MPS. Revenue grew 17.8% to INR 448.5 crores, and EBITDA grew 39% to INR 154 crores at a margin of 34.3%.

items.statement: Research Solutions margin reached 48.2% in Q2, up more than 6 points year-on-year
items.quote: Research margins reached 48.2% this quarter, up more than 6 points in a year.

items.statement: Corporate Learning H1 margin rose to 25% from about 16% a year ago
items.quote: In the first half, the margin rose to 25% from about 16%, and EBITDA grew 77% with 19% fewer people.

items.statement: Research demand strongest in research integrity and peer review; largest customers consolidating toward trusted partners
items.quote: Across the three segments, on the Research side, demand is strongest in research integrity and peer review. The largest companies in our market are consolidating towards the partners that they trust the most.

items.statement: New research mandates won in H1 start billing November; one of five largest market companies moving 110,000+ submissions annually onto MPS peer review platform
items.quote: In the quarter, one of our biggest customers gave us a large new production mandate and a research integrity mandate that bills from November. One of the five largest companies in our market is moving more than 110,000 submissions a year onto our peer review platform.

items.statement: Education bookings led by Florida math adoption with California to follow; order booking not yet revenue
items.quote: In education, the variable is the US adoption c alendar, as you pointed out, and the next wave is already showing in our bookings, though this is order booking, not revenue yet, led by Florida with California to

items.statement: Aggressively investing in product development and tech stack; all expenses flow to P&L, no capitalisation
items.quote: This is a time when MPS is aggressively investing in product development and the tech stack as well, and we do not capitalise our expenses at all. So it's all flowing to the P&L.

items.statement: DSO improved to 38 days from 45 days at end of June
items.quote: DSO came down to 38 days from 45 at the end of June.

items.statement: Fully repaid Unbound Medicine borrowing in August; zero debt as of 30 September
items.quote: In August, we repaid in full the borrowing we took for Unbound Medicine, so we carry zero debt, and we held INR 163 crores of cash as on 30th September.

items.statement: Billed 839 clients in Q2 vs 422 a year ago; top five client concentration fell to 46% from 51%
items.quote: We billed 839 clients in the quarter against 422 a year ago, and our top five clients fell to 46% of revenue from 51%.

items.statement: Education now 30.6% of group revenue vs 27.2% a year ago; Unbound contributed INR 41.6 crores in H1
items.quote: Education is the Learn side of MPS, and it has become a real second pillar. It is 30.6% of group revenue today, up from 27.2% a year ago.

items.statement: Unbound Medicine royalty model at lower margin but provides recurring subscription base; margin improved from 12-13% at acquisition to ~18% now
items.quote: We started at 12% -13% when we bought the company. We are at about 18% now, and it continues to step up.

items.statement: Expect next acquisition to close in FY27; pipeline active; walked away from deals where price exceeded value to shareholders
items.quote: Once our next acquisition closes, we'll give you a tighter view of FY'28, and we expect the next acquisition to close this financial year.

items.statement: AJE acquired for INR 70 crores in Feb 2024; payback period 2-2.5 years; earns more than half of purchase price in EBITDA annually
items.quote: we bought the company at around INR 70 crores. And this was a deal which we did in February 2024. So, over the last two and a half years, we have completed '25 and '26. And I think this would b e the third full year. So, I think we are easily looking at a payback period of two and a half years here. 2 to 2.5 years, which is well within our

items.statement: Rule of 50 (growth + operating margin) above 50 in H1; target is full year above 50
items.quote: We hold ourselves to a simple test, which we call the Rule of 50. Add how fast you're growing to how much of every rupee you're keeping as operating profit. Most well -run companies aim for 40. In the first half, we were above 50, and the full year is the bar we measure against.

items.statement: Customers expect to share productivity gains; pricing reductions made up through volume driving margin expansion
items.quote: With pricing as well, you know, customers expect to share in our productivity, and they do, but we make that up through more volume, and that's where the margin comes from.

items.statement: Research contracts typically 3-5 years long-term; pricing done in win-win format where volume offsets any price reductions
items.quote: The contract life cycle is pretty much the same. Typically, they tend to be three to five years and are long-term contracts. On pricing, as I was sharing earlier, it tends to be done more in a win -win format where even if pricing is reduced, it gets made up in volume, which is showing up in our margins.

items.statement: Democratic Congress seen as favourable: protects NIH/NSF funding, nursing workforce programs, education budgets; supports multi-year customer commitments
items.quote: A Democratic majority is highly favourable because it makes deep cuts to the NIH as well as the National Science Foundation much less likely. More funded research means more manuscripts, and more manuscripts mean more review, more integrity checks before they are published, which is a great positive for our research business.

items.statement: Hired ahead of new research mandates; headcount up; EBITDA per employee rose ~15% in Q2
items.quote: In the second quarter, EBITDA per employee rose about 15%, even as we hired ahead of new work.

items.statement: AI hollows out businesses selling hours; MPS sells outcomes so AI drives volume and margin expansion
items.quote: AI hollows out businesses that sell hours. We sell outcomes. So when AI makes us faster, our customers get more done with us and send us more work, and that volume is what is widening our margin.

items.statement: Certified to ISO 42001 in September for AI governance; 200+ engineers build AI in-house
items.quote: In September, we were certified to ISO 42001, the international standard for governing AI, so our customers can audit how we use AI the way they audit our security, and more than 200 engineers build that AI in-house.

items.statement: Returned over INR 650 crores between FY19-25; capital must earn return within 12 months or goes back to shareholders; distributions resume after acquisition capital deployed
items.quote: The principle has held since FY'19: capital must earn its return within 12 months, or it goes back to the shareholders. We've returned more than INR 650 crores between FY'19 and FY'25, and today we have zero debt and INR 163 crores of cash to work with.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of INR 1,500 crores combines organic growth with acquisitions; tighter view after next acquisition closes
items.quote: On the target itself, the INR 1,500 crore revenue figure for FY'28 has always combined organic growth with acquisitions. That has not changed. Once our next acquisition closes, we'll give you a tighter view of FY'28, and we expect the next acquisition to close this financial year.

items.statement: Largest research companies consolidating partners toward most trusted; MPS gaining share due to trust and platform ownership
items.quote: When the largest companies in our market consolidate their partners, they move towards the ones they trust most.

items.statement: Business planned at exchange rate well below current; new EBITDA floor does not depend on currency
items.quote: Also, because we plan the business at an exchange rate well below today's, the new floor does not depend on the currency.

items.statement: Research outside AJE grew ~22% in Q2 with no acquisitions; Excluding AJE, revenue grew ~22% at margin close to 50%
items.quote: Excluding AJE, revenue grew about 22% at a margin close to 50%, with no acquisitions in that number.

items.statement: Unbound Medicine subscription revenue INR 41.6 crores in H1; recurring base for Education
items.quote: It is subscription revenue that renews year after year, and it contributed INR 41.6 crores in the half.

items.statement: Corporate Learning focusing on healthcare workforce learning and APAC geography; first joint Unbound-Liberate sale won
items.quote: In Corporate Learning, yes, we are seeing an increase in budgets around AI, but a key focus area for us is around healthcare workforce learning and APAC specifically as a geography.

items.statement: Acquisition criteria: AI tailwinds, science/high-stakes content, low customer concentration, recurring revenue, defensible niche, clear integration path, price discipline
items.quote: The asset must have AI tailwinds. The field of content must be science or high -stakes content. Customer concentration should be low. Recurring revenue should be a key theme, as you suggested, and the business should operate in a defensible niche. And also, very importantly, a clear way for us to plug it into what we already do.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 stronger than H1 with double-digit growth in dollar terms for biosimilars
items.quote: We expect a much stronger second half as our growth drivers scale, while the opportunities such as Pertuzumab provide visibility beyond FY27.

items.statement: Biosimilars EBITDA margins expected in mid-20s range and improving with operating leverage
items.quote: We also remain comfortable with biosimilars delivering EBITDA margins in the mid-20s range that we have indicated earlier and improving on that as revenues scale and operating leverage improves.

items.statement: $400 million 10-year Pertuzumab contract in Brazil under PDP program with supplies starting Q4 FY27
items.quote: Biocon Biologics was recently awarded a landmark 10-year contract with a total contract value of $400 million under the Brazilian government's Productive Development Partnership, or the PDP program, as it is called, in partnership with Bahiafarma and Bionovis.

items.statement: Over $100 million in new contracts and major payor wins covering majority of U.S. population
items.quote: In parallel, we added over $100 million in new contracts and majo r payor wins covering a majority of the U.S. population

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 20% for H1 FY27; Biosimilars EBITDA margin 24% for H1 FY27
items.quote: For the H1FY27, our consolidated operating revenues grew 6% year-on-year to INR8,725 crores, and EBITDA stood at INR1,767 crores, translating to an EBITDA margin of 20% on a consolidated basis

items.statement: Generics EBITDA margin improved to 8% in Q2 FY27 from 1% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin was at 8%, up from 1% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Syngene EBITDA margin improved to 20% in Q2 FY27 from 15% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA was at INR175 crores, and EBITDA margin improved to 20% from 15% in Q1 of FY27.

items.statement: Strong demand for Insulin Glargine, Ogivri, Fulphila; encouraging momentum for Yesintek and Yesafili in U.S.
items.quote: Our established portfolio continued to demonstrate resilience with strong demand for Insulin Glargine, and Ogivri as well as Fulphila maintaining their leadership positions in their respective segments.

items.statement: Insulin franchise exceeding $300 million annual run rate with demand exceeding supply for Glargine
items.quote: You are right, it is exceeding 300 million, which continues to grow as more capacity comes online.

items.statement: Second insulin fill-finish line in Malaysia commissioned; EMA and U.K. MHRA approval received for supplies
items.quote: We also secured EMA and U.K. MHRA approval for our new Insulin Glargine fill and finish line in Malaysia, which of course expands our ability to support the growing demand that we see across these markets.

items.statement: Inventory buildup for new launches (aflibercept, aspart, ustekinumab, pertuzumab) with high order visibility
items.quote: See, the order visibility on aflibercept, aspart, ustekinumab, pertuzumab is very high. I think we are getting ready in terms of inventory buildup and all the commercial efforts.

items.statement: Higher freight costs ($5M) and solvent costs ($5M) impacted H1 margins; both easing in coming quarters
items.quote: One is the higher freight costs, about $5 million for the first half, and higher solvents cost, another $5 million. So, I think both gross and EBITDA margins are after subsuming these 2 things.

items.statement: Yesafili (aflibercept) launched in U.S. with >50% market access and key GPO partnership; Yesintek at 34% U.S. market share
items.quote: We've already established greater than 50% market access. We've established key strategic partnerships to support that commercialization with the largest GPO in the category.

items.statement: Pertuzumab (Pebrilzo) global settlement with Genentech secures EU/U.K. launch early CY2027 and U.S. launch Q3 CY2028
items.quote: this agreement secures the earliest licensed launch dates for our product across key global markets, incl uding the EU and U.K. from early calendar 2027, and the U.S. from Q3 calendar 2028

items.statement: Pertuzumab received positive CHMP opinion as first mAb biosimilar under EMA tailored clinical development approach
items.quote: Our Pertuzumab biosimilar received positive CHMP opinion, becoming the first monoclonal antibody biosimilar recommended under the EMA's tailored clinical development approach.

items.statement: FDA approval received for Yesintek single-dose prefilled autoinjector
items.quote: We received FDA approval for Yesintek single-dose prefilled autoinjector, further strengthening our immunology offering in the U.S. and Canada.

items.statement: 20 tender awards secured across Italy, Spain, France, and Denmark in Europe
items.quote: We also secured approximately 20 tender awards across key markets that included Italy, Spain, France, and Denmark.

items.statement: 10-year Pertuzumab partnership in Brazil with Bahiafarma and Bionovis; consortium received 100% PDP allocation
items.quote: A significant development is our 10-year Pertuzumab partnership in Brazil with Bahiafarma and Bionovis. The consortium received 100% allocation under Brazil's PDP program.

items.statement: 5% revenue deferral (~$20M) due to logistics/geopolitical issues; revenues booked in October, incremental EBITDA to flow in Q3
items.quote: The quantum is roughly $20 million or so.

items.statement: Interest costs declined 12% YoY to INR240 crores; expected to reduce further as debt is retired
items.quote: Interest costs continued to trend lower during the quarter, declining 12% year-on-year to INR240 crores, following the actions taken to strengthen our balance sheet.

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization stable; large changes unlikely except for accretive capacity additions
items.quote: Yes, very much. Look, once a while, subject to capacity addition, but that will be accretive. Like we referred to insulin capacity addition, both internal and external, through CMO network.

items.statement: COO Rhonda Duffy retiring March 2027; George Kaliviotis joining as COO April 2027; CTO transition from Mandar Ghatnekar to Mukesh Rathi January 2027
items.quote: Rhonda Duffy, our Chief Operations Officer, will retire from her current role in March 2027, having built a phenomenal team and significantly strengthened our commercial capabilities. George Kaliviotis has already joined us and will succeed her as COO starting April 2027.

items.statement: Commercial reorganization: regional heads now report directly to CEO; Matthew Erick (CCO advanced markets) departed; Joshua Salsi expanded to lead Biologics and Generics in North America
items.quote: We have also streamlined our commercial organization to make it leaner and bring us closer to our customers. Our commercial heads from North America, Europe, and emerging markets will now report directly to me.

items.statement: Biosimilars R&D investment at 7% of revenues

items.statement: Q2 FY27 net operating cash flow INR152 crores; H1 FY27 INR233 crores

items.statement: ~30% of collections converting to operating cash flow, indicating healthy margin profile

items.quote: Net debt stood at INR200 crores as on September 30, 2026 compared with INR215 crores as on June 30, providing us with adequate financial flexibility to support our growth plans.

items.statement: Comfortable with ~INR1,000 crores annual land outflow capacity given operating cash flow and debt headroom

items.statement: Construction outflows more than doubled YoY; on track per plan

items.statement: Focus on mid-to-premium residential; vertical developments to become majority of portfolio over medium term

items.statement: Mumbai entry strategy: competitive pricing with premium positioning, relying on brand, product quality, design and amenities to differentiate

items.statement: Underwriting assumes current prices, not dependent on price escalation; provisioned higher inflation/contingency buffers in last 1-1.5 years absorbing recent commodity cost spikes

On the cost side, we've in fact probably, in fact, started provisioning for more on inflation as well as on contingency in the last 1-1.5 years

items.statement: Inventory on balance sheet INR2,700 crores: mostly construction/overhead spend on near-completion JD projects, minimal land payments

items.statement: Propane pricing difficult to hedge as Saudi CP announced monthly with no mathematical logic

items.statement: Power plants running due to energy shortage; working on turnaround plan with utility entities

items.statement: GSPC LNG at 24-25% capacity utilization and now in cash profits

items.quote: Employee Benefit Expenses was INR 99 million in Q2 FY27 against INR61 million in Q2 FY26 and INR 84 million in Q1 FY27, a year-on-year increase of 62.3% and a sequential increase of 17.9%.

items.statement: PiiX AI-powered Apple Ads platform live with advertisers, gaining traction; enhancing keyword intelligence, AI bid optimization, custom product page intelligence

items.quote: I would say we will only utilize few marginal percentage of the rigid PCBs which are there. But the mounting, I think we will be utilizing at least 30% to 40% of the SMT or the PCBA capabilities.

items.statement: Kavach trials ongoing, difficult to quantify completion percentage; orders have 12-month delivery timelines
items.quote: But to answer your question, it is very difficult to give a number as to how much percentage has been completed.

items.statement: Healthy debt-equity ratio maintained; will approach bankers if working capital needs arise
items.quote: And if at all there would be a requirement, we still enjoy a very healthy debt-equity ratio. So, we will be reaching out to the bankers and the financial institutions as and when required.

items.statement: Over 100 R&D engineers focused on railway technology development
items.quote: In India, there will be very few SMEs who have more than 100 R&D engineers and they are working on technology development and growth. We are very proud to say that Concord happens to be one of them.

items.statement: IGBT propulsion system development ongoing per railway specifications; alternative fuel propulsion (battery/hydrogen) progress significant
items.quote: on the IGBT side, the project is alr eady ongoing as per our requirement and we are continuously doing the development of that

items.statement: Non-Kavach order book includes ~INR 100+ cr from locomotive subsystems and real-time monitoring/sensing applications
items.quote: Except that I think there is about INR 100-plus crores of an order book which is received from locomotive subsystems as well as some real -time monit oring and sensing applications

items.statement: Fusion PCB revenue expected to start in FY27; battery loco conversations translating to significant revenue
items.quote: We are very hopeful for that.

items.statement: Order book 4x FY26 revenue at INR 846 cr
items.quote: So, the un-executed order book as on 30th September 2026 stands at INR 846 crores all put together as a group which is almost 4 times of the entire revenue of financial year 2026.

items.statement: Targets INR2,500 crores revenue at 15-18% EBITDA margin by FY30
items.quote: strategic priorities remain clear: value -added yarns, vertical integration, green energy and operational excellence. These keep us on track towards our goal of INR2,500 crores revenue at a 15% to 18% EBITDA margin by FY30

items.statement: Expects FY28 revenue around INR1,800 crores
items.quote: So just continuation of that, H2 will be somewhere around -- will be closing at INR1,700 odd. So Yes, I would say INR1,800 odd number is something which is, yes, very likely for FY28.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 20.6% vs 11.2% YoY; Q3 margin expected between Q1 (17%) and Q2 (20.6%)
items.quote: that the Q3 margin, our view is that it will be closer to Q1 and maybe Q4 comes closer to Q2. So overall, I think somewhere between Q1 and Q2 is where our yearly margin would be

items.statement: Q2 spreads at INR173/kg vs Q1 INR160/kg; Q3 spreads expected between Q1 and Q2 levels
items.quote: The spread in Q1 was 160 and Q2 it is at 173. So the spreads actually went up. In Q3, we sort of expect the spreads to come somewhere in between these two.

items.statement: Demand absolutely no challenge, robust from all markets exports and domestic; shaping up to be a very good year for spinning industry
items.quote: Even going ahead also, we see the demand absolutely no challenge. Demand is quite robust from all the markets, exports and within domestic as well. There could be some impact because of raw material volatility. But overall, I think it is shaping up to be a very good year for the spinning industry.

items.statement: Domestic cotton prices rose from INR64,000 to INR69,000 per candy during Q2, now around INR67,000; at parity with global cotton
items.quote: Domestic cotton prices rose from around INR64,000 per candy to INR69,000 per candy during the quarter and have remained around INR67,000 since. This price is at parity with global cotton, helping in the competitiveness of Indian yarn.

items.statement: Government removed duty on imported cotton extended till December to stabilize prices and availability
items.quote: Proactive steps from Government of India to remove the duty on imported cotton and also extending it till December are steps in the right direction and will help stabilize the cotton prices and availability.

items.statement: Operating at ~99% capacity utilization; Meenakshi unit at full capacity; fabric revenue share increased to 16% from 11% YoY
items.quote: We continue to operate at around 99% capacity utilization. Our Meenakshi unit has reached full capacity and the share of fabric in our revenue increased to 16% from 11% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: INR410 crores approved for 58,368 spindles + 5MW rooftop solar; completion by end FY28, full benefit FY29; revenue INR400-420 crores at 14-15% EBITDA
items.quote: In addition, we have received a board approval for an investment of INR410 crores which includes margin money on working capital requirements, towards adding 58,368 spindles along with 5 megawatts of rooftop solar. This project will generate a revenue of I NR400 crores to INR420 crores at an EBITDA of 14% to 15%. We expect to complete this project by end of FY28, and the full benefit can be expect

items.statement: 11MW ground solar project under progress, commissioning by end Q3; total green energy to reach 76MW
items.quote: 11-megawatt ground solar project is under progress and will be commissioned by end of Q3. This will take the total green energy installation to 76 megawatts.

items.statement: Total MOU commitment INR1,035 crores with TN government; INR675 crores invested; balance under discussion for incentives
items.quote: Of the INR1,035 crores committed under the MO U with the TN government, INR675 crores have been invested. Our planned knitting expansion will be completed in Q3 with receipt of balance machines

items.statement: Repaid INR74 crores debt in H1; net debt INR48 crores; net debt-to-equity 0.03x
items.quote: During the half year, we repaid about INR74 crores of debt and now net debt is at INR48 crores, a net debt-to-equity of 0.03x.

items.statement: No buyback planned; focus on growth capex over shareholder returns
items.quote: Resham ji, no plan as of now. Our focus is more on growth side, right? So whatever margins and cash flow we will have, we'll sort of put it into the business to ensure that this company can grow even faster.

items.statement: Fabric contribution 16.5% in Q2, targeting 16.5-17% by year-end
items.quote: So, Saransh I think it was 15.6%, now it is around 16.5%. So definitely the contribution is inching upwards. We sort of plan to end the year somewhere in the range of 16.5% to 17% from our overall fabric contribution.

items.statement: Exports ~8% of revenue; 30-35% of exports to Bangladesh; LDC extension neutral for industry
items.quote: Our export is almost -- I think last quarter, in Q2, it is about 8% of our overall top line. Out of that, about 30% goes to Bangladesh, right? So 30% to 35%, depending on quarter to quarter, it goes to Bangladesh.

items.statement: UK and New Zealand FTAs in force; India-EU agreement expected early 2027; benefits visible in a year
items.quote: UK and New Zealand FTAs are now in force, and the benefits of the same will be visible in a year's time. The India-EU agreement is expected to be operational in early 2027, and there seems to be steady progress on other discussions -- other in-discussion FTAs.

items.statement: Fire incident at rented Tuticorin warehouse in Aug'26 caused INR27 crores exceptional loss; inventory fully insured; claim under progress; investigation conclusion expected by Q3 end
items.quote: the entire inventory was insured. Investigation is underway. So there are multiple steps in the investigation where police has to investigate, forensic has to investigate. That is all in progress. We expect a conclusion of this investigation by Q3 end

items.statement: Q2 revenue INR446 crores (+31% YoY), EBITDA INR92 crores (+141%), adjusted PAT INR56 crores (+249%); H1 revenue INR856 crores (+40%), EBITDA INR162 crores (+129%), adjusted PAT INR95 crores (+223%)
items.quote: Our revenue has reached INR446 crores, up 31% year-on-year. EBITDA came in at INR92 crores, up 141% with margin improving to 20.6% from 11.2% and PAT adjusted for the exceptional loss was INR56 crores, up 249%.

items.statement: Sequential growth: revenue +9%, EBITDA +31%, adjusted PAT +42%
items.quote: On a sequential basis, revenue grew 9%, EBITDA grew 31% and adjusted PAT grew 42%.

items.statement: Higher raw material prices may pressure near-term margins as cotton prices move up
items.quote: However, higher raw material prices will take time to be absorbed and margins may see some near-term pressure as cotton prices move up.

items.statement: PM MITRA Park delayed due to consultative approach on common infrastructure specifications and retendering; cushion added to timeline
items.quote: The delay comes because we have taken a very consultative approach where all the allottees are working with the SIPCOT, which is sort of the execution body, to ensure that the common infrastructure comes as per the requirement of the allottees.

items.statement: Total land bank ~250 acres including factory land; surplus land book value ~INR100 crores; land used for expansion projects
items.quote: The total approximately the land which, if I can say, including the land which we are already having utilized for the purpose of the factories and everything, will be in the range around 250 acres of land. Some land out of t hat will be a surplus land and the book value of the surplus land will be in the range of around INR100 crores

items.statement: Capital subsidy accounted as deduction from gross block
items.quote: Yes. Essentially, the increase in current assets is largely because of the cotton advances

items.statement: Garmenting viewed as logical next step after ready-to-cut fabric; evaluating favorably but no announcement yet
items.quote: It's a very logical next step because we anyways are planning to come to ready-to-cut fabric. It's a logical next step to look at garmenting. All I can tell you is that we are looking at it favorably, right? I have nothing to announce right now, but yes, we are looking at it favorably.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by fabric mix shift, green energy lowering power cost, product optimization, strategic customers, and market tailwinds; believes Q1-Q2 margins sustainable
items.quote: A large part of it is sustainable. We believe that the margins which we have achieved in Q1 and Q2 are sustainable because one, our vertical integration is there. We are constantly focusing on ensuring our power cost remains on the lower side. Third, as we have sort of said multiple times, we have an approach of focusing on strategic customers and ensuring that we are able to continuously bottom s

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR 159.9 crore, highest ever H1 revenue
items.quote: Coming to the first half performance, we recorded our highest ever H1 revenue of INR 159.9 crores compared to INR 53.5 crores in H1 of FY '26.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 54.3%, up from 49% in Q1 FY27 and 50% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Gross profits stood at INR 49.6 crores, registering a growth of 143% year-on-year and 47% on a sequential basis, with a gross margin of 54.3% compared to 50% in Q2 last year and 49% in Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 25.4%, five-fold sequential improvement
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 23.2 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.4%, compared to a loss of INR 8 crores in the corresponding quarter last year and a five-fold improvement on the sequential basis.

items.statement: Closing order book INR 202.2 crore as of 30 September, down from INR 256.8 crore in Q1
items.quote: Our closing order book as of 30th September stood at INR 202.2 crores compared to the corresponding period, INR 256.8 crores in Q1, reflecting the continued execution of our existing orders.

items.statement: Majority of INR 202 crore order book is defense orders
items.quote: The significant majority of that order book is in defense side itself. So, that is the primary sort of split there.

items.statement: Expecting order conversion in Q3 and Q4 as government procurement cycles favor second half
items.quote: Our typical business cycles imply that there will be a little bit lower realization in the first half of the financial year because of the way government procurement cycles pan out. So, Q3 and Q4 is where we expect a lot more conversion to happen.

items.statement: Fast-track procurement opportunities worth INR 20,000 crore across ISR and combat UAV categories progressing with RFPs expected
items.quote: As discussed in previous calls, the estimated INR 20,000 crore fast-track procurement opportunities across ISR and combat UAV categories represent a significant development for the industry. We are seeing progress across these programs.

items.statement: Annual product development investment of INR 80-90 crore ongoing
items.quote: Roughly about INR 80 crores to INR 90 crores get invested on a year on basis.

items.statement: ZOLT Hybrid demonstrated 100 km range and 6+ hours flight time in field testing
items.quote: In field testing, the platform demonstrated long-range ISR capabilities of up to 100 kilometers and 6+ hours of flight time with an advanced ISR payload and electronic warfare resilience.

items.statement: ZOLT UCAV variant launched in October with combat capabilities including air-launched precision effects
items.quote: In October, we launched the ZOLT UCAV variant, introducing combat capabilities to the platform. This idea expands ZOLT's applications beyond surveillance into tactical combat roles, including air- launched precision effects

items.statement: Combat UAV programs targeting customer field trials in H2 FY27
items.quote: Our focus is now on maturing the relevant systems and preparing them for customer field trials in H2 FY '27, including participation in emerging fast-track procurement opportunities.

items.statement: Q2 revenue driven by heavier defense deliveries changing product mix
items.quote: for this particular quarter the defense deliveries have been the most heavier ones, and hence the change.

items.statement: UAVs deployed by law enforcement for AI-enabled crowd monitoring at large religious gatherings
items.quote: During the quarter, our UAVs were deployed by law enforcement agencies for AI-enabled crowd monitoring and public safety at multiple large religious gatherings.

items.statement: Product demonstrations conducted for prospective customers in South America
items.quote: We also successfully conducted product demonstrations for prospective customers in South America and are pursuing these engagements towards commercial opportunities.

items.statement: Mutually terminated proposed JV with First Breach in US; no capital contributed; pursuing US market independently via subsidiary
items.quote: On the U.S. front, as recently disclosed, we have mutually terminated proposed joint venture agreement with First Breach. The joint venture had not been operationalized and no capital was contributed. Our commitment to the U.S. market remains unchanged.

items.statement: Blue SUAS certification paperwork ongoing; will take more time due to involved process
items.quote: paperwork is on insofar as the Blue SUAS certification is concerned. It will take some more time because it is a very involved process.

items.statement: Exploring partnership and JV opportunities in Middle East after Abu Dhabi visit
items.quote: From the Middle East standpoint, yes, I think there is a lot of positive developments in terms of opportunity. There is an explosion in terms of activity there as well. We are exploring partnership opportunities, joint venture opportunities there.

items.statement: Japan market showing interest in eVTOL category; early stage discussions underway
items.quote: particularly eVTOL category is an interesting category for that market. And we believe that that's a white space that can be leveraged in terms of how we can address the requirements of the defense and civil forces there.

items.statement: DAC cleared proposals worth INR 2.12 lakh crore including long-range UAS, surveillance UAV, integrated surveillance and strike systems, long-range kamikaze drone systems
items.quote: The Defence Acquisition Council has recently cleared proposals from defence services worth INR 2.12 lakh crore, including programs for long-range UAS, surveillance UAV, integrated surveillance and strike systems, and long-range kamikaze drone systems.

items.statement: Enhanced procurement powers for field commanders under Delegation of Financial Powers to Defence Services 2026 expected to support increased command-level procurement
items.quote: the enhanced procurement powers for field commanders under the Delegation of Financial Powers to Defence Services 2026 are expected to support increased procurement activity at the command level compared to historical levels.

items.statement: QIP of INR 500 crore completed; capital deployment split between debt repayment, product development, corporate purpose, and working capital
items.quote: Distribution is split between repayment of debt, product development, corporate purpose, and obviously for our working capital.

items.quote: This particular is a debt form that we have received. It is for a period of roughly about 10 years and for an interest of 4%.

items.quote: We have made 4-odd investments in various entities particularly Nautical Wings, one of our investments. They are one of our downstream suppliers who have helped us indigenize a lot of the carbon fiber propellers that we leverage on our UAV systems.

items.statement: Over 1 million flights completed by customers informing edge AI and payload improvements
items.quote: These efforts are informed by our experience from over 1 million flights completed by our customers.

items.statement: Persistent global supply chain constraints and customer approval delays impacting delivery commitments
items.quote: We have maintained this execution momentum despite persistent global supply chain constraints and certain delays in customer approvals for deliveries. These challenges remain, and our teams continue to work closely with suppliers and customers to minimize their impact on our delivery commitments.

items.quote: Some of them have been jet-based for long-range one-way attack systems, those kind of opportunities we do not have a ready product for that we could have bid with.

items.statement: Medium-term aspirations: loan book growth 25-30%, secured lending ~55% of portfolio, NIM ~8%, ROE ~15% for FY28
items.quote: Our medium-term aspirations remain focused on achieving loan book growth of around 25% to 30%, increasing secured lending to around 55% of the portfolio, maintaining NIMs of around 8% and delivering a ROE of ~15% for FY28.

items.statement: Expect ROE to exit FY27 in double digits, forming base for 15% ROE in FY28
items.quote: I remember mentioning a 2-digit ROE at the exit of FY27, which will become the base for the next year's ROE of 15%.

items.quote: We mentioned 25% to 30% is our growth expectation for this year. So, it is 25% plus.

items.quote: We are looking at further improving this over the next two quarters, hoping to get this around 70% or 75% in this year and maybe going back to ~65% because then we will have to catch up for the growth as we speak as we go along in the next year.

items.quote: Collection efficiency in the X bucket of JLG segment remained strong at 99.6% during the quarter compared with 98.6% in quarter 2 of FY26. The SMA pool within micro banking has contracted to 1.7% from 4.9% in September 2025.

items.quote: So, the overall PCR for September quarter stood at around 55.5%. Out of that, if you'll see our MFI/JLG book, PCR was 67.7%, and on the secured book, it stood at around 36%, and on the unsecured book, overall unsecured, including the retail unsecured, it stood at around 65.1%.

items.statement: Total disbursements grew 52% YoY in H1 FY27; JLG +2%, non-JLG +94%; gross loan portfolio +7.5% YoY, +2.3% QoQ
items.quote: Total disbursements during H1 FY27 grew by 52% year-on-year, with JLG disbursements increasing by 2% and non-JLG disbursements registering growth of 94%. This supported gross loan portfolio growth of 7.5% year-on-year and 2.3% sequentially.

items.statement: Disbursement yields: Retail MSME ~13%, Housing ~11%, CV/CE ~12.2%, Wholesale ~10.9-11%, Personal loan ~16%, Gold loan ~12%

items.quote: Retail MSME is giving us around 13%. Housing loan is about 11%. Your commercial vehicle and construction equipment is around 12.2%. Wholesale is around again 10.9% to 11%, personal loan is ~16% and gold loan is around 12%.

items.quote: The Bank had planned to raise INR500 crores through NCDs during the current financial year, of which INR300 crores was raised in September 2026 to support growth initiatives and reinforce capital adequacy. items.statement: Branch network mature at ~1,110 branches (780 MFI, 330 general banking); no new branches in 18+ months; growth to come from productivity, tech, existing network
items.quote: We have one of the largest network. And it's a mature network because we have not opened any branch during the last 18 months plus now. It's a mature one. items.statement: Reverse merger of holding company Utkarsh CoreInvest into bank: NCLT noted NOCs from regulators on Oct 22, 2026; next hearing Nov 19, 2026; expected completion in next few months
items.quote: On the proposed amalgamation of the holding company, Utkarsh CoreInvest Limited with and into the bank, the NCLT, during its hearing on October 22, 2026, took note of the NOCs and responses received from the concerned regulatory authorities. items.quote: The CGFMU window is currently not open for fresh loan guarantees, as the scheme is undergoing the government approval process for its next phase. We expect the window is about to reopen soon and have already accrued the requisite 1% guarantee fee towards the eligible disbursements.

items.value: INR85 cr Q2; INR149 cr H1

items.quote: Probably we should be doing that by the end of this month and applying for the customs clearance. The construction should begin sometime in the first quarter of the next financial year. And about 9 months' time, we should take to build the facility up and running.

items.quote: Currently, we are doing close to 8,000 TEUs there. We are expecting to do more than - close to 18,000 TEUs once the facility upgradation is complete. That particular initiative will basically make up to some extent of this transshipment business, which we are currently having.

items.quote: I think today, we've got a lineup of about - if you include Farukhnagar, the Chennai capacity that we have to do, JNPT expansion, the facility expansion that we pl an to do, Speedy renovation that we are trying to do, between all of that, about INR400 crores of capex requirement plus

items.quote: The way port sector, port demand in India, the port cargo in India is growing at a rate of 10% - 12%. I think similar volumes we are seeing growth in the CFS industry. items.quote: Roughly INR500 per TEU is a margin impact, which is there for the transshipment business. We expect this to continue for some time in the short run, maybe up to the next quarter. As we go along, it might taper down.

items.quote: The rate impacts are there to stay for coming quarters largely. As we go along and as the Gulf-related situation normalizes, the transshipment volume and the revenue would basically taper down going forward.
