items.statement: Evaluating JVs, tie-ups and M&A opportunities for growth, multiple discussions ongoing but nothing committed yet
items.quote: We're evaluating JVs, we're evaluating tie-ups. There are multiple discussions are going on. But until something is fructified or on table, which is comm itted, we won't be able to share that with you. But yes, everything that is within our scope to increase the volumes, increase the market share, that's on the table

items.statement: Dividend payout evaluation deferred for 6 months while assessing INR400 crore capex plus M&A opportunities and potential debt raise to 1:1 ratio
items.quote: We will have to just see - you will have to give us time to just see over the next 6 months, how does these opportunities evolve for us to evaluate our dividend payout. Plus also, we are not leveraged at all. I think when the growth opportunity comes to us, we will also like to get - take a bit of debt with us, maybe go up to 1:1 level.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 volume 190,100 TEUs up 12.6% YoY, H1 FY27 volume 366,599 TEUs up 10% YoY
items.quote: Total volume handled in Q2 FY27 stood at 1,90,100 TEUs, registering a 12.6% year-on-year growth. For H1 FY27, total volume stood at 3,66,599 TEUs, reflecting a strong 10% growth over H1 FY26.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR252 crores up 21.5% YoY, H1 FY27 revenue INR466 crores vs INR394 crores
items.quote: Revenue for Q2 FY27 stood at INR252 crores, representing a growth of 21.5% year-on-year and 17.4% sequentially. For H1 FY27, revenue stood at INR466 crores compared to INR394 crores in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA INR59 crores up 45.9% YoY, H1 FY27 EBITDA INR106 crores vs INR75 crores
items.quote: EBITDA, excluding other income, stood at INR59 crores in Q2 FY27, growing at 45.9% year-on-year and 24% sequentially. For H1 FY27, EBITDA stood at INR106 crores compared with INR75 crores in

items.statement: Q2 FY27 PAT INR21 crores up 85% YoY, H1 FY27 PAT INR27 crores vs INR20 crores
items.quote: At the bottom line, net profit for Q2 FY27 stood at INR21 crores a strong 85% growth year-on-year and 228% growth sequentially. For H1 FY27, net profit stood at INR27 crores compared to INR20 crores in FY26.

items.statement: Other expenses include INR1 crore one-time consultancy costs, expected to come down going forward
items.quote: Other expenses would come down because there has been certain onetime consultancy and related costs, which we have incurred to the extent of INR1 crores.

items.statement: Company currently not leveraged, plans to take debt up to 1:1 debt-equity ratio for growth opportunities
items.quote: Plus also, we are not leveraged at all. I think when the growth opportunity comes to us, we will also like to get - take a bit of debt with us, maybe go up to 1:1 level.

items.statement: Transshipment volumes and revenue dependent on Gulf-related geopolitical situation, expected to normalize and taper down
items.quote: As we go along and as the Gulf-related situation normalizes, the transshipment volume and the revenue would basically taper down going forward.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 operating cash flow guidance of INR750-1,000 crores; on track
items.quote: we had given a guidance that we will be looking at an OCF of close to INR750 crores to INR1,000 crores during the year, and we are on track for that for the full year.

items.statement: H1 FY27 presales INR3,200 crores across 521 units, ~60% of full-year FY26 presales
items.quote: This takes our first half year H1 presales to INR3000 -- approximately INR3,200 crores across 521 units, already about 60% of our full year FY26 presales.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 presales INR2,100 crores across 274 units from sustenance sales only
items.quote: We recorded presales of approximately INR2,100 crores across 274 units. This takes our first half year H1 presales to INR3000 -- approximately INR3,200 crores across 521 units, already about 60% of our full year FY26 presales.

items.statement: Embedded contracted revenue INR15,700 crores (83% of launched GDV) with estimated PBT INR4,800-5,700 crores yet to recognize
items.quote: On the embedded value of the INR18,700 crores we have launched across residential and mixed-use projects, approximately INR15,700 crores or 83% is now sold. Because revenue is recognized on handover, this contracted revenue with an estimated PBT of approximately INR4,800 crores to INR5,700 crores is yet to reach our P&L.

items.statement: Q2 average realization INR24,700/sq ft vs INR18,400 in FY24
items.quote: Our average realization in the second quarter was about INR24,700 per square foot compared with about INR18,400 in FY24.

items.statement: Q2 collections INR560 crores (~2x YoY); H1 collections ~INR1,100 crores
items.quote: Collections were also healthy at INR560 crores in Q2, roughly double the same quarter last year, taking H1 collections close to approximately INR1,100 crores.

items.statement: FY27 construction spend expected ~INR1,500 crores
items.quote: We execute in-house with various contractors and expect construction spend of about INR1,500 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Sector 59 Gurgaon project (GDV ~INR4,000 crores, 1.3 msf) planned for launch in Q3 FY27
items.quote: In terms of our new project, Sector 59 on Golf Course Extension Road, Gurgaon, it's a project with a GDV of approximately INR4,000 crores and is planned on a 7.25 acre land parcel with a development potential of 1.3 million square feet, which is expected to be launched in Q3 '27.

items.statement: Max Square 2 pre-leasing 3.1 lakh sq ft (~1/3 of leasable area) at ~25% premium to micro-market
items.quote: At Max Square 2 on the Noida Expressway pre-leasing has increased to 3.1 lac square feet from about 90,000 square feet last quarter. That is roughly one-third of the total leasable area, more than a year ahead of the occupancy certificate and at a premium of about 25% to the micro market.

items.statement: Max District Gurgaon pre-leasing 2 lakh sq ft at >35% premium
items.quote: At Max District in Gurgaon, about 2 lakh square feet is pre-leased at a premium of over 35%.

items.statement: Commercial portfolio targets rental income >INR1,000 crores near-term (currently ~INR700 crores run-rate)
items.quote: we are currently on a run rate of close to about INR700 crores of annual rental income from operational and under construction assets, and we look to scale this up to much beyond INR1,000 crores in the near term.

items.statement: Business development target: add 2-3 million sq ft residential development annually in NCR
items.quote: we are continuing to focus on business development and add 2 million to 3 million square feet a year.

items.statement: Total GDV pipeline ~INR29,000 crores from Q3 FY27 onwards
items.quote: And with that, we have a total GDV pipeline of close to INR29,000 crores from Q3 FY27 and continue to add approximately 2 million square feet a year of residential development annually.

items.statement: MoU for 9.7 acres Ghaziabad JDA (1.5 msf saleable, GDV INR2,500-3,000 crores) subject to diligence and approvals
items.quote: We signed an MoU for the proposed joint development agreement for 9.7 acres in Ghaziabad with a saleable potential of 1.5 million and an estimated GDV between INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores. Obviously, the transaction remains subject to diligence and requisite approvals and execution of definitive docs.

items.statement: MoU for 84.7 acres acquisition in West Delhi
items.quote: In addition, we've entered into the MoU for the acquisition of 84.7 acres in West Delhi.

items.statement: External debt INR2,100 crores (INR950 crores LRD); cash INR1,900 crores; net debt ~INR200 crores; net D/E <0.5x
items.quote: As of 30 th September 2026, external debt stood at INR2,100 crores, of which INR950 crores is lease rental discounting backed by operating commercial space. Cash and cash equivalents, including the other balances stood at INR1,900 crores, resulting in a net debt of about INR200 crores with net debt to equity well below our threshold of 0.5x.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consol revenue INR375 crores, EBITDA INR13.5 crores; lower EBITDA due to higher A&M spend (INR20 crores in Q2 vs INR12 crores YoY)
items.quote: For the half year, the consol revenue stood at INR375 crores and EBITDA of INR13.5 crores. The lower EBITDA is largely explained by advertising and marketing spend, which was close to INR20 crores in Q2 FY27 against INR12 crores in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: NCR office Q3 gross leasing 3.8 msf, 9M 10 msf; net absorption 2 msf > new supply 1 msf; vacancy down 200 bps YoY to ~17%; rentals up 6-10%
items.quote: On the commercial side, the office market has a steadier story as per reports NCR recorded gross leasing of about 3.8 million square feet in the third quarter and 10 million square feet in the first 9 months, with net absorption at about 2 million square feet, which outpaced new supply of about 1 million square feet, bringing vacancy down by about 200 basis points year-on-year to about 17% and ren

items.statement: Estate 128 Phase 1 delivery on track for FY28; Phase 2 at 9th floor slab
items.quote: Estate 128 is in the process of casting slab in Tower 2. 2 towers have already been completed. This is -- the first phase is on delivery is on track for FY28. Phase 2 work is in progress on 9 th floor slab and is on track as per our milestone.

items.statement: Estate 360 slab work at 6th-11th floor across 6 towers in 2 years from D-wall start
items.quote: Estate 360, slab work has reached between 6th and 11th floor across the 6 towers, which is in just 2 years of time from the starting of the D-wall work.

items.statement: Max One commercial tower delivery FY28; residential delivery FY30
items.quote: We have got -- the first part is the commercial tower, which is expected to get delivered in FY28. And then we have the residential collection -- residential piece, which is expected to be delivered in FY30.

items.statement: Noida auction projects (0.5 msf regulatory approval, 1.7 msf auction) timelines uncertain due to government/bureaucratic process
items.quote: It's difficult to share the time line given these are driven from a government and a bureaucratic process in terms of when the auction happens, etc. So it's very tough to put a final time line, and we are dependent on that.

items.statement: Collections structured at 20-25% of sales value annually; fund construction without incremental debt on assets
items.quote: Collections continue to be in line with the payment plan. It is structured to yield about 20% to 25% of the sales value each year and they fund construction across the residential projects without incremental debt being taken on the assets.

items.statement: Dual 5-star GRESB rating 2026 (2nd consecutive year); 100/100 in development, ranked #1 peer group; 93.5/100 standing investment
items.quote: we have secured a dual 5-star GRESB rating for the second consecutive year in 2026 with scoring 100 out of 100 in development, ranked number 1 in its peer group and 93.5 out of 100 in standing investment.

items.statement: Management expects reported margins to move closer to underlying run rate in coming quarters as major project investments are largely behind them
items.quote: With most of these projects going live and the major investment now largely behind us, we expect reported margins to move closer to the underlying run rate in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Q2FY27 EBITDA margin was 15% including INR 10 crore upfront RFP investment; normalized EBITDA margin was 18%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for Q2FY27 stood at INR 43 crores against INR 44 crores in Q2FY26, with an EBITDA margin of 15%.

items.statement: H1FY27 EBITDA margin was 12.8% including INR 28 crore upfront RFP investment; normalized EBITDA margin was 18%
items.quote: H1FY27 EBITDA stood at INR 71 crores versus INR 89 crores in H1FY26, with an EBITDA margin of 12.8%.

items.statement: Tax services revenue grew 13% YoY to INR 121 crores with market share increasing to 65.8% (+330 bps QoQ, +780 bps YoY)
items.quote: Our Tax Service business, which is a source of transactional revenue, grew 13% year-on-year to INR 121 crores. In a de-growing market, we have cemented our dominance by increasing our market share to 65.8%, an increase of 330 basis points sequentially and 780 basis points on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: CRA services onboarded 4.7 million new subscribers (+15% YoY), representing 95% of all new CRA ecosystem subscribers
items.quote: We onboarded 4.7 million new subscribers during the quarter, up 15% year-on-year, which is 95% of all new subscribers in the CRA ecosystem.

items.statement: Identity services revenue grew 24% YoY to INR 27 crores driven by 26% combined volume growth across all four digital identity facets
items.quote: Our Identity Service business, which is a strong source of transactional revenue, also delivered robust growth, with revenue up 24% year-on-year to INR 27 crores. It is driven by 26% combined volume growth across all the four facets of digital identity.

items.statement: Signed 20+ mandates and 30+ in pipeline for adjacent value-added BFSI offerings (eSignPro and CKYC bundled solutions)
items.quote: I am very happy to share here that this approach has also started translating into tangible business. We have signed 20+ mandates, key mandates already and 30+ in the immediate pipeline on these adjacent value-added offerings for BFSI customers.

items.statement: Property, plant and equipment grew from INR 63 crores to INR 150 crores reflecting ASK project investment
items.quote: Growth in property, plant and equipment from INR 63 crores in March 2026 to INR150 crores in September 2026 reflects investment in ASK project.

items.statement: 187 out of 192 mandated Aadhaar Seva Kendras live as of October 2026, up from 150 as of September 2026
items.quote: With 150 Aadhaar Seva Kendra's open till September and 187 out of the mandated 192 ASK centres live as of October'26, the major investments are all behind us.

items.statement: New initiatives contributed 16% of H1FY27 revenue (up from 12% in H1FY26), growing 56% YoY
items.quote: Our New Initiatives, in line with our strategy, contributed 16% of total revenue in H1FY27, compared to 12% in H1FY26, growing 56% year-on-year.

items.statement: eSignPro signed 25+ new enterprise customers in first quarter of full monetization including marquee BFSI and telecom companies
items.quote: eSignPro, which is our digital documentation suite, signed up more than 25 new enterprise customers in its first quarter of full monetization, including some very marquee BFSI and telecom companies.

items.statement: DSO increased from 64 days to 93 days primarily due to project receivables
items.quote: Also, DSO increased from 64 days to 93 days, primarily due to project receivables.

items.statement: Zero debt with approximately INR 750 crores cash and marketable securities as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong. We have zero debt and approximately INR 750 crores of cash and marketable securities as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Cash and marketable securities of INR 750 crores provides flexibility for technology upgrades, ASK mandates, product journeys, international expansion (JVs/branches), and potential inorganic acquisitions
items.quote: We have a balance sheet that gives us flexibility to invest in the right technology. It is our time to carpet in.

items.statement: PFRDA launched new schemes (NPS Vatsalya, e-Shramik, NPS Sanchay, NPS Swasthya, NPS Central) expanding addressable base for CRA
items.quote: There is also renewed push from the regulator, which is widening the product funnel by launching multiple new schemes: NPS Vatsalya for minors, e-Shramik for gig and platform workers, NPS Sanchay for the informal sector, NPS Swasthya which links retirement savings with health cover and NPS Central, a unified digital platform.

items.statement: Account aggregator interoperability guidelines by RBI will level playing field and benefit Protean's bundled approach
items.quote: But now with the interoperability coming into place, the stage is now equal for everyone and hence now as account aggregator for us becomes part of our bundled approach, we expect to see good volumes coming on the account aggregator side.

items.statement: PAN 2.0 transition risk: ~70% of PAN revenue from assisted model not part of PAN 2.0 mandate; pending clarity from ITD on revenue model evolution
items.quote: But I think we also have to appreciate the fact that bulk of our revenue actually comes from the assisted model. So, ~70% of PAN is done through the assisted model, which was never part of the PAN 2.0 mandate, right? But having said which, we are yet pending clarity with the ITD in terms of how the thought process is for handling that part.

items.statement: AgriStack monetization timeline depends on government decision to open stack for ecosystem use; stack ready with 11 crore farmer IDs onboarded
items.quote: But I would be quite hopeful that the government, now that the data is in place, we've seen statements made by the honourable minister and a lot of bureaucrats as well. We do believe that over the next maybe months or quarter, we should see this AgriStack being opened for the ecosystem to use.

items.statement: Management open to dividends but prioritizing cash deployment for technology upgrades, ASK mandates, product journeys, international expansion (JVs/branches), and potential inorganic acquisitions over buyback
items.quote: Of course, we always remain open for any inorganic acquisition which we believe could be strategic to us, which will either help our product line, revenue line, customer line and international expansion. Depending on some of these requirements, we do believe that this cash would be required if the company has to accelerate itself to the next level of growth. But in the meanwhile, of course, we con

items.statement: International 'DPI in a Box' strategy: partnership-led, capital-light approach targeting geographies with real need, ready funding, and geopolitical alignment; working with multilaterals, consultants, local SIs, and sovereign counterparts
items.quote: Our approach will be partnership-led, it will be capital-light and we will prioritize geographies where the need is real, the funding is ready and identifiable and our reference credentials travel well in terms of geopolitical relationships and partnerships as well.

items.statement: FY27 guidance reiterated: branch addition 40-45, spreads >6% medium term, credit cost 40-50 bps, Gross AUM growth 25-30%
items.quote: Given the progress we have made in H1, we remain confident of delivering on our FY27 guidance, which I would like to reiterate: Branch addition of 40-45 for this year. Maintaining spreads of more than 6% in the medium term. Credit cost of 40 bps to 50 bps. Gross AUM growth of around 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Gross AUM reached Rs 11,997 crores, normalized growth 26% YoY; on track for FY30 target of Rs 30,000 crores
items.quote: Gross AUM has reached Rs. 11,997 crores, a normalized growth of 26% year-on-year, and we remain well on track to achieve our FY30 Gross AUM target of Rs. 30,000 crores.

items.statement: Healthy demand in affordable housing segment continues; disbursement grew 21% YoY to Rs 1,126 crores
items.quote: Disbursement picked up well during the quarter to Rs. 1,126 crores, a growth of 21% year-on-year, and we are seeing this momentum continue into the second half.

items.statement: NIM stable above 9%; spread improved 20 bps YoY; portfolio yield 14.8% stable QoQ; finance cost 8.2% stable QoQ
items.quote: If you look at our net interest margin, it is stable above 9%. In absolute terms, NIM for the quarter is up by 27% on the back of growth in Gross AUM, and 20 bps improvement in the spread year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Collection efficiency improved to 98% from 97%; 30+ stable at 5.2%, GNPA stable at 1.5%; PCR Stage 3 at 25%; total ECL Rs 97 crores vs regulatory Rs 57 crores
items.quote: Our collection efficiency improved to 98% from 97% last quarter, with Stage 3 and 30 plus being stable at 1.5% and 5.2%.

items.statement: H1 credit cost ~60 bps due to Rs 6 cr scheduled write-off and denominator impact from disbursement booking change; confident full year within guided 40-50 bps
items.quote: If you look at our credit cost, for H1 it is at about 60 basis points. So, there is a factor generally a seasonality wherein H1 remains slightly higher in terms of the overall credit cost and H2 remains favorable in terms of credit cost.

items.statement: 53% portfolio variable/semi-variable (15% variable, 38% semi-variable); semi-variable starts turning variable from Q4 FY27 over 3 years; can pass on cost increases to new disbursements (30-35% of AUM)
items.quote: Further, over the last 4, 5 years, we have started disbursement in variable rate product and semi variable rate product. So now 53% of our portfolio is comprised of variable and semi variable rate product, wherein we have opportunity to pass on some cost impact to the customer as well.

items.statement: Investing in digital solutions, tech initiatives and collections; opex/AUM stable at 4%, cost/income at 36%; expect opex/AUM to improve ~15 bps YoY in FY27
items.quote: Over the last 2 quarters, we have been investing on digital solutions, tech initiatives and collections. So, we'll start seeing the impact of the same on our efficiency and productivity in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Opened 8 branches in Q2 (0 in Q1); on track for 40-45 branch additions in FY27; digital sourcing disbursement grew from 4% to 7% YoY
items.quote: So, this year, in the first quarter, we have not opened any branches as we were doing tweaks in terms of changing disbursement booking mechanism. And in quarter 2, we have opened around 8 branches. So, as we move in this rest H2, there you can expect the branches opening and reaching the same level of 40, 45 branches that we have planned.

items.statement: Borrowing profile diversified across 30+ counterparties; NHB share 14%; avg tenure >8 years; liquidity >Rs 700 cr + undrawn sanctions >Rs 1,400 cr; ALM positive all buckets; 20% fixed rate, 25-30% market-linked, 50% MCLR-linked
items.quote: On liquidity side, we are comfortably placed with liquidity of more than Rs. 700 crores and undraw sanction of more than Rs. 1,400 crores. Our ALM is positive across all the buckets.

items.statement: IRDA draft regulations may impact non-interest income; multiple levers to offset; final circular awaited; RBI co-lending guidelines (CLM-1) and GST on excess interest made co-lending unattractive currently
items.quote: On the IRDA side, we have got the draft regulations from the IRDA at this point of time. There will be some impact on the overall non-interest income, if the circular get implemented as such. But we have multiple levers to offset that particular impact.

items.statement: LAP 44% of AUM; balance sheet home loan ratio 68% (regulatory threshold 60%); PBC requirement ~63%; incremental mix ~57-58% home loans sufficient for compliance via DA of LAP
items.quote: So, let me just clarify the regulatory expectations. So, the regulatory expectation is to maintain a 60% home loan ratio at a balance sheet level, not at the portfolio level. So, we keep doing direct assignment transaction of our LAP portfolio to maintain our overall healthy ratio of HL and LAP mix at the balance sheet level.

items.statement: Self-employed 75-80% of portfolio; avg ticket size Rs 10-11 lakh; <Rs 8 lakh bucket shows higher delinquency but delivers ROE >20%; BT-out rate contained at ~4% (down 40 bps YoY)
items.quote: BT out rate for the quarter is around 4%, down by 40 bps year-on-year. This is stable quarter-on-quarter. Our focus driven approach of customer retention is helping us to contain BT out.

items.statement: No new prime player entry in Tier 3/4 self-employed segment; opex-heavy model (2.75-4% of AUM) deters large banks; BT-out stable 4-5%; each player has own niche
items.quote: We have not seen any kind of such challenge from prime entering typically into these Tier 3, Tier 4 markets where we're operating for the same self-employed customers. We have to understand the model is very opex-heavy model.

items.statement: Hired senior resources from leading tech-focused companies to strengthen engineering and AI initiatives; increased team size in Q1 for collections
items.quote: To strengthen these initiatives of engineering and AI, we have recently hired senior resources from leading tech focused companies.

items.statement: ROE 17.3% for quarter (up 30 bps YoY); ROA 5.7% at 3.1x leverage; H1 PAT grew 20% YoY (28% normalized for lower DA)
items.quote: ROE for the quarter is 17.3%, up by 30 bps year-on-year. ROE without considering direct assignment is about 16%.

items.statement: Identified ~750 pin codes across ~40-50 branches for tighter underwriting due to drought/agri-income risk; MP normalizing, Karnataka improving; <Rs 8 lakh bucket stress monitored
items.quote: We are working around 8,000 of pin codes. Out of that, some 750 pin codes have been identified, where we have tweaked our underwriting models and also created a cautionary environment.

items.statement: Rating upgrade expected in next couple of quarters (3-year vintage from last upgrade); engaging with India Ratings, CARE, ICRA; upgrade could reduce cost by 15-20 bps
items.quote: Our rating upgrade is scheduled like in another couple of quarters. Once that rating upgrade will come in, that will help us to bring down costs by about 15, 20 basis points from here.

items.statement: Maintains double-digit revenue growth target for FY27 with stronger second half in revenue and profitability
items.quote: Every team member is confident of delivering what we committed earlier, which is a double-digit revenue growth in '27 with a stronger second half in both revenue as well as the profitability.

items.statement: Targets 120-day receivables cycle by March 2027
items.quote: We are internally committed with each one of us to achieve the 120-day cycle by March 2027, which will be around that, we will be able to achieve either the number what I said around 120 or even better than that.

items.statement: Festive calendar shift moved significant budget share to Q3; multinational clients cautious due to global scenarios and fuel costs
items.quote: The timing of the festive calendar this year and measured approach to spend among multinational or global clients as Navratri began on 11th of October this year vis-a-vis 22nd September last year that moved a significant share of budget or wallet to the Q3 of this year.

items.statement: Bangalore Metro ~50% assets activated, targeting 75-100% by March; Kolkata streetscape 40-45% live, completion by March
items.quote: Given that we have already covered 50% of the installation capacity, we are confident of reaching 75% to 100% of the activation by end of March. Similarly, in Kolkata, 40% to 45% of the streetscape media is live and already generating revenue.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR48 crores mainly for new transit media assets, funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Capital investment during the first half amounted to INR48 crores directed mainly at new transit media assets and funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Operates 10,000+ display points across 30+ cities under long-term tenure; Bangalore Metro installation limited to 4-hour nightly window
items.quote: We operate around 10,000+ display points across the mentioned cities held under long-term tenure and the spaces as advertising rights where Urban India works, shops, travel and spends its leisure time.

items.statement: Cost of services rose 6% to INR83 crores in Q2 with new transit assets; fixed fees on long tenure media rights do not vary with quarterly billings
items.quote: Cost of services, which largely comprises fixed fees on long tenure media rights, rose 6% to INR83 crores with the addition of new transit assets.

items.statement: Fund-based debt INR195 crores (broadly unchanged); debt-to-equity improved to 0.61x from 0.68x; CRISIL upgraded long-term rating to A- Stable
items.quote: Fund-based debt stood at INR195 crores, broadly unchanged from INR196.1 crores in March, and our debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.16x (ERRATA: To be read as 0.61x) from 0.68x.

items.statement: Corporation Junction site upgrade expected to substantially increase revenue from INR33 lakhs/month; yield per sq ft improvement across portfolio without capital-intensive new assets
items.quote: As a conventional format, it currently generates about INR33 lakhs a month. Following the upgrade, we expect its revenue potential to increase substantially. Now this multiplied and applied across the portfolio, this is how we intend to raise yield per square feet without adding capital-intensive new assets.

items.statement: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation agreed to permit advertising-driven community-led public space projects adding art and culture
items.quote: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited has since agreed to permit such projects, which are advertising-driven but connecting with the community-led public spaces where we add art, culture and the celebration moment what a city is lacking for.

items.statement: Nagpur Airport revenue not expected to shift materially in next 1 year pending Phase 1 completion and traffic growth
items.quote: Overall, a growth of Nagpur in coming time, I don't expect anything to happen until we complete our Phase 1 with a private partnership, which is aligned with us because we are running that airport from our side more than 2 decades.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances increased to INR35.3 crores from INR24 crores; net worth INR321 crores as on 30th September 2026
items.quote: Cash and bank balances increased to INR35.3 crores from INR24 crores and net worth stood at INR321 crores as on 30th September 2026.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance same as before, aim to overachieve
items.quote: The guidance will be same. We will try to overachieve it.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR22,681 crores as of September 30, 2026, diversified across roads, transmission, renewable, metro and industrial
items.quote: As on Se ptember 30, 2026, our order book stood at INR22,681 crores, providing a strong execution visibility over the coming years

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY2027 is INR6,000 crores; already achieved close to INR5,400 crores in H1
items.quote: We have guided INR6,000 crores to the investors. We have already achieved close to INR5,400, and we have already quoted tenders more than INR10,000 crores, and INR6,000 is easily achievable.

items.statement: Total equity requirement for asset portfolio INR2,632 crores; INR669 crores infused till date, INR161 crores in current year, targeting INR700 crores this year, INR730 crores next year, INR397 crores in third year
items.quote: We have the requirement of INR2,632 crores, INR669 crores already infused till now, and INR962 crores is the balance, and INR161 crores we have already infused in this year. items.statement: Trade receivables INR 264.3 crore (Sept 26) vs INR 184.9 crore (Mar 26); inventories INR 245.2 crore vs INR 208.7 crore

items.statement: Cash profit before tax and depreciation H1 FY27 INR 69.7 crore; dividend paid INR 2.5 crore

items.quote: As far as the dues from the government agencies, what you are referring, we have only this major contract of the UP Jal Jeevan, which is presently in our order book, and the receivables will be around 10% of the total receivables.

items.quote: In case of operational EBITDA, we have been -- we are at 12% operational EBITDA, which was around -- which was 13% last year. So there's a -- at H1 level, it is only 100 basis points of impact, which is all coming from the raw material cost.

items.statement: Inventory and receivables temporarily higher in H1 FY27 due to TREM V change and commodity fluctuation
items.quote: Inventory, we had to do some increase of inventory due to the TREM V change that happened. And also the commodity fluctuation that has been happening, you would see that we have managed EBITDA better comparatively.

items.statement: Receivables and inventory expected to normalize in Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: You will see that coming down in Q3 and Q4, number one.

items.statement: Netherlands warehouse to reduce delivery time from 60-90 days to 2 weeks
items.quote: So this logistics warehouse, which is based out of Netherlands, will ease out this, and we should be able to deliver tractors to the distributors in 2 weeks' time is what we are targeting from their order.

items.statement: Distribution business growing at over 20%
items.quote: Other than these 2 businesses, our distribution business continues to grow at over 20%.

items.statement: Competitor selling at much lower price in Gujarat for last 2-3 months, expected to discontinue
items.quote: In one particular state, which is Gujarat, one competition has been selling at a much lower price for the last 2, 3 months. We expect that to discontinue now.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 6% to INR635 crores vs INR597 crores last year
items.quote: I'm happy to share that there's a revenue growth of 6%. The revenue stood at INR635 crores versus INR597 crores of last year same period.

items.statement: H1 FY27 PAT grew to INR71.5 crores vs INR69.9 crores last year
items.quote: PAT is -- our PAT for the half year is INR71.5 crores versus INR69.9 crores for the H1 last year.

items.statement: Drought in Maharashtra and North Karnataka impacting compact tractor demand
items.quote: Two key important markets of ours are under severe drought, one being Maharashtra and other being Northern Karnataka.

items.statement: Cyclone in Andhra Pradesh may temporarily hamper demand
items.quote: Andhra has different sorts of problem. They've just gone through a cyclone. So that might hamper temporarily.

items.statement: Music vertical revenue CAGR guidance of 20% to 23% over short to medium term
items.quote: On a short-to-medium-term basis, we maintain our guidance of 20% to 23% CAGR for the music vertical revenue.

items.statement: Music vertical EBITDA margin guidance of 60% to 65% over short to medium term
items.quote: We maintain our guidance of 20% to 23% revenue CAGR and 60% to 65% EBITDA margin for music vertical over short to medium run.

items.statement: New content spend guidance of INR300-350 crores for FY27
items.quote: Our spend on new content this year will be between INR300 crores and INR350 crores.

items.statement: Projected new content spend of ~INR1,200 crores over FY28-FY30 at 10% annual growth
items.quote: So, assuming Financial Year 2027 spends at the midpoint of INR325 crores, we are looking at new content spends of around INR1,200 crores over the three financial years from Financial Year 2028 to 2030.

items.statement: Music vertical EBITDA margin improved to 55.4% in H1 FY27 from 48.4% in H1 FY26
items.quote: I see that your music margin has been up 700 bps year-on-year, from 48.4% to 55.4% EBIT margin.

items.statement: Paid subscription growth significantly outpacing ad-based streaming in India
items.quote: It's paid subscription that is growing much, much faster than the ad-based stuff.

items.statement: 60% of FY26 music revenue came from post-2000 releases, indicating shift to new IP
items.quote: In Financial Year 2026, 60% of all music revenue of Saregama came from music which was released post-2000.

items.statement: Artist management represents 340 artists with 450M+ combined followers on Instagram and YouTube
items.quote: At the end of this quarter, we represent 340 artists with a combined follower base of more than 450 million on Instagram and YouTube.

items.statement: Executed 54 Carvaan Live shows serving ~10,000 audience members in Q2 FY27
items.quote: 54 such shows were produced in quarter two, serving around 10,000 audience members.

items.statement: Ilaiyaraaja US tour across 11 cities served 20,000 audience members in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The other big highlight of this quarter was our Ilaiyaraaja's US tour across 11 cities serving 20,000 audience members.

items.statement: Completed over 20 brand deals in Q2 FY27 with partners like Apple, Airbnb, Google, Cadbury, Tanishq
items.quote: This quarter, we did over 20 brand deals with partners like Apple, Airbnb, Google, Cadbury, Tanishq, etcetera.

items.statement: TikTok return to India would be very positive with better payment structures for IP owners
items.quote: Very positive. We believe the market is going to become far bigger than what it is today. That's what we are seeing in every other part of the world. Second, the payment structures of TikTok are better.

items.statement: Short-format platforms (Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) still on fixed-fee deals; seeking revenue-share model
items.quote: The short format apps in the country are still working with all the labels on a fixed fee basis. We want them to move on a share of advertising basis.

items.statement: AI created music winning on volume not listenership; focusing on licensed AI covers/remakes of catalog
items.quote: As of now, data and consumer research seems to be indicating that AI-created music is winning primarily on volume and not on consumer listening.

items.statement: Created two AI-dedicated teams for content creation and process optimization; releasing 100 hours of podcast content in Q3
items.quote: We will be releasing around 100 hours of podcast content in Q3 using these tools.

items.statement: Current liabilities increased by over INR100 crores in H1 FY27 due to customer advances
items.quote: So, this is towards the advances which we have received, and that's where you see a bit of a bump-up in current liabilities.

items.statement: QIP proceeds invested in Pocket Aces, Haryanvi catalog, and Bhansali Productions; interest income declining
items.quote: We were earning a decent amount from the interest income on the QIP money that was sitting with us. All of that has now been invested in Pocket Aces, some of the Haryanvi catalog that we ended up buying, and a positi on in Bhansali

items.statement: Pocket Aces reached break-even in FY26 and moving towards profitability in FY27
items.quote: Pocket Aces has reached break-even in financial year 26 and is moving towards profitability this year.

items.statement: Bhansali Productions gearing up for Love & War release in Q4 FY27 and working on FY28 slate
items.quote: Bhansali Productions is all geared up for its biggest release Love & War in quarter four and is actively working on the slate for financial year 28.

items.statement: Global recorded music market USD31.7B in 2025; India share only 1% despite 18% world population
items.quote: Global recorded music grew to USD31.7 billion in 2025, according to IFPI. India has just a 1% share of that.

items.statement: India internet users over 950M per IAMAI report; Spotify calls India biggest growth opportunity
items.quote: The latest IAMAI report places India at over 950 million internet users.

items.statement: Video vertical revenue declined 16% to INR183M in Q2 FY27 due to film business wind-down; may decline further
items.quote: Revenue of this vertical declined 16% to INR183 million. This follows a conscious decision to wind down the film business and invest in Bhansali Productions instead.

items.statement: Artist management vertical combines Saregama and Pocket Aces talent; cross-featuring in music videos
items.quote: Both Pocket Aces and Saregama have a similar vertical of talent management. Within Saregama, there's a much larger focus on music. At Pocket Aces there is a lot of focus on music, entertainment also. So both get combined here.

items.statement: Carvaan app in test phase; not a hardcore streaming app but community for older users; 4-6 months more testing
items.quote: The Carvaan app for us is still in the test phase. We have put some of our content out; we're experimenting with some of the other things to see if we can build a reasonably strong proposition for middle-aged to older people.

items.statement: Carvaan Club combines hardware, live events, and app for older community engagement; still in testing phase
items.quote: Carvaan Club is another way in which a community of people, older people who bought Carvaan at one time, can be connected. So, Carvaan Club people can go out there and meet each other on the Carvaan app or they can go for a Carvaan live event.

items.statement: Guidance given on 3-5 year basis, not per-year; H1 FY27 37% growth above 20-23% CAGR guidance
items.quote: Our guidance is always given on a 3-to-5-year basis. We don't give guidance on a per-year basis. Things move here and there. So, on a 3-to-5-year basis, we are expecting music vertical to grow at a CAGR of 20% to 23%.

items.statement: Content investments from FY24-26 now yielding revenue higher than cost charge-off, driving margin expansion
items.quote: Some of those content investments that we made in financial year '24, '25 or '26 have now reached a stage whereby the revenue increase on account of them is far higher than the cost charge that we are taking.

items.statement: Live events distribution via BookMyShow and District by Zomato; platforms charge nominal fee, P&L sits with Saregama
items.quote: We will typically do is list our events on both platforms, BookMyShow and District by Zomato. Different kinds of events have different deal structures. The booking platform charges a nominal fee to manage the entire backend, and the profit and loss of the rest of the event sits with us.

items.statement: Not doing Diljit Dosanjh India tour this season as financials not working out; focusing on IP-based events like UN40, HaHaKaar, Carvaan Live
items.quote: The only part I can tell you for sure is that we are not doing Diljit. We have very high respect for Diljit Dosanjh. I think he's the greatest performer this country has ever seen. The financials were not working out.

items.statement: EY-IMI study: 64% of free music users ready to shift to paid service if free stops; digital advertising growing 14%+ annually
items.quote: A recent Indian consumer study done by EY and IMI stated that 64% of free music customers are ready to shift to a reasonably priced paid service if the free service stops.

items.statement: Universal Music agreed to windowing in India (content to paid first, then free); Spotify increasing ad load to drive paid conversion
items.quote: There are moves being made by the world's biggest music label, Universal Music, which has agreed to a windowing concept in India, where some of its content goes first to the paid side and only at a later stage comes to free users.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR1,900-2,000 crores with ~20% EBITDA margin; 200-400 bps margin improvement by end FY27 and further 400-600 bps by end FY28
items.quote: On guidance for FY27, we're targeting about close to INR1,900 to INR2,000 crores with a margin of about 20% EBITDA. As we transition select manufacturing to India, we're also targeting an EBITDA margin improvement of about 200 to 400 basis points by the end of FY27. And a further 400 to 600 basis points by the end of FY28.

items.statement: Order book ~INR10,000+ crores, 90% international, strong long-term visibility
items.quote: Our order book as on date is about 10,000 plus crores. Out of which 90% is international, giving us a very strong long- term visibility.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 operational EBITDA INR82.28 crores at 19.7% margin; UK operations showing ~200% per quarter EBITDA margin improvement from Q3 FY26 to Q2 FY27
items.quote: Operational EBITDA stood at INR82.28 crores compared with INR61 crores in Q1 at a robust margin of 19.7%.

items.statement: Invested ~£8-9 million in Nasmyth and Bromford post-acquisition for working capital, equipment, automation; no further capex needed for next few years as capacity sufficient
items.quote: Between Nasmyth and Bromford, I think we've invested close to about £8 to £9 million. It's a combination of working capital infusion, right, capex into equipment, into new kit, which have significantly improved customer deliveries in terms of our operational metrics.

items.statement: India aerospace utilization ~15%, ammunition ~20%, defense electronics single shift; Sri City Phase 1 targeting 50-60% utilization by end FY28, full by FY29; UK execution stable with 15-20% annual growth, India facility 15% per quarter ramp
items.quote: By end of FY28, I think we'll achieve about 50 to 60% capacity utilization. That's why I said, the capex set, I mean, the facility is good for the next few years of our execution.

items.statement: Planning fundraise up to INR3,000 crores primarily for M&A acquisitions; targeting Q4 FY27 closure; subject to shareholder approval; no working capital need
items.quote: So, the fundraise is primarily to fuel our growth coming in from M&A, new acquisitions. We've been working on multiple opportunities over the last 6 to 8 months. And I think next quarter, Q4 is when we expect to close these transactions.

items.statement: Targeting acquisitions of USD100-150 million revenue companies with EBITDA positive, good customer base; evaluating US, Europe, UK; potential Q4 FY27 closure; not buying distressed assets
items.quote: Yeah. So the size of our acquisitions are somewhere between companies which are doing about USD100 to USD150 million. That's the size that we're talking about. And then these opportunities would be spread across different -by-different customers a nd a different set of capabilities.

items.statement: Term debt ~INR80 crores (INR76 crores term loan + scheduled repayments through CY2027); primarily working capital borrowings; almost debt-free on term basis; will decide repayment strategy for small term loan
items.quote: I think we barely have any leverage on the balance sheet. The current debt is only about INR80-odd crores. And we borrowed from the parent to fund previous acquisitions before the FLR point. And yeah, the rest is all working capital.

items.statement: INR350 crores cash on balance sheet (part from June preferential issue); businesses generating cash; preferential funds parked in fixed deposits; adequate working capital lines
items.quote: So as, as you would see on our balance sheet, we do have about INR 350 crores of cash, which is a portion of that is from the pref placement that we did in June.

items.statement: 90% export revenue (GBP, USD, EUR denominated), 10% domestic; defense exports growing faster; direct Tier 1 supplier to OEMs (Rolls-Royce, GE, Airbus, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, BAE); 25-30% UK revenue from defense programs non-transferable
items.quote: about 90% of our revenue is export-driven between both UK and India. Management: So if you look at our breakdown and the guidance we've given in Q1 also and for the year, our domestic business is around roughly 10% of that

items.statement: UK aerospace OTIF improved from 65% to ~97% over last few quarters due to investments
items.quote: We've taken it up from 65% to about 97% over the last few quarters. And yeah, that's the investment that we've made, and that's clearly reflecting in operational efficiencies.

items.statement: M107 shell margins expanding despite lower Q2 volumes due to insourcing (85% revenue recognized in H1, 15% in Oct); defense export margins moving in right direction
items.quote: About 85% of the revenue is already recognized in Q1 and Q2. And the rest 15% is already completed in October, right? And you'll see it in -- it'll reflect in the Q3 results.

items.statement: Aerospace EBITDA margin targeting 25-30% by FY28 (currently lower due to UK cost base); transfer of work 30% UK / 70% India model; P&L runs through Sigma UK
items.quote: Yeah, it's possible. I think 25% to 30% is what we should look at. Management: So FY28, we'll be in that 25% to 30% EBITDA margin for the rest of this

items.statement: Supportive environment: global aerospace OEMs seeking India engineering depth/scale; NATO allies strengthening ammunition capacity; counter-drone becoming everyday security need; GoI emphasizing indigenous defense manufacturing
items.quote: Global aerospace OEMs are increasingly looking to India for engineering depth and scale beyond cost advantage. NATO and allied nations are strengthening their ammunition manufacturing capacity, which requires dependable supply chain partners.

items.statement: Defense export order book dependent on global conflicts continuing medium term; NATO defense budgets rising; restocking needs driving demand
items.quote: so we see as long as there's conflict happening, as we see throughout the world for the m edium term, and also the restock piling that needs to happen and the defense budgets in NATO going up for what's being announced. We see the medium term that the order books will continue to rise

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth target expected to be surpassed; EBITDA margin outlook maintained at 13%-14%
items.quote: We are now confident of surpassing the revenue growth target, along with the full year's EBITDA margin outlook of 13%-14%.

items.statement: Confident of surpassing 18%-20% topline growth projection and achieving 13%-14% EBITDA margin for FY27
items.quote: we are pretty confident now that we should be able to surpass our 18%-20% topline growth that we had projected earlier, and also achieve the margin of 13%-14%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 27.4% YoY, predominantly volume-driven across sanitaryware, faucetware, tiles, and construction chemicals
items.quote: CERA continued to deliver healthy growth during Q2 FY 27, with revenues growing by 27.4% year -on-year.

items.statement: Volume growth driven by improved market demand and distribution initiatives, not pre-buying from price hikes
items.quote: Essentially, the volume is being driven by increased demand from the market, because pre-buying, like we have taken two price increases during the last two quarters, is something which only impacts a particular period.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 12.2% vs 14.2% YoY and 10.1% QoQ; sequential improvement from pricing actions and cost efficiencies
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 12.2% in Q2 FY27 compared with 14.2% in Q2 FY26 and 10.1% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Faucetware price hike of ~8% effective Sep 1, 2026 to offset brass costs; benefits expected from later part of Q3 FY27
items.quote: a further price increase of approximately 8% in the faucetware segment, effective from September 1st, 2026, to partly offset the impact of higher brass prices.

items.statement: Total faucetware price increases now 24% (16% in May + 8% in Sep); sanitaryware up 12% in May, no further hikes
items.quote: 16% in the month of May, 8% in the month of September, taking it to a total of 24%. In the case of sanitaryware, it is 12%, which we have taken in the month of May.

items.statement: Average gas cost INR 47.29/cu m in Q2 FY27 vs INR 33.79 YoY; brass cost INR 932/kg vs INR 589 YoY (+58%) and INR 837 QoQ (+11%)
items.quote: The average cost of gas during Q2 FY27 stood at INR 47.29 per cubic meter compared with INR 33.79 per cubic meter in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Similarly, the average cost of brass during Q2 FY27 stood at INR 932 per kg compared with INR 589 per kg in Q2 FY26 and INR 837 per kg in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Sanitaryware capacity utilization improved to 82%; faucetware monthly production increased from 4 lakh to 5 lakh units via balancing equipment
items.quote: Our sanitaryware facilities are currently operating at utilization level of 82%. In faucetware, we have been able to increase monthly production from 4 lakh units to 5 lakh units by adding certain balancing equipments of plant and machinery within the same facility.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR 27 crore against full-year plan of ~INR 43 crore; faucetware capacity can scale to 6-7 lakh units if demand warrants
items.quote: Capital expense incurred during the first half stood at INR 27 crore against our planned full year outlay of approximately INR 43 crore.

items.statement: Greenfield sanitaryware project decision by end of Q4 FY27; land already procured
items.quote: By the end of Q4, we will be in a better position to take a decision on the construction of the greenfield project.

items.statement: Revenue mix: sanitaryware 45%, faucetware 43%, tiles 10%, wellness 2%; CERA brand contributes 98%-99% of revenue
items.quote: It is primarily the CERA brand which is kind of contributing , you can say, 98% -99% of the entire amount.

items.statement: Channel mix Q2 FY27: retail 61%, projects 39%; expects stabilization at 60:40 retail-to-project ratio
items.quote: Going forward, we expect this mix to stabilize at around 40: 60.

items.statement: Net working capital improved to 58 days from 77 days YoY; inventory days 69 from 83, receivable days 28 from 33, payables unchanged at 39 days
items.quote: Inventory days decreased from 83 days to 69 days. Receivable days reduced from 33 days to 28 days, while payables remained unchanged at 39 days. Consequently, our net working capital improved from 77 days to 58 days on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents INR 897 crore as of Sep 30, 2026; balance sheet healthy with flexibility for strategic initiatives
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, our cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 897 crore. Our balance sheet remains healthy, providing us with the flexibility to support our ongoing business requirements and other strategic initiatives.

items.statement: Continuously evaluating acquisition opportunities including outsourcing partners; will exercise option if beneficial opportunity arises
items.quote: That is a continuous outlook that we keep on doing even otherwise. Like when we were taking that land also, we evaluated a lot whether in respect of we should be acquiring some outsourcing partners or whether we should be acquiring somebody from the industry as such.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation creates double-edged impact: higher gas costs but some shift from unorganized to organized players
items.quote: The geopolitical situation has created a kind of a double -edged situation. It has added problems as well as presented an opportunity also.

items.statement: No price reductions expected even if commodity costs taper; past losses need recovery; discounts may increase if demand weakens
items.quote: Traditionally, what has happened, and even in the current situation, I do not anticipate that there would be a reduction in prices even if the raw material prices do taper down.

items.statement: Freight cost 11%-12% of sanitaryware revenue, 8%-9% company-wide; gas cost 11%-12% of in-house sanitaryware production cost
items.quote: The freight cost will be in the region of, you can say, 11%-12% for sanitaryware. For the Company as a whole, it comes in the region of 8%-9%.

items.statement: Outsourcing partners' gas cost 30%-35% of their input cost; CERA absorbed 12% procurement cost increase from vendors (9% Apr-May + 3% Sep)
items.quote: I think the input cost for gas for outsourcing partners will be in the range of 30% -35%. So, if the cost is doubling, you find that the impact would be substantial for the outsourcing partners.

items.statement: Old project orders at previous prices largely delivered in last two quarters; remaining in Q3, new projects at new prices from late Q3/Q4
items.quote: Bulk of it has been materialized in the last couple of quarters. There would be some parts of it in still Q3, but going to the later part of Q3 and Q4, we could be all, we can say, more or less with new project orders, with new prices.

items.statement: Aggressively evaluating automation and AI tools for cost efficiency; expect visible benefits in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We are actively working on increasing cost efficiency using automation and AI tools. We are aggressively evaluating various costs in the system, exploring greater automation of processes, and identifying interventions that can yield savings.

items.statement: Market share gains likely over last 3-4 quarters but difficult to quantify due to unlisted peers and product diversity
items.quote: Would I say that we have gained market share; - I would definitely think that over the last three, four quarters, the way that our numbers have grown, market share would have gone up.

items.statement: Limited exports; container cost increases not materially impactful
items.quote: We are saved by the fact that we do not have too many imports, because over the years, the cost of containers has kind of increased exponentially. But because we have only limited exports, it did not impact us too much.

items.statement: FY28 revenue growth guidance deferred; will assess after FY27 close and March-end external environment
items.quote: We will continue to say that it is too early right now, because we want to wait FY27 to close and then see how the entire year went in respect of demand.

items.statement: No further price hikes planned for Q3 FY27; sanitaryware comfortable, faucetware September hike not fully reflected yet
items.quote: As of now, we are not looking at any further price increases. We had taken one for faucetware in the month of September. In sanitaryware, as of now, we are comfortable.

items.statement: Favorable APM-linked gas sourcing arrangement cushions energy cost impact vs peers
items.quote: Our favorable gas sourcing arrangement has helped us to cushion the impact of higher energy costs, positioning us favorably relative to several other industry participants.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing: sanitaryware 41%, faucetware 55%; outsourcing for simpler SKUs, in-house for higher value-added products
items.quote: In the current quarter, the sanitaryware manufacturing was 41%, and outsourcing was 59%. For faucetware, the numbers stood at 55% for in-house manufacturing, and outsourcing was at 45%.

items.statement: Core business capex to continue as per guidance; new growth bets (data centers, cloud) will see increased investment for future growth
items.quote: the core business will continue as per guidance. As you can appreciate , if there is a built -out strategy from 200-250 megawatt to a gigawatt, we are dialing up our cloud capabilities. So, in some of these new growth bets, we will invest for growth for the future.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 60,900 crores (+4% QoQ); Africa constant currency revenue growth 6.7% QoQ; India ex-passive infra revenue growth 3.2% QoQ; Consolidated EBITDAaL Rs 31,500 crores (+5.5% QoQ)
items.quote: Consolidated revenue came in at about Rs.60,900 Crores, growing 4% sequentially. Africa delivered yet another solid performance with constant currency revenue growth of 6.7% sequentially. India, excluding passive infra, recorded a strong growth of 3.2%. Consolidated EBITDAaL came in at about Rs 31,500 crores, growing at about 5.5%.

items.statement: Airtel Money Africa listed on London Stock Exchange in October at ~$7B valuation; one of London's largest IPOs; Airtel Africa and Airtel Money now both listed in London
items.quote: In October, Airtel Money Africa got listed on the London Stock Exchange at a valuation of about $7 billion and reported as one of London's largest IPOs. With this, two of our subsidiaries, Airtel Africa and Airtel Money, are now listed in London.

items.statement: Industry pricing architecture flat with unlimited data at low ARPUs; architecture correction requires industry-wide move to charge for data; postpaid differentiation strengthening via Fast Lane, international roaming, exclusive experiences
items.quote: when we speak about pricing architecture in the industry, it is largely got to do with the fact that it is a very flat architecture and at very low ARPUs, you are giving away unlimited usage and data, and you are not monetizing consumption in any way. The data is, in that sense is not charged and, therefore, that change of architecture will require, like, I think the industry to move more decisive

items.statement: No fund raise announced; Airtel Money Africa IPO completed in London at $7B valuation
items.quote: In October, Airtel Money Africa got listed on the London Stock Exchange at a valuation of about $7 billion and reported as one of London's largest IPOs.

items.statement: Large dividend payouts in Q2 from Indus, Airtel, and Airtel Africa impacted gross debt reduction
items.quote: If the dividend payouts were not there, as you would appreciate in Q2, Indus, Airtel and Airtel Africa, all had very large dividend payouts, of course.

items.statement: AI tools used for mass interview screening, recruitment, video KYC; no management changes or attrition data disclosed
items.quote: AI-led processes are changing across areas like quarterly financial book closure, recruitment, mass interview screening of candidates, and our video KYCs for our customer acquisition.

items.statement: Gross debt directionally coming down opportunistically across countries, subject to operations and dividend payouts
items.quote: If the dividend payouts were not there, as you would appreciate in Q2, Indus, Airtel and Airtel Africa, all had very large dividend payouts, of course. So, gross debt, you will see directionally coming down, opportunistically, basis the country and the operations.

items.statement: Current tax run rates can be taken as going-forward run rates for tax provisions and payments
items.quote: On taxes, yes, you could take the current run rates as the going-forward run rates for tax provisions and payments.

items.statement: Core business capex shows convergence between CWIP and actual capitalization; data center projects cause temporary mismatches
items.quote: If you look at the trend of capex on the BAU part, you will see a complete convergence between CWIP and capex spend and actual capitalization.

items.statement: Data center capacity is entirely in-house; no external capacity leased for resale
items.quote: How much is external capacity - Nothing is external capacity. We build data center for a living; it is our business. We have not leased capacity to sell it to somebody else.

items.statement: $800 million equity raise completed in June-July; future data center funding will mix debt and equity based on treasury decisions
items.quote: we have just done about $800 million in equity raise, which came in June, July. So, we, as of now, have cash in the bank. Will there be a mix of debt? Certainly, yes.

items.statement: GPU chips already purchased for internal workloads; evaluating GPU-as-a-Service and AI stack but no decision yet
items.quote: Will Airtel go to buy GPU chips from NVIDIA or TPU chips? I think, we already have them. Shashwat, in his opening remarks, mentioned about the workloads that are running for internal use, so we have that.

items.statement: No intention to acquire BT and OneWeb stakes from promoter entities
items.quote: No, there is no intention to buy out these stakes from Airtel.

items.statement: Churn in Q2 driven by seasonality and pricing intervention; competitive intensity unchanged with three operators in half the country and two in the other half
items.quote: There is some seasonality of Q2, which comes in, as well as the pricing intervention that we took, where there is always a temporary impact on customer continuity and we will keep playing this out in terms of ARPU versus base growth.

items.statement: No constraint on tariff headroom; will continue building industry-leading ARPUs when needed
items.quote: I do not see a constraint in terms of the headroom or tariff growth, etc., that we have. If ever and when this happens, we feel strongly about the fact that we should really need this increase in ARPU, we will continue to, just, keep building industry-leading ARPUs in this business.

items.statement: Home broadband EBIT softer due to investment phase in fiber and CPE; correcting low-ARPU acquisition quality issues from prior quarters
items.quote: A lot of investment has gone into fiber as well as CPE which are the two big capex and play that comes in. So, as a result of which, EBIT has looked a little bit softer.

items.statement: Radio capex moderated with less than 1,000 new towers this quarter; incremental capex directed to data centers and cloud growth bets
items.quote: if you look at the new towers being installed, it is almost very little now it is less than 1000, in the ballpark of five, six hundred sites this year, this quarter.

items.statement: Continued buyback in Airtel Africa and Indus; dividend payouts will keep increasing over time
items.quote: We have already announced a potential, continued buyback in Airtel Africa. We have also done that in Indus, so that will continue and we have also said in the past, and you see that reflected in our conduct that the dividend payouts will keep increasing over time.

items.statement: Dyes and dye intermediates demand expected stable in H2 FY27 supported by textile sector activity
items.quote: Looking ahead, demand for dyes and dyes intermediates is expected to remain stable throughout the second half of FY '27. Supported by continued activities in the textile sectors.

items.statement: Standalone material margin improved to 29.1% in Q2 FY27 from 26.4% YoY; EBITDA margin 2.4% vs loss last year; higher fuel, power, effluent costs weigh on operating profitability
items.quote: On a standalone basis revenue from operations for Quarter 2 FY'27 stood at INR 288 crores, registering a growth of 48% year -on-year. Material margin improved to 29.1% from 26.4% in the corresponding quarter last year. Standalone EBITDA stood at about INR 7 crores with an EBITDA margin of 2.4% compared to the loss of INR. 14 crores in the corresponding quarter last year. Higher operating expenses,

items.statement: Target consolidated EBITDA margin 8-10% at peak dye revenue of INR 1,300-1,500 crore; current margin 3-4%
items.quote: Well, right now if you look at the last quarter it was hardly 3% to 4% but I would say going forward we will be able to have at least 8% to 10%. The target is to have that.

items.statement: Running dye order book of 2-3 months; 95% intermediates consumed captively; Dystar remains major customer via Lonsen Kiri JV
items.quote: We have a running order book of at least two to three months of d yes. And those products which are being sold to d yes players, they are one of the global prominent players including D ystar. Even though Kiri exited from Dystar, Dystar continues to be a major customer. And for Dystar, Lonsen Kiri continues to be the single largest supplier globally.

items.statement: India H-Acid capacity ~60,000 tons/year vs consumption 30,000-40,000 tons/year; over-capacitized
items.quote: As far as India's capacities are concerned, we are already over - capacitized as on today. So, the consumption in India is somewhere around 3000 tons a month, around 30,000 tons to 40,000 tons a year and our production capacities are close to 60 ,000 tons a year.

items.statement: Acquired 40% stake in Makilala Mining Company Inc, Philippines; incorporated Andamina SPA in Chile for mineral resource opportunities
items.quote: During the quarter, we also completed the acquisition of 40% stakes in Makilala Mining Company Inc, in the Philippines and incorporated Andamina SPA in Chile to pursue mineral resource opportunities.

items.statement: China H-Acid disruption from new continuous nitration regulation replacing batch process; compliance timeline uncertain; Indian plants already zero-discharge
items.quote: One, the Chinese production has drastically reduced, and that has happened because of the implementation of the new regulation which requires the nitration to be conducted as a continuous nitration rather than a batch nitration. And that has caused reduction in production in China.

items.statement: Copper project hedging model: 100% hedged on purchase and sale side; spread constant regardless of LME price; hedging desk to be established
items.quote: It is completely hedged . It is 100% hedge business on the purchase and sale side so that you do not either make anything on the higher fluctuation , on the higher side or you do not lose anything on the lower fluctuation, on the lower side but your spread continues to remain constant and consistent.

items.statement: Celsius arbitration awards positive for Makilala development but Celsius appealing; Kiri committed to project and will represent in appeal
items.quote: there has been litigation involved as well. Now the court awards, the arbitration awards, till now are very positive for the development of the mine and for our investment as an overseas investment into Philippines. Celsius has, what we expect, has gone to appeal. And we will continue to deliberate and continue to address the appeals court in Philippines whenever the hearing takes place

items.statement: Lonsen Kiri JV (40% stake) contributed INR 16 crore share of profit in Q2 FY27 and INR 37 crore in H1 FY27
items.value: INR 16 crore Q2; INR 37 crore H1
items.quote: The company's share of profit from associates, p rimarily contributed by Lonsen Kiri Chemical Industries Limited, in which the company holds 40% equity stake, stood at INR 16 crores during Quarter 2 FY'27 and approximately INR 37 crores during H1 FY'27.

items.statement: Standalone FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-17%; manufacturing EBIT margin 12-13%, projects EBIT margin around 6% by year-end
items.quote: Looking ahead on a standalone basis, we expect FY 2027 revenue to grow by about 15% to 17%. Margins in the manufacturing business should stay in the range of 12% to 13%, and in the projects business should improve to around 6% by the end of the year.

items.statement: Standalone orders in hand at all-time high of INR 8,757 crores as of Sep 30, 2026; consolidated orders in hand at record INR 10,273 crores
items.quote: Order booking for the six months is excellent at INR 4,844 crores, and standalone orders in hand as on September 30, 2026 are at an all-time high of INR 8,757 crores.

items.statement: Isgec Hitachi Zosen order book at INR 1,161 crores including INR 800 crores export orders; booked INR 678 crores orders in H1 FY27
items.quote: Order book is very good at INR 1,161 crores. Just as Mr. Puri mentioned it in his opening remarks, they have booked large orders, and certainly they seem to be booking a lot of export orders. So out of these INR 1,161 crores of order book, about INR 800 crores are export orders.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBIT margin 13.7% in Q2 FY27, above guided 12-13% range; projects EBIT margin 5.7%, close to 6% target
items.quote: On the margin front, manufacturing EBIT margin for the quarter is 13.7%, better than the 12% to 13% range we guided. EBIT margin for the project business is 5.7%, better than the last few years and close to our target of 6%.

items.statement: Investing INR 502 crores to expand manufacturing capacity across product lines; INR 199 crores spent so far funded from internal accruals; new facilities at Bhartoli, Dahej SEZ, casting factories, tube and piping shops, standard mechanical
items.quote: As you know, the company is investing about INR 502 crores to expand capacity for our manufacturing segment. This net borrowing of INR 206 crores is after cumulative capital expenditure of INR 199 crores for this capital investment, which has been funded from internal accruals.

items.statement: Capacity expansion largely on schedule; some new production facilities to be progressively completed this year; expected to contribute to FY27 manufacturing growth; expansion to yield INR 1,200 crores additional revenue by FY29
items.quote: All these are running largely on schedule, and some of the new production facilities will be progressively completed this year. We are expecting the additional production to contribute to this year's manufacturing segment growth.

items.statement: Domestic market strong across all product lines; healthy export inquiries from Latin America and Africa; robust demand in almost all product and project lines both domestic and export
items.quote: The domestic market is strong across all our product lines, and we also have a healthy level of export inquiries from customers in Latin America and Africa.

items.statement: Export revenue INR 172 crores (11% of total income) in Q2 FY27 vs INR 90 crores YoY; H1 FY27 exports INR 557 crores (18% of total income) vs INR 425 crores YoY; weaker rupee supporting export competitiveness
items.quote: Export revenue during the quarter is INR 172 crores, about 11% of total income, compared to INR 90 crores in the same quarter last year. Export revenue during the first half of the year is INR 557 crores, about 18% of total income, up from INR 425 crores in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Standalone net borrowings fell to INR 206 crores from INR 381 crores (Mar 31, 2026); consolidated net borrowings reduced by INR 320 crores to INR 156 crores from INR 476 crores
items.quote: The company's standalone fund position improved by INR 175 crores during the six months, and net borrowings fell to INR 206 crores compared to INR 381 crores as on March 31, 2026.

items.statement: Commodity prices (steel, copper, aluminium, nickel) fluctuated up to 10% in Q2; shipping/logistics delays and sharply higher freight rates; most increased costs expected to be absorbed through contingency provisions
items.quote: During the quarter, commodity prices, particularly steel, copper, aluminium, and nickel, skewed up to 10% fluctuation, though they have come down slightly in October.

items.statement: Products division 38% of consolidated order book (up from historical 25-28%); orders from automobile, oil & gas, petrochemicals, cement, steel
items.quote: 38% is consolidated. What you are seeing at 38% is consolidated. Digant Haria: Okay. Kishore Chatnani: So that includes Isgec Heavy Engineering as well as Isgec Hitachi Zosen

items.statement: Isgec Hitachi Zosen FY27 turnover expected 7-8% higher YoY, profit 5-7% higher YoY; order book INR 1,161 crores with INR 800 crores export orders
items.quote: So we are expecting their turnover to be higher by about 7-8% compared to last year, and profit to be also higher, maybe about 5-7% compared to last year.

items.statement: Philippines ethanol plant (CBPI) loss INR 164 crores in H1 FY27 including interest, depreciation, forex loss; plant at 65-70% capacity; INR 41 crores forex loss in Q2; depreciation now INR 8-9 crores/quarter; expects 90% utilization in Q4 F
items.quote: During the six months, the segment incurred a loss of INR 164 crores including interest. Most of this loss relates to interest, depreciation, and forex loss.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions not affecting order booking/execution but raising material costs; shipping/logistics delays and higher freight rates; commodity price volatility up to 10%
items.quote: Current geopolitical developments have not affected order booking or order execution. However, the cost of some materials has risen because of the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, and this is having a small adverse effect on profitability.

items.statement: Strategy to take shorter-cycle, technology-oriented projects; avoiding long-duration civil-heavy projects; reduces uncertainty, improves cash flows, lowers customer liquidity risk
items.quote: We are not going to take very long duration projects. We are not going to take projects where it will form a very significant or a major part of the total order value. And we are trying and are being successful in taking projects which have some technology element linked to it.

items.statement: Most product orders fixed-price; manage material cost risk via back-to-back supplier offers, rate contracts, contingencies; material cost 50-60% of manufactured products
items.quote: We have back-to-back offers for raw material, we have rate contracts for certain items. So when we actually bid for an order, we usually know what each item is going to be costing us, and we still keep some contingencies.

items.statement: Government banned ethanol manufacture from B-heavy molasses and syrup; Saraswati Sugar Mills getting lower sales quotas due to lower cane availability last year
items.quote: Yes, because the government has banned manufacture of ethanol from B-heavy and from syrup.

items.statement: H1 FY27 order intake grew 25% YoY to INR 2,180 crore; Q2 order intake was INR 1,265 crore, up over 50% YoY
items.quote: If you look at the solid growth in terms of 25%, because you must have seen Q1, we were trailing in the orders, and in Q2, we were able to pick up the order, which is like -to-like comparison is more than 50% plus. So, we have closed the orders in this quarter is INR 1,265, and the next one become INR 2,180, which is actually the good growth.

items.statement: Sustained demand seen across energy transition, AI/data centers, urbanization, and Make in India; per capita electricity consumption expected to reach 2 MWh by 2030
items.quote: Overall, we have been seeing that this actually has been. The panorama in front of us has been good. Few macro snapshots, if you look at the slide at the top left, are primarily which are very supportive, is the GDP, which, I'm sure you are aware, we were at 7.8 the quarter which went by.

items.statement: Q2 EBIT margin improved sequentially to 7.2% from 4% in Q1; H1 EBIT margin 6.2%; material cost pressure from copper, transformer oil, steel continues
items.quote: EBIT, again, I will say from sequential quarter, we have been able to improve. You must have seen the Q1, due to the negative operating leverage, there was a profit, was there only close to 4% of the Q1. In Q2, able to do with 7.2%, and overall H1 is 6.2%.

items.statement: Copper, aluminum, steel up double digits; transformer oil also up; only 20-25% of project backlog protected by price variation clauses; standard product price hikes take time to pass through
items.quote: where the rupee stands d evaluated, copper, aluminum, steel have all gone double digit up, and also the repo rate has also sort of become slightly non-conducive.

items.statement: Kolkata MVC capacity expanded from 1.85 lakh to 2.5 lakh and now to 3.75 lakh units/year; Phase II board approved last week; partial capitalization started
items.quote: In KMVC capacity expansion, which we got approved last week from the Board, we started partially the capitalizations.

items.statement: Kolkata MVC interrupter capacity being ramped to 3.75 lakh units/year; shift from Salt Lake facility to new facility in coming quarters; space available for further expansion
items.quote: We started, if you remember, in Q3 of '23, we initiated this program of infusing capex and making interrupters. We already used to have, we used to make 85,000 pieces. We started working on a program which was to take the capacity to close to 180,000, 185,000.

items.statement: Emerging segments (data centers, semiconductors, renewables) contributing well to order backlog; supplied full powertrain for semiconductor fab, skid-mounted substation for data center, inverter duty transformers for renewables
items.quote: In this, in solid growth, in effect, the contribution is coming, as Udai highlighted, is emerging segment, with the good contributions in this order backlog.

items.statement: Wins across metals, glass, automotive, defense, EV batteries; supplied AIS panels, E-houses, compact stations, automation for Mumbai Metro, breakers for water infra in MP
