items.quote: We have been seeing and doing and reaching out to people in metal space, in the material, which is nothing but people who are making glass, in automotives, in defense, and also in the batteries.

items.statement: Exports currently 12-13% of revenue; Kolkata capacity built with export orientation; export margins governed by arm's length pricing, domestic by competitive L1 bidding
items.quote: as of now, the mix is close to what you mentioned, the 12%, 13%. And we expect that the mix is not going to be significantly different, because both market is growing.

items.statement: Order backlog aging: 20-25% beyond 12 months, 5-6 months for ETO/designer-specific, 5-12 months for others; large orders phase out in 6-12 months
items.quote: The large orders phase out in 6-12 months, and some of the orders which has a large order is more than 12 months. That's the aging. Any ETO or any designer-specific customer, its average time is five - six months.

items.statement: No incremental borrowing; finance cost increased due to RBI rate change from 6.1% to 6.7%
items.quote: Finance cost, again, this is just to confirm you, no incremental borrowing. The finance cost is increased just because the change in the rate what we are paying based on the RBI rate and the declare.

items.statement: Medium voltage breaker market size estimated at 55,000-60,000 units annually (11/24/36 kV); data center capacity 1.6 GW operational, 2.5-3 GW financially closed, targeting 8 GW by 2030
items.quote: Now, the size of the market is in terms of volume, I would say about close to, and I am telling you about medium voltage breakers, which are used in AIS panels, maybe anywhere, say about 55,000-60,000 breakers, is what the size of the market is in 11, 24, and 36 KV plus.

items.statement: RDSS scheme extended 2 years; INR 18,000 crore outlay for current year out of original INR 3.03 lakh crore; DPDP Act and MeitY guidelines mandating data localization driving data center demand
items.quote: The outlay which is under this scheme, if I'm not wrong, is about Public INR18,000 crore s for the current year, out of INR 303,000s crore, which was originally the scheme was conceived

items.statement: Gender diversity improved to close to 20%; trained ~1,900 youth across 16 skill centers in Gujarat over 2 years; ~320,000 people benefited through community health programs
items.quote: The gender diversity is something which we have been focusing, because it is important, because it is critical for organizational development, and we have moved the needle to close to 20%.

items.statement: Commodity volatility (copper, transformer oil) remains high; rupee depreciation; repo rate non-conducive; becoming choosy on orders with larger risk exposure due to limited price variation clauses
items.quote: We are conscious of this fact that RM I is going to be slightly volatile in days to come. Better than what it was, but still it will be an important element and factor to be considered. We are becoming a bit choosy and perhaps not taking an exposure where we see larger risk.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Demand trends remained broadly in line with previous quarters; Y-o-Y performance influenced by festive calendar shift and subdued wedding season
items.quote: Looking back at the quarter, demand trends remained broadly in line with the previous quarters. However, the Y-o-Y performance was influenced by the shift in festive calendar, including Pujo into Q3 this year, along with a subdued wedding season.

items.statement: Full-year cash flow guidance: end FY27 with INR400-500 crores standalone cash balance
items.quote: As we had mentioned, our full year cash flow guidance which we had given, which was about ending this year with about INR400 crores to INR500 crores.

items.statement: Standalone cash balance currently around INR350 crores; expect to improve marginally in H2 to achieve INR400-500 crores by year-end
items.quote: We are at this point of time at a standalone level, and I'm talking of standalone, Ashish, at this point of time. We are roughly around INR350-odd crores cash balance at standalone level. We expect to improve that marginally in the second half to achieve a similar number by the end of the year.

items.statement: Plan to raise capital in TMRW of $100-150 million in next 12 months for funding TMRW growth
items.quote: TMRW being the first prime example, which we expect to raise capital there, as I said, in next 12 months. The extent of fundraise is still being evaluated, but it could be between $100 million to $150 million.

items.statement: TMRW capital raise of close to INR1,000 crores expected to ease cash flow pressures
items.quote: We believe as we speak now, I think our largest need would be in TMRW, which is a substantial part of our cash flow, sort of where cash has been going in last Aditya Birla Fashion and couple of years. We will need to raise capital there close to INR1,000 crores or probably little more, little less

items.statement: Full-year capex guidance of INR600 crores for FY27; INR200 crores spent in H1
items.quote: In Q4, we guided that I will make investment of roughly INR600 crores in FY27, and then I will end up with around INR500 crores cash. In H1, if you see, we have consumed around INR700 crores.

items.statement: Full-year capex projected at INR300 crores; INR200 crores spent in H1
items.quote: No, no. INR300 was the number for the full year. There was a question regarding full year cash flow. So INR300 is projected for full year, INR200 is what we have spent so far.

items.statement: Pantaloons: 16-17 store closures in H1; full-year net additions marginal at ~20 stores; FY28 onwards plan to add 30-40 new stores annually
items.quote: This year, on a full-year basis, we may not see a significant change because as you can make out in the first half itself, we have shut down close to 16, 17 stores. On a full-year basis, maybe close to 20 stores. We are opening similar number of stores, about 20, 22.

items.statement: Pantaloons post-Ind AS EBITDA margins consistently near 18%; aspiration to exceed 20% over next couple of years
items.quote: We had indicated, we have been delivering close to 18% post-Ind AS EBITDA margins for Pantaloons pretty consistently. Despite some of the material cost increases, I think store throughput productivity improvements have created opportunity for us to stay at this level or do slightly better than that in the short term. As we go forward over the next couple of years, our aspiration is to get past 20%

items.statement: Cost inflation of 4-5% impacting Pantaloons; ~100 bps gross margin impact when fully played out; partially passed on
items.value: 4-5% cost inflation, 100 bps gross margin impact
items.quote: Overall, if I were to look at, it's been about 4%-5% kind of cost inflation that the businesses experience. A part of it we have been able to pass on, but not fully in case of Pantaloons. Therefore, there is about 100 basis point gross margin impact that we will experience in the full-blown scenario, which is when the entire cost inflation is played out.

items.statement: Cost inflation spread across quarters; some impact visible in Q2, continuing through Q3-Q4
items.quote: Some of it is already there. As I said, these products are not bought one shot at one point of time. Kunal Bhatia: Right. Ashish Dikshit: They're spread across a period of time. Some of it is already visible in our Q2, and will continue to flow through Q3 and Q4

items.statement: Pantaloons merchandise evolving towards women's western and fusion wear reflecting consumer preferences
items.quote: Today, clearly, the shift is largely on women's western and more on the fusion wear, and that's where you will see Pantaloons' merchandise also evolving towards.

items.statement: Pantaloons festive LFL growth: double-digit in Onam and Pujo; mid to high single-digit across rest of country
items.quote: Both Onam and Pujo have seen one of the highest same-store growth. We are close to double digit in Pujo and even higher in Onam on a smaller basis. Subsequently, for rest of the country, to some extent, some parts of the country which affected by rain have pulled down a part of it, but it is between mid to high single digit across formats.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio (ex-TCNS) grew 12% Y-o-Y; Luxury grew 11%; TMRW grew 10%; OWND grew 58% Y-o-Y
items.quote: Our ethnic portfolio, excluding TCNS, grew by 12%. Luxury delivered 11% growth, and TMRW grew by 10%. OWND continues its strong growth trajectory, recording 58% year-on-year growth, supported by the contribution from newer stores.

items.statement: TCNS facing near-term challenges; rationalized ~60 underperforming stores in past 12 months; H1 revenue negative overall, LFL low single-digit
items.quote: Over the past 12 months, we have rationalized our network by closing approximately 60 underperforming stores, which has impacted revenue growth. However, these changes are important to build a healthier business, with our focus now on restoring growth momentum, improving store productivity, and driving sustainable profitability.

items.statement: Consolidated gross cash INR1,143 crores; standalone INR628 crores; H2 historically stronger for revenue, profitability and cash generation
items.quote: We closed Q2 with gross cash of INR 1,143 crores at the consolidated level and INR 628 crores at the standalone level, providing sufficient liquidity to support our business requirement. Historically, H2 has been stronger for us in terms of both revenue and profitability, and we expect this trend, along with the release of working capital following the festive inventory buildup, to support cash ge

items.statement: Consolidated: subsidiaries can raise own debt; TMRW raise $100-150M; designer ethnic entities can raise own debt
items.quote: At consol level, I think then you will have to add back the potential fundraises. TMRW being the first prime example, which we expect to raise capital there, as I said, in next 12 months. The extent of fundraise is still being evaluated, but it could be between $100 million to $150 million. Each of the subsidiaries have ability to either raise debt on the balance sheet based on their strength, or

items.statement: Confident of stronger H2 driven by festive and wedding demand; historically better period for revenue, profitability, cash generation
items.quote: With festive and wedding-led demand expected to support business momentum, we remain confident of delivering a stronger H2, which has historically been a better period for us in terms of revenue, profitability, and cash generation.

items.statement: Suraj Bahirwani recently took charge as CEO Pantaloons; early festive results showing strong green shoots
items.quote: He's recently taken charge of the business, and some of the early results that we have got in the early festive period. Maybe Suraj, if you can speak through Onam, Pujo, what you've seen through Diwali.

items.statement: TCNS turnaround not yet visible; business remains under pressure from internal and market headwinds in ethnic wear
items.quote: But at this point of time, in H1, at an overall level, we've been negative, overall picture, as well as last year was also marginally low. So this is a business where we haven't got to a stage where we can start growing the portfolio. It continues to remain under pressure, and some of it is internal and some of it is market-related with the headwinds that ethnic wear business is experiencing.

items.statement: Portfolio review ongoing; managing capital allocation across businesses; will reassess strategy at end of FY28
items.quote: We will manage with that, and that will be our endeavor for next FY28, at the end of which we will look at where we stand, and we will take a fresh look at the strategy.

items.statement: Management expects second half FY27 to be much better than first half; Consumer & Industrial revenue to comfortably cross Rs 1,000 crore for full year
items.quote: We are hopeful that the second half should be much better than the first half. So in terms of if you look at Consumer and Industrial, we had.. normally we don't give guidance, but we still gave a guidance of 1,000 crores, and I think we would comfortably cross that because we are already at 615—so well north of 1,000 crores we would end up.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 11.74% vs 12.26% in Q1; management expects margins to stabilize around 12% by end of Q3 and target 12-12.5% for full year
items.quote: Q2 EBITDA margin stood at 11.74% compared to 12.26% in the first quarter. Input cost volatility and changing revenue mix continue to affect profitability.

items.statement: Order book at Rs 2,700 crore as of 2nd November 2026, with Metering & Systems accounting for over 96%
items.quote: Our order book stood at 2,700 crores as on 2nd November '26, with Metering and Systems accounting for more than 96% of the total order book.

items.statement: Wire & cables revenue grew 159% YoY to Rs 178 crore in Q2; H1 revenue of Rs 324 crore equals ~95% of full FY26 wire & cable revenue
items.quote: Wire and cables continued to lead this growth with quarterly revenue increasing 159% to 178 crores. First half revenue reached 324 crores, equivalent to approximately 95% of the revenue achieved in the whole of FY26.

items.statement: Consumer & Industrial revenue grew 64% YoY to Rs 337 crore in Q2 (55% of quarterly revenue); H1 revenue up 60% to Rs 615 crore
items.quote: Consumer and Industrial delivered another record quarter with revenue growing 64% year-on-year to 337 crores. It contributed approximately 55% of the quarterly revenue. First half revenue grew 60% to 615

items.statement: Metering & Systems revenue grew 18% YoY to Rs 271 crore in Q2 with 14% sequential improvement; H1 revenue up 17% to Rs 509 crore
items.quote: Metering and Systems maintained steady growth. Quarterly revenue grew 18% year-on-year to 271 crores with a 14% sequential improvement. First half revenue grew 17% to 509 crores.

items.statement: Wire & cable capacity expansion under evaluation for next 3 years including new products; metering capacity sufficient for government's 2028 smart meter deadline
items.quote: so, this is one part where we….this is one part where we see a good growth coming in, and now the next plan is for evaluating our capacity, including certain new products for the next 3 years. So I think that would entail certain capex, but which is currently under evaluation

items.statement: Fans business at low base but first pan-India summer season in 2027 expected to deliver meaningful volumes; modular switches (Cairo range) launched as growth driver
items.quote: when we are approaching the summer of let’s say '27, that would be the first summer season where we would be addressing on a pan-India basis. And definitely I think that is the time when the sales number would become much more meaningful. We

items.statement: Approved/preferred vendor with all major AMISPs including Adani/IntelliSmart and EESL; Adani acquisition of IntelliSmart seen as positive for order flow
items.quote: We are a preferred approved vendor with Adani and also we've been approved with EESL and we've been supplying to them. So I think that coming together, with major quantities now coming to the leading AMISP, I think that definitely helps us a lot.

items.statement: Management believes aggressive low pricing by new entrants in smart metering is unsustainable; expects industry consolidation toward established players with technology and warranty backing
items.quote: Anybody who tried to disrupt based on pricing has not grown or not survived. It's not easy. The meter has to work for 10 years, the technology has to be there, there needs to be a support, it's backed up by warranties.

items.statement: C&I price increases partially passed in Q2, more lined up post-Diwali; expect full pass-through by end of Q3. Metering fixed contracts prevent pass-through; relying on R&D and design changes to offset cost inflation
items.quote: In Consumer and Industrial, we have to some extent already passed on certain increases which have happened in the second quarter. There are some more increases which are lined up post-Diwali. So in all, I would say by the time we are coming to the close of Q3, the increased cost to a large extent would have been passed on to the consumer.

items.statement: Focus on improving balance sheet ratios including stock and debtors as key priority for second half
items.quote: What we are going to really work on is to ensure that the margins are in place, and certain, you know the, certain balance sheet ratios of, you know the—stock, debtors, and all—are much better placed as we go forward.

items.statement: Board gave in-principle approval to evaluate restructuring including potential demerger of businesses into separate entities via scheme of arrangement to unlock shareholder value
items.quote: Before I conclude, I would also like to address the Board's in-principle approval for a proposal of restructuring the company. This includes evaluating the segregation of one or more of these businesses into separate entities through a scheme of arrangement, with the objective of increasing focus across our product verticals and unlocking shareholder value.

items.statement: Smart meter installations at ~7 crore by end-September vs 22.5 crore target; 17 crore meters allocated to AMISPs; management expects 15-20% growth to continue for 3-5-10 years
items.quote: as per the government data, I think by end of September or something, almost 7 crore meters were installed, and I think that figure should have right now gone up because every month we are seeing more and more installations happening. Out of the 22.5 crore meters, I think 17 crores were given

items.statement: Metering business sustainable at 15%+ margins at current volumes; recent margin pressure attributed to one-off geopolitical material inflation
items.quote: What is interesting is that even at the current level of business what we are doing, the margins, I would say decent margins of let's say 15% plus are sustainable.

items.statement: Focus on converting scale into stronger earnings and cash generation through better margin quality, disciplined execution, and tighter working capital management in H2
items.quote: As we move through the second half, our focus is on converting the scale into stronger earnings and cash generation through better margin quality, disciplined execution, and tighter working capital management.

items.statement: Sales force expansion with geo-tagged 'long-arm salesmen' doing daily beat plans of 20-30 counters; team being enhanced significantly to support C&I doubling target
items.quote: We have special teams which are—what we call like a long-arm salesman—who are doing the daily beat plan, on you know, having the team on the street visiting 20–30 counters per day. So a lot of…that part of the team is also getting enhanced in a bigger way.

items.statement: Smart water meter pilots underway with customers; testing and approval process ongoing; meaningful revenue expected next year
items.quote: we have done a couple of pilots, with a lot of our customers. We are.. our teams are approaching for, you know, testing and approval of the products. So I think, that process is there; it's a time-taking process, but typically that work is happening. So hopefully next year we should start seeing some meaningful numbers coming

items.statement: Analytics and software solutions already deployed in Odisha and West Bengal; more updates to come on data analytics offerings for smart metering
items.quote: Actually we've done it, we have some solutions which we have done it I think in Odisha and one or two places which, or probably in West Bengal, but I think you should hear from us definitely.

items.statement: Consolidated capex expected around ₹1,250 crores in FY27; India capex around ₹1,100 crores
items.quote: We expect capital expenditure in FY 27 to be around ₹ 1,100 crores. Our consolidated capex is expected to be ₹ 1,250 crores.

items.statement: India capex in FY26 was approximately ₹800 crores vs ₹611 crores in FY25
items.quote: Our India capex in FY26 was approximately ₹ 800 crores, compared to ₹ 611 crores in the previous year of FY25, driven by investments in new growth areas.

items.statement: Standalone RMC increased to 70% of sales in Q2 FY27 from 66% in Q2 FY26; EBITDA margin declined 2% to 10.5%
items.quote: In Q2 FY26, standalone RMC was 66% to sales, and in Q2 FY 27, it is 70% to sales. In spite of a 4% increase in RMC% in Q2, our India standalone EBITDA percentage declined by 2% to 10.5%.

items.statement: Expect absolute 0.6% lowering of RMC percentage to sales in Q3 FY27; steel prices to increase, aluminum alloy prices softening
items.quote: In Q3 FY 27, we expect steel prices to increase, and we see a softening of the aluminum alloy prices. Overall, as of now, we see an absolute 0.6% lowering of RMC percentage to sales in Q3.

items.statement: Customer price increases from 1st October expected to give 0.5% positive impact on gross margin; commodity basket favorable by 0.5-0.6%
items.quote: Back of the envelope calculation suggests that should also have a positive impact of about 0.5% on gross margin. As we stand, we are seeing favorable commodity basket, as Anurang highlighted, about 0.5% to 0.6% positive impact it should have.

items.statement: Four greenfield facilities had negative PBT margin drag of 0.5% in Q2; drag to reduce progressively, positive contribution next financial year
items.quote: These four facilities drag had a negative PBT margin of about 0.5% in Q2, which we believe that progressively the drag should come down and in next financial year, we will have these facilities having a positive contribution.

items.statement: Total business win in H1 FY27 was ₹748 crores (ex-Bajaj); cumulative order book since FY22 at ₹6,372 crores with ₹3,798 crores yet to realize
items.quote: Total business win in half one was ₹ 748 crores, largely from HMSI, Tata Motors, Hero MotoCorp, TVS, Ather, and the US EV OEM. The total business won since FY22 is ₹ 6,372 crores, of which ₹ 5,125 crores i s new business. From ₹ 6,372 crores of order win, ₹ 3,798 crores of business is still to be

items.statement: EV share in order book increased to 24% in H1 FY27 from 11% in FY22; 4W India share increased to 23.5% from 16%
items.quote: The share of the EVs has increased to 24% as on Half 1 FY 27 versus 11% in FY22. b. The share of 4W from India has increased to 23.5% in Half 1 FY 27 versus 16% in FY22

items.statement: Consolidated total income grew 33% YoY to ₹4,811 crores in Q2 FY27; EBITDA grew 17.3% to ₹584 crores at 12.1% margin; PAT grew 21% to ₹274 crores at 5.7%
items.value: ₹4,811 cr revenue; ₹584 cr EBITDA; ₹274 cr PAT
items.quote: In Q2 FY 27, our consolidated total income grew 33% year -on-year to ₹ 4,811 crores. The EBITDA grew 17.3% to ₹ 584 crores, our margin was at 12.1%. The consolidated PAT grew 21% year-on-year to ₹ 274 crores with a PAT of 5.7%.

items.statement: Standalone total income grew 40% YoY to ₹3,761 crores; EBITDA grew 18% to ₹395 crores at 10.5% margin; PAT grew 14% to ₹213 crores
items.value: ₹3,761 cr revenue; ₹395 cr EBITDA; ₹213 cr PAT
items.quote: On standalone basis, the Company recorded a total income of ₹ 3,761 crores, a year-on-year growth of 40%. EBITDA grew 18% to ₹ 395 crores with a margin at 10.5%. The PAT grew by 14% year-on-year to ₹ 213 crores with a PAT at 5.7%.

items.statement: Europe total income grew 13% YoY to ₹1,029 crores (€93.9M); EBITDA grew 13.7% to ₹183 crores (€16.7M) at 17.8% margin; PAT grew 39.6% to ₹57 crores (€5.2M)
items.value: ₹1,029 cr revenue; ₹183 cr EBITDA; ₹57 cr PAT
items.quote: Our European business reported total income of ₹ 1,029 crores, a growth of 13% year -on-year, and EBITDA of ₹ 183 crores at 17.8% with a growth of 13.7% year-on-year. PAT was at ₹ 57 crores at 5.5%, which is a growth of 39.6% year-on-year.

items.statement: Maxwell revenue grew 94% YoY to ₹85 crores in Q2 FY27; PAT positive for consecutive quarters; H1 FY27 turnover ₹141 crores vs full FY26 ₹161 crores
items.quote: In Q2 FY 27, Maxwell revenue grew by 95% year-on-year and 50% quarter-on-quarter to ₹ 85 crores. Our strong R&D and innovation cell at Maxwell at Bangalore is also focusing on the IoT and V 2X solutions, TPMS, and high-voltage Battery Management Systems for 4W and e -buses.

items.statement: India EV sales grew 185% YoY to ₹229 crores in Q2 FY27, at 5% of total net sales
items.quote: I would like to inform you that our EV sales in India standalone for Q2 FY 27 grew by 185% to ₹ 229 crores, which was at 5% of our total net sales.

items.statement: Aftermarket business grew 36% YoY in Q2 FY27, comprising 4% of consolidated income; significantly margin-accretive
items.quote: Our India aftermarket business grew by 36% year-on-year in Q2 FY 27, comprising 4% of our consolidated income. It is a significantly margin-accretive business for us.

items.statement: ABS capacity of 1.54 million units per annum by Q4 FY27; 70% booked by Bajaj Auto and Royal Enfield; dual-channel ABS SOP started October for Bajaj
items.quote: By Q4 FY 27, for ABS, we will have a capacity of 1.54 million single and dual channel ABSs per annum, of which 70% is already booked by Bajaj Auto and Royal Enfield. For the dual channel ABS supplies to Bajaj Auto has started in October this year.

items.statement: AURIC Shendra plant started SOP 25th September for 4W aluminum casting (high/low pressure die casting, machining, powder coating); supplies to US EV OEM begun
items.quote: Our AURIC Shendra plant started SOP on 25 th of September this year and will serve four -wheeler OEMs in India, the UK, and the US. This plant does high-pressure and low-pressure die casting, critical machining, and powder coating. The supplies to the US EV OEM have also begun.

items.statement: Fifth aluminum forging press SOP expected Q4 FY27 for inverted front fork business and external customers
items.quote: To meet this demand, we are adding a fifth aluminum forging press with SOP expected in Q4 of FY 27.

items.statement: Upside down forks capacity reaching 100,000 units/month across 7 OEMs including exports by Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are adding capacities in line with the market growth for the ups ide down forks and we are reaching the milestone of 100,000 units per month, spread across seven OEM customers and including exports by Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Solar damper plant at Sanand ready; SOP for European client started Q2, US client expected H2 FY27, solar actuators SOP expected Q4 FY27
items.quote: For the solar US client, SOP is expected in the second half of this financial year. We are also gearing up for the supply of solar actuators, and the SOP is expected in Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Battery pack business: 2W OEM full ramp-up expected Q3 FY27; 4W OEM nominations with SOP Q1 and Q2 FY28; 2W line ~18,000 packs/month, 4W line ~8,000 packs/month
items.quote: We have commenced SOP of battery packs for EVs for a leading 2W OEM with full ramp-up expected in Q3 of this financial year. Also, we have received letters of nomination from two passenger vehicle OEMs for 4W battery packs with SOP scheduled for Q1 and Q2 of the next financial year, respectively.

items.statement: Fondalpress acquisition adds 16,400 sqm building, 16 automated die-casting machines (2,300-2,800 ton), land for expansion; enables insourcing Stöferle castings and truck segment entry
items.quote: We bought 16 fully automated die-casting machines, ranging from 2,300 ton to 2,800 ton. The equipment is in good working condition and will immediately scale our manufacturing capacity, allowing the production of parts, currently purchased from an external supplier.

items.statement: Consolidated net cash position ₹436 crores as on 30th September 2026
items.quote: In Q2 FY 27, our consolidated net cash position as on 30 th September 2026 was at ₹ 436 crores.

items.statement: India 2W sales grew 18% YoY in Q2 FY27 (motorcycles 13%, scooters 30%); PV sales up 24%; 3W up 25%; EU new car sales up 5.6% YoY
items.quote: In Q2 FY 27, in the Indian automotive sector, as per SIAM, 2W sales grew by 18% year-on-year, with motorcycles at 13% growth and scooters at 30% growth. Passenger vehicle sales increased by 24% year-on-year, while 3W sales rose 25%. In the European Union, new car sales saw a year-on-year rise of 5.6% in Q2 FY 27.

items.statement: EU market growth largely driven by Chinese OEMs (SAIC 23%, BYD 133%, Geely 26%, Chery 215%); excluding Chinese, growth only 0.7%; Endurance grew 3-4x market
items.quote: Except for the impact of the Chinese, the increase compared to the previous year should have been only 0.7%, because SAIC grew 23%, BYD 133%, Geely 26%, and Chery 215%. And so it means that more than 90% of the increase compared to the previous year has been done by the Chinese OEM.

items.statement: 4W proprietary products (suspension, brakes, driveshafts, battery packs) expected to scale from ₹100 crores FY28 to ₹800 crores FY31; non-auto (solar, railways, industrial) from ₹250 crores FY28 to ₹650 crores FY31
items.quote: SOP for 4W suspension, brakes and drive shaft to increase from ₹ 100 crores in FY 28 to ₹ 800 crores in FY 31. We believe, once we start execution in these new areas, engagement with customers would increase. Non-auto business includes supplies to solar, railways, and industrial applications for products like suspension and actuators. We expect cumulative SOP of ₹ 250 crores in FY 28, which should

items.statement: 4W suspension: advanced engagement with 2 Indian and 1 overseas customer; SOP H1 FY28, H2 FY29, third in Q4 FY27; 4W brakes/driveshaft: driveshaft SOP this quarter, brakes H1 FY28
items.quote: On the 4W suspension business, there has been advanced engagement with two Indian and one overseas customer. Out of this, SOP of one customer is expected in H1 FY 28, and the other in H2 FY 29. The third customer SOP timelines will get finalis ed in Q4 of this year. b. 4W brakes and driveshaft is also seeing good progress with passenger and commercial vehicle OEMs, with the commencement of SOP for

items.statement: Bajaj Auto contributes ~35% of group revenue (₹9,159 crores in H1 FY27); excluded from ₹748 crores H1 order wins
items.quote: So if you take our income in the first two quarters , it is ₹ 9,159 crores. So, you can take a figure of 35% for the group.

items.statement: 4W casting expanding with Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, Korean OEMs localization, commercial vehicles; AURIC Shendra serves India, UK, US OEMs
items.quote: We are expanding our 4W casting business with domestic OEMs like Tata Motors, Mahindra and Mahindra, and helping Korean OEMs to localise. We are also expanding in commercial vehicles, and are in active dialogue with multiple OEMs.

items.statement: Assist & slip clutches supplied to Royal Enfield and Kawasaki; Bajaj Auto validation in process, SOP expected Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are already supplying assist and slip clutches to Royal Enfield and Kawasaki. For Bajaj Auto, customer validation is in process and SOP is expected in Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Driveshaft SOP for Tata Motors expected this quarter; 3W driveshaft programs for Bajaj, Mahindra, TVS already supplying; expect driveshaft revenue >₹100 crores FY27
items.quote: For our 4W driveshaft program, the SOP for Tata Motors is expected in this quarter. Supplies had already begun for the 3W driveshaft programs of Bajaj, Mahindra and TVS and we expect our driveshaft revenue to cross ₹ 100 crores in FY 27.

items.statement: Europe Q2 FY27: €93.9M turnover (+5.9% YoY), €16.7M EBITDA (+5.9%), €5.2M net profit (+31.4%); cash flow €17.7M (18.8% of turnover)
items.quote: We closed the second quarter in Europe with € 93.9 million of turnover, compared 88.7 of the previous financial year, with an increase of € 5.2 million, 5.9%. In terms of EBITDA, we grew from € 15.8 million to € 16.7 million with an increase of 5.9%.

items.statement: EV business margins similar to corporate; overall EV business margin-accretive including battery packs, BMS, castings
items.quote: No. In fact, the margins will be similar. Of course, we will try and improve it, but the margins will be similar. Aditya Jhawar: Just, one thing to clarify. So when you talk about EV revenue, they are coming from our die casting products, our suspension, brakes, all our existing products. And there are new revenue streams that we have added, like battery pack business. So clearly, overall, EV busi

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia increasing energy price volatility and supply chain uncertainty; tighter global financial conditions weighing on outlook
items.quote: The global environment remains uncertain. The re-escalation of the conflict in West Asia has led to higher and more volatile crude oil prices and has added to uncertainty around energy costs, freight, and supply chains. Trade uncertainties and tighter global financial conditions also continue to weigh on the global outlook.

items.statement: Conversion cost increases for fuels (diesel, CNG, LPG) and cutting tools not adjusted by most OEMs in Q1-Q2 FY27; certain OEM increases settled from Q3 FY27 (1st Oct 2026)
items.quote: Q1 an Q2 FY 27, conversion cost increase of fuels, including diesel, CNG and LPG, and cutting tools were not adjusted by most OEMs, and certain OEM increases have been settled only from Q3 FY 27 or 1st October 2026 onwards

items.statement: Aditya Jhawar joined as Head, Growth and Business Transformation; excited to leverage strong execution track record and balance sheet for growth and diversification
items.quote: It's nice to be on this side of the conference call. I am quite excited to join Endurance and leverage the strong execution track record and a very strong balance sheet to push the pedal on growth and diversification.

items.statement: Management intends to chase double-digit PBT growth for FY27 but acknowledges it has become tougher due to El Niño impact on agchem and palm oil price volatility.
items.quote: Whether we'll hit double -digit PBT, I think more clarit y come every month. I never expected, for example, palm oil prices suddenly shift so much in last 48 hours. I wouldn't be surprised if the palm oil prices also come back maybe after two months, because as Malaysian stocks reduce, I'll expect balance to come back. So, it's a bit of open -ended question, but intent, I am not giving up on

items.statement: Oil palm business targets a healthy double-digit EBITDA CAGR for FY27 and the midterm.
items.quote: I will give you CAGR. I think a healthy double-digit CAGR is what we chase, and we think we should be able to deliver over this year itself, and over the midterm also.

items.statement: Oil palm downstream integration expected to add roughly 2 percentage points to segment EBITDA margin over a two-to-four-year midterm period.
items.quote: As this business scale up fully, the downstream business scales up fully, that in the midterm, which is over two to three, four-year period, this will add overall roughly around 2% to the overall EBITDA margin of the oil palm business.

items.statement: Oil palm FFB volume growth guidance of double-digits for FY27 maintained despite weather challenges.
items.quote: Our guidance for a double-digit volume growth on FFB stays.

items.statement: Oil palm OER target for FY27 is to recover to 19.7%+ annualized level after weather-related dip in Q2.
items.quote: Our attempt is very clearly, can we recover over the next four months and end the year at that 19.7 plus kind of a number?

items.statement: El Niño caused 13% below-normal monsoon and 10-year low reservoir levels, creating uncertainty for Rabi season and impacting crop care and dairy.
items.quote: El Niño intensified into a super event, with the monsoon ending about 13% below normal and reservoir levels at a 10-year low, creating uncertainty for the Rabi season.

items.statement: Crop care and Astec faced weak demand due to El Niño; cotton and chili segments particularly affected.
items.quote: Crop care was significantly impacted by the El Niño, and El Niño-led demand weakness and an unfavourable product mix.

items.statement: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej) growing at very high double-digit volumes across aqua, poultry, and dairy segments.
items.quote: In every single business, we are growing at very high double-digit volumes.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA stable at INR222 crores with 7.4% margin despite significant cost inflation.
items.quote: EBITDA remained stable at INR222 crores, despite significant cost inflation, with margin at 7.4%.

items.statement: Animal nutrition segment profit grew 32% with margin improvement from favourable mix and operating efficiencies.
items.quote: Animal nutrition delivered another strong quarter with revenue growth of 14% and segment profit growth of 32%. Growth was supported by higher realizations and volume gains across key segments, while margins improved through favourable mix and operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Dairy profitability affected by elevated milk procurement, packaging, and logistics costs; no respite expected for next two quarters.
items.quote: We are not seeing any respite. I can tell you about our take on dairy pricing, and that is something I think we will all have to start building in for future also. I think there are two parts which are playing on milk prices in India. One is temporary, one I believe is structural.

items.statement: Godrej Foods EBITDA plus working media margin expanded 20 bps to 5.8% despite hyperinflation in feed costs.
items.quote: Having said that, if I see the EBITDA plus working media margin put together, last year we were 5.6%. We have moved to 5.8% this year, which is 20 basis points higher still.

items.statement: Ashitaka® maize herbicide launch on track to cross INR100 crores revenue in first year.
items.quote: This would be the launch which in its first year would have crossed INR100 crores in revenue.

items.statement: Crop care pipeline targets seven crop segments by FY29-30 to reduce dependence on cotton and chili.
items.quote: We are targeting that by FY29-2030, we will have seven different crop segments playing in. Once that come into play, our dependence on cotton and chili would sharply reduce.

items.statement: Astec CDMO funnel strong with 90% inquiry-to-R&D conversion and 15 products in R&D pipeline.
items.quote: Currently, if you see quarter two, almost conversion from inquiries to R&D, means there are different stages of development a product goes through. So, conversion has been almost 90%. So, 90% of the inquiries has converted to an R&D stage.

items.statement: Oil palm integrated complex in Khammam commissioned with mill, CPKO refinery, and biogas plant; hydrogenation and fractionation to come in December.
items.quote: We commissioned a mill at the complex along with a CPKO refinery and biogas pl ant during the quarter, strengthening our integrated

items.statement: Added 13,000 hectares of oil palm plantations in H1 FY27.
items.quote: During H1, we added 13,000 hectares of plantations and inaugurated India's first integrated oil palm complex in Khammam in Telangana.

items.statement: PKO derivatives plant commissioned 1st September; meaningful financial impact expected from Q4 FY27, scaling in FY28.
items.quote: A meaningful impact will start coming in from, quarter four, and then scale up really in FY28.

items.statement: Palm oil prices expected to range INR4,250-4,400 over next couple of months, then potentially creep up by Feb-Mar depending on El Niño in Indonesia/Malaysia.
items.quote: My sense of what will happen is, it will remain in the range of INR4,300-INR4,400, maybe INR4,250-INR4,350 over the next couple of months. Then all eyes will be what happens to the El Niño effect in Indonesia and Malaysia over the next three months. If that remains high, the prices could surge back again.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh government fruit price order for oil palm not yet released; last year assumed 20.01% OER.
items.quote: The new order pricing has not come out as yet. We are all waiting for it. The fact is, the way the formula normally should proceed is the fact that it depends on the weighted average of the benchmark that is supposed to be followed on the ground of the mills, and it depends on the OER which has been th ere in the last one year

items.statement: PKO prices less volatile than CPO; expected to remain elevated but difficult to predict exact levels.
items.quote: The PKO prices have not seen as much of volatility as CPO. That is one thing. Now the question is, why? The answers are very difficult right now on this. Actually, honestly, I wish NBG were here. With his expertise, he would have given you a much deeper layer on this. I am genuinely missing his expert point of view here right now. Having said that, laurics have not behaved the same way as we are s

items.statement: Animal nutrition shifting focus to cattle feed (8% volume growth) and layer feed (double-digit growth), de-prioritizing broiler feed.
items.quote: We are doing a shift towards building more cattle feed business, and de-prioritizing broiler feed business. So, our core segments would be primarily dairy feed or cattle feed, followed by, in poultry, we'll try to focus a little more on layer feed.

items.statement: Godrej Foods B2C salience increased to 38% (from 25%), driven by 50% B2C growth and new product launches (frozen chicken, momos, nuggets).
items.quote: Godrej Foods continued to shift towards higher-value products, with B2C growing by 50% and its salience increasing to 38%, supported by consumer demand and successful launches.

items.statement: Dairy value-added products now 49% of portfolio; GTM revamp pilot launched in Chennai testing AM/PM distributor model.
items.quote: Dairy revenue grew 6%, led by calibrated pricing and growth in value-added products, which now account for 49% of the portfolio.

items.statement: Quick commerce (dark stores) providing structural tailwind for Godrej Foods frozen portfolio, enabling capex-light distribution.
items.quote: One is obviously, clearly, the frozen food segment is seeing a structural tailwind thanks to the change event of quick commerce in this country. You have a dark stores phenomena happening. You do not have to go and put coolers in every part of the nook and corner of the country or freezers in every part of the country. So, it becomes a little capex-light model in itself.

items.statement: Net working capital improved to 21 days from 32 days YoY; absolute working capital reduced to INR655 crores.
items.quote: Working capital management remains strong, with net working capital improving to 21 days from 32 days last year. Absolute working capital reduced to INR655 crores, strengthening balance sheet and returns on capital.

items.statement: Proactively increased inventory in Q2 to benefit from better prices; expected to normalize in H2, freeing cash.
items.quote: One of the things that Sunil mentioned earlier, what we have done during this quarter has been, we have proactively increased our inventory holding levels to take the benefit of better prices, given the inflation levels that we are seeing. Some of that inventory will sort of get consumed as we go through H2. Therefore, as we get into the second half, which should overall free up some cash.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity at ~0.8x; expected to remain around that level in H2 despite Q2 increase due to inventory build.
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity is at about 0.8, and we expect it to be pretty much in and around that level as we go through the second half as well.

items.statement: INR50 crores dividend received from Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej) in Q2; no one-off items in other income.
items.quote: The dividend of INR50 crores is from our Bangladesh JV, which has come in this quarter.

items.statement: Hired Head of Sales Transformation from Britannia/Marico; two more members joining by December; new CEOs for dairy and Bangladesh JV.
items.quote: We have created a center of excellence of sales transformation, where we have hired a head of sales transformation who is coming from Britannia and Marico. The brief to him is very clearly to help us build new sales transformation models for Godrej Foods, which is a poultry business. In fact, we call it Godrej Foods now. The dairy business is the second one. We will also, maybe a year down the lin

items.statement: Manpower cost increase expected from new hires; partly in FY27, annualized impact in FY28.
items.quote: The question is it going to take some extra cost? The answer is yes. There will be some extra cost which is going to come in manpower budget, which we have already started. Some of it, I would say, partly is coming into this year, but there will be some impact of it, I think annualized, will come into next year.

items.statement: El Niño impact on agchem and dairy may persist for two quarters; structural milk price reset expected due to value-added product shift.
items.quote: I expect this to come back, if monsoon is good, only after two quarters, not before that. So, I think we will have to expect that next two quarters there is no respite. Then structural part, I think, will stay here. So, that is where our take on milk pricing in India is.

items.statement: Palm oil price volatility from US election impact on crude, high Malaysian inventory, and potential El Niño in Indonesia/Malaysia.
items.quote: There has been a lot of volatility in the last 48 hours in the Brent. I mean, it was at 112, it went down sharply, and then now it's again back to 100. This has a linkage to what it does to the biodiesel mandate parity. I think this is one thing we'll have to wait and watch. I think this will remain range-bound, that's one. Second, which I think could impact over two months is a very high stock ho

items.statement: Oil palm OER in Q2 FY27 at ~18.9% vs higher last year; September recovered to last year level, October marginally ahead.
items.quote: We have ended up quarter two at around 18.9, which is lower than last year quarter two. The question is, what is happening? What I explained to Abhijit's question with the cyclones, with recovery happening, in the month of September, we have come back to last year, September. In the month of October, we have creaked little ahead.

items.statement: Oil palm FFB volumes grew 14% in Q2; H1 collections at all-time high despite three months of extreme heat.
items.quote: If you see actually quarter two, despite this huge challenge of June, July, August, I will say three months was crazy heat, yet we have grown in double-digits on FFB. And the quarter two overall collections that we had, they have been a record high collection for us now. It's all-time high.

items.statement: Godrej Foods new products launched in last year contribute ~25% of current business revenue.
items.quote: I think today roughly around 25% of our current business is already, and this is a number I can share, 25% of our current business has started coming from the new product which we have launched in the last one year.

items.statement: Astec CDMO target 50-55% of business in midterm; 15 products in R&D pipeline with 70-80% commercialization conversion rate.
items.quote: We are very clearly in the midterm; we are looking at CDMO business being 50% -55%. We could have deviations in one year or so because of toughness, but we would also like to tell you what is happening on our funnel pipeline of CDMO. Arijit, you want to pitch in that.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to be minimum double-digits in FY28 from new projects CIGNUS 2 and Taj Delhi Airport
items.quote: With these two significant projects coming online, it should contribute minimum double-digits to our revenue growth.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR 34-36 billion over FY27-FY29, largely funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have outlined a planned CAPEX of approximately INR 34 billion-INR 36 billion over FY27 to FY29 across our Hospitality and Commercial Real Estate portfolio.

items.statement: Target operational portfolio of 5,500 keys and beyond within five years, implying 75-80% capacity addition
items.quote: As Shwetank mentioned in his opening remarks, we expect to have an operational portfolio of 5,500 keys and beyond in five years. That means 75%-80% capacity addition.

items.statement: CRE monthly rental run-rate expected to reach INR 320 million by March 2027, and INR 500 crore annualized once CIGNUS 2 fully leased
items.quote: We expect monthly rentals to scale up further to INR 320 million by March'27. Commissioning of CIGNUS 2 at Powai will lead to a step change in growth towards FY28 onwards.

items.statement: Capex guidance increased to INR 34-36 billion for FY27-FY29 due to addition of two ATHIVA properties at Hyderabad and Pune, no cost overruns on existing projects
items.quote: The change in CAPEX guidance is due to addition of two ATHIVA properties at Hyderabad and Pune. The guidance includes committed investments and importantly is expected to be largely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: CIGNUS 2 Powai on track for substantial completion by FY27 end; Taj Delhi Airport expected to launch entire inventory in early FY28, monitoring GRAP restrictions
items.quote: For CIGNUS 2 Powai, we remain on track for substantial completion by FY27 end, and for Taj, we expect to launch the entire inventory in early FY'28.

items.statement: Total pipeline stands at 2,036 keys, about 60% of current operating portfolio; ATHIVA brand scaling with ~900 keys in pipeline across five properties
items.quote: Also, our total pipeline now stands at 2,036 keys, about 60% of our current operating portfolio.

items.statement: Varca Goa construction expected to start in Q4 FY27 after CRZ and MoEF approvals; Udaipur refurbishment of 141 rooms underway, expansion potential held back
items.quote: We should be starting construction in Varca definitely in Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Leisure portfolio delivered 34% RevPAR growth in Q2 FY27 with blended resort occupancy at 41.2% vs 32.6% last year; Westin Himalayas grew 50-55%
items.quote: Compared to business hotels, resorts did better this quarter with 34% RevPAR growth. All three resorts delivered strong growth as we moved towards stabilization, with resort occupancies on a blended basis at 41.2% against 32.6% last year.

items.statement: MMR business hotels saw weaker July due to rains, recovery in Aug-Sep from MICE; Hyderabad strong on GCC demand; Bangalore moderate, foreign tourist dependent; Pune healthy on corporate and retail demand
items.quote: Our business hotels in MMR, Hyderabad, and Bangalore saw mixed trends through the quarter, while our Leisure portfolio witnessed strong demand and delivered 34% RevPAR growth with a good mix of Occupancy and ADR.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin improved 110 bps to 45% in Q2 FY27; Hospitality EBITDA margin 41% (+110 bps); CRE EBITDA margin 83% (+95 bps)
items.quote: Our core business grew by 11% year-on-year to INR 5,110 million, with EBITDA of INR 2,274 million, up 13% year-on-year. Importantly, EBITDA margin improved by 110 bps to 45%.

items.statement: Margins improved as leisure assets stabilize and efficiency measures take hold; city hotel margins steady; quick action mitigated cost pressures from West Asia war
items.quote: Over the past few quarters, the margins were optically soft due to new additions and Leisure assets operating below critical occupancy. This has reversed in H1 as per our commitment.

items.statement: CRE September 2026 rental run-rate INR 300 million/month at 91% occupancy; LOI signed for remaining Bangalore space takes available area occupancy to 95%
items.quote: The monthly rental exit run rate in September 2026 stood at INR 300 million, marginally higher than INR 290 million for June 2026. Revenue for the quarter stood at INR 901 million, up 22% year-on-year, driven by higher occupancy.

items.statement: Crew contract of 20 rooms/day signed at Powai (lost ~100 rooms/day during construction); porch restored enabling large MICE events
items.quote: In an immediate win, we have signed a Crew contract already of 20 rooms per day. Just to remind you, we had lost about 100 rooms per day of Crew business at Powai due to the ongoing construction activity.

items.statement: Blended ADR grew 11.3% YoY in Q2 FY27, reflecting pricing power; RevPAR up 7.2%; F&B grew 6.4% but MICE/large groups only 4%
items.quote: For the quarter, our blended ADRs grew 11.3% year-on-year. This reflects our leadership position and pricing power in these markets.

items.statement: ATHIVA brand scaling: Navi Mumbai rebranded to ATHIVA Pulse (Autograph Collection) with INR 1 billion investment; Khandala operational; pipeline ~900 keys across 5 properties targeting 1,200-key portfolio
items.quote: First, ATHIVA, with Khandala and Navi Mumbai operational and approximately 900 keys already in the pipeline across five properties in four locations, ATHIVA is on route to become a 1,200-key portfolio.

items.statement: Strategy: use Marriott/Autograph for international-demand properties (e.g., Navi Mumbai), standalone ATHIVA for domestic-demand properties; Navi Mumbai retains Marriott distribution and loyalty access
items.quote: If the customer is largely domestically fed, then we will tend to stay on a standalone ATHIVA without the soft branding. If it is international market fed, as was the case with Navi Mumbai, we will focus on tie-ups with the likes of Marriott.

items.statement: Residential Phase-II Koramangala (168 units) near completion, RERA handover date Dec 2026; revenue booking to start Q3 FY27; commercial space ~160k sq ft under construction for lease by FY28
items.quote: 168 units of Phase-II of Koramangala residential project is near completion. The RERA date for handover is December 2026. We shall begin handover soon and subsequently book the revenue in Q3FY27.

items.statement: Net debt stable at INR 21 billion as of Sep 2026 (INR 14 billion allocated to under-construction assets); avg cost of finance 7.47%; credit rating upgraded to IND AA from AA-
items.quote: As of September 2026, our net debt stood at INR 21 billion, approximately INR 14 billion of this allocable to assets under construction or not operationalized yet.

items.statement: CRE rentals provide leverage advantage of INR 25 billion LRD eligibility; lease rentals cover debt servicing, freeing hotel assets for pipeline execution and acquisitions
items.quote: The current yearly rentals potentially give us a leverage advantage of INR 25 billion eligibility for LRD. Lease rentals also help us in debt servicing as it stands today, effectively freeing up our hotel assets to generate cash.

items.statement: No fresh equity raise mentioned; growth to be funded from hospitality cash flows and CRE annuity; credit rating upgrade reflects balance sheet strength
items.quote: Together, these put us on track for a portfolio of 5,500 keys and beyond within the next five years with a strong Leisure and geographic mix. We will fund this growth from our Hospitality cash flows and stable Commercial Real Estate annuity business.

items.statement: Taj Delhi Airport timeline monitored for GRAP restrictions in NCR; Varca Goa required CRZ clearance and MoEF approval causing delay
items.quote: However, we are closely monitoring the recent developments on GRAP restrictions in the National Capital Region to reassess the completion date.

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals impacted by West Asia crisis (50% connections via Middle East); US midterm election outcome seen as positive for travel recovery; Hyderabad GCC demand picking up
items.quote: The fact that almost 50% of these connections were through the Middle East, and nobody wanted to touch a very volatile market on the way over to India.

items.statement: Hospitality RevPAR grew 7.2% YoY (ADR +11.3%, occupancy blended); Resort RevPAR +34% YoY (occupancy 41.2% vs 32.6%); CRE rental yield 83% EBITDA margin
items.quote: RevPAR increased 7.2% year-on-year, largely driven by 11.3% growth in ADR. Compared to business hotels, resorts did better this quarter with 34% RevPAR growth.

items.statement: Geopolitical risk from West Asia crisis impacting air traffic and foreign arrivals; GRAP restrictions in NCR may delay Taj Delhi; Goa approvals notoriously difficult causing project delays
items.quote: We are closely monitoring the recent developments on GRAP restrictions in the National Capital Region to reassess the completion date.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR 70-75% FY25-FY28; EBITDA CAGR 40-45%; PAT CAGR 35-40%; EBITDA margin 12-13% and PAT margin 5-6% by FY28
items.value: 70-75% revenue CAGR; 40-45% EBITDA CAGR; 35-40% PAT CAGR
items.quote: We reiterate our earlier guidance of approximately 70% to 75% consolidated revenue CAGR over FY25 to FY28, supported by the phased commissioning and ramp-up of Bokaro, alongside continued strategic organic growth across our existing verticals. Over the same period, we expect operating EBITDA and PAT to grow at a CAGR of approximately 40% to 45% and 35% to 40%, respectively, with EBITDA and PAT mar

items.statement: Additional 60-65 days working capital needed for Bokaro; estimated Rs 350-400 cr absolute; aim for cash-and-carry but not 100% feasible
items.quote: The assumption right now is an additional 60 to 65 days of working capital requirement. The intention is to sell on a cash -and- carry basis, but as you will appreciate, 100% of the products cannot be sold that way

items.statement: Margins stable on rupee-per-ton basis; raw material price increases affect working capital and percentage margins but not absolute rupee margins
items.quote: Margins are typically more stable on a rupees -per-ton basis. As raw material prices increase, there will be two effects. One is the effect on working capital needs, and the other is a small effec t on the percentage numbers, because the rupee margins will remain fairly stable but percentages may not

items.statement: Not targeting exports initially; focus domestic; exports opportunistic later
items.quote: We are not averse to exports, but at this point in time, it's a little early for us to start targeting them. The current focus remains on the domestic market. Exports, as and when they happen, will be more opportunistic.

items.statement: Currently sourcing alloy-coated base from Eastern India sellers; will shift to HR coils as back-end (cold rolling, pickling) commissions; Eastern India has large HR coil suppliers
items.quote: We are currently sourcing the alloy-coated base product, and there are various sellers in Eastern India itself. As we continue to commission the back end of the plant, we will move to sourcing HR coils. Again, if you look at Eastern India, you have some of the country's largest suppliers of HR coil there, so that is the final plan.

items.statement: Targets INR3,000 crore revenue by FY30, with INR2,000 crore organic and INR800-1,000 crore from DYA JV
items.quote: Yes, that is correct. In addition to that, we have a few more initiatives that we are working towards to achieve our INR3,000 crore vision by FY30.

items.statement: Expects INR800-1,000 crore revenue from DYA JV executed in FY31
items.quote: We would estimate something between INR800 crore and INR1,000 crore that is going to be executed in FY31.

items.statement: Targets sustainable EBITDA margin of 11-11.5%
items.quote: Yes, that is the EBITDA number that we are targeting, it will be sustainable.

items.statement: Consolidated order book expanded to INR1,190 crore (INR1,150 crore standalone + INR40 crore NDR Hayashi JV)
items.quote: Our consolidated order book has expanded to INR1,190 crore and at the exit of the quarter under review, comprising of INR1,150 crore from NDR Auto standalone and INR40 crore from our NDR Hayashi Joint Venture.

items.statement: Standalone order book of INR1,150 crore to be fully executed by FY30
items.quote: All of the INR1,150 crore will be executed by FY30.

items.statement: Large portion of INR1,150 crore order book starts in 2 years, ramped up by FY30
items.quote: A large portion of it starts maybe in 2 years and is subject to ramp up, probably will all get ramped up by FY30.

items.statement: FY29 and FY30 expected to be bigger years for order book execution
items.quote: FY29 and FY30 should be bigger years.

items.statement: Major order wins from Maruti Suzuki, Suzuki two-wheeler, and Toyota
items.quote: We predominantly got orders from Maruti Suzuki and Suzuki two-wheeler, that is comprised of this order increase and we have also got some new businesses from Toyota.

items.statement: DYA JV to supply full seat assemblies to Hyundai Kia, standalone to continue seat covers and frames
items.quote: So currently we do seat covers and seat frame that will continue in our standalone entity. The joint venture will do full seat assemblies, which include assemblies and foams for Hyundai Kia.

items.statement: Confident of retaining Maruti Suzuki share and entering Kia Motors, also targeting Hyundai
items.quote: Having said that, we are quite confident to keep our share in Maruti Suzuki. And we are also quite confident into the entering Kia Motors. And in relation to that, we also want to add Hyundai as a client.

items.statement: Formed 51:49 JV with DYA (Korea), NDR to invest INR62.96 crore, JV to set up manufacturing facility for Hyundai Motors
items.quote: We are also delighted to partner with DYA a leading automotive system company based out of Korea. NDR Auto will hold 51% in the joint venture company, in which it will make an investment of INR62.96 crore.

items.statement: DYA JV to be fully consolidated, NDR share of profit at 51%
items.quote: It will be a joint venture where NDR owns 51%. So it will be fully consolidated.

items.statement: Board approved brownfield expansion of Gujarat and Kharkhoda facilities for seat frames, trim and other auto ancillaries
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved the Brownfield expansion of our Gujarat and Kharkhoda facilities, which will manufacture seat frames and trim and a range of other auto ancillaries.

items.statement: INR60 crore capex for announced projects, another INR60 crore for JV, plus yearly maintenance capex
items.quote: We are going to put INR60 crore as the projects we have announced, the joint bench is going to be another INR60 crore plus we will have some yearly capex that we are going to add.

items.statement: CWIP of INR39 crore includes Seat Belt Reminder System project and operational capex
items.quote: The revenue contribution is already included in our order book, which we have already released. Well, this includes a project of latch as Seat Belt Reminder System and other operational capex in in NDR auto.

items.statement: Capacity utilization approximately 90% across plants
items.quote: Our capacity utilization should be approximately 90% across our plants.

items.statement: New capacity expansions expected around January 2027, ramp-up started
items.quote: EBITDA, I think the ramp-up has started, yes, I think next year should be slightly better.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 11.08% despite challenges
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins remained healthy at 11.08% despite the environmental and supply chain challenges, which is a reflection of the efficiency of our operations.

items.statement: Other expenses increased due to Haryana minimum wage hike (INR2.5 crore) and NDR South execution (INR2.5 crore)
items.quote: Yes. So INR2.5 crore is NDR South and balance is on account of the Haryana minimum wage increase

items.statement: Negotiating with OEMs to pass on manpower cost increase from minimum wage hike
items.quote: So some of the cost has not passed down. Some of the cost has passed on. We are currently negotiating that number with them.

items.statement: JV to do full seat assemblies (including foam), standalone to supply seat covers and frames
items.quote: The joint venture will do full seat assemblies, which include assemblies and foams for Hyundai Kia.

items.statement: JV content per vehicle INR50,000-80,000, targeting 1-1.5 lakh volumes
items.quote: Yes. So, the content per vehicle for this joint venture is anything between INR50,000 and maybe INR80,000. We are targeting about one and a 1.5 lakh volume.

items.statement: Currently no exports, only Indian market supply
items.quote: So currently, we do not export any products. We just supply to the Indian market. We are working on some initiatives.

items.statement: Associate PAT up 2.5x QoQ; TSIL (Toyo Seats) turned profitable, NHI loss reduced due to price increase
items.quote: Our company TSIL, Toyo Seats, that has turned profitable. and NHI loss in this quarter is less because we received the price increase from customers.

items.statement: Share of associate profit INR5.2 crore considered sustainable
items.quote: Yes, I think that is a sustainable number.

items.statement: Job work arrangement at NDR South: INR2.76 crore other income, INR2.5 crore expenses (netted off)
items.quote: It is almost same. Expense is around INR2.5 crore, and the income is INR2.76 crore.

items.statement: Gabriel India-Forvia JV increases competition for new OEM entry, but confident on Maruti share and Kia entry
items.quote: Adding a new player, definitely makes it tougher to enter a new OEM. Having said that, we are quite confident to keep our share in Maruti Suzuki.

items.statement: Kia production started this quarter, ramp-up at 18x, full contribution from Q4
items.quote: So it started production sometime this quarter, ramp-ups at 18 times, but it should come for in Q4.

items.statement: Working on commercial vehicle and 2-wheeler client wins, some order wins from 2-wheeler segment
items.quote: We are working on that. When it converts , we will share that with you. So me of the order wins are actually from the 2-wheeler segment

items.statement: No annual guidance given due to ramp-up and model mix uncertainties
items.quote: We do not give annual guidance. The NDR auto south has started, and we have some more models starting at the end of the year.

items.statement: Order book execution subject to ramp-up delays, some last-minute delays possible
items.quote: So most of it is as per schedule, but there are always some last minute delays.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guidance maintained at 15% on constant currency basis
items.quote: our guidance for the full year growth remains same as 15% on constant currency basis

items.statement: Strong demand across CDMO and critical injectables driving revenue growth
items.quote: robust demand across our critical injectable business, successful product launches, improving operating leverage, and disciplined execution across the organization

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin at 27% for Q2 FY2027, up from 21% YoY
items.quote: Adjusted for non-cash ESOP expense of INR 226 million, adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 5,030 million, translating into adjusted EBITDA margin of 27%

items.statement: CDMO revenues grew 31% YoY to INR 8,227 million, contributing 45% of total revenue
items.quote: During the quarter, CDMO revenues grew 31% year-on-year to INR 8,227 million, contributing approximately 45% of total revenues

items.statement: Gross margin stable at 63% for Q2 and 64% for H1 despite higher R&D spend
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter was 63%, and the first half it was 64%, same as the corresponding period last year

items.statement: CDMO contribution increased to 45% of revenue in Q2 and 47% in H1 FY2027
items.quote: H1 FY2027, CDMO revenues increased 25% year-on-year to INR 17,142 million, contributing approximately 47% of consolidated revenues

items.statement: Strong customer engagement driving CDMO growth with new manufacturing contracts for microspheres and respiratory products
items.quote: During the quarter, we expanded our capabilities in respiratory products and secured manufacturing contracts for both microspheres and respiratory products

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 158 days driven by inventory optimization
items.quote: Working capital days improved to 158 days, driven primarily by inventory optimization initiati ves and enhanced inventory management practices across the business

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 32,216 million as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: After adjusting for debt, the company maintained a robust net cash position of approximately INR 32,216 million

items.statement: New CEO Deepak Sapra joining November 16; Ajay Sahni joined as Cenexi President; key hires in tech transfer, project management, strategy, BD China, and CIO China
items.quote: Gland Pharma's new CEO, Mr. Deepak Sapra, will join Gland Pharma on November 16th, while Mr. Ajay Sahni has joined earlier this week as President of Cenexi operations

items.statement: R&D spend at 6% of revenue (INR 1,077 million) in Q2; 11 ANDAs filed, 10 approvals, 4 US launches
items.quote: During the quarter, we spent INR 1,077 million, that is 6% of our revenues on R&D, and have filed 11 ANDAs, received 10 approvals, and launched four products in the US

items.statement: First in-licensed product from China ($800M) to be manufactured in India; milestone income INR 95 crore, profit share INR 202 crore in Q2
items.quote: Overall milestone is about INR 95 crores, and profit share is about INR 202 crores. 11% and 5%.

items.statement: Full-year price increase expected around 5-6%
items.quote: On a full year basis, it should be, say, around 5%-6% price increase, around six-ish, as of now.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 13.1%, up 50 bps YoY, flat QoQ despite cost pressures
items.quote: EBITDA at INR82.5 crores grew 19.1% year-on-year, with the EBITDA margin at 13.1%, an improvement of 50 basis points over quarter two of the financial year 2026, and held at the quarter one level despite a visible steeper cost environment.

items.statement: Quick commerce channel margins higher than general trade due to lower replacement and freight costs
items.quote: For us, margins are better in Q-com because of efficiency that comes in. I think our biggest cost is cost of replacement, which we sell in the market and comes back. I think Q-com as a channel is able to plan procurement far better using technology. So I think that inefficiency brings in a lot of benefit to us. And I think also from a freight perspective, it is better. So, as of now, Q-com is bett

items.statement: Domestic biscuit volume growth 4-5% in Q2; target high single-digit then double-digit
items.quote: On a domestic biscuit side in the quarter two, our volume growth was just about very low single-digit kind of number. It was around, sorry, it is about 4%-5% kind of growth, which was mid-single-digit kind of number on the domestic biscuit side.

items.statement: Bakery (English Oven) volume mid-teens, value high-teens; institutional bakery volume and value mid-to-high teens
items.quote: Even the volumes have grown in mid-teens, and the value has grown in a very high teens, right, for English Oven. Institutional bakery, again, it has grown in volume in a mid to high teens, and so has value grown in mid to high teens in the quarter two over same period last year.

items.statement: Export growth tapered due to Middle East crisis and freight delays; full-year export outlook mid-teens
items.quote: Our outlook for the year still is in mid-teens for exports, right?

items.statement: Premium launches (Zero Maida Pav, peanut butter brownie, sourdough, coconut cream) improving mix
items.quote: English Oven entered the pav segment in Mumbai with Zero Maida Pav and added a peanut butter on-the-go brownie. NaturBaked launched pre-sliced whole wheat sourdough, and Cremica launched coconut cream. These premium launches improved our mix and support profitable growth.

items.statement: Cremica Preferred Outlets contribute 13-14%; target 20%
items.quote: Our focus is also on our bigger outlet, which we call Cremica Preferred Outlet, and they contribute as of now 13%-14%, and we want to take it to 20%.

items.statement: Commodity inflation in edible oils, sugar, cereals; crude at multi-year high pushing freight and packaging costs
items.quote: However, headline consumer inflation rose from around 4.4% in June to 5.5% in September 2026, the highest in nearly two years, driven by edible oils, sugar, and cereals. Crude oil at a multi-year high has also pushed up inflation, freight, and packaging cost.

items.statement: Middle East crisis hit vessel availability and freight rates; FOB booking delays; US market momentum sustained
items.quote: Internationally, shipping conditions became more difficult during the quarter. The West Asia situation sharply impacted vessel availability and freight rates, adding to pressure on margins. Even so, exports continued to grow, and the U.S. market sustained its momentum.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target 14-15% maintained
items.quote: So, I think the 14%-15% EBITDA very much remains as our target to get there, right? The first milestone is always 14% and then move it to 15. So, I think we are very firm and committed as per our plan that we need to move to those EBITDA percentage levels over the next coming years.

items.statement: Reiterated ~20% revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: On this basis, we reiterate our guidance of approximately 20% revenue CAGR over the next three to five years.

items.statement: Order book at ~Rs.18,000 crores providing multi-year revenue visibility
items.quote: Finally, on our outlook, the order book position of around R s.18,000 crores gives us a strong revenue visibility for several years

items.statement: AP waste-to-energy projects capex ~Rs.670-680 crores; contract revenue ~Rs.700 crores over next 2.5 years
items.quote: This would, for example, when we are talking about a Rs.670 crores or a Rs.680 crores of capex for the waste -to-energy projects in AP, you will see at least R s.700 crores of revenue passing through my income statement over the next two and a half years as revenue and a proportionate cost sitting as contract cost in the books of accounts

items.statement: PCMC Moshi WTE facility expected functional by December 2026; processed 33,600 tonnes in Q2
items.quote: We expect the facility to be functional by December 2026.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 17.6% (Rs.58 cr); H1 17.2% (Rs.103 cr); held back by ECL provision and Moshi power loss
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was R s.58 crores, a margin of 17.6%. For the first half, EBITDA was Rs.103 crores, a margin of 17.2

items.statement: Targets core EBITDA margin ~22-23% by Q1 FY28; reported EBITDA softer due to contract revenue
items.quote: So the core EBITDA should go back to our historical trend of around 22%-23% by first quarter of FY 2028 onwards, for sure. But the reported EBITDA will be softer because of the contract revenue component.

items.statement: C&T volumes up 12% YoY to ~0.6 mn tonnes in Q2; total waste handled up 1% to 1.28 mn tonnes
items.quote: C&T volumes for the quarter rose 12% to approximately 0.6 million tonnes.

items.statement: C&D recycling volumes up ~70% YoY; recycling rate 96%; RDF sales up 23% to ~49,000 tonnes in Q2
items.quote: At our construction and demolition recycling facility in Mumbai, processing volumes rose about 70% year-on-year, and the facility achieved a recycling rate of 96%. In resource recovery, RDF sales grew 23% to about 49,000 t onnes in the quarter

items.statement: New private verticals: pest management/deep cleaning with marquee clients; PET bottle collection for leading FMCG in 1 city, adding 3 more; private township waste management deals closing soon
items.quote: In the previous calls, we had explained about our pest management and deep cleaning services that we offer to residential and commercial customers. That business has grown significantly in major parts of the country, including some very marquee clients with whom we have signed-up. Then the second business is the collection and baling of PET bottles for a leading FMCG company. That is something whi

items.statement: DSO 114 days at Sep 2026; collected Rs.108 cr post quarter-end; steady-state DSO 74-80 days; historical range 90-115 days
items.quote: as of September 2026, gross debt stood at approximately R s.449 crores against cash and bank balance of around R s.63 crores. This gives net debt of approximately Rs.386 crores. Net debt-to-equity ratio is 0.4x. Our weighted average cost of debt is about 10%, and day sales outstanding is 114 days

items.statement: Gross debt ~Rs.449 cr; cash ~Rs.63 cr; net debt ~Rs.386 cr; net D/E 0.4x; WACD ~10%
items.quote: as of September 2026, gross debt stood at approximately R s.449 crores against cash and bank balance of around R s.63 crores. This gives net debt of approximately Rs.386 crores. Net debt-to-equity ratio is 0.4x. Our weighted average cost of debt is about 10

items.statement: Finance cost fell due to absence of Rs.6.8 cr refinancing cost incurred in Q1; borrowing cost eased
items.quote: The reason for the fall in finance cost is the Rs.6.8 crores of refinancing cost that was incurred in Q1. That is absent in the Q2 reporting period. Going forward, yes, the interest cost benefit will definitely be seen as the cost of borrowing has eased significantly.

items.statement: C&D recycling full-year revenue expected Rs.34-38 cr; currently processing 450-475 TPD, targeting 500 TPD
items.quote: Going forward for the balance part of the year, we will be closing the C&D volumes at around anywhere between Rs. 34 crores-Rs.38 crores for the full year.

items.statement: AP WTE projects: each ~Rs.70-75 cr annual revenue post-commissioning (~20 months); combined ~Rs.150 cr
items.quote: The Andhra Pradesh contracts will, once commissioned, which is expected in about 20 months from now, each of these two projects will generate a top line of about Rs.70 crores-Rs.75 crores per year. Both put together will be close to Rs.150 crores.

items.statement: Mumbai C&T contract full operationalization from Q4 to add ~Rs.80 cr annual revenue
items.quote: The other key driver which would start from next quarter onwards is after the Mumbai C&T contracts are fully operationalized. That should give a revenue of N.G. Subramanian: Rs.80 odd crores

items.statement: Escalation claims approved for past periods flowed into revenue; Rs.27 cr ECL provision made against related receivables per Ind AS 109
items.quote: During the quarter, the client approved certain past escalation claims, and these flowed into revenue b ecause these claims relate to earlier periods, we have made an expected credit loss provision against the related receivables in line with the Ind AS accounting AS 109 standard

items.statement: BMC rules driving C&D volume growth; Solid Waste Management Rules mandate bulk generators to manage wet waste but they rely on private players
items.quote: Going forward, we expect this to stabilize around 500 tons per day because the rules laid down by BMC is taking control and we see upward trajectory there.

items.statement: Moshi restoration delayed due to Hormuz Strait embargo; parts now airlifted; confident of Dec 2026 restart
