items.quote: The delay was happening because of the Hormuz Strait embargoes, where the ships were not able to come in. Some of the parts were supposed to be coming through that strait, so now we are getting it airlifted. That is why the timelines are getting much more clearer.

items.statement: Exceptional expense Rs.20 cr for Moshi impairment, restoration, compensation; partially insured; survey ongoing; no further incremental expense expected in Q3
items.quote: We are partially covered for a portion of the amount, but as the survey is still going on, that is why for now, using prudent accounting norms, we have taken a hit in the P&L, but we will get some respite from the insurance claims.

items.statement: Started paying dividend in 25th year; no buyback mentioned; focus on growth and attracting quality investors (MIT, JFE)
items.quote: One of the feedback that we got was start paying dividend, which the company, which has completed 25 years, has started paying dividend. This was the first maiden year that we did. We have started doing that.

items.statement: H1 operating cash flow ~Rs.39.6 cr vs revenue Rs.582 cr; receivables Rs.474 cr at Sep 2026 vs Rs.402 cr at Mar 2026
items.quote: see that in first quarter of 2027, sorry, first half of 2027, revenue grew by 15% Y- o-Y to R s.599 crores, but operating cash flow was only around R s.39.6 crores. Also, the receivable increased to R s.474 crores in this second quarter of 2027 from R s.402 crores at FY 2026 year-end

items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth expected for full FY27; Q4 FY27 revenue base ~Rs.290-300 cr for future growth
items.quote: Yes, I think with the kind of projects that we are already executing and the construction revenue that we expect to book from our AP project provides us a canvas to report a double-digit growth for FY 2027.

items.statement: AP WTE contract revenue: Q4 FY27 large number; FY28 lion's share; ~Rs.300 cr in FY28

items.statement: AI cameras deployed to improve conversion; bottom 30% stores moving toward mid-40% conversion; target 1-1.5% annual conversion rate improvement.

items.statement: Competition consolidating: net store openings flat, regional players facing P&L pain; internal data shows quarter-on-quarter consolidation for last two quarters.
items.quote: Our internal data shows a little bit of consolidation from a quarter-on-quarter perspective for the last two quarters now.

items.statement: More than doubled design count over 2.5 years without increasing dead stock via improved inventory replenishment algorithms.
items.quote: We designed our internal systems and processes in a way where, even though we have doubled, rather more than doubled, the number of designs we make over the last two and a half years, we still will not generate any more dead stock.

items.statement: Mohey revenue salience just above double digits (~10-11%); area salience slightly higher; 6-7 exclusive Mohey EBOs.
items.quote: It is just above double digits now. It just touched double digits, broadly.

items.statement: No active M&A pipeline; open to opportunities in Indian wear segment; working with external partners and planning internal M&A team; synergy from dead stock reduction capability.
items.quote: Again, right now, there is nothing active in the pipeline. However, given that we're a cash-rich company, and fundamentally, our biggest moat is we can reduce dead stock in any company that we acquire, potentially. That gives us a very big synergy from a long-term angle.

items.statement: Key near-term challenge is new customer acquisition; confident marketing, product, competition consolidation and economy will drive future growth.
items.quote: The major challenge right now that we face is to grow from a new customer build point of view, and we feel with the efforts we are taking, consolidating competition, and hopefully the Indian economy doing even better from here, will gear us up for the incredible growth that the company can do and has the potential to do in the future.

items.statement: Other current assets rose to INR256 cr from INR56 cr due to mutual fund liquid redemption received in bank on Oct 1, 2026 (recorded as financial asset on Sep 30).

It is actually a bank balance only, because the funds we received in the bank account on October 1, that is why we have not included in the cash in bank, and rather we have the financial asset, for which we have included a note also in the results page in the last page.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin target of 17%

items.quote: So for the non-lighting, the working capital in terms of mmber of days, we can consider anywhere between 75 to 90 days

items.quote: electronic components, aluminum, plastic, that isit. Rest everything we do oursclves. Sanjeet Singh: So plastic in the raw form like the granules and the metal also, everything to do with metal, we have the complete capability in-house. So the processing of all metals, whether if's iron, aluminum, all of that is done in-house. Plastic, whether it is extrusion, co-extrusion, injection molding, all

items.statement: Middle East export revenue grew 70-80% QoQ from Q1 to Q2 FY27 despite geopolitical tensions
items.quote: And in fact, even with all the geopolitical tensions and the tensions in the Gulf, we were still able to record very good growth Q-on-Q in the Middle East, which was close to around 70%-80% from Q1 to Q2.

items.statement: EMS facility: 20-25% captive consumption, rest for external customers; targeting niche categories with design services
items.quote: But the new EMS facility that we have sct up, that, like I said, a small part of that, or maybe around 20% to 30% of that, 20%-25% of that is being used for captive consumption, and rest we are doing for other customers

items.statement: Automotive lighting: IKIO makes LED light source (lamp/driver) in-house; peers assemble complete headlamps/tail lamps; IKIO first in India at this scale for source manufacturing
items.quote: We make the source, they make the complete like, they make the complete headlamp or something like that, but the source inside, they were 100% of the Indian companics were importing from outside India, but we are the first one to make the source in India because of our expertise in drivers and LEDs

items.statement: Home lighting ODM: transitioned from single customer to multiple brands; product range expanding with new customers
items.quote: What we have done is we have onboarded newer customers, because, as you must be aware that carlier we just had one single customer, and that too they developed a JV for their home lighting category. So in order to make sure that we are able to make that business sustainable, we've been adding more customers, and that is something that will continue to happen

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Gulf, policy/duty changes) noted as risk; management keeping fingers crossed for no escalation
items.quote: m sure there are a lot of geopolitical factors and, now, I would say world is not the same as it used to be. So we are just keeping our fingers crossed that nothing really should

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 612 crores, up 39-40% year-on-year from INR 414-441 crores
items.quote: Having said that, as on date, our order book stands strong at INR 612 crores.

items.statement: Order book split is 22% railway and 78% infrastructure; target is 50-50 split
items.quote: The diversification, we've been able to actually carve this out where the railway orders are at 22% and 78%.

items.statement: Received new railway order last month converting old orders with 30% option clause on 2022-23 order worth INR 9,000-10,000 crore for 10,000 wagons
items.quote: Last month, the end of last month, we got a new order, which is converting the old orders and also getting a 30% option clause on the existing order that came out in 2022-'23. That was to the tune of almost INR 9,000 crore, INR 10,000 wagons.

items.statement: Total installed capacity 1,33,600 metric tons; standalone Cosmic CRF 55,000 MT, NS Engineering 65,000 MT, Cosmic Springs 13,600 MT (rising to 24,000-25,000 MT by FY27 end)
items.quote: We have a total installed capacity of 1,33,600 metric tons. Along with that, this standalone capacity is 55,000 thousand metric tons. The installed capacity standalone for NS Engineering Project Private Limited, which is our infra piece, is 65,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: Forging unit commercial production expected by April-May 2027 (Q1 FY28); delayed 2-2.5 months due to unseasonal rainfall
items.quote: We will complete the set up and build up probably by March on maximum. We've been delayed by two, two and a half months, and that's only because of the rainfalls.

items.statement: Without Amzen, revenue potential INR 1,178 crores at 80% capacity (Cosmic CRF INR 448 cr, NS Engineering INR 476 cr, Springs INR 136 cr, Forging INR 118 cr); could reach INR 1,200-1,300 cr, floor INR 1,150-1,160 cr; PAT margin 12-14%+
items.quote: Total will stand at INR 1,178 crores. If you ask me, it can shoot up to INR 1200 crores to INR 1300 crores. It cannot come down, it cannot reach INR 1000 crores. It cannot cross, it can't go down below INR 1150 crores to INR 1160 crores.

items.statement: Total installed capacity target 1,74,600 MT (from 1,33,600 MT) without Amzen; operating at 85% efficiency
items.quote: The total quantity today on the installed strength is 1,33,600, which we will jump to 1,74,600.

items.statement: Amzen installed capacity 3,600 wagons (RDSO assessed), scalable to 7,200 wagons; adds 1,50,000 MT standalone capacity
items.quote: Like Amzen, the installed capacity in Amzen stands at 3,600 wagons. It has been assessed by the RDSO. If you ask me, it can scale up to 7,200 wagons.

items.statement: Amzen acquisition: paid INR 32 cr upfront + INR 28 cr security deposit; NCLT approval procedural; team of 12 (6 ex-Amzen) working on-site for 1.5 months on refurbishment of 392 machines
items.quote: We have paid INR 32 crores as an upfront payment and INR28 crores as the security deposit, which will go as a payment once we make the rest of the payment.

items.statement: Amzen refurbishment: 392 machines under one roof vs 172 total across Cosmic CRF group; AMCs, transformer refurbishment, 5-axis machines, civil works underway
items.quote: In CRF with all its Cosmic CRF and subsidiaries, with all its subsidiaries and four locations, we have a total of 172 machines in totality. And this has 392 machines under one roof.

items.statement: Amzen commercial production expected to start April-May 2027 (Q1 FY28); full ramp-up within 6 months of plant access; cost analysis complete by Dec 2026
items.quote: By December end, we will be done with our analysis. We must have started our transformers as well as some couple of the CNC machines. The civil work will start off. From there, three to four months at best, you start off your commercial production.

items.statement: Expanding into containers (20ft/40ft via Amzen license), defence (R&D with DRDO/OEMs), bridge girders, loco shells, sheet piles (target 32% market share from 22%), trench boxes
items.quote: The container business is something that we're walking into. Amzen at large has a container business and a container license in its forehead for 20 feet and 40 feet.

items.statement: Railway demand slowed due to West Asian crisis, fiscal deficits, delayed government spending; wagon sector waiting for orders; infrastructure provides fungible strength
items.quote: We've seen the West Asian crisis happen. We've seen a lot of movement around the tariffs that has actually hindered the fiscal investments that has been promised by the central government, by the state governments.

items.statement: India needs 8 lakh wagons (Rail Plan 2031/33); currently 4.12 lakh on tracks (2 lakh in repairs); capacity gap: need 60,000-70,000 wagons/year vs industry capacity 32,000-33,000 at 85-90% utilization
items.quote: Rail plan 2031 and then 2030, 2031, and 2033 always said that India needs 8-odd-lakh wagons. We today, as we speak, we have 4,12,000 wagons running on the tracks.

items.statement: Galvanizing facility (12,000 MT with air wiping) adds 10.5-12% to infra top line and 1.5% to PAT
items.quote: This galvanizing strength adds and allows us to build on our top lines as well as bottom lines in the in fra piece to the tune of almost 10.5% to 12% of the top line and almost 1.5% on the PAT levels

items.statement: Forging business at RDSO/STR level yields 15-20% margins vs 5-7% in retail market; limited applicable participants create pricing power
items.quote: The moment you start to talk about only RDS O or STR-based limited applicable participants who are supplying these items, you're talking about 15% to 20% not in part limits.

items.statement: Carrying high stock and advances to creditors/debtors; finalizing rates post-Diwali; capacity utilization 78.6% (vs 80%+ last year) due to forward orders not yet booked
items.quote: The capacity utilization has been 78.6%. Why is that so? And last year, it was almost 80%-odd in totality. And this year also, we will cross 80%-odd in totality because we are carrying a lot of stock.

items.statement: India announced INR 10,000 crore subsidy/support fund for container builders; aligns with Amzen's intrinsic container license
items.quote: I think India shot out the policy of putting out INR 10,000 crores as subsidy and as a support fund to the builders of containers.

items.statement: Legal costs elevated in H1 FY27 due to Supreme Court hearings after NCLAT loss in March 2027; H2 FY27 legal costs to be much lower
items.quote: We had lost the case in the NCLAT in 2027 March. We won this back in Supreme Court only after the first quarter started. So actually, the Supreme Court cost one hearing of Supreme Court with the kind of foray of lawyers that we h ad to set up and the kind of intrinsic value that we had to create on our depositions was a very costly expenditure.

items.statement: Amzen refurbishment team of 12 (6 were involved in original Amzen setup 2012-14; experience from Titagarh, Jupiter, Texmaco) working on-site with COC/RP permission
items.quote: My team of almost 10 to 12 odd people, out of which 6 people of the 12 people team, are the guys who probably were involved with Amzen when it was being set up with its ex -promoter back in 2012 and '13 and '14.

items.statement: Over 3,000 SKUs; fungible manufacturing across CRF, springs, forgings, galvanizing, sheet piles, crash barriers, lighting poles, fabricated steel
items.quote: Today, we have more than 3,000 odd SKUs, and more than that, we have today the strength to switch and manufacture anything that we want under the sun if we get the designs.

items.statement: Preferred customer status via one-stop solution: NS Engineering, springs, forgings, CRF, body parts, specialized steel manufacturing for rail and infra
items.quote: Preferred customer point stands on a level where we talk about, if there is a value added ready to deploy products, so basically with NS Engineering, with springs, with forgings, as well as with CRF and body part building, specialized steel manufacturing, we supply and we are in a position to give them a one-stop solution.

items.statement: Component manufacturer becoming integrated wagon builder unprecedented in 100+ years of Indian wagon industry; 135% CAGR in capacity over 3 years (12,000 to 1,33,600 MT)
items.quote: I personally believe starting from a component manufacturing to jumping into, viewing yourself as an integrated wagon builder is a dream come true. It has not happened in the Indian market ever since the wagon industry in individual strength or in private sectors existed, and that's, I'm talking about almost like in a hundred odd years.

items.statement: H1 typically weaker due to government budget cycle; Q3-Q4 stronger as orders finalize and price escalation kicks in; H1 FY27 standalone revenue INR 151 cr vs INR 161 cr YoY but consolidated grew
items.quote: Last year to this year, we've dropped a little bit on the top lines in terms of our standalone, starting from INR 161 crores last year to INR 151 crores this year. But in totality, if you see, first year, H1 FY26 to H1 FY27, we've grown.

items.statement: Galvanizing capacity increased from 8,500 MT to 12,000 MT; air wiping facility to be announced by end of month (Nov 2026)
items.quote: The galvanizing that we had had a strength of 8,500 metric tons. We took it to 12,000 tons last year. This year, we've been able to add air wiping facility, which is still in the making, probably by the end of this month, we will be announcing the air wiping facility.

items.statement: Steel pricing at base case; General Steel Limited (GSL) supplying only 10-20% of 500,000-1,000,000 MT potential to railways; prices expected to rise
items.quote: If you ask me individually, personally, the price will only rise from here, because we have touched the base case position in the pricing of steel, in the price of supplies, in the position of supplies, in the demands, in all of it.

items.statement: Amzen acquisition funded internally; paying COC only when certain; legal delay not adverse as refurbishment proceeds in parallel
items.quote: We are ready with the amount in our own ways, but we will end up paying only when we are completely certain that this is good to go now. And that is a month, month and a half from now.

items.statement: Defence sector entry: R&D in-house and with OEMs; engaging DRDO officials; forging capability critical for one-stop solution requirement
items.quote: The defence sector is something that we are very strongly looking at. We are doing a lot of R&D back in the time, and also in -house, as well as we've also given this R&D business and the job to a lot of OEMs.

items.statement: Liquid metal units planned post-Amzen operationalization; on management's mind for 1.5-2 years
items.quote: Liquid metal units have been spoken about over the last two years -- last one and a half years actually. This is something that is on my mind, and we will touch base with this as soon as Amzen is completely taken over.

items.statement: Mainboard migration mentioned but not detailed; expected to be addressed
items.quote: Now, I'll link this answer to the question that you had on the first thing, which is the main board. Why did I mention the main board? Because I knew somebody would ask me this question.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 20-25% over last year for FY27
items.quote: we are still hopeful and very, very positive about achieving 20%, 25% on top of last year.

items.statement: Spring division PAT margin expected at 15% on INR 140-150 crore turnover
items.quote: In totality, we're looking at 15% easy. So when you talk about a total turnover of, like I said, in that sheet, almost INR 140 crores odd, INR 140 crores to INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Forging division PAT margin expected at 14-15% on INR 115-120 crore turnover
items.quote: Though forging will have a turnover of INR 115 crores to INR 120 crores, INR 20 crores shy of the spring section, but the margins will be pretty much 14% to 15% again, in terms of PAT.

items.statement: Amzen plant commercial production expected to start April-May 2027 (Q1 FY28) after refurbishment
items.quote: So if you ask me, I would say a layman's answer would be forging and Amzen, we would want to start productions, not in full go, but in the first trend to go by the month of April and May.

items.statement: Two wagon orders bagged, awaiting DM clearance before announcement
items.quote: We already have bagged two orders. Till such time, we don't get a clearance on the DM of the orders, we cannot post it.

items.statement: Amzen plant refurbishment analysis by December 2026, civil work and machine commissioning over 3-4 months
items.quote: By December end, we will be done with our analysis. We must have started our transformers as well as some couple of the CNC machines. The civil work will start off.

items.statement: Consolidated operating cash flow turned positive INR 18 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR 3 crore FY26; standalone INR 9-10 crore
items.quote: last year is the first year when we converted assets from a INR 78 crore minus operational cash flow to INR 3 crore positive cash flow. And this year in consolidated books, we've crossed INR 18 crores of positive cash flow.

items.statement: Promoter commits to no equity dilution for capital raise until FY28; past dilution was for warrant/swap settlements
items.quote: I had stated and I have still said that we will not dilute equity till FY28 for raise of capital.

items.statement: Container manufacturing promotion scheme INR 10,000 crore; indigenous demand expected 5x from 1 lakh to 5 lakh containers
items.quote: the requirement of containers is going to shoot up from 1 lakh indigenously to almost 5 lakh containers, which is 5x in terms of expansion.

items.statement: Supplying springs to all listed wagon manufacturers; two orders bagged awaiting DM clearance
items.quote: We supply to all of them. We supply to all of them. We already have bagged two orders.

items.statement: 12-person team stationed at Amzen plant in Jalandhar/Ludhiana for refurbishment; promoter visiting twice monthly
items.quote: base in Jalandhar, Ludhiana, in that stretch where we've taken a guest house and we've kept 12 people there. So even when I go once a month, like once in two weeks, so I'm going twice a month right now over the last one, two months

items.statement: Family office warrants and share allotments to account holders completed; AVP Endeavour swap pending BSE approval
items.quote: We have already got the listing approvals of the warrants that we had done from the family office, as well as from the share that was allotted to all the account holders. And the swap is now pending in the BSE.

items.statement: Promoter commits to continued video conference earnings calls; transparency emphasized
items.quote: I will always be there on video conferencing, I promise you till I'm not in a state to come in front of you, probably for any health reason or anything of that sort, God forbid.

items.quote: Our existing organic plan of 30% revenue growth, on a y-o-y basis, is easily visible for the next three to four years on the existing plan before the Advent deal.

items.statement: Target to build 7,000-8,000 bed franchise over next 3-5 years with Advent partnership
items.quote: With Advent as a partner, we now aim to build a larger franchise of 7,000 to 8,000 beds over the next three to five years.

items.statement: Advent investment of INR3,150 crores in two tranches: INR1,750 crores after CCI approval this month, balance after 15-18 months based on conditions
items.quote: The Advent money of INR3,150 crores will come in two tranches. The first tranche will be INR1,750 crores, which will be received after the CCI approval this month. And the next tranche will be received after 15 to 18 months based on certain conditions.

items.statement: Organic plan to reach 5,000 beds in 3-4 years; additional 2,000-3,000 beds from Advent capital in ~4 years; 40-50% of Advent beds may go live next financial year
items.quote: On our existing organic plan, we had announced going to 5,000 bed capacity, close to three to four years going forward. That remains the same. On top of that, around 2,000 to 3,000 beds we expect to add because of this recent deal, again, in close to four years going forward.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR4,314 million (52% YoY, 10% QoQ); H1 FY27 revenue INR8,241 million (52% YoY)
items.quote: The group delivered its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR4,314 million in quarter 2 FY27, representing growth of 52% year-on-year and 10% sequentially. Revenue for H1 FY27 stood at INR8,241 million, up 52% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA INR1,020 million (50% YoY, 11% QoQ); EBITDA margin 23.6%; adjusted EBITDA margin excluding ramp-up losses 28%
items.quote: Quarter 2 EBITDA was a record INR1,020 million, increasing 50% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA margin improved to 23.6% as the newer hospitals are now running profitably. Excluding the ramp-up losses at New Delhi and Faridabad Sector-20, our adjusted EBITDA margin was healthy at 28%.

items.statement: Existing hospitals (Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, Jhansi-Orchha) EBITDA margin upwards of 28%
items.quote: Our existing hospitals at Noida, Greater Noida, Noida Extension, and Jhansi-Orchha continue to deliver sustained performance with 24% year-on-year revenue growth. These have been true contributors to our profitability, with an EBITDA margin upwards of 28% for these specific hospitals.

items.statement: Cancer drug price caps (30% margin cap) reduce EBITDA by ~0.3%; company has strategies to compensate via operational efficiencies
items.quote: We have calculated that, for the existing list of cancer drugs where margins are capped at 30%, the overall impact on our EBITDA numbers is a reduction of around 0.3% because of that specific pricing on oncology drugs.

items.statement: Group ARPOB rose 11% YoY to ~INR36,000; Noida Extension ~INR51,000, Delhi ~INR47,000, Greater Noida ~INR43,000, Faridabad Sector-20 ~INR37,000, Noida ~INR37,000, Greater Faridabad ~INR33,000, Agra ~INR33,000, Jhansi ~INR14,000
items.quote: Group ARPOB reached an all-time high of INR36,000, up 11% year-on-year. Noida Extension and New Delhi reported an ARPOB of approximately INR50,000, Greater Noida approximately INR43,000, Faridabad at INR40,000, Noida INR37,000, Greater Faridabad INR35,000, and Agra at INR33,000.

items.statement: Payer mix: government 34% (down from 37% last quarter), private insurance and cash roughly equal with insurance slightly higher, international 4-5%; newer hospitals government mix 15-20%
items.quote: So payer mix for this quarter is close to 34%, which is down a few percent from the last quarter. Aryan Jain: That is the government institution business? Yatharth Tyagi: That is the government institution business, and the rest is equally divided between private insurance and cash patients, with private insurance having a few percentage points more than the cash business. The international busine

items.statement: Faridabad Sector-20 oncology: medical/surgical live, radiation/nuclear starting in 45-60 days; Model Town: medical/surgical started, radiation oncology in 8-9 months; Greater Noida adding nuclear/radiation oncology soon
items.quote: Faridabad, I think everything is done now. The equipment has already been installed. Now it's in some formalities with the AERB test every 40, 45 days. So we are in the last leg of these things. The clinical manpower is already on the rolls, right? So we think that in the next 45 to 60 days, we will have the entire spectrum of onco.

items.statement: Peak debt reached; additions from Gurugram facility (INR100 cr) and medical equipment (INR100 cr+); debt expected to decline from here; Advent funds may also be used to reduce debt if acquisitions delayed
items.quote: But we feel that this is the peak level of debt for us, at least for the next few quarters to come. Debt will eventually go down from here. We also feel that going forward, even though the full focus is on acquiring new hospitals with the Advent money, if the acquisitions take time as far as certain assets are concerned, we can also look to reduce debt marginally from that amount.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating cash flow INR1,113 million (49% YoY); cash and bank balances INR4,289 million; net debt INR392 million as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Our operating cash flow during H1 was INR1,113 million, an increase of 49% year-on-year. As of September 30, 2026, the cash and bank balances stood at INR4,289 million, and net debt stood at INR392 million.

items.statement: OCF/EBITDA conversion dipped in H1 due to seasonal collections; expect >70% conversion for full year
items.quote: Surya, normally the collection in H1 is lower than the full year collection. That is why you would see a slight dip in the OCF conversion rate. But at the end of the year, we should expect upwards of 70% conversion.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Advent International for INR3,150 crores primary capital via preferential issue of equity shares and warrants; awaiting regulatory approvals (CCI final stages, expected post-Diwali this month)
items.quote: We have entered into a strategic partnership with Advent International for a primary capital investment of INR3,150 crores through a preferential issue of equity shares and warrants. The transaction is awaiting necessary regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy: primarily 100% equity-owned assets, focusing on EBITDA-positive hospitals with upside potential; targeting chains in North India; may consider O&M for standalone hospitals in organic plan
items.quote: Yes, I think it would be a mix of both, but primarily they would be 100% equity-owned assets. Because with the large capital we have to deploy now, we can look at larger chains of hospitals. There are a few chains of hospitals available within the North market itself that we are carefully evaluating.

items.statement: Acquisition criteria: hospitals with good upside potential, ARPOB higher than group average, payer mix with more cash/private insurance than platform; premium paid based on growth percentage and quality metrics
items.quote: For us, the way we look at it is, if a hospital has good upside potential from where it is and if we can really expand it, that is the biggest criterion. For that too, the premium really depends upon the percentage of growth that is possible for a hospital.

items.statement: IT matter resolved; final demand received; assets and FDs released; appealing to significantly reduce demand; expect reduction in coming quarters
items.quote: I think as we said that the IT matter has been resolved, and then we have received the final demand… Akshat Mehta: Okay. Yatharth Tyagi: As we were saying, the final demand has come and the matter is resolved now. There has been no -- earlier, all the assets and FDs were also released for the company. Going forward, we feel

items.statement: Supreme Court may extend drug price caps beyond oncology; industry made representations; company will evolve strategies to maintain EBITDA guidance regardless of regulatory changes
items.quote: See, we have always, as an organization, tried to restructure and evolve our strategies according to regulatory policies and new framework. Just like in oncology, yes, there was a marginal and a small impact for us, but that impact was not high. But even then, we have already worked on certain other line items and operational efficiencies so that our EBITDA target guidance doesn't change.

items.statement: Hired star doctors for oncology at Model Town; sufficient clinical talent pool across 8 hospitals; new hospitals in region attract more talent
items.quote: However, we've already started medical and surgical oncology in Model Town, and recently we've hired certain star doctors as far as oncology for those specialties is concerned, and we have already started seeing good numbers.

items.statement: Agra hospital: added CTVS and cardiac surgery, planning pediatric cardiac, strengthening specialties, robotics at par with NCR hospitals; renovating facility and adding beds
items.quote: We recently added CTVS surgery and cardiac surgery. We recently -- we are planning to add paediatric cardiac as well. We are also strengthening a couple of the specialties which we felt were not up to the mark. That's happening, and as I just said, robotics is happening there.

items.statement: Noida, Greater Faridabad, Jhansi: no brownfield expansion scope; focusing on ARPOB and payer mix improvement
items.quote: There is not much scope for expansion in those three hospitals. However, we are looking to improve marginally as far as ARPOB and payer mix are concerned in those hospitals. But there are no specific plans for any brownfield capacity expansion in those hospitals.

items.statement: Model Town Delhi: Q1 loss INR55M, Q2 loss INR38M, expected breakeven in December (Q3)
items.quote: If you see, losses of Model Town have reduced quarter-on-quarter. For Q1, losses were INR55 million. This quarter we reported losses of INR38 million. Next quarter, we are very sure that December will be the break-even month for the Delhi hospital.

items.statement: Faridabad Sector-20: Q2 revenue ~INR40 cr, EBITDA positive, >80% cash/private insurance, ARPOB ~INR40,000
items.quote: Faridabad Sector-20 shows what our acquisition and turnaround playbook can deliver. The hospital has turned EBITDA positive in record time and generated revenue of approximately INR40 crores in the last quarter. More than 80% of its business comes from cash and private insurance patients, with ARPOB of approximately INR40,000.

items.statement: Profit after tax Q2 FY27 INR485M (17% YoY), H1 INR939M; cash profit up 36% YoY
items.quote: Profit after tax stood at INR485 million for quarter 2, up 17% year-on-year, and INR939 million for H1. However, cash profit, which adds back the impact of depreciation to the PAT, actually increased 36% year-on-year.

items.statement: Management expects a bumper Q3 with consumers back to shopping in October
items.quote: But having said that, in October we have seen that the consumers are back, they are back to shopping, the numbers are looking good. We are hoping to have a bumper Q3.

items.statement: Gross margin rose to 45.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 204 bps to 18.9% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Gross profit grew 15.7% year -on-year, and gross margin rose to 45.4%. EBITDA increased 8.2% to INR89 crores, with EBITDA margin expanding by 204 basis points to 18.9%.

items.statement: Diwali shifted 19 days later this year extending lean period and reducing peak season by 19 days
items.quote: If you see in comparison to last year, Diwali has shifted by 19 days. What that actually means is your lean period has extended 19 days, and your peak season has reduced by 19 days.

items.statement: Added 49 EBOs and 5 shop-in-shops in Q2 taking total network to 756 stores across 369 cities
items.quote: During Q2, we added 49 EBOs and five shop-in-shops, taking the network to 756 stores across 369 cities.

items.statement: Footwear accounted for 63% of Q2 revenue with apparel and accessories making up the balance
items.quote: Footwear remains at the heart of the business, accounting for 63% of Q2 revenue. Alongside it, we continue to build our apparel and accessories business.

items.statement: Online sales reached 31% of revenue in Q2 vs 22% in Q1; brand website sales grew to INR 31.9 cr from INR 3.9 cr YoY
items.quote: Online sales accounted for around 31% of revenue, compared with around 22% in Q1. This was closer to our historical channel mix, with a more balanced contribution from our physical and online channels.

items.statement: Retail business growing at high single-digit SSSG supporting margin improvement
items.quote: What we have also seen that retail is growing in a high single-digit SSSG. In that manner, because the cost remains fixed, the expenses remain fixed, if we get a good high single-digit SSSG in our retail business, that helps us gain more mileage, and gives us more momentum to post higher profit margin.

items.statement: Franchise model keeps retail expansion capital-light as franchisee invests in capex
items.quote: There is a second model, which is the franchise model, wherein the franchisee invests everything, and he invests in the capex. He gives us a security deposit, and we give him stocks.

items.statement: Footwear drops monthly; apparel has 3.5 drops per year (2 summer, 1 winter)
items.quote: Footwear drops happen almost every month. For apparels in summers, we have almost two drops. And in winter, obviously, because of the shorter period, we have only one drop. That is how it works. Basically, you can say that for apparel, there are three and a half drops a year. But footwear, we have something new coming in every month.

items.statement: Design team of 18-19 designers from NIFT and other institutions based at Noida corporate office
items.quote: We have a mix of almost 18-19 designers who have passed out of NIFT or other institutions, which are based out of our corporate office in Noida. We have a complete design merchandising and buying team.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target ~15% and EBITDA margin 11-12%
items.quote: For FY27, our objective remains to deliver approximately 15% revenue growth and improve EBITDA margins towards 11% to 12%.

items.statement: H2 FY27 EBITDA expected around Rs 45 crore
items.quote: It's around 45 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at Rs 20-25 crore, down from Rs 90 crore in FY26
items.quote: FY27 CAPEX is planned at approximately 20 to 25 crores, down from about 90 crores in FY26, primarily towards the catch expansion and deployed in line with actual demand.

items.statement: Kutch expansion of 10,000 IBCs/month expected commissioning by March 2027
items.quote: We are investing about 20 to 25 crores in a new facility with a capacity of about 10,000 IBCs per month, which is expected to be commissioned by March 2027.

items.statement: Wada facility utilization expected to reach ~80% in FY27
items.quote: We expect overall utilization to reach around 80% during this financial year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 installed capacity ~20,993 MT, utilization ~70%
items.quote: Installed production capacity for the quarter was around 20,993 metric tons, and volume rose to around 14,798 metric tons, taking capacity utilization to around 70%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 volume 14,798 MT, up 21% YoY and 14% QoQ; H1 volume 27,789 MT
items.quote: Volume rose to around 14,798 metric tons, taking capacity utilization to around 70%, up from 62% in Q1 FY27 to 62% in Q2 FY26. volumes grew 21% year-on-year and 14% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Average realization Rs 1.61 lakh/ton, up 22% YoY; raw material cost pass-through maintained
items.quote: Average realization was about 1.61 lakh per ton, up by 22% year-on-year basis. reflecting our pricing, product mix, and the pass-through of raw material cost to the customers.

items.statement: Gross margin steady at 23% as raw metal cost rose in step with price increases
items.quote: Gross profit rose about 28% year on year, 55.3 crore. while gross margin remained at 23% as raw metal cost rose in step with price increases.

items.statement: Value-added IBC business contributed ~32% of Q2 FY27 revenue
items.quote: Our value-added IBC business contributed about 32% of the revenue in this quarter Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Customer base diversified: top customer 6% of revenue, top 10 ~29%
items.quote: Our customer base remains well diversified with over 500 customers. Our top customer accounts for about 6% of the revenue and our top 10 customers together for about 29%.

items.statement: Solar capacity 14.25 MW; H1 FY27 savings Rs 3.89 crore; full-year expected ~Rs 15 crore
items.quote: We have achieved approximately 3.89 crore of savings in this half year financial year 2027. And the full 14.25-megawatt capacity is expected to deliver around 15 crores for annual savings.

items.statement: Recycling plant commissioned Oct 2025; Q2 FY27 EBITDA Rs 33 lakh; FY27 estimate Rs 2 crore
items.quote: The plant generated 33 lakhs of EBITDA in Q2 FY27 and we estimate its FY27 EBITDA contribution at around 2 crores.

items.statement: Government subsidy approvals: Wada Rs 24.9 cr over 10 years, Bharuch Rs 10.5 cr; Wada sanction expected by March 2027
items.quote: We have also received government subsidy approvals for our WADA and BHARUCH facilities, amounting to approximately 35 crores in total, 24.9 crore for WADA over 10 years and 10.5 crore for BHARUCH.

items.statement: H1 cash flow negative due to higher debtors (Rs 23 cr to Rs 33 cr) and shift to 80% local procurement
items.value: Debtors Rs 23 cr to Rs 33 cr
items.quote: Since the Hormuz issue started, we are not importing. So, the total purchase has been converted to 80% local. plus the sale has increased, so the debtors have also increased. In the last 6 months, I had a sale of 324 crores and now I have a sale of 60 crores. So if you look at my creditors, they have decreased from 23 crores to 23 crores.Debtors have increased from 23 crores to 33 crores.

items.statement: Advance tax paid in H1 FY27: Rs 3.75 crore
items.quote: Okay, I will tell you that. 3.75 crores in total. Before that it was 1.5.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton Rs 13,718 in Q2 FY27, up 33% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA per ton was approximately 13,718 in Q2 FY27, up by 33% from 10,326 in Q2 FY26, and from 10,082 in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Transportation cost increase due to long-distance dispatches; Kutch expansion planned to mitigate
items.quote: The Rs. 2 that you can see, sir, that has increased because of the transport cost. When we were supplying locally, it came down that much. But when it is a long-distance vehicle, from here to the south. So, the idea is that is why we are planning the Kutch expansion so we can be closer to customers and save on transportation costs, benefiting the company.

items.statement: Remaining 1 MW solar plant installation and pre-charging done; expected commissioning by next month
items.quote: Installation and pre-charging are done, so hopefully by next month we should start getting that benefit as well.

items.statement: Paint industry machine running full-fledged; delivered Rs 70 lakh revenue in first month (Oct)
items.quote: It is running full-fledged. It started commercial production in October and delivered around ₹70 lakh of revenue in its very first month.

items.statement: Solar savings achievement at 80-90% of plan
items.quote: Almost. We have achieved 90%. Not 100% but we are achieving 80%. Yes, sir.

items.statement: Same-store revenue growth guidance maintained at 9-11% long-term
items.quote: Since we met some of you prior to our IPO, which is May of 2023, we have remained consistent on saying 9% to 11% is same-store hotel growth.

items.statement: Same-store total revenue growth expected at 13-14% for H2 FY27
items.quote: So my sense is we should model the total revenue growth to be also in the ZIP code of about, I would say, 13%, 14% for same-store.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA target of 2.5x expected within 18 months
items.quote: We do think that the path from current 3x or, let's say, 2.9x going to 2.5x is another, I would say on a conservative side, 18 months.

items.statement: W Hyderabad expected to open in Q2 FY28
items.quote: We remain on track to open in Q2 FY28.

items.statement: W Hyderabad expected to add ~10% to FY27 income base at above-portfolio margins on stabilized basis
items.quote: On a stabilized basis, we expect it to add about 10% to our FY27 income base at margins above our portfolio average given our existing Marriott clustering in Hyderabad and no impact of GST regulation change.

items.statement: RARE India expected to generate INR 15-20 crores top line in FY28
items.quote: We think we should get to about INRIS crores to INR20 crores of top line in the next fiscal year, which is almost, interestingly, half a tum of our total investment in a single year.

items.statement: Navi Mumbai project capex guided at INR 900-1,000 crores, construction start early FY28
items.quote: In terms of capex, we've always guided the capex to be in the ZIP code of about INR900-odd crores to INR1,000 crores. We are in line with that. We do expect to be on ground in terms of starting the work probably carly in fiscal year 2028.

items.statement: Sriperumbudur Marriott capex ~INR 160 crores, yield on cost 15-17%
items.quote: We expect the capex to be in the ZIP code of about INR160-0dd crores plus/minus. And with that, we expect the total yicld on cost to be in the ZIP code of approximately 17%. Yes, about 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Net debt to remain in INR 1,450-1,500 crores range with quarterly +/- INR 100 cr fluctuation
items.quote: Our net debt is circa around INR1,450 crores -INR1,500 crores. Tt will remain in that ZIP code, Viraj, but please be patient and consider it that it may shift by INR100 crores plus/minus in quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Domestic travelers drove 80% of room nights; office absorption in Bangalore and Hyderabad surged to 7.9M sq ft in Q2 FY27
items.quote: About 80% of the room nights we sold this quarter were to domestic travelers. Much of that demand is created locally by the offices, GCCs, and industrial parks around our hotels. The offices in Bangalore and Hyderabad, our 2 largest markets, together absorbed about 7.9 million square fect of office space on a net basis this quarter alone against 5.1 million square fect a year ago.

items.statement: Hyderabad net office absorption more than doubled to 3.8M sq ft in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Hyderabad alone more than doubled, from 1.6 million to 3.8 million square fect of net absorption in the quarter.

items.statement: Upscale hotels delivered ~800 bps higher EBITDA margin than broader portfolio in last 6 months
items.quote: if you sce the last 6 months, the EBITDA performance of our upscale hotel was almost 800 basis points ahead of the broader portfolio.

items.statement: Expect reported EBITDA growth in high teens from Q3 FY27 as GST impact normalizes
items.quote: From quarter 3 onwards, there is no comparable because we have impact in both years. So we will go back to reporting the right EBITDA growth will be in high teens, honestly.

items.statement: Secured pipeline adds 1,670 rooms and 473 rooms rebranding; upper/upper-upscale share to rise from 42% to 60% by FY30
items.quote: Our secured pipeline adds about 1,670 rooms and moves another 473 rooms up market through rebranding. By FY30, we expect upper and upper upscale to rise from 42% of our income to about 60%.

items.statement: CWIP increased to INR 219 crores from INR 139 crores in March 2026, primarily for W Hyderabad and Westin Bangalore
items.quote: Capital work in progress increased to INR219 crores from INR139 crores in March, primarily reflecting ongoing investment in W Hyderabad and the Westin in Bangalore.

items.statement: Free cash flow Q2 FY27 ~INR 53 crores after INR 35 crores cash interest
items.quote: Free cash from the quarter was approximately INRS3 crorcs afier the cash interest payment of INR3S crores.

items.statement: Credit rating A+; effective interest rate ~7.8%, ~300 bps lower than at IPO
items.quote: Our credit rating remains strong at A+ Our effective interest rate is approximately 7.8%, which is around 300 basis points lower than at the time of our IPO.

items.statement: Finance cost declined 10.3% YoY to INR 38.3 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The finance cost declined by 10.3% year-on-year to INR38.3 crores, reflecting lower interest costs and improved eredit profile.

items.statement: Upper/upper-upscale share to rise from 42% to 60% of income by FY30 via pipeline and rebranding
items.quote: By FY30, we expect upper and upper upscale to rise from 42% of our income to about 60%.

items.statement: Domestic travelers 80% of room nights; demand driven by offices, GCCs, industrial parks near hotels
items.quote: About 80% of the room nights we sold this quarter were to domestic travelers. Much of that demand is created locally by the offices, GCCs, and industrial parks around our hotels.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR 279 crores at end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: The cash and cash cquivalents stood at INR279 crores at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: Exceptional gain INR 3.9 crores from sale of non-core land at Kusur in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we also recognized an exceptional gain of INR3.9 crores from the sale of non-core land parcel at Kusur.

items.statement: Same-store RevPAR grew 14% in Q2 FY27 (9% rate, 3.6% occupancy); occupancy 78.6% vs 75% YoY
items.quote: RevPAR growth for the same-store hotels was up about 14%. And in this quarter, it was driven 9% by average rates and about 3.6% in occupancy. For the quarter, our hotels ran at a 78.6% occupancy, up from 75% a year ago.

items.statement: Same-store revenue grew 12.6% in Q2 FY27, ahead of 9-11% guidance
items.quote: Our same-store revenue grew by 12.6%. This is ahead of our long-term guidance of 9% to 11%.

items.statement: Management cautious on H2 FY27 despite strong event calendar; acknowledges volatility beyond control
items.quote: So I've banked the performance, but we remain very cautious about how quarter 3 and quarter 4 will pan out. There's nothing on the statistics and data, which makes s worried. But of course, there arc events which are beyond control.

items.statement: Navi Mumbai timeline not reset despite OC receipt; development risks acknowledged
items.quote: it's too carly to call out for changing the opening time line, Karan. And you know that in development in India, the whole disclaimer comes true. Whatever may go wrong will go wrong. So I don't think we would like to reset optimism at this stage.

items.statement: Published first sustainability report in Q2 FY27 setting baseline for accountability
items.quote: I'm also pleased to publish our first sustainability report this quatter, which sets the baseline againstwhich we will hold ourselves to account.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR800 crores to be deployed over next three years for capex, working capital and general corporate purposes
items.quote: The deployment of this would be phased over the next three years. That was indicated in the offer document as well.

items.statement: Mahad Unit 3 capex incurred to date approximately INR250 crores, on track for H2 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: The total capex incurred at Mahad to date is approximately INR250 crores.

items.statement: Vizag Phase I envisages capex of about INR1,000 crores for integrated facility with contrast media, intermediates, peptides, sweeteners and multipurpose blocks
items.quote: For phase I, as indicated earlier, we envisage a capex of about INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Hyderabad R&D center now operational with ~50 scientists onboarded and ~100 fume hoods over two phases
items.quote: I am pleased to share that this center, that houses several synthesis labs, a world-class analytical facility, is now operational. We have onboarded approximately 50 high -performing scientists

items.statement: Mahad Unit 3 on track for H2 FY27 commissioning for backward integration of contrast media KSM
items.quote: We had earlier indicated that the facility would go on stream in the second half of this year, and we remain on track to achieve that.

items.statement: Good order visibility and strong order book in both contrast media and PI/API segments
items.quote: Going forward, while I would not recommend that you extrapolate these Q2 numbers, all that I would say is that we have good visibility and a strong order book.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin 49%, down 4% sequentially due to higher raw material, reagent, solvent and catalyst costs from West Asia disruption
items.quote: The gross margin for Q2 at 49% is lower by 4% over previous quarter.

items.statement: Price increases with select customers effective from Q3 expected to positively impact gross margin in coming quarters
items.quote: We are reviewing the selling price increases with our customers contract by contract, and price increase with certain select customers will come into force from Q3.

items.statement: Higher raw material prices across reagents, solvents and catalysts due to West Asia disruption; timing of purchases and inventory affects margin impact
items.quote: Following disruption of West Asia, we have seen higher prices of raw material, including reagents, solvents, and catalysts across board.

items.statement: Q2 revenue growth driven 25% by contrast media, 52% by PI API, -30% by artificial sweetener vs previous quarter
items.quote: This growth was driven 25% by contrast media, 52% by PI API, and a degrowth of 30% by artificial sweetener compared to previous quarter.

items.statement: H1 FY27 growth driven 47% by contrast media, 19% by PI API, -2% by artificial sweetener vs H1 FY26
items.quote: This growth was driven 47% by contrast media, 19% by PI API, and a degrowth of 2% by artificial sweetener.

items.statement: PI vertical supported by improving demand from existing programs and newer products; contrast media maintains healthy momentum
items.quote: Our PI vertical, supported by improving demand from existing programs and contributions from newer products. Our contrast media business also maintained healthy momentum

items.statement: Completed QIP raise of INR800 crores to strengthen balance sheet for strategic investments
items.quote: The successful completion of our qualified institutional placement has further strengthened our balance sheet and provides us with the flexibility to execute these strategic investments

items.statement: Renewable energy contribution at ~80% of overall consumption; achieved EcoVadis silver rating
items.quote: We have made meaningful progress in increasing the contribution of renewable energy to our overall consumption, which today stands at about 80%. We have also achieved a silver rating for EcoVadis

items.statement: Gross margin pressure from crude-linked chemical prices; unable to predict if crude has bottomed or peaked
items.quote: It will be too difficult for us to actually tell if the crude price has actually bottomed out or it has peaked out. That is something we will not be in a position to make any guesstimate

items.statement: Vizag pre-construction activities underway; statutory compliances (EC, Consent to Establish) in place for Phase I
items.quote: The pre-construction activities are underway. Statutory compliances like EC and the Consent to Establish are in place.

items.statement: Vizag Phase I designed for flexibility across chemistry platforms, customers, product life cycles; supports early-stage incubation to commercial manufacturing
items.quote: Our approach at Vizag is not merely to add capacity. We are consciously designing the facility to provide flexibility across chemistry platforms, customers, and product life cycles.

items.statement: Contrast media volume growth continues; no volume degrowth, only small volume discount impact
items.quote: In volume terms, there is a growth, and there is a very small impact in terms of volume discount.

items.statement: Peptide strategy starts with fragments/intermediates; may forward integrate to final peptide if customers want
items.quote: So in peptides, we call the intermediates fragments. So they are no different than intermediates. That's how we plan to start.

items.statement: Bulk of PI/API revenue from commercial products; clinical/validation quantities relatively smaller
items.quote: I would completely agree and endorse that the bulk is coming from the commercial products, and the relatively smaller value is coming from the products that we incubated.

items.statement: No revenue guidance given; CDMO business sequential growth hard to extrapolate but good order visibility for FY27
items.quote: See, in the CDMO business, I don't think it is possible for anyone to give that type of guidance. But then as you see there has been sequential and significant growth in both contrast media and PI. I won’t recommend you extrapolate but then, b oth cases we have good order visibility, and I think it is going to be a good year

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 20% remains intact and may be exceeded
items.quote: We had revised our guidance to 20% last quarter, and we remain committed to it. We will definitely achieve the guidance and may go beyond.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to be better than guided 2.5%-3% range
items.quote: On credit cost, we expect to do better than guidance level.

items.statement: NIM confident of being on upper end of guidance and exceeding it
items.quote: On net interest margin, we are confident of being on the upper end of our guidance. We will definitely do more than that.

items.statement: ROA expected to beat upper guidance bracket of 3.3%
items.quote: 3.3% is the upper bracket for ROA and 18% is the ROA. We definitely feel that we would be able to beat that guidance.

items.statement: Profit guidance of Rs. 425-450 crores for FY27 on track
items.quote: We had guided towards Rs. 425-Rs. 450 crores of profit. Knowing that Q3 and Q4 are very strong quarters for lending business, we definitely are very confident that we will be able to achieve those numbers

items.statement: Long-term AUM target of Rs. 30,000 crores by 2030 remains
items.quote: We remain fully committed to our long-term target of Rs. 30,000 crores by 2030.

items.statement: Q2 disbursement of Rs. 2,900 crores, up 28% YoY and 10% QoQ
items.quote: We disbursed Rs. 2,900 crores in Q2, a growth of 28% year-on-year and 10% over the previous quarter

items.statement: H1 FY27 disbursement of Rs. 5,545 crores
items.quote: taking our first half disbursement to Rs. 5,545 crores

items.statement: AUM grew 22% YoY to Rs. 15,323 crores, above guidance
items.quote: Our AUM grew by 22% YoY; this is above our guidance of 18%-20%. We closed the quarter with Rs. 15,323 crores of asset under management.

items.statement: JLG vs non-JLG mix improved to 69-31 from 83-17, surpassing 70-30 target
items.quote: Right now, our portfolio, the breakup between JLG and non-JLG product remains 69-31. It was around 83-17 in the end of March. We targeted 70-30 mix for the year, but we have already surpassed it

items.statement: Individual lending portfolio reached Rs. 4,164 crores (27% of AUM) with 90+ DPD at 0.02%
items.quote: This portfolio has now reached Rs. 4,164 crores, accounting to 27% of our total AUM and performance has been very encouraging. Delinquency level remains very robust. We have given our presentation 90 plus is just 0.02%

items.statement: Gold loan disbursement of Rs. 453 crores in Q2 via co-lending with Muthoot Fincorp
items.quote: We have disbursed around Rs. 453 crores of gold loans during the quarter.

items.statement: Active customer base of 32.7 lakh; 50% unique, 31% with one other lender
items.quote: Overall, our active customer base stands at approximately 32.7 lakh. Of these, around 50% of our customers are unique to Muthoot Microfin, while another 31% are us plus one.

items.statement: Graduated 2.7 lakh JLG customers to individual loans with 700+ credit score
items.quote: Out of the 32 lakh customers, we have graduated so far 2.7 lakh customers, and these are all customers who are having excellent track record and a relationship with us, long-standing relationship and a 700 plus score.

items.statement: NIM improved from 12% to 12.5% in Q2
items.quote: And our net interest margin, which is a very important aspect, has improved from 12%-to 12.5%, which is a very significant development that we are seeing.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio at 48.1% standalone, below 50% guidance
items.quote: And most importantly, our cost-to-income ratio, which we were guiding that we would be below 50%, we are already at around 48.1% standalone for the quarter.

items.statement: OPEX to AUM reduced from 7% to 6.1% YoY
items.quote: OPEX to GLP has come down from 7% same period last year to 6.1% this quarter.

items.statement: Target AUM per branch Rs. 12-13 crores and OPEX to AUM 5.5%-5.75%
items.quote: Our aim for AUM per branch is to be around Rs. 12-Rs. 13 crores and OPEX to AUM to be between 5.5%-5.75%.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing fell to 9.93% (single digit) from 10.13%
items.quote: We kept our credit cost within the guided range of 2.5% to 3%. We were at 2.6%, brought our average cost of borrowing for the first time in the history of the company in single digits. We are at below 10%, 9.93%

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing at 9.69%
items.quote: And our incremental cost of borrowing has come down to 9.69%.

items.statement: Raised Rs. 3,213 crores in Q2 including Rs. 250 crores NCD at 9.25%
items.quote: During the quarter, we raised Rs. 3,213 crores, taking our first half fund raised to Rs. 5,947 crores. This includes Rs. 250 crores of NCD at a coupon rate of 9.25%.

items.statement: PTC transactions at ~8% helping reduce cost of funds
items.quote: The biggest reason why we are able to bring this cost of fund down is the PTCs that we are doing are at a very fine rate. There is a huge demand of priority sector portfolio among the private banks and foreign banks. And they are doing on an average at around 8% the PTC transaction.

items.statement: No new infrastructure added for new products; using existing branches and centralized underwriting
items.quote: The third and most important aspect is we have grown our new product portfolio without adding any new infrastructure. Individual loans run from our existing branch infrastructure with centralized underwriting team. Gold loans are serviced through Muthoot Fincorp branches.

items.statement: Branch count at 1,675; deepening in South, Assam, Andhra, Telangana; entering J&K soon
items.quote: On the network side, we have now 1,675 branches. We continue to deepen our presence in our core market, which is South India. While expanding our operations in carefully selected states, we have selected Assam, we have selected Andhra Pradesh. We are deepening our presence in Assam and Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and we will be also entering into Jammu and Kashmir very soon.

items.statement: AUM per branch reached Rs. 9.1 crores vs Rs. 7.3 crores earlier
items.quote: There is AUM growth per branch. We have reached around Rs. 9.1 crores outstanding per branch as compared to Rs. 7.3 cror es earlier

items.statement: AUM per loan officer reached Rs. 1.8 crores
items.quote: AUM per loan officer has also reached around 1.8 million (errata: actual number to be read as 1.8 crore).

items.statement: Collection efficiency 98.1% in Q2, improved to 99.2% in October
items.quote: Our collection efficiency for the quarter is at 98.1%, but for October, it has reached to 99.2%.

items.statement: X bucket collection efficiency at 99.9%
items.quote: X bucket collection efficiency has reached 99.9%, almost every rupee that is used coming on time.

items.statement: GNPA improved 32 bps QoQ to 3.38%; NNPA at 1.05%; PCR at 69.6%
items.quote: On our GNPA, we have had an improvement of 32 basis points QoQ. It stands at around 3.38% as of now. Our net NPA is 1.05%. And our provision cover continues to remain strong at 69.6%

items.statement: Credit cost at 2.6%, within guided 2.5%-3% range
items.quote: with a credit cost of 2.6%, which is what we are guided for.

items.statement: Maharashtra X bucket collection at 98%; Karnataka at 100%
items.quote: On X bucket, Karnataka remains 100% and on Maharashtra, which was already at around 98%, it remained at 98%.

items.statement: ECL release of ~Rs. 54 crores; maintaining Rs. 24 crores contingency buffer
items.quote: We continue to have a buffer of around Rs. 24 crores, which is not really a management overlay, but there is a buffer for contingencies like these drought-like situations we have in our overall ECL model.

items.statement: Liquidity of Rs. 1,835 crores on balance sheet and Rs. 4,442 crores unavailed sanctions
items.quote: We close the quarter with Rs. 1,701 crores (errata: actual number to be read as Rs. 1,835 crores) of liquidity on the balance sheet and Rs. 4,328 crores (errata: actual number to be read as Rs. 4,442 crores) of unavailed sanctions in our hands.

items.statement: CARE Edge revised outlook to positive; CRISIL AA- rating
items.quote: More recently, we had a CARE Edge global rating revised our outlook to positive. This builds on the C RISIL upgrade and will help us access funds at better rates

items.statement: Plan to draw down ECB sanctions, possibly in Q3
items.quote: We already have a couple of sanctions in our hand where ECB is available to us. We will definitely draw them down. Maybe the first one would be this quarter itself.

items.statement: Digital collections at 47% monthly; targeting 75% well before 2030
items.quote: Now, digital collection amounts to 47% of our overall collection month-on-month basis and the guidance of 75% that we were guiding for 2030. We are very confident that we would be able to achieve much earlier that 75% digital collection.

items.statement: ROA at 3% and ROE at 14.8% for Q2
items.quote: And our ROA is at 3% and ROE is 14.8%.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 25.5%
items.quote: We have a strong capital adequacy ratio of 25.5%.

items.statement: CGFMU credit guarantee application pending budget allocation
items.quote: So, I think as far as the CGFMU credit guarantee is concerned, we have applied for it. There is a budget allocation still awaited at the CGFMU level.

items.statement: Gold loan co-lending with Muthoot Fincorp: 60% share, yielding ~12-12.5% effective
items.quote: On the margin, we are getting around 9.8% yield on this portfolio. So effectively, upfront and generally, these are the 3-6 months kind of a tenure weighted average, if you can say it is around 5 months kind of a tenure. On that, effective yield is in the range of around 12%-12.5%.

items.statement: Exposure to drought-affected Maharashtra/Karnataka districts limited to 3.6% of portfolio (Rs. 550 crores)
items.quote: The exposure for us is very limited. It is around 3.6% of our portfolio is in these two states, which is on-book portfolio, about Rs. 550 crores.

items.statement: Assam portfolio <Rs. 100 crores with 100% NATCAT cover; Bihar portfolio ~Rs. 1,000 crores with 85% NATCAT cover
items.quote: Assam is one of the areas that we have newly entered. So, our portfolio exposure there is limited. We are just about less than Rs. 100 crores portfolio there in Assam. And all of those customers have a natural calamity insurance, 100% there. And in Bihar, we are close to around Rs. 1,000 crores of portfolio in Bihar.

items.statement: SROs guiding empathetic collection; avoiding miscommunication with unregulated lenders
items.quote: So, from the SRO side, collectively, we have decided to be more vigilant and responsible. So biggest challenge in this scenario is miscommunication. A lot of the time, the communication goes like that coercive collection practices are being used and stuff like that. There is a standing guidance from both the SROs that be more empathetic and more careful in collection.

items.statement: Management guides 8-10% revenue growth for FY27 and 8-10% of revenue for marketing spend
items.quote: Given the current geopolitical scenario and inflationary pressures, we remain cautious, but we will try to maintain 8% to 10% growth for this year, and we should be able to do that.

items.statement: Management expects 4-5% like-for-like growth for full year FY27
items.quote: Well, given the current scenario, we co uld say we might be at 4%, 5%. We should be able to hold on to this

items.statement: Q2 FY27 saw positive same-store sales growth for third consecutive quarter

items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free with zero borrowings as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Franchisee-run EBOs operate on commission model, not profit-sharing
items.quote: So for those stores, those franchisees get commissioned. Instead of margin, they get paid i n the form of commission basically

items.quote: The evolving geopolitical situation also brings with it potential inflationary pressures, which could weigh on consumer sentiment and discretionary demand in the coming quarters.

items.statement: No brand ambassador planned; focusing on content-led digital marketing via Google and Meta

items.statement: FY27 guidance: ~23% consolidated revenue growth (excl. new acquisitions), EBITDA margin 5%, EBITDA-to-OCF conversion 50%
items.value: 23% revenue growth, 5% EBITDA margin, 50% OCF conversion
items.quote: We remain confident of sustaining the momentum in second half of the financial year and are in a comfortable position to deliver better than our stated FY 2027 guidance - which is consolidated revenue growth of approximately 23% (excluding any contribution from new acquisitions), alongside an EBITDA margin of 5% and EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion of 50%.

items.statement: Management confident of beating FY27 guidance on both growth and margin but not giving revised numbers
items.quote: What I told before is that we are very confident that we would be able to do better than what we had guided before. What I am not doing right now is not giving a specific revised number for H2 or a revised number for the full year.

items.statement: Organic growth driven by customer base expansion, wallet share improvement, and new product categories
items.quote: It is an all-round growth. It includes expansion in customer base, it includes improvement in wallet share from the customers, it includes new product categories, growth coming from new product categories. It is a combination of all three.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 126 bps YoY to 11.5%; EBITDA margin expanded 135 bps to 5.3% in Q2
items.quote: Gross margin expanded 126 basis points year-on-year to 11.5%, and EBITDA margin expanded 135 basis points to 5.3%, and EBITDA grew by 78% year-on-year.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by procurement economies, MedTech share growth, and exit from low-margin accounts
items.quote: Margin expansion was driven by three levers: scale-led procurement economies, a growing share of revenue from MedTech business, and the deliberate exit from certain low-margin accounts.

items.statement: Trade margin cap/MRP reductions unlikely to impact distributor margins; only 2% of sales from notified molecules
items.quote: But when I look at my sales, these 137 molecules that has been as of now notified by NPPA, that those molecules total sales in our portfolio is only 2% as of now. Okay. So, I do not see any material impact that can come on this.

items.statement: MedTech revenue ~15%+ of total; H1 MedTech revenue ~INR600 crore; full year will exceed INR1,000 crore
items.quote: MedTech, as we have guided before, it is in a range of 15%+ of our total revenues.

items.statement: No new acquisitions in H1 FY27; evaluating opportunities >INR100 cr in pharma and MedTech for portfolio/geography expansion
items.quote: We are not looking at something which is lower than INR100 crore.

items.statement: INR166 cr paid in H1 for deferred consideration from prior acquisitions; not related to put/call options
items.quote: The consideration payouts that you're seeing, you are right, these are deferred considerations. Our agreements have various time periods in which the deferred consideration will get paid.

items.statement: INR55 cr delayed from Maharashtra govt received in November; full-year OCF guidance of 50% EBITDA conversion maintained
items.quote: I think it was around INR55 crore.

items.statement: Debt repayment for FY26 acquisition starts Q3; board mandate not to exceed 2x net debt/EBITDA; prioritize growth investments over debt repayment
items.quote: Currently, we have taken a debt for one of the acquisitions last year. The repayments will commence from Q3. So, as and when we commence the repayment and we reduce the debt over a period of time, you will see the interest cost coming down.

items.statement: Interest cost INR20-25 cr/quarter expected to decline as debt repaid from Q3
items.quote: The repayments will commence from Q3. So, as and when we commence the repayment and we reduce the debt over a period of time, you will see the interest cost coming down.

items.statement: Evaluating large acquisitions (>INR100 cr) in pharma and MedTech for portfolio expansion and new geographies; hopeful to close in FY27
items.quote: Yes, there are large acquisitions still available in the market, both in pharma and MedTech space.

items.statement: No acquisitions in H1 FY27; calendarisation benefit from prior acquisitions tapering in Q3/Q4
items.quote: There were no acquisitions done in first half of this year.

items.statement: Served 92,200+ retail and 2,900+ hospital customers across 500 districts, 20+ states/UTs; 90,400 SKUs from 3,200+ manufacturers
items.quote: In H1, we served over 92,200 retail customers and more than 2,900 hospital customers, spread in approximately 500 districts in more than 20 states and union territories, and distributed over 90,400 SKUs sourced from more than 3,200 healthcare product manufacturers.

items.statement: MedTech growing share, higher margin profile; margin depends on value-add (demand generation) not just product type
items.quote: The margin is more dependent on the value- add that you have provided rather than by the specific product that you are selling.

items.statement: INR11.87 cr provision for subsidiary customer default (pharmacy) in Q2; legal rights and post-dated cheques held for recovery
items.quote: Entire amount, as we said in that note, has been provided in, regarding that receivable in our books in Other Expenses line.

items.statement: ROCE 22.0%, ROE 22.4% in Q2; H1 ROCE 21.8%, ROE 21.3%
items.quote: Our return ratios continue to show improvement in the quarter. ROCE and ROE were 22.0% and 22.4%, respectively.

items.quote: The Westin is positioned as an entry-level luxury brand in the country. The prices will be very competitive. For us, it wouldn't matter if it's crew or groups as long as the price points and the ARR is being achieved.

items.quote: If you see the comp set today, so there are three properties. We have Taj Bangalore having 370 keys then Leela Bhartiya City 281 keys. Varun Saraf: Can I -- so just to add, there are two assets that you want to see. There's the Hyatt Centric that has opened up and the Moxy

items.quote: During off-season, if there is demand that is being generated by the park -- by the theme park, we will of course partner with them but that does not automatically result in discounted rates. items.statement: Gross borrowing reduced to INR703 crore at Sep-end, cash INR70 crore, net debt INR633 crore at 1.4x EBITDA

items.statement: Debt profile long-term 10-12 years, AA- rating stable, undrawn facility INR125 crore

items.statement: Headroom for additional debt for strategic acquisitions at current 1.4x net debt/EBITDA
items.quote: Net debt stood at approximately INR633 crores at 1.4 times EBITDA giving headroom for additional debt for strategic acquisitions.

items.statement: Proceeding with dilution for MPS compliance in Q3, seeking advice on best permissible mode

items.statement: Signed binding MOU for Novotel Imagicaa acquisition at INR248 crore, consolidation in Q4 FY27
items.quote: In October, we signed a binding memorandum of understanding with Imagicaa World Entertainment Limited for the proposed consideration of approximately INR248 crores at INR80 lakhs per key. The hotel should start contributing to our top line in Q4 of FY27.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 ARR INR11,514 (+8.6% YoY), occupancy 75%

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue from operations INR499 crore (+11% YoY), total income INR510 crore (+10%), EBITDA INR180 crore (+4%), PAT INR70.4 crore (+173%)
items.quote: Moving to our half-yearly performance, revenue from operations grew 11% to INR499 crores, while total income increased 10% to INR510 crores. EBITDA increased 4% to INR180 crores while profit before exceptional items and tax grew 51% to INR94.2 crores. increased to INR94.2 crores from INR41.6 crores last year and PAT registered a strong growth of 173% to INR70.4 crores compared with INR25.8 crores

items.statement: Post-completion of greenfield projects, ROCE targeted at 19%
items.quote: ROCE post-completion of these projects will be at 19%.

items.statement: ROFO for Hyatt Regency Mumbai and Chennai delayed, not dropped; shareholders will decide via majority of minority when opportunities arise

It would be the majority of the minority who would decide since we would be -- the promoters would be related party, right? So they have no say in it.

items.statement: Promoters are related party for ROFO assets, majority of minority shareholders will decide on acquisition
items.quote: It would be the majority of the minority who would decide since we would be -- the promoters would be related party, right? So they have no say in it.

items.statement: Finance cost declined 50% to INR15.3 crore from INR30.3 crore YoY in Q2
items.quote: Finance cost declined by 50% to INR15.3 crores from INR30.3 crores

items.statement: Depreciation and amortization reduced to INR26.7 crore from INR29.5 crore YoY in Q2
items.quote: depreciation and amortizations reduced to INR26.7 crores from INR29.5 crores

items.statement: Gas price volatility impacting HLP costs, mitigating by switching to electric equipment
items.quote: we see the gas prices staying there. But corrective actions have been taken to address those challenges. And we believe that this is a quarter where you have to see-- we've seen some impact but going forward it will automatically come back up.

items.statement: GST 2.0 ITC credit impact of ~INR2 crore in Q2 due to rooms sold below INR7,500
