items.quote: I do not see a constraint in terms of the headroom or tariff growth, etc., that we have. If ever and when this happens, we feel strongly about the fact that we should really need this increase in ARPU, we will continue to, just, keep building industry-leading ARPUs in this business.

items.statement: Home broadband EBIT softer due to investment phase in fiber and CPE, plus prior low-ARPU acquisition quality issues now being corrected.
items.quote: A lot of investment has gone into fiber as well as CPE which are the two big capex and play that comes in. So, as a result of which, EBIT has looked a little bit softer.

items.statement: Radio capex moderated with less than 1,000 new towers this quarter (~500-600 sites); incremental capex directed to data centers and cloud growth bets.
items.quote: if you look at the new towers being installed, it is almost very little now it is less than 1000, in the ballpark of five, six hundred sites this year, this quarter.

items.statement: Continued buybacks in Airtel Africa and Indus; dividend payouts will keep increasing over time.
items.quote: We have already announced a potential, continued buyback in Airtel Africa. We have also done that in Indus, so that will continue and we have also said in the past, and you see that reflected in our conduct that the dividend payouts will keep increasing over time.

items.statement: Wireless capex seasonal in Q2 due to weather; assess trailing 12-month capex; no per-megawatt data center capex thumb rule given location and design variability.
items.quote: I can not give you a number, because there are very, very many vulnerabilities, changes that happen. It is about where is it located, what is the design, what is it fit for purpose.

items.statement: Data consumption per sub gap versus peers narrowed from 35-40% to ~20% due to network strengthening and plan upgrades; monetization shift to consumption-led pricing architecture needed.
items.quote: On this one, I feel in terms of how we monetize data consumption per sub going forward, I think it is back to what we discussed earlier, I think a very detailed discussion on what we need to do on pricing architecture.

items.statement: Pricing intervention revenue accretive; B2B growth accelerated to 11.5% from ~7% driven by digital businesses offsetting managed decline in commodity messaging.
items.quote: Now, if you look at 11.5% growth that we have had, obviously, you can see that there is an acceleration that is happening on the digital side, which is actually compensating for some of that managed decline on the core commodity messaging.

items.statement: Home broadband focus on net adds acceleration via fiber footprint expansion, GTM pivot, and quality customer acquisition; recovery will take time.
items.quote: overall growth and acceleration in the net adds is for me right now the metric to look at on this business, so, I would just leave it there and say, we have to accelerate.

items.statement: 5G user base exceeds 200 million.
items.quote: More than 200 million.

items.statement: Hexacom Q2 revenue Rs 2,580 Cr (+2.9% QoQ), EBITDAaL Rs 1,250 Cr (48.6% margin), mobile base 29M, smartphone adds 48K, ARPU Rs 264 (aided by extra day), home net adds 71K, OpFCF Rs 920 Cr, net debt ex-leases Rs 1,575 Cr.
items.quote: We delivered strong performance with revenue of over Rs.2,580 Crores, growing at about 2.9% sequentially. EBITDAaL for the quarter came in at over Rs.1,250 Crores with a margin of 48.6%.

items.statement: Hexacom mobile churn impacted by pricing intervention and severe Northeast weather disrupting recharges; early signs of improvement seen for Q3.
items.quote: it also impacted existing customers' continuity because those days they could not recharge. I would not read too much into how is this exactly different to the last rupee? One day has come, which has come for Airtel as well as it has come for every player who is on a number of days pack, outside of that, it is the mix of customers and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Hexacom postpaid ARPU increase broadly Rs 50 flow-through, barring minor international roaming access charges.
items.quote: On the postpaid ARPU, ye s, broadly, it is a Rs.50 increase, so barring a bit of ARPU, yes, certainly, there could be some access charges for the people who actually go on international roaming, but at ARPU level, yes, broadly, it should be a flow through

items.statement: Hexacom ARPU growth slower than Airtel due to different customer mix, affordability, lower postpaid share, and Northeast disruption; no structural underperformance assumed.
items.quote: if somebody has lesser percentage of customers on postpaid, then the flow-through as percentage of top-line would be lesser that is arithmetic, but on the prepaid cohort, whether growth will lag Airtel or lead Airtel is something which will be played out in the market competitively.

items.statement: Hexacom home broadband net adds decelerated to 70K from 100K+ due to deliberate shift to quality fiber-led acquisition; will claw back with higher-quality customers.
items.quote: what we have now clearly decided that we will drive quality customers, driven primarily through fiber. Of course, Northeast, there are places where the fiber is a challenge, and so on and so forth, but we are working on that.

items.statement: Access charges (IBR) for Hexacom to be viewed on trailing 12-month basis due to seasonality; home broadband too small to materially drive access charges.
items.quote: If you look at the trend of access charges, IBR, look at it at a trailing 12-month basis because there is seasonality and all of that, there are a lot of other things.

items.statement: Voice-only minimum recharge cohort very small and declining; no significant impact on Hexacom headline ARPU.
items.quote: this cohort of people who are only on voice plans is very small, and it is coming down. We are talking of upgrades of feature phone to smartphone slowly or becoming fast, and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Hexacom reported vs cash capex difference noted; management to circle back with explanation.
items.quote: Reported and cash capex. I do not have a ready answer for you, Aditya. Allow me to circle back to you on this one.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance of 18-20% disbursement growth and 20% AUM and PAT growth for full year FY27
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain committed to our medium -term guidance of 18% to 20% disbursement growth and 20% AUM and PAT growth for the full year.

items.statement: Confident of delivering 20% plus disbursement growth in H2 FY27
items.quote: We expect our disbursement momentum to continue and are confident of delivering a 20% plus disbursement growth in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 25 bps for FY27, headline NPA expected at 1.10-1.15% by year-end
items.quote: We have always been holding out a credit cost number as a guidance of 25 basis points. I think we are quite confident as we end the year, our credit cost will be aligned with the 25 basis points, and the headline NPA would be in the range of about 1.10%-1.15%.

items.statement: AUM at INR32,643 cr as of Sep 2026, up 18% YoY (20% like-to-like)
items.quote: Our AUM as of 30th September 2026 stood at INR32,643 crores, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 18%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 disbursements at INR2,577 cr, up 22% YoY (21% like-to-like in H1)
items.quote: Disbursement for Q2 FY 2027 stood at INR2,577 crores, representing a Y-o-Y growth of 22%.

items.statement: Assignment volume guidance of INR2,000-2,050 cr for FY27
items.quote: Broadly, the way of looking at assignment is that probably during the year, we will probably end up doing around INR2,000 crores of assignment during the current financial year.

items.statement: Exit portfolio yield 13.4%, exit spread 5.73% as of Sep 2026
items.quote: The portfolio yield exit is 13.4% as at the end of quarter two FY 2027, and the exit spread stood at 5.73%.

items.statement: Adjusted cost-to-income 33.9% in Q2 FY27, down 230 bps YoY; 34% in H1 FY27, down 215 bps YoY
items.quote: Adjusted for this item, the cost to income is 33.9%, which is a year -on-year decline of 230 basis points, and 34% in H1 FY 2027, which is a year -on-year decline of 215 basis points.

items.statement: Focus on protecting spreads rather than chasing yields in rising rate environment
items.quote: In this environment, our focus will be to continue on prudent underwriting, disciplined funding, and margin management while catering to underlying demand for the affordable housing finance and maintaining the quality of our portfolio. Our approach is to protect spreads rather than chase yields.

items.statement: 75% of assets and liabilities floating, enabling pass-through of rate changes with max one quarter lag
items.quote: In terms of fixed and floating nature of our book, broadly 75% of our assets and liabilities are floating in nature. This gives us the ability to reprice our assets whenever the change in interest rate happens and we get passed on by banks or other floating -rate liabilities.

items.statement: ALCO to meet in Dec/Jan to decide on rate hike pass-through after RBI policy
items.quote: We will have a meeting of the ALCO probably in the third quarter, probably in December or January, and we will take a call at that point of time, depending how about the RBI announcement happening in January.

items.statement: GNPA 1.34% as of Sep 2026, improved 8 bps YoY; NNPA 1%; collection efficiency 99%
items.quote: Collection efficiency for the said quarter stood at 99%, while gross NPA stood at 1.34% as of September 2026, which is an improvement of 8 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Stage 2 (GS2) at 3.55%, up 30 bps QoQ but flat YoY; attributed to seasonality, no geographic stress
items.quote: I think it is more of a seasonality sort of a moment. We are not seeing any specific state or any cause of undue worry in terms of this 30 basis points moment on the GS2.

items.statement: Branch network at 632 across 23 states, 555 districts; added 1 branch in Jammu in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter, we expanded our footprint to Jammu, an important territory for us, by adding one branch there, taking our network to 632 branches across now 23 states and covering over 555 districts as of September '26.

items.statement: Branch addition guidance of 40-50 for FY27; 5-6 added so far, ~40 in pipeline
items.quote: Our guidance to the market and to all of you has been that we will add 40 to 50 branches for the current financial year. We have added about five, six branches as we speak, and there are close to about 40 branches in pipeline.

items.statement: Disbursement momentum strong; October run-rate ~INR900 cr vs avg INR800 cr; Q3 minimum 20% growth expected
items.quote: October numbers, we are very comfortable. From an average of about INR800, we moved upward to about close to about INR900, so numbers are sta cking up good. In terms of disbursement growth for the quarter, we are looking at a minimum of 20% growth for Q3.

items.statement: Non-home loan share at 26% of AUM, targeting 28% by Q4 FY27 and 30% next year
items.quote: If you look at the quarter one to quarter two performance, I think the number has moved from a 24% to a 26%. We have opened whatever levers had to be opened. From here on, I think by the end of this year, we should stabilize at about 28% odd. Next year, we carry on to about 70 %/30% as 70/30 home loan to non -home loan.

items.statement: Total borrowings INR20,400 cr as of Sep 2026 (53% banks, 22% NHB, 15% NCD, 7% ECB, 3% others)
items.quote: Our overall borrowings on 30th September stood at INR20,400 crores compared to INR17,600 crores on 30th September 2025. The borrowing mix as at end of 30th September 2026 is 53% from banks, NHB share is 22%, NCD share is 15%, ECB is 7%, and others are 3%.

items.statement: Undrawn sanctions INR1,466 cr; fresh NHB sanction of INR1,000 cr received in October
items.value: INR1,466 cr undrawn + INR1,000 cr fresh
items.quote: Undrawn sanctions as of September 30, 2026, is INR1,466 crores. Further, in this week, we have received a fresh sanction of INR1,000 crores from National Housing Bank.

items.statement: Rating upgrade to AA+ stable from all three agencies (India Ratings, CARE, ICRA); enables 20-30 bps cheaper NCDs and access to pension/insurance funds
items.quote: During the quarter in question, I am proud to say that our credit profile was further strengthened with India Ratings and ICRA upgrading our long-term rating to AA+ stable. Now all the three rating agencies, that is India Ratings, CARE, and ICRA, have rated the company AA+ on a stand -alone basis.

items.statement: H1 FY27 PAT INR591 cr (up from INR504 cr); Q2 PAT INR308 cr (up from INR266 cr); adjusted PAT growth 22% H1, 20% Q2

Adjusted for ESOP cost, the PAT has grown by 22% in H1 and a growth of 20% in quarter two FY 2027.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 ROA 4.2%, ROE 15.2% (adjusted 4.4%, 15.8%); H1 ROA 4.3%, ROE 15.5% adjusted
items.quote: The quarter two FY 2027 ROA and ROE are 4.2% and 15.2% respectively. Again, adjusted for ESOP cost, the ROA and ROE will stand at 4.4% and 15.8% for quarter two, and 4.3% and 15.5% for H1 FY 2027.

items.statement: Capital adequacy: Tier 1 41.7%, Tier 2 0.5% as of Sep 2026
items.quote: Capital adequacy ratio for quarter two FY 2027 stood at 41.7% for Tier 1 and 0.5% for Tier 2.

items.statement: Headcount 6,112 on-roll employees as of Sep 2026
items.quote: The number of employees as at the end of September 30, 2026, on roll was 6,112 employees.

This was given to employees at an exercise price of INR425 per share.

items.statement: Board changes: Shri Deo Shankar Tripathi appointed Interim Non-Executive Chairman; Shri Nikhil Goyal (Blackstone MD) added as Additional Director
items.quote: Following this unfortunate event, and in accordance with the applicable regulatory requirements, Shri Deo Shankar Tripathi, previously Executive Vice Chairman of the company, has been appointed as Interim Non-Executive Chairman. I would also like to welcome Shri Nikhil Goyal, Managing Director , Blackstone, who has joined our Board as an Additional Director with effect from 12th of August 2026.

items.statement: Monitoring El Niño impact on 30 high-priority districts (5-6% of AUM); bounce rates stable; calibrated underwriting in East, Kerala
items.quote: Out of about 88 high -priority districts under El Niño, we are available only in 30 districts. Close to 5% -6% of my AUM would be in those districts. In the current cycle of EMI banking, that is what we are closely monitoring, that if bounce moves. Right now, it i

items.statement: RBI repo rate hike to 5.5% and calibrated tightening; 75% floating book allows pass-through with max one quarter lag
items.quote: In the recent revision in RBI monetary policy, with 25 basis points increase in repo rate to 5.5% and a shift towards calibrated tightening, marks a change in the interest rate environment. While the impact on borrowing cost and housing affordability will depend on the extent and timing of transmission, we remain mindful of its implication both for customers and lenders.

items.statement: IRDAI draft guidelines on insurance income; industry submitted recommendations; will calibrate fee income/opex levers when final guidelines issued
items.quote: The third one on insurance, I think, these were draft guidelines. The entire industry has sent out their recommendation. We will have to wait out for the final guidelines to come in. Having said that, we work with multiple levers. There are levers like fee income, there are levers like Opex. If it were to be calibrated as and when the final guidelines come, we will do that calibration, ensure that

items.statement: Portfolio: 73% home loans, 27% non-home loans; avg ticket INR11.3 lakh; LTV 61%; 55% salaried
items.quote: Our portfolio continues to remain fully secured and retail in nature, with home loans accounting to 73%, non -home loans accounting to 27% of our AUM. Our average ticket size stood at INR11.3 lakh, with a loan -to-value ratio at comfortable 61%. The salaried segment contributed 55% of our AUM, reflecting a diversified nature of our portfolio.

items.statement: Balance transfer outflows 5.1% in Q2, improved 40 bps YoY; industry average 6.5-7%; controlled via AI-driven retention
items.quote: Balance transfer outflows during the quarter two FY 2027 was at 5.1%, which improved by 40 basis points as compared to Q2 FY 2026, supported by focused retention efforts and AI -driven customer engagement.

items.statement: Leveraging AI across lending cycle; building in-house platforms for document, voice, decisioning, enterprise, management intelligence
items.quote: On technology, we continue to leverage AI and data analytics to strengthen business operations across the lending cycle, including origination, underwriting, portfolio monitoring, collection, and customer retention. We are also building in -house platforms across document intelligence, voice intelligence, decisioning intelligence, enterprise access, and management intelligence to improve informati

items.statement: Market remains soft except property where pricing discipline emerged from mid-September; no TP price hikes yet
items.quote: The market is still soft other than property, where since mid-September, we have seen some increase. No TP price hikes till now.

items.statement: Chose profitability over growth; CISR combined ratio 99.8% vs 94.9% last year, 97.4% excluding floods
items.quote: And overall, we continue to choose profitability over growth, and we continue to hold that choice as we speak.

items.statement: Flood losses Rs 63 crore net in Q2 vs Rs 10 crore last year; PAT excluding MTM Rs 208 crore vs Rs 277 crore
items.quote: In Q2, flood losses were about Rs. 63 crores on net basis. The amount last quarter, which is last year Q2, was about Rs. 10 crores.

items.statement: Motor market share 5.68% in Q2 vs 5.58% in Q1; own damage share improved to 4.99% from 4.76%
items.quote: Motor market share is about 5.68% in Q2, slightly better than Q1 of 5.58%. Own damage share improved from 4.76% in Q1 to 4.99% in Q2.

items.statement: AUM (book value) grew 15.9% to Rs 24,371 crore; long-term advanced premium Rs 3,556 crore vs Rs 3,209 crore in March 2026
items.quote: AUM have gone up to now Rs. 24,371 crore. This again is book value. We started looking at book value from last quarter, and this is up 15.9%.

items.quote: So the attritional loss ratio came down from 85.3% in Q1 to 81.1% in Q2. So we actually saw the improvement.

items.quote: Despite the flood losses which we saw in Q2, our fire gross earned loss ratio, and this is I am giving figures just on a gross earned premium basis, no discounting, nothing, is 59%.

items.statement: Premium retention increased to 84.3% from 79.1%; higher retention core strategy driving AUM growth
items.quote: I think premium retention a figure which we have continuously been sharing, increases to 84.3% versus 79.1%.

items.statement: Investment yield ~7.4% including small capital gains; core insurance profitability focus, not dependent on capital gains
items.quote: So overall, when you look at the yield with a small capital gains, we are looking at roughly about 7.4%, close to 7.4% of the yield in this.

items.statement: IRDAI discussion paper acknowledges EoM guidelines failed; suggests crop weightage 1/3; will not speculate on final guidelines
items.quote: I think when you look at this discussion paper, I think it acknowledges that the present EoM guidelines have not resulted in the outcome which was intended.

items.quote: But on overall basis, on outstanding liabilities plus IBNR, we have close to about 20% impact for TP of discounting.

items.statement: Onerous contracts from motor TP and group health; testing granular by line of business
items.quote: So basically, I think our onerous contract is coming from motor TP and group health.

items.statement: Group health employer-employee ~80% of health/PA book; retail ~6%; loss ratios >100% for industry in group health vs 65-75% retail
items.quote: My sense would be only on health because or maybe health and PA together, the employer-employee would be 80%, slightly up and down, but it will be 80%.

items.statement: Health loss ratios stable; pricing improvement needed; fraud engines improving, hospital MoUs expanding for cost efficiency
items.quote: We are now negotiating and discussing to have MoUs with more and more hospital, which are becoming more efficient, I think, from a cost perspective.

items.quote: And as Fairfax press release had also said that Fairfax intends to sell their shareholding in Digit GI, which is Fairfax shareholding in Digit GI to the IDBI Bank.

items.statement: Solvency strong at 2.40x; ROE 4.4% on iGAAP net worth; additional Rs 3,300+ crore net worth not distributable or usable for writing business
items.quote: Solvency continues to be strong at 2.40x. ROE for this quarter is 4.4% on iGAAP net worth, because solvency is still on iGAAP.

items.statement: CISR combined ratio 99.8% vs 94.9%; excluding floods 97.4% vs 94.5%; reinsurance net cost Rs 70 cr vs Rs 382 cr last year
items.quote: The CISR combined ratio is 99.8% versus 94.9%. Excluding flood, this 99.8% would actually be 97.4% versus 94.5% of last quarter, so about 2.9% higher.

items.statement: Insurance finance expense Rs 171 cr in Q2 offsets discounting benefit; CISR with loss expense and commission split is right comparison metric
items.quote: In the Indian Accounting system, claims are booked at present value. The interest on that money is charged back as insurance finance expense. So Rs. 171 crore this quarter is an expense against our investment income.

items.statement: New business two-wheeler grew 15% on collected basis in Q2
items.quote: New business in two-wheeler in this quarter grew by 15% on collected basis.

items.quote: And within private car, standalone own damage premium is down 40% after the price corrections we had taken specifically in April and May.

items.statement: Fire gross written premium -29.9%; pricing discipline from mid-September; protecting commercial treaties
items.quote: written premium is minus 29.9%. In terms of number of accounts, etc., we continue to be present across. Some pricing discipline coming in from mid-September, and as I already said, that we continue in our philosophy to protect the treaty for all commercial lines of business

items.statement: Commercial product launched, building capabilities; giving quotes, full pricing model developed, portal integration started; expect 6 months to assess scale
items.quote: So we have introduced the product also in the market, that product has come. So we have started now building good capabilities in that.

items.statement: Gujarat flood fire loss share less than market share; motor flood loss comparison difficult due to EV battery salvage values
items.quote: I think in case of non-motor, our share of fire, I would say more precisely, our share of losses in fire would be less than what our market share is.

items.statement: Acquisition expenses not paid to third parties (employee incentives) <1.5% of premium
items.quote: But on an overall basis, we would not expect this number to be more than 1.5% of the premium.

items.statement: Degrowth reducing substantially quarter-on-quarter; pricing discipline returning in fire; hope next quarters better
items.quote: And we also, as I said, we are looking at on a quarter-by-quarter basis in the last two quarters, the de-growth, etc., is now reducing substantially. items.quote: As on date, our diversified order book stands at approximately INR6,778 crores, comprising INR3,439 crores from water and wastewater infrastructure and INR3,340 crores from renewable energy.

items.quote: India continues to witness significant investment in water management, wastewater treatment, and clean energy infrastructure. items.statement: Completed 58 water and wastewater projects with cumulative treatment capacity of 1,018 MLD built to date
items.quote: We have completed 58 water and wastewater projects with a cumulative treatment capacity of 1,018 MLD built to date, demonstrating our ability to undertake complex treatment infrastructure projects.

items.statement: BESS order book of 930 MWh from NTPC plus one IPP project from Bihar; major chunk expected to be completed by June

Right now, we are executing these two projects. To our understanding, a major chunk of these project is expected to be completed by June.

items.statement: Price escalation clauses exist in contracts but do not pass through 100% of cost increases; some cost borne by company leading to lowered EBITDA margin guidance to 21% for water segment

At the same time, our total borrowings stood at approximately INR703.9 crores compared with INR422.3 crores at the end of previous financial year.

items.statement: UBR (unbilled receivables) from MP Jal Nigam and Har Ghar Jal projects reduced significantly to around INR100 crores or less; expected to be near nil by March 2027

Can be somewhere around INR100 crores or maybe less than INR100 crores now.

This is one which takes this OCF to negative figures.

items.quote: The moderation in EBITDA margin at consol levels are attributed to some accounting entries on account of interest cost on the payments to be made at a later stage for acquisition of Suyog Urja Limited and reversal of profits from EPC to EPC of IPP projects.

items.quote: We have not lowered our profitability guidance on the projects while we are bidding. items.quote: Regarding the two Bangalore projects, the total value of which was around INR220 crores, both the projects are now under execution and are moving smoothly. We are maintaining the timelines, and we expect to complete projects well ahead of schedule.

items.statement: Overseas bids submitted; expecting at least 1-2 international projects to accrue to order book
items.quote: Apart from this, there are some overseas projects for which we have submitted our bids. We look forward to at least one or two projects from overseas which should get accrued in our order book.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 18-23%
items.quote: Like I earlier said, the target is to be between an 18% to 23% EBITDA margin company. We are well on track to achieving that.

items.statement: Growth expected for next 12-16 quarters
items.quote: We're expecting a very good third and fourth quarter, and not only for the next two quarters, but we're expecting this growth at least for the next 12-16 quarters to continue.

items.statement: No exact FY27 revenue guidance given
items.quote: See, I can't give you exact numbers as I can't give a forward-looking outlook.

items.statement: EBITDA and PBT margins improving with scale
items.quote: Definitely, if you can see even in our results, our EBITDA margins and our PBT margins are improving, and that should continue happening with the scale we are seeing.

items.statement: Confirmed PO order book INR910 crores executable over 2.5 years
items.quote: We have two different kind of order books. One is a confirmed PO, which, you're correct, is INR910 crores. That needs to be executed over the next 2.5 Years.

items.quote: Then we have strategic agreements as well of over INR3,100 crores. That needs to be executed over a period of five years.

items.statement: Fresh orders INR430 crores and bids INR1,350 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: During the first half of the financial year, the company secured fresh orders worth approximately INR430 crores and submitted bids aggregating approximately INR1,350 crores.

items.statement: Semiconductor revenues to scale meaningfully over coming quarters and years
items.quote: Based on our ongoing customer interactions, qualification progress, and visibility into future opportunities, we expect semiconductor revenues to scale meaningfully over the coming quarters and years.

items.statement: Semiconductor segment growth to continue for at least next three years
items.quote: And that growth that we see will definitely continue at least for the next three years in the semicon space as well.

items.statement: Non-aerospace defense revenue INR130-140 crores in H1 FY27, targeting 50/50 split by year end
items.quote: Not currently, but we probably will be there by the end of the year. On the INR345 crores, approximately INR130 crores-INR140 crores was non-aerospace and defense.

items.statement: Space and semiconductor revenue INR140 crores in H1 FY27 vs INR100 crores full year prior
items.quote: If you look at it last year, between space and semiconductors, we did INR100 crores, and this year we've already crossed INR140 in the first two quarters.

items.statement: Onboarded another leading global semiconductor equipment manufacturer
items.quote: A key highlight during the period was the successful onboarding of another leading global semiconductor equipment manufacturer.

items.statement: Now dealing with two large multinational semiconductor companies
items.quote: The semiconductor business, I did just mention that we have been able to get another customer on board, so now we are dealing with two very large respected multinational companies in the semicon domain.

items.statement: New 140,000 sq ft facility in Aerospace Park with option to expand to 210,000 sq ft, commencing early next quarter
items.quote: As part of these celebrations, we inaugurated our new facility within the Aerospace Park. This additional facility, taken on lease, comprises of approximately 140,000 sq ft, with an option to expand to 210,000 sq ft, and is expected to commence early next quarter.

items.statement: Inventory months improved from 7.98 to 6.67, target 4 months (3 turns) over 24 months
items.quote: Despite operating at a significantly larger scale, inventory carrying levels have improved from 7.98 months in quarter two of FY 2026 to 6.67 months in the second quarter of FY 2027.

items.statement: Internal target to be a four-month inventory company over next 24 months
items.quote: The internal target of Rossell is to be a three-turn inventory company, that means a four-month inventory company. We should see a good improvement on this quarter on quarter moving forward, or year on year.

items.statement: INR300 crores capital raise used for debt repayment and growth
items.quote: It's a mix of both. A lot of it is going to be used for strengthening our balance sheet and repaying back some of the loans. It's also going to be used for our future growth, for operational excellence, and infrastructure.

items.statement: Interest cost reduction expected from Q3 FY27 as working capital loans repaid
items.quote: We should see a benefit of that starting in the third quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: Completed INR300 crores capital raise with SBI Mutual Fund and Kotak Mutual Fund
items.quote: Another landmark achievement during the period was the successful completion of our INR300 crores capital raise, which was met with overwhelming interest from the institutional investor community.

items.statement: No further fundraise planned anytime soon
items.quote: Not anytime soon. This fundraise will take the company to a different level. This is what the company needed on today's basis, looking at the demand, what we foresee to grow over the next three to four years.

items.statement: Employee strength 1,352 professionals, special bonus announced
items.quote: Our workforce continues to expand in line with business requirements, and we ended the period with a total employee strength of 1,352 professionals, representing one of our strongest competitive advantages.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR345 crores, EBITDA INR52 crores, PBT INR22.3 crores
items.quote: The revenue after the first six months is INR345 crores, with an EBITDA of INR52 crores and a profit before tax of INR22.3 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 highest ever quarterly revenue INR185.56 crores, EBITDA INR29 crores, PBT INR12.91 crores
items.quote: In the second quarter, Rossell Techsys reported its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR185.56 crores, representing a growth of 47% over the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Historically Q3 and Q4 are strongest quarters, expecting same trend
items.quote: Historically, the third and fourth quarters have always been the strongest quarters for Rossell Techsys, and we enter the second half of this financial year with considerable confidence and positive momentum.

items.statement: MRO capability established, partnering with big companies in India and US including Boeing
items.quote: We are already talking to some big companies where we can partner with them and become an MRO service partner in the Indian market. This MRO capability is also helping us do some work for Boeing and other companies in the U.S.

items.statement: Expects second half of FY27 to be stronger than first half
items.quote: As we had indicated in our earlier calls, we expect the second half of FY27 to be stronger than the first half.

items.statement: Seeing continued interest from large pharma and increased traction from integrated outsourcing model
items.quote: We are seeing continued interest from large pharma, increased traction from our integrated outsourcing model, and steady progress on our capacity expansion programme.

items.statement: Uptick in enquiries from biotech customers pointing to revival in biotech sector
items.quote: We also witnessed an uptick in enquiries from Biotech customers, that points to a revival in the biotech sector.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 28% of revenue for Q2 FY27 and H1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was 28% of the revenue and was in line with the year-on-year margin trajectory. For the first half, EBITDA margins stood at 28%.

items.statement: Added one molecule to late-phase pipeline and one molecule moved from late-phase to commercial
items.quote: Over the quarter, we added one molecule to our late-phase pipeline, while one molecule moved from late-phase to commercial.

items.statement: Incurred INR621 crores capex in H1 FY27, on track for INR1,100-1,300 crores full year FY27
items.quote: We have incurred expenditure of approximately INR621 crores during the first six months of fiscal '27, of which INR358 crores was incurred in Q2. We remain on track with our overall capex plan of INR1,100 crores-INR1,300 crores for fiscal '27.

items.statement: Expanded small molecule manufacturing capacity of 220 KL at Bidar ready, final quality trials underway before commercial batches
items.quote: The expanded small molecule manufacturing capacity at Bidar, of around 220 KL, is now ready. We are currently completing the final quality trials at the site ahead of commencing commercial batches.

items.quote: As a result, the commissioning of the additional capacity of 225 KL is now expected to be available by early Q3 of fiscal '28, compared with our earlier timelines.

items.quote: We have also commenced the design work on our new manufacturing site in Telangana. The planning and design process is progressing, and we currently expect to break ground in Q4 of fiscal '27.

items.quote: The CRO and the CDMO businesses contributed to 38% and 62% of the half-yearly revenue, respectively.

items.quote: Building on this success this quarter, we have converted another large pharma relationship into a similar strategic engagement. We are also working on extending this model to other large pharmaceutical companies.

items.quote: The two integrated programs that Krishna mentioned in his speech is from the 19 out of 25.

items.quote: I would believe over the next two, three years that some of these things in terms of relationships and strategic focus from the customer end changes from a Sai perspective, some of the top 10 customers would itself rejig and then would come back in a different order.

items.quote: The advantage increasingly lies with CRDMOs that have scientific depth, infrastructure, and customer relationships to take on larger, more strategic engagements.

items.quote: I do not see any impact from that, from the CDMO sector. If anything, you have more molecules in the clinic, that helps the development side. I see AI as a net positive for India.

items.quote: These contract negotiations always move slow. Nothing moves fast. For us to go come and predict where it is, so they never give you timelines on anything maturing. Again, look, it may or may not mature as well.

items.quote: general True North target of INR3,000 crores that we've given for FY 2030, we continue to be optimistic about that while continuing to reduce our leverage. items.statement: Capacity utilization improved to 67% in Q2 FY27 from 65% in Q1; installed capacity ~41,000 tons currently
items.quote: Capacity utilization improved to 67% in Q2 from 65% in Our installed capacity currently stands at approximately 41,000 tons

items.statement: Raw material prices rose 40-45% due to West Asia conflict and shipping costs; crude decline helps but shipping cost larger component
items.quote: First, average prices across our key polymers rose by 40% to 45% and prices that had begun to stabilize in Q1 of FY '27 moved sharply higher once again compared to Q4 of FY '26.

items.statement: Price revisions implemented in domestic market second week of November; export prices fixed at order confirmation
items.quote: For domestic business, we are taking a gross change in the second week of this month, we are trying to roll out that change. And for other customers, we would have been able to pass only 50% up to now.

items.statement: Launched Hydration range and new categories in domestic market; 36 new customers added in H1 FY27
items.quote: We added 36 new customers during the first half of this year and introduced a new Hydration range of bottles, jars, alongside launches of many other product categories.

items.statement: Bamboo facility commercial production starts mid-November 2026; split-processing model with Guwahati and Khatalwada
items.quote: commence in mid-November 2026, with sales beginning in Q4 FY '27. We expect revenue from this facility in Q4 of FY '27. The split-processing model is now in place with engineering bamboo boards produced at Guwahati and value -added engineering undertaken at Khatalwada

items.statement: US customer stationery category moved to core assortment; expected to become second largest customer by end FY27
items.quote: So we are expecting that this customer will be our second largest customer by end of FY '27.

items.statement: US revenue share dropped to 10% in Q2 from 19% in Q1 due to shipment timing; EU 59%, UK 10%
items.quote: The United States contributed approximately 10% of revenue this quarter compared with approximately 19% in Q1. This reflects the timing of shipments rather than any loss of business.

items.statement: Polymer processing volume 6,910 MT in Q2 FY27 (+9% QoQ); H1 volume 13,234 MT (-7% YoY)
items.quote: Volume of polymers processed in Q2 FY '27 was 6,910 metric tons. This compares with 6,323 metric tons in Q1 FY '27, an increase of 9% and 6,864 metric tons in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: MoU with North East Cane and Bamboo Development Council under Ministry of Development of North East Region for policy support
items.quote: Our memorandum of understanding with North East Cane and Bamboo Development Council under the Ministry of Development of North East Region provides a structured policy support entry into this ecosystem.

items.statement: Fixed costs increased due to labor and staff at new Khatalwada and Bamboo facilities carried ahead of full utilization
items.quote: Our fixed cost has also increased relatively to H1 FY '26. This is on account of labor and staff costs at our new Khatalwada and Bamboo facilities, which we are carrying ahead of our full utilization.

items.statement: Acquired 51% stake in Drashti Surfaces for up to INR31.12 crores plus loan commitment up to INR20 crores
items.value: INR31.12 crores equity + INR20 crores loan
items.quote: I am pleased to share that yesterday we announced the acquisition of 51% gross stake in Drashti Surfaces Private Limited for an investment of up to INR31.12 crores along with a loan commitment of up to INR20 crores.

items.statement: Drashti laminates plant at 70-75% utilization, veneer plant at 45-50%; surplus FSI of 180,000 sq ft at Bhilad factory for expansion
items.quote: Currently, Drashti has 70% to 75% capacity utilization in the laminates plant which they are achieving at present. In a veneer plant, we are achieving close to 45% to 50% capacity.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: Our intention is to grow at least 25% to 30% CAGR in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin 36%, PAT margin 26.5%; acquired entities at 18-19% EBITDA; blended EBITDA ~37%, PAT 25-26%
items.quote: In our core business, which is being driven by Euro Pratik and Glorio, excluding our acquired entities, we have achieved a gross margin of 44.8%, in spite of a material and freight cost pressure. The EBITDA margin stood at 36%, and net profit margin stood at 26.5%.

items.statement: Wall panels 50-55% of revenue, laminates rest; veneers to add significant contribution post-Drashti
items.quote: 50% to 55% would be the broad range which will be contributed by the wall panels, and rest of the composition would be contributed by laminates. And now with Drashti we will have a significant contribution from the veneer.

items.statement: 75% of core business sales from products launched within 12-14 months
items.quote: Like if you see almost 75% of the sales driven in the core business is of the products launched within 12 to 14 months which we have launched.

items.statement: Drashti supplies to top builders Lodha, Adani, Rustomjee, Godrej; URO Veneer World retail outlets give direct customer feedback
items.quote: Also, the last acquisition which we have done they are mainly into projects. They are supplying to all the top builders in and around Mumbai like Lodha, Adani, Rustomjee, Godrej.

items.statement: Working capital ~150 days +/-10% excluding URO Veneer World consolidation distortion
items.quote: Having said that, if we exclude that, our working capital remains in the same range around 150 days plus or minus 10%, which is in line with the past few years.

items.statement: Monthly net cash surplus of INR7.5 crores from operations; acquisitions funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Even – net cash from the operations on a monthly run rate basis, we currently enjoy a net cash surplus of INR7.5 crores on a monthly basis, which adds a fuel for our growth expansions and inorganic acquisitions.

items.statement: Company aims to remain net debt-free; comfortable cash position maintained for acquisitions
items.quote: So company has always remained and tried to remain a net debt-free company, and comfortable cash positions was always there.

items.statement: Drashti peak capacity can generate INR180 crores turnover; margin expansion expected as utilization rises from current 16-17% EBITDA
items.quote: At a peak level, if you convert the present capacity into INR terms, we can generate safely INR180 crores of turnover at a peak level capacity utilization, point number one.

items.statement: Core business maintained margins despite crude, logistics, freight cost increases; most products made outside India
items.quote: Also there were a lot of challenges in terms of most of our products are made outside India. So, in terms of the crude, logistics, the costs have gone up, but still we have maintained the margins profitability of the core business.

items.statement: Drashti strong in overseas markets; will strengthen Euro Pratik's US and UAE subsidiaries
items.quote: Third is the overseas market. Drashti is very strong in terms of the overseas market so this will strengthen Euro Pratik including its US and UAE subsidiary.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, crude oil volatility, elevated raw material costs, rising freight expenses creating margin pressures
items.quote: The quarter gone by witnessed a challenging operating environment marked by ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, volatility in the crude oil prices, elevated raw material costs, and rising freight expenses.

items.statement: Wall panel manufacturing may be evaluated in stages at Drashti's surplus 180,000 sq ft FSI after integrating veneers and laminates
items.quote: However, it lays an important groundwork for a future further wall panel manufacturing base as Drashti has a surplus land and a room to build a manufacturing facility in 180,000 square feet balance FSI which is enough to expand.

items.statement: Future acquisitions considered if they fit one-stop solution vision; ROCE target 18-20% for targets
items.quote: Having said that, in future, a similar opportunity if arises and if it fits in the Euro Pratik's larger vision to provide a the one-stop solution for the surface decorative, we will consider those type of opportunities as well.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 30-40% for FY27 based on historical 40% CAGR
items.quote: I strongly assume that this year also will be growing 30% to 40% depending on the situation.

items.statement: Volume growth expected to increase across all segments subject to raw material availability
items.quote: Overall, I can say that, of course, the company is a growth path and the volumes are going to go up only.

items.statement: Copper cathode Phase I capex approximately INR120 crores for entire value-added copper complex
items.quote: Approximately around INR120 crores of the capex will be in the entire land building shared power and the machines and the other infrastructure.

items.statement: Plastic recycling facility capex of around INR15 crores targeting Q3 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: The second is our dedicated plastic recycling facility with a planned capital expenditure of around INR15 crores. We are targeting commencement of operations in quarter 3 financial year '27.

items.statement: Copper anode plant both phases commissioned, total installed capacity 1,600 metric tons per month
items.quote: Both phases of copper anode plant, each with a capacity of 800 metric tons per month have now been commissioned, taking our total installed capacity to 1,600 metric tons per month.

items.statement: Copper cathode Phase I commissioning imminent, Phase II targeted for Q4 FY27

In fact, the commissioning is at a very advanced stage and would be executed any day from now. For Phase II, we are targeting quarter 4 financial year '27.

items.statement: Copper wire rod and Busbar & Profiles facilities targeted for Q3 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: The copper wire rod facility has planned capacity of 600 metric tons per month. The Busbar & Profiles facility has planned capacity of 1,500 metric tons per month. Both are targeted for commission in quarter 3 financial year '27.

items.statement: Antimony facility planned output 100 metric tons per month targeting Q3 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: The planned output is approximately 100 metr ic tons per month, and we continue to target commissioning in quarter 3 financial year '27

items.quote: With input capacity to process approximately 71,000 metric tons of scrap annually, the plant can produce around 25,000 metric tons of copper products per annum at full capacity ramp-up.

items.statement: Long-term opportunity in organized nonferrous metal recycling with customers prioritizing recycled materials
items.quote: We continue to believe there's a meaningful long-term opportunity in organized nonferrous metal recycling. Customers are placing greater importance on recycled materials and source efficiency and substantial manufacturing.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 4.2% in Q2 FY27 from 4% in Q1 FY27, H1 FY27 margin 4.1%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 4.2% in quarter 2 FY27 compared to 4% in quarter 1 FY27, resulting in an H1 FY27 margin of 4.1%.

items.statement: Expect some EBITDA margin moderation due to evolving product mix but absolute EBITDA to grow with volume
items.quote: we continue to scale up our copper volume, we expect some moderation in EBITDA margins due to the evolving product mix. However, the increase in volume is expected to drive healthy Mayank Pareek: growth in absolute EBITDA

items.statement: Copper EBITDA per ton improved to INR37,237 in Q2 FY27 from INR31,825 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA per ton also has improved from approximately INR31,825 to INR37,237.

items.quote: EBITDA per ton has improved from INR18,660 to INR19,310 per ton.

items.quote: So, we have shown around close to INR14,434. This will generally improve because it's an initial phase, and we have just commissioned in the last quarter.

items.statement: Downstream value addition from anode to cathode to wire rod to busbar expected to add 2-3% to bottom line on average
items.quote: Overall, on an average, I believe it would be between 2% and 3% of addition to the bottom line from the present levels.

items.statement: Value-added copper sales volumes approximately 3,575 metric tons in H1 FY27
items.quote: In the first half of financial year '27, sales volumes were approximately 3,575 metric tons.

items.quote: The unit has commenced commercial operations and recorded approximately INR25.4 crores of revenue during quarter 2.

items.quote: Broadly, I think it will be 50 to 70 days.

items.quote: Importantly, we also generated positive cash flow from operations of approximately INR137 crores, (Please note INR137 crores was mentioned erroneously, it should be read as approximately INR 130 crores).

items.statement: Net cash inflow from operating activities of INR129 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: During the first half, we have also generated approximately INR129 crores of net cash inflow from operating activities.

items.quote: The net debt to the equity has improved to around 0.5x from 0.7x at the end of the March 2026.

items.quote: Presently also, we do domestic sourcing close to 38%, 39% of the overall purchase what we make.

items.statement: Confident of raw material availability for next four months until March 2027
items.quote: I'm very confident up to this current year, March, we have all the raw material for next four months to come.

items.statement: RCM on e-waste scrap not expected to significantly help sourcing unless GST on scrap purchases reduced
items.quote: RCM will not help much because the reason is RCM got own challenges and RCM is notified, but I don't think it's going to much help in sourcing side. not unless the government reduce the GST on the scrap purchases.

items.statement: Kuwait project machinery ready, shipment expected within 30 days, commissioning to follow

Those were not available, but the development of last two weeks is that those are also available. And I believe the machine would now be transported over the next, I mean, shipped out over the next 30 days.

items.statement: Geopolitical and shipping disruptions in West Asia affecting Kuwait project timeline and freight costs
items.quote: We are also closely watching the geopolitical situation and shipping disruptions, especially in the West Asia. Our diversified sourcing relationship and hedging practices helped us to manage the risk, but we remain cautious about development outside our control.

items.quote: So, one quarter, you will see one quarter it's not a steady working cycle. It will have up and down cycle of the number of days. like it can go to sometimes 60 days and sometimes goes to 45 days. So, 15, 20 days cycle will be up and down.

items.quote: Copper and copper ingot volume increased by around 74% year-on-year quarter 2 FY27, while our copper business including the new initiative contributed 8% of total revenue.

items.quote: This will be, this year we 750 tons of cathode we are planning to produce. Substantially around 600 tons of wire rods, and it depends on the value-added product, how much marketing we do.

items.quote: JRRL is a diversified multi -metal recycling company, although JRR L is one of the leading producers of leading in India. That accounts only for approximately 30% of company's overall turnover. Copper alone contributes more than 65% of our turnover

items.statement: Full-year FY27 guidance maintained at mid-teens revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margin

items.quote: Backed by a strong first half, though our guidance for full year FY27 was in mid -teens revenue growth and early double-digit EBITDA margin remains same.

items.statement: Invested INR8.7 billion in Q2 FY27 on tangible assets, mainly Sri City plant

items.quote: Commercial production for compressor begins in quarter three of this financial year, and air conditioner manufacturing follows in quarter four, around January 2027.

items.statement: B2B revenue currently 10-11% of total, targeting 15%+ in three years
items.quote: Today, B2B is approximately 10%-11% of our total revenue, and over the next three years, our goal is to meaningfully grow this share, and we believe 15% plus is a realistic and achievable target.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 63 bps to 9.5%; Home Appliance segment margin improved to 8.7% from 8.2%; Home Entertainment margin improved to 12.9% from 12.6%
items.quote: Our profitability kept pace with this growth, with EBITDA rising sharply by 28% to INR7.01 billion and margin expanding meaningfully by 63 basis points to 9.5%.

items.quote: This year, we have already taken two rounds of price increase. These were selective increases, not same across all products.

items.quote: We have just come out from Q2, where our every single product category has delivered a double-digit revenue growth.

items.quote: Our fully automatic portion has now crossed 60% of our overall washing machine sales.

items.statement: Export countries expanded from 50 to 68; distribution partners from 112 to 151; Essential Series in 21 countries; expect significant YoY export growth
items.quote: We have expanded our presence from 50-68 countries, and our distribut ion network has grown from 112 -151 partners.

items.quote: This reflects a well-planned buildup in our working capital of INR6.56 billion, as we invested proactively in channel stocking ahead of the festive and wedding season.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance INR50.51 billion as of September 2026, down from INR57.07 billion at quarter start due to working capital investment
items.quote: Moving to our balance sheet, our cash and bank balance stood at a healthy INR50.51 billion as of September 2026, compared to INR57.07 billion at the start of the quarter.

items.statement: B2B Information Display business emerged as second profit engine alongside TV with steadier margin profile

items.quote: Today, I am very proud to announce that we are entering the Vehicle Solutions business in India. Vehicle Solutions is one of LG Electronics' key global B2B business, covering automotive infotainment and telematics products.

items.statement: Received Great Place To Work Award for third consecutive year
items.value: Great Place To Work Award third time

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties remain but export strategy diversified across countries to offset regional difficulties
items.quote: As for the geopolitical environment, uncertainties remain, and we are not immune to their effects. However, by strengthening our country portfolio through geographic expansion, we are not overly dependent on any single country or region.

items.statement: Guiding full-year operating EBITDA margin to 24% plus, up from prior 23% plus guidance
items.quote: If you remember, we last quarter said it will be about 23% plus, which is over our 22%, 23% said earlier. We are happy to report that now we are guiding it to 24% plus for the full year.

items.quote: Coming to operating EBITDA, which is at 25%, which is up over our Q1 number.

items.quote: Pricing continues to remain stable, driven by our focus on specialty or differentiated products.

items.quote: On New Jersey facility, our c apex or the fixed asset base grew by INR85 crore s, whereas the cash payout was INR29 crores. We had INR55 crores worth of non-cash item in the form of right-of-use

items.statement: Peptide orders from Indian customers ~INR 150 crores in last six months; large peptide capacity investments planned in India; China glass-lined orders improving driven by CDMO; Europe defence (TNT/nitrocellulose) and US semiconductors growi
