items.quote: We have closed our U.K. facility and implemented the workforce reduction plan in Germany. The European restructuring program is ongoing. Across these operations, our objective is consistent: address structural losses, reduce fixed costs, improve capacity utilization, and establish a more competitive operating model.

items.statement: H1 FY27 European loss-making entities EBITDA loss ~INR 43 crores; expect Germany to break even in next few quarters, profitable by FY28; Switzerland small (30 people) but expensive, reducing 8-10 people for significant savings
items.quote: During H1 FY 2027, our loss-making European entities reported an EBITDA loss of approximately INR 43 crores, impacting the group's reported profitability.

items.statement: Diversification progressing: non-traditional sectors growing (PPT, HET, PST); reducing dependence on chemicals/pharma; peptides, nuclear, thermal, defence, semiconductors, critical minerals as new growth drivers
items.quote: We are seeing the progress on the non-traditional sectors. This will continue to grow because the three businesses where we need to grow much faster, which is PPT, HET, PST, you will see much more growth. So, our share in the non-traditional sectors will keep growing up, and over a period of time, our dependency on chemicals and pharma will keep reducing that we have seen in the past.

items.statement: CRT division: Q2 revenue INR 500 crores (flat YoY, +7% QoQ); order intake INR 556 crores (+15% YoY, +11% QoQ); H1 revenue INR 966 crores (+5% YoY); H1 order intake INR 1,058 crores (+19% YoY)
items.quote: Corrosion Resistant Technologies reported revenue of INR 500 crores during the quarter, flat year-on-year and up 7% sequentially. Order intake stood at INR556 crores, up 11% sequentially and up 15% year-on-year.

items.statement: PPT division: Q2 revenue INR 331 crores (+34% YoY, +30% QoQ); order intake INR 364 crores (+85% YoY, flat QoQ); H1 revenue INR 586 crores (+29% YoY); H1 order intake INR 731 crores (+74% YoY)
items.quote: Moving to PPT, the division reported revenue of INR 331 crores, growing 30% sequentially and 34% year-on-year. Order intake stood at INR 364 crores, which is flat Q-o-Q and up 85% year-on-year.

items.statement: HET division: Q2 revenue INR 92 crores (+38% YoY, +24% QoQ); order intake INR 201 crores (+254% YoY, +248% QoQ); H1 revenue INR 165 crores (+17% YoY); H1 order intake INR 258 crores (+306% YoY)
items.quote: HET reported revenue of INR 92 crores, growing 24% sequentially and 38% year-on-year. Order intake during the quarter stood at INR 201 crores, which is up 248% on a sequential basis and 254% year-on-year.

items.statement: PST division: Q2 revenue INR 142 crores (+57% YoY, +8% QoQ); H1 revenue INR 273 crores (+51% YoY); H1 order intake INR 157 crores (incl INR 77 crores in Q2)
items.quote: PST reported revenues of INR 142 crores, growing 8% sequentially and 57% year-on-year. For H1 FY 2027, revenue stood at INR273 crores, representing a growth of 51% year-on-year. Order intake was INR157 crores for the first half, including INR77 crores in Q2.

items.statement: Key pharma customers in India: Divi's, MSN, Sai Life adding capacity; global CDMOs like Cambrex investing; China CDMOs adding glass-lined capacity; nuclear orders from NPCIL and Megha Engineering; defence orders from NATO-sponsored projects
items.quote: In India, if you see over the last maybe two quarters, it is really mainly pharma and Hyderabad pharma, Divi's, MSN, Sai Life, these companies continue to add so, that is the normal kind of play here in India.

items.statement: Export momentum improving: large glass-lined order won in Italy (USD 5 million); Middle East and Africa adding to HET backlog; Europe defence inquiries increasing; US semiconductor demand growing for Edlon
items.quote: We recently won another large glass-lined order just yesterday in Italy in the tune of USD 5 million. So, things are improving. There is some kind of investment coming back.

items.statement: Glass-lined pricing improving in India and globally; operating leverage benefits expected as volumes increase; Shikhar cost reduction program to benefit from higher volumes
items.quote: We already see an improvement here in India in glass-lined prices. I think across the world you'll see some of that. And then with the operating leverage kicking in with the volumes now being much, much higher.

items.statement: Focus on disciplined working capital management alongside debt reduction and cash generation; no specific debtor/inventory days mentioned
items.quote: We remain focused on improving cash generation and managing working capital with discipline.

items.statement: H1 PAT INR 57 crores (+20% YoY), surpassing full FY26 profit; improving EBITDA to PAT conversion a priority; FCF positive enabling debt repayment
items.quote: For H1 FY 2027, reported PAT stood at INR 57 crores, up 20% year-on-year, with a margin of 2.9%, which has already surpassed the FY 2026 full-year profit.

items.statement: No active acquisition plans; would only pursue if it brings growth and high profitability without restructuring needs; lessons learned from past acquisitions
items.quote: From an acquisition perspective, there's no plan right now. There's a lot of work to happen, but at the same time, we keep seeing, meeting, talking, so that's an ongoing process. Again, if an acquisition has to make sense, it has to make sense from the perspective of growth.

items.statement: Europe chemical industry reset with plant closures and low investment impacting European operations; restructuring execution risk; dependence on pharma/CDMO/peptide cycle; forex volatility in debt structure
items.quote: Europe's chemical industry is going through a major reset with multiple plant closures and low investment in new large-scale capacity. These conditions have particularly impacted and affected some of our European operations, where relatively high-cost base is becoming difficult to sustain at current business volumes.

items.statement: CRISIL ESG score improved to 61 in FY26 from 50 in FY25 (strong category vs below average); reflects progress in ESG framework and responsible business practices
items.quote: On sustainability, I am pleased to share that CRISIL has awarded GMM Pfaudler an ESG score of 61 for FY 2026, placing us in a strong category compared with a score of 50 in FY 2025, which was classified as below average.

items.statement: No order cancellations; only slight deferments; expect additional urgent supply queries due to European freezer hacking incident
items.quote: There are no cancellations whatsoever. Yash Somani: Yes. So that's what I was asking. Milan Dalal: Yes. So in fact, they are very different. It's not giving any other hope, but generally, like post- COVID, post war, we have seen numbers, there would be a pent

items.statement: 60% of 3,300 MT unshipped orders shipped in October; remaining spillover to be completed in Q3
items.quote: Yes, almost 60% of the material already shipped out in the month of October itself because as Mr. Milan told that freight situation is much better. And yes, we expect that entire carryforwards or spillover will be completed in Q3 only.

items.statement: Contracts on FOB basis; no penalty costs for delayed shipments; freight surcharge issue resolved by customer with shipping company
items.quote: No, because our contract is on FOB basis. So it is more from a customer point of view because we have to take the approval for the freight. Since the freight rate was very high, the customer was not agreeing, and now it is starting softening.

items.statement: Spray Drying division EBITDA margin around 18%
items.quote: It's a good EBITDA. I mean it's a very positive EBITDA side. Its EBITDA will be around 18% EBITDA in the Spray Drying division.

items.statement: Spray Drying capacity expansion of 120 MT per annum; commercial production likely by mid to end January; Gujarat warehouse completion by mid-December
items.quote: We have taken a capex for our enhancing the capacity by around 120 metric tons per annum. So that is the capex in the books, part of the capex and in the capital WIP. And by January, mid or by end of January, the commercial production likely to start.

items.statement: Spray Drying H1 volume 474 MT (15% growth), value INR11 cr (7% growth); H2 volume expected >550 MT; annual volume growth 18-19%
items.quote: In H1, I'm telling. H1, we will be having around 474 metric tons, which is 15% volume growth. And value-wise, it is round INR11 crores with value growth is around 7%. But next H2, we are expecting that it should cross 550 metric ton.

items.statement: Overall volume growth likely 17-18% YoY; no revenue guidance due to agricultural commodity price uncertainty; cost-plus model
items.quote: For us, it will be difficult to give you any revenue guideline, but we can always tell that overall volume growth likely to be around 17% to 18% compared to last year because we are in agricultural commodities.

items.statement: Long-term borrowing increased to INR91 cr from INR53 cr due to Central Bank facility for shipment delays; repayable over 4 years; no further borrowing needed; short-term borrowings to reduce by March-end
items.quote: That is recently due to this war disturbance, Central Bank has extended some long-term facility to us due to overcome this delay in shipment and all these things. So that we awaited. That was a very timely and competitive interest rate. So we have availed that. That has gone up, and that has to be repaid over a period of 4 years.

items.statement: September balance sheet shows peak inventory, creditors and borrowings due to mango season completion in August; September-to-September comparison shows similar range
items.quote: You are comparing the March balance sheet with the September, for our organization, Mango contributing more than 72% to 73%. So mango production completed just first week of August. So, September balance sheet is having always a higher - I mean highest inventory, highest sundry creditors, these are the 2 as well as highest borrowing if you compare the whole year.

items.statement: Forex loss of INR10.6 cr from forward contracts due to rupee depreciation; notional loss; company decided to stop forward covers from April; will discuss penal interest with banks
items.quote: It's a forward contract because to comply with the RBI guideline against the export sale, we are supposed to hedge it if banks may penalize with the higher interest rate. So this thing is continuing with us for last several years.

items.statement: Selected by National Horticulture Board for cluster development in Nashik region onboarding 15,000+ farmers; PM virtually inaugurated program on Oct 30; government gives 35-38% capex subsidy for frozen capacity expansion
items.quote: Under the new scheme of - though it is mentioned in the investor note, the National Horticulture Board, we were one of the 12 companies which got selected for doing the cluster development and Honorable Prime Minister, in fact, virtually inaugurated that program on 30th of October.

items.statement: Strong traction in US and GCC markets; tied up with Saudi customer for frozen mango pulp and vegetables; expect 25-30% average growth in frozen segment over next 3 years
items.quote: We are getting a very good traction in the U.S. market, as you rightly said, and that segment is growing, and we are also focusing that segment. And now recently, we participated in the Gulf food.

items.statement: Revenue split: Pulp (Mango, Guava, Papaya, Tomato) 80%+; Frozen, Spray Drying and others ~20%; Spice business (Kusum) separate entity, not in standalone
items.quote: On the revenue breakup, I can tell you that pulp content, that is Mango, Guava, Papaya, Tomato, everything contribute 80% plus and Frozen and Spray Drying and other segment is growing around 20%.

items.statement: Supply to major brands (Pepsi, Coke etc.) on cost-plus model; working on pricing strategy for Spray Drying and frozen to capture inflation; pulping segment pricing discussions ongoing with brands
items.quote: Yes, we work as a cost-plus model as we discussed. In the cost-plus model, the issue came that when the dispatch is delaying and when the dispatch is getting delayed, they give the interest reimbursement.

items.statement: Promoter (Dalal family) intends to consolidate holding at current low valuations; Board meeting held Nov 5; debarred from trading until Monday; evaluating secondary market or private acquisition
items.quote: Plans are on whether one should do it in the secondary market, one should look at some private thing. There are a lot of regulations to do about it. Currently, the Board meeting was just over on the 5th. So I am debarred until Monday.

items.statement: Frozen segment at full capacity; target 3x growth in 3 years; government cluster development provides 35-38% capex subsidy for frozen capacity expansion
items.quote: Our objective is that in next 3 years, frozen segment should go to the 3x level. That's the way we are working because that's giving us better margin and better revenue everything.

items.statement: Green Top brand launched in North India, reaching Kashmir; monthly sales INR60-70 lakh growing phenomenally; South India launch soon; building own brand in domestic and international markets
items.quote: North, we have launched our Green Top brand, and it's really doing very well. Though we are very low - I mean, just started monthly sales figure, maybe around INR60 lakhs, INR70 lakhs, but it's growing in a phenomenal pace.

items.statement: Number 1 in Mango pulping; Jain Irrigation not in tomatoes; no direct listed peer with same combination (pulping, frozen, spray dry, Tetra Recart); non-listed players at #2, #3 positions
items.quote: We are number 1 in Mango, which is there. Jain currently is not into tomatoes in a big way. So there is no such direct peer competition doing it. There are a lot of players in the non-listed segment, which are at the number 2, number 3 position.

items.statement: Forex MTM loss of INR5 cr in cash flow statement; additional INR5 cr loss from sales vs realization gap due to forward contract accounting; total forex loss INR10.6 cr
items.quote: Yes. Okay. This is the MTM entry. Another entry comes in the books, that is sale versus realization. When your forward books are, say, INR100 and rupee depreciated to INR110, then your sales has to book at INR110, but realization will come at INR100.

items.statement: Export margins better than domestic for frozen (100% better); Spray Drying 95% domestic with 18-19% EBITDA; Pulping mix: Alphonso export premium, Totapuri domestic better margin
items.quote: If you talk about the frozen segment, yes, margin definitely in the export is much better than the domestic 100%, and that's a good part. Spray Drying is 95% is the domestic. So we have a good margin.

items.statement: Cluster development to control pesticide use and agricultural practices for quality raw material; climate change and pesticide issues causing procurement uncertainty and order losses
items.quote: For that, we have joined hand with government for the cluster development where we will have a full control on the pesticide uses as well as agricultural practices. So if we get the - it's basically garbage in, garbage out.

items.statement: No equity raise mentioned; promoter considering secondary market or private acquisition to consolidate holding
items.quote: Plans are on whether one should do it in the secondary market, one should look at some private thing. There are a lot of regulations to do about it.

items.statement: October saw highest ever monthly Spray Drying sales (100 MT); freight rates softening and container availability improving post geopolitical changes
items.quote: In fact, we are very happy to say that in the month of October, we have seen the highest sales in Spray Drying division in history of Foods and Inns. We never able to do such. So that's a very positive part.

items.statement: Guided annual growth of 20-30% for Emerging Market LAP and 35-40% for GROx
items.quote: Going forward, as indicated in Slide 10 of our investor presentation, we are guiding annual growth of 20% to 30% for Emerging Market LAP and 35% to 40% for GROx, with GROx earlier growth have come off of a low base.

items.statement: Target ROA of 3% to 3.5% by FY29 on pro forma basis
items.quote: Our FY29 objective is a steady-state ROA ranging between 3% to 3.5% as against 2.7% today on a pro forma basis.

items.statement: Quarterly operating cost guidance of INR490 crores for FY27
items.quote: On cost, quarterly operating cost has come down from INR205 crores in the fourth quarter of FY26 to INR127 crores this quarter, in line with our FY27 guidance of INR490 crores and above.

items.statement: Guided prime intermediated book rundown of 15-20% per year
items.quote: On the rundown of the prime intermediated book, we guided 15% to 20% a year.

items.statement: Expect every quarter to be better than previous quarter on profit
items.quote: From a profit guidance perspective, every quarter should be better than the previous quarter.

items.statement: AUM at INR15,019 crores, up 23% YoY, flat QoQ by design
items.quote: Total AUM stood at INR15,019 crores, up 23% year-on-year. It was flat quarter-on-quarter by design.

items.statement: Focused businesses (Emerging Market LAP and GROx) now 53% of AUM at INR7,929 crores
items.quote: Our two focused businesses, Emerging Market LAP and GROx now account for INR7,929 crores or 53% of our assets under management of INR15,019 crores.

items.statement: Emerging Market LAP AUM grew to INR4,268 crores, up 10% QoQ and 42% YoY
items.quote: In this business, AUM has now grown to INR4,268 crores, up 10% in the quarter and 42% over the year.

items.statement: GROx AUM grew to INR3,661 crores, up 22% QoQ from INR1,270 crores a year ago
items.quote: GROx AUM has grown to INR3,661 crores, up 22% in the quarter and from INR1,270 crores 12 months ago.

items.statement: Defocused book fell 13% in quarter and 32% over 9 months to INR7,090 crores (47% of AUM)
items.quote: Through repayments and foreclosure, the book fell 13% in this quarter alone and 32% over 9 months and is now 47% of AUM.

items.statement: Portfolio yield rose to 18.7%, up 53 bps QoQ and 108 bps YoY
items.quote: Portfolio yield now was up to 18.7%, which is up 53 basis points on the quarter and 108 basis points on the year.

items.statement: Net interest margin improved with cost of borrowing at 10.19% on total debt of INR10,973 crores
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing was 10.19% on total debt of about INR10,973 crores.

items.statement: Gross NPA stable at 2.7%, collection efficiency 97%, provision coverage 45%
items.quote: Asset quality was stable with gross NPA of 2.7% and collection efficiency of 97%.

items.statement: Focused businesses gross NPA 1.7% (EMLAP 2%, GROx 1.4%) vs defocused book 3.9%
items.quote: Gross NPA in the two focused business is 1.7% against 3.9% in the defocused book.

items.statement: Credit cost at 3.6% of average on-book loans (2% of average AUM for H1), within lifetime expected losses
items.quote: Credit cost was ₹86.9 crore, against ₹65.6 crore in the previous quarter, or 3.6% of average on-book loans against 2.8% earlier.

items.statement: Target average branch productivity of INR80-85 lakhs monthly disbursement
items.quote: Our target is to take the average productivity to INR80 lakhs to INR85 lakhs per month disbursal per branch in a month over the next few months.

items.statement: Liquidity of INR1,500 crores at quarter end, adequate for growth
items.quote: We closed the quarter with liquidity of about INR1,500 crores, which gives us adequate headroom to support growth.

items.statement: Borrowing mix 50-50 floating/fixed, floating rate reset mostly 1-year MCLR linked
items.quote: We are almost 50%-50%, 50% of our borrowings are on a floating rate basis. And generally, on the floating rate borrowings, the reset tenures are in 1 year.

items.statement: Expect 15-20 bps impact from recent rate hikes on longer term loans
items.quote: We do expect that there will be an impact of the recent rate hikes in our longer term loans as well, which can range between 15 bps to 20 bps.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 18.8% standalone, ~22% pro forma merged, well within headroom
items.quote: Our capital adequacy stand-alone today is 18.8% and about 22% on the merged pro forma basis.

items.statement: Plan to fund growth through FY29 without new equity
items.quote: This, coupled with the annuity-led income, would allow us to fund our plans through FY29 without any new equity required.

items.statement: Profectus Capital merger NCLT final hearing on 20th November, approved by shareholders/creditors 22nd September
items.quote: The merger of Profectus Capital into UGRO approved by shareholders and creditors on 22nd September has its NCLT final hearing on 20th November.

items.statement: Merger remeasures co-lend/DA income on behavioral tenure, adjusts goodwill/acquisition cost against reserves, no P&L charge
items.quote: Under the scheme, the income on our co-lend and assigned loans is remeasured on the life over which those loans are actually run based on observed repayment behavior rather than on their contractual life.

items.statement: Pro forma net worth after merger ~INR2,454 crores (INR158/share) vs reported INR3,029 crores (INR195/share)
items.quote: Pro forma net worth after the scheme is about INR2,454 crores or about INR158 per share against a reported book value of INR195 a share.

items.statement: Pro forma H1 PAT INR126.3 crores vs reported INR118.6 crores, ROA 2.7%, ROE 10.6%
items.quote: On a pro forma basis, reversals for the first half year fall from INR120.5 crores to about INR58 crores. And the first half profit after tax moved from INR118.6 crores to INR126.3 crores.

items.statement: Net disbursements INR3,159 crores in Q2 (highest ever), >INR1,000 crores each month
items.quote: Net disbursement for the quarter was INR3,159 crores, up 77% from a year ago and 24% from the previous quarter.

items.statement: Branch productivity: mature branches INR86 lakhs/month, 1-year branches INR60 lakhs/month, avg INR73 lakhs/month
items.quote: Average monthly disbursements per branch rose to about INR73 lakh per month this quarter from INR62 lakhs in the previous quarter and INR48 lakhs in FY26.

items.statement: GROx concentration risk with partners/geography being mitigated, diversifying in coming quarters
items.quote: One of the risks which we are very aware is not to be too concentrated with one particular partner or with one particular geography. And that we have been working quarter-on-quarter, and that is also we are mitigating and we will now be very well diversified in coming few quarters.

items.statement: GROx credit risk stable after 2 full loan cycles, short tenure allows quick repricing/tightening
items.quote: been now in this business from September 2024, so about 25 months complete. Typical tenure of the loan is about a year. So now we have seen 2 full cycles. And now we are very confident that given our technology platform expertise, and the business rule engine, the way it has worked, we don't see too much of credit risk significantly deviating from what we have seen so far

items.quote: two of our long-term strategic shareholders, which is IFU 15.5%, ADV, which is roughly around 9.5% Samena, which is currently not on our Board, but were on our Board, potentially may have come back to the Board there. For some internal reason, they have stepped out of the Board. Investors who are part of our Board and insider to the company are not in

items.statement: Rating surveillance expected to begin end of calendar year, results after that
items.quote: Our annual surveillance is around the corner. We expect the surveillance to begin by the end of the last quarter of the calendar year, and we should be out with the results after that.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue of INR 375-400 crore with 15-17% volume growth; targets INR 450-500 crore in FY28 with 20% volume growth
items.quote: See, this year, I think we'll be able to close around INR 375 crore to INR 400 crore rupees what we are aiming for. So, it can achievable if we grew by the 20% of volume growth.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margins of 24-25% in H2 FY27 subject to no sharp raw material price increase
items.quote: On profitability, we expect EBITDA margins to improve towards 24% to 25% in H2 FY27, subject to there being no further sharp increase in raw material prices.

items.statement: Long-term ambition to build INR 500 crore business and progressively move towards INR 1,000 crore
items.quote: Our ambition is to build a INR 500 crore business and progressively move towards INR 1,000 crore driven by volume growth, geographical expansion and stronger brand preference and manufacturing scalability.

items.statement: Greenfield facility in Gujarat with 1,500 tons/month capacity and estimated investment of INR 45-50 crore
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are working towards a greenfield facility in Gujarat with an initial capacity of 1,500 tons per month and an estimated investment of INR 45 crore to INR 50 crore.

items.statement: Debtor days currently elevated at ~160 days (mature markets 75-100 days, newer markets 120-150 days); targeting return to 120 days (FY23-24 levels) within 1-2 quarters; channel financing discussions underway
items.quote: We are aiming to maintain that debtor cycle what was into the FY '23-FY'24 that was around 120 days. So, it is a little higher side right now but as I always explain about the newer markets, newer geographies what we are developing. So, it is because of the ease of doing policies and because maintaining the relationship with the dealer and we are more focused to spread our width and go to the deep

items.statement: VAM price currently ~$1,000/ton (peaked at $1,100-1,150); company maintains 60-90 day inventory and direct import contracts; crude price decline expected to reduce VAM costs
items.quote: VAM price is right now it is $1,000 around and yes in between it was went around $1,100 - $1,150 at the time, if I talk about the last month, last one and a half month. But as I mentioned that we have procured our material. So right now, that the increased price is not affecting us.

items.statement: Maintains quality standards over price matching with lower-tier brands; runs two loyalty programs (dealer-reimbursed and direct-to-carpenter app-based)
items.quote: So, as a Euro we have been always focus ed on the quality and consistency into the quality. So, we have that lower grades also right now but we are not compromising any quality compromise regarding the price to match the prices with the regional very lower brands.

items.statement: Geopolitical situations, raw material fluctuations, and consumer buying behaviour affected Q1 real estate activity; VAM price volatility linked to crude and dollar
items.quote: But you know, the situation is about the geopolitical situations, the fluctuations in the raw materials also and that e ffect all over environment of the purchase and buying behaviour of the consumers also. Maybe if we can see into the quarter one, we observe that there are so many sites and so many real estate developments went slow into that journey.

items.statement: Booked business reached USD 106 billion, up from USD 96 billion in FY26 and USD 59 billion in FY23, reflecting 13% CAGR.
items.quote: Our booked business has reached USD 106 billion and providing strong growth and reflecting the confidence our customers place on Motherson across businesses and geographies.

items.statement: Full-year capex guidance of INR 6,000 crores with a range of plus or minus 10%.
items.quote: We incurred capex of INR1,971 crores in second quarter of current financial year, taking our first half capex to INR3,585 crores. This is in line with our full year guidance of INR6,000 crores with a range of plus or minus 10%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex was INR 3,585 crores (56% of H1 EBITDA); Q2 capex was INR 1,971 crores.
items.quote: We incurred capex of INR1,971 crores in second quarter of current financial year, taking our first half capex to INR3,585 crores.

items.statement: 17 facilities at various stages of development; 10 expected to become operational in FY27; one greenfield PCB facility became operational in Q2.
items.quote: our greenfield facilities, which will manufacture PCBs, became operational. This facility will provide valuable backward integration for our lighting and vision system businesses. We also announced five additional facility expansion during the quarter, taking the total number of facilities at various stages of development to 17. Of these, 10 are expected to become operational during the current fi

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 8.8%, down ~20 bps YoY due to acquisition integration; excluding acquisitions, margins improved YoY and sequentially.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 8.8% compared with 9% in Q2 FY 2026, representing a small contraction of approximately 20 basis points, but this was primarily attributable to the integration of the newly acquired businesses, which I mentioned before.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved ~20 bps to 8.8% despite commodity inflation.
items.quote: For the first half of FY 2027, EBITDA grew by 25% to INR6,457 crores, outpacing revenue growth. EBITDA margins improved by approximately 20 basis points to 8.8%, despite significant commodity cost inflation.

items.statement: Cost pass-throughs for commodities like copper, aluminium, polymers are ongoing but vary by contract, customer, product, and location; some resolved, some pending.
items.quote: We do have pass-throughs in some commodities, but some others, it also depends on customer, it depends on product, it depends on location. Yes, of course, during the quarter, of course, depending on the contracts with the customers, some things are also resolved. There are some things that are still pending.

items.statement: Global light vehicle production declined 2.3% YoY in H1 FY27 (China -5.5%, North America -3.8%, Europe -0.6%); India grew 15%. Commercial vehicle production grew 7.6% globally (North America +43.6%, India +18.9%).
items.quote: Global light vehicle production declined by 2.3% year-on-year, while China witnessed a decline of 5.5%. North America declined by 3.8%, and Europe just down at -0.6%. India, however, remained a clear bright spot, recording a growth of 15%.

items.statement: Expect positive momentum in commercial vehicle production to continue in H2 FY27.
items.quote: We expect this positive momentum in commercial vehicle production to continue in the second half of FY 2027.

items.statement: Non-automotive businesses growing: aerospace >20% YoY; consumer electronics robust revenue growth and improved profitability; GF3 plant trial production started, commercial production in Q4 FY27.
items.quote: Our aerospace business registered growth of more than 20% year-on-year during the quarter. We also announced the acquisition of Rotary Connectors during the quarter, further strengthening and broadening our aerospace and defence capabilities. Our consumer electronics business continues to build strong momentum, delivering robust revenue growth and improved profitability during the year. We have al

items.quote: We are doing all the German car makers. BMW is the biggest customer for Autoelectric. We are doing Daimler as well as Porsche and Audi.

items.statement: Autoelectric (wiring harness) consolidated for full quarter; Yutaka Giken (emerging business) consolidated for two months; combined annual revenue potential ~$2 billion in first full year.
items.quote: Both of these businesses put together, they have ability to give us, to start with, around annual revenue of around $2 billion or thereabout. That is what we should expect, generally speaking, in the first full year of operations.

items.statement: Acquired Rotary Connectors to strengthen aerospace and defence capabilities.
items.quote: We also announced the acquisition of Rotary Connectors during the quarter, further strengthening and broadening our aerospace and defence capabilities.

items.statement: Acquired Irillic in medical devices (diagnostics) to enhance capabilities and market visibility.
items.quote: We've also done an acquisition of a company called Irillic, which is making full devices in the diagnostics place, which is doing well.

items.statement: Leverage stable at 0.8x despite capex and acquisitions; within policy ceiling of 2.5x and internal target <1.5x. Effective net debt INR 11,292 crores (up from INR 9,757 crores in June) due to copper price, capex, lease liabilities from acqu
items.quote: Our leverage ratio remained stable at 0.8x despite significant capex investment and the acquisition of Autoelectric and Yutaka Giken. This remains comfortably within our financial policy ceiling of 2.5x and our internal aspiration of maintaining leverage below 1.5x.

items.statement: Strong liquidity of INR 1,747 crores; comfortable debt maturity profile.
items.quote: We ended the quarter with strong liquidity of INR1,747 crores and a comfortable debt maturity profile.

items.statement: Net debt increase driven by higher working capital due to copper price increase.
items.quote: Effective net debt increased to INR11,292 crores at the end of September compared with INR9,757 crores at the end of June. The increase was primarily attributable to higher working capital on account of copper price increase, higher capex, and lease liabilities arising from the consolidation of Autoelectric and Yutaka Giken.

items.statement: Consumer electronics total capex plan ~INR 7,500 crores; GF3 plant (largest) commercial production in Q4 FY27; full ramp-up expected by next year.
items.quote: I think total is around INR7,500 crores. The two plants are up and running, and as Vaaman mentioned a while back, the fourth plant should be, commercial production should start in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: GF3 consumer electronics plant almost finished, running pilots; commercial production in Q4 FY27; full capacity by next year.
items.quote: The GF3, which is the biggest plant that we have, is almost finished and also already running pilots and all those kind of things. We definitely should see in the next couple of quarters, I would say two quarters, it just depends on how.

items.statement: Wiring harness business grew ~68% YoY in Q2; roughly one-third from Autoelectric acquisition, balance from commercial vehicle growth (North America +40%, India post-GST) and underlying momentum.
items.quote: This was perhaps one of the better quarters for our wiring harness business. As you would have noticed in the presentation, this particular business grew almost 68%. I think there are two or three drivers for this growth. One is in the American market, commercial vehicle industry grew almost north of 40%, which contributed to this growth. Second, as Vaaman and Mr. Sehgal mentioned, India continues

items.statement: Emerging business EBITDA INR 543 crores quarterly, crossing vision systems and integrated assemblies; growing faster.
items.quote: As I was just looking at your segmental numbers, what struck me was that your emerging business EBITDA now on a quarterly basis is hitting INR543 crores, which is actually crossing the vision systems and integrated assemblies and growing faster.

items.statement: No margin guidance provided; margin is a moving target depending on commodity volatility, customer contracts, and pass-through timing.
items.quote: We don't really guide on margins. It's a moving target for us. We do have pass-throughs in some commodities, but some others, it also depends on customer, it depends on product, it depends on location.

items.statement: High commodity volatility (copper, aluminium, polymers) causing frequent pass-through negotiations; lag of ~3 months (up to 6) for copper pass-through.
items.quote: There are some implications that have also happened with how price moved up in this quarter and then subsequently came down. All those things are constantly going on. It's not a one-quarter kind of a thing that happens. It'll constantly keep happening, and especially because the volatility is high, so it happens even more.

items.statement: Copper price pass-through lag ~3 months (mostly) to 6 months; commodity inflation in copper, aluminium, polymers pressuring margins.
items.quote: Yet, there is a pass-through of the commodity prices, which has a lag of about three months. In some cases, six, but mostly three.

items.statement: Launched 1,000+ automation initiatives (physical, digital, AI) across group; pipeline of ~940 projects (robots, cobots, AGVs) for assembly, intra-logistics, end-of-line testing; target implementation by next year.
items.quote: As part of our Vision 2030 strategy, the 1,000-plus automation initiatives which we have kicked off in the group, which brings together physical, digital, and AI-led automation capabilities across the group, with the goal of implementing over 1,000 automation projects by next year.

items.statement: Medical devices: first plant operational in Chennai; order book growing organically; acquired Irillic (diagnostics); targeting B2B partner for top global brands.
items.quote: Medical's first plant is already up and running in Chennai. The same strategy what we are doing that was successful for the automotive piece, which was B2B kind of supply to our, the top brands in the world. They are very enthused by seeing Motherson capabilities. The order book is growing gradually, organically.

items.statement: Humanoid/robotics revenue marginal; in concept phase; using cobots/robots in 1,000+ automation projects as step toward humanoids.
items.quote: The revenue is very, very marginal right now because these are all in concept phase, and nothing that we can, again, report that is hugely substantial. But yes, exciting part of the 106 billion portfolio order book, record of order book that we have.

items.statement: AIS-184 (driver drowsiness monitoring) regulation evolving; OEMs using workarounds short-term but mature camera tech needed long-term; Motherson invested in Autocruis (China) for commercial vehicle tech.
items.quote: You are right, there are workarounds being managed by the OEMs as of now, not to use expensive technologies. But again, you can imagine this is not going to be like this forever. It is going to evolve because they will not really deliver the outcomes which are intended. So they can be there for a short while, but then eventually, more mature technologies will have to be brought into regulation.

items.statement: Diversification strategy (3CX10: no country, customer, component >10%) enabling growth despite regional headwinds; winning contracts in US, growing in India.
items.quote: Because definitely some customer or some product group in some location is growing, and we're able to catch those waves to counterbalance where we see the headwinds coming due to many difficulties, which is not just single pointed.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy customer-led across all businesses (auto and emerging); will acquire if customer asks to take over troubled supplier.
items.quote: We will acquire. The customer doesn't come to us and tells us, 'Look, this is a good company. Take it over,' or something. The customer is 99% in trouble because of that company going into trouble. So, he wants us to take it over.

items.statement: ~60% of full-year capex guided for non-automotive businesses (emerging markets focus).
items.quote: Approximately 60% of our guided full year capex is earmarked for non-automotive businesses. This reflects our confidence in the growth potential of these segments and is aimed at supporting their expansion and strengthening our capabilities over the coming years.

items.statement: Aerospace targeting multiples of $1 billion revenue before Vision 2030; mix of organic (greenfields) and inorganic growth; customer-led opportunities live.
items.quote: Absolutely. I think if it is just $1 billion, we will be short of where we want it to be. I hope it is in multiples of that. Again, I do not see any reason why not, because we are performing. There are challenges in that. There are a lot of growth opportunities, and it is a sector which is really growing globally.

items.statement: Consumer electronics backward integration (GF3) targeting 40% ROCE; attractive margins, accretive to group; 5-year plan to reach target returns.
items.quote: Look, we stick to the 40% ROCEs, and of course, we are only going to go after businesses where we can see a sight to be able to get those. You cannot get that with the size of scale of executions that we are doing in year one. It does take a five-year plan to get that. But yes, it has got very attractive margins.

items.statement: Yutaka Giken supplies brake discs to major two-wheeler OEMs in India, ASEAN (Indonesia 5.5M units); already in India, not just exhaust systems.
items.quote: Besides exhaust, they are also doing brake discs. In India, of course, we are supplying to all the major two-wheelers. In ASEAN, they are in Philippines, they are in Indonesia, in Thailand. Two-wheeler market is a big market for Yutaka.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin of 22.8% ahead of 20%-21% guidance range
items.quote: EBITDA increased year-on-year by 48.3% to INR214 crores, with EBITDA margin expanding by 274 basis points to 22.8%, ahead of our 20%-21% guidance range.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expected in 21%-22% range
items.quote: I think our EBITDA should be pretty much in the range of 21%-22%, whatever we performed this year, this quarter. I do see our overall EBITDA being in that same range.

items.statement: Target $300 million US order book within three years from current $225 million
items.quote: Within the next three years, I do believe our order book will increase from $225 million to $300 million.

items.statement: Expect to hit INR4,000 crores revenue next year (FY28)
items.quote: I think next year we should touch INR4,000 crores. I mean, we are trending right now very close to INR1,000 crores a quarter, so I think very comfortably we can say that next year we will hit INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Target INR5,000 crores revenue in three years and INR6,000 crores in five years
items.quote: We do believe we are trending and we are working and trending towards achieving INR5,000 crores in the next three years and possibly doubling our revenue from where we were last year within the next five years, INR6,000 odd crores.

items.statement: Australia business expected to grow to $100 million subsidiary over next three years
items.quote: We see Australia growing over the next three years to a $100 million subsidiary.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance maintained at 55%-56% for Q3 and Q4
items.quote: I will probably maintain it at 55%-56% again.

items.statement: Q2 revenue INR940 crores, up 30.5% YoY; strongest quarterly performance
items.quote: Q2 was a record quarter for us, with revenue from operations reaching INR940 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 30.5%.

items.statement: Underlying business grew ~25% excluding QliniQ acquisition
items.quote: Even excluding the contribution from QliniQ, our underlying business delivered a growth of approximately 25%.

items.statement: North America revenue INR421 crores, up 8.7% YoY; highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: North America, which remains our largest market and contributed 44.8% of the revenue, we recorded our highest ever quarterly revenue of INR421 crores, representing a growth of 8.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Australia and New Zealand revenue up 64% to INR101 crores
items.quote: In Australia and New Zealand, revenue grew by 64% to approximately INR101 crores.

items.statement: Rest of World impacted by geopolitical disruptions in Middle East affecting shipment timing
items.quote: Our Rest of World business remained impacted in the quarter by ongoing geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East and other regions, which affected the timing of certain shipments in the region.

items.statement: US order book healthy and building; confident for coming quarters despite single-digit price erosion
items.quote: Our order book remains healthy and continues to build, giving us confidence that as we look ahead in the coming quarters, price erosion in our prescription products, although being in single digits, we are still looking extremely optimistic in the U.S. market.

items.statement: Freight costs nearly doubled; contributed ~INR20 crores to sequential increase in other expenses
items.quote: Notably, freight costs have nearly doubled in the current environment. Higher freight contributed approximately INR20 crores to the sequential increase in other expenses.

items.statement: Employee costs up ~INR8 crores sequentially due to team strengthening and new market investments
items.quote: There has also been a slight increase in employee costs, of approximately INR8 crores, as we continue to strengthen our team and invest in the newer markets.

items.statement: H1 capex INR46 crores; free cash flow INR275 crores
items.quote: After capital expenditure of INR46 crores, free cash flow stood at INR275 crores.

items.statement: Planning manufacturing expansion in India - adding blocks at Teva plant and evaluating plant acquisition; timeline ~12 months
items.quote: dialogue with two companies today, but nothing concrete. We are looking at basically expanding our manufacturing capabilities, hopefully, maybe for which we will probably need a year down the line or so. Immediate effect, but maybe a year and a half down the line. Saksham Tyagi: Okay. Is there any expected timeline for that? Mark Saldanha: I would probably put 12 months

items.statement: Current capacity sufficient for 2-3 years; planning expansion for dosage forms beyond oral solids
items.quote: No. So far, we are good for the next two years, two to three years. But you always want additional capacity.

items.statement: OTC ~75%, Rx ~25% of revenue mix in Q2 and H1
items.quote: Yes, it was broadly very much similar. I think between 70% and 75%, around 75% OTC and the 25% will be Rx.

items.statement: US store brand OTC: positioned as strategic partner for innovation and first-to-market launches with retailers
items.quote: We are, and we are already with some of the retailers, we are already positioned there, where we talk of launching first to market or we talk of innovations. We always have dialogues with them on innovations, and quite a few of our retailers look to us for those directions.

items.statement: No price increases in base finished product portfolio; competitive intensity fluctuates but focus remains on own strategy
items.quote: No, we are not witnessing any of that.

items.statement: Working capital cycle reduced to ~128 days in H1 from 138 days in FY26
items.quote: We also continued to make progress in working capital management. The working capital cycle reduced to approximately 128 days in the first half of the year from 138 days in FY 2026.

items.statement: H1 operating cash flow INR322 crores vs INR75 crores YoY; cash conversion 75.2% vs 30.7%
items.quote: Cash generated from operations was INR322 crores compared with INR75 crores in the corresponding period last year. Cash conversion, measured as operating cash flow as a percentage of EBITDA, improved to 75.2% from 30.7%.

items.statement: Net cash position INR1,095 crores as of September end; cash and investments INR1,124 crores
items.quote: As of September end, cash balance and current investments stood at INR1,124 crores. Our net cash position was therefore at INR1,095 crores.

items.statement: Lease liabilities up INR120 crores due to new lease in UK
items.quote: Yes, we have taken a new lease in U.K., and it has come from that geography.

items.statement: QliniQ (Netherlands) contributed INR84 crores in H1; ABCnow and Marksans GmbH strengthening Germany platform
items.quote: QliniQ in the Netherlands contributed approximately INR84 crores for the first half, while ABCnow and Marksans GmbH are strengthening our platform in Germany.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A in Europe; hope to conclude a couple within 12 months
items.quote: We are looking at and exploring more M&As in Europe, and we do hope to conclude a couple of them down the line, hopefully within the next 12 months.

items.statement: Dividend policy historically ~1/3 of free cash flow; FY27 policy not yet finalized
items.quote: Historically, like, 1/3 of our free cash flow generation, we have been distributing as dividend. Broadly, it will be in line with that.

items.statement: Buyback remains an option if no other capital deployment opportunities
items.quote: Buyback is always an option, and we have discussed this, and we will continue evaluating as and when we feel if nothing else is happening, that could be a possibility also.

items.statement: Depreciation accounting changed for intangible assets - now finite 10-year life vs indefinite; Q2 impact from QliniQ and ABCnow intangibles
items.quote: From this quarter, we basically are treating intangible assets as having a finite useful life, and we have started depreciating it over a period of 10 years. The reason for the increase in this figure was, we have also started providing for depreciation on acquired intangible assets from QliniQ and ABCnow.

items.statement: R&D expenditure 2.6% of revenue in H1
items.quote: For H1, R&D expenditure was 2.6% of revenue.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month ROCE 24.7% (up from 18.7%); ROE 18.6% (up from 13.6%)
items.quote: On a trailing 12-month basis, return on capital employed increased to 24.7% from 18.7%, while return on equity improved to 18.6% from 13.6%.

items.statement: API costs (paracetamol, ibuprofen) elevated due to crude oil and war; expect cooling in 30 days if crude improves
items.quote: I do see that prices should cool down maybe in the next 30 days or so.

items.statement: Target to bring operating expenses down to about 7% of AUM by March 2027 from peak of 9-10%
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, we had set ourselves a target of bringing down operating expenses down to about 7% of AUM by March 2027, compared with a peak of approximately 9% or 10%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM crossed INR3,000 crores for the first time, reaching INR3,209 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: For the first time, our consolidated AUM crossed INR3,000 crores, reaching INR3,209 crores, and we recorded our highest ever quarterly profits of INR51 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM grew 51% year-on-year to INR3,209 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our consolidated AUM grew by 51% year-on-year to INR3,209 crores.

items.statement: Disbursements for Q2 FY27 stood at INR818 crores, growing 72% year-on-year and 19% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Disbursement for the quarter stood at INR818 crores, growing 72% year-on-year, and approximately 19% over the previous quarters.

items.statement: Consolidated NIM for Q2 FY27 stood at 18.2%
items.quote: Consolidated NIM for the quarter stood at 18.2%, and annualized return on AUM improved to 6.7%, and annualized return on equity to 20.5%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to approximately 42.6% in Q2 FY27 from peak of 51.7% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio has now improved approximately to 42.6% in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Overall collection efficiency for Q2 FY27 stood at 96.5%, GNPA at 2.73%, NNPA at 0.92%
items.quote: Our overall collection efficiency for the quarter stood fairly stable at 96.5%. GNPA was 2.73% compared to 2.76% in Q1, while NNPA was about 0.92%.

items.statement: X bucket collection efficiency remained healthy at around 99.4% with marginal seasonal decline during monsoon
items.quote: Our X bucket collection efficiency remained quite healthy at around 99.4%, with a marginal seasonal decline during the monsoon period.

items.statement: Loans originated under new credit structure show roughly 15% lower default rates than earlier model
items.quote: When we compare similar groups of customers, loans originated under the new credit structure have shown roughly 15% lower default rates than those originated under the earlier model.

items.statement: Substantial investments made in credit, recovery, technology, and people over past several quarters pushing up operating expenses
items.quote: Specifically to all of these changes that we have made over the last couple of years, it has come at a cost. Over the past several quarters, we have made substantial investments in credit, recovery, technology, and people.

items.statement: Separated credit and recovery from branch operations; independent credit team assesses and approves customers while separate recovery team handles collections
items.quote: But the biggest operational change we have made was separating credit and recovery from branch operations. Today, for MFI customers, we have an independent credit team that assesses and approves customers, while a separate recovery team handles collections in the branches that require additional support.

items.statement: Process approximately 110,000 applications per month, disbursing to 25,000-30,000 customers after full assessment chain
items.quote: So, I guess, quantitatively, we probably push through maybe 110,000 applications through our processes and systems in a month. We'll wind up disbursing to maybe 25,000-30,000 customers after going through the entire chain.

items.statement: Around 49% of microfinance collections came through digital channels (UPI and e-NACH) as of September 2026
items.quote: As of September 2026, around 49% of our microfinance collections were coming through digital channels.

items.statement: Individual lending now accounts for almost 40% of microfinance portfolio
items.quote: This is particularly important as individual lending now accounts for almost 40% of our microfinance portfolio.

items.statement: Namra Finance (MFI subsidiary) AUM stood at INR2,424 crores, growing 61% year-on-year and 12% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Namra's AUM stood at INR2,424 crores as of September 2026, growing 61% year-on-year and 12% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Namra Finance PAT for Q2 FY27 was INR34 crores vs loss of INR1 crore in Q2 FY26; H1 FY27 PAT INR63 crores vs INR13 crores for full FY26
items.quote: Profit after tax was INR34 crores compared with a loss of INR1 crores in the same quarter last year. For the first half, Namra's PAT stood at INR63 crores compared with INR13 crores for the whole FY26.

items.statement: Namra Finance NIM improved to 16.6% from 15.37% in Q1, helped by growing share of individual lending
items.quote: NIM improved 16.6% compared with 15.37% in Q1, helped in part by the growing share of individual lending.

items.statement: Arman standalone AUM at INR784 crores, up 26% year-on-year and 3% sequentially; MSME 74%, LAP 13%, two-wheeler 12%
items.quote: AUM stood at INR784 crores as of September 2026, up 26% year-on-year and 3% sequentially. MSME continues to be the largest part of this business, contributing approximately 74% of the AUM, followed by LAP at around 13% and two-wheeler at 12%.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost reduced from 11.7% in Q1 to 11.3% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We are seeing some improvements in the cost of borrowing. Our incremental borrowing cost reduced from 11.7% in Q1 to 11.3% in Q2.

items.statement: Acuité reaffirmed A- rating with outlook revised from stable to positive; CARE Ratings reaffirmed A- with stable outlook
items.quote: During the quarter, Acuité reaffirmed our A- rating while revising its outlook from stable to positive. CARE Ratings also reaffirmed our A- rating with a stable outlook.

items.statement: Capital adequacy comfortable at 36.26% (Arman standalone) and 37.19% (Namra), well above regulatory requirements
items.quote: Our capital position remains quite comfortable with capital adequacy of 36.26% at Arman standalone and 37.19% at Namra level, both well above regulatory requirements.

items.statement: CGFMU Credit Guarantee Scheme renewal pending government approval; eligible loans up to March 31, 2026 remain covered; loans from April 1, 2026 not yet covered
items.quote: The renewal has taken longer than we had anticipated. However, eligible loans originated up to March 31st, 2026, continue to remain actively covered under the existing scheme. Loans originated from April 1st, 2026, are currently not covered yet.

items.statement: As of September 30, approximately 51% of microfinance portfolio and 30% of MSME portfolio remain covered under CGFMU scheme
items.quote: As of September 30th, approximately 51% of our microfinance portfolio and 30% of our MSME portfolio remain covered under this scheme.

items.statement: Maharashtra and Karnataka drought declarations affect 7.6% of consolidated portfolio; marginal deterioration in repayment behavior seen in Maharashtra, especially in October
items.quote: In particular, both Maharashtra and Karnataka have declared droughts in a very large number of talukas. These two states together account for 7.6% of our consolidated So far, the portfolio in these states have remained largely stable, although we have seen some marginal deterioration in repayment behavior in Maharashtra, especially after the declaration was made

items.statement: Collection efficiency dip of 40 basis points in Q2 FY27 (96.9% to 96.2%) attributed to normal post-monsoon seasonal pattern and floods in Bihar/UP, drought in Maharashtra/Gujarat
items.quote: I think historically, if you look at us for the last 15 years, post-monsoon quarter always has a minor dip. That is not unexpected. As I said to the previous person who was asking that, there is always places with too much rain or too little rain.

items.statement: 1% dip in fresh delinquencies observed in Maharashtra in October; monitoring situation closely and adjusting lending where necessary
items.quote: There has been a dip of about 1% in fresh delinquencies. Nothing major, but definitely deserves attention. We are taking whatever steps are needed right now.

items.statement: UPI MDR cost impact being evaluated; industry pushing for exemption; not currently factored into 7% opex-to-AUM target
items.quote: I mean, you are taking this 7% target too literally. I mean, these are more visions than like very detailed algos and models and stuff like that. It may be 7.1%, it may be 7.2%, it might be 6.9%. No, we have not really. When I made that statement, I have not really considered it in that overall vision of 7%.

items.statement: INR5,000 crores AUM target definitely achievable; possible within 18 months per CFO; no capital raise needed before reaching that level
items.quote: INR5,000 crores is definitely there. I think you know that I don't give specific guidance or when we may reach that. But yeah, is it possible to reach it by FY- Vivek Modi: 18 months. Aalok Patel: In 18 months? Definitely.

items.statement: Opex-to-AUM target of around 6% at INR5,000 crores scale; lowest historical was 4.5-4.75% for microfinance
items.quote: If we can reach around 6%, that would be fairly good, and I would be happy with that number.

items.statement: No need to raise capital before reaching INR5,000 crores AUM; can grow indefinitely at close to ROE without raising capital
items.quote: No, no. We do not need to raise capital. Akhilesh B.: Yeah. Aalok Patel: I guess one of the advantages of not growing very, very quickly, although I would not say we are not growing quickly, but one of the advantages is that, if you continue to grow at close to your ROEs, you can grow indefinitely without raising capital, right

items.statement: Approximately 5,200 employees across 11 states (corrected from 5,700 mentioned in call)
items.quote: We have now, what, 5,700 (Errata: actual number to be read as 5,200) employees across 11 states.

items.statement: Founder and Chairman Shri Jayendra Patel passed away on August 25; acknowledged his contribution to building the organization
items.quote: Before I get into the numbers, I would like to take a moment to acknowledge the passing of Arman's founder and my father, Shri Jayendra Patel, on August 25th.

items.statement: Management guided for double-digit revenue growth in H2 FY27 and beyond
items.quote: I would say it would be double-digit growth. That is my way forward that I would look at. As we historically said, we would look at a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Capex outlook for FY27 and next 2-3 years is ₹2,000 crores plus or minus 20% per year
items.quote: Considering the RFPs we have currently and basically looking at those RFPs from a strength point of view, I would say it would be around ₹ 2,000 crores, plus or minus 20%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capitalization was ₹1,223 crores; CWIP stood at ₹1,638 crores as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: During the second quarter, the Company capitalized assets amounting to ₹ 772 crores, taking a total capitalization for the first half of financial year to ₹1,223 crore. The capital work in progress stood at ₹ 1,638 crore s as of September 30, 2026.

items.statement: Installing several 3,000 litre SPPS lines for peptide programs; future peptide capacity to be among top three globally
items.quote: We continue to add capacity and are currently installing s everal 3,000 litre SPPS lines to meet the requirements of the programs we are working on

items.statement: Three dedicated projects near commercialization; one very close, other two in next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Apart from the three projects where one of them is very close to commercialization, other two we expect in the next one or two quarters, slowly the commercialization factor will come in.

items.statement: No capacity shortage currently; multipurpose plants can be quickly changed; only 3 dedicated blocks out of 53 total
items.quote: s Unit 1 has about 22 production blocks, Unit 2 has 25, and about 11 in -- no, sorry, six production blocks in Unit 3. We have dedicated only three production blocks across all the units. Shrikant Akolkar: Understood. Dr. Kiran S. Divi: The capacity, the total plants are multipurpose and can be quickly

items.statement: Net material consumption improved to 32% of sales revenue in H1 FY27 from 40% in H1 FY26
items.quote: Net material consumption for the first half stood at approximately 32% of the sales revenue compared to 40% in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Management declined to raise EBITDA margin guidance despite 40%+ H1 margins
items.quote: I would say that is what we all wish for, right? We would wish that this would be consistent and this would be playing along. But as I said earlier, the guidance would be revenue growing at double-digit growth rate, and I cannot comment more than that at this point.

items.statement: Custom synthesis grew ~50% YoY in H1 driven by validation batches, past commercializations, and new projects
items.quote: Several of the molecules which have been worked and validated in the past have slowly been commercialized. What I am talking about are the new commercialization and new investments we have taken up in the last few years, where we have validated those products and they are waiting.

items.statement: Peptide portfolio seeing sustained customer interest across multiple therapeutic categories beyond GLP-1
items.quote: Apart from this, it is not just that we are working on GLP-1, we are working on several therapeutic categories with several customers.

items.statement: Custom synthesis contributed 62% of sales revenue in H1 FY27; generics 38%
items.quote: In terms of business composition, generics contributed 38% of sales revenue during the first half, while custom synthesis accounted for the remaining 62%.

items.statement: Nutraceutical revenue grew to ₹571 crores in H1 FY27 from ₹492 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: Our global nutraceutical business recorded revenue of ₹571 crores for the first half compared to ₹492 crores in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Input cost volatility elevated, especially petrochemical solvents; logistics costs higher due to Red Sea disruptions
items.quote: While the availability of key raw materials and solvents has remained largely stable, we have witnessed increased volatility in input costs, particularly in petrochemical-based solvents, where prices have remained elevated.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations declined despite PBT growth due to large capex cycle and advances for CWIP
items.quote: See, as explained earlier, we are in a large capex cycle. Huge capitalization was seen this quarter, around ₹700 plus crores. And with the work in progress, capex that is being incurred at this point of time, which is about ₹879 crores in -- no, I think the CWIP is about ₹ 1,638 crores, where certain advances have also been disbursed.

items.statement: Cash balance ₹2,181 crores; trade receivables ₹3,705 crores; inventories ₹5,325 crores as of Sep 30, 2026
