items.statement: Subansiri interim tariff order reserved; revenue booked at 80% of filed petition; petitions updated progressively as units commission
items.quote: As far as hearing is concerned, the hearing has been over and the order is now reserved for interim tariff. Therefore, we are expecting the interim tariff very soon in respect of Subansiri Lower Project. As already stated, we are booking revenue at the rate of 80% of the tariff petition which we have filed.

items.statement: Etalin project (3,097 MW) transferred from SJVN; Rs 800 Crore consideration to be paid after PIB approval; Boards of both companies approved
items.quote: No, that amount is not paid yet. It will be paid once PIB happens for the Etalin. I told already that PIB is expected anytime now. The process has already been initiated by Government of India and Ministry of Power basically. Once we get the PIB approval, then we will be in a position to give the money to SJVN. But principally, it is already decided and it is approved by the Board of SJVN as well

items.statement: Solar projects delayed due to connectivity/evacuation issues; 23,120 MW tendered, 73 projects awarded, only 9,000 MW PPA signed; 5,000-7,070 MW more expected; 5,000 MW may not get tied up
items.quote: We have tendered out in NHPC around 23,120 MW of the bids. Out of that, we have awarded 73 projects. PPA has been signed only for 9,000 MW. Also, we are expecting that around 5,000 - 7,070 MW will also be signed, totalling to around 15,000. So around 5,000 MW capacity is there which may not be tied up.

items.statement: States reluctant to sign 25-year PPAs for vanilla solar due to changing energy patterns; NHPC discussing hybrid configurations (solar+wind+BESS)
items.quote: Because it can be solar, it can be solar wind-based, so they are not clear yet. Earlier they were having a very clear-cut adequacy plan, but we have seen in the past one year the energy requirement, energy pattern has changed drastically in all the states. So now, we are in fact in discussion with many states for a combination of various powers.

items.statement: NHPC Green Energy (solar) not being hived off; bullish on RE; exploring JVs with states for solar+storage/wind projects
items.quote: We are not going to do anything till commissioning as of now. After commissioning, we will see what to do. But we are, in fact, in discussion with the various states. They are interested to have some floating solar or the solar projects or solar plus BESS, not only the solar as vanilla. So they are in discussion with us to join hand with them for JV and do the projects in their state.

items.statement: Subansiri full commissioning impact largely in FY28; expected AFC Rs 5,500 Crore/year; regulated equity ~Rs 9,000 Crore; expected PAT Rs 1,500-1,600 Crore/year at 17% ROE + incentives
items.quote: On yearly basis, we are expecting AFC of Rs. 5,500 Crore approx. from Subansiri on full commissioning basis. Since last unit of Subansiri is spilling over in next financial year, the full impact of Subansiri would be largely in FY'28 and then FY'29 onwards, you will be having full top line, then the expected PAT also. The regulated equity of Subansiri, considering 30% of the capital cost is around

items.statement: Adjusted Q2 FY27 PAT = reported PAT Rs 1,549 Crore + Rs 231 Crore Teesta-IV provision = ~Rs 1,780 Crore (90% YoY increase vs 65% reported)
items.quote: So, if you add back this Rs. 231 entirely to the reported PAT, you will arrive at the adjusted PAT. This is the only one adjustment you have to make in adjusted PAT and if you calculate the adjusted PAT, so that will be 90% higher than the corresponding quarter, against the 65% which we have shared. These are on standalone basis.

items.statement: Taken 140-200 bps of calibrated price increases using ML models; further hikes possible if needed
items.quote: We have taken about 140 or 150 to 200 basis points of price increases, very calibrated through machine learning models versus taking blunt price increases, where we can utilise day parts, channels etc.

items.statement: Covered for cheese supplies for FY27; seeing inflation in dairy, chicken, vegetables due to monsoons and West Asia crisis
items.quote: we are fairly covered for this financial year on our cheese supplies. But whether in dairy or any of the other commodities, we are seeing similar kind of inflation coming across.

items.statement: Full-year same-store sales growth target of 5%-7%; Q3 planned to be in that range
items.quote: I think we've planned to have a full year in the 5%-7% range. Therefore, if you see from Q4 to Q1 to Q2, you see an uptick, and we have planned Q3 to be in that range, Nihal.

items.statement: MAU growing ~25%, MTU growing ~9%; divergence due to new customer acquisition with lower initial conversion
items.quote: while the MAU is growing at 25%, the MTU is sort of seeing only a 9% growth.

items.statement: Popeyes gross margin has further 100-200 bps improvement potential; store-level profitability work ongoing on manpower, marketing, rentals
items.quote: I do believe there is another 200 basis point of gross margin improvement that we would like from here. That is one. Second is the lines below, i.e., store operating cost, manpower, and marketing; all need to flow in for us to come to the right restaurant profitability.

items.statement: Domino's absorbed 140 bps of 200 bps unforeseen cost inflation (LPG, wages); 60 bps drag remains; more levers available if needed
items.quote: Unfortunately, they have been hit by 200 basis points of unforeseen, unplanned costs very suddenly, but they have been able to absorb almost 140 basis points with all the action they have taken. 60 basis points is still sitting.

items.statement: Innovation portfolio contributing almost double-digit to overall top-line growth; mix accretive and gross margin positive
items.quote: if you look at innovations over the last year, they now contribute almost double-digit contribution to our overall top-line growth.

items.statement: No broad consumption slowdown seen; QSR peers reporting positive growth; demand concerns more on inflation side than volume
items.quote: If you see, most QSR companies have reported very positive growth. So I don't think some of the rural pressures because of monsoon or some other factors which may be there is impacting us.

items.statement: Cafe Domino's at 15-20 stores, mostly dine-in, adds materially to ADS/LFL; early stage, no negative surprises
items.quote: We are like 15, 20 stores, and it does add materially to average daily sales or like-for-like growth. Most of it is dine-in. That is the very early read on it.

items.statement: Turkey Domino's transaction growth positive, price hikes ahead of inflation; negative LFL due to accounting inflation adjustment, not business weakness
items.quote: Domino's average order growth per store is positive. They have been able to take price hikes ahead of the own inflation. The inflation that the company has faced. Yet the LFL is negative.

items.statement: Co-located Domino's-Popeyes stores (3-4 locations) are ROI/ROCE accretive with shared seating, bikes, commissary; not a programmatic rollout yet
items.quote: These stores are ROI or ROCE accretive to JFL, and we're doing it more opportunistically. It's not a program where the two brands go together, want to co-build the location.

items.statement: Print advertising revenue grew 5% in English and 11% in Hindi YoY driven by volume market share gains and government DAVP price increase
items.quote: One, from a market share point of view, both in Hindi and English markets, we managed to consolidate a little bit, so we've got those volume gains. Also, if you remember, the industry got a certain DAVP price increase last year. Which has provided an impetus as far as the government revenue is concerned, which has contributed here.

items.statement: Circulation revenue flat YoY at INR 54 cr consolidated; Hindi circulation revenue flat at INR 39 cr
items.quote: Circulation revenue, as we said, is exactly flat, as it was same quarter last year, which is INR 54 cr.

items.statement: Newsprint costs have peaked out but remain elevated; no downward impetus seen yet
items.quote: Well, they've flattened at a certain level. We are not seeing any downward impetus at this point in time, but I believe they've already peaked out.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 15% YoY; Print EBITDA declined 6% due to newsprint costs and festive shift
items.quote: EBITDA has a 26% growth at INR 88 cr. As a consequence, our EBITDA margins are at 17% versus 15% same period last year.

items.statement: Radio station rationalization completed; loss-making stations surrendered to government
items.quote: As step one what we have already done is that whatever were the loss-making stations or frequencies, we have since surrendered to the government. And hence, we are a smaller network than what we were earlier.

items.statement: Radio operating EBITDA turned positive at INR 2 cr with 9% margin after station rationalization
items.quote: Radio performance, as you are aware and we have been pointing towards rationalization of a number of licenses based on profitability and viability. These Q2 results are for the existing stations. So operating revenue came at INR 25 cr, which is a decline of 23% because we surrendered certain = IIHT Media Limited ~GGldlril ~ November 5, 2026 4 stations and operating EBITDA after many quarters with

items.statement: Digital operating EBITDA at breakeven to slight positive INR 1 cr on revenue of INR 28 cr
items.quote: The Digital performance at INR 28 cr, is a decline of 30%. Operating EBITDA however is at a breakeven to a slight positive at INR 1 cr.

items.statement: Employee costs reduced to INR 95 cr from INR 99 cr QoQ and INR 105 cr YoY due to cost rationalization program
items.quote: Yeah, we've been on a cost rationalization program on all indirect costs and therefore it is reflecting that. Across quarters, I think we've consistently shown a saving.

items.statement: Management engaged in conversations with substantial shareholder Matthew Cyriac (near 10% holding); Board runs company affairs
items.quote: Well look, I would not like to go into the detail, but suffice to say, yes, we are in conversation with such a substantial shareholder in our Company. Now, whatever his particular style of investing / management is, I won't like to comment or engage on that. But yes, we are very much engaged with that shareholder who holds a substantial part through his investment firm is what I'd like to say.

items.statement: No new capital allocation decisions currently; OTTplay investment did not pan out but Hindi Print investments have borne fruit
items.quote: Nothing as of now, but as we put up the cautionary statement at the beginning, we don't give any forward guidance. Suffice to say that most of our capital allocations, if you're specifically talking about capital allocations, are for trying to create long-term sustainable value for all shareholders. Now, OTTplay, of course, did not pan out very well. But all our investments in the Hindi Print busi

items.statement: AFE (Ad for Equity) investments of INR 25 cr, INR 13.51 cr and INR 50 cr approved in HMVL board meeting; these are investments in future advertisers
items.quote: Mehul, these are all AFE investments. I think, if you go back any quarter, we bring all these AFE investments to the Board and they are the ones that you are reading out of. As to how they are beneficial, I have told you these are future advertisers as well as we take investment positions. So, they are very beneficial to the Company and these are all AFE investments.

items.statement: Radio profitability depends on government revising license fee structure under GOPA framework; industry lobbying ongoing
items.quote: The second obviously is our lobbying that we are doing to the government as an industry body for looking at the license fee structure. Now that activity, the government still hasn't come back to us. Now once that happens, the profitability and the economics of the Radio business will change substantially.

items.statement: Net cash remains healthy at INR 930 cr
items.quote: PAT as a consequence went to INR 39 cr and PAT margins grew from 4% to 8% and net cash remains a very healthy INR 930 cr.

items.statement: No forward-looking estimates provided; company does not give guidance
items.quote: We would not be providing any forward-looking estimates and would request that no reliance be placed on any such statements.

items.statement: Order book INR15,964 cr as of Sep 30, 2026; plus INR1,257 cr post-Sep orders, total INR17,222 cr
items.quote: As on September 30, 2026, order book stands at INR15,964 crores, excluding orders received post September 30, which are almost INR1,257 crores, totalling to INR17,222 crores.

items.statement: Order inflow Q1 INR362 cr, Q2 INR1,966 cr, October INR391 cr plus L1 for INR866 cr
items.quote: In Q2, the order intake was INR1,966. And for Q1, I will just tell you. INR362 crores for Q1.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance INR3,000-5,000 cr for remainder of FY27
items.quote: What we are targeting is INR3,000 crores-INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth target ~10% for FY27 (~INR6,600 cr); 15% CAGR over three years
items.quote: Based on the order intake, which is coming late, we may achieve 10%, which is approximately INR6,600 revenue by March end.

items.statement: Capex YTD INR62 cr; full-year target ~INR125 cr
items.quote: Up to date, capex was around INR62 crores and target is approximately INR125 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR2,781 cr; after four HAM asset sale, debt to reduce to ~INR2,000 cr (project debt INR800 cr, rest working capital)
items.quote: Today we have a total debt of INR2,781 crores. The four assets debt will go off the console of ABL. We will be left with INR2,000 crores of debt.

items.statement: Standalone lender debt INR1,169 cr; target INR600-700 cr by Mar 2027 after monetization and new investments
items.quote: The estimated standalone debt as of March 2027 would be in the range of INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: Equity infusion for HAM projects: INR153 cr in H2 FY27, INR114 cr FY28, INR72 cr FY29; INR68 cr infused in H1
items.quote: Equity to be invested is around INR340 crores for the HAM projects, including Bowaichandi, to be invested for 2026-2027, INR153 crores, 2027-2028, INR114 crores, and INR72 crores for 2028-2029.

items.statement: Four HAM assets monetization: first tranche ~INR600 cr in next two weeks, total ~INR1,000 cr for four plus two assets
items.quote: Proceeds from the four assets will be in the next two weeks' time. Vaibhav Shah: No. Paresh Mehta: We have already signed off on the sale of the transaction

items.statement: Bid pipeline INR51,000 cr across NHAI, MoRTH, railways, states; INR800-8,000 cr bids pending opening
items.quote: Total bid pipeline for Ashoka Buildcon is INR51,000 crores immediately, which includes NHAI, MoRTH, railways, states.

items.statement: Order book mix: roads/railways 58% (HAM INR1,436 cr, EPC INR6,173 cr), Power T&D 24%, building EPC 6%, subsidiaries 12%
items.quote: Breakup is roads and railway project comprise around INR9,275 crores, which is 58% of our total order book. Among the road projects of order book, HAM projects are to the tune of INR1,436 crores and EPC of INR6,173 crores.

items.statement: New LOAs: RVNL Uttarakhand rail INR602 cr; REC Power TBCB transmission INR? (first TBCB project); NER railway INR290 cr
items.quote: During Q2 FY 2020, the company received LOA from RVNL, Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, for the project of new BG rail line in the state of Uttarakhand. The project cost is INR602 crores, including GST.

items.statement: Overseas order book 10% currently; targeting 20% in 2-3 years across roads, railways, transmission, distribution
items.quote: Today, if you say it is 90/10 is overseas and 90% is domestic. Going ahead, it could be 80/20, and we will see how we move ahead with our experience in various countries.

items.statement: NHAI awards up 62.9% YoY Apr-Sep FY27 (2,236 km); FY27 target 5,200 km (+66%); construction down 18% YoY
items.quote: NHAI plans to award 5,200 kilometer in FY27, which is up by 66% compared to last year.

items.statement: Jaora-Nayagaon toll collection INR73.5 cr in Q2; BOT stake sale largely received (~INR1,700 cr), INR15 cr deferred to Mar, rest over 2-3 years
items.quote: In Q2 FY 2027, in our BOT division, the company recorded a gross total toll collection from its Jaora-Nayagaon Toll Road Company of INR73.5 crores.

items.statement: Entered TBCB framework in transmission via REC Power project (400/220/132 kV lines, 24-month build, 35-year O&M)
items.quote: This is first-ever Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding, which is popularly known as TBCB project by the company, and this project is in the state of Maharashtra.

items.statement: Dedicated team in place for BOT projects; working with investors on various BOT opportunities
items.quote: Definitely, there is a team in place already, and we are working with investors on various BOT projects.

items.statement: Targets H2 FY27 disbursements of INR500-600 crores and AUM of INR1,100-1,200 crores by March 2027
items.value: INR500-600 crores disbursements; INR1,100-1,200 crores AUM
items.quote: internally, our target is to disburse anywhere between INR500 crores to INR600 crores in H2, which will lead to an AUM of between INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: Aims to reach monthly disbursement run rate of INR100 crores as soon as possible
items.quote: that's the goal that as soon as possible, we reach a monthly disbursement rate of INR100 crores

items.statement: Targets opex to AUM ratio below 10% over next 2 years
items.quote: Our medium-term objective is to bring the opex to AUM ratio below 10% over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Monthly disbursements more than doubled from INR24.5 crores in August to INR50+ crores in October 2026
items.quote: Monthly disbursement increased from INR24.5 crores in August 2026 to INR32.4 crores in September and crossed INR50 crores in October 2026.

items.statement: AUM reached INR802 crores as of September 2026 with 13,000 live customers across 148 branches
items.quote: As of September 2026, we operated through 148 branches across 12 states with approximately 13,000 live customers and an AUM of INR802 crores.

items.statement: Solar lending AUM grew to INR17 crores in H1 and INR22.5 crores after October disbursements
items.quote: During first half, our solar lending business reached an AUM of INR17 crores. Last month, we disbursed about INR5.5 crores. So this is growing.

items.statement: H1 FY27 average lending IRR 24.8%, borrowing IRR 12.7%, NIM 11.9%; expects IRR to move up quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: On the margins front, our average lending IRR stood at 24.8% during H1, while the average borrowing IRR was 12.7%. Our net interest margin stood at 11.9%.

items.statement: Solar financing yield at 22.7% minimum, currently 23.5%
items.quote: Current yield is 23% plus, 23.5%, but take an approximate average of 22.7%, that's the minimum we see here.

items.statement: 90+ PAR declined to 2.56% in September 2026 from 6.25% in March 2026; on-book gross NPA at 0.01%
items.quote: Our asset quality indicators have improved. The 90-plus PAR declined to 2.56 as of September 2026 compared to 6.25 as of March 2026. Our reported on-book gross NPA stood at 0.01% as of September 2026.

items.statement: Collection efficiency 92.5% overall, ex-bucket above 98%; 3x growth in NPA collections starting September
items.quote: On the collections front, our collection efficiency stood at 92.5%. This is on an overall basis, ex-bucket stands at above 98%.

items.statement: Operating expenses at INR29.67 crores in Q2, opex/AUM ratio 14.3% in H1; expects operating leverage to improve as AUM grows
items.quote: Operating expenses stood at INR29.67 crores during the quarter, remaining broadly controlled despite the investments required to strengthen our technology, people and operating infrastructure.

items.statement: Raised INR110 crores via NCDs in Q2; NCDs now 46% of borrowings; 36 lenders including 12 banks; liquidity INR170 crores; CAR 26.35%
items.quote: During Q2, we raised approximately INR110 crores through NCD issuances, increasing the share of NCD to 46% of our total borrowings. We now have relationship with 36 lenders, including 12 leading banks alongside NBFCs, development-focused institutions and capital market participants.

items.statement: Borrowing costs increased 25-30 bps in MSME space; bank funding expected to remain competitive with possible betterment
items.quote: Borrowing costs have increased a bit because of the changes in rate. We do see, especially in MSME space, we do see 25 to 30 basis points of increase as of now.

items.statement: Evolving into 4 growth engines: MSME lending, livestock finance, rooftop solar finance, digital small lending on common tech platform
items.quote: We are gradually evolving into a diversified NBFC platform with 4 key growth engines; MSME lending, livestock finance, rooftop solar finance and digital small lending.

items.statement: Solar financing targets INR25 crores monthly disbursements; Loom Solar partnership scaling to INR10+ crores/month by January
items.quote: In terms of monthly disbursements, our target is to reach INR25 crores per month. So that's the kind of target we have in terms of...

items.statement: In-house LOS Moneyboxx ONE reduced secured TAT from 10-11 days to 6.5-7 days; unsecured processing under 2 days from 4 days; Cattle AI cuts manual screening 30-40%
items.quote: TAT, which used to be around 10-11 days earlier has come down to around 6.5-7 days in terms of end-to-end processing. This I'm talking about from origination to PD to legal, technical and then the final sanction. We do unsecured processing in less than 1.5-2 days which again is a marked improvement from 4 days that

items.statement: Classified as middle-layer NBFC in Q2; no material regulatory changes expected except additional compliance and auditor change requirement
items.quote: No, nothing which is worth mentioning because we have been following -- there is nothing which materially changes from here. There are obviously some compliance requirements which are additional. But having said that, there is nothing -- change of auditors will be required, but nothing which is very material on the normal business operations.

items.statement: Liquidity of INR170 crores as of September 2026; funding not a concern for next 2-3 quarters even with 50-70% AUM growth
items.quote: you would notice in the result that our liquidity remains strong. We have liquidity INR170 crores ending September. So liquidity remains strong.

items.statement: Partnership-led models (Akshayakalpa, Bachatt, solar) have FLDG/guarantee structures providing credit protection; solar has 10% second loss guarantee, 3% first loss
items.quote: The partnership is also supported by FLDG, first loss default guarantee arrangement, which provides an additional layer of credit protection. We are encouraged by the initial progress and continue to evaluate further partnerships in this segment to build a scalable livestock financing business.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance for FY27 revised to 16%-18% from earlier 18%-20%
items.quote: In terms of revenue guidance for the year as a whole, this will be in the range of around 16%-18%, which we have earlier also guided 18%-20%.

items.statement: Laminates revenue growth for FY27 may fall short of earlier 10%-12% guidance
items.quote: Whether 10%, 12% we will be able to achieve, probably it will be in that range, but may not be 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Debt reduction target of around INR100 crores for FY27 remains near target despite lower H1 reduction
items.quote: Difficult to say whether it will be exact 100, but it will be very near to that figure.

items.statement: Q2 laminates degrowth driven by high domestic base and export logistics issues, not demand weakness
items.quote: In the domestic, yes, we had a last year was a high base because of our flagship catalogue was launched in terms of that. That is one of the reason for the domestic. In the export, as we already mentioned, that we have faced challenges in terms of availability of containers, ships, and the freight cost extremely high in that and longer transit period.

items.statement: Management sees Q2 as aberration and expects H2 to be better than H1 across segments
items.quote: I think H2, in our view, will be better than what we have done in H1. We focus on driving utilization at our plants, and at this moment, the entire energy is focused on execution.

items.statement: Laminates EBITDA margin before forex fell 590 bps YoY to 12% in Q2
items.quote: EBITDA margin before forex fluctuation stood at 12%, a decline of 590 basis point on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Chipboard segment EBITDA positive at INR9 crores in Q2, second consecutive profitable quarter
items.quote: This segment continues to be in operating profit for the second consecutive quarter with EBITDA before forex fluctuation turned positive at INR9 crores.

items.statement: Two laminate lines at Andhra Pradesh plant on schedule for commercial production by Q4 FY27
items.quote: We are adding two more lines in Andhra Pradesh plant, and that's running on schedule, and we should be able to begin commercial production by Q4 of this FY.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh site can accommodate up to 8 laminate lines (currently 5 after expansion) and 2 chipboard lines
items.quote: The two lines will have five lines in Andhra Pradesh. We can add three more lines in Andhra Pradesh. We have one chipboard line of the 300,000 cubic meter. We can add, let us say, one more line at some point if needed. So I think you see a full capacity of AP, then you can have two board lines. And we can have, let us say, up to eight production lines of laminates.

items.statement: Laminates sales volume fell 12% YoY in Q2 to 5.09 million sheets due to export container delays
items.quote: Sales volume for the quarter stood at 5.09 million sheets, lower by 12%, mostly on account of export sales due to delay in containers, vessel availability, longer transit time, etcetera.

items.statement: Chipboard HMR share 15%-20%, pre-lam share 45%-50% of volume, mix improving quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: it's in the range of 15%-20%. In terms of how the product mix, it's going on a continuous basis. In the pre-lam also, it is in the range of around 45% to 50% of the total volume. It's moving on a quarter-on-quarter basis on positive side

items.statement: Plywood expansion into West and East India markets; launched tier-2 brand in South India in October to drive utilization
items.quote: Currently, we are meaningfully present in South India. We added Western India about a year back, and East market we started in the early part of this financial year. We were only playing in the premium segment of the market, and in the month of October, we've added the tier two brand for South India market.

items.statement: Winning market share in Europe despite flat demand as local manufacturers struggle with costs
items.quote: The local manufacturing plants are struggling, and we are winning market share despite the fact that markets aren't growing. There isn't organic growth in the market. I think it's more of our internal ability to work and win more market share.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved by 3 days to 53 days in Q2 vs 56 days in Q1
items.quote: In the current quarter, working capital cycle improved by three days to 53 days as compared to 56 days in quarter one.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR19 crores to INR922 crores as of Sep 30 vs Mar 26
items.quote: Net debt as on September 30 stood at INR922 crores, a reduction of INR18 crores [Errata: To be read as 19 crores] as compared to March 26.

items.statement: Laminates ROCE pre-tax at ~30% on existing capital base in H1
items.quote: I think we're seeing the data with the show on H1 mainly 30% ROCE pre-tax on the existing, because we see we've hardly added capital, the capital involvement has not gone up.

items.statement: No significant demand destruction expected in Europe; market share gains offset flat market
items.quote: As we see things now, I don't see much of a demand destruction relevant to us. But as a market, yes, there's a challenge at overall level. But I think that's an opportunity to win market share versus the local European producers.

items.statement: Expects double-digit volume growth in H2 FY27, targeting 12%-13% YoY in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: We do expect double-digit growth in the second half, in terms of volume.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth target of 7%-8% remains intact
items.quote: The full-year 7%, 8% cement volume growth target can largely remain intact?

items.statement: October volume growth was more than 12% YoY
items.quote: October was actually more than 12%.

items.statement: Cement prices increased by INR10 in Northeast and INR10-15 outside Northeast in October
items.quote: In September, the prices were broadly flattish, but in October, we have seen that the prices have increased a bit. I think there has been about INR10 increase in Northeast. I think there has been about INR10-INR15 increase in outside Northeast, which is basically West Bengal as well.

items.statement: Per-ton EBITDA was INR1,372 in Q2 FY27 vs INR1,651 YoY; H1 FY27 per-ton EBITDA INR1,438 vs INR1,716 YoY
items.quote: On the per-ton EBITDA front, it is INR1,372 during this quarter as against INR1,651 per ton same quarter last year.

items.statement: Siliguri grinding unit (2 mtpa) capex ~INR350 cr vs Bihar greenfield ~INR550 cr; decision by next call; EC applied for Siliguri
items.quote: I think Siliguri would be about INR350 crores of capex, whereas Bihar would be about INR550 crores of capex. So I think in the next call, we will give full clarity about whether it is going to be Siliguri or Bihar. items.statement: Mozambique 5 locomotives: 1st loco target Q4 FY27, full order completion by H1 FY28
items.quote: the first locomotive, we are directly aiming that it gets ready by Q4. And we are quite confident that seems to be on track as of now. And we will definitely aim that we finish the order latest by H1 of the coming FY

items.statement: Sri Lanka order: L1 declared for $41M (~INR 400 crores), 5 sets of 7-coach PMUs, 12-month delivery from LC opening
items.quote: Right now, as of last this Monday, we have been only declared L1, and being an important event and a substantial value, we declared it to be exchanged. It's about $ 41,000,000 about INR 400 crores

items.statement: REMCL renewable energy consultancy: 7-8 orders in last 6 months, ~INR 10 crores order book, revenue started in Q2
items.quote: In terms of consultancy in renewables and net zero, etc., we've already got about 7-8 orders in the last six months, an order book of roughly about INR 10 crores. And this is a recent development. So, these will start generate -- some of it has already started generating revenue in Q2

items.statement: Regular employee strength stable (~100 fresh inductions offset superannuation); contract staff up ~500 due to project deployment
items.quote: the regular employee strength is in fact not dropping. There has been a fresh induction of about nearly 100 regular employees, which equalize the large number of superannuation, which happened in about 15 to 18 months

items.statement: NICC JV not materializing, on hold; RITES Africa JV under closure; only REMCL subsidiary and SAIL Kulti JV active
items.quote: as of now, that JV is not materializing. This was in advanced rate of negotiation. But as of now, it is not materializing. So, let's see. It's on hold right now

items.statement: Q2 revenue muted due to 10-15 day milestone slippage into Q3; export revenue lumpy on final dispatch basis
items.quote: The performance has been muted, and an analysis of it shows that it is primarily due to two to three important revenue milestones sliding marginally by a few days (10-15 days) into Q3

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Bliss GVS Pharma on September 28, 2026, holding 50.07% equity
items.quote: Completion of Bliss GVS Pharma acquisition as on September 28, 2026, marks an important milestone in our journey towards building an integrated pharmaceutical platform. Anupam Rasayan now holds approximately 50.07% of the equity capital of Bliss GVS Pharma.

items.statement: Bliss acquisition funded via INR300 cr term loan and INR1,450 cr non-controlling non-voting instrument from Bain Capital-led investors
items.quote: The transaction was funded through a INR300 crores term loan and a INR1,450 crores raise through a non-controlling and a non-voting instrument from a group of financial investors led by Bain Capital, including Trust Group and Investec.

items.statement: Guides H2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR2,400-2,500 crores, implying INR4,800-5,000 cr annualized run rate
items.quote: we should be looking at a consol revenue of around INR2,400 crores-INR2,500 crores in the ballpark of that number on a consolidated basis. Because Anupam, Jayhawk, Tanfac, and Bliss, all four, we will be able to consolidate.

items.statement: Expects organic growth of 20-25% over next 3-5 years from the annualized run rate
items.quote: we see the organic growth from there on to be around 20-25 percentage points on a near-term three to five-year time period.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 25% in Q2 FY27 vs 19% YoY; H1 margin 25.5% vs 22.2% YoY
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 25% in Q2 FY27 compared to 19% in the corresponding quarter last year, while H1 margins improved from 26% from 22%.

items.statement: Guides consolidated EBITDA margin at 22-24% steady state including Bliss; cautions against revising guidance higher
items.quote: I think what we can say is that the active Bliss, yes, we believe that 22%-24% EBITDA margin, which we have said is an average consolidated EBITDA margin for Anupam as well, on a consolidated basis. I think that is the number that we should be looking for.

items.statement: Cumulative LOIs and long-term contracts stand at ~INR17,496 crores providing multi-year visibility
items.quote: Our cumulative portfolio of LOIs and long-term contracts now stands at approximately INR17,496 crores, providing visibility over multiple years.

items.statement: Signed 6-year supply agreement with leading U.S. specialty metal manufacturer, entry into geological resources sector
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, we also signed a six-year long-term supply agreement with a leading U.S.-based global specialty metal manufacturer. This marks our entry into a new segment within the geological resources sector and represents an important step in diversifying our customer base and expanding our presence in specialized industrial applications.

items.statement: New metal contract expected to contribute INR100-150 crores in current year, doubling run rate over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: This year, at least we can say that the balance will be at least INR100 crores to INR150 crores or plus or minus few tens of crores should be what we should expect in this year. It should increase further significantly. Even if I take a run rate, you can double the run rate from there over the next year to year and a half per month.

items.statement: Multipurpose plants and pre-built capacity enabled 4-month commercialization of new metal product
items.quote: Also, the capex that we had done and kept it ready really helped us ramp up very quickly. Our multipurpose plants that we have set up as the approach that we have always taken of multipurpose plant has really helped us.

items.statement: Excluding Bliss, working capital cycle improved from 276 to 271 days; Bliss balance sheet consolidated but revenue only for 3 days
items.quote: If we exclude Bliss GVS balance sheet, we have seen a slight improvement in our overall working capital cycle, which has reduced from 276 days to 271 days.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating cash flow INR328 crores vs full year FY26 INR334 crores; focus on balancing growth with financial discipline
items.quote: Compared with the previous full year's operating cash flow of INR334 crores, the operating cash flow generated in H1 FY27 was INR328 crores, driven by stronger profitability and a greater focus on working capital optimization.

items.statement: Bliss acquisition debt of INR300 cr at single-digit interest on WOS; quasi-equity of INR1,450 cr with buyout right over long period
items.quote: Around about INR1,450-odd crores is basically quasi-equity financing, where we have a right to buy them out at any given point in time over a reasonably long period of timeframe. Two, around INR300 crores is what we have borrowed on our wholly owned subsidiary as debt. The debt pricing is in the single digit, which is similar to what we take debt on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Bliss plant utilization in 40s%, growing with significant revenue growth; synergies expected in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: See, if you look at it, they have grown significantly. Their utilizations will be in the 40s, because if you see, they have a very meaningful growth from the last year. That has started, and their capacity utilization continues to grow, and we believe that will continue, one.

items.statement: Actively evaluating API acquisition targets to complete pharma value chain; no public updates yet
items.quote: We have been evaluating alternatives, and we continue to have conversations. Right now, we have nothing to really share to the public right now. But as and when we have it, we will definitely announce it for now. But yes, we are actively looking for it.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue mix: Life Sciences 42%, Performance Materials 28%, Other Fluorinated 29%
items.quote: Revenue breakup for Q2FY27 was as follows: Life science-related specialty chemicals contributed 42%, Performance Materials contributed 28%, other fluorinated products contributed 29%.

items.statement: Received Strong CRISIL ESG rating of 62 and Strong CRISIL Core ESG rating of 63, up from Adequate 54 previous year
items.quote: We have received a "Strong" CRISIL ESG rating of 62 and a "Strong" CRISIL Core ESG rating of 63, compared with an "Adequate" rating of 54 in the previous year.

items.statement: Appointed Rahul Adakmol as new CEO of Bliss GVS, veteran from DRL and Bharat Serums
items.quote: If you see that the approach that we have taken with Tanfac is the approach that we are taking with Bliss as well. That the team has been the same, but however, that we have got a new CEO, Rahul Adakmol. He is an industry veteran with very strong experience from DRL and Bharat Serums.

items.statement: Elementium LOI contract discussions ongoing, supplying volumes monthly on schedule
items.quote: The second point on the Elementium side, the contract discussions are right now ongoing, and we believe that we should be able to come out, conclude this soon. On the supply side, we started supplying some volumes to our customers on the schedule on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Cautions that Q2 standalone revenue decline vs YoY due to INR180 cr one-time sale in Q2 FY26; underlying run rate normalized
items.quote: The decline in the standalone revenue for quarter two of FY27 compared to quarter two of FY26 is primarily attributable to one-time sale of approximately INR180 crores in Q2FY26. Excluding this one-time sale, the underlying performance should be viewed in context of the normalized business run rate.

items.statement: Maintains standalone EBITDA margin guidance of 24-26% despite 34% current run rate; attributes outperformance to product mix
items.quote: Tanya, yes, we have done better on the margins, but it is also to do with the product portfolio and the products that we have sold in this quarter versus the other quarters. I would urge to caution and continue to guide at the numbers that we have been guiding.

items.statement: Management does not provide segment-level or quarterly guidance; growth should be viewed over the long term
items.quote: we don't give guidance, but we would also like to re-emphasize that how we look at it and how we also would appreciate if all the shareholders also look at our numbers is not in the light of a particular quarter or a smaller portion of the year

items.statement: CDMO revenue grew 34% YoY to INR215 crores in Q2 FY27 and 32% to INR422 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: Customers have entrusted us with a larger share of their portfolios and new products, which lifted Q2 FY27 revenue by 34% to INR215 crores, and H1 FY27 revenue by 32% to INR422 crores

items.statement: Trade generics and institutional revenue was INR36 crores in Q2 FY27 and INR66 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: This vertical generated revenue of INR36 crores in Q2 FY27 and INR66 crores in H1 FY27

items.statement: Exports revenue grew 26% YoY to INR12 crores in Q2 FY27 and 46% to INR23 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: resulting in Q2 FY27 revenue growth of 26% to INR12 crores, and H1 FY27 revenue growth of 46% to INR23 crores

items.statement: Excluding ESOP, Q2 FY27 EBITDA was INR36 crores (13.7%) and PAT INR25 crores (9.5%); H1 FY27 EBITDA INR70 crores (13.7%) and PAT INR50 crores (9.7%)
items.quote: Excluding non-cash ESOP expenses, EBITDA for Q2 FY27 was INR36 crores, 13.7%, and PAT INR25 crores, 9.5%, while H1 FY27 EBITDA stood at INR70 crores, 13.7%, and PAT INR50 crores, 9.7%

items.statement: Reported EBITDA and PAT were INR29 crores and INR18 crores for Q2, and INR56 crores and INR36 crores for H1 FY27
items.quote: On a reported basis, EBITDA and PAT were INR29 crores and INR18 crores for the quarter, and INR56 crores and INR36 crores for half year

items.statement: Plant 6 commercialized on 28 September 2026; Plant 4 and Plant 5 injectable facility received EU GMP certification in Q2 FY27
items.quote: the commercialization of Plant 6 in September 2026 marks a key addition to our manufacturing infrastructure. During Q2 FY27, Plant 4 and Plant 5 injectable facility received EU GMP certification

items.statement: Plant 6 adds capacity to serve up to INR1,100 crores at company level with 10% further improvement scope; phase-wise capacity addition approach
items.quote: With Plant 6, as we have mentioned earlier, we can serve up to INR1,100 crores at company level. However, there is a scope of up to 10% of improvement in capacity through consistent efforts

items.statement: Plant 6 depreciation and opex will flow into Q3 FY27 as commercialization was on 28 September 2026
items.quote: September towards end, I think 28th of September is the commercialization date, so it'll be flowing in Q3

items.statement: Trade generics portfolio reshaped by replacing codeine-based products with new launches for broader base
items.quote: we have used this period to reshape the portfolio, replacing codeine-based products with new launches that give the business a broader and more resilient base

items.statement: Injectable EU GMP approval enables stronger export mix with higher margins; domestic business also benefits from quality validation
items.quote: These markets have different margin profile for exports, and as we choose our product portfolio, as we choose clients in these markets, it gives us a stronger base to build on

items.statement: CDMO growth driven by combination of existing product offtake, new products with existing customers, and new customers; no concentration
items.quote: It's a combination of several factors, few of them already mentioned by you: more business in existing products and new products with existing customers, and new products with new customers as well

items.statement: Regulatory tightening (Schedule M, increased FDA testing) favors organized players like Windlas; management sees this as positive
items.quote: if the regulatory standards become tougher, it should help more organized players. That's sort of a textbook situation

items.statement: Net liquidity of INR223 crores at H1 FY27 end after INR47 crores buyback, INR13 crores dividend, and capex funded internally
items.quote: With the INR47 crores buyback successfully completed without promoter participation, the dividend paid, and capex funded from our own resources, we closed the half year with healthy net liquidity of INR223 crores

items.statement: Balance sheet supports shareholder returns and growth; no debt details disclosed
items.quote: a balance sheet that supports both shareholder returns and growth

items.statement: Dividend of INR13 crores (INR6.30 per share) paid for FY26; INR47 crores buyback completed without promoter participation
items.quote: the company paid dividend of INR13 crores, INR6.30 per share related to FY26. With the INR47 crores buyback successfully completed without promoter participation

items.statement: ESOP scheme performance aligned with expectations; management view unchanged since announcement
items.quote: We continue to hold the exact same view when we announced the ESOP and how we see everything being panned out. Our view stays consistent

items.statement: Actively looking for acquisition opportunities for new dosage forms; nothing in final stages; will build internally if no deal finalized
items.quote: For other dosage forms, we have been actively looking for any acquisition opportunity, nothing in final stages as of now. At some point of time, we would take a call to start internally working on our own

items.statement: Management ensures capacity will never be a constraint; will add capacity proactively before peak utilization
items.quote: We would ensure that never happens

items.statement: Indian pharma market volume growth 2.3% in quarter; Windlas delivered 15th consecutive quarter of record revenue with 19% YoY growth
items.quote: The Indian pharmaceutical market reported volume growth of 2.3% during the quarter. Windlas Biotech, extending its track record to 15 consecutive quarters of record revenue, with 19% year-over-year growth to INR264 crores

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue guided at INR 4,250-4,300 crore
items.quote: We are looking at a quite a healthy H2. I mean, as we see, we definitely see that for the full year, we would be anywhere between INR4,250 crores-INR4,300 crores of revenue.

items.statement: FY27 capex raised to INR 8,000 million, ~50% for ADS
items.quote: To deliver these orders, we have raised FY27 Capex projection to INR8,000 million, fased with the customer validations, while keeping firm discipline on working capital, cash and leverage.

items.statement: Non-ADS order book (peak annual revenue) at INR 22,410 million as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Our order book as on September 30, 2026, which is the peak annual revenues of the sale of new businesses, excluding ADS, stands at INR 22,410 million.

items.statement: ADS lifetime order backlog executable over 5 years at INR 58.7 billion
items.quote: At quarter end, our cumulative unexecuted lifetime order book backlog for ADS business executable over next five years stood at INR58.7 billion, giving us strong revenue visibility.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps YoY to 19.4% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA crossed INR2,000 million mark for the first time at INR 2,112 million, up 48%. The margin expanded by about 200 basis points year -on-year and 15 basis points sequentially to 19.4% on our richer mix and operating leverage.

items.statement: Karnataka minimum wage revision added INR 167 million provision in Q2; ~30% base wage increase expected to continue
items.quote: Employee costs rose 25% to INR 1,469 million, slower than the revenue, and include a provision of INR 167 million for the Karnataka minimum wage revision.

items.statement: ADS second bay completed; defense facility operational by end Q3/Q4 FY27; new ADS facility by end CY2025
items.quote: The current aerospace facility will be fully operational by the third quarter with the expanded bay. The defense should be operational towards the end of the third quarter or from the fourth quarter. I would say the new facility, what we are planning, towards the end of the next calendar year.

items.statement: Added new aerospace customers; semicon customer #2 expected in Q3 FY27; won first Safran business this quarter
items.quote: We have added a couple of new customers in the aerospace business, but in the semicon business, we still are with our only customer while we are making good progress towards adding the customer number two.

items.statement: Strong domestic PV demand with wholesale >5 lakh units in Oct; export demand strong as global OEMs diversify supply chains
items.quote: October marked a milestone for the industry, with domestic passenger vehicle wholesale crossing 5 lakh units in a single month for the very first time. Elevated order backlogs and lean dealer inventories, with demand still running ahead of the supply, give us good visibility into quarter three FY 2027.

items.statement: Auto ICE ~65% of sales; non-auto segment 20.9% of total sales in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Auto ICE now accounts for about 65% of our sales on a much l arger base, broadly in line with the target we set ourselves at the time of our IPO.

items.statement: Working capital rose to INR 8,544 million (19.6% of annualized Q2 revenue) due to higher ADS share and volumes
items.quote: Working capital rose to INR8,544 million at the end of September from INR7,359 million in March, mainly due to higher revenue share from ADS business, meaning inventory support and further increased volumes. This represents about 19.6% of the annualized Q2 revenue.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR 2,612 million; leverage conservative at 0.3x annualized H1 EBITDA
items.quote: Net debt rose by about INR 2,000 million to INR 2,612 million at the end of September from INR604 million in March, as we invested in growth. Leverage remains conservative at about 0.3 x of the annualized EBITDA for H1, with ample headroom to fund our plans.

items.statement: H1 operating cash flow INR 2,073 million; capex INR 3,260 million + JV INR 300 million exceeded OCF by INR 1,487 million
items.quote: In H1, we generated operating cash flow of INR2,073 million. Against this, an investment was made of about INR 3,260 million in the Capex for automotive and ADS business. INR 300 million was invested in our joint venture with Nichidai. Together, these investments exceeded operating cash flow by about INR 1,487 million, contributing to increase in the net debt.

items.statement: Nichidai JV commercial production expected end H2 FY27; targeting steering/driveline parts; humanoid robot discussions active with North American OEM
items.quote: Commercial production at the Sansera -Nichidai JV is expected to commence towards the end of H2 FY 2027.

items.statement: Target ADS share 35-40% of total revenue by end of decade (currently ~15%)
items.quote: I am sure that we should be targeting anywhere between 35% to 40% of our overall Sansera revenue target. Today, if you see, our ADS business is about 15% of our business. Going forward, I think towards the end of this decade, maybe around 35%- 40% is something that we would like to achieve.

items.statement: Aspire to reach INR 8,000 crore revenue by FY30; momentum making it more realistic
items.quote: Yes, we continue to aspire to achieve that number, and we strongly believe that possibility is becoming more and more realistic as we cut through our segment and see what we can achieve in every segment.

items.statement: US plant plan on hold due to tariff uncertainty; board reevaluating risks; prefer India outsourcing tailwind instead
items.quote: Now, I think, considering the developments in the U.S. and the tariffs and the uncertainty for the last 14, 15 months, there has been a hold by the buyers in the respective companies with whom we were having very, very active discussions. But also now, internally, the board is weighing the risks, the additional risks associated with operating or setting up a plant in the U.S.

items.statement: MMRFIC associate (47% post-CCPS) not consolidated; Chairman on board; iDEX project wins; no significant capex needed
items.quote: MMRFIC is not part of whatever expansion, I mean, the revenue growth that we are talking about. We have kept MMRFIC since it is not a subsidiary yet. It is just an associate company because our shareholding post the full CCPS conversion would be about 47%.

items.statement: No negative forex or US tariff impact; tariffs now paid by customers through different mechanism
items.quote: Forex, when we say this is basically the standard we've translated at the actual levels, but no negative impact from that. The U.S. tariff also, since now it's being paid through a different mechanism by the customers, so we don't have any additional exposure on that.

items.statement: Sansera Sweden benefiting from competitor failures adding volume; operating at 80-85% efficiency
items.quote: There has been pressure from the customer. Of course, there has been some failures from the competition, which is adding some volume into our kitty.

items.statement: Monitoring Labour Codes for further impact after Karnataka minimum wage revision
items.quote: We continue to monitor the Labour Codes for any further impact, and we will keep you updated on this.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR1,000 crores for FY27 maintained
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain focused on achieving our INR1,000 crores revenue milestone by FY '27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance revised downwards to 23%-25% for FY27
items.quote: we are revising our EBITDA margin guidance downwards to 23% - 25%.

items.statement: Expects 20%+ revenue growth for next 3-4 years
items.quote: we have always guided and we continue to guide 20% plus growth in revenue. So, I think that's the same we would like to continue moving forward in the next 3, 4 years.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 22%, down from 34-35% typical range
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR45 crores, a decline of 37.5%, with an EBITDA margin of 22%.

items.statement: Ambernath facility expenses of ~INR60 crores for full year impacting margins by ~6%
items.quote: we are looking at almost INR60 crores of expenses from Ambernath for the full year. So that is a direct hit to the margin, I would say, which cannot be recovered this year

items.statement: LATAM regulatory changes and product mix shift impacting margins by ~3%
items.quote: the balance 6%, I would say 3% is coming in because of this regulatory change and the product mix change

items.statement: Raw material and solvent price increases impacting margins by ~3%
items.quote: the balance 3%, I would attribute to the increase in the raw material and the solvent prices.

items.statement: LATAM regulatory changes affected demand for higher-margin controlled products
items.quote: regulatory changes in the LATAM market, which affected demand for certain products.

items.statement: LATAM contribution dropped from 21% to 12% due to regulatory changes
items.quote: LATAM had scaled almost from 10% to 21%, which has gone back to 12% in this quarter.

items.statement: New products seeing good traction in semi-regulated markets
items.quote: the new launch products that we have done in the last couple of quarters, they are seeing good traction, but that is mainly happening in semi-regulated markets

items.statement: Q2 FY27 capex at INR18.8 crores, H1 FY27 at INR35.4 crores driven by Ambernath facility
items.quote: Our capex for Q2 FY '27 stood at INR18.8 crores, whereas for H1 FY '27, it stood at INR35.4 crores. This was largely driven by spends on the Ambernath facility

items.statement: Ambernath facility EU audit scheduled for November, approval needed for commercialization
items.quote: we are scheduled for an EU audit in the month of November for Ambernath, in fact, starting next week.

items.statement: Ambernath facility designed for INR450-500 crores revenue potential
items.quote: Ambernath is also one area which can be a big growth driver because once we have the EU approval, that site is designed to generate at least INR450 crores, INR500 crores of revenue moving forward.

items.statement: Backward integrated products account for ~74% of total revenue
items.quote: Products that are fully backward integrated now account for approximately 74% of total revenue

items.statement: Launched 2 new anesthetic liquid inhalation products from Ambernath in Q2 FY27
items.quote: we launched 2 new anesthetic liquid inhalation products from our Ambernath facility during Q2 FY '27.

items.statement: Contrast media product launch expected by next quarter
items.quote: we are very close to launching that product. Hopefully, by next quarter, we would be in a position to launch it

items.statement: Whey protein samples approved, commercial orders expected soon
items.quote: Whey protein, we have actually made some progress on that. We have been successfully able to send out the samples and customers have approved of. And we are looking at starting of the commercial orders.

items.statement: Large CMO contract for anesthetic product close to signing, API-focused initially
items.quote: one large CMO opportunity that we are discussing, on the anesthetic project that is very close to signing. Hopefully, in the next coming weeks, we'll be able to announce that.

items.statement: Raw material and solvent prices remain high due to geopolitical tensions
items.quote: due to the ongoing war and geopolitical tensions, raw material and solvent prices remained high, which has also impacted on our margins during the quarter.

items.statement: Price hikes communicated to customers, full effect visible in next 2-3 quarters due to contract lag
items.quote: the new prices have been communicated to them. The POs at the new prices have also started coming in. But the full effect of that will only be seen in the next 2 quarters

items.statement: Exports account for 80% of revenue: Europe 43%, Asia 36%, LATAM 12%
items.quote: Exports continued to be a key contributor to the business, accounting for 80% of revenue in Q2 FY '27. Within exports, Europe contributed 43%; Asia, 36%; and LATAM, 12%.

items.statement: No working capital limits utilized except LC and bank guarantees for full year
items.quote: for the full year we have not utilized any working capital limits except for letter of credit and bank guarantees.

items.statement: Mangesh Vaze joined as COO with 30+ years API manufacturing experience
items.quote: I would like to take a moment to welcome Mr. Mangesh Vaze, who has joined us as our Chief Operating Officer. With over 30 years of experience in API manufacturing and operations, he will lead operations across our API and formulation businesses.

items.statement: Ambernath revenue contribution may be near zero for FY27 due to EU audit delay
items.quote: the revenue generation, which was to happen from Ambernath for this financial year might be closer to 0 for this year now because of the delay in the regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Anesthetic molecule global market size $400-500 million
items.quote: the anesthetic molecule itself is at about $400 million, $500 million and it sort of continues for the other products as well.

items.statement: Management expects positive margin outlook for FY28 driven by product mix optimization and expense efficiency
items.quote: We have a very positive outlook on margin for 2027-28 as well.

items.statement: VNB margin improved 470 bps YoY to 22.3% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Further, the net VNB margin has improved by 470 basis points on a year-on-year basis to 22.3% for the period ended 30th September 2026 from 17.6% for the same period of the last year ended 30th September 2025.

items.statement: VNB margin declined 60 bps QoQ from 22.9% to 22.3% due to RFR movement
items.quote: If you compare from Q1 27 to Q2 27, it has come down from 22.9% to 22.3%.

items.statement: Net VNB grew 33.95% YoY to Rs 6,846 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: The net VNB has registered a growth of 33.95% on a year-on-year basis to 6,846 crore rupees for the six months ended 30th September 2026 from 5,111 crore rupees for the same period of last financial year.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 21.52% YoY to Rs 25,568 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: The profit after tax for the six months ended 30th September 2026 was 25,568 crore rupees as compared to 21,040 crore rupees for the six months ended September 30th, 2025, registering a growth of 21.52% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Total APE grew 5.72% YoY to Rs 30,696 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: The total annualized premium equivalent, APE, for six months ended 30th September 2026 is 30,696 crore rupees.

items.statement: Individual protection APE grew 58.59% YoY to Rs 157 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our protection business on APE basis has witnessed a growth of 58.59% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Total premium income grew 11.64% YoY to Rs 2,74,269 crore in H1 FY27
