items.statement: Individual new business premium grew 14.86% YoY to Rs 32,725 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: The individual new Life Insurance Corporation November 05, 2026 business premium income for the first half of this year was 32,725 crore rupees, and for the corresponding period last year, it was 28,491 crore rupees, registering a growth of 14.86% on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Group new business premium grew 20.63% YoY to Rs 1,11,685 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: Group new business premium income increased by 20.63% to 111,685 crore Rupees.

items.statement: Bancassurance and alternate channel premium grew 21.44% YoY to Rs 2,458 crore in H1 FY27
items.quote: Bancassurance and alternate channels registered a growth of 21.44% with a premium collection of 2,458 crore Rupees.

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 2.35 as of September 2026 from 2.13 a year ago
items.quote: The solvency ratio as on 30th September 2026 improved to 2.35 as against 2.13 on September 30th, 2025.

items.statement: Indian Embedded Value decreased 1.95% YoY to Rs 7,97,378 crore but increased 1.04% from March 2026
items.quote: The Indian embedded value as on September 30th, 2026 has been determined as 7,97,378 crore rupees as compared to 8,13,230 crore rupees on September 30th, 2025. Therefore, the IEV has registered a decrease of 1.95% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: AUM grew 4.16% YoY to Rs 59,60,941 crore as of September 2026
items.quote: The assets Life Insurance Corporation November 05, 2026 under management as on September 30th, 2026 was 59,60,941 crore rupees as compared to 57,22,896 crore rupees as on September 30th, 2025. Thus, our AUM has registered a growth of 4.16% on a year-on-year

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE decreased to 34.02% from 36.31% YoY
items.quote: Our non-PAR share of individual APE is 34.02%, and PAR is 65.98% for the six months ended September 30th, 2026. As you may recall, for the six months ended 30th September 2025 last year, our non-PAR share of total individual business based on APE stood at 36.31%.

items.statement: Non-par savings APE grew 35% YoY, increasing its proportion from 10.7% to 13%
items.quote: non-par savings proportion, which has increased by 35% on APE basis, thereby taking this proportion, non-par proportion from 10.7% to 13%.

items.statement: ULIP APE de-grew over 40% YoY due to market conditions
items.quote: ULIPs has seen a de-growth, and I am sure that the market improving will come back, and we expect it to be good on ULIPs as well.

items.statement: Launched 5 new non-par individual products in H1 FY27 and 3 more in October 2026
items.quote: During the first six months of the current financial year, we have launched five new non-par individual products. On June 1, 2026, LIC's New Jeevan Sathi Single Premium and LIC's New Jeevan Sathi Limited Premium were launched, and on August 10, LIC's New Bima Jyoti was launched. Further, on September 7, 2026, LIC's Jeevan Raksha and LIC's Bima Platinum were launched.

items.statement: Total product suite expanded to 63 products excluding PMJJBY as of October 2026
items.quote: Therefore, as on date, we offer a total of 63 products, of course, excluding Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, which include 41 exclusive individual products, 13 exclusive group products, one common product for individual and group, seven individual riders, and one group rider.

items.statement: Bima Sakhi program covers 66% of gram panchayats with 3.04 lakh women agents
items.quote: As on September 30th, 2026, a total of 3.04 lakh women have been designated as Bima Sakhis, successfully selling 10.64 lakh insurance policies and generating a new business premium income of 1,548.80 crore rupees in six-month period ended 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Digital adoption growing: ANANDA app policies up 41.23% YoY, MyLIC app has 98.4 lakh unique logins
items.quote: In our digital initiative through the agent-assisted ANANDA app, we have completed 12,40,676 policies during the six months ended September 30th, 2026, as compared to 8,78,470 policies for the same period of last year, thereby registering a growth of 41.23% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Expense ratio improved 87 bps YoY to 10.41% in H1 FY27
items.quote: For the six months ended 30th September 2026, the overall expense ratio was 10.41% as compared to 11.28% for the same period last year. You will observe that there is a decrease of 87 basis points on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Persistency mixed: 13th month premium persistency 74.69% vs 75.29% YoY; 49th month improved to 64.31% from 63.70%
items.quote: On premium basis, the persistency for 13th, 25th, 37th, 49th, and 61st month up to the six months ended 30 September 2026 stands at 74.69%, 69.62%, 67.17%, 64.31%, and 61.03% respectively, as compared to 75.29%, 71.37%, 67.70%, 63.70%, and 63.81% respectively for the same period ended 30th September 2025.

items.statement: Office rationalization and digital process re-engineering underway, expected to optimize expenses in coming quarters
items.quote: Offices rationalization is a work in progress. We are working on it. Not only on that, on digital adoption as well as the process re-engineering is being undertaken. It will get rolled out in the next few quarters to come.

items.statement: Optimistic about IRDAI distribution sector consultation paper; submitted feedback protecting agent interests
items.quote: We remain very optimistic about the positive impact of the proposed distribution sector regulation consultation paper that has been announced by the IRDAI in September 2026. We believe that most of these changes are in the best interest of the customers and will lead to further accelerated growth of the life insurance industry in India.

items.statement: Hedging program covers ~80% of non-par premiums; hedged maturities up to 8 years at good rates
items.quote: Regarding this non-par product, we are continuing with our hedging program as usual. We usually hedge around 80% of the premium. So, our hedging program is continuing, and we are able to hedge at very good rates because of the hardening of the interest rates. And we have already hedged maturity up to the 8 years period.

items.statement: Confident of competitive position under new distribution regulations due to controlled expense ratio
items.quote: Anybody else reducing the cost of distribution alone will still have to do a lot of work to bring their overall expense ratio to be under that. So, we stand to be on a distinctly advantageous position, and will be closely watching the market as it unfolds.

items.statement: Focus on enhancing agent productivity and earnings through training and higher ticket sizes
items.quote: We will be working certainly towards enhancing the earning capability of the agent as well as bringing in products that meets the needs of the customers.

items.statement: IDBI Bank dependence in bancassurance moderated to 20% of total bancassurance business from 40%
items.quote: What it used to be around 50% to bank-driven business and almost 40% to total bancassurance business of Corporation, it has moderated to around 20% of total and 30% to bank.

items.statement: Group business margins expected to improve with focus on group term assurance and group annuity over fund-based products
items.quote: As of now, the majority of the sale is on the fund-based products, but we also have that group annuity and the group term assurance on which we are focusing, where the margins are higher. So once we are able to have a good business in GTIS and group annuity, more growth compared to the fund-based business, the margins of the group business also is likely to be improving.

items.statement: Expect convergence of APE and WRP growth by year-end as ULIPs recover and new products contribute
items.quote: We expect as the year-end approaches, there will be more convergence of APE and WRP growth in the current year as well.

items.statement: Capital management decisions await final RBC guidelines and IFRS implementation
items.quote: We keep maintaining that we are watching, we keep working on the current solvency margins with a clear outlook as to how the RBC as well as the IFRS reporting pans out. Then based on that, take a final call on the distribution of profits or the engaging the capital in a more profitable way.

items.statement: Raised INR372 crores via preferential allotment primarily to repay borrowings
items.quote: As you would be aware, the company has raised INR372 crores through a preferential allotment to investors with the primary objective of repayment of borrowings.

items.statement: Retiring INR344 crores of debt from preferential allotment proceeds
items.quote: The total would be INR344 odd crores, that will be retiring. So we have started paying the same, and we believe it will be sooner completed, the entire INR344 odd crores.

items.statement: Targeting 15% volume growth for full year FY27
items.quote: We see around 15% overall growth should be there in volume for overall basis. Sneha Talreja: For the entire year

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 revenue of INR70 crores from data centre spooling at >30% EBITDA margin and INR40-50 crores from fittings at 17-18% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We are contemplating for the H2 around INR70 crores odd from data center, wherein we expect a margin of, an EBITDA margin of exceeding 30%. Further, we expect around INR50 odd crores from fitting business in the coming quarter to go, where we expect an EBITDA margin of exceeding 17% -18%.

items.statement: Order book at INR670 crores plus INR156 crores LOI expected to convert over next 12 months
items.quote: Our order book also remains strong at over INR 670 crores, including INR ~30 crores order recently received from data center. This order book is excluding the remaining INR 156 crores LOI, which expected to be converted in phases in coming quarters.

items.statement: Expanding into spooling for data centres, then power, oil & gas, nuclear; fittings revenue to ramp up in H2
items.quote: In the second phase, we are planning to move in the power sector. Then in the third phase, we are planning to go in oil and gas sector. After that, we are planning to go into nuclear sector. It will be in a phased manner.

items.statement: Freight costs hit margins in Q2; passing on higher freight in new orders; freight trending down recently
items.quote: On the pipe front, as we said, it will be moving. See, again the freight cost has started depleting from last two days. If this continue and it start depleting, definitely this INR2-INR3 should be

items.statement: Exports hit all-time high of INR147 crores (41% of revenue), grew >50% sequentially
items.quote: Our export business achieved a new milestone, with exports reaching an all-time high of INR 147 crores and constituting 41% of revenue. Exports grew by over 50% sequentially, reflecting strong demand and improved market reach.

items.statement: Order book growth >30% YoY
items.quote: It is around more than 30%.

items.statement: Annual interest savings of INR28-30 crores from debt repayment; H2 savings INR12-13 crores
items.quote: currently we are paying ar ound 344-odd crores on the private placement we made. If you see that number, annual interest saving of up to INR28 crores to INR30 crores would be there. For the coming H2, I believe INR12 crores, INR13 crores would be the saving on the front of interest

items.statement: Employee costs up 34% due to capacity additions over past year
items.quote: Employee fee over a period, we have been adding plants; you have been seeing that also. We finished capacity expansion in the month of May for fitting and expanded capacity of stainless. In the last year also, post this quarter, few more plants were added.

items.statement: ARR net new money guidance of 22%-25% of opening balance for FY27; on track at 11%-12% in H1
items.quote: If I take Q1 plus Q2 put together, we are about 11% to 12% of the opening balance, and our guidance has always been that we will be between 22% to 25%, which I think we are on track.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth MPIS client assets crossed INR46,000 crores; net flows INR3,300 crores in Q2 and over INR6,000 crores in H1
items.quote: Client assets have now crossed about INR46,000 crores, and net flows were very, very strong. For the last six months, we have had more than INR6,000 crores, and Q2 was about INR3,300 crores.

items.statement: Nuvama Private ARR assets crossed INR60,000-62,000 crores; net new money INR5,000 crores in Q2
items.quote: The ARR assets have now crossed about INR60,000-INR62,000 crores. Again, very strong momentum in net new money in Q2. We saw about INR5,000 crores getting added.

items.statement: Total client assets at INR5.5 lakh crores, up 25% YoY; Wealth Management assets at INR3.7 lakh crores; MPIS and ARR assets at INR1.1 lakh crores, up 27%
items.quote: Our overall client asset, that has grown to INR5.5 lakh crores, which is a 25% growth and within the wealth management, our assets are now at INR3.7 lakh crores and as Ashish has also alluded to the fact that MPIS and ARR asset is growing much faster than what is our overall growth. It has grown to INR1.1 lakh crores at a 27% growth.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth loan book at INR6,000 crores, growing 60% YoY; 75% in LAS and ESOP financing
items.quote: Our loan book in this business is about INR6,000 crores, growing about 60% year-over- year. You know that the composition is all liquid assets like LAS, ESOP financing, margin financing, or MTF, with LAS and ESOP being almost 75% of the portfolio.

items.statement: Nuvama Private lending book grew 50% on H1 basis; NII also grew 50% H1; yields stable
items.quote: Here also, we had said that we will leverage the lending book to improve revenues, productivity, and yield. Here, the book has grown by about 50% on an H1 basis, and NII also has grown by about 50% on an H1 basis.

items.statement: Asset Management AUM at INR12,000 crores; Commercial Real Estate Fund I 50-55% committed, targeting 70% in 2-3 months; Fund II targeting INR5,000 crores launch in ~2 weeks
items.quote: Management. Asset Management, starting with commercial real estate first, our previous fund is now about 50-55% committed. Another two to three months, 70% we will reach. So it is time to now launch the second fund, which is going to get launched anytime soon, in maybe another two weeks or so. The target is to raise about INR5,000 crores there

items.statement: Private Credit fund launch in 25-30 days, targeting INR1,500-2,500 crores over 8-10 months; SIF approval received, launch in 25-30 days
items.quote: Private credit, the full team is intact, now in place, and we will launch a private credit fund also in the next maybe 25 days to 30 days. This is the first fund. We will see how the progress goes, but we will target somewhere between INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores or INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Asset Services client assets crossed INR1.6 lakh crores; revenues up 50% YoY; H1 retention 2.7%; Q2 yield 2.5%; full-year yield expected 2.6%-2.8%
items.quote: Client assets have now crossed INR1.6 lakh crores. Retention for H1 remain healthy at 2.7%. We mentioned in the last quarter that there were some new clients which had very high cash collateral composition, and that have now normalized. So Q2, you will see yields are moderated to about 2.5%. But I think if I take a full year perspective, we will be anywhere between 2.6% to 2.7%-2.8% range.

items.statement: Capital Markets: 40 transactions in pipeline (13 ECM, 10 advisory); probability-adjusted revenue target INR85-90 crores; ECM participation share 15%-18%
items.quote: We have right now about 40 transactions in the pipeline, about 13 in ECM, and about 10 in advisory, with a reasonably high two-digit or early three-digit revenue target on that.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth cost-income improved ~200 bps YoY; net new money and client assets per RM up 25-30% YoY
items.quote: Overall margins or cost income ratios have improved by about 200 basis points year-over- year.

items.statement: Nuvama Private ARR assets and ARR revenues per RM up 15-20% YoY; margins improved ~70 bps
items.quote: Here also, I see the impact on the productivity improvement in terms of ARR assets and ARR revenues per RM have almost grown by about 15% to 20% year-over- year, and margins have improved by about 70 basis points across the board.

items.statement: Wealth Management cost-income improvement guidance of 100-200 bps YoY for next couple of years
items.quote: I think in both the businesses this year over last year, we would see an improvement anywhere between 100 basis points - 200 basis points, and that journey should continue for the next couple of years at least.

items.statement: New head office in BKC finalized; rent-free period starts November; ROU accounting charge ~INR25 crores in FY27; full-year opex expected INR550 crores including new HO
items.quote: As we mentioned in the last call also, we have finalized our new HO in BKC. Our rent-free period will start from November. That typically, again, as per the accounting standard, you will have to do a ROU, right of use accounting for that, and that will lead to around INR25 crores of charge for this year, FY27.

items.statement: Added ~250 employees (7% capacity) in last 12 months; 85-90% in business-facing roles; added 90 RMs in Nuvama Wealth and 14-15 RMs in Nuvama Private
items.quote: If you look over the last 12 months, we have almost added 7% capacity give and take 250 odd employees in the company, of which 85%-90% of the people will be in the business facing units, whether it is RMs or the investment people and all.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth NIM saw marginal improvement due to positive MLD hedging gains; yields on lending book stable
items.quote: Yields also saw an uptick in this quarter with marginal improvement in NIM, because we have always maintained that a part of our borrowing happens through MLD, and some hedging gains and losses can lead to these changes in the NIM. For Q2, we were on the positive side of the same.

items.statement: Nuvama Private ARR contributes 64% of revenue; transactional income run rate INR80-90 crores/quarter (60-70% recurring); Pinnacle UHNI offering launched to increase wallet share
items.quote: ARR now contributes about 64% of the revenue. On our initiatives to improve this even further, we spoke about Pinnacle as one of our UHNI offering, which brings together multiple things.

items.statement: Asset Services adding Trustee and RTA services for AIFs/PMSs; RTA live by Nov/Dec (minimal), full by March; Trustee live Q3-Q4
items.quote: Yes, Trustee and RTA for AIFs and PMSs. Trustee services, both should go live. At least RTA will go live with minimum value proposition by end of November or December, and full-blown by March. Trustee also between Q3 and Q4 will go live.

items.statement: Nuvama Private: ~40% of ARR net flows from beyond Tier 1 cities via distribution leverage; NPS in Nuvama Wealth at all-time high of 89
items.quote: Now about 40% of that is coming from beyond tier 1, which is not a reflection that whether we are really present there physically, but it is a reflection of how we are leveraging our distribution to access even places where we are not present.

items.statement: Private Wealth attrition normal; one team movement but 75-80% arrested; RM count higher QoQ; no dent in revenue flows expected
items.quote: On Private Wealth Management, attrition remains normal. There was one team movement that happened, but we were able to arrest about 75% to 80% of that. We looked at the numbers on a quarter-over-quarter basis. We will actually end up with higher number of RMs on the basis previous quarter.

items.statement: Asset Services faces 18-19 strong competitors; new domestic custodian licenses expected but FPI licenses 2-3 years away; confident in value proposition and market share (25% of new PMS/AIF registrations)
items.quote: On a book basis, on a full book basis, on PMS, I think we are around 6% to 7%, and on AIFs, we would be order of magnitude maybe around 8% to 9% of the total book. Of the new registrations that happen every year, this is not of the AUM, this is about the new players who get added every year. We are able to capture 25% of those new additions as our clients.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity at 2.9x; target 2.5x; H1 dividend skipped to manage gearing; loan book grew INR2,000 crores in H1; internal accruals sufficient for 40% lending growth without capital raise
items.quote: Our loan book, as Ashish was also mentioning, that it has gone up by INR2,000 crores in the first six months of this year. We are already at a debt-to-equity gearing of around 2.9x. So basically the idea is that we will be more comfortable if our debt-to-equity is around 2.5x plus minus few basis point here and there, but 2.5x is where ideally we want to be.

items.statement: Board decided no H1 FY27 dividend; reviewing 40-60% payout policy given 29% ROE and growth opportunities; final dividend decision at annual results in April 2027
items.quote: One other thing which we would like to update to the investors and the community is that the board has decided not to declare any H1 FY27 dividend.

items.statement: Asset Services yield expected 2.5%-2.8% for next 2 years assuming 15-25% collateral growth; yield falls if collateral doubles due to cash/G-sec mix shift
items.quote: I think for your purpose, you can assume the yields to remain between 2.5%-2.8% for next two years.

items.statement: Capital Markets: ECM participation share 15-18% of transactions; stronger in IPOs/QIPs, weaker in blocks; actively improving block market share
items.quote: In terms of the total number of transactions, we would range between 15%-18% participation share. So, let's say out of every 100, we would be there in 18- 20 mandates. We are not so strong in blocks, and maybe slightly better in QIPs and even better in IPOs.

items.statement: Wealth Management insurance revenue: 12-13% of Nuvama Wealth revenue; zero in Nuvama Private; monetization clients contributed 35-38% of net new money over last 15 months
items.quote: In Private, insurance is zero. In Wealth, insurance would be about 12%-13% of the revenue. That was first. In Private, when we spoke about the yields, and you said there is a yield improvement, so it would be largely because the proportion of category 2 AIF may have gone higher, and that is the only thing that changes the yield apart from lending.

items.statement: Venture debt fund pre-closed due to strategy underperformance (equity warrants); one-time post-tax charge INR16 crores; accelerated amortization INR9-10 crores over next 12 months
items.quote: This is a one-time charge wherein we pre-closed our venture debt fund, which we launched sometime in FY23. This fund was with a seven-year tenure, the underlying strategy for the fund was to deploy in combination of debt as well as equity warrants. As you know that over the last few years, the growth stage companies has got a lot of multiple ways to have a fundraise which is non-dilutive in terms

items.statement: Debt-to-equity at 2.9x vs 2.5x target; rating agencies and lenders comfortable below 3x; further DE increase could trigger rating watch and covenant tightening
items.quote: If we continue to increase the DE, it puts rating also under watch. It pulls up the covenants of banks also who have given lending. It pulls up the covenants of NCDs also. For an NBFC of our type, generally we have seen rating agencies, banks, everybody is comfortable if you are below 3x, and they are very, very comfortable if you are around 2.5x.

items.statement: ESAR scheme granted September 2026; INR6 crores pre-tax charge in Q2; INR20 crores/quarter for next 4 quarters (INR45 crores full year FY27); then tapering
items.quote: Our employee cost for quarter two also includes our new ESAR scheme, which we have granted sometime in the first week of September. The cost of that ESAR charge is around INR6 crores. I am talking all numbers as pre-tax, so INR6 crores is the opex charge because of that employee cost. That for the full year of FY27 will come to around INR45 crores or a INR20 crores a quarter charge.

items.statement: Custody JV (49%) profit minimal; revenue largely from referrals to clearing; plan to acquire 51% and merge as license regime changes; no impact on clearing revenues
items.quote: That is a very small profit entity, and much of the revenue actually comes through referral into the clearing entity itself. It may have been related to some costs that would have been incurred in that. The overall quantum of profit there, which sits there, is actually minimal.

items.statement: Commodities opportunity ~7-8% of equity derivatives size; 4-5 clients started, ramping margins; steady state in 2-3 quarters; no infrastructure restrictions, just sequencing
items.quote: They are starting out, but overall assessment of the opportunity, what we see right now is like 7%-8% of the size of the opportunity in equity derivatives. People are keen. Out of our client set, I think four or five have started, and some are ramping up the margins also. Maybe it will take another two, three quarters to see the steady state levels.

items.statement: PAG stake sale process ongoing by shareholders; no material update requiring disclosure as of now
items.quote: Nothing as of now. I mean, that process is being done by the shareholders. As I said, if anything meaningful happens which requires us to disclose, we will immediately disclose.

items.statement: Annual sales guidance maintained at INR100 billion; 38% achieved in H1
items.quote: our overall guidance for the year at the start of the year was a hundred billion, which still remains a hundred billion, and we are more confident about it because we've managed to achieve about 40% of the annual sales target during the first six months.

items.statement: Annual completions guidance maintained at INR50 billion; INR14 billion recognized in H1
items.quote: we stay confident with regard to our overall annual guidance of about INR50 billion of completions for this particular year, which will also give a good push to the collections.

items.statement: Full-year operating cash flow expected between INR12-15 billion; INR4.8 billion surplus in H1
items.quote: this can land up anywhere between INR12 billion INR15 billion by the end of the year.

items.statement: H1 sales of INR38 billion (~675 units, 1.6 msf); 40% of annual target achieved
items.quote: we've recorded sales to the tune of about INR38 billion, which is effectively close to about 675-odd units, which have been sold by the company, and about 1.6 million square foot of underlying area has been sold by us.

items.statement: Added ~10 msf developable area in H1 via Farrukhnagar (194 acres) and Sohna (31 acres) acquisitions
items.quote: in terms of new business development, we have added almost close to 10 million square foot of developable area. So there is a net addition of about 8.4 million square foot of developable area.

items.statement: H1 gross margin 31%, Q2 gross margin ~36%; H1 EBITDA margin 13%, Q2 EBITDA margin ~18%
items.quote: The gross profit for the entire six-month period stood at about 31%, whereas for the second quarter, where we saw more mid-income completions rather than affordable housing completions, was almost close to 36%. Likewise, the EBITDA margin for the full half year, as in for the half year, was 13%, but for the second quarter, it stood at about 18%.

items.statement: Portfolio realizations crossed INR17,000/sq ft; single-digit price escalation continuing
items.quote: Overall realizations have crossed INR17,000 at a portfolio level. This will look higher than the entire previous year realization.

items.statement: H1 collections INR17 billion; steady trend of ~INR10 billion per quarter over 8-10 quarters
items.quote: Collections also stood at about INR17-odd billion. The last quarter was a bit of an aberration where the collections were slightly lower. But if we look at a trend of the last eight to 10 quarters, I think collections have been staying steady at about INR10-odd billion per quarter.

items.statement: H1 operating cash surplus INR4.8 billion (28% of collections); prior to land investments and debt repayments
items.quote: we have created about INR4.8 billion surplus during the first six months. This is prior to investments into land and approvals for upcoming projects or any debt repayments.

items.statement: Net debt INR4.5 billion (gross debt INR28.7 billion, cash INR24+ billion); CARE A+ stable rating maintained
items.quote: Our net debt number, if you look at it, stands at about INR4.5 billion, wherein gross debt remains high at INR28.7 billion, but there's a lot of cash sitting in the balance sheet of about INR24 plus billion.

items.statement: H1 business development spend ~INR5 billion; full-year BD spend expected to match OCF of INR12-15 billion
items.quote: If the OCF is going to cross, be anywhere between INR12 billion-INR15 billion, you may also expect business development to that tune for the current year.

items.statement: Delivered 19 msf to date; 9 msf nearing delivery; 23 msf launched since Feb 2024; 27 msf in launch pipeline over 2 years
items.quote: we have delivered till date about 19 million square foot. There is another 9 million square foot which is reaching the delivery stage fairly soon. Besides that, we still have about 50-51 million square foot, of which about 23 million square foot has been launched over the last two and a half years.

items.statement: Launched Tonino Lamborghini Residences (800+ units) in Sector 71; entering premium/branded residences segment
items.quote: We've also done a recent launch where one can say that we've entered the upper middle segment or entry-level premium segment when we launched our first branded residences project by the name of, branded as Tonino Lamborghini Residences. The project had more than 800 units.

items.statement: Farrukhnagar 194-acre land parcel for farmhouse/villa community and resort; low-density development outside zoned area
items.quote: The land can be utilized for doing farmhouses/low-density developments. It is outside the zoned area. We cannot do high-rise developments over there. The intent is to develop this as one of its kind farmhouse/villa community alongside a small but very high-quality resort sort of development.

items.statement: GRAP/NGT construction bans factored into annual planning; assume 10 months of construction activity per year
items.quote: the way we plan is to work for about 10 months in a year, and we are always assuming that these NGT ban on construction activity will arise every year. This is not going away anytime soon. So, this is kind of planned.

items.statement: Construction cost escalation running at 7-9% annually; full-year construction spend expected >2x H1 but <INR2,000 crores
items.quote: if you look at the last decade, every year, we see that on a yearly basis, as labor and material put together, the numbers tend to escalate anywhere between 7% - 9%.

items.statement: H2 launches planned: 2+ msf in Sector 71, 300-400k sf in Sector 37D, 400 units in Sohna Dakshin, iconic tower on Dwarka Expressway
items.quote: Sector 71, we intend to come up with another 2 million plus square foot launch. The last one was in May. I think I can't put an exact month to it right now, but it is at very advanced stages of pre-launch stage work.

items.statement: GDV of recently launched portfolio ~INR350 billion; forthcoming 27 msf pipeline GDV INR300-350 billion
items.quote: If you look at the recently launched portfolio, the GDV stands at about close to 35 odd, INR350 odd billion. For the forthcoming projects as well, which is 27 million square foot, the number will stand anywhere between INR300 billion INR350 billion.

items.statement: Brokerage on Lamborghini project ~4% (typical range 3-5%)
items.quote: Usually, brokerage slabs are in this 3%-5% range. PL will be closer to about 4%.

items.statement: Market holding steady despite macro headwinds; limited secondary stock driving price support for primary sales
items.quote: Market is holding up steady despite whatever macro headwinds which we have seen over these last six months. The market is still holding up quite steady.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target ~10% YoY; FY28-29 aspirational growth 17-18%
items.quote: I think by the end of this year, we should be looking at about a 10% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: FY28-29 aspirational growth 17-18% if momentum sustains
items.quote: I think next year we can definitely think about those numbers. That is what we are working on, to deliver stronger year next year.

items.statement: Festive demand shifted from Q2 to Q3; October demand good, channel inventory low
items.quote: October has been a good month overall, and channel inventory is pretty low now because a lot of it got used up during the festive season.

items.statement: Gross margin 50.2% (+70bps YoY, down sequentially); EBITDA margin 21.3% vs 24% YoY; PAT margin 12.9%
items.quote: Gross margin stood at 50.2%, around 70 basis points higher year-on-year, but lower sequentially as these pressures built through the quarter.

items.statement: Glassware EBITDA breakeven this quarter; gas cost 30% of glassware cost doubled to INR53-54/SCM
items.quote: Higher gas prices have been pretty crazy because we were working at INR53, INR54 in SCM, and we had costs doubled. Gas is almost 30% of our cost.

items.statement: Steelware margins lower due to ramp-up inefficiencies; expected to recover as utilization improves
items.quote: The margins are a lot lower than what it used to be because we are in the setting up phases and starting efficiency optimization phases.

items.statement: Cello Pens margins <1/3 of Unomax; revamping product lines to margin-accretive SKUs
items.quote: The problem has been more from there were a lot of product lines that were running previously that were not making any money for the company.

items.statement: Writing Instruments revenue grew 69.5% YoY led by Cello brand
items.quote: Writing Instruments delivered strong growth of 69.5% year-on-year, led by a robust performance from the Cello brand.

items.statement: Opalware utilization ~80%, marginal YoY growth; target 85% this year, 100% next year
items.quote: Basically, on the opalware front, we are at about 80% capacity. We saw a marginal growth year-on-year. We hope to exhaust this capacity by next year completely.

items.statement: Glassware utilization ~60%; maintenance upgrade ongoing, restart by December
items.quote: On the glassware front, we are still at 60% utilization, though our revenues have started increasing quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Steel bottle capacity ~5M pcs (incl. 2 new lines next quarter); current run-rate ~2M pcs
items.quote: The capacity is almost about 5 million pieces out of this. We are currently at about 2 million.

items.statement: Capex largely done; only maintenance capex going forward
items.quote: Capex, not much. We have done most of the capex. It will just be maintenance capex going forward.

items.statement: Glassware price hike ~8-10% taken last quarter; no hike this quarter
items.quote: Price hike was about 8%-10% in glassware, but it was not only the price hike, it was more of a product mix change that we were able to do during this quarter.

items.statement: Polymer costs still high; crude softening impact visible in 1.5 months; gas price drop would help glassware
items.quote: The impact of lower crude oil, if this stays, will come down in the next one and a half months. So I think, yes, post that we should see some expansion in gross margins.

items.statement: Steel bottle SKU expansion to 50-55 SKUs by December to support ramp-up
items.quote: We are expanding the range to about 50-55 SKUs, which should support a gradual ramp-up through Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Online + quick commerce 15.2% of revenue (15.7% by channel); profitability in line with general trade
items.quote: Our online channel continues to gain share, with e-commerce and quick commerce together contributing 15.2% of revenue.

items.statement: Low-price Chinese glassware imports persist; initiated MIP (Minimum Import Price) representation
items.quote: We have initiated the same in, not an ADD, but an MIP in glassware. We are waiting for how things pan out there.

items.statement: Chinese shipping costs rose during quarter providing temporary relief from dumping
items.quote: Import pressure is still there, though a little higher shipping prices have touched during the quarter because from China, the shipping prices were pretty high.

items.statement: Working capital cycle target 10-15 days; currently elevated due to glassware inventory; receivables controlled
items.quote: We want to bring it down to about 10-15 days overall cycle, which we are striving for. It's just that sometimes the inventory has gone up, sometimes the receivable has gone up.

items.statement: Large cash balance on books; no debt details discussed
items.quote: See, return on equity, basically the idea is that there is a lot of cash on the books, of course. Dharmendra Vora: Yes. Gaurav Rathod: A large part of our balance sheet is

items.statement: Actively seeking acquisitions or new verticals to deploy cash and improve ROE; prefer synergistic businesses
items.quote: We are waiting for an opportunity to have a good company that we can acquire, number one, or we can start something new.

items.statement: Consumerware revenue flat at INR417.2 cr; Writing Instruments 69.5% YoY growth; Moulded Furniture -6.5% YoY
items.quote: Consumerware revenue remained broadly flat at INR417.2 crores during the quarter, reflecting the shift in festive demand to a later period.

items.statement: Segment gross margins: Consumerware 53.4%, Writing Instruments 52.6%, Moulded Furniture 39%
items.quote: Segment gross margin stood at 53.4% for the Consumerware, and 52.6% for the Writing Instruments, and 39% for Moulded Furniture and Allied Products.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Consumerware 64.8%, Writing Instruments 21.5%, Moulded Furniture 13.7%
items.quote: In terms of revenue mix, Consumerware contributed 64.8% of the revenue, Writing Instruments 21.5%, and Moulded Furniture and Allied Products the remaining 13.7%.

items.statement: Channel mix: General trade 70.3%, Online 15.7%, Export 8.1%, Modern trade 5.9%
items.quote: By channel, general trade contributed 70.3% of the revenue. The online channel share rose to 15.7%, with profitability in line with the general trade.

items.statement: Margin recovery dependent on steelware efficiency, gas prices, Cello Pens cost optimization
items.quote: I think it can be significantly higher from here. This is our lowest that we have gone, and it has been that kind of a year. But I think from now on, things are looking better.

items.statement: Moulded Furniture volumes sensitive to polymer price cycles (30-40% hikes hurt volumes)
items.quote: the raw material goes and shoots that high, it becomes difficult for us to sell as much. The volumes do come down because it's a very big hike. It's not a small hike. It's a 30%, 40% hike

items.statement: Glassware inventory reduced drastically; exact rupee/tonnage not disclosed on call
items.quote: I do not think on the call I can tell you those numbers, but it has come down drastically already.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth guidance maintained; full-year profitability margins expected roughly similar to FY2026
items.quote: Supported by our healthy order book, we remain well-positioned to meet our full-year volume growth guidance. items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew ~30% YoY with 24% volume growth and 5% realization improvement to Rs.260/kg
items.quote: For H1 FY27, revenue grew by around 30% year-on-year, supported by a 24% increase in finished goods volume, reflecting a positive demand momentum across our key end markets, and realizations grew by around 5% to Rs.260 per kg.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue crossed Rs.500 crore with ~33% YoY growth, 25% volume growth and 6% realization improvement to Rs.267/kg
items.quote: Our quarterly revenue crossed Rs.500 crores milestone, registering year-on-year growth of approximately 33%. Finished goods volume sales increased by around 25%, where realizations improved by roughly 6% to Rs.267 per kg.

items.statement: H1 FY27 gross margin expanded 161 bps to 60.8%, EBITDA margin expanded 127 bps to 30.9%, PAT margin expanded 86 bps to 19.9%
items.quote: On a cumulative basis for H1 FY2027, our performance was equally compelling. EBITDA rose 35.5% year-on-year to Rs.294 crores, expanding EBITDA margin by 127 basis points to 30.9%. Finally, PAT for the first half expanded 35.8% year-on-year to Rs.189 crores, with PAT margin broadening by

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 60.8% (+52 bps YoY), EBITDA margin 30.6%, PAT margin 19.5%
items.quote: For Q2 FY2027, gross profit reached Rs.305 crores, delivering a robust year-on-year growth of 33.8%, with gross margin expanding 52 basis points to 60.8%. EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.153 crores, up 32.2% year-on-year, maintaining healthy and stable EBITDA margins at 30.6%. Our PAT came in at Rs.98 crores, marking an impressive 32.8% year-on-year growth, with PAT margin holding steady at 19.

items.statement: Export order book ~50%; gained Rs.95 crore export orders to Asian region last quarter
items.quote: So right now, we have roughly 50% of the order books that we have in hand is from the export sector. We have also gained almost Rs.95 crores of orders in last quarter, and that is for exports to Asian region, largely for the exports to Asian region. The overall, if you see it, is upwards of 50% that we have from exports.

items.statement: Rs.80-100 crore projected sales from North American PV dedicated line; more orders from end FY27 and FY28

items.statement: Rs.650 crore ultra-heavy component capex on track for Q4 FY28 commissioning with 20 MW captive solar
items.quote: The Rs.650 crores capex on ultra-heavy component manufacturing is going as per the scheduled timelines. This facility, with our 20 MW captive solar power plant, is expected to be completed and commence operation in the quarter four of FY2028.

items.statement: Board approved additional Rs.500 crore capex for machining (70%) and forging (30%) across FY28-29 funded by debt and internal accruals
items.quote: Further considering the strong demand visibility, healthy order books, and existing capacity utilizations now nearing their peak, our board has approved an additional capex of Rs.500 crores. items.statement: Rs.300 crore debt planned for new Rs.500 crore capex; Rs.300 crore already invested in Rs.650 crore project
items.quote: We propose there is a Rs.300 crores of the debt, which we will be raising from the banks against this Rs.500 crores expansion. As a bridge loan type, you can say. Of course, we also expect there will be still cash liquidity into the balance sheet at the year-end also, regularly.

items.statement: Current capacity: 158,000 MT forging (60% utilised), 82,000 MT machining (77% utilised); new press and hammer commissioned in H1 FY27
items.quote: On the capacity front, our installed capacity forging capacity stands at 1,58,000 metric tons, while our machining capacity stands at 82,000 metric tons. items.statement: Planned additions: 59,000 MT forging and 34,000 MT machining over 2-2.5 years to reach 217,000 MT forging and 116,000 MT machining
items.quote: These plans involve an additional 59,000 metric tons of forging capacity and 34,000 tons of machining capacity, leading to a total capacity of around 2,17,000 tons in forging and 1,16,000 tons in machining in next two to two and a half years.

items.statement: Machining utilisation peaked at 80% last quarter, expected to touch 90% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: We look at our machining capacity utilization levels, they were already peaked out at 80% in last quarter, which is expected to touch close to 90% by Q4.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-throughs, negotiated price increases and favorable mix drove 6% realization improvement in Q2
items.quote: The improvement in realizations was supported by raw material cost pass-throughs, negotiated price increases to recover higher conversion costs, and a favorable product mix.

items.quote: The renewable energy program, which is nearly for 33 megawatt, 30 megawatt DC plus another 3.5 megawatt, is on track, and we expect some generations to happen in Q4. items.statement: Promoter dilution to meet SEBI requirements will be completed within prescribed timeframes
items.quote: Sir, it will comply as per the SEBI requirements. We are clear that it will be done within the time frames.

items.statement: No concern on data center capex from US elections; customer has invested, orders secured, and market opportunity large
items.quote: Not at all. There is a very strong requirement. The Rs.500 crores of order books that we are seeing to be closed by this financial year is a very small number. items.statement: Heavy forging hammer line capacity 2,000 MT/month at Rs.800/kg realization = Rs.1,600-1,800 crore annual opportunity
items.quote: Basically, if you look at the capacity for the hammer line, we have almost 2,000 tons of capacity, and the realization goes up to Rs.800 a kg if we have to sell as machine, which is opportunity size of almost Rs.1,600 crores-Rs.1,800 crores per annum.

items.statement: Capex intensity to increase over next 5 years vs last 5 years; targeting Rs.500 crore top-line addition per year with Rs.150 crore EBITDA
items.quote: The base is bigger. We are looking at, say, adding Rs.500 crores of top line in one year. Jinesh Gandhi: Right. items.quote: On the MHCV side, we have some programs which are already in trial phase and testing phase, for which we have secured some Rs.80 crores of business out of this Rs.950 crores order books, plus some Rs.500 crores we have gained in last quarter. items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin for long-term horizons (FY29-30) guided at around 2.75%.
items.quote: I would like to say that around 2.75% EBITDA margin is a safe bet to consider for such long-term horizons.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to remain in the same range as H1 FY27, including acquisition debt.
items.quote: So, we give guidance of the interest cost remaining in the same range.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target maintained at 1:1, barring temporary opportunities where ROCE makes sense.
items.quote: Yes. So, debt equity, as we have maintained that we would like to go up to 1:1, barring opportunities where ROCE makes sense or not for the temporary phase.

items.statement: India PC market grew ~12% YoY in Apr-Jun quarter led by commercial, education, SMB and premium AI-capable notebooks.
items.quote: IDC reported that India's PC market grew by about 12% in the April to June quarter, led by commercial, education and small business demand and also by premium and AI-capable notebooks.

items.statement: Commercial and enterprise demand expected to be steadier in H2; consumer demand cautious due to higher prices affecting affordability.
items.quote: We expect commercial and enterprise demand to be steadier part of the market in the second half, and we are managing inventory and credit accordingly.

items.statement: Commercial market (~70% of India ICT) continues to grow very strong; consumer impact from price rises is miniscule so far.
items.quote: While because of the continued price rise, there is a possible contraction in the consumer market. But the commercial market continues to grow very strong, which is almost 70% of India's total ICT market.

items.statement: AI implementation in India at very nascent stage; good opportunity seen for next 2-3 years with remote probability of crash.
items.quote: AI usage or implementation in India is at a very, very nascent stage. So, since we are already not into that volume, the probability of any crash is very remote, and we see good opportunity even on AI front in India for at least next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Consolidated Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 106 bps to 3.56%; PAT margin improved 69 bps to 2.1%.

items.statement: Gross margins improved ~100 bps in Q2; expansion driven by mix and pricing discipline, not just operating leverage.
items.quote: Gross margins improved by close to 100 basis points in the quarter. So, the expansion is coming from mix and pricing discipline, not only operating leverage.

items.statement: Semiconductor business margins broadly 2x company-level margins; H1 FY27 semiconductor revenue 2x full FY26, targeting 3-4x for full FY27.
items.quote: Broadly, it is 2x on margin front. As far as top line is concerned, last year -- last financial year, Rashi alone in semiconductor, we did about $20 million of business. What I can say right now is in just first 6 months of the year, we have done 2x of the last year number.

items.statement: Enterprise/data center opportunity >INR20,000 crores of orders placed in last quarter; company chose not to play active role due to 50% growth and lower ROIs.
items.quote: To the best of my estimates, last one quarter itself, more than INR20,000 crores of orders have been placed. But there, we chose not to play a very active role because our growth was already at 50%.

items.statement: Targeting enterprise business to contribute ~20% of revenue next year; semiconductor and VDA to contribute >10% of top line.
items.quote: So, enterprise, I think next year should be about 20%. And semiconductor is just the start with the JV, but it will be a substantial in terms of top line and more importantly, on the bottom line as well.

items.quote: With regards to the QIP, yes, you're absolutely right that this QIP preparation is a little -- we are doing as an advanced preparation for growth engine.

items.statement: INR900 crores QIP with 1:1 debt-equity gives INR1,800-2,000 crores deployable capital, supporting INR12,000-15,000 crores additional revenue at 6-7x working capital cycles.

items.statement: Acquired 67% stake in VDA Infosolutions for enterprise IT, cloud, cybersecurity, system integration and managed services.
items.quote: We have acquired a 67% stake, bringing system integration, cybersecurity, cloud and managed services.

items.statement: Formed JV with Restar Corporation (Japan) for semiconductor and embedded solutions; 2 Japanese brands added, design center in Bangalore with Restar engineer deputed.
items.quote: We also formalized the joint venture with Japan-based Restar Corporation to establish a dedicated semiconductor and embedded solutions business. items.statement: Q2 FY27 growth breakdown: 30% from price increases, 10-11% from volume, 10% from new businesses (VDA, semiconductor).
items.quote: Our 50% growth can be very simply dissected in 30% growth has come from the price increase, which is the trend. 10% to 11% has come from the volume increase, which is the unit increase and 10% has come from new businesses.

items.statement: DRAM prices forecast to continue rising for at least 1 year; flash and storage prices flattened.
items.quote: In the product categories, DRAM, particularly, which is the core reason for price elevation, the forecast is that it will continue to grow even at least in next 1 year, although I see SK Hynix and Samsung stock prices already dropping, but the trend that we are told is going to be only increasing. items.statement: Non-PC products (accessories, peripherals, CPUs, motherboards, hard drives) contribute >35-37% of business, enabling extra margin capture.
items.quote: For Rashi Peripherals, as we all know that more than 35%, 37% of the business is non-PC, predominantly accessories, peripherals, CPUs, motherboards, hard drives. All these places, we always have an opportunity to earn some extra margin.

items.statement: Channel partner ecosystem expanded to 10,280 partners across 728 towns; focus on deeper engagement and wallet share.

items.statement: JV with Restar enables access to Japanese manufacturers in India (e.g., Maruti, Daikin); discussions started with 5 Japanese manufacturers this month.

items.quote: Working capital days improved to 55 days from 61 days. Debtors days reduced to 43 from 46 and creditors days increased to 48 from 44.

items.quote: Net debt to equity rose to 0.76x. Both reflect deliberate choice. We built inventory to secure supply in a constrained market and to committed enterprise and AI projects. We also funded VDA acquisition through this route.

items.statement: QIP of INR900 crores prepared as advanced growth capital; may not execute if internal accruals and factoring suffice.
items.quote: With regards to the QIP, yes, you're absolutely right that this QIP preparation is a little -- we are doing as an advanced preparation for growth engine. items.quote: However, to your question about VDA, we've just added Q2 revenue of VDA, which is at this moment, very small, less than about 2% only. So, it's not very significant at this moment.

items.quote: Restar Corporation, it's a Japanese distribution -- semiconductor distribution company. It's a $4 billion Japanese conglomerate. They are like us only, but they are focused only on semiconductor business and more focused on design and supply both.

items.statement: Annualized ROCE and ROE both ~23% in Q2 FY27, highest since listing.

items.quote: On the domestic front, we have secured two orders aggregating INR30 crores for flare packages with an overall execution timeline of 16 months.

items.statement: Current bidding pipeline stands at INR5,000 crores excluding recent order win, broadly balanced between domestic and international opportunities
items.quote: Our current bidding pipeline stands at INR5,000 crores, excluding the recent order win, with a broadly balanced contribution from domestic and international opportunities.

items.statement: Healthy opportunity landscape across domestic (refining, petrochemicals, fertilizers, metals, minerals) and international markets (Africa focus: Nigeria, Kenya, Ethiopia)
items.quote: Beyond our existing order book, we continue to see a healthy opportunity landscape across both domestic and international markets.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA grew 50% YoY to INR39.4 crores with 10.6% margin; Q2 FY27 EBITDA grew 6.6% YoY to INR20.8 crores with 11.1% margin
items.quote: EBITDA for first half of this year stood at INR39.4 crores, registering a growth of 50% year-on-year, while EBITDA margins stood at 10.6% for first half of this year.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance mentioned; working capital funding expected from customer payment terms, reserves, and bank limits without additional debt
items.quote: We are quite confident that this year and next year, with whatever the customer payment terms what we have, and reserves and the bank limits what we have, we should be able to fund the working capital.

items.statement: H2 FY27 expected to be more execution-intensive; historically H2 contributes 60%-70% of annual revenue
items.quote: Historically, H2 contributes approximately 60%-70% of our annual revenue, supported by the progress of ongoing projects and the achievement of project milestones.

items.statement: Commodity price risk (copper, nickel, aluminum) managed via back-to-back arrangements, hedging, pre-booking; PSU contracts have steel price variation clauses
items.quote: We do have some provisions of mitigating this risk by doing some back-to-back arrangement with our sub-vendor, hedging it, or pre-booking it.

items.statement: Expanding into adjacent opportunities: green hydrogen, sustainable fuels, sustainable chemicals via JNK Chemdist; 50% of INR5,000 crores bid pipeline is non-heater opportunities
items.quote: Around 50% of it is other than the, basically the core heater opportunities.

items.statement: Kenya refinery inquiries expected in 2-3 months, order finalization in 4-5 months; Nigeria refinery additional heaters (INR700-800 crores) yet to be awarded
items.quote: In the bid pipeline which is there is almost something like INR700 crores-INR800 crores for the existing Nigeria and the fertilizer opportunity.

items.statement: BPCL Vizag refinery tenders likely in 6-8 months, ordering in 12 months; opportunity size ~INR5,000 crores for players like JNK; not in current bid pipeline
items.quote: Total opportunity size, you can say, will be around INR5,000 crores for people like us.

items.statement: Q2 revenue deferred by INR30-40 crores due to logistical challenges and monsoon disruptions; recovery expected in Q4 (Jan-Mar)
items.quote: It is around INR30 crores-INR40 crores, which was like logistically and delays and due to rains, which we could not dispatch around that amount.

items.statement: Commodity price fluctuation (copper, nickel, aluminum) remains major risk for project business; ongoing projects not significantly impacted
items.quote: But yes, largely, we need to find out when the risk arises. At least ongoing project, we do not see that having any significant impact on our numbers. But yes, going forward, as a part of project business, that remains one of the major risk.

items.statement: JNK Chemdist order book ~INR20 crores (process equipment); main focus on R&D for green hydrogen/sustainable fuels; larger revenues expected in ~2 years
items.quote: The order book per se is about INR20 crores as of now for JNK Chemdist, and which is mainly on the process equipment side. But our main focus is on the R&D and on the renewable fuel, green hydrogen side, which will take some time, maybe about two years or so, to actually culminate into a larger amount of revenues.

items.statement: Non-heater bid pipeline: INR1,000 crores already bid/under negotiation; INR1,500 crores to be bid in 1-2 months; largely domestic opportunities
items.quote: About INR2,500 crores is the non-heater opportunities which we have, out of which around INR1,000 crores is where the bid is, bid pipeline, we already bid, and it is under discussion and negotiation. And INR1,500 crores is something which we would bid soon, say in about one month or two months or so.

items.statement: Dangote Nigeria refinery balance scope (site erection, commissioning, supervision) under discussion; possible materialization in 2-3 months; JNK Global contractual timeline not yet started
items.quote: We can expect in another two to three months, this can get materialized. In another two to three months, not more than that.

items.statement: NTPC bid due date is November 20, 2026; ONGC offshore and steel company projects already bid
items.quote: Bid due date is 20th November as of now.

items.statement: Management acknowledges wide order disclosure range (300-600) was error; will narrow range going forward for better visibility
items.quote: Sir, I can say there was some error in the disclosure, error to the extent we should not have given 300 to 600. We should have given 500 to something, whereas the order value is. Then, yes, going forward, we will be narrowing the range.

items.statement: Investing Rs 25 crore in further debottlenecking of bio-based chemicals
items.quote: the investment of about Rs. 25 crores in further debottlenecking bio-based chemistry.

items.statement: Total distillery capacity stands at 800 kL per day with multi-feedstock capability
items.quote: Our total distillery capacity stands at 800 kL per day.

items.statement: Strong demand for bio-based chemicals driven by sustainable alternatives and fossil cost increases
items.quote: We continue to see opportunities across domestic and international markets supported by demand for sustainable bio-based alternatives.

items.statement: Bio-based chemical EBITDA margin improved to 10.8% in Q2 FY27 from 10.2% year ago
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 10.8% from 10.2% reflecting the benefits of earlier debottlenecking initiatives and improved operating efficiency.

items.statement: Bio-based specialty chemicals contributed 52% of H1 FY27 chemical revenue
items.quote: it is about 52% of bio-based specialty chemicals.

items.statement: Maize prices are high creating margin pressure on grain-based ethanol production
items.quote: the rise in maize prices has further increased maize margin pressures on grain-based ethanol production.

items.statement: Government restricted diversion of sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses to ethanol for upcoming supply year
items.quote: The government has recently restricted the diversion of sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses towards ethanol for the upcoming ethanol supplier with the objective of ensuring adequate domestic sugar availability.

items.statement: Inventory decline from Rs 775 crore to Rs 260 crore is seasonal due to sugar stock cycle
items.quote: The inventory largely is coming because of the seasonal nature of the business. In March, the inventory is high because the sugar stocks are at the highest. And in September, you see those stocks much lower.

items.statement: Bio-based chemical H1 FY27 EBITDA of Rs 41.2 crore is 86% of full FY26 annual chemical EBITDA
items.quote: H1 FY '27 EBITDA of bio-based chemical is 86% of annual EBITDA of FY '26.

items.statement: Drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka affecting feedstock availability and farm economy
items.quote: Maharashtra and Karnataka are both suffering from a drought and this can affect the farm economy.

items.statement: Secured European patents for anti-cancer pharmaceutical composition and bio-based rubber enforcement technology
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured European patents for our anti-cancer pharmaceutical composition and bio-based rubber enforcement technology along with a Chinese patent for our antiviral compounds.

items.statement: DME pilot plant with ICT Mumbai expected to complete by March 2027
items.quote: this pilot plant stage is expected to complete by March of 2027.

items.statement: Triple-negative breast cancer drug discovery applied for CDSCO permissions for preliminary efficacy trials
items.quote: We are hoping that we will get this permission in this current quarter.

items.statement: Preliminary efficacy trials budgeted at Rs 15-20 crore max, plan to out-license if positive
items.quote: A budgeting for this would be in the range of Rs. 15-Rs. 20 crores max. If we get positive results in these preliminary efficacy trials, then we would look to out-license this molecule to pharma companies in India and abroad.

items.statement: Grain-based distillery commissioned end of June 2024, operating at capacity for OMC ethanol orders
items.quote: we have commissioned the facility in the end of June, i.e. end of Q1 and the facility, it is operating at capacity to meet the orders we had for the ethanol-based program.

items.statement: Expects PAT positive in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as historically strong quarters for sugar business
items.quote: Q3 and Q4 are always strongly positive and we are hoping for the same this time.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: revenue >₹4,700 crore, EBITDA >₹200 crore, PAT ₹100 crore
items.value: Revenue >4700 crore, EBITDA >200 crore, PAT 100 crore
items.quote: Based on our performance during the first half of the year, the momentum across our verticals and the strong execution pipeline ahead of us, we remain firmly confident of achieving our FY27 guidance of crossing ₹4,700 crore in revenue, crossing EBITDA of ₹200 crore and delivering a PAT of ₹100 crore.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 188 bps YoY to 5.4%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter expanded by 188 bps year-on-year to 5.4% in Q2 FY27, demonstrating our continued focus on operational efficiency and disciplined execution.

items.statement: H1 FY27 added new contracts with ACV >₹900 crore, mostly in Smart Infra, Energy and Engineering
items.quote: Our half yearly revenues stood at ₹2,180 crore jumping 35% year-on-year, driven by addition and mobilization of the new contracts with an Annual Contract Value of over ₹900 crore over this period.

items.statement: Purchase consideration for two acquisitions in H1 FY27 was ₹340 crore, largely funded by acquisition debt
items.quote: The purchase consideration paid for the 2 acquired entities was ₹340 Crore which was largely funded by acquisition debt.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating cash flow 76% of operating EBITDA; net debt ₹126 crore
items.quote: We generated operating cashflows of 76% of operating EBITDA during the first half of the year with our net debt position at ₹126 Crore.

items.statement: Working capital days 38 in Q2 FY27, expected to settle at ~40 days for full year
items.quote: Our working capital days stands at 38 days as of Q2, almost flat quarter-on-quarter. With growth trajectory in H2 and also large deal mobilization taking full shape, we expect that the working capital days likely to settle down at 40 levels.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of LSG Sky Chefs India in August 2026; STEAG consolidated full quarter
items.quote: We successfully completed the acquisition of LSG Sky Chefs India in August 2026, and its financials have been consolidated into our results effective August 2026.

items.statement: Smart Infra, Energy & Engineering revenue share to rise from 1/5 in FY26 to >1/3 by end FY27
items.quote: The share of revenues in this segment is expected to rise from one-fifth in FY26 to more than one-third by end of the year.

items.statement: Industrial sector revenue share increased to 37% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We are strategically accelerating our presence in the industrial sector, and our share of revenues from industrials sector has increased to 37%.

items.statement: Workforce >100,000; added 8,000+ employees in H1 FY27 including 2,800 from acquisitions
items.quote: Our overall workforce stands over one hundred thousand employees, and we added over 8,000 employees during the first half of the year. This also includes additions due to inorganic growth which added over 2,800 head counts.

items.statement: Foundit sales ₹30 crore in Q2 FY27 (62% YoY, 19% QoQ); EBITDA loss reduced to ₹12 crore
items.quote: In foundit, our business continued to witness upwards momentum, sales for the quarter stood at ₹30 Crore registering a 62% year-on-year and 19% quarter-on-quarter and EBITDA losses reducing from ₹14 crore to ₹12 Crore sequentially.

items.statement: Foundit targeting near breakeven by Q4 FY27; FY27 burn <₹40 crore (H1 ₹26 crore, H2 ₹12-13 crore)
items.quote: As you can see from the results the H1 burn has been around INR26 crores from this business. And we expect to reduce this to 50% of the H1 burn in the H2. So, we have already burned INR 26 crores. We may burn another INR 12 crores to INR 13 crores in the H2, bringing down our EBITDA burn from this business to below INR 40 crores for the current year.

items.statement: Board approved ₹150 crore loan limit to foundit; ₹106 crore lent as of Q2 FY27
items.quote: At a board level we have a total approval of close to around INR 150 crores of loans to be lent to foundit. As of now, as we speak we have around INR 106 crores of already loans have been lent as of now.

items.statement: Organic growth target 18-20% for FY28 on FY27 base; long-term 3x GDP growth rate
items.quote: I want to put my neck out and say that we'll be able to repeat performance, at least from an organic growth perspective now after integrating these businesses to grow at least 18% to 20% on this base for next year.

items.statement: Security Services margin at 3.2% in Q2 FY27; target 4-4.5% market margins
items.quote: Security obviously is a separate segment given the focus that we have to also turn around that business and take it to market margins of, 4%, 4.5% levels. It's still hovering around,3%, 3.2%.

items.statement: STEAG contributed ~₹280 crore revenue and ~₹30 crore EBITDA in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In the Smart Infra segment, you will see close to around INR 280 crores of revenues coming in from STEAG itself and close to around INR 30-odd crores of bottom line is already accounted.

items.statement: LSG contributed ₹18 crore revenue and ₹4-5 crore EBITDA in Q2 FY27 (Aug-Sep)
items.quote: INR 18 crores in revenues and almost INR 4 crores to INR 5 crores in EBITDA.

items.statement: Unbilled revenue ~35 days; only ₹11 crore non-current (>1 year) from STEAG milestone billing
items.quote: From an unbilled perspective, only INR 11 crores is actually exceeding 1 year mark which is classified as non-current UBR because it is milestone billing in STEAG. Other than that, everything is current unbilled revenue. The unbilled revenue should hover around 35 days.

items.statement: Tax rate guidance maintained at 22% for FY27 despite H1 ETR ~18%
items.quote: H1 level, ETR is around 18%, if I am not wrong. So, I think we should stick to 22% guidance, what we have done in the last quarters.

items.statement: Thermal power O&M TAM large: peak demand 271 GW, 66% thermal; thermal share 50-55% through FY30-36
items.quote: This summer the peak demand was 271 gigawatts, of which 66% came from thermal. And with massive investments that are happening in renewables, it's still expected over FY30, FY36 that thermal will continue to hold 50% to 55% of the share of the peak power consumption.

items.statement: STEAG has international footprint in one African country; targeting more global contracts
items.quote: We also have an international footprint with STEAG in one of the African countries and as an integrated service provider, we're trying to increase our international presence. And that's going to be our next vector of growth to expand

items.statement: Borrowing costs elevated due to macro environment and tighter liquidity; mitigated by strong cash generation
items.quote: While borrowing costs are expected to remain elevated given the prevailing macroeconomic environment and tighter liquidity conditions, our strong cash generation outlook provides confidence in our ability to accelerate debt repayment and mitigate the impact of higher financing costs.

items.statement: No fresh equity issuance mentioned; acquisitions funded largely by debt and accruals
items.quote: The purchase consideration paid for the 2 acquired entities was ₹340 Crore which was largely funded by acquisition debt. Also to note that the acquired entities came with cash balances of approximately ₹188 Crore.

items.statement: FY2027 revenue guidance raised to INR 6,500-6,800 crores (54-61% growth), EBITDA margin maintained at 14-15%, PAT margin raised to 9-10%
items.quote: Revenue, we are raising it to INR 6,500 crores, INR 6,800 crores, up from INR 6,000 crores, INR 6,500 crores, which is a growth of 54% to 61% over the year. EBITDA margins, we are maintaining still at 14%-15%, while the PAT margin we are now raising now to 9% to 10%, which earlier was 8.5% to 9.5%.

items.statement: FY2027 market share guidance revised to 43-45% from current ~42%
items.quote: On our revised guidance, our FY2027 share is expected to be in the range of 43% to 45%.

items.statement: H1 FY2027 gross margin 30.4% (+374 bps YoY); Q2 gross margin 30% flat YoY, down from Q1 30.8% due to SOC/memory cost absorption
items.quote: On the margin side, our gross margin for the first half was 30.4%, up 374 basis points year-on- year. Three things drove it: a richer brand and product mix, deeper localization initiatives, and operating leverage. In Q2, gross margin was 30%, flat year-on-year, and slightly below Q1, 30.8%, as we began absorbing part of the input cost

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin guidance kept at 14-15% despite 16.3% in H1 to cushion market share strategy amid volatile input costs
items.quote: That is why we are keeping our full-year EBITDA margin guidance at 14%-15%, even after a 16.3% in the first half, so as to keep enough cushion to support our market share growth strategy in such a volatile input cost environment.

items.statement: SOC, DDR, flash prices risen sharply; strategic inventory buildup in SOC and memory to secure supply and margins; gradual price pass-through to avoid channel shock
items.quote: Critical semiconductor components like SOC, DDR, and flash prices have risen sharply across the electronics industry. Ahead of this, we took strategic positions in SOC and memory, which is why inventory is on the higher side on our balance sheet.

items.statement: ~INR 650 crores capex planned over next 2-3 years to double capacity by late FY2029/early FY2030 across Kadapa Phase 3 (22 acres acquired) and Greater Noida (civil construction starting next quarter)
items.quote: Broadly, we had called out about INR 650 crores will go into capex, and we are looking at about doubling our capacity by late FY2029 to early FY2030. This capacity expansion will happen across two of our campuses.

items.statement: Kadapa plant at 2.5M units/month; plan to more than double via Kadapa Phase 3 and new Greater Noida facility funded from QIP; lens plant (2M/month) in Greater Noida, housing/enclosures plant in Kadapa trials this quarter, cable plant in Q4
items.quote: Our Kadapa plant capacity is at 2.5 million units a month, and we plan to more than double this through Kadapa phase 3 and a new facility in Greater Noida, funded from the QIP.

items.statement: CP PLUS contributed 88% of Q2 revenue (vs 86% YoY); IP products 79% of CP PLUS portfolio (vs 71% YoY); market share ~42% in 12 months to Sep 2026 (vs 30% at IPO)
items.quote: CP PLUS remains the core engine of this growth. It contributed about 88% of revenue in quarter two against 86% a year ago. Within CP PLUS, IP products are now about 79% of the portfolio, up from 71%.

items.statement: Multi-brand strategy: CP PLUS flagship, CP PLUS PRO premium enterprise (Q4 FY2027 launch), NEXIVUE entry/mid-market (launched April, good pickup), EYRA entry-level (launch end of month/December)
items.quote: Through our multi brand strategy, we now have a portfolio that addresses every segment of the market, from entry level to the most premium enterprise. CP PLUS is our flagship and mainstream brand. The new range of CP PLUS PRO series targets the premium enterprise segment, and its rollout is planned in the Q4 of FY2027.

items.statement: Working capital up in H1 due to strategic component inventory buildup; receivable days improved to 87 in Q2 from 93 in Q1 and 105 YoY; expected to normalize as component positions used up
items.quote: up in the half mainly due to increase in inventory because of strategic component buying that I described to maintain supply strength. It was a deliberate choice to secure supply and cost. Collections have improved. Receivable days came down to 87 in Q2 from 93 in Q1 and 105 a year ago

items.statement: QIP of INR 1,500 crores completed September with leading domestic/global institutions; proceeds for debt repayment, capacity expansion via AIL Dixon, inorganic acquisitions, general corporate purposes
items.quote: In September, we completed our qualified institutions placement and raised INR 1,500 crores. Leading domestic and global institutions took part, and I thank them once again for their confidence in the company and management.

items.statement: Invested INR 45.4 crores for 30% stake (fully diluted) in BLUE KGraph AI Solutions; video compression tech cuts storage/bandwidth up to 90%, no GPU needed, works with installed cameras; 1 board seat + 1 observer seat
items.quote: Our board approved, and we signed agreements to invest INR 45.4 crores for a 30% stake on a fully diluted basis in BLUE KGraph AI Solutions.

items.statement: Management estimates 18-20% unit CAGR over 3-5 years; value growth higher than unit growth due to ongoing SOC/memory price rises; backward integration benefits to flow from next financial year
items.quote: From a unit growth perspective, we still see that from a three- to five-year horizon, there should be a CAGR of 18%-20% on unit terms.

items.statement: 40+ STQC-certified brands online but no significant ground traction from new entrants; government strict on trusted supply chains, no land-border companies certified yet; competition-crushing strategy to grow share
items.quote: As per the online portal, there are almost 40-plus brands now which are STQC certified, and I am sure there will be new entrants also trying, but we are not seeing any significant traction on the ground levels at the moment.

items.statement: Export strategy over 18-24 months targeting China-plus-one markets; product range (CP PLUS PRO, entry-level) varies by country; entry mode flexible (own brand, partnership, inorganic, ODM)
items.quote: we look at markets where it is more of a China plus one strategy. Those markets are where it is more conducive to go for us initially. The products that would go are products that are fit for those markets

items.statement: No new government notification yet on mandatory STQC for DVR/NVR from April 1; policy under work-in-progress; when implemented will further boost domestic brands' recorder market share
items.quote: There is no new notification as such from the Government of India as yet regarding the DVR and NVR. Yes, there have been instances of communicating with the industry, and government is working on a policy, but until that is out, we can't say when this will kick in.

items.statement: 30,000-35,000 installers/resellers on app; 2,000 system integrators; pan-India presence; CP PLUS de facto standard in most shops/installers
items.quote: We have 30,000 - 35,000 installers and resellers connected with us on our app where they collect points and get some small incentives and they buy our products. That's the time, dealer base and then 2,000 installers, system integrators who are parallelly doing installations and projects.

items.statement: H1 operating cash flow absorbed by 90% growth; comfortable with current working capital strategy; improvement in receivables and other working capital elements
items.quote: If you see in the H1, when you grow at 90%, most of the operating cash flow does go into growth. I think otherwise, we are fairly comfortable where it is.

items.statement: Standalone revenue guidance for FY27 is around INR2,300 crores
items.quote: To meet the overall annual guidance of around INR2,300 crores, you would require to deliver INR1,875 crores in H2 alone.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue guidance for FY27 is INR950-1,000 crores plus power sale revenue
items.quote: Consolidated revenue should be around INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores. For the entire year, but overall, we should cross INR2,300 crores on, the standalone basis, and power sale revenue will get added on top of this.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 revenue target INR850-900 crores
items.quote: We are planning to do around INR900-odd crores, we are hoping to do around INR850 to INR900 crores in Q3 and, the remaining in Q4.

items.statement: H2 FY27 power sale revenue guidance INR40-50 crores
items.quote: Overall for the H2 we are expecting about INR40 crores to INR50 crores of revenue from the sale of power.

items.statement: NOPL project completion expected by end of Q1 or early Q2 FY28
items.quote: We are expecting, completion to happen by the end of Q1 or a little bit of spill over can happen in the Q2 of FY28.

items.statement: NOPL peak generation to start from Q2 FY28
items.quote: But Yes, so peak generation will start from Q2.

items.statement: NOPL project expected to generate INR100 crores free cash flow annually
items.quote: INR100 crores of free cash flow, can be expected, from this project every year.

items.statement: NOPL project PAT expected INR70-75 crores annually (~12% margin)
