items.quote: A PAT with including depreciation will be around INR70-odd crores, INR70 crores to INR75 crores, around 12%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance ~15% (+/-1%) for T&D projects
items.quote: Our current guidance is that we will maintain the similar EBITDA margins, around 15% odd, plus or minus 1% here and there.

items.statement: Full year FY27 interest cost guidance INR70-75 crores
items.quote: Our overall interest cost for the whole year as last year it was about INR 65 crores it will remain around seventy INR70 crores, INR75 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Quarterly interest cost guidance INR18-20 crores
items.quote: Around INR18 crores to INR20 crores we can expect as a quarterly interest cost.

items.statement: Debtor days reduction target 40-50 days by year-end vs last year
items.quote: We can expect at least about 40 to 50 days reduced from our debtor days as compared to the last year.

items.statement: Received two Power Grid orders worth INR120.69 crores and INR153.76 crores
items.quote: During the period, we received two significant orders from Power Grid Corporation of India Limited. One order valued at approximately INR120.69 crores for 400 kV GIS substation package from Power Grid covering the Baroda and Rajgarh substation. Also received another valued approximately INR153.76 crores from Power Grid for the 400 kV AIS substation package SS-136T for the TBCB at the Tumkur II poo

items.statement: NOPL solar EPC contract valued ~INR3,517 crores for 969 MW AC across 152 locations
items.quote: In solar EPC, our NOPL project covers 152 locations across Maharashtra with a plant capacity of 969 megawatt AC equivalent to 1,163 megawatt peak. Vikran's EPC contract for this project is valued approximately INR3,517 crores.

items.statement: NOPL signed long-term facility agreement with IREDA for INR2,941.19 crores financing
items.quote: Recently, NOPL entered into the long-term facility agreement with the IREDA agency for financing of up to INR2,941.19 crores against the estimated project cost of approximately INR4,200 crores.

items.statement: NOPL project estimated cost ~INR4,200 crores
items.quote: against the estimated project cost of approximately INR4,200 crores.

items.statement: Commissioned ~90 MW across 18 sites in NOPL project; advanced stage for further 100 MW
items.quote: At present, the company is able to commission nearly 10% of the required capacity even before the start of first disbursement from the lender. So now we have commissioned around 18 sites with a capacity of nearly 90 megawatt within, and we are in advanced stages for further 100 megawatt, which is expected to complete in the next couple of months.

items.statement: NOPL project targets 500 MW execution in FY27
items.quote: Actually, we are planning to do around, 500 megawatt is what they are planning to push this financial year.

items.statement: Standalone H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.3% vs 14.3% YoY; PAT margin improved to 6% from 4.4%
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 11.3% compared to 14.3%. Profit after tax for the first half increased at INR25.38 crores as compared to INR14.78 crores in H1 FY26, representing a growth of approximately 72%. PAT margin has also improved to 6% as compared to 4.4% in corresponding last year.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 9.5% vs 14.3% YoY; PAT margin 1.9% vs 4.4%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for the first half is INR33.53 crores as compared to INR48 crores in H1 '26. EBITDA margin is stood at 9.5% as compared to 14.3% for corresponding period last year. The consolidated profit after tax for the first half is stood at INR6.74 crores as compared to INR14.78 crores in first half of FY26. PAT margin is 1.9% compared to 4.4%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin 9.1% vs 14.4% YoY; PAT margin 3.6% vs 5.2%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR20.12 crores as compared to INR25.43 crores in Q2 FY26. EBITDA margin was at 9.1% compared to 14.4% corresponding to last year. The profit after tax for the quarter is at INR7.87 crores compared to INR9.12 crores in Q2 FY26. PAT margin stands at 3.6% compared to 5.2% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Unrecognized price variation revenue INR13-16 crores expected in H2 FY27
items.quote: So around INR13 crores to INR16 crores of price variation revenue is not yet recognized.

items.statement: Most costs covered by price variation clauses; only small portion exposed to commodity inflation
items.quote: There's only a very small portion of our business which is not covered by price variation. So the impact of that small portion is, can be plus or minus, but most of our purchase or most of our sale is pass-through.

items.statement: IREDA loan interest rate 9.15%
items.quote: The loan carries an interest of 9.15%.

items.statement: Borrowing cost ~11-11.5% ROI
items.quote: We are looking at about 11%, 11.5%.

items.statement: Standalone H1 FY27 operating cash flow INR258 crores vs negative INR166 crores YoY
items.quote: Our standalone statements reflect a net cash generation from operating activity of INR258 crores during the H1 FY27, compared to net cash used in operation activity at INR166 crores in the last year first half.

items.statement: Debtors reduced ~INR200+ crores vs last year
items.quote: This is almost around INR200 plus crores has been reduced in debtors.

items.statement: Received INR45 crores from Jal Jeevan Mission in H1 FY27
items.quote: Yes,we received significant funds around INR45 crores was received in Q2, and this is going to continue in the subsequent years. INR45 crores is the entire H1.

items.statement: NOPL IREDA loan sanctioned INR2,941 crores at 9.15%
items.quote: NOPL has entered into a long-term agreement with IREDA for financing INR2,941 crores against an estimated project cost of INR4,200 crores. The loan carries an interest of 9.15%.

items.statement: Vikran infused funds into NOPL via NCDs; interest cost to continue until subsidiary repays
items.quote: There will be some interest cost will continue at Vikran level because whatever funds we have infused in NOPL, that will remain, I mean, that will cost some interest at Vikran level. But yes, we are expecting a good cash flow from our subsidiary, and that's where we will be able to repay these loans as soon as possible and reduce the interest cost.

items.statement: NOPL project generated INR4.66 crores revenue and free cash in H1 FY27
items.quote: So already this year we saw -- this first half or last quarter itself we saw around INR4.66 crores of revenue and free cash coming in from the project.

items.statement: NOPL project expected to generate INR130 crores free cash flow to Vikran annually
items.quote: Rather, it gives INR130 crores of free cash flow to the to the investor, that is Vikran Engineering.

items.statement: NOPL solar project 969 MW AC (1,163 MW peak) across 152 locations in Maharashtra
items.quote: In solar EPC, our NOPL project covers 152 locations across Maharashtra with a plant capacity of 969 megawatt AC equivalent to 1,163 megawatt peak.

items.statement: Commissioned 132 kV Miao-Namsai transmission line (40.6 km, 138 towers) in Arunachal Pradesh
items.quote: The project involves approximately 40.6 kilometers of transmission line and 138 tower foundations.

items.statement: Commissioned India's first 400 kV GIS substation with process bus system for Power Grid at Malerkotla ahead of schedule
items.quote: We have commissioned this substation with their process bus system. So Vikran become the first, the company to execute this project in India for the Power Grid as the process bus system.

items.statement: Power Grid Corporation of India is key client; received two major substation orders
items.quote: During the period, we received two significant orders from Power Grid Corporation of India Limited.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission fund flow improving; authorities chasing for more water projects
items.quote: Now they will start to chase us to do more in water.

items.statement: Planning international base in UAE to co-invest with large investors for renewable projects
items.quote: We are planning to set up international base also in UAE. The whole point of doing this is so that we can build long-term relation with large investors who will co-invest alongside Vikran to develop large projects where at the end of the day Vikran wants to hold a minority stake in the project and ensure EPC comes to us.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing crude oil price spikes affecting non-price-variation items
items.quote: Recently what we have also observed is because of this West Asia crisis, we have observed that a few items which are generally not covered by price variation have seen significant increase because of the increase in crude oil prices.

items.statement: NOPL project land acquisition: 10-15% land not yet identified
items.quote: The only challenge that we see is the last 15% of the land, the 10% of the land that we have, which is not yet identified.

items.statement: Solar EPC (NOPL) and T&D (substation, transmission) are main verticals; data center opportunities being selective
items.quote: Only if there is an opportunity that comes to our door which is super high profit which is very urgently required those are the opportunities that we are pushing for targeting right now.

items.statement: Reiterated full-year FY27 guidance of 20% top-line growth and 20% PAT growth over previous year
items.quote: Based on the opportunity pipeline and the seasonality of our business, we are reiterating our full year guidance of 20% growth in top line and 20% growth in PAT over the previous year.

items.statement: Tracked funnel increased to INR 6,900 crores from INR 6,150 crores a quarter ago
items.quote: Our tracked funnel has increased to approximately INR 6,900 crores from INR 6,150 crores a quarter ago.

items.statement: Large enterprise deal closures skewed to H2; Q3 billings already exceed full Q3 FY26 billings
items.quote: If I look at the billing, which has happened so far in October and the billings or the bookings, which we have for the next two months, which can be converted into billings in this quarter, broadly, this number has already exceeded the number which we have done for the entire quarter of Q3 last year.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin 9.6% includes one-time high-margin deal; normalized Q2 margin 8.9%, H1 margin 8.6% vs 7.6% last year
items.quote: The Q2 gross margin includes one-time benefit because of a specific large high-margin deal. Excluding this impact, the normalized margins for us would be around 8.9% for Q2 '27 and 8.6% for H1 '27.

items.statement: Medium-term gross margin target 9-9.5%; expect 70% of incremental gross margin to flow to EBITDA, driving 20-25 bps EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: When the gross margins continue to be 9% to 9.5%, there is always an operating leverage available in our business. I think in the previous call or the one before that, I have mentioned that we see at least 70% of the incremental gross margin moving into EBITDA directly.

items.statement: Annuity sales 53.5% of H1 gross sales, grew 16.1% YoY; Q2 annuity 59% of gross sales, up 17.8% YoY
items.quote: For H1 '27, the annuity sales stood at INR 734.2 crores, up 16.1% year-on-year, contributing to 53.5% of our gross sales.

items.statement: Cybersecurity 48% of H1 revenue, Data Center Infrastructure 19%, ILM 14%, ALM/Cloud/Others 19%
items.quote: Cybersecurity remains the largest or the biggest segment for us, contributing approximately 48% of our total revenues. Data center infrastructure contributed 19%, ILM contributed 14% and ALM, cloud and others contributed 19% in H1.

items.statement: One Indian partner defaulted; INR 4.4 crore receivable written off as settlement
items.quote: Operating expenses also include a onetime write-off of around INR 4.4 crores receivable from a single partner of ours. A partner has defaulted on our payments, hence, we have taken a prudent call to make appropriate provisions in our books.

items.statement: Net working capital 48 days as of Sep 2026 vs 46 days a year ago
items.quote: Net working capital stood at 48 days as on 30th September 2026. The same during September 2025 was 46 days.

items.statement: Sold vacant land for INR 3.7 crore gain recorded in non-operating income
items.quote: The company has sold one of its vacant land, which it possesses. This resulted in a gain of around INR 3.7 crores. This has been included as a part of our non-operating income.

items.statement: Headcount investments for growth and ASEAN expansion; 15% YoY manpower cost increase in H1 (8-10% appraisal hikes)
items.quote: We have got in the right talent, and we have filled in multiple roles, which we wanted to do for growth, which are required for growth. That is one. Second, we also have said in the last call saying that we have made investments in terms of people in our international business, especially in the ASEAN region.

items.statement: INR 1 crore forex MTM hit on P&L in Q2; all payables hedged
items.quote: Based on that, you can see that there is an impact of approximately INR 1 crores hit on the P&L this period, which is predominantly because of the M2M.

items.statement: OEM consolidation occurring; have backup OEMs signed in same space with funnel running
items.quote: But fortunately, we have not taken a hit yet. But in the due course of time, definitely, that could be a potential. But then however, we have taken a cover and we have other OEMs signed in the similar space, and we already have a funnel running for that.

items.statement: H1-H2 seasonality historically 40-60; H1 INR 1,372 crores implies ~INR 3,430 crores full year at same split
items.quote: Our H1 to H2 ratio is around 40% to 60%, 40% in H1 and 60% in H2. So, in this H1, we have done around INR 1,372 crores. If I go by the same 40%, 60% ratio, I will be doing INR 3,430 crores full year.

items.statement: Working on 5-6 large deals (>INR 100 cr each); none lost from Q1 pipeline; several at L1 stage
items.quote: If we see our current pipeline, we are working more than 6 to 7 deals, which are large in nature. Some of them, as Sunil mentioned, are at a stage which are closer to conversion, which means that the partner with whom we worked on has been called out as the L1 partner.

items.statement: Customer budget constraints driving renewals over tech refresh; heavy post-award negotiations delaying deals
items.quote: Customers while they are awarding or they are declaring who is the partner who has won the deal, but they are taking and pushing it by at least 2, 3 months, and they are negotiating very heavily after even the deal is structured.

items.statement: Will use FY27 to find acquisition target; if none, capital allocation call (dividend/buyback/bonus) in Q1 FY28
items.quote: We will use this financial year to find a suitable target for acquisition. In case we don't do that, probably in Q1 of next year, we will do a capital allocation call.

items.statement: AI amplifying cyber threats; breaches accelerating from years to days; customers doing POCs for AI guardrails
items.quote: AI definitely will give us an uptick in our business. And as you very rightly mentioned that has it amplified? Yes, it has amplified in fact, AI brought the threat closer to customer. What could potentially happen in a year's time or in 2 years' time and all it started happening immediately.

items.statement: ROCE 24.7% for Q2 FY27 and 22.9% for H1 FY27
items.quote: Our ROCE is at 24.7% for Q2 '27 and 22.9% for H1 '27.

items.statement: Cash adjusted for debt INR 124 crores as of Sep 2026
items.quote: The cash adjusted for debt stood at INR 124 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY27 total income grew 23% YoY to about INR 145 crores; EBITDA about INR 20 crores at 14% margin; PAT about INR 12.6 crores
items.value: INR 145 crores revenue; INR 20 crores EBITDA; 14% EBITDA margin; INR 12.6 crores PAT
items.quote: Coming to our financial performance for H1 FY27, our total income grew by 23% year-on-year to about INR 145 crores. EBITDA stood at about INR20 crores with an EBITDA margin of 14% and profit after tax at about INR12.6 crores.

items.statement: Vizianagaram facility targeting commercial production in Q4 FY27; adds 35,000 MT capacity taking India total to 53,000 MT
items.quote: Work progressed as planned during the half year, and we are working towards commercial production in Q4 FY27. The facility will add 35,000 metric tons, taking our capacity in India to 53,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Post Pacific Global acquisition combined capacity will be 113,000 MT across India and West Africa including Vizianagaram
items.quote: Once completed, our processing capacity will increase from 18,000 metric tons to a combined of 113,000 metric tons, across India and West Africa, including Vizianagaram, giving us capacity close to our customers in India and at origin for international markets.

items.statement: Target 60-70% utilization at Vizianagaram greenfield in FY28 while maintaining near 90% at current plant; combined 85-90% utilization targeted for FY29
items.quote: Our new greenfield project will get into its full commercial production mode. So we anticipate, as communicated earlier, 60% to 70% of utilization from the greenfield while continuing near 90% utilization at the current plant. Also, with the new proposed acquisition of the plant based in Cote d'Ivoire, we look at stabilizing operations across the plants and making sure that we are ready for FY29,

items.statement: Pacific Global acquisition expected to be EPS accretive; earnings from acquired interest sufficiently higher relative to new shares issued
items.quote: Because we have -- it is very clear that it is a very strongly EPS accretive transaction. We kept that very much in mind for before arriving at any conclusion. So if you will see, our investment case is very clear here, that the earnings expected from this acquired company's interest will be sufficiently significant, sufficiently higher, I would say, relative to the new shares issued, such that th

items.statement: IPO proceeds being deployed towards Vizianagaram project as planned
items.quote: Our IPO proceeds are being deployed towards the project as planned.

items.statement: Current India plant operated at around 95% utilization in H1 FY27 vs 86% in FY26; demand ahead of current capacity
items.quote: Our plant operated at around 95% utilization during the half year compared with 86% in FY26. With demand now ahead of our current capacity, adding capacity has become our priority both in India and at origin.

items.statement: Pacific Global operates 60,000 MT cashew processing facility in Cote d'Ivoire; recently started production
items.quote: our board has approved the acquisition of 100% stake in Pacific Global FZCO, which operates a 60,000 metric ton cashew processing facility in Cote d'Ivoire, the world's largest producer of raw cashew nuts, and serves customers across the US, Europe, Middle East, and

items.statement: Vizianagaram greenfield delayed by ~45 days due to three cyclones in Andhra Pradesh; trials now expected by February 2025
items.quote: So as communicated in our May call regarding November-December timeline, that is a little -- it is unfortunate that it will be delayed by a couple – we look at a delay of couple of months. there are two-three factors that are contributing to this. For the first, the major one is that in the last 45 days, Andhra has seen three cyclones.

items.statement: Pacific Global valuation close to NAV by independent valuer; share price per SEBI regulations; pure share swap with no cash consideration
items.quote: So it is a clear share swap deal without any cash consideration to the promoters of Pacific Global or the current Pajson Agro promoters. So the valuation has been done by the independent valuator, getting a valuation close, almost close to the NAV of Pacific Global. And the share price has been determined as per the SEBI regulations.

items.statement: Pajson Global DMCC carved out cashew business to Pacific Global; raw cashew nut trading operations remain in DMCC
items.quote: No. So Pajson Global DMCC has other operations also. It had the raw cashew nut operations also, and it is a trading entity, which runs other operations also. So from that entity, we have just carved out cashews and given it to Pacific Global. For the entire interest of one business remains in one company.

items.statement: Demand for kernels remained healthy; institutional customers contributed 37.5% of revenue in H1 FY27 vs 34% in FY26; 178 distributors across 20+ states
items.quote: Our institutional business continues to grow. Institutional customers contributed 37.5% of the revenue during the half year compared with 34% in FY26, with large and recurring orders from leading food and snack confectionery companies, while our 178 distributors across more than 20 states continue to give us good reach across the country.

items.statement: Direct farm-gate procurement eliminates middlemen; manages procurement timing, quality, pricing; cashew quality difficult to maintain at harvest vs other nuts
items.quote: There is definitely a big difference in these procurement models when you are buying from the merchant traders or the exporters compared to when you have your own network of the farmers, the local buying agents, and the cooperatives based out of the origin countries itself. So, when you have the direct relationships over there, so that is how you are able to manage your procurement timings, procur

items.statement: Interest rates in Cote d'Ivoire at par with India; Nigeria rates 20-24% not feasible for working capital
items.quote: is almost at par with India. Kumar Vivek: And in Nigeria and other countries, like which are the big cashew countries? Pulkit Jain: No, Nigeria is not a big cashew country. Nigeria is not doing much of processing. So we are sourcing some from Nigeria, but if you go and take working capital lines in Nigeria, they are above 20% to 24% per annum. So it is not very feasible to take working capital lin

items.statement: Pacific Global acquisition from promoter-held entity; valuation by independent valuer at NAV; share price per SEBI regulations; no premium charged; corporate governance standards higher than legal compliance
items.quote: Let's see, our guiding principle is very straightforward. Our corporate governance and corporate ethics are supreme. We do not believe that management has the right to create value for itself by short-changing minority shareholders. Like for instance, for all these transactions, like for related party transactions, all our standards must be higher than merely complying with the letter of the law.

items.statement: Cote d'Ivoire government provides tax holidays and subsidized tax rates for processing facilities for next decade (5+5 years)
items.quote: It definitely helps. So there are definitely subsidies have been given by government in Africa, in this Cote d'Ivoire, for setting up these processing facilities also. So like that, we enjoy a few years of tax holidays over there and a few subsidized tax rates for certain categories. So that is a very good support which government is giving over there, which is going to for next 5 years is one sub

items.statement: Sourcing relationships (13 years) are biggest moat; better quality and yield vs competitors; peers have trading businesses making margin comparisons difficult
items.quote: So our sourcing being our biggest moat, Pulkit has been in the business of raw cashew nut trade for 13 years, and that gives us an edge over our competitors, which helps us source a better product, not only in terms of price but quality is very, very important when it comes to procurement of raw cashew nuts. A same specification raw nut might give two different yields to two different processors.

items.statement: Expect Q3 FY27 to be another great quarter with elevated margin levels, backed by U.S. advertising peak from midterm elections and recurring cloud savings
items.quote: Looking ahead from here, when we think about Q3, we expect it to be another great quarter with elevated margin levels.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 underlying EBITDA margin expected to stay close to 16.5% after excluding one-time tailwinds, as company reinvests operating leverage into people, product and AI
items.quote: For the full year, we expect margin to stay close to that range. That's deliberate, as we'll reinvest some portion of our operating leverage back into people, product, and AI.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 Adjusted EBITDA margin 18.7%, up 7.6pp YoY; underlying margin ~16.5% after removing >200bps one-time tailwinds (FX, delayed hiring, reserve releases)
items.quote: Current quarter margins were inflated by more than 200 basis points due to specific timing factors: favourable FX rates, some delayed hiring, and certain reserve releases. Excluding these timing benefits, our underlying margin was closer to 16.5%.

items.statement: Incremental EBITDA flow-through ~47% on Q2 revenue growth; structural leverage not significantly influenced by currency
items.quote: For every INR100 of incremental sales, INR 47 reaches Adjusted EBITDA. That 47% flow-through on incremental growth is a key number you may want to watch as we continue to give future updates.

items.statement: Gross margin 68.1% in Q2 FY27, down 1.6pp YoY but up 0.8pp QoQ; ex-base effect flat YoY and within guided 67-69% range
items.quote: We ended the quarter at INR324 crores, or 68.1% of revenue. This is down 1.6 points year-over-year, but up 0.8 points sequentially. The year-over-year deceleration is entirely the base effect.

items.statement: Net revenue retention (trailing 12 months) 125%, consistently above 120%; customers >$1M ARR rose to 15 from 11 a year ago
items.quote: Our NRR has consistently hovered over 120%, which is considered best-in-class.

items.statement: Added 22 customers in H1 FY27, total 503; channel deliveries 10,787, up 29% YoY; distributors 477, up 24% YoY
items.quote: We've added 22 more customers in the half year right now. So, we're at about 503 customers. Our deliveries expanded to 10,787, and the net retention across the last trailing 12 months continues to be 125%.

items.statement: Ad impressions grew 65% YoY to 16 billion in Q2 FY27; content processed crossed 1 million hours, up 43% YoY
items.quote: More importantly, our ad impressions grew 65% to 16 billion this quarter.

items.statement: Revenue mix stable: Cloud Modernization ~20%, Streaming Unification ~55%, Monetization & Marketplace ~25%; Cloud Modernization grew 36% ex-base, Streaming Unification 35%, Monetization 28%
items.quote: Cloud Modernization is roughly 20% of our revenue, Streaming Unification is 55%, and Monetization & Marketplace is 25%. Across the three years, the mix is broadly stable, showing that our growth has been broad-based across segments.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR 9 crores; free cash flow INR 85 crores; business remains capital-light
items.quote: Overall, free cash flow also was INR85 crores, just INR9 crores of capex, so we remain capital-light.

items.statement: H1 FY27 adjusted operating cash flow INR 94 crores (67% of Adjusted EBITDA), vs outflow INR 98 crores a year ago; DSO materially lower, working capital absorption fell to INR 14 crores from INR 145 crores
items.quote: As a result, our operating cash flow swung from an outflow of INR98 crores to an inflow of INR94 crores.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 1,774 crores with no debt; provides room to invest and pursue M&A disciplined on fit and price
items.quote: Overall, to wrap up on cash, a strong first half and a balance sheet of INR 1,774 crores of cash with no debt.

items.statement: Active corp dev function exploring M&A in video supply chain, distribution, live sports production; in exploratory to preliminary diligence stages; nothing material to disclose this quarter
items.quote: We have an active Corp dev function that is shopping. We are in different gates, from exploratory to preliminary diligence on a few of them, and we will make appropriate disclosures when we reach a point where we think we are getting into some sort of a binding commitment.

items.statement: Hiring focused on GTM overlay roles (specialized sales, customer success), AI/engineering talent refresh; leadership restructuring for AI-first organization underway
items.quote: We are obviously trying to go through the motions and make sure that in areas like service as a software and all that stuff, we are starting to see some outside-in talent.

items.statement: Launched four AI products in Q2 (STUDIO, FANPULSE, Integrated Localization, Agentic NOC); NEWSPULSE live in production with major U.S. network; products tracked across beta, launch, paying, scaling gates
items.quote: This quarter we delivered four products. This is one of the highest product velocities we've seen as a company so far.

items.statement: Base case aspiration: durable growth with ex-base constant currency growth north of 20%; R&D steady-state ~20% of revenue; no artificial cap on margins but will balance growth and AI investments
items.quote: Our aspiration on the base case is to continue delivering the way we've been delivering for the last couple of years. So, the base layer remains unchanged.

items.statement: New AI products moving toward output/outcome-driven pricing: fixed minimum guarantee plus volume variability; not yet outcome-related but directionally consumption-driven
items.quote: So, you're going to see a fixed minimum guarantee pricing along with external variability on top of it. That's the way I think we're going.

items.statement: AI not a headwind; gross margin improved sequentially for two quarters, no deflationary impact seen; top-of-funnel shows no AI-related downsell
items.quote: If we had seen a deflationary impact on AI, it would have manifested in our gross margin by now. But sequentially, we have been improving gross margin for two quarters in a row.

items.statement: Top 10 customer concentration ~41% (39-40% range); growth rates of top 10 and long tail in line with portfolio; top 10 customers have $50M+ annual spend potential
items.quote: Top 10 is 41% of our Q2 revenues, and it's been hovering around that range, 39%-40%.

items.statement: Operating 10,700+ channels; building Agentic NOC platform with design partner (top 10 customer) to automate operations using AI agents; dogfooding internally
items.quote: Given we have 10,700-plus channels that are available, we have the operating know-how in-house, and that's what we're leveraging today.

items.statement: Proposing Dr. Bhaskar Ghosh (ex-Accenture Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer) as Independent Director and Co-founder/CTO Srividhya Srinivasan as Director; subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: We propose Dr. Bhaskar Ghosh as an Independent Director and Srividhya Srinivasan, our Co-founder and CTO, as a Director.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected in line with blended growth over last 3 years; H1 tracking ahead due to consolidated entities
items.quote: we continue to expect revenue growth this year to be in line with the blended growth over the last 3 years and the first half is tracking ahead of this range held by entities we consolidated

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 21.2% vs 25.2% YoY; gross margin 45.7% in line with FY26 full-year 46%
items.quote: Margin EBITDA for the half was INR54.9 crores, up by 11.9% from INR49.1 crores, at a margin of 21.2% of total income against 25.2% last year. Our gross margin of the first half was 45.7%, broadly in line with our full year level of 46% in FY26

items.statement: Full-year gross margin expected to be in line with last year; profitability to improve progressively in H2 as new product supplies ramp
items.quote: if we see from the complete financial year last year, are near to that number, maybe about a percentage more than like complete last year's number. So overall, if you see in the complete financial year, it will be in line with the last year's number

items.statement: Traditional business order book 3-4 months; OEM visibility 1-2 years
items.quote: for traditional business the order book is approximately 3 to 4 month and for the OEMs, we have visibility approximately 1 years or 2 years

items.statement: 5 expansion projects commissioning between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28 with aggregate peak revenue potential ~INR500 cr
items.quote: we are adding 5 projects which are commissioning between FY27 Q4 and Q3 of FY28, with an aggregated peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores at full utilization

items.statement: H1 revenue grew 33.7% to INR255 cr; exports more than doubled to 37% of product revenue; organic export growth ~45%
items.quote: In the first half of FY27, our consolidated revenue grew 33.7% to INR255 crores. Exports more than doubled to about 37% of our product revenue

items.statement: OEM business expected to reach ~15% of revenue next year; fuel cell sensor orders for ~1 year; life science furnace supplies started Oct, ramp by March; JV Victura confirmed exhaust heater contract; AdBlue heater prototype with European aut
items.quote: we expect this OEM business, either from fuel cell or with this emission control kind of jobs that we are doing, to be about 15% of our revenue in the next year to come. And specifically talking about fuel cell, so we are ramping up to meet the customer expectations, so we have got orders for almost a year from the customer

items.statement: IPO fresh issue INR95 cr; INR55 cr used to repay debt; borrowings down to INR40.7 cr from INR77.9 cr (Mar'26); debt-to-equity 0.06x from 0.15x
items.quote: We have used the full INR55 crores against the debt repayment, total borrowings as on 30th September was INR40.7 crores against Tempsens Instruments ( INR77.9 crores as on 31st March 2026 and our debt-to-equity ratio is now 0.06 times from 0.15 times

items.statement: Employee cost up 41% to INR42.1 cr (new capacity teams, corporate structure, consolidated entities, INR1.1 cr ESOP); ~80 R&D staff across thermal, mechanical, electronics
items.quote: Employee cost grew 41% to INR42.1 crores for main three reasons. We are building teams for new capacity. We invested in strengthening our corporate structure for future growth, and we added the newly consolidated entities. Employee cost also includes an ESOP charges of INR1.1 crores against almost nothing last year

items.statement: Capacity utilization ~80%; 95% make-to-order, 5% standard products currently; targeting 80% traditional / 20% OEM mix in 3 years
items.quote: our capacity utilization would be close to about 80% and like what we do is completely make-to-order. So exactly, we cannot give an exact capacity utilization. So in general, we can say that it is about 80% capacity utilization. And can you repeat like today most of what we do is make-to-order and the standard products are now getting in because of this OEM business

items.statement: Gross margin dip in H1 due to lower-margin acquired entities and absence of high-margin defense order from base; raw material fluctuations built into customer prices
items.quote: in this particular quarter, we see new joint -- these new acquired entities also merge so that's why for this entities have a lower cross margin comparative to the Tempsens India which we have standalone. So that's why a little higher is there and also in the last year in last FY26 half year we have executed one of the defense order, the big defense order on in which the gross margin is very high

items.statement: No specific revenue guidance provided for next 2-3 years; management expects similar trends to continue as new hospitals mature
items.quote: Yeah, there is no guidance as such which we are sharing. However, you have seen the trend of our revenue, and revenue growth is healthy.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex was INR 90 crores invested across units including new Gurgaon 2 facility
items.quote: Half1 capex has been at INR 90 crores invested across various units, as well as payments for our new Gurgaon 2 unit.

items.statement: Plan to operationalize 200-250 beds in H2 FY27 and FY28, taking operational beds from 1,500 to ~1,800; 300 beds in Gurgaon 2 and 500 beds in Ludhiana over next 12-18 months
items.quote: There would be about 200 to 250 odd beds which are yet to be opened, which would take up our operational beds, which currently stand at 1,500, will go up closer to 1,800 within the overall capacity.

items.statement: Kanpur has 435 bed capacity with half operationalized; remaining wings to open by end of FY27
items.quote: We had opened half the beds, so there are two more wings which are yet to be opened. And out of the capacity of 435 beds, we had opened roughly half the beds, and half the beds are yet to be opened.

items.statement: Mature hospitals EBITDA margin at 28.9% in H1 FY27, up 330 bps YoY; emerging hospitals at 18.3%, up 586 bps; new hospitals at 18.7% from negative last year
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA grew by 23.1% in both Q2 and the half year, with Q2 margin being 29.6%, that is closer to 30%, a growth of 360 basis points compared to last year.

items.statement: Long-term blended EBITDA margin target in mid-20s range as hospitals mature
items.quote: The blended EBITDA which we are looking at in the long steady state should be in the mid-20s range. That's the way we are envisaging our business as a model.

items.statement: Group occupancy at 73% in H1 FY27 vs 59% YoY; mature hospitals 76.5%, emerging 68.6%, new hospitals 68.4%
items.quote: For H1 of the FY27, our occupancy stood at 73% compared to 59% the previous year, an increase of 1,400 basis points.

items.statement: Inpatient volumes up 27.3% and outpatient volumes up 20.4% YoY in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our volumes, both in terms of inpatient and outpatient volumes, have grown by 27.3% and 20.4% respectively in the H1 on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: ARPOB improved to INR 48,900 in H1 FY27 from INR 48,400 YoY; ALOS reduced to 2.8 days from 2.9 days
items.quote: Our ARPOB for H1 FY27 stood at 48,900 compared to 48,400 in the H1 of the previous year, showing improvement in our ARPOBs. Our ALOS has gone down from 2.9 previous year H1 to 2.8 days in the H1 of FY27.

items.statement: Surgical and procedural mix improving; quaternary care programs added (liver transplant, kidney transplant, bone marrow transplant, robotic surgery)
items.quote: Our surgical mixes are improving our procedural mix is improving. Plus, the second point is that we have added quaternary care programs across some of our units.

items.statement: Payor mix in H1 FY27: 32% cash/self-pay, 24% insurance, 44% government schemes and PSUs; focus on reducing government dependency
items.quote: Our payor mix in H1 FY27 stood at 32% as cash or self-pay, as we call it, 24% insurance, and remaining 44% coming from the government schemes and the PSUs.

items.statement: Receivables increased from INR 350 crores in March to INR 518 crores in September; DSOs at 92 days vs 79 days in March; working capital absorption of INR 172 crores in H1
items.quote: Receivables have increased from INR 350 crores in March to INR 518 crores. This is with the payor mix change, settlement cycles, and lumpy payments from certain payor groups.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of INR 68 crores in H1 FY27 despite INR 172 crores working capital absorption
items.quote: The OCF, operating cash flow, for Half 1 was at INR 68 crores, despite working capital movement of a negative INR 172 crores.

items.statement: Gross borrowings INR 979 crores, cash INR 360 crores, net debt INR 620 crores as of September; INR 375 crores repaid from IPO proceeds, pro forma net debt INR 143 crores
items.quote: Our gross borrowings as of September were INR 979 crores. We held INR 360 crores of cash as well, giving us a net debt of INR 620 crores as of end September.

items.statement: IPO of INR 500 crores completed; INR 375 crores used for debt repayment as per offer document
items.quote: Of the INR 500 crores of fresh issue, INR 375 crores has already gone to repay and prepay borrowings.

items.statement: Rajasthan state government scheme temporarily suspended across hospitals, impacting Udaipur; 30-40% of lost government business recovered via cash/insurance
items.quote: In Udaipur, rather the entire region of Rajasthan or the state of Rajasthan, the state government scheme is being reviewed. That is being reviewed by the state government, that is being reviewed by the central government, and it has been temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals in Rajasthan.

items.statement: CONGOR specialty mix at 74% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our CONGOR specialty stood strong at 74% in H1 of FY27.

items.statement: Revenue to ramp up from Q4 FY27, all plants fully ramped by Q2 FY28, targeting annual revenue run rate of over INR1,300 crores by end of FY28, reiterating long-term annual growth guidance of over 25%
items.quote: We expect revenue to ramp up Q4 of FY27 onwards, and all the plants will be fully ramped up by Q2 of FY 2028. Our current installed capacity positions us to reach an annual revenue run rate of over INR1,300 crores by the end of FY28, more than double of our FY 2026 revenue.

items.statement: Six customer-dedicated facilities commissioned totalling 44,800 sq m for MHI, GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Baker Hughes; two new GE Vernova gas facilities inaugurated in September; all plants production-ready with teams hired and delta quali
items.quote: In September, we inaugurated two new dedicated lean manufacturing facilities for GE Vernova. All six customer-dedicated facilities are now commissioned. 44,800 square meters for four global OEMs, namely Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, and Baker Hughes.

items.statement: Order book close to over INR6,500 crores, rolling contracts based on 5-7 year demand visibility by product and customer; not a traditional backlog but annual recurring demand
items.quote: Our current order book is close to over INR6,500 crores. Like Mr. Chopdar mentioned, this is a rolling order book. Across each of our segments, today this is our order book, and there are contracts that are under discussion.

items.statement: BHEL approved as long-term source with two-year rate contract worth INR52.68 crores for gas turbine airfoils; Baker Hughes supply agreement extended to 2030
items.quote: BHEL approved as a long-term source with a two-year rate contract worth about INR52.68 crores for their gas turbine airfoils. This deepens our domestic energy business. Baker Hughes, our supply agreement with Nuovo Pignone, has extended up to 2030.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps YoY to 37.5%; gross margin before depreciation at 45.2% (+150 bps YoY); indirect costs steady at 7.7% of revenue despite 33% larger business
items.quote: Our reported EBITDA grew 37.1% year-on-year to INR70.4 crores and 9.9% over quarter one. The EBITDA margin was 37.5%, an extension of 150 basis points, as I explained earlier, over 36% of quarter 2 FY26, in line with the 37.6% in quarter one.

items.statement: Energy & oil/gas 81% of H1 revenue (INR290 crores, +28.5% YoY); Aerospace & defence 17% (INR60.4 crores, +28.3% YoY); domestic revenue 2.5x to INR43 crores (12% of business) driven by BHEL indigenization
items.quote: Growth was balanced across segments. Energy, oil and gas grew 28.5% to INR290 crores, at 81% of revenue. Aerospace and defence grew 28.3% to INR60.4 crores, at a 17% of revenue. Domestic revenues grew more than two and a half times to INR43 crores, and is now 12% of our business, up from 6%, helped by our indigenization work with BHEL.

items.statement: One OEM agreed to 50% advance on POs, expecting $4.5 million; bill discounting lines with ICICI Bank and DP World available from Q4 FY27; exports ~85% of revenue
items.quote: We are fortunate that one of the OEM has agreed to give 50% advance on each PO, and we are expecting $4.5 million from that particular update. Based on this template, we are trying to talk with all other OEMs and try to see what best we can do on this particular front.

items.statement: Expect cash flow generation from Q4 FY27 end as throughput converts to revenue; Q1 FY28 should see consistent cash flow; bill discounting and customer advances to reduce debtor days
items.quote: I think by Q3 end and Q4, sorry, Q4 end, and Q4 is where we can see the cash flowing out of the company now. That is the period we see that coming in. Consistently, if you talk, Q1 of next year would be perfectly in thing, but we can see something in Q4 as well, the cash coming out of the company.

items.statement: Aero engine airfoil qualifications ongoing with Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney Canada, Safran; first production deliveries expected next fiscal; GTRE indigenous turbojet engine delivered, positioned for end-to-end engine assembly
items.quote: Aeroengine airfoils with Rolls-Royce and Pratt & Whitney and Safran, extending our airfoil expertise from power turbines into aircraft engines. We are now going to be starting to delivering this from the next fiscal onwards. The developments that we did on aero engines for GTRE, building on a delivery for India's first indigenous expendable turbojet engine, with end-to-end manufacturing, assembly,

items.statement: Mangampet land ready for Phase II expansion beyond current Tuniki Bollaram facilities; current installed capacity supports INR1,300+ crores ARR by FY28, with visibility beyond that
items.quote: The Mangampet is all ready for the phase II. So that is also covered, very well covered. So once we are done with this, definitely we have a plan for that land and we are going to start up there.

items.statement: Customer advance arrangement involves minimal discount (~1%); no material margin impact from working capital support negotiations
items.quote: No, we have not given any material discount. It's hardly 1% or so. That is not something we have given very large discount for these advances.

items.statement: Delta qualifications ongoing across all customer lines - mandatory revalidation when moving parts to new facilities; throughput improvement begins H2 FY27, revenue ramp from Q4 FY27, full ramp by H1 FY28
items.quote: When a part that is already qualified moves to a newer facility or a newer machine, the customer requires us to do a delta qualification. This qualification process is shorter than qualifying a newer part. A new part can take anywhere up to 30- 48 months, but a delta qualification is still not as lengthy, but is a rigorous process.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-16% YoY
items.quote: We are on track to achieving around 15% to 16% growth over last year.

items.statement: Target ROE and ROCE of approximately 25%
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain committed to achieving ROE and ROCE of approximately 25%.

items.statement: Jamshedpur 155-bed hospital to commence operations in March-April 2027
items.quote: The Jamshedpur project is progressing as planned with the upcoming 155-bed tertiary care hospital expected to commence operations in March, April 2027.

items.statement: Lease expense for Raipur ~INR4 cr/year; Jamshedpur similar
items.quote: Raipur is already operational with the lease expense of almost INR4 crores a year. Jamshedpur would also be a similar amount.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion potential of 100 beds each at Agartala and Raipur
items.quote: Both the hospitals we can add another 100 beds.

items.statement: No further brownfield bed addition scope at Kolkata hospitals
items.quote: In the Kolkata hospital, there is no further scope for brownfield bed addition.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 inpatient volumes up ~11% network-wide driving revenue growth
items.quote: We had almost 11% increase in the inpatient volumes at a network level, which obviously led to a higher throughput and increased occupancy levels.

items.statement: International patient flow from Bangladesh showing slow recovery with increased visa requests
items.quote: The international patient flow is showing a slow recovery. It is not back as per the previous estimates or previous historical numbers. It is showing a slow recovery, but there is increased momentum.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps to 21.5%; H1 margin up 221 bps to 21%
items.quote: EBITDA grew at a faster pace, increasing by 23.9% year-on-year to INR29.8 crores. The EBITDA margin expanded by 150 basis points to 21.5% compared with 20% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Oncology revenue contribution ~4% currently, expected to stabilize at 10-15% in next 4 quarters
items.quote: We are seeing revenue contribution of around 4% at this point in the hospital, which is growing every quarter. We expect it to stabilize around 10% to 15% in the next 4 quarters.

items.statement: Nephrology contribution at Dum Dum reduced from ~30% to <15%
items.quote: The contribution of the department is now less than around 15% compared to it being almost 30% earlier.

items.statement: Raipur has even specialty mix across gastro, cardiac, renal sciences with high-end procedures
items.quote: All specialties from gastro sciences to cardiac sciences, renal sciences have been contributing evenly across the spectrum. And a lot of it is coming from high-end procedures.

items.statement: Raipur empanelled with ~70% of insurance providers; rest in progress
items.quote: We've been able to have the empanelment of almost 70% of the players. There are still some insurance providers who are not on board.

items.statement: Raipur taking Ayushman Bharat and corporate patients (SAIL, Coal India) mindful of cash flow
items.quote: We have been taking Ayushman Bharat patients there. But obviously, we have to do it keeping in mind the overall cash flow position. So we have been taking some Ayushman Bharat patients along with that, we've also started corporate patients from SAIL, from Coal India, etcetera.

items.statement: Corporate patient payment cycle generally within 90 days
items.quote: The payment cycle generally is within 90 days.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 ARPOB INR40,721 (+7.1% YoY); network occupancy 50.3% vs 47.4% YoY; mature hospitals 59.8%
items.quote: ARPOB for the quarter stood at INR40,721, reflecting year-on-year growth of 7.1% network occupancy improved to 50.3% compared with 47.4% in the corresponding quarter last year. Excluding Raipur, occupancy across our mature hospitals stood at 59.8%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 ARPOB INR41,490; network occupancy 47.9% vs 44.7% YoY; mature hospitals 56.7%
items.quote: Our H1 ARPOB stood at INR41,490 while network occupancy was 47.9% compared with 44.7% in H1 FY26. Occupancy across mature hospitals stood at 56.7%, excluding Raipur.

items.statement: Salt Lake H1 occupancy 65.4%, ARPOB INR43,284; crossed 850 robotic surgeries
items.quote: ILS Salt Lake continued to deliver a strong performance, recording an occupancy of 65.4% in H1 and the highest ARPOB across our network at INR43,284. The hospital also registered year-on-year growth of 12% and crossed the milestone of 850 robotic surgeries.

items.statement: Dum Dum H1 revenue INR84.8 cr, occupancy 69.4%, ARPOB INR43,086; started cardiothoracic unit
items.quote: During H1 FY27, it recorded revenue of INR84.8 crores with occupancy of 69.4% and an ARPOB of INR43,086. Further strengthening its clinical capabilities, the hospital has commenced a cardiothoracic and vascular surgery unit.

items.statement: Howrah H1 revenue +25% YoY, occupancy 45.8%; launched MAKO robotic knee, nearing 100 procedures
items.quote: ILS Howrah, the hospital is witnessing encouraging growth with revenue increasing by 25% year-on-year basis in H1 FY27, supported by higher patient volumes and improved occupancy of 45.8%. The hospital has also strengthened its orthopedic capabilities with the launch of the MAKO robotic knee surgery system and is nearing the milestone of 100 robotic procedures.

items.statement: Raipur Q2 revenue INR9 cr, occupancy ~16.5%; achieved NABH, first TAVI, liver transplant, 11 renal transplants
items.quote: It achieved NABH accreditation within its first year of operations, performing its first TAVI procedure and liver transplant in Q2 FY27. It has also completed 11 renal transplants in just under a year.

items.statement: Network ALOS optimized: Salt Lake 2.9-3 days, Dum Dum reduced from 5.5 to 4.3 days
items.quote: Salt Lake, the ALOS is around 2.9 to 3. Even Dum Dum, the ALOS has gone down from almost 5.5 to just 4.3.

items.statement: Raipur exit occupancy target 25-30% by Q4 FY27
items.quote: We expect the average occupancy to be around the 25% to 30% mark by the end of Q4.

items.statement: Artemis entry in Raipur caused clinical talent attrition; gaps now filled
items.quote: Yes, Artemis has entered into Raipur, and that led to some amount of attrition, but we've been able to make good that attrition again.

items.statement: Supreme Court trade margin cap on essential medicines; impact to be assessed post November order; will adjust service pricing to maintain margins
items.quote: That is something which will be -- we'll have more clarity once the order comes out and once the effect comes out in November 2nd week. But that is -- health care has to be seen on an overall basis. These were just components in the overall service pricing. Obviously, service pricing basis that has to be corrected so that the margins are maintained.

items.statement: Room rent cap discussions at statutory level; healthcare cannot be compared to hotel star ratings; pricing at 10-15% discount to peers like Apollo, Fortis, Manipal, AMRI
items.quote: Those are topics which are still under discussion at the statutory level. There are various healthcare, representations also towards that because healthcare cannot be looked or compared from a hotel star category perspective. Hospitals need to have that independent ranking system. That being said, our service delivery is in line with peers like Apollo, Fortis, Manipal HOSMAT (27:52) AMRI. So our s

items.statement: Ranchi MOU failed due to owner legal troubles; pivoted to Jamshedpur commissioning
items.quote: The Ranchi MOU, which was signed could not be executed because the owner -- it was an asset-light hospital where the owner landed into some -- went into some legal troubles. So we could not complete that project. However, we deviated and we are on the verge of commissioning our Jamshedpur hospital.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth target 10%-15%
items.quote: First half revenue growth of 15% sits within the target range of 10% to 15%, which we indicated, and we expect the full year to remain within that range.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to reach double digits (10%+)
items.quote: My realistic guidance will be, we will touch a double digit. So it will be 10% or 10% plus.

items.statement: FY27 capex around INR100+ crore, similar for FY28
items.quote: I think we were talking about roughly INR100-plus crores of capex for FY27. We will have a similar amount for sure in FY 2028.

items.statement: Target revenue INR2,500 crore in FY27, double-digit growth next year
items.quote: And this year, we are intending to close, close to INR2,500 crores. So this is as far as our revenue is concerned, which we are very confident to speak, and that is why I spoke that first.

items.statement: Long-term target EUR350-400 million (INR3,500 crore) turnover by 2030
items.value: EUR350 million to EUR 400 million or INR3,500 crores
items.quote: But as we said originally from day 1 that we are targeting towards the EUR350 million to EUR 400 million or INR3,500 crores turnover for Carraro by 2030.

items.statement: Domestic tractor retail demand healthy; wholesale moderated due to high base, uneven monsoon, festive timing
items.quote: Tractor retail demand has remained healthy, reflecting encouraging underlying demand. Wholesale volumes have moderated in recent months, influenced by a high base, an uneven monsoon and the timing of the festive season.

items.statement: 4-wheel drive tractor penetration structural, targeting 35%-40% over coming years
items.quote: We remain confident that penetration will keep rising towards the 35% to 40% range over the coming years, and we are adding axle capacity to serve it.

items.statement: Export demand uneven; Europe agriculture subdued, Turkey volatile, US customers measured
items.quote: Across our export markets, conditions remain mixed. European agriculture continues to be subdued. Turkey remains volatile. And in the U.S., greater clarity on trade arrangements is a positive development even as customers remain measured in their volume commitments.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 9.2% vs 10% YoY; gross margin 23.3% vs 26.4% YoY
items.quote: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margins stood at 9.2% compared with 10% a year ago, while gross margin for the first half was also lower than the last year.

items.statement: Margin pressure from steel, casting, energy, freight, supplier labor; commodity recovery lag 3-6 months
items.quote: This was largely driven by the combined increase in steel and casting prices, energy, logistics and supplier labor costs.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve progressively as recoveries catch up, localization moves to target, new capacity lifts utilization
items.quote: We expect margins to improve progressively as recoveries catch up, localization moves towards target and new capacity lifts utilization.

items.statement: TBH axle ramp-up for major international OEM progressing as planned; target INR300 crore in 3 years
items.quote: We had estimated in the beginning INR300 crores in 3 years. We are in the second year now. And it is well as per their plan.

items.statement: TBH export revenue ~INR180 crore in FY27 (55-60% of 3-year target)
items.quote: When we talk about 3, 3.5 years about this one, so we have already reached almost 55%, 60% of this in this year itself.

items.statement: 4-5 TBH programs at prototype or field validation stage; 2 in series production
items.quote: We now have a couple of Tele-boom Handler programs in series production and 4 to 5 more at the prototype or field validation stage.

items.statement: Backhoe Loader driveline exports through Indian OEMs performing well; Turkey ramp-up yet to gain momentum
items.quote: Backhoe Loader driveline exports through Indian OEMs continue to perform well. Higher-horsepower transmission, R&D and engineering services. Series production of our customer in Turkey commenced in Q1 FY27. However, the ramp-up is yet to gain momentum, temporarily impacting offtake.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR204 million; paint shop building commenced, side-drive sub-assembly line and backlash machine commissioned
items.quote: During H1 FY27, the company incurred capital expenditure of INR204 million. Construction of the new paint shop building commenced, while a side-drive sub-assembly line and a backlash machine were commissioned to enhance portal axle capacity and increase differential support capacity on the 4-wheel drive line.

items.statement: OEMs blocking capacity for future 4-wheel drive models; company expanding proactively
items.quote: And the good part is that the OEMs whom we are working, they are already projecting us the future numbers. And they are also blocking the capacity with us. So that is not a constraint. Rather, they are giving us the future visibility for which we are already doing the expansion.

items.statement: Customer contracts index steel and casting with 3-6 month lag; energy, freight, supplier labor only partly covered, require separate negotiations
items.quote: First, commodities, namely steel and casting. These are indexed in our customer contracts, but recovered with a lag of 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Cost recovery negotiations constructive; 30-40% remaining; initial results visible from Q3
items.quote: I think from Q3, we will already start seeing the initial result of this negotiation.

items.statement: Domestic revenue 70% of total in H1 FY27, up 30% YoY; agricultural revenue grew 23% YoY
items.quote: Domestic revenue grew 30% in the first half and now accounts for about 70% of our revenue. Agricultural revenue grew 23%, well ahead of domestic tractor industry wholesales, which grew by high single digits over the same period.

items.statement: 4-wheel drive axle volumes growing faster than overall tractor market; company focused only on 4-wheel drive
items.quote: Our domestic 4-wheel drive axle volumes continue to grow faster than the overall tractor market.

items.statement: Non-captive 4-wheel drive market share ~55-59%; captive ~30% (estimated)
items.quote: So when we say that we have almost 60% in the non-captive -- 58%, 55%, 59% as a market share of Carraro. So we believe that 30% would be with the captive.

items.statement: No customer or project lost in exports; supply chain and demand issues temporary
items.quote: No project or no customer has been lost. It is all safe over there. But our team took that additional effort and went to customers and made sure that we are more than covering the loss or, I would say, the setback that we have received in export.

items.statement: Net working capital ~40 days in H1 FY27; close control of inventory, collections, supplier terms
items.quote: Net working capital was about 40 days as we kept close control of inventory, collections and supplier terms while supporting higher volumes.

items.statement: Debt to equity 0.34x; cash and equivalents ~INR955 million
items.quote: Debt to equity was 0.34x and cash and cash equivalents were about INR955 million.

items.statement: Annualized ROCE 26.3%, ROE 24.5% in H1 FY27
items.quote: On an annualized basis, return on capital employed was 26.3% and return on equity was 24.5%.

items.statement: Raw material localization recovered to ~80% in Q2 FY27 from 74% in Q1; target 86-88%
items.quote: Raw material localization recovered to about 80% in Q2 FY27 from 74% in Q1 FY27 as supply from local partners normalized. Our target remains 86% to 88%.

items.statement: Export revenue Q2 INR2,106 million, down 4% YoY but up 27% QoQ; H1 export INR3,758 million vs INR4,113 million YoY
items.quote: Export revenue was INR3,758 million against INR4,113 million last year.

items.statement: 4-wheel drive tractor penetration ~23-25% currently, moving to 27-28% in coming months
items.quote: And I would say unofficial sources that the industry is roughly at around 23%, 24%. It is in that range, but seems like it will move to, say, 27%, 28% in the coming months.

items.statement: West Asia conflict driving elevated energy, fuel, freight, insurance, steel and casting costs
items.quote: The ongoing conflict in West Asia, now in its eighth month, has kept energy and fuel prices elevated, while also increasing freight, insurance and input costs, particularly for steel and castings across our supply chain.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance uncertain due to war duration; confident of double-digit margin eventually
items.quote: I don't know when the war will end. It all depends on that. We are confident that we should achieve a double digit at least for this year closure.

items.statement: Infrastructure investments continue at steady pace but near-term headwinds from state government spending below budget and contractor payment delays are dampening equipment demand in some states
items.quote: Government spending on infrastructure projects, more particularly by some state governments, has been below budgeted allocations, resulting in this slower pace of execution.

items.statement: Volume growth in Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh offset by softness in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar
items.quote: While we have seen good volume growth in Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, it has been offset by the softness of the industry in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar.

items.statement: Raw material costs increased by close to mid-single digits in H1 FY27 due to rising steel prices and crude-linked commodities
items.quote: Meanwhile, rising steel prices and other costs of crude-linked commodities have driven a sharp increase in raw material costs, prompting several suppliers to seek price revisions.

items.statement: Price hike of around 2% taken in Q4 FY26, another 1% in September, and further calibrated pricing actions planned over coming quarters
items.quote: Following the price increase of around 2% that we took in Q4 FY26, we have taken another price hike of around 1% in September and will continue to evaluate further pricing actions in a calibrated and phased manner over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Additional 1% price increase taken in November and another 2% planned for Q4 FY27 to address commodity inflation
items.quote: Obviously, it required a certain redressal, which we've done with a 1% price increase coming in in the month of September, and another 1% that has been taken in the month of November. But please understand that in this industry, it's never easy because certain deals have already been done at certain prices.

items.statement: Gross margins improved marginally by about 20 basis points year-on-year in Q2 FY27 supported by price hike despite raw material cost increase
items.quote: Despite the increase in raw material cost, the gross margins for Q2 FY27 improved marginally by about 20 basis points on a year-on-year basis, supported by the price hike.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for H1 FY27 at 11.5% compared to 11.7% in H1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin for H1 '27 came in at 11.5% compared to 11.7% in H1 '26.

items.statement: SLCM retail market share increased to 75.5% in H1 FY27, up 480 basis points from 70.7% in H1 FY26 and 200 basis points from FY26 average of 73.5%
items.quote: Our SLCM retail market share increased to 75.5% in H1 FY27, representing an expansion of approximately 480 basis points over the 70.7% in H1 FY26 and 200 basis points over the average FY26 number of 73.5.

items.statement: Roads share of application mix declined from 70% in FY25 to 40% in FY27 YTD, while factories/buildings and urban infra rose sharply to 39% YTD
items.quote: Roads used to be, in year '25, 70% of the application mix for our business, which is Ajax's business. In FY26, it came down to 67%, and on a YTD basis in FY27, it is at about 40%.

items.statement: Non-SLCM revenue grew 64.7% year-on-year in Q2 FY27 to INR55.8 crores led by concrete pumps, batching plants and boom pumps
items.quote: Non-SLCM revenue for Q2 FY27 at INR55.8 crores has shown a robust 64.7% over Q2 FY26. Growth was led by concrete pumps, batching plants and boom pumps.

items.statement: UDAAN series volumes grew from 49 units in H1 FY26 to 216 units in H1 FY27, now selling in 20 states with 6 new states added in H1
items.quote: Last year, I think we had a base volume in H1 of only about 49 units. That in H1 has gone to about 216 units.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 47% year-on-year in H1 FY27; export share was 7.4% of revenue in Q2 FY27 with 65% from SLCM and 35% from non-SLCM
items.quote: Export revenue grew by 47% on a year-over-year basis in H1 FY27. While exports currently contributes a small proportion of our overall revenue, we see good headroom for growth.

items.statement: ARGO 4000 launched to address gap in SLCM portfolio; nearing launch of additional products including potential paver
items.quote: We are also nearing the launch of our ARGO 4000. In fact, it has already been launched. It will address an important gap in our SLCM portfolio, further broadening our product offering and strengthening our overall value proposition.

items.statement: Working capital cycle maintained at healthy 22 days in H1 FY27
items.quote: Working capital cycle continues to be maintained at a healthy 22 days.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents at INR1,151 crores as of September 26, providing financial flexibility for growth and strategic inorganic opportunities
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to be a key source of strength, with a cash balance of nearly INR1,150 crores as of September 26, providing significant financial flexibility to capitalize on future growth opportunities, including strategic inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: Expect customer sentiment and demand momentum to improve in second half; around 60-65% of annual revenue typically generated in H2; aim to end year in strong position with close to double-digit growth
items.quote: We expect customer sentiment and demand momentum to improve in the second half of the year. As we have highlighted previously, around 60%-65% of our annual revenue is typically generated in H2.

items.statement: Steel prices risen from INR58/kg to ~INR70/kg, anticipated to reach INR75-76/kg; commodity inflation expected in 2-3% range
items.quote: Steel prices have gone up quite significantly. The steel price has gone up from INR58 per kilo to close to about INR70 per kilo as we speak. INR68 was the last program. There is an anticipation that that number will go up closer to about INR75, INR76.

items.statement: Spares and services revenue declined 4.7% year-on-year in Q2 FY27 to INR35.4 crores; machine running hours down ~25%
items.quote: Spares and services revenue for Q2 FY27 stood at INR35.4 crores, falling by 4.7% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: ROCE at 19% and ROE at 14% for H1 FY27
items.quote: ROCE and ROE for H1 are at 19% and 14% respectively.

items.statement: Top 10 states contribute ~78% of total SLCM volume; 9 of top 10 states showed market share growth, 6 states have building/urban infra share above national average of 39%
items.quote: You know that the top 10 states contribute close to about 78% of the total SLCM volume. Of these, the two large ones, which is essentially Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, have to do their bit, while the others are holding up.

items.statement: 62 of 68 dealers have sold at least one concrete pump; 12-15 dealers now selling across concrete pumps, boom pumps and batching plants
items.quote: 62 out of 68 dealers have had a chance to sell at least one pump. That expansion is a very powerful way of addressing it. I can also say this, that about 12-15 dealers are ones that have started getting into this act across the spectrum.

items.statement: Market share gains achieved despite machines commanding price premium over competing products, reflecting brand strength and value proposition
items.quote: Notably, this market share gain was achieved despite our machines commanding a price premium over competing products, reflecting the strength of our brand and the enticing value proposition.

items.statement: Streamlined organizational structure by bringing all manufacturing under single leader; Obadenahalli plant head moved to procurement and supply chain
items.quote: To drive greater operational agility and better execution, we have streamlined our organizational structure by bringing all manufacturing under a single leader.

items.statement: Diversifying supplier base and engaging alternate vendors to secure competitive procurement terms amid raw material cost increases
items.quote: These include diversifying our supplier base and actively engaging with alternate vendors to secure more competitive procurement terms.

items.statement: Commodity cycle uncertainty, particularly steel and aluminum prices, forex movements, and geopolitical developments could impact margins
items.quote: It will be a challenging task, Vaibhav. I am only saying this because we do not know the trajectory of how the commodity cycle and up move happens, particularly in the area of steel, aluminum, how the forex plays out, and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Services and spares function aligned with strategy and product planning to strengthen customer excellence
items.quote: The head of the Obadenahalli plant has now moved to procurement and supply chain, while the services and spares function have been aligned with strategy and product planning to further strengthen customer excellence.

items.statement: No financing challenges on wholesale or retail front; Ajax portfolio A-rated with all major financiers including HDFC, Kotak, Chola
items.quote: As far as financing is concerned, we haven't seen any challenge either on the wholesale front or the retail front. The good news is that Ajax, over a long period of time, has been A-rated in the portfolio of all our financers.

items.statement: Export product mix better than domestic with 65% SLCM and 35% non-SLCM; established in Kenya, Nigeria, Algeria (40-42% of export volume); targeting South Africa and LATAM expansion
items.quote: I think as far as exports is concerned, I think the mix is better than domestic in the sense that 65% comes from SLCM, 35% comes from the non-SLCM portfolio.

items.statement: Mechanization level in concreting equipment continues to be low; cement per capita usage in India at 11% vs 5-6x globally; anticipate mechanization to grow from 75/25 split
items.quote: I think two, three things. First is cement per capita, the level of concrete usage in India and its penetration at 11% versus five, six times that in global markets. The third piece centered around the fact that the level of mechanization in concreting equipment continues to be lower, right?

items.statement: Management will not revise full-year revenue guidance now; will review after Q3 results
items.quote: We will review it, sir, during the Q3 results, basically. We have taken the stand basically, that we will not revise the guidance this time, sir.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 18-19% sustainable range
items.quote: It will be sustainable as per our last guidance, basically.

items.statement: Ratlam 2 GW power electronics commissioned in August; lithium-ion battery upsized to 3 GWh coming online next quarter; Hathras 1 GW tubular battery plant expected next quarter; TOPCon 1.2 GW cell line on track for Q1 FY28
items.quote: In August, we commissioned 2 GW of power electronics facility at Ratlam. Ratlam now runs both solar panels, which started in May, and power electronics. Three more additions are coming. Lithium-ion battery at Ratlam. We have upsized our facility from 2 GWh to 3 GWh and expect it to come online in coming quarter. That will take our lithium-ion capacity to 3.5 GWh. Tubular batteries at Hathras, Utta

items.statement: More than 50% of H1 revenue from on-grid and DCR-based market linked to PM Surya Ghar subsidy
items.quote: Right now, more than 50% of our revenue is coming from this on-grid and DCR-based market.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 17.1% vs 18.9% in Q1 due to seasonal softness, Ratlam overheads before volume ramp, Bawal fire forcing external tubular battery purchases, and front-loaded sales/marketing spend
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin was 17.1% in Q2 against 18.9% in Q1. Though our gross margin is similar in both the quarters. Quarter-on-Quarter decline is mainly from seasonal softness, which is normal in rooftop solar industry, as absorption of operating fixed cost continued in quarter. Additionally, overhead rose because we staffed and ran the Ratlam facility before its full volume arrived. That is the cost

items.statement: Conscious strategy of passing cost benefits to customers through competitive pricing to expand market share
items.quote: This was driven by significantly higher sales volume, supported by our pan-India network of on-role service engineers and a conscious strategy of passing on cost benefits to the customers through competitive pricing to expand market share.

items.statement: DCR cell shortage persists at 2.2 GW monthly run rate vs higher demand; ALMM List-II implementation from Jan 1 2027 may push DCR cell prices up; geopolitical factors increasing fuel prices
items.quote: DCR cell shortages are still there because the current run rate of DCR solar cell production is only 2 GW if you compare to the last month. 2.2 GW to be precise last month, whereas demand is much higher than that. So that's why if ALMM List-II comes up from January 1, then again, we believe that DCR solar cell prices might go up further.

items.statement: 70-80% of DCR panels sold in H1 used in-house cells; 20-30% from outside purchases
items.quote: Just to give you a rough estimate, you can say around 70%-80% is in-house and 20% to 30% of the DCR we sold is from outside.

items.statement: Added 100+ distributors and 1,000+ dealers in H1; Odisha and Uttarakhand now fully covered; 10,200+ channel partners across 25+ states/UTs
items.quote: In this half year, we added more than 100 distributors and more than 1,000 dealers. Odisha and Uttarakhand moved into the fully covered category.

items.statement: Module overcapacity hurts commodity sellers; Fujiyama's panels go into captive systems sold through own channel; brand, distribution, service moats hard to replicate; new entrants unlikely to sustain retail model
items.quote: Our panels go into our own captive system and are sold through our own channel. So the module price is not what drives our economics. The complete system and service behind it are. Within the solar chain, the important part is cell, and we own them. Also important is trusted brand with distributor in every district and an engineer who reaches to the roof. We have spent close to three decades in bu

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 59 from 83; receivable days 10 from 15; inventory days 99 from 123 (on COGS basis); payable days 50 from 55
items.quote: Net working capital days improved to 59 days in H1 FY27 from 83 days in FY26 on an annualized basis. Receivable days come down to 10 from 15 and inventory days to 99 from 123, while payable days were 50 against 55.

items.statement: Operating cash flow before working capital changes INR 490 cr in H1; invested INR 661 cr in working capital and INR 184 cr in capex
items.quote: In the first half, operating cash flows before working capital changes was about INR 490 crores, which shows the earnings are converting to cash. We invested about INR 661 crores in working capital to support a business that has been doubled in size and spent about INR 184 crores on investing activities.

items.statement: Board evaluating QIP for debt repayment; approval pending
items.quote: On the debt side, I think as the market is already aware that we are taking a resolution on the QIP side. So as soon as this is approved by the board, maybe we can also plan for the debt repayment from that.

items.statement: MNRE requires PM Surya Ghar inverter suppliers to keep apps, servers, data in India with M2M SIM dataloggers from Aug 2026; CEA cybersecurity regulations July 2026; Fujiyama fully compliant with domestic dongles, data loggers, monitoring on
items.quote: Since August 2026, MNRE has required inverter suppliers under PM Surya Ghar to keep their apps, servers and data strictly in India, alongside mandatory M2M SIM dataloggers. The Central Electricity Authority's new cybersecurity regulations, (July 2026) push the whole sector to the same way. We have confirmed our full compliance to MNRE. Our dongles, data loggers, and monitoring system are made in I

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar covered 60+ lakh households, 19+ GW installed, INR 36,000+ cr subsidy released as of Oct 31, 2026; 5 lakh households remain in current phase until Mar 2027
items.quote: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana has been remarkable program according to national portal.
