It has covered more than 60 lakh households, installed more than 19 GW, and released over INR 36,000 crores of subsidy as on October 31, 2026. About 5 lakh households remain to be covered in this current phase, which runs until March 2027.

items.statement: Service engineers increased to 1,000+ on-roll from 650 in March 2026; 80+ R&D engineers; board member Sunil Kumar (ex-Google) guiding UTL AI platform development
items.quote: Fujiyama now has more than 1,000 on-roll service engineers, up from about 650 in March this year. They are our own employees, not outsourced, and they support dealers in person for on-sales and installation. Every complaint they log goes back to our 80 plus R&D engineers.

items.statement: Insurance claim filed for full carrying value of Bawal fire damaged assets (INR 143 cr pre-tax loss recognized in Q1); salvage disposal done; expect resolution and cash inflow in FY27
items.quote: The insurance claim has been filed for the full carrying value of the damaged assets. Salvage disposal has already done. We expect resolution and realization of the insurance claim in this financial year, which will provide additional working capital cash inflow.

items.statement: Guidance revision deferred due to ALMM List-II implementation uncertainty, PM Surya Ghar 2.0 policy clarity, DCR cell shortage/price volatility, geopolitical fuel price risk
items.quote: Since ALMM List-II is also at the door, with this ALMM List-II, the market might further shift to DCR cells, and since shortages are still continuing on the DCR cell side. PM Surya Ghar 2.0 is also under discussion, and it is very important to see how government and by when the government will give clarity on that thing. So that is why Pawan sir wants to wait for another quarter, and we will cover

items.statement: Chinese solar technology transfer ban not a risk; TOPCon cell line machines already received, no execution challenge seen
items.quote: Machines are already received, and we don't see any challenge, basically.

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue or earnings guidance because 70-80% of capacity is on spot market and rates are driven by unpredictable geopolitics
items.quote: We don't do revenue guidance because we don't know what rates our ships will earn. 70%+ of our capacity, close to 80% of our capacity, is open to the spot market.

items.statement: Crude tanker spot rates have fallen sharply from $350k-400k/day peak to $130k-150k/day currently due to renewed traffic through Strait of Hormuz reducing inefficiencies
items.quote: Suezmaxes, the rates that we are talking about, $350,000 - $400,000 at the peak month ago, are currently at about $130,000-$150,000 a day.

items.statement: Product tanker (MR) spot rates around $50k-60k/day, have not yet corrected like crude tankers; LPG spot rates exceptionally strong at ~$140k/day in H1 vs $55k/day prior year
items.quote: Product tankers took some more time to react, so now they are at an MR tanker is probably around $50,000 to $60,000 a day.

items.statement: Dry bulk rates profitable but off peaks: Capesizes down from ~$40k/day in September to $30k-35k/day currently, still above prior year
items.quote: Capesizes, which were at around 40,000 in September, have now come down to the 30,000 -ish level, 30,000 - 35,000 level.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 average TCY for crude carriers fell from ~$93k/day in Q1 to ~$73k/day; Aframaxes from ~$85k to ~$50k; product tankers from $45k to $32k; LPG up slightly from $41k to $46k; dry bulk small improvement
items.quote: We had average TCY of about USD 93,000 a day for crude carriers i n Q1, which came down to about USD 73,000. The big impact was felt by the Aframaxes, which were averaging about almost USD85,000 in the first quarter and that came down to about USD50,000 in the second quarter

items.statement: Order book high: crude tankers 28% of fleet (only 7.5% delivering by end-2027, rest 2028-2030), product tankers 22%, LPG ~40%, dry bulk ~16%; scrapping minimal due to high earnings
items.quote: the supply of ships and this 28% order book is fairly rear-ended. So you have, of the 28%, only 7.5% which is coming between now and end of 2027. Most of it is coming in 2028, 2029, and now pushing into 2030 as

items.statement: Added two vessels in last week: 2015-built Kamsarmax Jag Amit and 2015-built VLGC Jag Vikrant (with 3-year charter to Sep 2029); committed to 2019-built Kamsarmax delivery within 1-2 months and newbuild Suezmax delivery in ~2 years
items.quote: We have added two vessels in the last week. That's one Kamsarmax, the Jag Amit, which is 2015 built and the Jag Vikrant, which is a very large gas carrier, which is also 2015 built.

items.statement: Newbuild Suezmax ordered as 'insurance' because secondhand prices too high and deployment of >$1bn capital may not be possible in weak markets; IRR close to hurdle but not strictly meeting it
items.quote: We are just doing this as a little bit of insurance in case we are not able to buy those cheap ships. What also happens...

items.statement: Fleet coverage for Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec) at 58% for crude carriers as of last week; coverage will be 'much higher' now; two Suezmaxes fixed on 1-year charters (Aug/Sep 2026 to Aug/Sep 2027), one LR2 on 1-year charter from July, VLGC on 3-year c
items.quote: This is as of last week, really. Yes, this is as of last week. So after 30th September status. No, but it is for the period. So it is the status of last week, taking the full period, that is from 1st October to 31st December, into account.

items.statement: Asset prices up sharply: Suezmax prices ~50% higher in quarter (reflected in NAV), smaller tankers up 5-20%, bulk carriers up 5-10%; NAV at highest ever
items.quote: Tanker prices for the large crude tankers, the Suezmaxes, it has probably gone up 50% in the last quarter, which is reflected in our net asset value.

items.statement: If ships priced at Jan 2026 levels, NAV would be ~INR250/share lower; crude tanker prices ~$80m vs fair value ~$40m (or $20m) per management
items.quote: If we priced, or rather we just put all the ships at their prices of January this year, we would probably be lower by about INR250 or so per share in NAV.

items.statement: Interim dividend maintained at INR14.40/share; buyback at INR1,530 cap to be completed ASAP (cannot do another buyback for 12 months after closure); buyback viewed as capital allocation (buying own fleet at discount) not dividend substitute
items.quote: The interim dividend has been maintained at the previous quarter's level of INR14.40 per share for this quarter.

items.statement: Net cash ~INR8,500 crore on balance sheet; management acknowledges NAV accretion largely from cash flows
items.quote: We hold about INR8,500 crore s of net cash on our balance sheet, right?

items.statement: Geopolitical risk dominates: Iran war closure of Strait of Hormuz created inefficiencies (shuttle service adds 8-9 days/voyage, 18-20% efficiency loss) driving rate spikes; cessation would normalize rates but inventory rebuild and shadow fl
items.quote: Typically, a Middle East to Far East voyage takes about 45, 46 days on a VLCC. This shuttle process, because you have to load twice, you have to discharge twice, the ship is loading inside, coming outside, then offloading to another ship, and that adds eig ht to nine days on average to the voyage time, which is an 18%, 20% reduction in efficiency

items.statement: Management refuses to operate in high-risk routes (Strait of Hormuz loading, Black Sea Novorossiysk) due to crew safety; also avoids Russian trade since 2022 to avoid sanctions risk
items.quote: Finally, we think about the crew. We have our crew on board these ships, and we cannot knowingly send them into a situation of danger.

items.statement: Blended fleet break-even ~$13,000/day across entire fleet
items.quote: The number should be around the $13,000 per day mark. At $13,000 a day across our fleet, we will be around break-even.

items.statement: Offshore: 2 rigs fixed on 3-year contracts in India (repricing H2 FY30), 1 rig left to find employment, 8 vessels up for repricing (4 bid into Indian tenders awaiting outcome); 4 offshore vessels on short-term contracts now repricing H2 FY2
items.quote: We have got two contracts in India, 3-year contracts for two of our rigs. So those now show on the extreme right of this graph, as the two rigs which next need repricing in H2 FY30.

items.statement: Offshore EBITDA run-rate ~INR1,000 cr/yr but next couple of quarters weak due to 60-90 day downtime and capex for rig turnarounds before new 3-year contracts; one rig repricing down $25k-30k/day vs prior contract
items.quote: One of them was coming off from a short-term contract, so not really comparable. The other, the pricing has reduced significantly. From the previous contract, it was down by about $25,000-$30,000 a day.

items.statement: Indian flag preference: foreign-flagged ships (Marshall Islands) rank below Indian-flagged for Right of First Refusal on Indian cargo; tonnage tax applies to foreign-flagged ships owned by Indian company
items.quote: In line of preference, we will be below an Indian-owned Indian flagged ship. We will be below that level in preference when it comes to, say, the Right of First Refusal for an Indian customer's business.

items.statement: IOC and other end-users buying ships to control supply chains (just-in-case vs just-in-time); Middle East oil companies (Iraqi Oil, ADNOC, Aramco) buying crude/LPG tankers; GE Shipping willing to participate in EXIM trade at fair price but
items.quote: I think there are different strategic considerations. What is also happening and let me make this into a bigger picture thing. I think beyond finding the efficient way to do things, the world is moving into a situation or has been shaken so much that you say that I want to move from just in time to just in case.

items.statement: Foreign flag (Marshall Islands) used for operational reasons (minimal port disruption) and indirect tax benefits; ships owned by GE Shipping Mumbai, tonnage tax paid in India
items.quote: The Marshall Islands Flag has a better reputation internationally. Some of our customers, and you know that 80% Plus of our ships are working in the international market, and they prefer to have the Marshall Islands flag because it leads to minimal disruption at ports.

items.statement: Time charter rates at 60-70% discount to spot in hot markets (e.g., Suezmax spot $300k vs 2-yr TC $60k-70k); only in normal markets discount ~20%; old ships (>18 yr) hard to fix on term
items.quote: The rates that are available in the time charter market were at a very, very big discount to the spot rates. So, for instance, when rates were at USD 300,000 a day in the spot market for a Suezmax, the 2-year time charter rate was probably around USD60,000 or max USD70,000 a day.

items.statement: VLGC spot rates ~$140k/day in H1 FY27 vs $55k/day prior year; 1-yr VLGC period charter rumored at ~$100k/day in India; MGC repricing in Jan estimated $40k-50k/day; two VLGCs coming off charter in Mar-Apr and May
items.quote: The contract that I saw, which was a one-year contract in India, I heard rumors of a $100,000 a day contract for one year for an Indian business.

items.statement: Offshore fleet: 4 vessels outside India, 15 in India
items.quote: We have four boats currently outside India. Remaining 15 are in India.

items.statement: New vessel integration takes 3-5 days for flag change and crew familiarization, then earning immediately
items.quote: In some cases, it takes up to three to four days to do the change of flag, to do everything, because in effect, your people have to familiarize themselves with the ship.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% YoY top-line growth and sustainable EBITDA margin of 12-13% in next 3-4 years
items.quote: the management targets are, of course, growing 25% to 30% year- on-year top line growth, seeing, capturing more and more of the market share. Also, along with taking the turnover growth, also stabilizing and GEE Limited Q2 & H1FY27 Post Earnings Conference Call November 13, 2026 4:30 PM IST reaching a sustainable, healthy EBITDA margin of around 12% to 13% in the next three

items.statement: Expects 0.5% EBITDA margin increase in FY27 and 0.5-1% in FY28, reaching double digits in FY28
items.quote: I think I can comfortably say that you would see a 0.5% increase in FY27 and of course, another 0.5% to 0.75% to 1% in FY28. So, we definitely look at a double digit in FY28 for sure and taking it up by a notch higher next year, FY29.

items.statement: Targets INR 1,000 crore revenue by FY30
items.quote: So, that is we are looking at FY29, FY30. I would say more realistically, FY30 is when we are targeting to reach the INR 1000 crore mark.

items.statement: Expects export contribution of 15-20% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, we expect to do an export turnover of around 15% to 20% in the next two to three years at least.

items.statement: Plans INR 35-40 crore capex over next two years for new product lines and capacity expansion
items.quote: So, we are looking at a CapEx outlay of anywhere between INR 35 crores, INR 35 crores to INR 40 crores over the next two years.

items.statement: Expects 18-20% returns from planned capex
items.quote: I think the returns that the company is expecting it is anywhere between 18% to 20% from this CapEx.

items.statement: Current consolidated capacity 59,000 MT; targets 71,000 MT and >90% utilization by FY29-30
items.quote: Taking up the capacity installation from 59,000 metric tons to 71,000 metric tons and efficiently utilizing more than 90% of it by FY29, FY30.

items.statement: Flux-cored wire line commercial production starting last week of November; MIG wire capacity doubling from 12,000 to 24,000 MT
items.quote: Commercial, production is expected to begin by last week of November, and SOFT FLUX lines as well. Thirdly, already the company has around 12,000 metric ton capacity of MIG wires, which is continuous wires and wire rods. Company expects to take up that production because that is 100% utilized to 24,000. So, adding another 12,000 metric ton to that product line.

items.statement: Real estate project at Wagle Estate expected to generate INR 400+ crore revenue over 5 years; cash accruals from Q1 FY28
items.quote: As mentioned before, the company expects a revenue of INR 400 crores plus from this project accruing to the company over the next five years.

items.statement: Real estate project on revenue share model; company handles sales with developer facilitation
items.quote: No, no, because it is a revenue share model that is an area share model that is happening. So, the company is taking charge of its area that we are getting from the deal.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin declined due to raw material price spikes; expects restoration to 9%+ in Q3-Q4
items.quote: However, as I mentioned, this seems to be more of a temporary phase because the company is already working towards higher value-add products. It is also supplying and adding more and more of such products and not only concentrating on the commodity products. So that, I would say that going forward in Q3 and Q4, we are looking at already restoring the margins to 9% and above.

items.statement: Peer margin gap due to better price realization by Ador/ESAB; plans to close via product mix, scale, quality
items.quote: ESAB definitely has a higher margin percentage, but Ador historically was also operating at anywhere between 7% to 9% bracket. It is gone up because the only reason is because definitely ESAB and Ador have higher sales realization for the same product. They are currently enjoying a better realization, price realization vis-à-vis us, although we are operating in the same ecosystem.

items.statement: Specialized/niche products at 27% of revenue; target 35-40% in coming year
items.quote: As you rightly mentioned in earlier calls, I have said that the specialized and the niche products currently own a 27% share in the product basket. We're looking at taking it up to 35% to 40% in the coming year itself.

items.statement: Specialized products sell at INR 275-1,500/kg vs commodity at INR 100-125/kg
items.quote: Whereas the spectrum of a specialized product, if it is a silver brazing alloy wire or if it is a nickel wire or any of these specialized GTX series or something, they could go anywhere between even INR 275 to around INR 1,500 per kg. So the spectrum is actually extremely broad depending upon the technical configuration of the product and the raw materials used.

items.statement: Working capital at 100+ days; targets sub-100 days and peer levels by FY28 via leaner inventory
items.quote: Right now, I think we are at 100 days plus. And I think even if I don't give drastic reduction numbers, but I would like to bring it down to sub-100 first and then bring it down to market peer levels by FY28.

items.statement: Inventory days rose to 127 due to steel price spikes and growth strategy; advancing payments to JSW, SAIL, Tata Steel
items.quote: Frankly, the working capital also being a bit high is because of higher inventory holding days for the company rather than anything else. And that has been done primarily because of the high steel prices. So, we've also been stocking up a bit considering, the sharp spikes in prices.

items.statement: Only working capital limits (INR 100 crore); utilization ~INR 40 crore; no term loans
items.quote: Company is having quite a good cushion because we have limits of around INR 100 crores of working capital limits from the banks, whereas we are utilizing only around INR 40 crores.

items.statement: Borrowings spike to INR 56.6 crore due to advance payments to steel suppliers; normalized post-September
items.quote: However, in the last couple of months, because there has been quite a lot of work happening, the company is also paying advance to key steel suppliers like JSW, SAIL, and TATA, because of which as on September end, actually these numbers are looking quite high.

items.statement: Price pass-through lag of 15-25 days for steel price changes; symmetric on increases and decreases
items.quote: There is a lag of anywhere between 15 to 25 days to pass on that price increase because definitely it doesn't happen overnight that if today's steel prices have gone up tomorrow I'm able to increase the price immediately for my finished good but that is also as far as reduction in prices is concerned.

items.statement: 55:45 direct (B2B) vs dealer/distributor split; direct to BHEL, DRDO, L&T, JCB, NPCIL
items.quote: So, as you have seen, there is almost a 55:45 ratio that we do. So, we do both B2B and B2Cs to a lot of these customers like BHEL, DRDO, L&T, JCB, all of them we supply directly.

items.statement: High wallet share with key accounts (NPCIL, BHEL, DRDO); among few approved suppliers
items.quote: I think currently in India there are very few and I when I say very few I think there are only two or three max customers who are actually approved to supply to these client customers. Like even when I said NPCIL we took the approval of NPCIL we were the second or the third company only in the country to actually bag this approval prestigious approval even to BHEL.

items.statement: Market share ~6-6.5% of organized market; targets 10-12% at INR 1,000 crore; growth from unorganized conversion and regional players
items.quote: Coming to your first question, see when I'm talking about capturing more of the market share currently I'm at around anywhere around 6% to 6.5% of the market share and I'm talking about the organized market only right now. Going forward even to INR 1,000 crores I will be at small 10% to 12% of the market share.

items.statement: Added 130+ new dealers in last 6 months; expanding in south India, cement, infrastructure sectors
items.quote: We're definitely, I can say that we've added more than 130 new dealers in the last six months. We are penetrating in areas on markets where we weren't really present earlier in sectors where you know our presence was more dominant like the cement sector or a few of the infrastructure execution companies or in the southern part of India.

items.statement: Key growth drivers: defence/shipbuilding, power/energy (nuclear, solar), infrastructure; India defence export shift
items.quote: The key growth drivers, I would say, over these next six to eight years would be, of course, primarily defence and shipbuilding opportunities. There is a huge potential where the country now, as India has now converted from being a defence importing country to almost a defence exporting country in the last financial year.

items.statement: H2 seasonally stronger (55%+ of revenue); confidence from ground-level activity and India's structural growth
items.quote: If you see historically also company has done around 55%, more than 55% I think revenue in it's H2 rather and 40% to 45% in H1. Again as I say that of course this quarter was a more of a temporary quarter as because of the war situations and ongoing geopolitical turmoil.

items.statement: Welding consumables market $1.2B in 2024; projected $2.4B by 2032-33
items.quote: Potential for a dramatic transformation and growth from a global $1.2 billion industry today in 2024. In fact, two years back, the projections are the market estimates are that it would go up to $2.4 billion by 2032-'33.

items.statement: Nuclear power capacity 8 GW now; government targets 3x by 2031, 100 GW by 2040
items.quote: Right now it is at 8 gigawatts and the country the government is looking at taking it up to 3x times by 2031 and taking it up to 100 gigawatts by 2040.

items.statement: Real estate proceeds to fund brownfield acquisitions in welding equipment/other lines; avoid debt-heavy deals
items.quote: First and foremost would be brownfield acquisition and growth. So there are quite a few tier two, tier three, companies which can be acquired and broaden the entire horizon of the company. So as far as welding equipments and other product lines are considered, company has already outlined a strategy for that as well.

items.statement: Real estate proceeds also to reward shareholders; no significant debt to reduce
items.quote: Second is also, of course, to adequately reward its shareholders and owners. And by owners, I mean to say shareholders and only because they all are the owners of the company.

items.statement: Existing capacity (INR 370 cr revenue) can add INR 300 cr incremental with minimal capex
items.quote: So, see currently, if we are operating at anywhere last year, if I take last year numbers, fiscal numbers of around INR 370 crores, without any significant CapEx also definitely the company can add incremental around INR 300 crores.

items.statement: Growth split ~60% volume, 40% value; driven by capacity utilization scaling and defence/infra sectors
items.quote: I would say it would be roughly between 60% to 40%. I would say a lot of it would also come from volume and by volume I'm not only talking about mass commodity products but value you as I see this the nature of this industry is the entire as I am being repetitive here but I'll say that the entire project will only use 2% of its cost as welding consumable.

items.statement: Geopolitical (Middle East war, container issues) caused temporary margin pressure; sees India's structural resilience
items.quote: Of course, as Mohsin is projecting on the screen, there has been a very -- the company has achieved the milestone of handing over the possession of the Wagle Industrial Estate land to the developer, where the real estate project is supposed to take off in record time.

items.statement: Retained FY27 EBITDA guidance for Acquired Group at EUR35 million, factoring in VP4 divestment impact
items.quote: In the retained guidance, we've taken that into account, that the VP4 sale is gone. I think Q3 last year was quite a subdued quarter. We don't expect such a subdued quarter this quarter, but we are tending cautiously because this is the first normal two, three quarter, which we are going to experience as we have acquired this business. Hence, we are keeping the guidance as today.

items.statement: Acquired Group EBITDA margin currently at 6-6.5%, targeting 9-10% via cost reduction, backward integration, AI, and operational leverage
items.quote: From the time of acquisition till now, if you could help us, what are the things that we have been able to achieve on capturing the value, and what would be the things that are still pending for us to reach that EUR90 million to EUR100 million mark that we are planning over the next three to four years?

items.statement: Most FY29 EBITDA margin improvement to 12% will come from Acquired Group, with some scope in Legacy Sudarshan business
items.quote: I think most of the improvement, Manjeet, came from the acquired group. Of course, there is some scope within the Legacy Sudarshan business also to improve, but most of the improvement came from the legacy.

items.statement: EUR15-20 million inventory reduction expected in FY27, but H1 inventory increased due to longer lead times and demand variation
items.quote: Management expected a further EUR15 million-EUR20 million inventory reduction coming through in FY2027. However, if we look at the inventory days, I mean, that has actually gone up in the first half, if we have to look at. And even on the absolute number, I think it's up by 25% over the 31st March.

items.statement: Backward integration projects not yet started; will require new capacity investment in India to produce molecules using shared IP
items.quote: What we've not done so far is any backward integration, right? We want to kick start some of the backward integration projects. The second is use of artificial intelligence or AI in the business. This is the second leg which we've not still kind of leveraged.

items.statement: Swiss aluminum dyes site acquired for business continuity; toll manufacturing by Clariant ending; cost improvement opportunities identified
items.quote: This business was being toll manufactured. The business belonged to us, but this was toll manufactured, these products, by Clariant for us. And Clariant, in the long term, didn't want to do this. And in order for us to continue the business, this was very important to maintain, get that site.

items.statement: Customer destocking over; customers buying only for immediate needs, not stocking up; geopolitical uncertainty keeping demand muted
items.quote: From the customers' bit, I think the destocking is over and I am hoping that it is over because it cannot be forever and ever. But we do not see a destocking impact now coming in. In fact, it is the high inventory scenario. So customers are buying only when there is a requirement. They are not stocking up enough, but of course there is a general external geopolitical uncertainty which keeps the de

items.statement: Regained trust of global key accounts in Europe and US; winning back lost business across coatings and digital inks segments
items.quote: We have been able to gain business and trust of all our global key accounts, and several of the businesses are coming back to us. But of course, this is an ongoing process, but we are well on that track.

items.statement: Lost business was dispersed across industries and suppliers; some business already returning; full recovery will take time
items.quote: We lost business across industries. It is not a concentrated portfolio where one or two suppliers have gained in. It has been a loss across. What gives us the confidence is we have already seen some of this business come back. It is not just talk now. We are seeing some of the business come back. I think to the fullest extent would take some time to build that up.

items.statement: Integrated functional organization across legacies; retained most critical talent; some rehiring done; leadership based on meritocracy regardless of location
items.quote: We worked on a meritocracy basis. We have a functional organization, and whether the functional head sits in India, Europe, US, is irrelevant, but I think we've chosen the best. From that perspective, and we've been able to retain most of the critical talent. We've also done some rehiring in some areas. But I think all in all, the org structure is quite well set, sir.

items.statement: Post VP4 sale (INR800-850 crore) and CHF7 million acquisition, company expects to be meaningfully net cash by year-end
items.quote: You sold this business for INR800 crores-INR850 crores. You are acquiring a small business potentially for CHF7 million. So you should be meaningfully net cash by the year-end.

items.statement: No immediate acquisition plans to expand footprint; board continuously evaluates opportunities; backward integration focus for now
items.quote: I think the north for backward integration, but I think the management and the Board kind of always keeps looking for opportunities, but nothing where it can expand our footprint. But I think nothing. At the right time, of course, if we do find, we will come and talk about it.

items.statement: Merger with Sudarshan Colorants under board review but deferred due to multiple moving parts; focus on operational integration first
items.quote: So, Gupta, I think there are several aspects which the board is looking at. But given that there are too many moving parts, I think we will come back to this in some time. Currently, I think we are looking at how to improve our operations, how to integrate our systems, and then look at some of the structural changes.

items.statement: Legacy Sudarshan revenue growth split roughly half volume, half price; Acquired Group growth mostly price-driven with muted volumes
items.quote: I would divide it into half and half between price and volume , given this other factor not being there, and the rest is all good. On the Acquired Group, we have some volume growth, muted volume growth, but rest is all price increase.

items.statement: Production of commoditized products moved to India but not fully commercialized; further margin upside pending
items.quote: So the production has been moved, sir, but I don't think we've got the full mileage. We've not been able to still fully commercialize those businesses. So that's a scope where we can win some.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow 9% revenue vs 3-4% industry growth by regaining lost sales; two-thirds of EBITDA growth from cost reduction, one-third from sales growth
items.quote: I think the first is, our thesis was that we will be able to win back some of the businesses which we've lost. That will give us some growth. That is first aspect. But given that, I mean, our aspiration to grow EBITDA, like I said, two-third of the aspiration, two-third of it comes more from internal cost reduction. Maybe one-third of the EBITDA growth comes from driving sales up from that perspec

items.statement: No unfunded pension liabilities in Acquired Group; all factored into deal consideration
items.quote: No. Yes, sir, everything. There is no unfunded. There are none.

items.statement: VP4 captive usage is 5-10% depending on demand; single-digit percentage
items.quote: So, Nitesh, it is between 5%-10%, I think a very low amount depending on the demand situation. I mean, the matter of fact is it is quite low, right? In the single digit.

items.statement: Competitive edge is regained customer trust, relationship reliability, and service quality after Heubach insolvency period
items.quote: I think that was the very basis that customers had lost trust in us, and we have regained that trust, the relationship, ensuring that we serve them well, rebuild relationships, and the reliability with them.

items.statement: Purchase cost reduction achieved via global buying and Asia-based sourcing; further procurement optimization pending
items.quote: The third has been purchase cost reduction, looking at more global buying, looking at Asia-based buying globally. These are some of the areas we've been able to achieve.

items.statement: IT integration consolidating four SAP instances into one; considerable progress made but still in progress
items.quote: IT integration had two phases. One is, of course, cost reduction, but also looking at how we are able to reduce our costs. As I mentioned, the transactions which we are doing today are four transactions. We have four SAPs. Consolidating them into one.

items.statement: Manufacturing cost reduction achieved via yield improvements, throughput gains, and utility cost reductions across sites
items.quote: Second is manufacturing cost reduction. So we've really worked across, whether it's yield improvements, throughput improvements, utility costs and reductions across our sites.

items.statement: Organization restructuring reduced overhead costs; lean functional structure implemented across legacies
items.quote: First on the org structure build. We've done a lot of work and reduced costs there.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue guidance for FY27 revised to INR600-650 crores from earlier INR700-750 crores
items.quote: Having said that, this year's revenue may hover around INR600 crores to INR650 crores, the delayed orders we are banking upon will contribute to revenue early next financial year.

items.statement: Reaffirmed 20-25% CAGR target from FY26 base to FY28
items.quote: We remain committed to achieving our guidance of a 20% to 25% CAGR growth on the base numbers of FY '26 by FY '28.

items.statement: Targeting blended EBITDA margin of around 20% long-term
items.quote: we have always maintained that for our business, we should be around the 20% EBITDA mark. And we still stick to that, that lo ng term, we should remain in the averages of around 20

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR471 crores as of 30 Sep 2026, new orders of INR136 crores won in Q2
items.quote: Our consol order book stood at INR471 crores as on 30th September, broadly in line with INR485 crores at the start of the quarter, even after executing INR151 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Order intake target of INR800 crores for FY27, over INR300 crores booked YTD with large orders expected in next 1-3 months
items.quote: The INR800 crores was the order booking for the year. We have booked over INR300 crores till date. And we believe there are some large orders which would be getting converted in the next 1 or 2, 3 months.

items.statement: Stand-alone revenue declined due to slower customer decision-making from geopolitical uncertainty, not structural issues
items.quote: Many of our customers, especially in the export and capital goods markets have postponed the finalization and dispatch schedules because of the current geopolitical uncertainty.

items.statement: Over INR250 crores of opportunities near finalization including Middle East, Far East and domestic nuclear orders
items.quote: We are sitting on more than INR250 crores of opportunities, which we are about to close any time. I mean, we've been -- it's got deferred by a couple of quarters.

items.statement: INR25 crores approved for Monga Strayfield Pune facility expansion for data center enclosures over 6-9 months
items.quote: The Board has approved an investment of INR25 crores primarily at Monga Strayfield's Pune facility to be implemented over the next 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Kilburn Saravali plant expansion and ME Energy Pune Phase 2 underway, completion by Q3/early Q4
items.quote: Expansion at Kilburn Saravali plant and Phase 2 of ME Energy's Pune plant are underway and expected to be completed by Q3, early Q4.

items.statement: Group building manufacturing infrastructure to support >INR1,000 crores annual revenue capacity via brownfield expansions
items.quote: Together with the planned expansion of Monga Strayfield's Pune plant, we are building the group manufacturing infrastructure to support more than INR1,000 crores annual revenue capacity.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield capacity addition kicking in from January, revenue potential scaling to >INR200 crores from INR100 crores base
items.quote: On Monga Strayfield, the capacity addition would start kicking in from January. So you will have additional capacity in the last quarter of this year and full capacity increase in the first 6 months of FY '28. With that, Monga Strayfield as a company will have a revenue potential of scaling up to over INR200 crores from a INR100 crores base.

items.statement: ME Energy theoretical capacity could reach INR300+ crores post expansion, two subsidiaries combined can deliver >INR500 crores subject to orders
items.quote: Regarding ME Energy Limited, we are already completing the capex program where 2 bays have been added in the Pune plant. And their theoretical capacity could also be upwards of INR300 crores. So together, the 2 subsidiaries can comfortably deliver over INR500 crores, subject to getting the orders in FY '28.

items.statement: Kilburn stand-alone plants can handle INR750-800 crores revenue with current infrastructure and vendor leverage
items.quote: When it comes to Kilburn, both our plants at Ambernath as well as Saravali, given if the order book is strong, I think we can easily touch INR750 crores to INR800 crores.

items.statement: Data center enclosure business with Vertiv expected to generate INR50-60 crores in FY27, ~INR100 crores in FY28, full capacity potential INR120-130 crores
items.quote: On current capacity, we expect revenue of INR50 crores to INR60 crores from this business in FY '27. Vertiv with whom Monga Strayfield has had a long-standing relationship has indicated a requirement of INR90 crores in the current financial year. Based on this, we expect the enclosure business with Vertiv to generate approximately INR100 crores in annual revenue in FY '27-'28. Once fully utilized,

items.statement: ME Energy entering ferrous alloy waste heat recovery via Bhutan order, pursuing steel and cement sector waste heat recovery boilers
items.quote: What is heartening for the group is our entry into the ferrous alloy space using ME Energy Limited. The ferro-alloy sector is seeing a lot of capex and especially with the waste heat recovery systems provided by ME Energy, we believe our entry into the sector through our Bhutan order has opened up opportunities for many more orders in the sector to come through.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin ~16.5% due to product mix and higher raw material value consumption percentage, employee cost increase
items.quote: So it's a combination of both. So I would say partially because of the mix of the products, yes. And second one, there has been a increase in cost for a number of reasons. One is the employee cost has gone up. Secondly, when you talk about the cost of raw materials, it is not the escalation in the cost of raw material, but more of the value of the raw materials consumed.

items.statement: Typically no price escalation clauses in orders; margins protected by booking key raw materials immediately after order receipt
items.quote: Typically, when we take orders across our group, we normally book our raw material in the next few days itself. Typically, we do not have any price escalation in any of our orders, but we try to protect our margins by ordering the key raw materials ASAP once we get the order.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to remain negative at year-end due to debtor and unbilled revenue buildup unless higher advances received
items.quote: No, it will be -- the negative will reduce, but it will remain negative. With the year-end activity increases, there are higher sales at the end of the year. So naturally, there's a buildup of debtors and unbilled revenue. So unless we get higher number of orders and advances against that, otherwise, it will remain more or less in the same level.

items.statement: Receivables over 120 and 180 days exist due to project commissioning milestones
items.quote: Yes, there are some over 180 days. There are some over 180 days.

items.statement: Promoter pledge of <1% holding created for corporate requirements at entity level
items.quote: The pledge is less than 1% of the promoter holding, and it was required for certain corporate requirements at that entity.

items.statement: Subsidiary revenue doubled from INR73.4 crores to INR141.7 crores in H1, now contributing >50% of group revenue
items.quote: Revenue from the subsidiaries roughly doubled from INR73.4 crores in H1 last year to around INR141.7 crores this year, and they now contribute more than half of the group revenue.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR153.1 crores in Q2 (flat YoY, +30.9% QoQ), H1 revenue INR270.1 crores (-4.5% YoY), PAT INR16.5 crores Q2, INR29.6 crores H1
items.quote: At the consol level, revenue from the operations for Q2 was INR153.1 crores, almost unchanged from INR153.6 crores in the same quarter last year. It was also 30.9% higher than Q1. For the half year, consol revenue was INR270.1 crores against INR282.8 crores last year, a decline of 4.5%.

items.statement: Revenue recognition timing risk: delayed orders may spill into FY28 due to POC accounting
items.quote: Now some of the orders are coming in later and the fact that we realize our revenue on a POC basis, there could be a spillover to the next year.

items.statement: Targeting export of more than 5 million tons of bauxite over next two quarters (H2 FY27)
items.quote: With the monsoon impact expected to ease, we are targeting the export of more than 5 million tons of bauxite over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Expect iron ore operations to start next financial year with reasonable update on guidance
items.quote: I think that we would have first of all a reasonable update in terms of guidance by the next financial year.

items.statement: Boffa port capacity enhanced from 5 to 8 MTPA; GSM jetty expansion from 6 to 10 MTPA expected by March 2027
items.quote: Our Boffa port is now fully operational with its handling capacity enhanced from 5 million tons to 8 million tons per annum. At GSM, construction of our new jetty is progressing and upon its completion, it is expected to increase capacity from 6 million tons to 10 million tons per annum.

items.statement: Planning capex of INR150-170 crores across India business verticals for manufacturing capabilities and product portfolio expansion
items.quote: As stated previously, we are also planning capex of INR150 crores to INR170 crores across various projects and business verticals across the India portfolio.

items.statement: Q2 Guinea bauxite exports declined to 1.21 million tons from 2.34 million tons in Q1 due to seasonal monsoon
items.quote: During Q2, we exported 1.21 million tons of bauxite compared with 2.34 million tons in Q1. This decline was primarily due to seasonal monsoon conditions, which typically affect mining and dispatches during Q2 and part of Q3.

items.statement: Customer base in Middle East and Europe impacted by elevated ocean freight rates over last two quarters
items.quote: Our customer base, particularly in the Middle Eastern Europe has been impacted over the last two quarters due to elevated ocean freight rates.

items.statement: Guinea EBITDA per ton at USD5.3 in Q2 vs USD6.3 in Q1; expect improvement as freight normalizes
items.quote: Despite these challenges, we were able to maintain a positive EBITDA contribution of USD5.3 per metric ton. While this was slightly lower than USD6.3 per metric ton we achieved in Q1, we believe the performance demonstrates the resilience of our operations in a difficult operating environment.

items.statement: Sulfuric acid prices have corrected from peak; expected to improve bleaching clay margins
items.quote: We feel that sulfuric acid prices may reduce, and they have already corrected from the peak. This should contribute to improving margins in times to come.

items.statement: If Guinea quota system implemented at 150 million tons, expect at least couple of dollars EBITDA improvement per ton
items.quote: But like I said that if the quota system comes a nd it comes near 150 million, so at least we should expect couple of dollars improvement in EBITDA, even conservatively

items.statement: Bauxite prices between Q2 and Q3 remained largely stable or slightly increased
items.quote: So, first point is ba uxite prices between quarter 2 and quarter 3 have remained largely stable or slightly increased. That is a broad comment

items.statement: Higher ocean freight and fuel costs impacted Guinea operations in Q2
items.quote: In addition to the lower volumes, the business also faced higher ocean freight and the fuel costs during the quarter.

items.statement: Bleaching clay business faced cost pressures from higher sulfuric acid input costs
items.quote: Our bleaching clay business continues to face cost pre ssures during the quarter, primarily due to higher input costs, particularly sulfuric acid

items.statement: India business targeting value-added products to reach ~40% of India turnover over next four years
items.quote: A longer-term target, I think, would be to say that at least the new value- added products should be maybe about 40% of our turnover in the India busi ness over the next, you can say, four years or

items.statement: Capex focused on oil and gas, foundry, paint and coatings, paper industries with import substitution and new technology products
items.quote: we are basically doing capex to develop new applications into oil and gas, pet-related products. We are doing some of the capex to improve our overall volumes also in the business. We are also trying to develop some new produc ts for coating industries, which we have had successful POCs, and the capex will help us to commercialize the same

items.statement: Strengthening focus on domestic, Asian and African markets where supply chain conditions are more manageable
items.quote: In the interim, as highlighted in our previous earnings call, we continue to strengthen our focus on domestic, Asian and African markets, where supply chain conditions remain relatively more manageable.

items.statement: Guinea quota system would benefit smaller producers like Ashapura vs large Chinese companies
items.quote: the expect ed reduction in bauxite export from a quota system would be a positive move for suppliers such as Ashapura, who are smaller than the very very large Chinese companies

items.statement: No formal Guinea export quota system implemented yet; expecting government update by end of quarter
items.quote: currently as of now, there is no formal quota system which has come out yet. We are expecting to get some update from the government by the en d of this quarter

items.statement: Combined port capacity of 18 MTPA (Boffa 8 + GSM 10); targeting 15 MTPA utilization in FY28
items.quote: Well, we can say very easily that next year out of 18, 15 should be utilized. That's the expectation.

items.statement: Iron ore resource of 300 sq km; targeting 3-4 million tons annually once commercialized
items.quote: So, maybe definitely more than -- over a longer term, once we commercialize, 3 million or 4 million tons can be something we can easily think that should happen.

items.statement: Income tax liability expected to increase gradually as past losses are utilized up over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: However, we do expect that as the company's profitability improves gradually, maybe in the next two or three quarters, the income tax cost as a pe rcentage of PBT will increase

items.statement: Consolidated income from operations INR1,063 crores in Q2 FY27 (12% YoY growth); EBITDA INR138 crores
items.quote: For quarter 2 '27, consolidated income from operations stood at INR1,063 crores as compared to INR953 cror es in quarter 2 '26, registering a year-on-year growth of 12% and EBITDA stood at INR138 crores compared to INR132 crores in the corresponding quarter last year

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated income from operations INR2,680 crores (16% YoY growth); EBITDA INR327 crores
items.quote: For H1 '27, consolidated income from operations increased to INR2,680 crores from INR2,308 crores in H1 of '26, representing a growth of 16%. EBITDA increased to INR327 crores from INR320 crores.

items.statement: Guinea bauxite EBITDA per ton USD5.3 in Q2 vs USD6.3 in Q1; previously reached USD9-10 when freight was lower
items.quote: I think EBITDA in the near term may remain similar because of the environment being quite challenging. You know, in the earlier quarters, I would like to highlight that when our EBITDA was USD9 or USD10, somewhere closer to that level, freight levels were much lower compared to the total bauxite cost.

items.statement: Worst-case scenario close to current conditions with weak alumina demand, high freight, and geopolitical issues
items.quote: What we are witnessing in last couple of quarters is close to the worst-case scenario only, that alumina business is in a little bit difficult time. The freight costs are elevated, specially because of this war and other situations.

items.statement: Quartz purification for semiconductor applications at R&D stage, not close to commercialization
items.quote: We are studying it, but as of now, it is an R&D level project, which is not very close to commercialization.

items.statement: Received six bentonite mines in Gujarat; small deposits but support long-term resource sustainability for value-added products
items.quote: company has received these six mines, and it is a good development for the company, as developing these mines and utilizing the be ntonite for our own factories and value-added operations will help us to contribute to our volume and margin

items.statement: Consolidated net debt target for FY27 end is INR650-700 crore including BTPL merger and shareholder settlement
items.quote: At the year end, when we close this financial year, including BTPL, we are targeting to end with a net debt at around INR650 crores-INR700

items.statement: Africa revenue guidance for FY27 revised to $50-55 million in H2 due to customer de-risking, down from earlier $60 million
items.quote: We might slow that down to close to about $50 million or thereabout in Q2, in H2, I am sorry.

items.statement: Atraco EBITDA margin expected to reach 10% within six months (by Q4 FY27)
items.quote: Six months down the line, I am confident that we should be at the 10% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: BTPL expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in Q3 FY27 and PBT breakeven in Q4 FY27
items.quote: Q3, we are expecting BTPL to be EBITDA breakeven. In Q2, the EBIT DA was slightly negative. In Q4, we are expecting the revenue to go to the region of about INR250 crores or thereabouts. We are expecting, or we are working towards a PBT level breakeven

items.statement: Double-digit volume growth in India business expected from FY28
items.quote: Double-digit volume growth we should start seeing from FY 2028.

items.statement: India revenue capacity target of INR4,000 crore, Africa INR1,250 crore, BTPL INR1,200 crore by FY28
items.value: INR4,000 crore (India), INR1,250 crore (Africa), INR1,200 crore (BTPL)
items.quote: India will be INR4,000 crores. Africa will be about INR1,250 crores. Revenue capacity. BTPL will be about, I would say, INR1,200 crores revenue capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin targets for FY28: India 13%, Africa 10%, BTPL 10%
items.quote: The India EBITDA margin, in my assessment, should be 13%. The Africa EBITDA margin should be 10%. For the first year, which is FY 2028, BTPL or the fabric EBITDA margin should be 10%.

items.statement: Capex plan: INR150-175 crore in FY27, INR200+ crore annually for next three years, total INR450-500 crore FY26-29
items.quote: Our capex, for instance, this year we are planning about INR150 crores. We might ratchet it up to INR175 crores based on the volume growth. The projections which I am getting from certain customers in the years ahead would necessitate us to book capex in excess of INR200 crores in three years every year.

items.statement: Working capital days target of 75 days for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: On an average, we are targeting around 75 days. Even though we ended with 72 days in this quarter, we should budget 75 on an overall basis.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to be very low or near zero for some time due to BTPL accumulated losses of INR600+ crore
items.quote: Tax rate going forward will be low because once the BTPL asset merges with us, we will have accumulated losses coming into the company. BTPL carries an accumulated loss in excess of INR600 crores or thereabouts, and hence there will be a tax shield which will come from there.

items.statement: US apparel imports returned to positive growth in August; NRF projects 4.2% holiday retail sales growth; sourcing recovery expected over coming quarters
items.quote: Imports into the U.S. and EU returned to positive growth. Looking ahead, the year-end holiday season in the U.S. is expected to remain healthy. The National Retail Federation projects retail sales growth of 4.2% year-on-year.

items.statement: European customers growing 60-70% YoY; European revenue share target 25% in 4-5 years from current 15%
items.quote: Some of those customers are growing at some 60%, 70% year-over-year. That tempo of growth will be sustained. My sense is that it may also, over a period of four, five years, grow to about 25% odd of total revenue.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin improvement of ~2% from exchange rate benefit (1.3-1.4%) and tariff discount elimination (0.5%)
items.quote: So that itself is about 1.3% to 1.4% in EBITDA margin. So that's an additional gain that will come purely out of exchange rate. Then, till Q2, there were some discounts that we had passed on to our customers. Effectively, that was about of the order of 0.5% of gross total revenue, gross revenue of the company. that is no longer in effect from Q3, so that is an added margin gain that we will see fr

items.statement: Wage cost increase of 8-9% absorbed; RoSCTL at 3.5% may halve to 1.75% but will be absorbed via productivity
items.quote: In fact, we see wage cost increases, this year, our wage cost increase has been about 8%-9%, and wage being 25% of our revenue, the impact of that itself was over 2%-2.5%. We have absorbed that. I am not particularly concerned. We will be able to absorb it. We are working towards absorbing that in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Strong order book visibility; two new Africa customers (one American, one European) starting April FY28; European customer growth robust
items.quote: We have actually secured two new customers in Africa, which will start from April onwards, one American and one European. There is a fair amount of demand.

items.statement: Bhopal Phase 2 (3.5M pieces, INR200 cr revenue) ramping up by FY27 end; Ranchi 1,000-machine factory (2,000-machine equivalent, INR400 cr revenue) ready by Q3 FY28; two more 1,000-machine factories planned
items.quote: Bhopal phase two is on a ramp-up as we speak. By this financial year-end, that phase two will be fully ramped up. Ranchi, we have started work on a new factory, which is a 1,000-machine factory which will run in two shifts, so effectively 2,000- machine factory. 2,000-machine factory effectivel y will contribute INR400 crores in top line, and that we anticipate to be ready for ramp-up somewhere by

items.statement: India capacity 59M pieces by FY27 end, Africa 45M pieces; targeting 2-3 new factories adding 3.5M pieces each in FY28
items.quote: For India operations, the expected total capacity by the end of this year would be around 59 million. For Africa operation, it will be 45 million. Lakshmi Narayan: Okay, sir. For next year, sir? Sathyamurthy: Next year, We are targeting at least two to three factories to come on board. Each factory will add 3.5 million pieces

items.statement: India capacity utilization ~92-93% in Q3 FY27; Africa utilization ~80-85% and climbing
items.quote: I think in India, I would say we are utilizing. In Q3, we would be utilizing close to about 92%- 93% or thereabouts. In Africa, we will be utiliz ing at about 80%-85%, and that also will be climbing up

items.statement: Exchange rate hedges: Q2 at INR91, Q3 at INR93, Q4 at INR94-95; input cost pass-through to customers from Q3
items.quote: In Q2, for instance, our exchange rate, because we hedge our foreign exchange receivables, our exchange rate was at about INR91. In Q3, we are holding an average hedge at about INR93, and in Q4, we are holding it closer to INR94. INR50 or INR95.

items.statement: Higher ASP in Q1/Q2 from outerwear/autumn-winter; strong traction for autumn-winter 2027 (production in Q1/Q2 FY28)
items.quote: We are seeing a very strong traction in that space. So when I look at autumn-winter 2027, which will be actually production in Q1 and Q2 of FY 2028, we are seeing a strong growth in those product types, including volumes.

items.statement: One Africa customer (20-25% of Africa revenue) being ramped down due to financial strength concerns; de-risking customer portfolio
items.quote: It is about 20%-25% revenue, but at the moment, yes. And they are usually a little Q2, H2 heavy customer, pre-summer customer.

items.statement: US Section 301 tariffs (July 2026) put India on equal footing with Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Sri Lanka; 12.5% advantage over China and Vietnam
items.quote: They place India on an equal footing with several competing sourcing countries, including Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, etcetera. India also has kept a clear advantage over China and Vietnam, both of which face about 12.5% tariffs.

items.statement: Bangladesh LDC status expires Nov 2026 with 3-year grace to Nov 2029; if not extended, India-EU FTA would create significant advantage
items.quote: There is a least developed country status which gives them zero duty access to Europe, and that is expiring in November 2026 with a three-year grace, so which will technically expire in November 2029. If that is not getting extended, then India, which will, of course, in the future, have zero duty FTA with Europe, and Bangladesh, which may lose the duty-free status, that may have a much bigger pla

items.statement: Creditors days increased by extending vendor credit terms to align with customer credit cycles; no procurement cost impact
items.quote: No, Prerna, we have worked this out with our vendors, to extend the credit period, aligning with the customers' credit terms. That was one of the key activities we were working on to improve our working capital. We intend to align the pay cycle in line with credit cycle of our customers, and that's the reason for the increase in trade payables.

items.statement: All capex and working capital in FY27 funded from cash generation; INR80-100 crore cash component for BTPL shareholder settlement
items.quote: We have also accounted INR80 crores-INR100 crores towards settlement to BTPL shareholders, the likely cash component. All the capex and working capital, during this financial year, is being funded out of cash generation.

items.statement: Dividend decision deferred until tariff stability and geopolitical clarity; paid dividend before 2025 tariff impact
items.quote: We had paid dividend before all the tariff impact, tariff impacted us in 2025. I think once there is some clarity on stability of tariffs, etcetera, since we are profitable, there is enough cash flow being generated by the business, we will take a call on paying dividend once there is a little more stability on the tariff front as well as geopolitics front.

items.statement: No significant labor shortage; using migrant labor in south; incremental expansions in central/eastern India with training camps including DDU-GKY program
items.quote: No, I don't think we are facing that. I mean, wherever we are facing shortfalls, we are using migrant labors, particularly in the south. Our incremental expansions are all happening in central India, eastern India, where we don't seem to ha ve any concerns as far as labor availability is

items.statement: Legal review ongoing on BTPL/Bombay Rayon asset transfer allegations; early indication shows no strength in allegations; seller comfort obtained
items.quote: At the moment, we are getting legal input on this topic, and early indication is that there seems to be no strength in those allegations. In fact, we have derived the comfort from the sellers also that all the procedural requirements have been fulfilled, and they are also extending that comfort to us.

items.statement: India apparel exports grew only 1.2% YoY in Q2 FY27 vs Gokaldas India business 10% YoY growth, indicating market share gains
items.quote: Our India business grew a robust 10% Y-o-Y in a seasonally weak quarter, supported by a strong order book and improved execution. This is particularly notable because overall Indian apparel exports grew only by 1.2% year-on-year over the same period.

items.statement: No sewing machine import restrictions faced for industrial/export-oriented manufacturing
items.quote: We do not face any sewing machine import restrictions, so I am not sure about households. As far as industrial imports are concerned, especially for export-oriented manufacturers, we do not have any such restrictions in place, and we have not seen any problems on that count.

items.statement: Expect gross margin pressure to ease progressively as pending price revisions are approved and cost recoveries realized; significant EBITDA margin improvement expected in H2 FY27
items.quote: We expect the pressure on margins to ease progressively as pending price revisions are approved and the corresponding cost recoveries are realized.

items.statement: Expect battery business to achieve zero EBITDA loss in Q3 FY27, eliminating operating losses
items.quote: I am quite hopeful that in this quarter 3 also, we should be able to achieve a zero EBITDA kind of a situation, thereby eliminating all the losses at least on the operating level of the company.

items.statement: Expect Hutchinson technology partnership breakthrough with first order win in Q4 FY27
items.quote: What we are expecting is that in quarter 4, we should be able to achieve some breakthrough in the first order win using Hutchinson technology.

items.statement: Plan to increase aftermarket contribution from 5% to 10% of group sales over coming years
items.quote: Currently contributing approximately 5% to the group sales, this business has significant growth potential. We are building the necessary capabilities and infrastructure to increase its contribution to approximately 10% of group sales over the coming years.

items.statement: New Chennai plant expected fully operational by Q3 FY27; further capacity expansion to be evaluated in Q3 based on order book and utilization
items.quote: The new plant in Chennai is progressing well with the investments made expected to become fully operational by quarter 3 of financial year '27. Further capacity expansion investments will be evaluated in quarter 3 based on the order book position, business growth prospects and capacity utilization levels.

items.statement: Meraki tooling slump sale expected completed by end of Q3 FY27 subject to approvals
items.quote: The slump sale is expected to be completed by the end of quarter 3 of this financial year, subject to the requisite approvals.

items.statement: Avinya Batteries merger with PPAP expected completed by end of Q4 FY27 subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: The proposed merger of Avinya Batteries Limited with PPAP is on course and is expected to be completed by the end of this financial year, probably by the end of quarter 4, again, subject to the requisite regulatory and statutory approvals.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share
items.quote: It gives me immense pleasure to share that the Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share, reaffirming our commitment to rewarding our shareholders and sharing the benefits of the company's growth and performance.

items.statement: Indian auto industry recorded highest ever Q2 sales across all major segments; domestic sales grew 18.2% YoY to 83.88 lakh units
items.quote: The Indian automobile industry continued its strong growth momentum during the second quarter of financial year '27, recording its highest ever second quarter sales across all major vehicle segments. Domestic sales grew by 18.2% year-on-year basis to 83.88 lakh units

items.statement: SIAM expects positive growth momentum to continue in H2 FY27 supported by festive demand, new launches, infrastructure development, fleet replacement and last mile mobility
items.quote: SIAM expects the positive growth momentum to continue in the second half of financial year '27 as well, which will be primarily supported by festive demand, new vehicle launches, infrastructure development, fleet replacement and increasing demand for last mile mobility.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin declined to 39.8% in Q2 FY27 and 40.7% in H1 FY27 from 45.6% and 45.4% respectively due to elevated raw material costs and higher tooling/battery revenue mix
items.quote: However, gross margins stood at 39.8% in quarter 2 and 40.7% in the 6 months period compared with 45.6% and 45.4%, respectively, in the corresponding periods last year. The moderation in gross margins was primarily attributable to elevated raw material costs and a higher contribution from tooling and battery businesses to the overall revenue mix.

items.statement: 68% of gross margin reduction from raw material price increases already recovered from customers; balance expected to settle in H2 FY27
items.quote: So out of that, 68% we have already recovered from the customer and balance is in process because when we have the price increases, with that kind of price increases, so our first priority is that we need to uninterrupted supplies to our customer.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 8.8% in Q2 FY27 and 8.4% in H1 FY27 despite gross margin pressure
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased by 23% year-on-year to INR15.7 crores in quarter 2, while in the first 6 months, EBITDA grew by 27.4% year-on-year to INR28.1 crores. EBITDA margin stood at 8.8% in quarter 2 and 8.4% in H1 financial year '27, reflecting a sequential improvement in operating performance.

items.statement: Secured lifetime order wins of INR300 crores in Q2 FY27, taking cumulative H1 FY27 order wins to INR429 crores
items.quote: We secured lifetime order wins of approximately INR300 crores in quarter 2 financial year '27, taking our cumulative H1 financial year '27 order wins to INR429 crores.

items.statement: EV-related order wins increased to INR156.5 crores in H1 FY27 from INR27 crores in H1 FY26, nearly 6x growth
items.quote: Particularly encouraging has been the substantial growth in EV-related order wins, which increased to INR156.5 crores in H1 financial year '25 from approximately INR27 crores in H1 financial year '26, representing a nearly 6x growth in the new orders received.

items.statement: Tooling business secured orders for 50 new molds in Q2 FY27, total mold order book at 196 molds valued at INR40 crores
items.quote: During the second quarter of this financial year, we secured orders for 50 new molds, taking our total mold order book to 196 molds valued at approximately INR40 crores.

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved to ~78% in Q2 FY27 from 73% in Q1 FY27 and 68% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Capacity utilization also improved significantly to approximately 78% in quarter 2 compared with 73% in quarter 1 of financial year '27 and 68% in quarter 2 of financial year '26.

items.statement: Tooling capacity utilization at 86% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Capacity utilization stood at 86% during the quarter, while revenue from our Meraki tooling business grew by approximately 60% year-on-year to INR8.3 crores, reflecting strong business momentum.

items.statement: Battery plant capacity utilization improved to ~15% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Plant capacity utilization also improved to about 15%.

items.statement: OEM pricing and cost pass-through mechanism has inherent time lag; pending price revisions expected to be approved and cost recoveries realized progressively
items.quote: The OEM pricing and cost pass-through mechanism involves an inherent time lag in recovering increased input cost. We expect the pressure on margins to ease progressively as pending price revisions are approved and the corresponding cost recoveries are realized.

items.statement: Raw material price fluctuations continue daily due to Western disturbance and crude oil prices; 68% of price increases recovered, balance expected to settle in H2 FY27
items.quote: If you there are -- still because of the Western disturbance, there are a lot of fluctuation in the raw material prices is still there. Daily, there is changes in the raw material prices and the base crude oil prices. So it is continuing. So as of now, it is very difficult to give any numbers on the EBITDA margin improvement, but we are sure that there would be significant improvement in the margi

items.statement: Higher contribution from tooling and battery businesses to revenue mix mechanically diluted gross margin percentage despite full cost recovery
items.quote: It is important to note that the pass-through of increased raw material costs to customers results in a corresponding increase in reported revenue without a proportionate increase in gross profit. Consequently, this leads to a mechanical dilution in the gross margin percentage even when the underlying cost increase is fully recovered.

items.statement: Developing ~400 new SKUs expected to enter production over next 12 months strengthening product portfolio
items.quote: In parallel, we are developing approximately 400 new SKUs, which are expected to enter production over the next 12 months, further strengthening our product portfolio and growth opportunities.

items.statement: New customer wins include JSW (standalone and MG Motors), VinFast; engaging with Volkswagen as JSW-VW partnership progresses; strong presence on new Tata Motors platforms
items.quote: JSW, we've already received business. MG -- see, JSW has 2 relationships in India and the third one is getting under progress now with the Volkswagen. For their stand-alone company, JSW independent company, we have orders. For JSW MG Motors also, we've received new orders for this Windsor vehicle, which is there. Volkswagen, we don't know yet. They have not announced any platform together with JSW

items.statement: Aftermarket distribution network at 154 distributors; plan to add 2 regional warehouses (West and South) by Q4 FY27, East next year
items.quote: Distribution network we have set up is both offline distribution network through these distributors, and we are strengthening our online presence also through our own website, through Amazons and Flipkarts and we are exploring further opportunities where we can expand our online presence and drive more business from those things. Distribution side, we currently have one warehouse, which is located

items.statement: Battery business faces competitive environment with cell price volatility, cell quality consistency issues, market pricing pressures and shorter customer delivery timelines
items.quote: The business continues to navigate a competitive environment with volatility in cell prices, consistency of cell quality from suppliers, market pricing pressures and shorter customer delivery time lines posing as key challenges.

items.statement: Exports from Industrial Products to US (sealing systems for air handling units) and Africa (body sealing for diesel gensets); automotive parts CKD exports ~10% of revenue; aftermarket and industrial products key export focus areas
items.quote: Industrial Products also, we have done -- started exports to U.S., again, for a sealing system solution for a U.S. customer. And we've done some exports to the African market also for, again, a sealing system application, for a body sealing application for diesel gensets. When you talk about exports for the entire group, so Industrial Products business is one area where we are focused on export ma

items.statement: Net finance costs declined ~28% to INR6.12 crores in H1 FY27 from INR8.5 crores in H1 FY26 due to treasury income from JV stake divestment proceeds invested in short-term funds
items.quote: The treasury income generated from these investments contributed to a reduction of approximately 28% in consolidated net finance costs to INR6.12 crores in the first 6 months compared with INR8.5 crores in the first half of previous financial year.

items.statement: Proceeds from JV stake divestment prudently invested in short-term funds pending strategic deployment
items.quote: The proceeds from the divestment of our stake in the joint venture have been prudently invested in short-term funds pending their strategic deployment.

items.statement: Meraki tooling slump sale to 100% subsidiary Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited expected completed by end Q3 FY27 subject to approvals
items.quote: As communicated earlier, we have been working towards creating a more focused operating structure for the tooling business under a 100% owned subsidiary of PPAP, which is called as Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited. This initiative is aimed at improving operational flexibility, strengthening the customers' engagement and creating a very clear and dedicated platform for future growth in the

items.statement: New program contribution to revenue expected to grow from 10% in H1 FY27 to 15% in H2 FY27 driven by ramp-up of Maruti and Tata Motors programs and new SOPs in Q3/Q4
items.quote: And around 10% of the top line is contributed from the new orders, from the SOPs, which we have at the start of the year or the Q4 of FY26. Same way in H2 also, the key assumption that there's a ramp-up of programs, which started at the start of the year, and certain SOPs are also lined up in Q4 and Q3. So that contribution we are expecting to grow from 10% to 15% in H2.

items.statement: Raw material price movements and geopolitical uncertainties remain important factors to monitor; inflationary pressures, interest rate hikes and geopolitical uncertainties may pose challenges
items.quote: While raw material price movements and geopolitical uncertainties remain important factors to monitor, we remain focused on operational excellence, cost optimization and sustained margin improvement.

items.statement: Order book reached lifetime high of INR 20,207 crore at end of H1 FY2027 with H1 order intake of INR 5,200 crore
items.quote: Our order book reaches a lifetime high of INR 20,207 crore at the end of H1 FY2027, supported by order intake of INR 5,200 crore during the first half.

items.statement: Medium-term objectives reiterated: revenue CAGR 15%-20%, EBITDA margin 13%-15%, ROCE above 20%, ROE above 15%, O&M progressing to 20% of revenue, sustained positive net cash
items.quote: We reiterate our medium-term objectives: revenue CAGR of 15%-20%, EBITDA in the 13%-15% band, ROCE above 20%, ROE above 15%, and O&M progressing to 20% of revenue, and a sustained positive net cash position.

items.statement: H1 FY2027 consolidated EBITDA margin at 13.8%, PAT margin expanded to 10.3% from 9.6% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA grew by about 21% to INR261 crores at a margin of almost 14%. PAT grew faster, up by almost 30% to INR195 crores, and PAT margin expanded to 10.3% as against 9.6% in the same period last year.

items.statement: H1 FY2027 consolidated operating cash flow INR 225 crore, over 1.1x PAT; net working capital improved to 101 days from 104 days
items.quote: Consolidated operating cash flow for H1 was INR 225 crores, over 1.1x our PAT for the same period. Net working capital also improved to 101 days from 104 days as of March 2026.

items.statement: Net cash excluding HAM reached all-time high of over INR 1,100 crore vs INR 950 crore end FY2026; including HAM net cash INR 1,036 crore; 15th consecutive quarter positive net cash
items.quote: Net cash excluding HAM reached an all-time high of over INR 1,100 crores as compared to INR 950 crores at the end of FY2026. Including HAM, net cash stood at INR 1,036 crores.

items.statement: O&M order backlog at historic high of INR 6,500 crore, building steadily towards 20% revenue objective
items.quote: O&M is building steadily towards the 20% objective on the back of a historic high order backlog in O&M of INR 6,500 crores.

items.statement: Strong order pipeline across geographies; next 12-18 months expected to be bumper order intake; peak bidding activities with large ticket inquiries in Europe, Middle East, India
items.quote: We are very hopeful the next 12-18 months is going to be a bumper order intake for us. We are just trying to establish that we reach a preferred bidder status.

items.statement: Contracts have commodity price pass-through formulas; international orders hedged within few months; major equipment orders placed early to lock commodity prices
items.quote: Most of the Indian contracts, we go with the escalation formula. Internationally, we immediately hedge. As we get our order, within a few months, we also place some of the major orders so that future commodity price is fixed, is locked.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance given; focus on asset-light model, efficient capital deployment, and disciplined execution
items.quote: We remain focused, technology-led growth, disciplined execution, and efficient capital deployment, while selectively pursuing opportunities in desalination, reuse, and digitalization and resource recovery areas.

items.statement: Chennai Metro 400 MLD Perur desalination plant 90% concreting done, 1 lakh cubic meter poured, 7 million safe man-hours; Al Haer STP civil works 80-85% complete, mechanical erection started
items.quote: We have done about 90% concreting, poured overall almost 1 lakh cubic meter of concreting. We also clocked 7 million safe man-hours on the project.

items.statement: Secured mega orders from Kuwait Ministry (60 MIGD desalination with 5-year O&M), Reliance Industries (201 MLD desalination expandable to 302 MLD + 72 MLD remineralization), Adani (O&M contract), Ajman UAE wastewater project
items.quote: During H1, we signed and commenced the contract with the Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy, Kuwait in partnership with HEISCO for a 60 MIGD or approximately 272 million liters per day of seawater reverse osmosis desalination facility.

items.statement: International revenue 54% of H1 FY2027, India 46%; Middle East ~60-70% of international order book, Chennai ~15-20% of EPC order book
items.quote: The revenue mix remained in line with our strategic targets, international markets contributing 54% of H1 revenue and India 46%.

items.statement: Middle East geopolitical situation causing shipment delays; mitigating via longer shipping routes and air freight for critical components; project sites unaffected; monitoring closely for next 3-6 months
items.quote: What we are facing, other than the commodity price pressures, is a huge delay in shipments. This is something we have taken it to the client, and they have recognized the issue and told us to go ahead with taking a longer route.

items.statement: Succession planning ongoing with homegrown and lateral talent; knowledge management software being enhanced with AI platforms; promoter's son Rohan Mittal handling Middle East/GCC/Africa for 9 years
