items.quote: We have been always talking about this succession planning, and I think not only our HR, but our top management is very focused on it. Some of the actions are already taken. We are grooming some people, we are taking some lateral entrant.

items.statement: EPC 82% and O&M 18% of H1 revenue; targeting O&M to reach 20% of revenue; EP orders targeted at 20-30% of order intake (Kuwait and Reliance orders are EP model)
items.quote: By business, EPC accounted for 82% and O&M for 18%. O&M adds a high-margin, asset-light, recurring revenue stream alongside our EPC execution pipeline, and we remain focused on building this business out for the future.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 20.5% in H1 FY2027 from 19.5% in March 2026; ROE improved to 16.3% from 15.7%
items.quote: Return on equity improved to 16.3% in H1 as against 15.7% in March 2026, and return on capital employed improved from 19.5% in March 2026 to 20.5% in H1 FY2027.

items.statement: Wage Code changes impacting employee costs (PF, gratuity) fully reflected from Q2; no one-off impact
items.quote: This is in line because we give the increments in this quarter. So with the performance and also the Wage Code change impact also you would see in full stead now, whether it is PF, whether it is gratuity, all of those.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet and net cash position provide competitive advantage in PPP model projects; engaging with developers (ACWA, BESIX, sovereign entities) as EPC partner with local presence advantage
items.quote: We certainly play a very vital and a very important role in this. We are keeping a watch on the PPP model, and not necessarily we are not participating. We are also discussing and engaging with the developers.

items.statement: Sunrise sectors (semiconductors, data centers, solar PV, green hydrogen) showing traction; modular smaller ticket orders (12-15 month gestation); specialized team formed; water-cooled solutions for data centers gaining traction
items.quote: These are the new sectors which we are focused, and we have a separate team and a vertical which are focusing on it because they are comparatively smaller ticket size orders. So we need to have a specialized team who focuses on it and also executes this order.

items.statement: Bangladesh project (World Bank funded) engineering ~complete, ordering 90% done, 30-40% material dispatched, civil works 30-40%; ~6 month delay due to political disturbances but payments on time
items.quote: Engineering is more or less complete. Ordering is also 90% done. About 30% to 40% of the material is dispatched, and civil works are also at about 30% to 40%. So the project is moving.

items.statement: Indosol Solar project land acquisition progressing (900 of 1000 acres secured); 1 GW plant near commissioning; multi-GW project to follow once balance land acquired
items.quote: I think out of 1,000 acres, they have already secured 900 acres, another 100 acres which they should get pretty fast. So one would expect that in a quarter from now, they should be able to get this balance 100, and then they will kickstart the mega project.

items.statement: Net working capital improved to 101 days from 104 days as of March 2026; focus on efficient working capital management continues
items.quote: Net working capital also improved to 101 days from 104 days as of March 2026.

items.statement: No specific dividend or buyback announcement; focus on sustained positive net cash position and capital efficiency
items.quote: Our priorities remain disciplined execution, healthy margins, efficient working capital management, and robust cash generation.

items.statement: Signed exclusive licensing and global designated supplier agreements for Forever 21 and Dockers in South Asia; export revenue yet to build
items.quote: During the quarter, the company strengthened its international brand portfolio by entering into licensing and global designated supplier agreements with Forever 21, IPCO LLC, a subsidiary of Authentic Brands Group for Forever 21 for India, Nepal and Bangladesh.

items.statement: Improvement in demand trends; encouraging response to Dussehra and Diwali sales supporting seasonal growth expectations
items.quote: During this quarter, we witnessed an improvement in demand trends and entered the festive season with a well-planned inventory position. Post this in the more recent quarter, the responses to our Dussehra and Diwali sales have been very encouraging, providing a positive start of the festive period and supporting our expectations of seasonal demand growth.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 39% YoY to INR79 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: For the second quarter of the financial year 2027 revenue from operations grew 39% year-on-year to INR79 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 13.31% in Q2 FY27, down from prior year due to festive season timing shift
items.quote: EBITDA stood at around INR11 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 24% with EBITDA margin of 13.31%.

items.statement: PAT grew 34% YoY to INR6 crores in Q2 FY27 with PAT margin 7.98%
items.quote: Profit after tax stood at approximately INR6 crores, growing 34% year-on-year while PAT margin came in at 7.98%.

items.statement: Men's apparel 76%, women's 17%, women's accessories 5% of H1 FY27 revenue; women's wear growing strongly
items.quote: Within our product portfolio, men's apparel contributed 76% of the H1 FY27 revenue while women's accounted for 17% and women's accessories contributed about 5%. The women's wear segment continues to witness strong growth extending its contribution to the overall portfolio and supporting greater category diversification for us.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 31% YoY to INR145 crores; EBITDA grew 31% to INR19 crores at 13.13% margin
items.quote: Moving to our performance for the first half of financial year 2027, revenue from operations grew 31% year-on-year to INR145 crores, EBITDA increased 31% year-on-year to INR19 crores with EBITDA margin at 13.13%.

items.statement: Own brand Thomas Scott revenue INR28 crores in Q2 FY27, up 28% YoY; licensed brands INR49 crores, up 52% YoY; contract manufacturing down 29% to INR2 crores
items.quote: Thomas Scott, our own brand recorded revenue of INR28 crores, up 28% Y-o-Y driven by increasing brand acceptance, an online first approach, rapid product launches. And also, an increase in the amount of inventory that we push to distribution models especially to online distributors and aggregators. Licensed and other brands delivered INR49 crores, up about 52% Y-o-Y, supported by strong marketplac

items.statement: Fulfilment cost per unit declined from INR24 in FY24 to INR18 in H1 FY27, a 25% reduction
items.quote: Further operational efficiency has continued to improve with our fulfilment cost per unit decline declining from INR24 per unit in FY24 to INR18 per unit in H1 FY27, representing a reduction of about 25%.

items.statement: Spent INR6.4 crores net on capex in H1 FY27, mainly for Bhiwandi and Gurgaon warehouses and Solapur manufacturing extensions; minimal tech capex
items.quote: So, net-net I think we've spent close to about INR6.4 crores in the last quarter net, on a net basis on capital expenditure in the last half year, out of which, as I said, majority of it has gone into our warehousing facility and natural extensions to the Solapur facility.

items.statement: Funding through internal accruals, working capital improvements, and term loans matching asset gestation; no immediate equity plans
items.quote: No. So, at the moment, we are sufficiently funded with our current sources. We are looking at certain working capital improvements over a period of time, and debt as and when required from a working capital standpoint only. Some of our future infrastructure requirements would be met through say term loans, which match the gestation period of those expansion plans.

items.statement: Purchases from Bang Overseas/Vedanta Creations at ~70% currently, targeting 30-40% in a year; sales to them to cease by FY28; INR100 crore approval was blanket compliance, not planned utilization
items.quote: Right. So currently about on a real-time basis, it's closer to about 70% that we are purchasing. This percentage has been going down over the period of time. We believe a year out, this will be as low as 30% to 40% on the purchase side and same would be absolutely zero.

items.statement: Export revenue initiated via global designated supplier model using same inventory; Q3 FY27 saw good export quantities with better margins than India business
items.quote: We have made good quantities of export sale in this particular Q3 quarter, which is not yet reported. So along with that, there are also learnings in terms of how to work out this business. So, as they settle in, essentially, we'll figure out what is the right path to scaling it. Definitely so far, our margin profile has been better than the India business and we are hoping we can find the right k

items.statement: Targeting high double-digit growth rate similar to past years; no specific FY27/FY28 revenue guidance given
items.quote: Generally speaking, we are targeting a very similar growth rate that we have exhibited over the last few years, which is high double-digit growth rates, and we want to continue on this path.

items.statement: Own brand Thomas Scott sales diversified across Myntra, Amazon, AJIO, own website (~four-way split); licensed brands focused on Myntra/Flipkart
items.quote: In terms of own brand portfolio, which is our own brand Thomas Scott, we are seeing a higher percentage shift towards channels like Amazon and AJIO. While Myntra has retained its pole position, the other two are also very close, so it is almost a four-way split in terms of overall revenue between our sales on AJIO, Amazon, Myntra, and our own website.

items.statement: Own brands compete with Snitch, The Souled Store, Bewakoof, Campus Sutra; licensed brands compete with Rare Rabbit, U.S. Polo Assn.
items.quote: We have certain brands that compete with the likes of the likes of Snitch, the likes of The Souled Store, the likes of Bewakoof, the likes of Campus Sutra. These are largely online first brands that a part of our portfolio competes with. The other part of our portfolio which includes international brands largely competes with other international or premium brands. Some of these brands could be the

items.statement: Dockers expected to improve licensed portfolio margin profile; Forever 21 margin similar but higher sell-through; both expected to deliver similar or better ROCE
items.quote: Yes, it is likely that a brand like Dockers would improve the overall margin profile. In the case of Forever 21, the margin profile is largely like-for-like, but we are expecting a higher sell-through rate in terms of the inventory investments that we make. Largely both brands are expected to make a similar or better return on capital employed than our current investments in inventory.

items.statement: Gurgaon warehouse partially operational, largest to date; Solapur manufacturing capacity extended naturally; no major automation capex
items.quote: We have invested over the last 6 months in two warehouses, one in Bhiwandi and one in Gurgaon. So, we're opening, and we have actually opened, a quite large warehouse in Gurgaon. It is yet to be fully operational. It is partially operational right now, but this is our largest warehouse, till date that we -- that would that it would be once fully operational.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 margins not comparable YoY due to Dussehra shifting to Q3; festive revenue moved to Q3
items.quote: So, I think Dussehra was on 3rd October last year. This year most of the Dussehra sale, which is one of our bigger sales, was in almost entirely in October. So, there is some seasonal variation and this is essentially one -- and we were sitting on inventory for Dussehra at the end of this period, right? So, since the cut off is 30th September, there was not any Dussehra sale this quarter -- this y

items.statement: Targets 15-20% year-on-year revenue growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: See -- I mean, we project to be -- our target is to grow anything between 15% to 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 14-15% with potential upside from Lost Foam Casting ramp-up
items.quote: Margin, we -- I mean, number one is our target is to maintain the same healthy margin of roughly 14% to 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: Expects exports to contribute 10-15% of sales in next 3-5 years
items.quote: And that -- I mean, we -- what we expect in next 3 to 5 years, exports should contribute minimum 10% to 15% of our sales.

items.statement: Subsidiary secured INR12 crore per annum export order from Italian precision engineering manufacturer with potential to grow to INR40-50 crore in 3 years
items.quote: Our subsidiary, Pritika Engineering Components Limited, has secured a high-value export order of approximately INR12 crores per annum from a prominent precision engineering manufacturer based in Italy.

items.statement: KION USA product approved, regular production expected to commence in FY27-28
items.quote: We are pleased to inform you that the product has now received customer approval, and regular production is expected to commence in FY27-'28.

items.statement: Current installed capacity 72,000 metric tons per annum; targeting 1 lakh metric tons by end of 2028
items.quote: We continue to work towards our long-term target of achieving installed capacity of 1 lakh metric tons by year 2028.

items.statement: Adding 7,800 tons capacity at Pritika Engineering by end of current month; another 24,000 tons via greenfield by March 2028
items.quote: We plan to add another 24,000 tons by, say, March 2028. For that, which we are, I mean, in process of acquiring a land.

items.statement: Green sand capacity utilization at ~90%; Lost Foam Casting at ~50%
items.quote: See, capacity utilization, as far as we are concerned today, for our green sand, we are working almost at 90% capacity. And for our LFC, we are yet at 50% capacity.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 13.85% vs 15.99% YoY; sequential improvement from 13.45% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27 stood at 13.85% compared to 15.99% in Q2 FY26. While margins continue to be impacted by elevated input costs and the evolving product mix, we have seen an improvement on a sequential basis with EBITDA margin increasing from 13.45% in Q1 FY27 to 13.85% in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Raw material cost volatility (scrap and pig iron) impacted Q2 margins; pass-through period is one quarter
items.quote: This is 1 quarter -- quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Major raw materials are scrap and pig iron; Q2 saw significant price increases
items.quote: Our raw material is scrap. Scrap is our -- and pig iron are our major raw materials. Pig iron and scrap are our major raw materials.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 production volume 15,665 metric tons, up 22% YoY; H1 FY27 30,000 metric tons, up 19% YoY
items.quote: Our production volume for Q2 FY27 stood at 15,665 metric tons compared to 12,881 metric tons in the corresponding quarter last year, registering a growth of approximately 22%.

items.statement: Tractor demand supported by agriculture mechanization, government initiatives, rural demand; CV segment ~7% of business with growth opportunity
items.quote: Demand for tractor continues to be supported by agriculture mechanization, government initiatives and underlying rural demand. At the same time, infrastructure development and increasing requirements in the commercial vehicle segment provide opportunities for the broader casting industry.

items.statement: Long-standing relationships with M&M (22+ years), Escorts (50+ years), TAFE (28 years); receiving repeat and incremental business
items.quote: With M&M, it is almost 22 years, more than 22 years. With Escorts, it's almost 50 -- more than 50 years. With TAFE, it is 28 years. So we are having a very, very strong relation with our customers.

items.statement: Diversifying into construction equipment (ACE, KION India) and railways (RDSO trials by Jan-Feb, supply from H2 FY28)
items.quote: We are already going to -- giving to ACE, then we have added -- recently added KION India. And then, we are adding -- there are a few more new customers with which we are under discussion to add construction and material handling equipment to our portfolio.

items.statement: Shifting from small/medium to large castings using Lost Foam Casting technology; developed 530 kg SG iron casting previously imported from China
items.quote: Since recently around 3 years back, we added a new technology, Lost Foam Casting. So that has given us a lot of advantage in large castings and some critical castings, I mean, which are still being imported from China.

items.statement: Solar power MoU with Spark Grid for 25-year supply; expected INR110 crore group savings (INR70 crore for PEC & Meeta Castings, balance for PAIL)
items.quote: In August 2026, Pritika Engineering Components Limited on behalf of Pritika Group signed a memorandum of understanding with Spark Grid Private Limited for supply of solar power at a competitive tariff period for over 25 years. This arrangement is expected to generate savings of approximately INR110 crores for the group over the tenure of the agreement.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity 0.67 in FY26; expected to increase with expansion funded by mix of debt and equity
items.quote: It will most probably be a combination of debt and equity. Debt position is comfortable, debt-equity will be comfortable. So some -- I mean, major part would be debt only and some part would be equity.

items.statement: Interest expense increased to INR6.33 crore in Q2 FY27 from INR5.60 crore YoY; management says percentage-wise same as before
items.quote: You are saying that interest has increased. But percentage-wise, it is same, Vikrant. Percent wise, it is roughly around the same percentage what it was in the last quarter, and it has -- from 25%, it has reduced. It has reduced as a percentage. Yes, it is in line with the growth only.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR153.19 crore (+31.55% YoY); EBITDA INR21.21 crore (+13.97% YoY); PAT INR7.43 crore (+12.41% YoY)
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the company reported net revenue from operations of INR153.19 crores compared to INR116.45 crores in Q2 FY26, registering a year-on-year growth of 31.55%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR298.16 crore (+29.04% YoY); EBITDA INR40.72 crore (+12.93% YoY); PAT INR14.55 crore (+14.52% YoY)
items.quote: Consolidated net revenue from operations for H1 FY27 stood at INR 298.16 crores compared to INR 231.06 crores in H1 FY26, representing a growth of 29.04%.

items.statement: Mechanizing foundry operations (fettling automation) and adding robotics/gantry in machine shop to reduce manpower cost
items.quote: We have now started the mechanization of -- in our foundry also, and fettling was -- is one of the bottleneck areas, and we are procuring some machines for fettling automation. That is one. Then secondly, in machine shop, we are going for robotics, and gantry, wherever it is possible, wherever it is high volume, we are going from -- we are going for robotics and gantry application to reduce the ma

items.statement: Tractor industry seasonal (7-8 month selling season); Q3 typically lower due to planned maintenance in December
items.quote: Q3 -- I mean, as of now, I mean, normally, Q3 for us is -- for tractor industry for India, and general industry also, is, I mean, lower than Q2 sale wise because all planned maintenance is taken in December and all -- after Diwali, sales of all -- I mean, all productions drop in India whether it is commercial vehicle, whether it is passenger vehicles, 2-wheelers or tractors.

items.statement: Subsidiary Pritika Engineering Components currently ~23% of capacity; expected to grow to 30-35% in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: See, at present, if we say it is almost -- if we see capacity-wise, it is almost -- I mean, if I say subsidiary, Pritika Engineering is roughly -- at present capacity is roughly 23%, 25% -- 23%. It is -- we are expected to grow -- Engineering should grow to around 30%, 35% in coming 1, 1.5 years.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance upward to INR720 crores plus from INR700 crores
items.quote: Given the strong business momentum and an accelerating pace of product registration, we have further revised our FY27 revenue guidance upwards to INR720 crores plus.

items.statement: FY28 revenue expected between INR950 crore and INR1,000 crore plus, potentially crossing INR1,000 crore with more registrations
items.value: INR950 crore-INR1,000 crores or INR1,000 crores plus
items.quote: We do believe that FY28, we can close anywhere between INR950 crore-INR1,000 crores or INR1,000 crores plus also.

items.statement: FY27 revenue achievable target between INR720 crores and INR750 crores, kept conservative due to KPMG standards and holiday season
items.quote: Sir, INR720 crores is a conservative figure. We believe that around INR750 crores is an achievable target.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 27.5%, PAT doubled to INR29 crores
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, our consolidated revenue grew by 63% year-on-year to INR181 crores compared to INR111 crores in the corresponding quarter last year. EBITDA margin expanded to 27.5%, while profit after tax doubled to INR29 crores, reflecting improved operating leverage and a strong product mix.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 27%-28% sustainable at INR720-750 crore revenue; 29%-30% achievable at INR1,000 crore plus revenue
items.quote: No, sir, these margins are 28%, 27%-28% is very much achievable. 29%-30% margins would be achievable if the sales revenues are with the same operating cost, the sales revenue crosses INR1,000 crores plus.

items.statement: Partner export margins 24%-26% EBITDA; own registration margins 28%-32% EBITDA
items.quote: When partners are exporting, the margins are between 24%-26% EBITDA. When we have our own registration, the EBITDA margins are between 28%-32%.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to improve to 54%-55% (cost 44%-46%) with R&D increase from Q1 FY28
items.quote: Yeah, there will be increase in the gross margins, probably to 44% or 46%. Sorry, the gross cost will come down to 44%, 46%, and the margins will increase to 54%, 55%.

items.statement: 19 BE studies completed, 19 dossiers ready for global filing; 7-8 molecules to commercialize in FY28, 12-13 more by FY29
items.quote: Ma'am, in FY28, probably the first round of seven to eight molecules would be easily commercialized, specifically in the South Asian and the Latin market. I think INR80 crore-INR90 crores could be the number we would be able to achieve from the first seven products. But the entire increased number you could see in FY29. That number could cross around to INR300 crores mark also.

items.statement: Cephalosporin facility EU-GMP certified; registrations expected Mexico Q4 FY27, Brazil and Europe Q2 FY28
items.quote: We have already filed for registration in all these three markets. The Mexico, which is the least profitable one, in case of cephalosporin, we would be getting registration in Q4 of FY27, the Brazilian by Q2 of FY28, and probably at the same time, we'll get for the European market as well.

items.statement: Hormone facility targeting PIC/S and ROW audits by FY28, potential INR100-150 crore sales in FY28, INR200 crore by FY29-30
items.quote: Basically, sir, the idea is that by next year, we should be able to get the PIC/S audit done and ROW five or six countries audits done, and immediately commercialize at least in the, you can say, the Islamic countries wherein a fast-track permit could be generated, and we could make at least INR100 crores or INR150 crores sales.

items.statement: Biologics: Erythropoietin biowaiver commercialization started, INR25-30 crore FY27, INR30-40 crore FY28, INR80-100 crore FY29; Pembrolizumab biowaiver application ready by January 2027
items.quote: This year itself, probably up till Q4 of FY27, I think INR25 crore, INR30 crores sales revenue would be easily generated from using the Biowaiver application, and that could be generated. So INR80 crore, INR90 crores in FY28 is a very conservative number. FY29, 2030, after finishing the clinical trials, we have a huge potential of this molecule.

items.statement: INR140-150 crore capex planned for FY27 nearly complete, INR20-25 crore pending by April 2027; next capex for Unit 7, BE studies, R&D facility
items.quote: As of now, INR140 crore-INR150 crores capex, which we had planned to do before completing FY27, we are almost through with it. Another INR20 crore-INR25 crores is still pending from our end. That we will probably be able to finish by at least April 2027.

items.statement: Unit 7 capex INR200-250 crore over three years (FY28-30); 200 BE studies require additional INR250-300 crore; total INR500-600 crore over three years
items.quote: I think roughly around INR200 crore-INR250 crores would be required in the new expansion of the seventh unit. Along with this, if we talk about up till FY30, if we have to do around 200 new bioequivalences, then probably another INR250 crores or INR300 crores would be required. You can see, say, around about INR500 crores or INR600 crores capex to be made in three years' time.

items.statement: Biosimilar clinical studies INR150-200 crore to be funded by external partners, not in company capex plan
items.quote: Let's say, if we have to do clinical studies of around INR150 crore-INR200 crores for three molecules, this will be entirely funded from the external partnerships what we have, and that will be an exclusivity partnership.

items.statement: Unit 7 to be built in three phases FY28-30, sufficient for 200 BE products, potential 3x-4x revenue increase, up to INR2,000-4,000 crore at full utilization
items.quote: Basically, sir, Unit 7 will be completed in three phases, in FY28, 29, and 30. This new unit, the basic idea is all the bioequivalences what we have done, we are going to commercialize from this new unit. This unit is adjacent to the existing facility. Probably we could start using the same model and everything. Basically, you can say that 200 bioequivalences, we can run across 40, then another 40

items.statement: Third shift started in oral solids and few injectable lines; full third shift needed at INR1,000-1,200 crore revenue when generics facility 80% saturated
items.quote: Sir, as of now, only in the oral solid and few lines of injectables, we have already started with the third shift. There is still not a requirement of doing the third shift. Probably once we are close to INR1,000 crores or INR1,200 crore, I think the capacity would be 80% saturated in the generics facility.

items.statement: Biologics CDMO model enabled by 27D license expected by January-February 2027; can handle 6-7 CDMO projects currently
items.quote: 27D is for allowing you to make the biological finished formulation without the drug substance part. That application we have already made. We are more or less likely to get it by December or January. The 27D audit has already completed. After 27D, we'll be able to do all the L-asparaginase, peg-asparaginase, and the CDMO products of the biological, fill to finish.

items.statement: Working capital cycle reduced to 130 days from 170 days in FY26; debtor days reduced from 208 to 178 days
items.quote: Equally encouraging in the improvement in our working capital cycle, we have reduced to 130 days from 170 days in FY26 and reduced reduction in debtor days from 208 to 178 days.

items.statement: Additional working capital INR60-80 crore needed over 2-3 years; INR50-60 crore over internal accruals
items.quote: There could be increased, another working capital of, you can say, INR60 crore, INR70 crore, or INR80 crores would be required across two or three years. Utkarsh Somaiya: You mean at INR50 crore, INR60 crores over and above internal accruals

items.statement: Capex to be funded through internal earnings and some bank loans; no equity dilution planned currently
items.quote: That would probably be financed through some amount of loan, but more or less, it will be again through the internal earnings or retained earnings of Kwality. Because we believe that the PAT margins are going to improve a lot, and we will have enough profits to be able to make those expenses.

items.statement: PAT expected INR170-180 crore at INR1,000 crore revenue; internal accruals INR150-160 crore per year for expansion
items.quote: I think, sir, the PAT margin should increase at least INR150 crore, INR160 crore. If you are looking at INR1,000 crores revenue, then probably INR170 crore, INR180 crores PAT would be achievable. Then, considering the cash flows, we could internally do year-on-year INR150 crore, INR160 crores expansion.

items.statement: No equity dilution planned currently; will consider only if cash flows fall short of expansion needs
items.quote: As of now, no, sir. As of now, there is no such plan for equity dilution. We are not going to stop. If we have made a plan, a strategy, and where we want to finish all these bioequivalences, we want to finish all the peptide-based registrations and the infrastructure of the new plant. If we believe at some point we are falling short with the cash flows or we are not having enough breathing space,

items.statement: No plans for dividend, bonus issue, or stock split; earnings to be used for expansion
items.quote: As of now, no, sir, because the entire earnings are going to be used in expansion plans. When it comes to split and those, we have not made any plan or something, nor for the dividend, nor for any bonus issue or something.

items.statement: 85% API procurement from India, 10-15% from China; Indian API prices up 4-5%, sustained by replacing low-margin products with high-price registered products
items.quote: Sir, as of now, our major procurement is from India itself. So, 85% is from India, 10%-15% is only from China. There has not been much increase in the prices of the Indian API prices, but more or less you can say 4% or 5% has been increased.

items.statement: Export prices in USD pegged to INR; currency appreciation offset by price adjustment (e.g., $0.50 at INR89-90 becomes $0.48 if USD strengthens); fully hedged
items.quote: Basically, the prices of our sales revenue or sales, the unit price, which is in USD, is also determined by INR. Let's say, if you have decided for a proposal, we have decided a $0.50 price. A $0.50 price is based on the INR89 or INR90. If there is an increase in US dollar, probably $0.48 is the number which we are going to get. This impact is not applicable on us, sir

items.statement: 63% YoY revenue growth driven by MENA (Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia) and LATAM (Mexico, Colombia) registrations; Middle East crisis impacted debtor days in Q4 FY26 but resolved
items.quote: But when it comes that what has been the major driving force in that 63%, it's entirely specifically MENA region, which is Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia. Another set of region is Mexico and Colombia. That new set of registration has been the major driving growth.

items.statement: Unregulated/non-registered product sales depleting each quarter; registered product mix improving margins
items.quote: As of now, the unregulated market and the without registration products, what Kwality was earlier supplying, that is depleting from each quarter. And that is why there are more margins and all these costs can easily be sustained.

items.statement: 20% sales via partner-owned registrations (African/unregulated markets); 80% via Kwality-owned registrations (regulated markets); own registrations growing
items.quote: Basically, sir, if you see in FY29 or 2028, if the total sales revenue model would be INR1,000 crore, 200 crores sales will still remain with the MAs which are owned by the partners, not by Kwality. But INR800 crores sale would be entirely from the Kwality's MA registration.

items.statement: Biologics commercialization subject to clinical trials, regulatory approvals, partner capabilities; erythropoietin INR800-1,000 crore potential conservative but subject to external factors
items.quote: But again, this is subject to a lot of factors, whether the regulatory team or whether the partners are able to get the registration done. There are a lot of factors that come into play. If we are able to get it done, then this number could be INR900 crores or INR1,000 crore. But again, that is subject to a lot of external forces and things.

items.statement: BE study revenue potential: INR20-30 crore per study from 20-30 countries; 200 studies could yield INR2,000-4,000 crore
items.quote: Every BE study could generate a revenue of at least INR20 crore-INR30 crores from 20-30 countries. A very, very conservative number, INR20 crore-INR30 crores from one BE study. When we do 200, you can make the multiplication. This facility is suffice for 200 BE studies. This number could be more than INR2,000 crore, INR3,000 crores also, INR4,000 crore.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 Matchmaking revenue expected to post double-digit year-on-year growth; billing expected to reach single-digit year-on-year growth due to Shradh and Navratri period shift
items.quote: On the billing and revenue outlook for quarter three, Matchmaking revenue on a year-on-year basis is expected to post a double-digit growth in quarter three. Matchmaking billing are expected to reach a single-digit year-on-year growth in quarter three, reflecting impact of the Shradh and Navratri period falling in quarter three of this year compared to the quarter two of last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 consolidated PAT expected to achieve triple-digit year-on-year growth; profit may be similar to Q1 or slightly less than Q2 FY27
items.quote: On the outlook of Q3 margins, we expect to achieve a triple-digit year-on-year growth in PAT. Profit may be similar level of Q1 or slightly less than Q2 of current year.

items.statement: Management expects margins to continue improving with growth, targeting 25% then 30% EBITDA margin over time
items.quote: Margin with the growth, sir, the growth in the billing and revenue in the coming year, it will only grow only. It is not the rate. When the growth happens, the margin will continue to get better. Now we are reached 20 plus percentage. You want to take it to 25%, then 30%. I think that is the level of growth we will be aspiring for.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 paid subscriptions added 3.02 lakh, up 26.6% year-on-year and 11.2% quarter-on-quarter; ATV declined 12.2% year-on-year and 13.3% quarter-on-quarter due to shorter duration packages
items.quote: Added 3.02 lakh paid subscription during the quarter, which is a growth of 26.6% year-on-year and 11.2% quarter-on-quarter. ATV for the Matchmaking is declined by 12.2% year-on-year and 13.3% quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Introduced one-month subscription packages for specific user cohorts to increase conversions without affecting revenue from longer-duration users
items.quote: Basically, we introduced a shorter duration package, a one-month package, to a certain cohort of customers. So first of all, it's not to all the users and not at the same time frame. It's based on the analysis, based on the user and their spending capacity.

items.statement: Launched regional versions of Luv.com: Premam in Kerala, Priyam in Tamil Nadu, Premalu in Andhra Pradesh; early traction encouraging, plans to extend to other regional languages
items.quote: During the quarter, we also launched the regional versions of Luv.com, that is our serious matchmaking initiative. The brand names are Premam in Kerala, Priyam in Tamil Nadu, Premalu in Andhra Pradesh. These offerings are still at an early stage, and the initial traction has been very encouraging.

items.statement: Secured government approval for voluntary Aadhaar authentication for matchmaking platform; only matrimony company approved by Government of India for Aadhaar-based verification
items.quote: Another significant milestone during the quarter was securing the government approval for voluntary Aadhaar authentication for our matchmaking platform. At this point, we are the only matrimony company approved by the Government of India to get the Aadhaar-based verification of members.

items.statement: Marketing spend for Matchmaking expected to remain at similar level (~INR45 cr per quarter); no substantial increase anticipated
items.quote: In terms of the margins, in terms of marketing spend, so marketing spend will be at a similar level at this point of time. We don't think any substantial increase in the matchmaking marketing.

items.statement: Share buyback cooling period not yet over (one year completes next year); Board will decide on future buybacks or special dividends after that
items.quote: Share buyback, I think we are still one year is not over, and after one year over, board will decide what to do in order to say. Gunit Singh: Got it, sir. Thank you very much. Murugavel Janakiraman: One year is over only yearly next year only. I think Board will decide

items.statement: CFO position not yet finalized; search ongoing
items.quote: In terms of that CFO thing, Yes, we are not yet finalized. So, that is on the CFO side.

items.statement: Return on capital employed at 39.8% annualized in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Return on capital employed is at 39.8% annualized.

items.statement: Management will provide revenue guidance after Q3 results, not now
items.quote: I would like to give revenue guidance maybe when we do our call for Q3 and see how this main season quarter goes, especially in the wine category.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance for FY27 maintained at 77-80% range
items.quote: our gross margin guidance, which has been between 77% to 80%, remains intact.

items.statement: Net profitability expected from Q1 or Q2 FY28
items.quote: we expect net profitability to come in from either Q1 or Q2 of next year.

items.statement: Current RTD capacity sufficient to double from present levels
items.quote: Our capacity today is more than sufficient for RTD to grow even double from where we are today.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA improved to INR1.4 crores profit from INR1 crore loss YoY
items.quote: EBITDA moved from a loss of approximately INR1 crores to a profit of INR1.4 crores for the same H1 period.

items.statement: Uttar Pradesh market down ~30% in H1 due to excise policy change; Karnataka also subdued
items.quote: UP as a market is roughly down 30% for us at an H1 basis, and that was one of the major attributors to the H1 bottles dip that we saw. Another market where we saw subdued performance was Karnataka.

items.statement: Excluding UP and Karnataka, bottle business grew ~6-7% in H1
items.quote: if you don't include Karnataka and if you don't include Uttar Pradesh, we'll be about 6%, 6% to 7% up, on the bottle side.

items.statement: RTD marketing spend expected at 8-10% of RTD sales for next 2-3 quarters; overall brand spend 5-6% of net sales
items.quote: this figure is something as I commented before as well, will be between the range of 8% to 10% for another two-three quarters as we're still just hitting a lot of markets for the first time.

items.statement: HoReCa channel ~65% of bottle revenue, retail ~35%; RTD ~97-98% retail
items.quote: Our revenue split is approximately 65:35 across both the channels, and I'm only talking about the bottles business. When you look at the RTD portfolio, it's about 97%, 98% in retail itself.

items.statement: HoReCa market share >35% in key markets (Delhi, Bangalore, West Bengal, Hyderabad), >50% in some
items.quote: we maintain a very, very healthy market share. You know, beyond 35% in most of these markets that I've mentioned. In some of them, the market share is even higher than 50%.

items.statement: Vineyard tourism project deferred; 10 acres owned for hospitality, 200 acres vineyards under long-term lease from promoter family
items.quote: the company owns that 10 acres of land which has been earmarked for the hospitality project, so that is in our possession. And that 10 acres is around almost 200 acres of vineyards, which are not owned by the company, but they are under active farming by Fratelli.

items.statement: Shotgun RTD classified as aromatized wine, no excise/regulatory risk; fortified wine risks not applicable
items.quote: So in this there is no excise or regulatory risk because we come under the category of aromatized wine. There are some risks pertaining to fortified wine as a segment. However, Fratelli doesn't make any fortified wine at all.

items.statement: India-EU FTA keeps wine duty at 150% up to EUR 2.5; no major shake-up expected, category expansion seen as positive
items.quote: Even with the FTA, the duty remains at 150% on wines up to EUR 2.5. So, we don't expect any major shake-up. Some change will be there. I think more, better-quality wines will become accessible to the market.

items.statement: VAT refund of ~INR18 crores due from Maharashtra govt; Telangana govt outstanding also large; both expected to ease cash flow
items.quote: We have the VAT refund from the Maharashtra government, there is a major backlog which we expect to ease in the next year or so. We have a fairly large outstanding from the Telangana government which we expect to receive and that will help ease our cash flow.

items.statement: DSO being vigorously followed up with opportunities to improve efficiency
items.quote: we are extremely aware, we are following up our days sales outstanding very vigorously and there are opportunities to bring efficiency there, which the company is working on.

items.statement: High bulk wine inventory being reduced; corrective measures taken, will take few quarters
items.quote: We are aware of carrying much higher inventory of bulk wine today in our system than we would like to, and we have already taken corrective measures to reduce that inventory. Of course, it will take a few quarters.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds not aimed at major debt reduction; debt-equity ratios healthy; focus on growth and cash ease
items.quote: We don't see a major reduction in debt at the moment. Temporarily some working capital utilization will drop because we'll have some funds available after this rights issue. We are not really very focused or at this point concerned about our debt levels, our debt-equity ratios are very much in line with healthy businesses.

items.statement: Rights issue of up to INR29.87 crores open till 17 Nov; promoters subscribing full entitlement and unsubscribed portion
items.quote: Fratelli is raising up to INR29.87 crores through a rights issue, which is now open and closes on the 17th of November. As promoters, we are subscribing to our entire entitlement and we'll also take up any portion that remains unsubscribed.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds for balance sheet strengthening, trade payables settlement, winery equipment/oak barrels at subsidiary, general corporate purposes
items.quote: The funds will be directed towards strengthening the company's balance sheet, settling trade payables, funding winery equipment and oak barrel requirements at our subsidiary, the operating companies, and meeting general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Operating cash flow under pressure; VAT refunds, inventory reduction, and RTD revenue growth expected to improve cash flow from mid-FY28
items.quote: We also expect to continue to grow at a good clip rate thanks to our initiative, like the RTD project, which now is in its second year and showing good results. And Fratelli is at a position where it is geared up for actually over revenues of maybe in excess of INR350 crores or INR400 crores, but today we are achieving maybe half of that.

items.statement: Distribution footprint at 32,000 touchpoints across 28 states; Shotgun in 11,000+ touchpoints
items.quote: Our distribution has now also grown to 32,000 touchpoints and Shotgun is already over 11,000 of them.

items.statement: International footprint expanded to 18 countries with 4 new markets entered in H1
items.quote: In H1, we have entered four new international markets, taking Fratelli to 18 countries.

items.statement: UP excise policy change caused 30% H1 decline; new policy effective 1 April; Q3/Q4 expected similar to prior year H2
items.quote: This year due to the change in the excise policy, we've seen a bit of a slowdown across the wine category in the state. So, H1 was slow, quarter 3 looks slightly better, but I don't see any major pressure on account of the elections because now the new policy will be applicable from 1st April.

items.statement: No interest received on delayed government VAT refunds
items.quote: We are not getting any interest.

items.statement: Promoters subscribing full rights entitlement and taking up unsubscribed portion, showing commitment
items.quote: As promoters, we are subscribing to our entire entitlement and we'll also take up any portion that remains unsubscribed. This reflects our commitment to the long-term journey of Fratelli.

items.statement: 200 acres vineyard land leased from promoter family on flat dry lease; no lease expiry risk
items.quote: Those lands are owned by the promoter family of Fratelli, because it's agricultural land and there is a setup it was a challenge for the company to own agricultural land, but it is on just a flat lease, dry lease to Fratelli and Fratelli is undertaking active farming on these lands.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance revised upward to 80% from earlier 60%
items.quote: The initial guidance given was between 30% to 40%. It was revised upward to 60%. And with the current order inflow and the expected inflow, we can look to revise it upwards to 80%.

items.statement: FY27 effective tax rate guidance of approximately 15%
items.quote: The guidance on effective tax rate will come to between 15% approximately during the entire year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be more than 45% going forward, currently at 50-55%
items.quote: To give you a number range, it should be more than 45% going forward as and when it gets stable. But you will see a current expansion even up to 50%, 55% levels as we move towards stabilization.

items.statement: Shipbuilding revenue to contribute 40% of overall revenue by FY28-29
items.quote: Going towards the future, we would project the shipbuilding revenue to contribute towards 40% of the overall revenue and the balance 60% would come from dredging and the chartering revenue.

items.statement: Current order book at ₹1,732.55 crores with pipeline exceeding ₹3,500 crores
items.quote: Our balance order book stands at approximately ₹1,732.55 crores, comprising of dredging order book of ₹ 467.75 crores, Charter and Hire order of ₹ 1,100 crores and shipbuilding order book of ₹164 crores, excluding the captive business of ₹ 275 crores in the shipbuilding.

items.statement: Order book expected to exceed ₹2,000 crores on continual basis going forward
items.quote: We believe in the next year going forward, the order book on a continual basis should be in excess of ₹2,000 crores going forward.

items.statement: ₹1,000 crores capex over 2 years, 6-7 months already executed
items.quote: This ₹1,000 crores of capex will be executed over a period of 2 years, from which we have already gone through a phase of 6 to 7 months.

items.statement: Saphale shipyard Phase 1 completion targeted by February 2027
items.quote: We are targeting completion of Phase 1 development by February '27, which is expected to unlock construction capacity.

items.statement: River Pearl 48 TSHD acquired, nearly fourfold increase in hopper capacity
items.quote: This acquisition represents a nearly fourfold increase in our hopper capacity and significantly enhances our ability to undertake large volume maintenance dredging projects.

items.statement: Maintenance dredging market at major and minor ports ~150 million cubic meters per annum
items.quote: The maintenance dredging segment volume-wise for major ports in minor ports put together is close to 150 million cubic meters per annum.

items.statement: Indian port maintenance dredging ~₹2,000 crores annually, capital dredging ~₹3,000 crores annually
items.quote: When it comes to dredging along the Indian coast, the major ports and the minor ports do a maintenance dredging of close to ₹2,000-odd crores on an annual basis and capital dredging. If averaged out, would fall within the range of ₹3,000-odd crores on an annual basis.

items.statement: Green Tug Transition Programme requires ~98 green tugs across major Indian ports
items.quote: The Government of India's Green Tug Transition Programme represents a substantial opportunity for the maritime sector with an identified requirement of approximately 98 green tugs across major Indian ports.

items.statement: Three Green Tug contracts aggregate value ~₹928 crores over 15-year tenures
items.quote: Together, these 3 contracts have an aggregate value of approximately ₹928 crores and represents an important addition to our long-term revenue portfolio.

items.statement: New Mangalore Port maintenance dredging contract ₹256.92 crores for 15.9 million cubic meters over 3 annual cycles
items.quote: The significant milestones in KMEW's history has been securing the ₹ 256.92 crores maintenance dredging contract from New Mangalore Port Authority.

items.statement: Inland Waterways Authority contract for 10 electric hybrid passenger ferries worth ₹62 crores
items.quote: One of the important achievement has been securing a contract from the Inland Waterways Authority of India for the construction of 10 electric hybrid passenger ferries with an order value of ₹ 62 crores.

items.statement: Bidding for several contracts at other major ports and defense naval establishments on West Coast
items.quote: We've already placed a bid for several contracts in other major ports and for the defense, naval establishments along the West Coast of India.

items.statement: In discussions with 3 different clients for export shipbuilding orders
items.quote: Currently, we are in discussion with 3 different clients on export orders. And we find that the clients have been assessing the yard and finding the suitability of the yard.

items.statement: ₹55 crores outflow in other current assets due to vendor advances in shipbuilding segment
items.quote: So these are the advances that have been given to the vendors in the shipbuilding segment and because the expenses to that are booked once the bill of entries are passed and the materials are received properly.

items.statement: Shipbuilding payments staged across 5-10 milestones with 10% advance via bank guarantees
items.quote: So presently, the shipbuilding segment has staged the payments. So with various stages of completion, various milestones that are certified by class or the flag authorities, the payments are tied.

items.statement: Will raise debt as needed for further asset acquisitions alongside internal accruals
items.quote: As far as debt is concerned, we are on a continual basis, making bids and shall be acquiring further larger assets. And as and when required, we will be raising debt for the same and along with the internal cash flow that we have, internal accruals that we have.

items.statement: ₹150 crores equity raised via preferential issue from institutional investors
items.quote: Another significant development has been the successful equity fundraising of ₹ 150 crores through a preferential issue supported by institutional investors such as 360 ONE PIPE Fund, Bank of India Mutual Fund and Four Lion Capital.

items.statement: ₹100 crores secondary market sale to SBI Funds Management
items.quote: Subsequently, we also engaged in a secondary market sale of ₹ 100 crores with SBI Funds Management.

items.statement: Dredging segment EBITDA margin ~50%, shipbuilding ~35-38% at EBIT level
items.quote: Even if I look at the segmental margin, shipbuilding and repairs was somewhere around 35%, 38% margins and on EBIT level and dredging was around 50%.

items.statement: River Pearl 48 revenue potential north of ₹150 crores per annum
items.quote: But the revenue generation with this particular vessel should be north of ₹ 150 crores per annum.

items.statement: Asset turnover ratio historically 1:1 to 1:1.5, expected to remain in that range
items.quote: The kind of revenue that the capex would generate in the past, we've had an asset turnover ratio of 1:1 or 1:1.5, it will remain in that range.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue ₹186.21 crores, up 89% YoY; PAT ₹84.27 crores, up 267% YoY
items.quote: During H1 FY 27, our revenue from operations stood at ₹ 186.21 crores, registering a growth of 89% compared to the corresponding period of the last year.

items.statement: Shipbuilding revenue ~₹40 crores in Q2, targeting 3-4x growth in FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: We in this present quarter have generated revenue close to ₹40-odd crores from shipbuilding. And the asset / the shipyard that we have purchased and which we are constructing right now, the numbers from the yard have already started flowing in. And we are looking to have a substantial increase in revenue from the shipbuilding segment as compared to the last year with a multiple of between 3x to 4x

items.statement: Bahrain operations paused until safety and insurance coverage assured
items.quote: Bahrain we are not looking to resume unless we are confident of the safety and security of our manpower and materials at Bahrain. Once the insurance covers the same and we find a stable situation, then we look to resume the operations there.

items.statement: Myanmar operations not prioritized as Indian contracts fully utilize assets
items.quote: For Myanmar, presently, all our assets are very well engaged in India, and there is a huge potential in all the 3 businesses that we are doing. So we are not looking to immediately move any vessel to Myanmar given the contracts that we have in hand.

items.statement: Chartering vessels at 100% utilization; dredging vessels fully utilized Oct-May post monsoons
items.quote: For the chartering business, all the vessels deployed with the ports are on a long-term basis. They are at 100% utilization. The dredging vessels during the second quarter, usually are waiting for the monsoons to complete. And right after or post monsoons in the month of October till the month of May, they are fully utilized in various parts of India.

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 to see phenomenal jump in dredging revenue; shipbuilding also substantial rise
items.quote: Thus, the third and the fourth quarter shall see a phenomenal jump in revenue from the dredging business. Shipbuilding has seen a steady growth. Current quarter saw a growth of 3x compared to Q2 last year. Revenue from shipbuilding shall also see and witnessed substantial rise in the third and the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Management targets minimum 25% revenue growth for the year and 10% same-store sales growth for Q4
items.quote: we usually tell everyone to keep a 25% revenue growth as the target for the year. But on the ground, you know that H1 was much better. Q3 as we speak, the momentum is great. And Q4, we know that the base is even stronger.

items.statement: Management confident of beating targeted revenue growth for the year
items.quote: No, we are actually very confident. We are very confident of beating the targeted revenue growth.

items.statement: PBT margins stable in Q2 after adjusting for customs duty benefit and silver/platinum gains; confident H2 PBT margins will be better than H1 and stable
items.quote: PBT margins, if you look at in Q2, it is very stable, wherein if you negate the -- of course, the onetime benefit of the customs duty and if you also negate the silver and platinum gains, which was there in the previous year quarter, Q2, you negate both that, the margins are stable.

items.statement: Exchange program at 42% overall with 7-8% gold for cash; encash program margin accretive
items.quote: So 7% to 8% is gold for cash and now the overall is 42% and that is why you see that the margins are stable in Q2.

items.statement: Demand robust with healthy same-store sales growth across key markets; Q3 started very well with excellent growth during Navratri and Dhanteras
items.quote: Demand remained robust during most part of the recently concluded quarter on the back of very healthy same-store sales growth across most of the key markets.

items.statement: Volume growth seen in Q2 and Q3 as customers buy more grams for same budget; studded share increasing organically over 4-5 years
items.quote: Yes. So volume growth, as I mentioned, we have seen volume growth in Q2 also, if you see, because the SSGs have been in the range of 20% and the gold price inflation is single digit.

items.statement: Launched ATM regional brand in T. Nagar, Chennai in August; plans for 4 more showrooms in FY27 (2 in Q3, 2 in Q4)
items.quote: We have drawn up plans for the launch of the next 4 showrooms over the course of the current financial year, 2 will be in the ongoing quarter and 2 more during the fourth quarter.

items.statement: No immediate plans to launch ATM in new state beyond Tamil Nadu; will focus on strengthening existing showrooms and flagship stores
items.quote: no more immediate plans to launch ATM in a new state. We will continue only in Tamil Nadu because it has to shape up in one state, and which will at least take a couple of years.

items.statement: Non-GML debt now debt-free; 50% collateral released with one land parcel sold for INR86-87 crores and INR16 crores pending; remaining 50% land parcel release process started
items.value: INR86-87 crores sold; INR16 crores pending
items.quote: it is debt-free non-GML now, as you mentioned, and 50% of the collateral is already out of which we have sold one land parcel of INR86 crores, INR87 crores, and INR16 crores to be done on the ongoing quarter.

items.statement: Cash flow to be used for strengthening existing showrooms with more inventory and a few flagship stores; cash flow planning for next financial year coming shortly
items.quote: predominantly, we want to utilize to strengthen our existing showrooms where certain showrooms need more inventory to drive more SSGs. There can be a few flagship stores which we have not done over the last two, three years.

items.statement: Coin sales remain single digit; no major shift from ornaments to coins/bars; studded jewelry share increasing organically due to young population preference for design over investment
items.quote: If you look at our coin sale, it is only what, single digit, okay? And we don't focus too much in that area. So we don't see any major shift from ornaments to coins or bars, et cetera.

items.statement: Market share gains continuing post-COVID driven by shift from unorganized to organized; young population prefers choice, service, transparency
items.quote: Every year you see that SSGs are strong. That should come from market share growth only. Of course, I do not want to comment on other players, but I think market has a tailwind because of the shift from unorganized to organized.

items.statement: India Q2 revenue INR9,007 crores (up from INR6,843 crores); India EBITDA INR549 crores (up from INR432 crores); India PAT INR424 crores (62% growth)
items.quote: For this just concluded quarter, India revenues came in at INR9,007 crores versus INR6,843 crores when compared with the corresponding quarter of the previous year. India EBITDA came in at INR549 crores versus INR432 crores when compared with the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Middle East Q2 revenue INR960 crores (up from INR860 crores); EBITDA INR71 crores (up from INR61 crores); PAT INR12 crores (down from INR15 crores)
items.quote: revenue for the quarter was INR960 crores compared to INR860 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. EBITDA in the Middle East was INR71 crores versus INR61 crores for the same period of the previous year.

items.statement: Competition intensity always present; Kalyan equipped to handle competition strategically; not reactive to short-term changes
items.quote: Again, competition intensity is always there in our sector, okay? And players like us, we are equipped to treat those competition in the way it is necessary during the necessary times.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu government 1-gram gold coin on childbirth contract started generating revenue; very small quantity, thin B2B margins, primarily for brand building
items.quote: the revenue has started coming, but it's very small. It's not going to move the needle. This is actually more to spread the brand name rather than making margins there.

items.statement: Volume guidance: FY27 at least 6.5 lakh tons, FY28 8.5-9 lakh tons, FY29 1.1-1.2 million tons
items.value: 6.5 lakh tons; 8.5-9 lakh tons; 1.1-1.2 million tons
items.quote: So Pallav-ji for FY27, we are confident of doing at least 6.5 lakh tons of sales volume for FY27. FY28, with our increased capacity, we should be between 8.5 lakh tons to 9 lakh tons. And FY29, between 1.1 million tons to 1.2 million tons of sales volume.

items.statement: Adding 3 lakh tons capacity in Q4 FY27 via three projects; total capacity to reach 1.35 million tons by FY27 end, 1.7 million tons FY28, 2 million tons FY29
items.value: 3 lakh tons; 1.35 million tons; 1.7 million tons; 2 million tons
items.quote: Yes. So in this year, we are adding 3 lakh tons, which is in Q4. I mentioned these 3 projects in my speech. So Q4, these capacities will be up and running. So by the end of this financial year, we will be at 1.35 lakh tons -- 1.35 million tons, sorry. And FY28 at 1.7 million tons and FY29, we'll be at 2 million tons.

items.statement: H2 FY27 capex INR150-200 crores to complete 3.5 lakh tons capacity; FY28 capex around INR150 crores; funded via internal accruals and term loans
items.quote: Pallav-ji on capex spend, if you see balance sheet, it is showing CWIP of INR200 crores and further some advances in the non-current assets. So in H2, our capex is going to be in the range of around INR150 crores to INR200 crores, which will complete 3.5 lakh tons of capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton maintained at INR3,500 in H1 despite energy, logistics, freight challenges; confident of maintaining volumes and EBITDA per ton in H2
items.quote: So, I think we have managed that period quite decently, and we have maintained our INR3,500 per ton EBITDA. This is despite that the new facilities just got operationalized in Q4 of FY26. And all these facilities now are at their good optimum utilization level.

items.statement: Target VAP share increase from 40% to 55%; blended EBITDA per ton expected INR4,000-4,500 at 55% VAP share
items.quote: So with the new VAP and if we reach 55% VAP share, our EBITDA per ton will range from INR4,000 per ton to INR4,500 per ton.

items.statement: H1 volume grew 30% despite war and monsoon challenges; expect much higher demand in H2 especially from solar sector at peak season
items.quote: But despite of that, the company was able to achieve a formidable growth of 30%. And while the effects of this war and the monsoon season getting over, so we see a much higher demand projection for H2.

items.statement: Solar segment addressing 1 million ton market (40-50 GW annual installs at 20-22 tons/MW); expect solar to be highest growing segment over next 3 years
items.quote: And looking forward, as India is installing 40 to 50 gigawatt of solar plants every year, so every 1 megawatt requires at least 20, 22 tons. So this becomes like a 1 million ton market in itself.

items.statement: Net working capital days decreased from 56 to 33 days in H1 FY27; targeting under 30 days
items.quote: Yes. Pallav-ji, so -- yes, now this was a very conscious decision and we are very strong on this. And we'll -- in fact, we are trying to bring it under 30 days.

items.statement: Revenue potential ~INR9,000 crores at 2 million tons capacity with 65% utilization
items.quote: So, taking like a 65% utilization level, we can expect approximately INR9,000 crores of revenue from this capacity.

items.statement: VAP share currently 40%; new 1 million ton capacity mainly value-added; targeting 55% VAP share
items.quote: Right now, we are at 40%. And with our new capacity of this 1 million tons, this is mainly in the value-added segment. And we hope to take our VAP share from 40% to 55% in the next phase of growth.

items.statement: DFT facility Sanand Unit II Phase 3, API pipes facility, Hindupur integrated coated facility all expected commissioning by Q4 FY27
items.quote: DFT facility at Sanand Unit II Phase 3, the project is progressing as scheduled and is expected to be commissioned by Q4 FY27. This will enhance capabilities in high-quality and specialized pipe segments. API facility, the work on the API pipes is also advancing as planned, with readiness expected by Q4 FY27. This facility will enable us to serve niche markets, including the oil and gas transporta

items.statement: Export business performing very well with encouraging demand from international markets
items.quote: Our export business is also performing very well, with encouraging demand from international markets.

items.statement: Solar segment dealing with all top players in module mounting structures and solar tracker business
items.quote: And we are now in a position to command a good respect when it comes to the module mounting structures and the solar tracker business. And we are dealing with all the top players in this category.

items.statement: New incentives and schemes by Central and State Governments expected to increase solar capacity
items.quote: And going forward, with the current plans and the new incentives and schemes by the Central and State Governments, we see this capacity increasing.

items.statement: Denied market rumors of APL Apollo buying shares in Hi-Tech Pipes; no such development or talks
items.quote: Rithik, your query about this APL buying shares in Hi-Tech, this is absolutely not correct. And I would like to reiterate that no such development, no such talks are there.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance 20-25% and EBITDA margin 35-40% maintained
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain confident about our growth trajectory and maintaining our FY27 guidance of 20% to 25% revenue growth and EBITDA margins in the range of 35% to 40%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 order inflows INR 1,046 crore including INR 929 crore in Q2
items.quote: Our order inflows during H1 FY '27 have been particularly encouraging. We secured fresh orders worth INR1,046 crores during the first half, including INR929 crores in Q2 FY '27, compared with INR167 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Order book INR 1,742 crore on hand plus INR 956 crore negotiated orders awaiting formal receipt
items.quote: As of April 1, 2026, our order book stood at INR927 crores. As of date, orders on hand are at INR1,742 crores. In addition, we have successfully concluded negotiations for orders worth INR956 crores, which are awaiting formal receipt. Including these negotiated orders, our overall order book visibility stands approximately at INR2,698 crores.

items.statement: Pipeline of INR 1,500-2,000 crore additional orders expected before March 2027
items.quote: We still expect another INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores order before March. Those are all in the pipeline, where some are under negotiation, some the inquiry is supposed to happen.

items.statement: Capex will substantially exceed INR 150 crore with new building, factory and production infrastructure underway
items.quote: The kind of product roadmap we are trying to put in the last 6 to 8 months we have planned. It will probably involve a substantial investment. We can't talk about numbers presently. We will take it to the Board and then get an approval before we can talk about how to make the -- then talk to the market. But this is a lot of thinking within our management to see that we do substantial investment in

items.statement: Building new factory and production infrastructure in advance of large production orders
items.quote: We're building up another building and factory. That's also in place. It's already going on, and building has started. We need to -- we're also putting production infrastructure in case the contracts will become fructified and we get a production order. I should also have a capability to produce it in volumes. So we need to have space and infrastructure and test equipment.

items.statement: Shift from parts/subsystems to complete systems and integrated solutions for larger defence programs
items.quote: We're increasingly seeing customers engage with us for complete systems and integrated solutions rather than individual parts and subsystems, which provides us with opportunities to participate in larger programs and enhance our value creation proposition.

items.statement: Developing counter-drone systems including radars, passive RF detection, jamming and electro-optics
items.quote: During the period, we made progress in the development of drone defence systems, including different kinds of radars, passive RF detection and jamming, maritime and airborne radars for small and large UAVs and helicopters, long-range radars with advanced beamforming, and completing the development of jammer pods, development of next generation COMINT and ELINT and Radar Warning Receivers, among ot

items.statement: Entering satellite manufacturing with in-house design of 100-500 kg class satellites and payloads
items.quote: Today, a decision internally is taken to go ahead with the development. At the present moment, I can only comment on that. Let's see how the next 6 to 8 months goes, and then we can be able to give you more clear directives on those areas, what we've done.

items.statement: Acquired 100% stake in ST Advanced Composites Private Limited effective September 17, 2026
items.quote: Another important strategic development during the quarter was the acquisition of 100% stake in ST Advanced Composites Private Limited, which became a wholly-owned subsidiary effective September 17, 2026. This acquisition strengthens our advanced composite design manufacturing capabilities, enhances our ability to offer integrated solutions and create opportunities across radars and other defence

items.statement: Co-investing in radars with British company and targeting civil aviation avionics for export markets
items.quote: We are also co-investing in some radars with a British company. We see that we can look at worldwide markets. We're also trying to make offers for civil aviation avionics and sensors. If that happens, I think there can be a large revenue post-qualification.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances plus investments over INR 500 crore as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a strong balance sheet with cash and bank balances and investments of more than INR500 crores as on September 30, 2026, providing us with the financial flexibility to support our growth initiatives and strategic investments.

items.statement: Pre-ordering materials and components to accelerate execution once contracts fructify
items.quote: We are getting ourselves prepared for all of this and buying material components, keeping it in stock in case we need a faster turnaround. Once the contract comes, we are in a position to address the market. So we are actually planning ahead of materials and inventories, but the contract is -- we still not got the contracts.

items.statement: H2 FY27 expected stronger than H1 FY27 supported by healthy order book and execution momentum
items.quote: During the current quarter, several program milestones are progressing, with deliveries expected to pick up in the second half of FY27. Accordingly, we expect H2 FY27 to be stronger than H1 FY27, supported by a healthy order book and execution momentum.

items.statement: Key risks: government-driven business timelines, competition from foreign OEMs with lower pricing, contract win uncertainty
items.quote: Risk is always there in any development, and to achieving getting a contract, because it's not everything is in our control. It's a government-driven business, so it's going to be very difficult, and we don't know the competition, how they're going to come up. We know the competition as they are to a large extent in India. But some foreigner may try to invest or they finally give a lower support p

items.statement: Defence budget allocations growing, Acceptance of Necessity (AoNs) released every 2 months at higher rate than previous year
items.quote: I don't see ecosystem constraints. I think the budget allocations are becoming bigger. The Acceptance of Necessity, AoNs are getting released every 2 months, which is going to be much higher than what was the previous year's numbers. The opportunities are growing.

items.statement: Continuing work with PSUs and DRDO while adding direct MoD tenders for complete systems
items.quote: continue to work with our PSUs, they are our large customers today. We don't intend to replace this market. We continue to work with DRDO, address their requirements because they are very large, and new technology requirements is coming up in the country. And investments within DRDO and further contracts with PSUs also are there. We will continue to look at our markets the way we are. But in conti

items.statement: Differentiating through indigenous complete systems vs foreign OEM partnerships for MoD tenders
items.quote: We are doing an alternative thing. And we're trying to develop these in-house in India with indigenous technology and compete with all of them. So that is where the large resources are being spent, in terms of money and manpower, building those technologies and products to address the large opportunities.

items.statement: MoD tenders require indigenous content and validation processes for complete systems
items.quote: We want to address the large part of the business. But there -- the difference is that we have to have the end product ourselves. Either you do it yourself or have a collaboration with a foreign OEM who has a product, and then offer it for trial here, go through the validation process and meet the indigenous content requirement, which comes as part of the tender

items.statement: FY27 guidance for continuing business: revenue INR175 cr, EBITDA INR46 cr, PAT ~INR32 cr
items.value: 175 cr revenue, 46 cr EBITDA, 32 cr PAT
items.quote: Our FY '27 guidance for the continuing business remains intact at INR175 crores in revenue and INR46 crores in EBITDA and a PAT of about INR32 crores, with growth expected to be supported by expansion in government test preparation, scaling of the academic business into new geographies, managed schools and continued operating leverage.

items.statement: 5-year target: revenue INR600 cr, EBITDA INR120-140 cr for non-commerce business
items.quote: So on the guidance, Ashish, so what we're expecting is with the current guidance of INR175 crores this year to reach INR600 crores in the next 5 years, both government test prep and school business on the top line front. On the EBITDA front and the current expectation currently at INR45 crores, we are planning to reach EBITDA of INR120 crores to INR140 crores.

items.statement: Government test prep revenue grew 31% YoY in Q2; enrollments grew 12% in H1
items.quote: Revenue from operations for quarter stood at INR51 crores, registering a healthy growth of 17% year-on-year, driven by healthy enrollment and admissions traction in government test prep, which posted a 31% year-on-year top line growth.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 25% vs 23% in Q1; government test prep EBITDA grew 79% on 31% revenue growth
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded to 25% in quarter 2 compared to 23% in quarter 1.

items.statement: Management sees current 23-25% EBITDA margins as sustainable despite Karnataka expansion
items.quote: I would believe that the current margins that we have, EBITDA margins are sustainable margins. Mohasin Khan: 23% to 25%. Yes.

items.statement: Target to scale managed schools portfolio to over 30 schools in next few years from 6 currently
items.quote: Our target is to scale this portfolio to over 30 schools in the next few years.

items.statement: Government test prep network: over 40 centers across exams including UPSC, SSC, Banking, TNPSC
items.quote: We have a strong presence across examinations, including UPSC, SSC, Banking, Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission and other state level examinations with an established network of over 40 centers across.

items.statement: Fees increased 7-10% YoY; cost increases average ~4% annually
items.quote: First is we typically increase the fees by about 7% to 10% year-on-year. That generally contributes to an increase in revenue without increase in any capacity expansion or operating costs? We do have an increase in costs, which are typically on an average about 4% in a year.

items.statement: Finance costs fell 58% YoY to INR4.8 cr from INR11.5 cr due to deleveraging and refinancing
