items.statement: H1 FY27 net cash from operating activities INR14.9 crores; net cash used in investing INR36.5 crores for capacity expansion
items.quote: During the first half, net cash generated from operating activities stood at INR14.9 crores, while net cash used in investing activities stood at INR36.5 crores, reflecting our ongoing investment in capacity expansion, new product line addition and manufacturing infrastructure.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio 0.68x as of September 2026; CRISIL upgraded bank facilities rating to BBB+/Stable
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.68x during the quarter. CRISIL also upgraded the rating of our bank facilities to BBB+/Stable.

items.statement: Chinese import competition in extrusion (ceiling paneling, doors) has almost vanished in last 2-3 years; import tariffs more than doubled/tripled making domestic manufacturing competitive
items.quote: Earlier, there used to be wider competition from the Chinese import of profiles related to the ceiling paneling and doors also. But in last 2 to 3 years, we have observed that competition is almost vanished basically. I would say not reduced, it's almost vanish.

items.statement: PVC extrusion B2B business through 800+ channel partners contributes 65%+ of total revenue
items.quote: Almost 65% plus revenue comes from this PVC extrusion B2B business, which is generated through channel partners.

items.statement: Studio Arezzo retail model contributes 20-22% of Modular Furniture revenue, expected to become major contributor going forward
items.quote: Current contribution of this in the Modular Furniture, it's somewhere around 20%, 22%, which is coming from the Studio Arezzo business.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by refined product mix (fluted/soffit panels, furniture profiles, higher range doors/windows, refined modular furniture) not price hikes
items.quote: It's purely because of our refined product mix. In fact, we have upgraded our offerings throughout different segments. Earlier wherein the volumes were coming from the low cost or high competition sort of products. So now -- which we have upgraded by adding the fluted and soffit panels, furniture profiles, higher range of the doors and windows and very refined range of Modular Furniture products t

items.statement: Import tariffs on Chinese profiles more than doubled/tripled, benefiting domestic manufacturers
items.quote: The import tariff has also improved a lot. So it is almost double -- more than double and 3x. So the cost of the product -- imported products are also very competitive with the Indian manufacturing products.

items.statement: Aluminum project execution involves design approvals, structural calculations, customized system development; revenue conversion from Q4 FY27 subject to project schedules
items.quote: Since it involves many processes related to the design approvals, certain structural calculations and customized system development. So everything is on time. From the Q3 itself, executions will start happening relative to this project business of aluminum. Q4, specifically, we mentioned that Q4 will witness certain figures, which we can separate as a segment also going forward.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY27 revenue and EBITDA split to remain at 55/45 and 60/40 respectively, consistent with historical seasonality.
items.quote: We will stick to that it should be 55/45 and 60/40.

items.statement: Corporate demand remains muted due to geopolitical uncertainty, inflation, and weak IT hiring, while non-negotiated retail demand is compensating.
items.quote: The corporate demand is still muted and within corporate demand, one of the main segments we depend on in certain cities like Gurgaon is new hirings, joinees and this is very large business from the IT sector that has not, frankly, yet picked up.

items.statement: Fleur owned hotels hotel EBITDAR margin rose 112 bps to 53% in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Their hotel EBITDAR margin percentage rose 112 basis points to 53%.

items.statement: Keys hotel EBITDAR margin rose 748 bps to 50% in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Keys hotel EBITDAR margin rose 748 basis points to 50%.

items.statement: Opened 8 managed/franchised hotels with 523 rooms in Q2 FY27; signed 11 managed/franchised hotels with 825 rooms.
items.quote: In Q2 FY27, on the asset-light side, we opened 8 managed and franchised hotels with 523 rooms. We also signed 11 managed and franchised hotels with 825 rooms, about 1.6x of the inventory we opened during the quarter.

items.statement: Combined operational and pipeline inventory stands at 24,061 rooms across 285 hotels in 170+ cities; 130 hotels with 12,131 rooms operational.
items.quote: Our combined operational and pipeline inventory now stands at 24,061 rooms across 285 hotels in 170+ cities, of which 130 hotels with 12,131 rooms across 80+ cities are already operational.

items.statement: Acquired land in Bandra East, Mumbai for ~Rs. 120 crore to develop 172-room Lemon Tree Premier, expected to open in FY30.
items.quote: This quarter, we acquired land in Bandra East, Mumbai, adjoining BKC, for about Rs. 120 crore to develop Lemon Tree Premier Bandra. An owned upscale hotel with approximately 172 rooms, expected to open in FY30.

items.statement: Aurika Shimla (90 rooms) scheduled to open in Q3 FY27; Aurika Shillong (165 rooms leased) expected FY28; Aurika Varanasi (47 rooms leased) piling begun, expected FY29; Aurika Nehru Place (610 rooms) DDA letter extended to Aug 2027, expected
items.quote: Our own 90-room hotel, Aurika Shimla, is scheduled to open in Q3 this year. Aurika Shillong, our 165-room leased hotel, is progressing well and is expected to open in FY28. At Aurika Varanasi, our 47-room leased heritage hotel, piling work has begun and is expected to open in FY29. Lastly, for Aurika Nehru Place, DDA has extended the letter of award till August 2027, which gives us ample time to s

items.statement: ARR grew 8% YoY to Rs. 6,751 in Q2 FY27; RevPAR grew 18% to Rs. 5,137 driven by balanced ARR and occupancy growth.
items.quote: For the quarter, our Gross ARR stood at Rs. 6,751, up 8% YoY and occupancy was at 76.1%, up 633 basis points YoY. As a result, RevPAR grew at 18% to Rs. 5,137.

items.statement: Aurika ARR growth 9% in Q2 FY27, highest in many quarters; management intends to push ARR further as occupancy stabilizes at ~75%.
items.quote: At 9% ARR growth, this is the highest ARR growth in the Aurika portfolio in many quarters from the past. You can start seeing this already that we are pricing Aurika to its potential and to its positioning.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced 11% YoY to Rs. 1,429.2 crore as of Sep 30, 2026; cost of debt down 28 bps to 7.44%.
items.quote: Our gross debt as on 30th September 2026 stood at Rs. 1,429.2 crore, down 11% from Rs. 1,610.2 crore a year ago. Our cost of debt reduced to 7.44%, down 28 basis points versus a year ago.

items.statement: Warburg Pincus Rs. 960 crore investment on call, no restrictions; will be drawn only if deployable in acquisitions/developments; nearly 100% sure to be fully utilized.
items.quote: It is entirely dependent on acquisitions/developments. There is no restriction. We can call for it. They said they need 2 weeks. Obviously, we will take the money if and only if we can deploy it. But based on what we are seeing right now, we are nearly 100% sure that we will take the entire amount.

items.statement: Demerger scheme: CCI, stock exchange, SEBI approvals received; filed with NCLT, first hearing done; expect shareholder approval next; target Fleur listing in CY27.
items.quote: After receiving that, last month we have filed the scheme of arrangement with NCLT and for which the first hearing has already happened and now we are looking at proceedings to go on further. Then we reach a stage where we seek the shareholders' approval for the scheme. We expect, as we discussed earlier, that within next calendar year, which is CY27, we list Fleur Hotels on the stock exchanges.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 RevPAR grew 18% YoY to Rs. 5,137; occupancy 76.1% (+633 bps); ARR Rs. 6,751 (+8%).
items.quote: As a result, RevPAR grew at 18% to Rs. 5,137.

items.statement: Keys RevPAR up 29% YoY to Rs. 3,109; occupancy 69.7% (+976 bps); ARR Rs. 4,460 (+11%).
items.quote: Keys RevPAR in Q2 FY27 was up 29% YoY to Rs. 3,109 on the back of a 976 basis points improvement in occupancy to 69.7% and 11% growth in ARR to Rs. 4,460.

items.statement: Fleur owned hotels RevPAR grew double digits across all brands and regions (11% Mumbai to 25% Delhi).
items.quote: RevPAR grew in double digits across every brand and every region, ranging from 11% in Mumbai to 25% in Delhi.

items.statement: Aurika and Lemon Tree Premier contribute 63% of hotel EBITDAR on 58% of revenue for Fleur owned portfolio.
items.quote: Aurika and Lemon Tree Premier together earned 63% of hotel EBITDAR on 58% of revenue.

items.statement: Management sees structural supply-demand deficit in India; supply growth concentrated in Tier 2/3/4 where Lemon Tree is asset-light; not concerned about luxury supply from IHCL/ITC/international brands.
items.quote: Structurally, what is happening to India is there is a clear deficit between supply and demand. Like just Patu said, while in the deep demand, let us say, districts of the country, there is little supply coming up. Most of the supply is coming in Tier 2, Tier 3 markets, where while there is competition, but I guess there is enough demand

items.statement: Leadership restructuring announced: Mudit Kumar Singh as Chairman, Deep Saraf as Managing Director, Vinita Saraf as President Business Excellence and Development, Ashish Saraf as President Strategic Planning and Business Development
items.quote: Mr. Mudit Kumar Singh as Chairman will lead the board and keep our focus on governance and risk oversight as we scale. Mr. Deep Saraf as Managing Director will run operations and execution, manufacturing supply chain, capacity utilization, and delivery of our proposed projects. Mrs. Vinita Saraf as President, Business Excellence and Development will strengthen our processes, operational capabiliti

items.statement: Management expects healthy top-line growth for full FY27, with debottlenecking capacity to be completed by end of FY27 and new capacities commissioning around Q3-Q4 FY28
items.quote: We remain confident of our healthy top-line growth for full FY27 as well. With relates to the volume growth, we expect our capacities to be commissioning around Q3, Q4 of FY28. So we should be wise enough to expect gradual contribution from FY29 onwards or around Q4 FY28 onwards from some of the projects and capex.

items.statement: Current plant utilization at approximately 85% on expanded capacity of 47,500 tons; new capacities expected to commission in Q3-Q4 FY28 and ramp to 85-90% utilization over 2-3 years
items.quote: Our plant utilization remains approximately around 85% on the expanded capacity, which we believe currently is operating 47,500 tons of capacity on 85% utilization roughly.

items.statement: Invested INR70-75 crores so far on current capex projects; expect to invest more in H2 FY27 and FY28; total capex guidance INR225-250 crores
items.quote: Including our working progress and the amount we already have capitalized, we have invested around INR70 crores-INR75 crores towards our current capex, and we expect to invest more in the coming quarters, in the second half of the year and in the next fiscal year as well.

items.statement: Capacities fully booked for next year; healthy demand with no slowdown or order deferrals from global chocolate or cosmetic customers
items.quote: Currently, our capacities are also quite booked for the next kind of year. We do not see that kind of a thing in our products.

items.statement: Value-added products (CBE and stearin) contribution increased to 70-75% of revenue; expected to remain in 70-80% range with existing capacity
items.quote: Currently, if you see the value contribution from CBE and stearin has gone to 75% approximately in the range, which was earlier 65% and 70%. Now it is currently 70%, 75%. We believe it should be there, and going forward, the range should be healthy. It should be in the range of 70%, 75% only.

items.statement: EBITDA margin band of 25-27% considered comfortable; modest quarterly movements possible due to macro factors; structural improvement expected over 2-3 years from operating leverage and product mix changes
items.quote: We see that is going well on the band of around 25%-27% currently from the business. It can see modest movements quarter to quarter, depending on lot of macroeconomic reasons as well, and business has risk also.

items.statement: Raw material cost increase driven primarily by higher inbound freight costs due to Red Sea shipping disruptions; shea seed prices up 5-7% from inflation; freight cost increase reflected in COGS
items.quote: The raw material cost elevation is primarily what we see in our gross profit level. That is because of our costing with respect to freight cost, due to the macroeconomic events what we are seeing globally, with the Red Sea movements and hikes in the prices, like fuel and every other cost.

items.statement: Inventory increased to INR1,000 crores from INR728 crores due to early shea procurement from West Africa alongside seasonal sal and mango seeds; expected to normalize through H2; operating cash outflow INR252 crores in H1 due to inventory t
items.quote: Inventory was INR1,000 crores as of 30th September, 2026, compared with INR728 crores in March. The main reason is that our shea procurement started earlier this year, alongside our seasonal procurement of sal and mango seeds.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.04x from 0.38x at end of FY26; cash and bank balances INR498 crores; working capital funded through existing banking limits and internal resources
items.quote: As of 30th September, 2026, net debt-to-equity was 0.04x compared with 0.38x at the end of FY26. Cash and cash equivalent and other bank balance was INR498 crores.

items.statement: Exports at 61% of H1 revenue; serving customers in 39+ countries across Asia, Europe, US, South America, Middle East, Africa; H1 forex gain INR15 crores
items.quote: Exports were at 61% for H1 revenue, and we now serve customers in more than 39 countries across Asia, Europe, U.S., South America, the Middle East, and Africa.

items.statement: Healthy demand across product portfolio; 85% of revenue growth from volume, 10-15% from price realization; no slowdown or order deferrals seen
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, we see that contribution from volume growth has been around 85%, and 10%-15% we can take a price realization benefit on the prices.

items.statement: 4,500 MTPA debottlenecking under planning in Q3 FY27; Burkina Faso backward integration project in design/engineering phase with land acquired, targeting Q3-Q4 FY28 commissioning; LATAM facility ramping gradually over next year
items.quote: See, that is under planning in Q3 only, but we will update you once we have completed that application. That is under planning in Q3 only.

items.statement: Asset turnover of 5-7x on optimum utilization from forward integration investments; new capacities expected to start at 40-50% utilization and reach 85-90% in 2-3 years
items.quote: Generally, we have received around 6x from the investments towards our forward integration. That kind of directionally guidance we can share with you. That is how on an optimum utilization, we believe around 6x, 5x, 6x-7x kind of a asset turn we can see from our business.

items.statement: H1 operating cash outflow INR252 crores due to inventory build-up; other income INR25 crores (INR15 crores forex gain, INR10 crores FD interest); receivables increase due to September revenue timing, normalized at 30-day average
items.quote: On cash flow side, operating cash outflow for H1 was INR252 crores. This is timing impact from inventory, not a reflection of the business.

items.statement: Backward integration in Africa expected to yield only 2-3% company-level cost advantage; project execution risk on complex fractionation plants; macroeconomic impacts on freight and margins
items.quote: We see hardly 2%-3% company level, maybe we will get the advantage of this.

items.statement: Targets AUM of approximately ₹2,500 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: Month-on-month disbursements for FY27 have been rising steadily, and AUM is growing in line with our projected target of approximately ₹2,500 crores by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: AUM reached ₹1,766 crores as of September 30, 2026, up 71.8% year-on-year
items.quote: Our AUM as of September 30, 2026 stood at ₹1,766 crores, up 10.4% from ₹1,599 crores as of June 30, 2026, and up 71.8% from ₹1,028 crores as of September 30, 2025.

items.statement: Disbursements for Q2 FY27 were ₹590 crores, up 31% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter were ₹590 crores, up 31% from ₹449 crores in Q1 FY2026-27.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 1.77% and Net NPA to 1.50% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Gross NPA improved from 1.91% to 1.77%, and Net NPA improved from 1.63% to 1.50%.

items.statement: Only ₹1 crore of total ₹30 crore NPA from new digital products, rest from legacy EV retail book
items.quote: Out of total NPA of around ₹30 crores, only about ₹1 crores is from the new book, and recovery is still possible on that amount, so it remains on the books. The rest is entirely from EV retail.

items.statement: Aims to bring Gross NPA below 1.50%
items.quote: Gross NPA has improved steadily, from 2.50% in Q4 FY25 to 1.77% now, and we aim to bring it below 1.50%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing declined by more than 100 basis points over the last year
items.quote: Even so, our cost of borrowing has declined by more than 100 basis points over the last year.

items.statement: ROA approximately 4% in current period vs 1.5% in FY26
items.quote: This time, our ROA is approximately 4%, compared to about 1.5% in FY2025-26.

items.statement: Investing in technology infrastructure and cybersecurity with senior hires and AWS migration
items.quote: They have migrated all our servers to AWS. To ring-fence our systems against external breaches, we have deployed SentinelOne, one of the most capable tools for blocking external attacks.

items.statement: Employee base reduced from 500 in FY26 to 306 currently, AUM per employee improved from ₹1.89 crores to ₹5.77 crores
items.quote: In FY26, our employee base was around 500; it is now 306. Our target for this year was 300, so we are on track. AUM per employee has improved from ₹1.89 crores to ₹5.77 crores.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity increased to 2.89x from 2.43x, well within lender limit of 4x
items.quote: Debt-to-equity increased from 2.43 times to 2.89 times. The standard leverage permitted by our lenders is approximately 4 times, so we are well within that limit.

items.statement: No fresh capital needed until AUM reaches ₹3,000-3,500 crores, not before FY28
items.quote: We will not need fresh capital until we reach approximately ₹3,000 to 3,500 crores of AUM. I am ambitious, and I could commit to a number for FY2027-28, but even without an ambitious target we will generate good profits.

items.statement: RBI approved AD-II (Authorised Dealer Category II) forex licence directly without FFMC route
items.quote: With the blessings of all of you and our team, two days ago, on Dhanteras, the RBI approved Mufin Green's AD-II licence. This is a unique approval.

items.statement: 50 players replicating Mediclaim financing but market large enough; edge in Arthum via PPI licence, ERP platform and NBFC ecosystem
items.quote: Today, around 50 players are replicating that product. But the market is so large that we are the leader and will remain so, even if 50 players enter.

items.statement: Launching life insurance financing in about a month; will be only player in that ecosystem
items.quote: We began with health insurance, and we are now entering life insurance. There are some hurdles, but we plan to go live in about a month. Once we go live, we will be the only player in the country in that ecosystem.

items.statement: Arthum workforce platform (20% stake) enables financing contract workers via PPI licence wallet architecture
items.quote: Another product is through Arthum, a workforce platform in which we have taken a 20% stake. To put it simply, thousands of workers are engaged through contractors and are not on the payroll of the companies they work for.

items.statement: Salary Saathi/Arthum pricing approximately 3-5% per month with EMI deduction via wallet ecosystem
items.quote: We will offer pricing of approximately 3 to 5% per month. The amount the contractor has to pay the worker on the due date will not go directly to the worker; it will come into our wallet-based ecosystem, where we will deduct our EMI with interest and pass on the balance to the worker.

items.statement: Mediclaim financing yields 18-24%, average ticket size ₹51,000, tenure 2-60 months, 10 insurance partners
items.quote: Our average ticket size on this product is approximately ₹51,000. Tenure ranges from 2 to 60 months, yields are in the range of 18 to 24%, and we are onboarded with 10 insurance companies.

items.statement: Borrowing profile diversified across DFIs, listed NCDs (20,000+ investors), NBFCs, PSU banks, private banks via ECBs, DA, NCDs, PTCs
items.quote: Our borrowing profile is well-diversified. We have raised funds from every segment available to us — DFIs; listed NCDs, where more than 20,000 investors have subscribed; NBFCs and financial institutions; PSU banks; and private banks — through ECBs, DA, NCDs and PTCs.

items.statement: Technology infrastructure investment expensive but economies of scale will kick in as AUM grows
items.quote: It is certainly expensive. But as AUM grows, economies of scale will kick in, so it will not be a challenge or a significant burden on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Digital lending sector on high alert for cyber threats; hackers targeting data and money
items.quote: In India, digital lending is currently on high alert. Digital lenders are being targeted by hackers, and data is being compromised. There have been attempts to breach companies in our own ecosystem to extract data or money.

items.statement: Hired senior cybersecurity talent: Harish Arora (ex-Ambit) and Amit Sharma CISO (ex-SBI Cards)
items.quote: Mr. Harish Arora has joined our information security function, along with Mr. Amit Sharma, the company's Chief Information Security Officer. Both have experience in large organizations — Mr. Amit Sharma worked at SBI Cards and Mr. Harish Arora at Ambit.

items.statement: H1 FY27 PAT approximately ₹29 crores vs ₹10-11 crores in H1 FY26; PBT close to ₹40 crores
items.quote: Look at our profit. Earlier, our half-year PAT was about ₹10 to 11 crores. This half-year, PAT is approximately ₹29 crores, and at the PBT level it is close to ₹40 crores.

items.statement: Legacy rickshaw book impact ₹20-25 crores; BluSmart loss ₹15-20 crores; still absorbing past impacts
items.quote: We can hold our heads high: we are earning well in our new journey, even after a financial impact of ₹15 to 20 crores from the old one. Most of you know I tend to speak at length. I will stop here and take any questions you may have.

items.statement: Targets annual PAT of ₹500 crores without equity dilution
items.quote: We will take pride in achieving an ROA that surpasses our industry peers and reaching an annual PAT of ₹500 crore without any equity dilution.

items.statement: Climate finance book running down: ₹100-110 crores L3/L5 vehicle loans, ₹60-70 crores battery loans, remaining pain ₹25 crores
items.quote: Within climate finance, about ₹100 to 110 crores of L3/L5 vehicle loans and about ₹60 to 70 crores of battery loans remain; the rest comprises cars and buses. In this, the pain that is left in the books today is 25 crores of pain.

items.statement: 25-30% of international lenders have switched classification from climate to impact lending; rest switching gradually
items.quote: About 25 to 30% have already switched, and the rest are switching gradually.

items.statement: Using AI in DevOps for coding and collection bots for multilingual reminder calls; not using AI for underwriting as collections secured via third-party anchors
items.quote: The first is DevOps, where part of our coding is done through AI. The second is collections: we have introduced collection bots that make multilingual reminder calls to customers — for example, informing them that their policies will be cancelled if they do not pay.

items.statement: Planning to add R&D spend, AI initiatives and infrastructure investment tracking slide from next quarter
items.quote: From next quarter, we could add a slide covering R&D spend, AI initiatives and new infrastructure investments — how much we have invested so far and what capabilities we are building.

items.statement: Interest income grew 80.2% YoY, interest expense rose 103.7% due to surplus liquidity for 3-4 months EMI obligations
items.quote: Interest income grew 80.2% year-on-year. Interest expense rose 103.7%, as we are holding surplus liquidity to meet the next three to four months of EMI obligations; this is why interest expense has grown faster than interest income.

items.statement: Net interest income improved 52.4%, operating expenses increased 27.7%, PBT up 135.9%, PAT up 148.5% YoY
items.quote: Net interest income improved by 52.4%, while operating expenses increased by 27.7%. Profit before tax increased by 135.9% and PAT increased by 148.5%.

items.statement: Onboarded IDBI Bank and South Indian Bank in Q2 FY27; PSU banks include SBI, Indian Overseas Bank, Union Bank of India
items.quote: Our lenders now include State Bank of India, Indian Overseas Bank, Union Bank of India and IDBI Bank, and more banks are being onboarded. IDBI Bank and South Indian Bank were onboarded during the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

items.statement: Monthly disbursements for Arthum product could reach ₹1,200-1,500 crores with 45-day tenure
items.quote: Monthly disbursements could reach ₹1,200 to 1,500 crores. Profitability will rise, and AUM will build alongside it.

items.statement: Order book of INR 300 crores and sales pipeline of INR 625 crores
items.quote: In addition, we have a very strong order book of about INR 300 crores, while our sales pipeline is also very strong based on, this kind of initiatives, plus also our CivitCITY, CivitPORT and CivitINDUSTRY based bigger ticket accounts, we have about INR 625 crores sales pipeline.

items.statement: Expect to deliver INR 100-125 crores from order book in next 12 months
items.quote: So, in the next 12 months, we would be able to deliver, around INR 100, INR 125 crores out of this order book.

items.statement: Expect 40% conversion of INR 625 crore pipeline, with 50-75% of that delivered in next 12 months
items.quote: And from the sales pipeline, the INR 625 crores of pipeline, we are expecting 40% achievement in this pipeline. And out of that 40%, in the next one year, more or less 50% to 75%, we are going to deliver in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Target INR 55 crores revenue from order book in FY27
items.quote: In this financial year, we're targeting that out of 300, we book about INR 55 crorein this financial year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 32.5% in H1 FY27 from 29.7% in H1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 37.9% to INR 21.07 crores, while EBITDA margin improved to 32.5% from 29.7% in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Standalone Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 35.1% from 29.6% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA increased 50.8% to INR 11.47 crores, with EBITDA margin expanding to 35.1% from 29.6% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 26.3% in H1 FY27 vs 26.7% in H1 FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA margin stood at 26.3% compared to 26.7% in the previous year.

items.statement: Recurring revenue grew 46.2% to INR 28.21 crores, contribution improved to 43.5% from 37.5%
items.quote: During H1 FY27, recurring revenue increased 46.2% to INR 28.21 crore compared with INR 19.29 crore in the corresponding period last year. Its contribution to total sales improved to 43.5% against 37.5% in the previous year.

items.statement: SaaS/transaction-based revenue grew 32.7% to INR 18 crores
items.quote: Our SaaS or transaction-based revenue also grew 32.7% to INR 18 crore, reflecting increasing traction in our platform lead offerings.

items.statement: JNPA order of INR 92.95 crores for AI-powered digital twin solution
items.quote: During the first half of FY27, our major breakthrough has been towards JNPA, which is a INR 92.95 crore order from Jawaharlal Nehru Urban Port Trust.

items.statement: Advanced stage permitting solution engagement with Middle East government, contract signing expected soon
items.quote: It's almost like we can sign the contract anytime now is what we are expecting very soon. And we will be able to declare it, I would say, definitely, in a very near timeline.

items.statement: eTDR platform live in Mumbai, negotiating with multiple cities for expansion
items.quote: In Mumbai, we have implemented it, very successfully, and we are negotiating with multiple cities to take it forward.

items.statement: Higher depreciation and amortization due to product development investments for overseas markets and platforms
items.quote: However, the higher amortization of depreciation is nothing but the investments which we are making in our product for the growth path for the year going forward, we will see the impact of these amortization and depreciation.

items.statement: Absolute depreciation/amortization costs to remain stable or increase slightly, but percentage of revenue to decline as sales scale
items.quote: But if you look at absolute numbers, they will not go down, and they will almost remain this or maybe slightly more also. But in terms of the growth, could be something which I can see in the future definitely.

items.statement: Finance cost declined to INR 1.89 crores from INR 2.16 crores due to better fund utilization
items.quote: Finance cost declined to INR 1.89 crores from INR 2.16 crores supported by better fund utilization.

items.statement: Invested significantly in aligning products for German market with local building codes and GIS maps
items.quote: We have invested significantly for aligning our products to the German market for, and are bringing in their data sets onto our platform, their building codes, their entire GIS maps onto our platform, and this is what we have done in last few quarters.

items.statement: Middle East order of INR 1.7-1.8 crores deferred due to geopolitical situation, INR 1 crore revenue reversed in Q2
items.quote: The order size was somewhere around 1.7 or 1.8 crores in INR terms, okay. But the impact during the quarter was not that. It was somewhere around INR 1 crore approx, the amount reversed during this quarter, and this is purely a reversal.

items.statement: No risk of cancellation for deferred Middle East order, situation improving
items.quote: As of now, there is no risk of cancellation of this order. This is because of the geopolitical situation in that particular area, the order is deferred.

items.statement: eTDR exchange charges 0.5% transaction fee on TDR value as revenue model
items.quote: On the exchange, we have available TDRs who are actually the owners of the TDR, and they sell this TDR to the buyers. They exchange the transition. And based on the transition value onto the platform, we charge 0.5% as fees.

items.statement: Permitting solutions deployed in 1,500+ cities across 18 states with 5 lakh architects and 40,000+ contractors on platform
items.quote: Our permitting solutions are deployed in more than 1,500 plus cities across the country, spread over 18 states, which is helping the governments day and night in terms of getting the approvals faster.

items.statement: 3 billion square feet of permits issued over last two decades
items.quote: And there are about three billion square feet of permits we have issued in the last about two decades in the country.

items.statement: Real estate market slowdown impacted eTDR volumes in Q1-Q2, but recovery seen in current month
items.quote: But if you look at the situation of the real estate market as a whole, unfortunately, the market last quarter was very, very slow in real estate sector totally.

items.statement: Expanded business development activities in Germany with new sales director
items.quote: From the German point of view, again, I would like to say that we have expanded our business development activities by way of introducing some powerful sales director there, and we look forward to an overall growth in this.

items.statement: Employee costs stable at INR 13.01 crores standalone, INR 15.44 crores consolidated in H1 FY27

items.statement: eTDR platform operates with SBI Bank escrow account and regulatory authority oversight

And in between, our transition facilitation fees is transferred to SoftTech, and there is transition fees to the authority as well.

items.statement: First-of-its-kind eTDR exchange platform in the country
items.quote: So, we have created an eTDR exchange platform, which is first of its kind in the country.

items.statement: Launched AI-based permitting solution CivitPLAN for architects on platform
items.quote: We have recently launched AI based permitting solution, what we call as CivitPLAN, which actually can be offered to our architects who are already on to our platform.

items.statement: No downside seen for FY27 guidance despite Middle East deferral, standalone strong and Middle East permitting deal expected to be larger
items.quote: So, we don't see any downside in FY27. The standalone anyway is very strong, and as we are very confident of winning this Middle East opportunity, it will be much bigger in amount wise, and it will actually kind of address all the kind of downsides which we can see in this.

items.statement: Expect gross margin to moderate progressively from Q4 FY27 as procurement mix normalizes with harvest 2027
items.quote: However, from Q4 onwards, we expect this cost to moderate progressively as the procurement mix normalizes with harvest 2027.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 22-23% over next couple of years
items.quote: Our immediate goal would be to at least to go to 22%-23% over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expect WIPS grant of INR 49-50 crores for full year FY27
items.quote: Somewhere around INR 49 to INR 50 crores on a full-year basis on WIPS.

items.statement: Elite and premium portfolio grew 9% YoY in Q2 FY27, contribution expanded 400 bps to 82% of own brands
items.quote: Our elite and premium portfolio continued to lead growth, delivering a healthy 9% year-on-year increase in Q2.

items.statement: Telangana delivered almost 40% YoY growth in Q2 FY27, now second-largest market in elite and premium segment
items.quote: Telangana continued its strong momentum, delivering almost 40% YoY growth in Q2.

items.quote: Wine tourism's contribution to total revenue, including the D2C wine sales at our tourism facilities, increased by 220 basis points YoY to nearly 20% in Q2.

items.quote: Despite the 4% net revenue growth in Q2, gross profit declined by 280 basis points versus last year, primarily due to two major factors.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 85 bps to 20.3% in Q2 FY27 driven by premium portfolio strength and 4% reduction in operating expenses
items.quote: In terms of margin, our EBITDA margin improved 85 basis points to 20.3% in Q2.

items.statement: Fourth hotel at York Estate: 35-key property, INR 25 crore investment, targeted payback 5-6 years, opening Q4 2028
items.quote: This project would involve an investment of around INR 25 crores and with a targeted payback period of just five to six years.

items.statement: Vintage Room event pavilion at Nashik campus now operational, 5,000 sq ft, 300 guest capacity, expected incremental revenue in H2 FY27 and FY28
items.quote: We expect the Vintage Room to contribute incremental revenues in H2 of FY 2027 and further in FY 2028.

items.statement: Room capacity to expand by ~20% to 185-190 rooms with fourth hotel at York Estate
items.quote: Once operational, the new hotel will expand our room capacity by another 20% to approximately 185 to 190 rooms.

items.statement: Battery energy storage capacity to double from 2 MW to 4 MW in coming months
items.quote: with further benefits expected as we double our battery energy storage capacity from the current 2 MW to 4 MW in the coming months.

items.statement: Table grape prices expected to plunge in harvest 2027, benefiting economy/popular portfolio margins
items.quote: This time, we're expecting the exact opposite with a plunge in table grape prices. So, in fact, that's going to have a salutary effect on our margins and all wine producers on the cheaper wines.

items.statement: Packing material costs (glass, fuel, oil) rose due to Middle East troubles but appear to be calming down
items.quote: We did see some rise, unfortunately, in terms of glass, fuel, oil, et cetera. I would say things are looking pretty good.

items.statement: Launching wine-based RTD segment early next month to reach new consumers and broaden portfolio
items.quote: I am excited about our upcoming entry into the wine-based RTD segment, with our first launch expected early next month.

items.statement: Telangana overtook Karnataka as second-largest market in elite and premium segment
items.quote: Telangana has now overtaken Karnataka to become our second-largest market in the elite and premium segment.

items.statement: Sula gained market share in premium wine segment in H1 FY27, holds 70-75% share in Indian premium wine market
items.quote: Sula gained market share in the premium wine segment in the first half of FY27, as indicated by industry data that is available to us from select corporation markets.

items.statement: EU FTA duty reduction on wines above EUR 2.50 CIF delayed to May 2027 from earlier Dec/Jan expectation
items.quote: The latest news is, it looks like it is moving out to May of 2027, so we are not really sure when it is going to kick in.

items.statement: Wine inventory reduced by ~80 days from Q2 FY26 to Q2 FY27
items.quote: I'm told by our team that we are down around 80 days in wine inventory from Q2 FY 2026 to Q2 FY 2027.

items.statement: WIPS outstanding receivables INR 88 crore as of Sep 2026, received INR 4.2 crore in Nov reducing to ~INR 85 crore
items.quote: Our WIPS outstanding receivables stood at INR88 crores as of September 2026, compared to INR86 crores at the end of March.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 49 crore YoY to INR 306 crore as of Sep 2026, debt-to-EBITDA below 3x on trailing 12-month basis
items.quote: Net debt declined significantly by INR49 crores while closing at INR306 crores as of September 2026, 14% lower than INR355 crores a year ago.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing declined 30 bps to 7.3% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Average cost of borrowing for the quarter stood at 7.3%, lower by 30 basis points versus 7.6% last year.

items.statement: Cash generated from operations after working capital increased ~20% to INR 5 crore in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Cash generated from operations after working capital increased by nearly 20% to INR 5 crore, reflecting a significant improvement in cash generation.

items.quote: Solar energy now accounts for 97% of our winery energy requirements and 80% of our overall energy needs.

items.quote: Its contribution as a result of this to own brands expanded over 400 basis points Y-o-Y to an all-time high of 82%.

items.statement: The Source brand grew over 30% YoY in Q2 FY27, contribution to own brands expanded 300 bps to over 11%
items.quote: Our flagship elite brand, The Source, continued its exceptional performance, growing by over 30% Y-o-Y in Q2.

items.statement: Sula Merlot grew over 100% YoY in Q2 FY27, now contributes nearly 5% of own brand sales
items.quote: Sula Merlot has been another standout performer, recording growth of over 100% Y-o-Y in Q2.

items.statement: Wine tourism room revenue grew 32% YoY in Q2 FY27, ARR increased 3%
items.quote: Room revenue grew 32% year-on-year, driven by launch of The Haven and increased ARR by 3%.

items.statement: Karnataka market remains subdued due to excise policy changes favoring beer over wine and spirits
items.quote: Karnataka, our second-largest market, remained relatively subdued, with consumption trends following the recent excise policy changes favoring beer in over wine and spirits.

items.quote: We have a policy that unfortunately at this point is a bit discriminatory towards Indian wines vis-a-vis imported wines. Imported wines get included in a quota system for the retailers, whereas Indian wines are not in it.

items.statement: Potential irrigation controls from April 2025 could impact following year's grape harvest
items.quote: It will not be a surprise if the state puts some major controls on irrigation once we are in about, starting around April next year, which could have an impact on the following year's harvest.

items.statement: Logistics operations to be brought in-house at Domaine Dindori facility, expected annual savings of INR 1 crore from Q4 FY27
items.quote: This initiative is expected to deliver annual savings of INR 1 crore, with benefits starting to reflect from Q4 FY 2027.

items.statement: Management expects healthy profitability improvement in remaining FY27 quarters from price hikes, cost reduction, and subsidiary turnarounds
items.quote: For the remaining quarters of FY27, the management expects healthy improvement in profitability on account of core business profitability improvement supported by the recent price increase, price hikes from the customers, strong cost reduction measures being undertaken by the company, improvement in performance of Aceware and Radiant valuable logistics and better growth in revenues from core busin

items.statement: Price hike impact visible from Q4 FY27, steady impact in FY28
items.quote: I think the impact can be seen from the fourth quarter onwards. And it will be a definite impact from the fourth quarter. I mean, currently in the third quarter, it's being applied. It will have a definite impact in the coming financial year that you will be seeing.

items.statement: Aspiration for mid-teens revenue growth in core business
items.quote: Revenue growth, we have -- as in our aspiration is to meet mid-teens of revenue growth.

items.statement: Cash volumes flat at INR 0.41 trillion in Q2 FY27 YoY; points grew 5% YoY to 79,374
items.quote: We handled cash volume of INR0.41 trillion during the quarter, a flat performance over the same period last year.

items.statement: Core retail cash management grew 6.2% YoY in Q2 FY27 driven by BFSI and organized retail
items.quote: The retail cash management business grew at 6.2% during this quarter over same period last year.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 7.62% from 15.2% YoY due to sharp manpower cost increase
items.quote: The standalone EBITDA margin for the quarter was 7.62% as against 15.2% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 6.8% from 13.1% YoY; subsidiaries near breakeven
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA margins for the quarter also correspondingly fell to 6.8% from 13.1% in the same period last year as the subsidiary performance improved to near breakeven levels in this quarter.

items.statement: PAT margin 3.5% and ROCE 5.4% in Q2 FY27; management confident worst is behind
items.quote: Overall, profitability for the quarter was poor at 3.5% PAT margin and 5.4% ROCE. However, the management is confident that the worst is behind us, and the coming quarters will report much healthier numbers.

items.statement: Price hikes of 12-15% secured across majority of clients; most implemented by December
items.quote: We have been able to speak to the banks, and we are looking at a price hike, as I mentioned in my initial presentation of 12% to 15% price hike across the board.

items.statement: No fuel cost pass-through mechanism; wages above minimum in southern states
items.quote: No, there is no pass-through of fuel cost.

items.statement: Manpower costs (70% of total) rose sharply due to minimum wage hikes and armed gunmen shortage in southern states
items.quote: Sharp increase in minimum wages in a few states and shortage of licensed gunmen in several southern states resulted in higher manpower costs.

items.statement: Direct client revenue share rose to 19.2% from 15.7% YoY; target one-third in 1-2 years
items.quote: Direct clients accounted for 19.2% of our revenues for this quarter, up from 18.4% in the previous quarter and 15.7% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Radiant Acemoney near EBITDA breakeven; 20,000 BCs, 21,000 sound boxes deployed, INR 200 cr transaction volume
items.quote: Currently, we have a network of close to 20,000 BCs as of this quarter. We freshly deployed 21,000 sound boxes and facilitated transaction volume of close to INR 200 crores in this quarter.

items.quote: Radiant valuable logistics reported revenues of INR29.9 million, reporting sequential growth of 35% in Q2 of FY27 over Q1 of FY27 and is well on its way to achieve positive EBITDA in the current financial year.

items.statement: 80% revenue via banks, 20% direct; bank contracts renegotiated mid-term for price hikes
items.quote: No, no. 80% of our business are through banks. Only 20% is direct customers.

items.statement: Focus on organized retail, NBFCs, hospitals, government for direct client acquisition
items.quote: Largely, the focus areas for us will be wherever there is a large amount of cash volume. So organized retail, NBFCs, hospitals, government businesses, these are the areas where we are seeing fairly good traction in terms of prospects to add more new clients.

items.statement: Industry-wide price hike after joint representation to IBA; no competitor undercutting
items.quote: No, this was -- the whole industry together because of increase in minimum wages and increase of the fuel price following the Iran situation. So it was a unanimous decision taken by all of us.

items.statement: Debtors at ~80 days revenue in Sep 2026; September dip collected in early October
items.quote: The working capital management continued to remain excellent with debtors at about 80 days revenue in September '26.

items.statement: Net debt nil; cash and equivalents INR 1.5B own funds as of Sep 30, 2026

items.statement: No major capex expected; vans leased, subsidiary sound boxes treated as self-liquidating inventory

items.statement: Hiring sector-specific senior resources for direct business development
items.quote: We have hired senior resources, sector-specific senior resources who have rich experience in specific sectors. So that should help improve -- add more clients.

items.statement: Gunmen shortage persists in specific southern states; no clear visibility on easing
items.quote: The gunman shortage is -- we don't have a clear visibility when it will ease. But at this point of time, gunman costs are high and across specific states only.

items.statement: Elections have no material impact on cash movement volumes
items.quote: No, this is a new question. We have not encountered this so far. And in our own movement of cash, elections have no material impact.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% revenue growth in Q3 and Q4 FY27 sequentially, aiming to match FY25 full-year revenue in FY27
items.quote: We are hopeful that in Quarter 3, we will be 30%-35% up from the Q2 and in Quarter 4, we will be 30%-35% up from Q3. So, that should aggregate the figure ending of FY25.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin around 25% by end of FY27
items.quote: Yes, definitely, we should be able to around 25 plus minus, always happens in the industry. So, around that, because in this quarter, we are 22.26% and we hope that because Q1 was low, so maybe the end of the financial year may be around this or plus 1% type of thing.

items.quote: The water supply and sewage sector is a tremendous sector in India and about Rs. 15 lakh crores as estimated by Namami Ganga and Amrit, they have to be executed in less in next 10 years to 15 years.

items.quote: This quarter we have achieved EBITDA of 22.26% and PAT margin of 14.25%. And our establishment cost is fixed; machinery cost is fixed. So, if our revenue goes up, EBITDA and PAT margin is going to increase.

items.quote: As far as this is concerned, it is more than 6 months liability which is pending. And this also includes unbilled debtors also. So, this is looking like 6 months withheld, but it is unbilled debtors also.

items.quote: In UP, it has already normalized. And in Uttarakhand, because they have changed the portal. items.quote: Basically, in Uttarakhand, the thing happened because we were more in the network lane. The works which were being done in the campus like STP works and WTP works were unaffected. items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA decreased 41% year-on-year to INR150 million, translating to 11.96% adjusted EBITDA to gross margin ratio. As a result, the company reported a net loss of INR7 million.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue declined 28% YoY to INR4,015 million; gross margin grew 3% YoY to INR2,482 million; adjusted EBITDA down 40% YoY to INR301 million (12.12% of gross margin); net loss INR4 million.

items.statement: Corporate gross bookings grew ~18% YoY; ~54% of existing customers expanded business; 177 new corporate customers went live during the year.
items.quote: During quarter 2, corporate gross bookings increased approximately 18% year-on-year. What is particularly encouraging is the broad-based nature of the growth. So comparing it versus March of 2026 versus September of 2026. In March, the trade receivable was about INR535 crores, which has now increased to INR610 crores. This increase is largely coming from increase in business and a certain amount which is coming

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents plus term deposits stood at INR2,180 million as of Sep 30, 2026; net cash position improved by INR331 million QoQ via collections streamlining.
items.quote: On the liquidity front, cash and cash equivalents and term deposits stood at INR2,180 million as of 30th September 2026. The net cash position improved by INR331 million quarter-on-quarter by further strengthening the streamlining of the collections process.

items.statement: Aims to operate at 30% ROE and distribute 40-50% of profits
items.quote: We aim to operate at a 30% ROE and are looking to distribute around 40% to 50% of our profits.

items.statement: Dry powder estimated at INR20,000-25,000 crores within total AUM
items.quote: So that number will be closer to INR20,000 crores to INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: Raised nearly INR20,000 crores in H1 FY27 across all strategies
items.quote: together we have raised close to INR20,000 crores of capital in H1.

items.statement: Raised INR31,000 crores over FY26 and H1 FY27, including INR11,000 crores in InvITs
items.quote: over FY26 and first half of FY27, we have raised nearly INR31,000 crores of capital, of which around INR11,000 crores capital will be raised on our listed strategies, which is on the InvIT side.

items.statement: Total income grew 35% YoY to INR616 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our total income for the first half of the year was INR616 crores, which was a 35% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Management and advisory fee grew 24% YoY to INR333 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our management and advisory fee has also touched INR333 crores for the first half, a growth of 24% year-on-year.

items.statement: PAT grew 35% YoY to INR169 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: Our PAT for the first half was INR169 crores, again a 35% growth from INR125 crores PAT in a similar period in the previous financial year.

items.statement: PAT yield stable at 0.72% of fee-paying AUM for H1 FY27
items.quote: Our PAT yields are stable at around 0.72% of fee-paying AUM for us.

items.statement: Quarterly PAT was INR88 crores, up 28% YoY and 9% QoQ
items.quote: Our quarterly PAT was INR88 crores, and the same is a 28% growth on annual Y-o-Y basis. While it is a 9% growth over Q1.

items.statement: ROE improved to nearly 29.5% from about 25% a year ago
items.quote: Our ROE has improved to nearly 29.5%, up from about 25% a year ago.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio steady at 64-65%
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio remains steady in the range of 64% to 65%.

items.statement: Announced dividend of 140% of face value at INR7 per share
items.quote: We are pleased that the company has announced a dividend of 140% of face value at INR7 per share.

items.quote: Our aspiration is to distribute around 50% of our annual earnings on a long-term basis, and we will welcome any views around the same.

items.quote: we have recently been awarded the Toll-Operate-Transfer, or TOT-19 bundle, which was part of the National Monetization Plan, where we won the bid at INR2,259 crores.

items.statement: Acquired 95% occupied Grade A office park in Pune of nearly 1 million sq ft
items.quote: We have also recently acquired a 95% occupied Grade A office park in Pune of nearly 1 million square feet with marquee clients as tenants.

items.quote: when I say that my 49% of our AUM is from institutional clients, those clients are being approached directly, while the 51% of the AUM that is coming out of HNI, UHNI and family office universe comes through a distributor-led approach for us.

items.statement: 77% of AUM from repeat clients across diverse strategies
items.quote: nearly 77% of our AUM comes from repeat clients who have not only experienced the fund returns over long durations and have seen fund vintages but have also invested across our diverse investment strategies.

items.statement: Nearly 5,750 unique client relationships across fund strategies
items.quote: We now have nearly 5,750 plus unique client relationships across our fund strategies.

items.statement: Plans fundraising across Special Situations, Infrastructure Yield, Commercial Real Estate Fund II, and Private Equity Fund II next quarters
items.quote: all our 3 flagship funds will be in the fundraising over the next few quarters -- our Special Situations Fund, our Infrastructure Yield Fund, as well as the second vintage of our Commercial Real Estate Fund.

items.statement: Private Equity Fund 2 expected to be nearly 3x size of previous fund
items.quote: we do believe that the Private Equity Fund 2 will be nearly 3x of the previous fund that we raised on private equity side.

items.quote: The distribution cost on an average as we mentioned is close to 30 basis points for us. And given the mix is 50-50, your understanding is correct. The distribution cost is 60 basis points on the P&L side.

items.statement: Distribution cost paid 1/3rd upfront, 2/3rd over fund life
items.value: 1/3rd upfront and 2/3rd over the trail period
items.quote: As a matrix, this cost is paid from a cash flow perspective 1/3rd upfront and 2/3rd over the trail period of the fund life.

items.quote: We have grown, as I said earlier, at a 23% CAGR on a 3-year rolling basis, and which is what is also the number for 30th September 2026.

items.quote: we have our in-house operating platform called Sekura and it has 66 plus domain specialists across sectors with expertise delivering high-quality portfolio operations and management.

If the Middle East situation settles, then you could see a drop in the cost and therefore a drop in the selling prices also.
