items.statement: Indian auto industry record Q2 FY27: PV +30.7%, 2W +15.2%, CV +28.7% YoY
items.quote: The Indian automotive industry delivered a record performance in Q2 FY27. Domestic automobile sales grew 18.2% year-on-year to 83.88 lakhs units in the July to September quarter, with passenger vehicles, 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, commercial vehicles, all recording their highest ever second quarter sales.

items.statement: EV penetration rising: e-PV +84%, e-2W +80% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Simultaneously, electrical mobility continued to gain traction with electric passenger vehicle sales growing at 84% year-on-year to over 1 lakh units in Q2 FY '27, while electric 2-wheeler sales grew around 80% to 5.89 lakh units, taking the EV penetration in 2-wheeler above 11%.

items.statement: Gasket division: single source for 5 key customers, strong OEM demand
items.quote: We remain a single source supplier for 5 of our key customers, a testament to the trust and the quality standards we uphold.

items.statement: Forging exports 57% of division revenue; customers: JCB, DANA, Carraro, GKN, Musashi, JLR
items.quote: Exports constitute approximately 57% of the Forging division revenues with customers, including JCB, DANA, Carraro, GKN Driveline, Musashi and JLR.

items.statement: Marelli JV: Stellantis ramp-up INR15.85 cr H1, target INR35 cr H2, INR120 cr+ FY28
items.quote: Here, Marelli has two businesses. One, Stellantis has started, but not the way we want it. There are initial issues of starting here and there. So in the first 6 months, we started from the month of June end, till September, we did a sale of around INR15.85 crores. And we expect the sales for the next 6 months should be around INR35 crores in the business. And next year, it should cross INR120 cro

items.statement: Marelli JV: JLR EV business INR40 cr H1 FY27, target INR75-80 cr FY27, INR90 cr FY28
items.quote: Now there are new business of JLR has also been started in this division in a big way because they have started making e-vehicle for where we have orders of e-vehicle. E-vehicle some model has started, 2-3 models will start in the coming 6 months. So in the first 6 months, we expect this year JLR should be around INR75 crores to INR80 crores as against INR47-48 crores last year.

items.statement: Heat Shield revenue INR35 cr H1 FY27; exclusive partnership for lightweight aluminum heat shields for hybrids/EVs
items.quote: The Heat Shield segment continues to scale meaningfully with H1 '27 revenues of about INR35 crores. Our exclusive partnership with global companies for lightweight aluminum heat shield is exciting. These products offer value-added features, including noise reduction, emission control, thermal insulation for new generation engines, including hybrids and EVs, making this futuristic product interesti

items.statement: Marelli JV EV revenue ~5% of JV sales; Body-in-White orders from luxury carmakers overseas
items.quote: Over 90% of Marelli's revenues come from passenger vehicle segment and EV revenues now account for almost 5% of this joint venture. As you know, we've also won a lot of Body-in-White components from luxury carmakers in the overseas market.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through: Gasket ~2%, Forging ~2.5-3%, Marugo ~7-8%, Marelli pending
items.quote: Regarding question of how much is raw material increase, etc, it's very difficult to give you, but in gasket, it's around 2%. In forging, again, it's around 2.5%, 3%. Marelli, nothing because they are yet to receive price increases. Marugo, it's about 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Freight and steel/aluminium/labour cost inflation absorbed in H1 FY27
items.quote: the West Asian region led to an increase in our raw material and freight costs. Profit growing faster than revenue reflect the operating leverage in our business, a better 1 Mentioned as 40% on the call, however, the correct figure is 49% product mix and our focus on cost. We have delivered this while absorbing higher steel, aluminium, labour and freight costs during this half year

items.statement: Exports 26.5% of H1 FY27 revenue; Q2 alone 28%
items.quote: Overall, it's 26.5%. Last quarter, it was 28%, last quarter alone last quarter.

items.statement: China+1 and Europe supplier consolidation driving forging export orders
items.quote: With European OEMs consolidating their supplier base and India emerging as a preferred alternative to China, this structural opportunity for our Forging division is larger than any point in our history. This is basically with a lot of Tier 1 European companies facing the heat of leveraged balance sheet, automatically, the business is moving towards India.

items.statement: Marelli JV H1 FY27 revenue INR226 cr (+49% YoY), EBITDA INR36 cr (+31% YoY)
items.quote: Marelli Talbros Chassis Systems reported an H1 FY27 revenues of INR226 crores, up 49% year-on-year with EBITDA growing 31% to INR36 crores.

items.statement: Talbros Marugo JV H1 FY27 revenue INR86 cr (+32% YoY), EBITDA INR10 cr (+37% YoY)
items.quote: Coming to Talbros Marugo, a 50-50 joint venture with Marugo Japan reported H1 revenues of INR86 crores, up 32% with an EBITDA of 37% to INR10 crores.

items.statement: Forging division H1 FY27 revenue INR171 cr (+13% YoY), EBITDA INR29 cr (+13% YoY)
items.quote: In H1 of FY27, total revenue of this division was INR171 crores as against INR150 crores in H1 of FY26, up by 13% on Y-o-Y basis. EBITDA of H1 of FY27 stood at 29 crores as compared to INR26 crores for H1 of FY26, a growth 13% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Gasket & Heat Shield H1 FY27 revenue INR340 cr (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR63 cr (+35% YoY)
items.quote: In H1 of '27, the division delivered revenues of INR340 crores with a growth of 22% year-on-year with EBITDA growing 35% year-on-year to INR63 crores.

items.statement: Marelli US bankruptcy does not affect Indian JV operations
items.quote: No, not at all. The Marelli bankruptcy, as you know, which is in public domain is at the U.S. courts. It does affect the companies that are maybe based out of Europe or whatever, but I think the joint venture in India. It's not at all affected.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions may cause temporary cost pressures but hedged balance sheet and customer base provide resilience
items.quote: While there are geopolitical tensions in the world and the ongoing war may lead to some temporary cost pressures, but inquiries remain strong, and we believe in Talbros, having a very hedged balance sheet and a customer base, we will be able to navigate these costs going forward.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic growth opportunities
items.quote: We're also looking and evaluating inorganic growth opportunities.

items.statement: Lohum JV: product samples approved by Apollo Tyres and MRF; setting up own pyrolysis plant
items.quote: Regarding the Lohum, our product sample has been approved by 2 tire manufacturers, Apollo Tyres and MRF, okay? Now they are making the final product out of that sample, I think and approved the process will be over within the next 3 to 4 weeks. Now Lohum team is working on a site where the project to be set up. Most probably it will set up in the south of India. Firstly, they decided that they wil

items.statement: Marelli JV Stellantis business: INR15.85 cr sales in first 6 months (Jun-Sep), targeting INR35 cr next 6 months
items.quote: So in the first 6 months, we started from the month of June end, till September, we did a sale of around INR15.85 crores. And we expect the sales for the next 6 months should be around INR35 crores in the business.

items.statement: Management expects operating environment to improve in H2 with bounce back in production, sales and consumption; cautiously optimistic on Rabi season and Kharif if El Niño turns neutral
items.quote: Overall, we can see a moderation in the global raw material prices. While Urea has come off some time back, we have seen softening approach in Sulphur as well. Sulphur is now likely to go below USD900 due to stiff resistance from metal segment as well as in the fertilizer segment.

items.statement: Management expects NPK/NPK volumes to recover with new NBS rates and MRP correction; channel inventory not very high, 5-7% above last year
items.quote: With the announcement of NBS rates, I think NP/NPK volumes will come back, and that will also reduce the import of DAP to a greater extent. I think what it used to be 60/40 between NPK and DAP turned out to be 30/70, 30% for NPKs and 70% for DAP in last few months.

items.statement: Management targets full capacity utilization of new Kakinada granulation plant next year; plant commissioning expected by February
items.quote: Our target would be to operate the plant at full capacity for the next year.

items.statement: Management expects backward integration spreads to improve in H2 after Sulphur subsidy; safe assumption of USD300-350 spread
items.quote: I think it's a safe assumption to make.

items.statement: Q2 saw unprecedented challenges: 20-30% rainfall deficit in key markets, rupee depreciation, elevated raw material prices, lower NBS rates, weak consumption; NPK production and consumption fell 40%
items.quote: All these factors resulted in sharp industry-wide decline in fertilizer volume, with production and consumption of NPKs has fallen considerably by 40% during this quarter.

items.statement: Crop protection demand soft due to rainfall impact; export demand recovery gradual; improvement in global agri commodity prices should improve offtake
items.quote: Crop Protection demand remains soft during the quarter. The impact of rainfall has had a cascading effect on the agrochemicals as well. The exports demand recovery has been gradual as farm economics was impacted due to high fertilizer costs and relatively docile agri prices.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA declined 18% YoY to INR944 crore in Q2 due to NPK margin compression from higher input prices not compensated by Kharif NBS rates
items.quote: The decrease in EBITDA is mainly due to higher input prices on account of ongoing Middle East crisis and not commensurate with some of the revisions in the NBS rates and the MRP.

items.statement: Crop Protection standalone PBIT margin 16% in Q2, 17% in H1; margins comfortable despite crude-linked intermediate variability
items.quote: PBIT, CPC standalone is 16% for the current quarter. The half year is 17%.

items.statement: NACL EBITDA significantly lower at INR12 crore due to high-cost inventory carryover and market price compression; synergistic initiatives underway for recovery
items.quote: It is a one-off aberration the company witnessed due to significant margin pressure after carryover of high-cost inventory and the corresponding pass-on could not happen due to market compression.

items.statement: Fertilizer primary sales down 30% to 10 lakh tons in Q2; consumption declined 33%; production moderated 15% to 7.7 lakh tons; market share increased from 17% to 19% in H1
items.quote: Our primary sale for the quarter was down significantly by 30% to 10 lakh tons, and consumption also declined 33%.

items.statement: Industry POS sales: NPK 60 lakh tons vs 77 lakh tons last year; DAP flattish at 44 lakh tons; total DAP+NPK 104 lakh tons vs 121 lakh tons
items.quote: NPK is 60 lakh tons as against last year 77 lakh tons, and DAP is flattish at 44 lakh tons.

items.statement: Crop Protection revenue grew 22% in Q2 driven by strong export performance; exports contributed 44% growth and >40% revenue share
items.quote: Crop Protection business delivered 22% revenue growth during the quarter, supported by strong performance in export market. Our diversified global presence continue to provide opportunities to deepen our presence across key geographies.

items.statement: Retail network expanded by 80 stores in Q2 to 1,300 stores; target 2,000 stores in next two years; white label brands expected to cross INR100 crore annual sales
items.quote: We also continue to expand our physical reach, adding 80 stores during Q2 and taking the overall network to 1,300 stores across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra.

items.statement: New Phosphoric acid and Sulphuric acid plant at Kakinada commissioned; operated at lower capacity until Sulphur subsidy in August, now at full capacity; investment INR1,100 crore
items.quote: Having invested INR1,100 crores in setting up the PA-SA plant last year, it is important for us to ramp up the volume and generate the cash out of that investment.

items.statement: Granulation plant at Kakinada progressing well; expected commissioning by February; will be available for next year
items.quote: Our granulation plant project is progressing well in Kakinada. We hope to commission this by February of this year. This capacity should be available for the next year.

items.statement: Fluoro launch plant at Ankleshwar planned; commercial plant capex estimated INR250-300 crore after customer sign-up; leveraging NACL R&D for fluorination chemistry
items.quote: Once we have a visibility on the product getting cleared with key players, we should be able to set up a commercial plant which may involve capex of about INR250 crores-INR300 crores, once we establish the feasibility and viability.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid backward integration at ~70%; management plans to realize value of Kakinada investment first; will not go 100% captive, will keep some bought-out acid exposure
items.quote: First, we want to realize the value of the investment what we have made in Kakinada, operate the plant at full capacity. Having invested INR1,100 crores in setting up the PA-SA plant last year, it is important for us to ramp up the volume and generate the cash out of that investment.

items.statement: Expanding capacity of one key molecule in Crop Protection; coming on stream by month end
items.quote: We are expanding the capacity of one of our key molecules - that will come on stream by this month end.

items.statement: Government announced NBS rates for Rabi 2026-27 and special support for Sulphur/Sulphuric acid price increase; cabinet approved; expected to improve viability and pricing balance between DAP and complexes
items.quote: Happy to note that government yesterday announced the NBS rate for Rabi '26-'27 season. This is a very timely and positive intervention, particularly given the fact that there has been significant volatility in international fertilizer and raw material markets.

items.statement: Sulphur prices likely to go below USD900; opportunity to bring below USD500 with smart purchases; DAP stable; Phos acid rolled over at USD1,700
items.quote: Sulphur is now likely to go below USD900 due to stiff resistance from metal segment as well as in the fertilizer segment. In Sulphur, which used to be a disposal problem, there is an opportunity to bring it down below USD500 as well if we sustain our approach in terms of smart purchases.

items.statement: MRP moderation of 10-15% expected for NP grades like 20:20 (from INR2,100 to ~INR1,350-1,800) after NBS revision; ammonia price spike a risk
items.quote: But at least I feel NP grades, like 20:20, which has seen a very sharp increase from INR1,350 per bag to INR2,100, there we expect moderation to happen. It can be minimum 10%-15% of moderation in those fertilizers.

items.statement: Specialty nutrients, organic and biological business performing well; water solubles and specialties gaining traction during water stress; retail white label brands scaling up
items.quote: Our specialty nutrients, organic and biological business also performed well. In this stressful situation, the adoption of water solubles and the specialties are gaining traction, and Coromandel is rightfully positioned in terms of making these differentiated product offerings to the farmers.

items.statement: Nano DAP adoption very good; market leader in nano DAP; exports started to Latin America, Middle East, South Asia; state bans in UP, Maharashtra temporarily dampening volumes
items.quote: We have become a market leader on nano DAP. Globally also, we have started exporting certain consignments. We are in the process of registering this product in Latin American markets, Middle East and South Asian countries.

items.statement: Retail business strong quarter; farmer engagement and crop-specific campaigns driving traction; new stores reaching break-even faster than expected; 80 stores added in Q2
items.quote: Our retail business had a very strong quarter, supported by continued focus on farmer engagement and crop-specific campaigns across markets. We are seeing good traction on our proprietary product portfolio.

items.statement: Framework for Fertilizer Sale pilot launched; operational challenges include longer purchase process, digital access, farmer choice; industry feedback submitted to Department of Fertilizers
items.quote: The initial implementation has also highlighted certain practical challenges, including longer purchase process for farmers, access to digital infrastructure, and accommodating farmer choice and brand preferences.

items.statement: Regulatory tightening in AgChem: restrictions on Carbosulfan and Paraquat; impact on Coromandel not significant; state bans on non-subsidy fertilizer sales in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra being engaged with
items.quote: In AgChem, we continue to see regulatory tightening, including restriction around certain molecules like Carbosulfan and Paraquat. However, impact on Coromandel is not significant.

items.statement: Crop Protection exports grew 44%; exports >40% of revenue; diversified global presence across 80-90 countries; rupee traded INR94.5-96.6 in Q2; conservative hedging
items.quote: Coromandel Crop Protection business exports growth has been 44%, and the revenue share has been more than 40%.

items.statement: Working capital managed well in Q2; subsidy receipts prompt - received till September 4th week; INR3,086 crore received in Q2, INR1,200 crore in October; subsidy outstanding INR3,535 crore vs INR3,199 crore last year
items.quote: During the quarter, company received INR3,086 crores towards subsidy claims. Government has been prompt in clearing all the subsidy dues. As of today, we have received subsidy claims till the September fourth week.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; forex hedging conservative; rupee range INR94.5-96.6 in Q2
items.quote: With regard to forex, during the Q2, rupee traded in a range of about INR94.5 - INR96.6. Coromandel continues to hedge its exposure on a conservative basis.

items.statement: El Niño impact on Kharif; rainfall deficit 20-30% in key markets; ammonia price spike risk; state bans on non-subsidy products; Framework for Fertilizer Sale operational challenges
items.quote: Deficit rainfall in key markets, rupee depreciation, elevated raw material prices, lower NBS rates, and weak consumption impacted the operating environment.

items.statement: Dhaksha drone business: new agri drone variants launched; scaling volumes through retail; drone spraying driving liquid fertilizer/agrochemical volumes; defence drone registration underway; sector growing at 25% CAGR
items.quote: This sector is growing at the annual CAGR of 25%, and not many established players are there. We have created a large ecosystem and are trying to develop indigenous vendors.

items.statement: 300 MW Phase II power expansion at MEL targeting commissioning in July 2027
items.quote: Our 300 megawatt Phase II power expansion at MEL continues to advance, with commissioning targeted for July 2027.

items.statement: Integrated sugar complex at Kawambwa estimated at USD200 million with 50/50 debt-equity financing
items.quote: The integrated sugar project is estimated to cost around USD200 million. That is getting financed as a 50/50 debt-equity ratio.

items.statement: 100 MW solar plant in Zambia commissioned 88 MW as of call date, full 100 MW expected by month-end
items.quote: As of date, we have commissioned 88 megawatt, and by, I think, this month end, we would have the entire 100 megawatt flowing to the grid.

items.statement: Indian power plants operating at PLF of 82% or higher
items.quote: In India, our energy operations deliver healthy performance, with all the power plants operating at a PLF of 82% or higher.

items.statement: Phase II plant expected to reach 80%+ PLF within 2-3 months; Phase I to undergo major overhaul unit by unit
items.quote: We should be pretty instant in terms of what we planned on achieving is going up to 80% and over in terms of PLF in a couple of months, say about two to three months.

items.statement: 150 MW merchant capacity in India largely contracted through bilateral contracts until May
items.quote: Moreover, I think we have concluded, through bilateral contracts up until May, most of the available surplus.

items.statement: Operating margin impacted by forex losses on capital advances due to Kwacha depreciation
items.quote: When it comes to our operating profit, certain capital advances have resulted into forex losses impacting the operational margin.

items.statement: Zambia 100 MW solar plant receiving emergency tariff of USD0.09/kWh for first year from September
items.quote: For the first year, we are receiving an emergency tariff of USD0.09, which has commenced from September onwards.

items.statement: Zambia Phase I tariff escalates annually based on US CPI
items.quote: So that's an annual increase based on US CPI. So that's an annual increase that we experienced basically during the start of September.

items.statement: Zambia Kwacha depreciated 8% QoQ, reducing deferred tax liability but causing forex losses on capital advances
items.quote: Zambia Kwacha depreciated by 8% when compared to the previous quarter. That is one good thing for us. The current Deferred Tax Liability has come down on account of this Kwacha depreciation.

items.statement: Peak debt for Zambia projects at USD450 million with 3-year moratorium and 7-year repayment
items.quote: The peak debt is USD450 million. The repayment period is three plus seven years. Three years moratorium, and seven years repayment period. So, total 10 years is the repayment period.

items.statement: Average debt level expected around USD300-350 million over next four years as drawdowns and repayments overlap
items.quote: Over a period of time, we could expect about 300 million, 300 million-350 million as the number that we could probably talk about in the next four years.

items.statement: Cash balance over INR2,000 crores held in dollar accounts for Zambia project payments, earning ~4.5% interest
items.quote: These monies are drawn from the lenders for Phase II project in Zambia. It is in dollar terms. There is some kind of dollar deficiency there in African countries. That is why we wanted to secure our funds there in our current accounts. And these dollars are yielding interest around 4.5% or so.

items.statement: M&A opportunities being evaluated; will inform market when projects presented to board
items.quote: That we are currently looking at, and once these projects are presented to the board, we will let the wider community know.

items.statement: ZESCO receivables recovery of USD10.5 million, remaining balance USD2.6 million
items.quote: Another positive development has been the recovery of USD10.5 million in outstanding receivables from ZESCO as on date, bringing the remaining balance down to only USD2.6 million.

items.statement: Mining PAT flat YoY due to Kwacha depreciation forex loss and higher fuel costs
items.quote: The PAT was flat on the mining division because there is a forex loss with the Kwacha depreciating, and then mining costs have increased with increased fuel costs.

items.statement: Resumed silicomanganese production at Odisha operations
items.quote: We have also resumed silicomanganese production at our Odisha operations.

items.statement: Avocado operations in Zambia preparing for first commercial harvest and sales
items.quote: On the agribusiness front, our avocado operations in Zambia are preparing for its first commercial harvest and sales.

items.statement: Lithium exploration in Zambia: land dispute resolved, drilling to commence taking close to a year
items.quote: In terms of the lithium mine, like I said, there was a hurdle, a certain land dispute that has been resolved. So now we will undertake drilling activities. Drilling activities will take close to a year.

items.statement: Manganese concession in Côte d'Ivoire: 2 sq km exploration results encouraging, converting to exploitation license
items.quote: We have done detailed exploration in a small area, which is of 2 square kilometer, and the results of which were encouraging. So, while we also continue to explore the remaining areas, we are right now under the process of converting that from exploration to exploitation, so mining can actually begin.

items.statement: Phase I major overhaul maintenance to start around May, each unit shutdown ~2 months
items.quote: I am not going to commit on the months, but it is approximately around May timeframe that the shutdowns are going to start. Each shutdown for each unit takes about two months.

items.statement: Other income includes INR45 crore fair value gain from Singapore restructuring (fluctuating) plus interest income
items.quote: Part of that other income consists of fair market value gain at the Singapore company level in respect of two downstream subsidiaries, which are kind of restructured. That provision will keep fluctuating. The amount is about INR45 crores.

items.statement: Renewable projects in Zambia under evaluation but not yet disclosed
items.quote: Currently, there are certain renewable projects that we are looking at. But until they take shape, I would not want to talk further on them. But there are couple of projects that are currently being considered, evaluated.

items.statement: Cash flow from new projects to fund equity commitments for agri projects and concept-stage opportunities
items.quote: We are also catering a certain amount for other projects that are still in the concept stage.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target above 30% near term and towards 40% long term once renovated portfolio complete
items.quote: Together with continued cost discipline, these keep us firmly focused on taking our EBITDA margin above 30% in the near term and towards our long-term benchmark of 40% once the renovated portfolio is complete.

items.statement: Renovation budget on track at INR110-115 crores total; Courtyard Phase 1 complete, convention center Phase 2 on track for December completion, Marriott rooms Phase 3 planned for FY28
items.quote: So we are on track to -- so we completed Courtyard and we are on track to complete the convention center also within about INR100 crores, about INR110 crores to INR115 crores. So that is what we are at now. So we're sticking to the budget we had presented earlier. And the Marriott budget also, we're just going to stick to that INR40 crores to upgrade the rooms.

items.statement: Hyderabad RevPAR up 19-20% in September driven by global capability centers taking 37% of July-September office leasing; branded room demand outpacing new supply
items.quote: Hyderabad remains one of the country's strongest business hotel markets with September RevPAR up around 19% to 20%. The driver is global capability centers. They took record office space in the first 9 months of the year, and Hyderabad accounted for about 37% of July-September leasing.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin expanded 221 bps to 26.5%; Q2 margin 26.7% despite INR2 crore EBITDA loss from convention center closure and INR66 lakh Vayu launch cost
items.quote: For the first half, total income grew 61% to INR94 crores and EBITDA grew at 81% to INR24.7 crores with EBITDA margin expanding by 221 basis points to 26.5%.

items.statement: Convention center ramp-up expected within 9 months (by Q3 FY28) vs typical 18 months; targets 2x banquet revenue with 18-24 month payback
items.quote: We expect our ramp-up time to be half of that, like within 9 months of being live, I think we'll be at full throttle, which is basically also coincides with your strongest quarters. So I think by Q3 next year, we will be at full occupancy and like extremely high ADRs for any business that is coming through the convention business.

items.statement: Combined ADR rose 9% QoQ to INR6,655; Executive Apartments ADR grew 12% YoY to INR15,337; Courtyard new rooms sell at 35-40% premium to old inventory
items.quote: In terms of the parity, we sell the newer inventory at about 35% to 40% higher than the older rooms.

items.statement: Room revenue grew 39% YoY in Q2; F&B down 20% due to convention center closure; Executive Apartments room revenue 75%+ of total, F&B growing via corporate catering to GCCs
items.quote: But what we've recently also started doing is a lot of catering to the likes of Genpact and some of these other GCCs that are in the micro market. So that's where we have scope in terms of increasing the F&B contribution in that hotel.

items.statement: Marriott/Courtyard complex: 85% domestic, 15% foreign; Executive Apartments: 20-30% foreign; Q2 saw return of Middle East business paused in Q1
items.quote: In terms of the mix between foreign and domestic demand, usually, our complex that is Marriott and Courtyard runs at about 85% domestic business versus 15% of foreign business. That percentage contribution in our Marriott Executive Apartments, which is in a different micro market is slightly different, where 20% to 30% of that business comes from foreign demand versus domestic demand.

items.statement: Operating profit before working capital changes doubled to INR24 crores in H1; operating cash flow INR18.1 crores with higher payables and lower receivables
items.quote: On cash generation, operating profit before working capital changes more than doubled to INR24 crores in the first half.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds INR105.8 crores; INR80.25 crores repaid in early October reducing debt to INR182 crores; blended rate 9.15%, tenure 10-12 years; FY28 interest cost ~INR17 crores
items.quote: Yes. The loan tenure is ranging from 10 to 12 years and the blended rate is 9.15%. And in the month of October, in the first week, we have repaid INR80.25 crores of the loan. So that brings down the overall debt to INR182 crores.

items.statement: Completed INR105.8 crores rights issue oversubscribed 1.19x; shares allotted 15 September; proceeds primarily for debt repayment and meeting SEBI 25% minimum public shareholding
items.quote: We completed our INR105 crores rights issue, which was oversubscribed 1.19x. And I want to thank every shareholder who participated for your confidence in us. The issue brings our public shareholding in line with the regulatory requirements, and most of the proceeds are going towards reducing debt, which gives us more room to grow.

items.statement: Equity share capital rose from INR67.6 to INR76.8 crores; promoter holding reduced from 84.11% to 74.03% to meet SEBI 25% MPS; no further dilution planned unless opportunities arise
items.quote: See, the main reason was to come to the SEBI requirement, and that's why the dilution was done, even though the debt level which we had before was sustainable, and we were very comfortable with that. Since no new acquisitions were there, the strategy was to pay down the debt on the books and raise the capital so that we can meet the SEBI requirement of 75%.

items.statement: Scouting distressed assets, operating assets outside Hyderabad, and brownfield projects; also evaluating government land parcels for greenfield with caution
items.quote: So the strategy is still to find these good sweet deals in the distressed market and add it to our portfolio. But because of the 3 years of very good run in the hospitality industry, there's not much stress. So we're not getting such good deals, but we are still scouting for them on an everyday basis, and that is our first number 1 priority if something comes up.

items.statement: Combined RevPAR grew 39% YoY to INR5,272 in Q2 (twice industry pace); Courtyard RevPAR up 2.5x to INR5,711 at 87.4% occupancy; Executive Apartments RevPAR up 17% to INR13,461 at 88% occupancy
items.quote: Combined RevPAR across Marriott and Courtyard grew 39%, roughly twice the industry's pace. Much of this came from Courtyard, which, with all the 168 rooms back in service after Phase 1 ran at over 87% occupancy.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR110.5 crores at H1 end (up from INR19.4 crores); INR80.25 crores debt repaid in October; balance for convention center capex and operations
items.quote: So out of INR105.83 crores, we have repaid INR80.25 crores of debt in the month of October, first week of October. And the balance funds are earmarked for utilizing it for the capex for the convention center and for the daily operations.

items.statement: Promoter holding reduced from 84.11% to 74.03% via rights issue where promoters did not participate; done to meet SEBI minimum public shareholding requirement
items.quote: equity share capital rose from INR67.6 crores to INR76.8 crores with the rights issue, in which the promoters will not participate, taking promoters holding from earlier 84.11% to 74.03%.

items.statement: West Asia conflict kept international arrivals subdued; convention center closure cost INR2 crore EBITDA per quarter; Marriott room renovation in FY28 may disrupt operations
items.quote: The conflict in West Asia has kept international arrivals subdued, but with most demand coming from within India, the impact has been contained. Part of this growth also reflects a softer base last year.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 17.68% within indicated 15%-18% range; expect modest margin decline for 2-3 quarters as new capacity costs absorb
items.quote: The quarter's margin was within the 15%-18% range we had indicated earlier. We are encouraged by this performance while recognizing that the cost of bringing new capacity into operation will influence margins over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target 15%-18% for non-regulated markets; regulated markets target 18%-22%
items.quote: We have consistently said that our long-term margin target in this industry is 15%-18%, and we are currently within that range.

items.statement: Tarapur Phase II greenfield facility commissioned 24 Sep 2026; fully staffed and operational
items.quote: We also commenced production in Phase II of our Tarapur greenfield facility on 24 September 2026, completing the commissioning of the project.

items.statement: New Tarapur Phase II facility expects 30%-40% utilization over next 2-3 quarters; can accommodate both regulated and unregulated demand for at least 3 years
items.quote: We currently expect utilization to reach approximately 30%-40% over the next two to three quarters, subject to customer demand, product mix and the pace of production ramp-up.

items.statement: Phase I commissioned last year already contributing to sales ramp-up; further capex decision within a year if capacity exceeded
items.quote: To remind you, Phase I was commissioned last year, and we have already been meeting part of the demand from that facility. It has contributed significantly to our ability to ramp up sales in the current year.

items.statement: 17 regulatory filings in Europe (9 approved: 4 CEP + 5 ASMF); 9 US VMFs filed; target completion of EU transfer program by end CY2027
items.quote: We have four CEP approvals and have filed CEP applications for four more products. We also have five ASMF approvals, with four more applications filed. That makes a total of 17 filings, of which nine are currently approved.

items.statement: US customer expected to complete filings by Dec 2026; EU business critical mass expected 2028-2030; may miss FY27 Europe revenue target of Rs 50-60 cr
items.quote: We might therefore miss the target we set for the current year, hopefully not by a very large margin. As I said, we anticipate the business reaching critical mass only between 2028 and 2030.

items.statement: Q2 revenue Rs 158.71 cr (+32% YoY, +14% QoQ) driven primarily by volumes; H1 revenue Rs 297.87 cr (+33% YoY); international market growing 10%-12%
items.quote: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was Rs. 158.71 crores, an increase of 32% over the corresponding quarter last year and 14% over Q1 FY27. Revenue also exceeded the Rs. 149.23 crores reported in Q4 FY26. Growth continued to be led primarily by volumes, supported by demand across our

items.statement: Inventory destocking cycle (2023-2025) complete; expect very strong growth in non-regulated markets going forward
items.quote: We believe that inventory adjustment is now complete. Going forward, we see very strong growth in this segment.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA Rs 28.06 cr (+64% YoY), margin 17.68% vs 14.27% YoY and 16.73% QoQ; improvement from partial price pass-through and fixed cost absorption
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 64% year-on-year to Rs. 28.06 crores. The EBITDA margin was 17.68%, compared with 14.27% a year earlier and 16.73% in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin at 55%-56% last two quarters (historical range 50%-55%); expect to remain within 50%-55% range going forward
items.quote: It is very difficult to say because the long-term gross margin has always been in the 50%-55% range. We are probably at the upper end of the spectrum currently. Going forward, it should remain within that range, although it can move up or down by a couple of percentage points.

items.statement: No price increases expected for next 3-5 quarters; Fluralaner prices may erode further for ~6 months then stabilize
items.quote: I do not see that possibility in the near future, at least for the next three to five quarters. I do not expect prices to rise over that period.

items.statement: Fuel costs up due to gas usage; transportation costs nearly doubled last 6 months due to Gulf War; hope increases temporary
items.quote: Within other expenses, the main increase has been in fuel costs because we use gas as fuel at a couple of our plants. Distribution expenses have also increased, as logistics costs have risen sharply over the last six months due to the Gulf War. Our transportation costs have nearly doubled.

items.statement: Animal health APIs ~95% of revenue; top 10 customers ~26% of sales; top 10 products ~65% of sales
items.quote: Animal health APIs remain the core of NGL, accounting for approximately 95% of revenue this year. Our top 10 customers contributed approximately 26% of sales, and our top 10 products contributed approximately 65%.

items.statement: H1 operating cash flow Rs 35.80 cr; inventories rose from Rs 70.28 cr (Mar) to Rs 118.38 cr (Sep) due to make-to-stock shift and Gulf disruption buffer; expect inventory pressure to ease in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Inventories increased from Rs. 70.28 crores at the end of March to Rs. 118.38 crores at the end of September. This reflects higher business activity and the stock required to support the new facility and our sales growth.

items.statement: Total borrowings ~Rs 122 cr vs Rs 108 cr end FY26; expect short-term debt to rise slightly for working capital; no increase in long-term debt expected
items.quote: Total borrowings were approximately Rs. 122 crores, compared with Rs. 108 crores at the end of FY26.

items.statement: Depreciation to increase ~Rs 3 cr more vs H1; finance costs not to exceed 20% increase from current; 50% plant staffing in place, remaining 50% to be added
items.quote: Compared with the half year just ended, we anticipate a further increase in depreciation of probably no more than about Rs. 3 crores.

items.statement: EU: 4 CEP approved, 4 CEP filed, 5 ASMF approved, 4 ASMF filed (17 total, 9 approved); target all 17 approvals by end CY2027
items.quote: By the end of the next calendar year, definitely, yes.

items.statement: US: 9 VMFs filed; customer to complete filings by Dec 2026; plant audit timing 3 months to 1 year after filing; USFDA approves plant not products
items.quote: Our customer is expected to complete its filings by December 2026. This is an important step in progressing the regulatory process, but the timing of an inspection and subsequent commercialization remains dependent on the regulator, customer requirements and satisfactory completion of the applicable reviews.

items.statement: EU customer onboarding slower than expected (2-3 years post-approval); US sponsor customer eager; several dual-market customers waiting for US audit outcome
items.quote: Customer acquisition has not been as fast as we anticipated. It is taking two to three years to onboard customers after receiving regulatory approval.

items.statement: Regulated markets mature with established supply chains; must win business via better value proposition (dual EU/US registrations, integrated chain, pricing)
items.quote: There are no readily available gaps that we can simply step into. This is a mature market, and most of our products have been off patent for a substantial period. Established supply chains already exist, so we need to win business by offering a better value proposition.

items.statement: International animal health API market growing 10%-12% currently
items.quote: We feel growth is quite substantial; the international market is currently growing at a healthy 10%-12%.

items.statement: Margin pressure for 2-3 quarters as new capacity costs absorb; regulatory approval timelines uncertain; geopolitical logistics costs; price erosion risk on Fluralaner
items.quote: We therefore expect some pressure on margins during this transition. Higher volumes should support earnings over time, but the pace of improvement will depend on utilization, realizations and operating efficiency.

items.statement: FY27 PAT guidance raised to ₹775-800 crore from earlier ₹700-750 crore
items.quote: I think we'll probably be a little less than ₹800 crores of PAT. I think we'd like to bump it up a little bit. I think it will be between ₹775 to ₹800 crores is what I feel.

items.statement: FY28 topline growth expected around 10-15% driven by ROW and US business
items.quote: But we expect to grow around 10%-15%. I think that's our expectation. But I think more precise guidance will give closer to the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Annual capex run rate ₹350-400 crore; ₹300 crore spent in H1 FY27 on Chennai, Mekaguda API facilities, Nagarjuna Sagar oncology line, semaglutide cartridge line
items.quote: I think we target about ₹400 crore worth of Capex every year. We are upgrading our Chennai and Mekaguda facilities, our API facilities. Our API new blocks we have built, so that has taken away most of the cash.

items.statement: New oncology line at Nagarjuna Sagar site started production; semaglutide cartridge line to be ready next financial year
items.quote: We added a new oncology line in our Nagarjuna Sagar site, just coming to market. We just started production now. And also we are setting up a cartridge line to make semaglutide internally, so that Capex is also ongoing. That line will get ready next financial year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 30.4%; management says current margin level is sustainable base
items.quote: I think so, Rashmi. I think where things are going, I think, yeah, this is a sustainable base. Yes, absolutely.

items.statement: Domestic formulation base business ₹130-135 crore per quarter; Q2 was ₹145 crore including Semaglutide stocking; expect 15-20% growth next year
items.quote: Domestic is like, I would say about Rs 130 to Rs 135 Crore would probably be the domestic base, is what probably we're running at. This particular quarter was Rs 145 Crore, but I think there's a little bit of stocking of Semaglutide, which it's not going to be repeatable.

items.statement: Earnings more diversified: South Africa, Brazil, base US business contributing; less concentrated on Lenalidomide
items.quote: I think a good portion has come from South Africa, a good portion has come from Brazil, a good portion has come from a base US business. And this has come even without Lenalidomide being in the numbers. So, I think that way it's more well diversified earnings.

items.statement: Semaglutide India pricing very competitive, not profitable near term; vial ₹1.2-1.5 crore/month, pen ₹40-50 lakh/month; volume share ~5-6%, value share ~3%
items.quote: It's been bad. I think it's not been great, honestly. I think everybody's trying to get market share. So, the pricing has been really bad. I think everybody's hoping that you just stick in there and then hope get that 5-6% share and just hope that the wave gets better over a period of time in the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Adcock Ingram: acquired additional 13.25% stake in July 2026, total 49%; Q2 share of profit ₹29.2 crore after PPA adjustment; steady state PAT contribution estimated ₹55-60 crore/quarter
items.quote: In July 2026, we acquired additional 13.25% stake in Adcock Ingram Holding Limited, taking our total holdings to 49%. This further strengthens our strategic position in South African market and enhances our participation in the performance of Adcock Ingram.

items.statement: India DSO 90-120 days expected to continue; consolidated tax rate 29-30%, standalone 27-27.2%
items.quote: Coming to the working capital, yes, I think it is a mix of, if we just look at from our India business perspective, I think the DSO would be between 90-120 days. And that is the range we expect to continue.

items.statement: All loans repaid after rights issue proceeds; net cash position ₹2,250 crore as of today
items.quote: So, in terms of the loan, yes, as of September 30, we did have loan. But once we raised the funds, we have repaid the entire loan. So, as on today, we don't have any loans right now.

items.statement: Rights issue completed last month with 10% dilution; proceeds used to reduce Adcock acquisition debt, working capital, and for possible acquisitions
items.quote: It's already done; Rights is already done. So, I think this was done last month. So, it was already completed. There's a dilution. Yes, there was a dilution, but we gave opportunity for all the shareholders to participate. There was a dilution of 10%.

items.statement: Actively pursuing one acquisition transaction; spent ~₹3,500 crore on acquisitions in last 4-5 years; have first right of refusal on remaining 51% of Adcock
items.quote: We are trying, Subhash. We are trying one transaction. We are running it, I think, quite seriously. Hopefully, we will be able to close it. But, again, it is all subject to all the regulatory and all the agreements getting done. But we are. Yes, we are actually trying to do one more transaction.

items.statement: Steady dividend policy unchanged; dividend not linked to rights issue fund raise
items.quote: We've been giving steady dividend, Digvijay. This is no different from what policy we've had in the past. I don't think we are really...Raising the funds is not anywhere linked with the dividend.

items.statement: Adcock Ingram appointed new CEO Rhulani from Pfizer; prescription business uptick seen
items.quote: He is Mr. Rhulani. So, he has been appointed recently. He comes from very good experience in Innovator Pharma. I think he was with Pfizer, I think was his last job before he joined us. He is a good person, and I think he has a lot of experience in prescription business, which has been the weakness of Adcock.

items.statement: R&D spend 8-10% of topline; FY27 expected ₹300-350 crore vs ₹400+ crore last year; Q2 high, Q3 expected higher
items.quote: Last year, obviously, our R&D spend was more than ₹400 crore. This year, overall, it would be 8 to 10% of our top line. So, we may end up around ₹300 to ₹350 crore, depending on how the programme runs.

items.statement: Pomalidomide first-to-file shared with 5-6 competitors; steep price erosion limited earnings bump despite 180-day exclusivity
items.quote: We did get the first-to-file, Shekhar. But it is a shared first-to-file. I don't remember the exact number of generic competitors. I think about 5 to 6 generic competitors came in the first wave. Because there were 5 and 6 competitors, the price erosion was quite steep.

items.statement: Crop Health Sciences demerger delayed 4-6 months due to rights issue capital structure change; refiling with SEBI; target mid-calendar 2027
items.quote: Because of that, we have to resubmit the file to SEBI. So, it pushes out by 4 to 6 months from the original plan. So, we're looking at maybe by mid-year, calendar year next year is when we hope to get the demerger done.

items.statement: Upcoming launches: Carfilzomib (60mg shared FTF, one lower strength sole FTF), Trabectedin (one of two FTF), Olaparib in Brazil/Canada; Imbruvica settled and approved with exclusivity
items.quote: For one is definitely Carfilzomib launch is there. It is coming up in the next few quarters. And of which one strength we have first-to-file. 60 mg is shared first-to-file and then we have Trabectedin coming up, which is a smaller product. But we are one among the two first-to-file. Then we have, these are 2 major ones in the US and then we are expecting launch of Olaparib also in the next few qua

items.statement: Semaglutide US: settled with innovator, answering FDA queries, no approval yet; exclusivity subject to FDA clarity
items.quote: Yeah, we do not have an approval yet, Rahul. We are answering some queries from the FDA. Subject to us answering the queries and getting the clarity from the FDA, then we can speak about our exclusivity. But at this time, we do not have approval.

items.statement: eGenesis investment: substantial single-digit stake, <$25 million; monetization via India license or IPO; Phase III data readout expected in 12 months
items.quote: Regarding stake percentage, I'm not supposed to disclose. So, it's a substantial single digit stake. So, that's all I can say. And in terms of, little less than $25 million into the entity.

items.statement: Carfilzomib 60mg has multiple filers (6+), limiting exclusivity value; lower strengths have sole FTF due to later approval dates
items.quote: So, let us start with carfilzomib. There are 3 strengths in carfilzomib. So, majority sale is the 60 mg. There is 60 mg, there is 30 mg, and there is 10 mg. So, 60 mg has, I think, I do not remember exactly, about 6 filers, I think, or multiple filers.

items.statement: Crop Health Sciences: Q2 marginal profit ₹10 lakh; 15-17% revenue growth YoY; targeting 15-20% full year growth despite El Niño impact
items.quote: But having said that, Kunal, again, there are multiple things. We are also battling few other credit-related provisions that we have taken. So, from a business perspective, I would say last year to this year about 15%-17% growth. But our aspirations were even much higher.

items.statement: Adcock Q2 PAT lower due to seasonal flu effect in Q1, ₹6.5 crore PPA amortization from additional 13.25% stake, and VRS one-time charge
items.quote: This quarter, obviously, we had the additional acquisition of 13.25% and we had to do purchase price location. There's a one-off amortization because of that allocation, which is around ₹6.5 crores.

items.statement: Rights issue completed with 10% dilution; all shareholders given participation opportunity
items.quote: There's a dilution. Yes, there was a dilution, but we gave opportunity for all the shareholders to participate. There was a dilution of 10%.

items.statement: ROW business driven by MENA, Canada stable with big launches expected in 2027, Brazil 80% growth this year
items.quote: I think ROW business, especially the MENA region, has done well. And Canada has been stable. It has not increased, but we have some big launches coming up in '2027. So, we expect '2027 will be a blowout year in Canada. And Brazil also continues to do well. And I think we had almost 80% growth in Brazil-based business this year.

items.statement: R&D spend increase driven by programme milestones, FDA facility fees, legal expenses; unpredictable quarter to quarter
items.quote: So, Abdul, largely, the reasons are primarily R&D spend itself. But there are a couple of other spends as well, like annual FDA facility fees and programme fees are also there. And there are some legal expenses etc. But large portion of the increase is R&D. That's how I'd put it.

items.statement: Agro-chemical business expected to lose ~₹20 crore at EBITDA level in FY27; loss embedded in PAT guidance
items.quote: So, we expect that the Agro business will lose about ₹20 crore at EBITDA level. So, that is already embedded in the earnings. So, when we give a PAT guidance, the loss of the Agro is part of the PAT guidance.

items.statement: NRC-2694 Phase-I done; Phase-II strategy being re-evaluated; no timeline for commercialization
items.quote: As of now, no, Subhash. I think we are still trying to redo the strategy. So, we've done some Phase-I data, so I think now we're trying to see what the right strategy is in terms of what our Phase-II strategy should be. At this time, I have nothing to report.

items.statement: Adcock Ingram laid off staff in one factory line; one-time charge reflected in Adcock earnings
items.quote: They have laid off some people recently in one of the lines, I think. And that one-time charge is already reflected in Adcock's earning, yes. Yes, in one particular factory this has happened. Yes, that's correct.

items.statement: International generics base revenue ~₹800-850 crore/quarter; Q2 ₹1,019 crore includes one-time sale
items.quote: No, I am saying consol numbers. Consol numbers are about ₹1,000 crores. So, what I am saying is that base is around ₹800-₹850 crores, and then we always get these one-times, so that is why it is up to ₹1,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects gold loan AUM growth of 25%-30% in FY27
items.quote: We expect gold loan growth of 25% to 30% this year, supported by branch expansion and digital channels, and governed by the same appraisal and loan-to-value and custody standards.

items.statement: Targets ROA of 3.5%-4% and ROE of 15%-18%
items.quote: We told ROA to be somewhere between 3.5% to 4% and ROE between 15% to 18%. We stick to that.

items.statement: Expects cost of borrowing to increase 25-30 bps by Q4 FY27 exit
items.quote: from an overall Q4 exit, you could probably expect my cost of borrowing to go up more towards the 9% handle. And that is in line with what was communicated in the Q1 call as well. So, that is what we are holding to, that in terms of the exit cost of borrowing will probably increase by about 25 to 30 basis points.

items.statement: Plans to add 500 branches by March 2027; 100 opened in H1, 250 more in progress
items.quote: We plan to add around 500 branches by March 2027 to our existing consolidated network of 5,375 branches.

items.statement: Branch opening work in full swing for 250 branches; confident of reaching 500 target
items.quote: Even though we have opened nearly 100 branches so far, another 250 branches, the work is in the full swing, and we expect that to be opened in another couple of months. We are really confident about reaching 500 branches with regard to branch opening.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM at INR73,303 crores, up 5.3% QoQ and 60.1% YoY
items.quote: Our consolidated AUM for Q2 FY27 was INR73,303 crores, up 5.3% sequentially and 60.1% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM at INR60,640 crores, up 6.4% QoQ and 92.5% YoY
items.quote: Gold loan continues to be our key growth driver with an AUM of INR60,640 crores, up 6.4% quarter-on-quarter and 92.5% year-on-year, supported by strong customer demand.

items.statement: Added 3.15 lakh new gold loan customers; total customers at 27.2 lakh, up 2.9% QoQ and 11.7% YoY
items.quote: Strong momentum in customer acquisition continued, and we were able to add INR3.15 lakh new customers. Our outstanding number of customers was INR27.2 lakh, an increase of 2.9% quarter-on-quarter and 11.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross yield on EMI and bullet loans combined expected at 17.5%-18.5%
items.quote: The gross yield on the EMI and the bullet payment combined will remain somewhere around 17.5%-18.5%. That is the expectation. Yield will remain somewhere within that range.

items.statement: Expects gold loan yields to settle around 17%-18% in three years
items.quote: I expect that to be somewhere in the range of in three years, maybe around 17% in three years. But all depends on the borrowing cost, how it is going to be, the borrowing cost, the policy. Accordingly, then that can be changed also. It can be even 18%, even more also.

items.statement: Pricing remains one of the lowest in industry; not engaging in price war
items.quote: Regarding the pricing, our pricing remains one of the lowest in the industry. We are able to look at our customer acquisition and tonnage increase.

items.statement: Board-approved pricing policy with floor and ceiling; reviewed periodically
items.quote: Yeah. See, we have the board-approved policy. We go by the board-approved policy. Yes, this changes from time to time with regard to the market rate, etcetera. It is taken to the board and that takes the board approval. So, it is all market-related. Yeah.

items.statement: Gold loan Stage 2 at ~5% of AUM, up from ~50 bps in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Stage 2, I would say it is about 5% or thereabouts. Sanket: Okay. Buvanesh Tharashankar: This is on the gold AUM

items.statement: Stage 2 spike attributed to new EMI/short-tenor products; early reads show customers regularizing
items.quote: It is largely behavioral, right? in April, you had this change to regulations that came into effect, and you had a set of new products that were launched, which were the shorter tenor and the EMI-based products. These products are something that the customers have never experienced before. They are used to the traditional one-year consumption kind of loan, which is traditionally a bullet payment,

items.statement: Microfinance net NPA improved to 1.1% from 1.4% QoQ; Asirvad CRAR 29.2%
items.quote: Net NPA is at 1.1% versus 1.4% in Q1 FY27. Asirvad CRAR as at September 30th stood at 29.2%.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio LTV stable at 64.5% vs 65.6% QoQ
items.quote: Our average gold loan LTV remains stable at 64.5% in Q2 versus 65.6% in Q1.

items.statement: Auction amount INR100 crores in Q2; INR115 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: Auction amount is nearly INR100 crores in this quarter. Gold price is on this quarter two is INR13,526 crores.

items.statement: Gold price per gram at INR13,526 in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Gold price mentioned earlier is INR13,526.

items.statement: Online gold loan book constitutes 91% of total gold loan book
items.quote: Online gold loan book constitutes about 91% of the total gold loan book.

items.statement: CEO resigned on personal grounds; new CEO to join Jan 1, 2027; CTO resigned due to travel
items.quote: Regarding the operational aspect of CEO, the earlier CEO has resigned on personal ground, etcetera,. New CEO is expected to take charge. The recruitment is already over, and he is expected to take charge from 1st of January. The CTO also resigned due to frequent travel between Mumbai and

items.statement: No attrition among new recruits; stability in new hires
items.quote: Other than that, from the new recruitment, there is no attrition. There is great stability with regard to new recruitments. These are the two attrition levels.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR1 per share for Q2 FY27
items.quote: Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.statement: Opex to AUM expected to decline despite 500 branch additions; employee cost to AUM to fall
items.quote: When we add 500 branches, we do not expect much of the employee cost to increase because we are in the process of rationalizing the field employees. We do not expect that. The opex to AUM will come down even in spite of opening 500 branches. The employee cost to AUM will come down.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT before OCI and minority interest INR701 crores, up 20% QoQ and 223% YoY
items.quote: For Q2, consolidated PAT before OCI and minority interest was INR701 crores, which is up 20% sequentially and 223% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone PAT before OCI INR665 crores, up 20% QoQ and 77% YoY
items.quote: For the quarter, our standalone PAT before OCI and minority interest was INR665 crores, which is up 20% sequentially and up 77% year-on-year.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 22.36% vs regulatory requirement of 15%
items.quote: Our capital position is strong and our capital adequacy is at 22.36%.

items.statement: Standalone borrowing cost down 2 bps QoQ
items.quote: Standalone borrowing cost has gone down by 2 basis points in the second quarter.

items.statement: Asirvad MFI disbursements INR1,461 crores vs INR1,055 crores QoQ; new book proportion 79%
items.quote: For the quarter, MFI disbursements was at INR1,461 crores versus INR1,055 crores in the prior quarter. The proportion of the new MFI book has gone up to 79% versus 68% in Q1 and 23% in Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Asirvad PAT before OCI INR32 crores vs INR21 crores QoQ; H1 FY27 PAT INR53 crores vs loss of INR436 crores YoY
items.quote: PAT before OCI was INR32 crores in Q2 FY27 versus INR21 crores in Q1 and a loss of INR168 crores in Q2 of last year. For the first half, Asirvad PAT was at INR53 crores versus loss of INR436 crores in the first half of last year.

items.statement: Microfinance disbursements paused; focus on collections and running down book; reassessment in April 2028
items.quote: In microfinance, we have paused credit disbursements. Our focus is on strengthening collection, protecting asset quality, and running down the existing book in an orderly manner. We reassess the business in April 2028.

items.statement: Gold loan book 90%+ bullet loans; EMI/short-tenor products <10% of incremental disbursements
items.quote: large component, I mean, the majority of our book is largely bullet. And given that, you know, these schemes are been recently introduced, you know, in the first quarter, they are a smaller component, both the IGGL and the EMI based loans, they are much smaller component. Majority is all bullet schemes. Nidhesh Jain: So majority basically 90

items.statement: New regulations in April led to launch of shorter tenor and EMI-based gold loan products
items.quote: in April, you had this change to regulations that came into effect, and you had a set of new products that were launched, which were the shorter tenor and the EMI-based products.

items.statement: Target 2030 roadmap: >15% volume growth, 20%+ revenue and profitability CAGR, EBITDA margins >8%, ROCE >20%, >60% revenue from value-added products
items.quote: Looking ahead, our target 2030 ramp-up roadmap remains focused on achieving over 15% of volume growth, 20% plus CAGR in revenue and profitability, EBITDA margins of over 8%, ROCE exceeding 20%, and deriving over 60% of revenue from value-added products.

items.statement: Copper cathode facility 36,000 tpa at Thervoy Kandigai, INR200 crore total investment, INR60 crore spent, fully funded by internal accruals
items.quote: We are establishing a 36,000 tons per annum copper cathode facility at our Thervoy Kandigai plant in Tamil Nadu, with a total investment of approximately INR200 crores, fully funded through internal accruals. Of the project outlay, around INR60 crores has already been incurred, with major equipment deliveries and key construction activities underway.

items.statement: Phase I 18,000 tpa copper cathode targeted for commissioning by Dec 2026, trial runs Q4 FY27; Phase II 18,000 tpa by Q3 FY28
items.quote: The project is executed in two phases, with phase I of 18,000 metric tons per annum targeted for commissioning by December 2026, followed by trial runs in Q4 FY27. Phase II, comprising the balance 18,000 metric tons per annum, is targeted by Q3 FY28.

items.statement: Incremental 6,000 tpa copper recycling capacity commissioned Q4 FY26 ramping to ~90% utilization in FY27; expanded 72,000 tpa lead capacity at 40% utilization in H1 FY27, expected to ramp to 70%
items.quote: The incremental 6,000 metric ton per annum copper recycling capacity commissioned in Q4 FY26 continues to ramp up well and is expected to achieve approximately 90% capacity utilization during FY27.
