items.statement: Tamil Nadu repowering policy formal approval pending; regulatory commission reconstituted 1.5 months ago; interim approvals used for current projects
items.quote: The formal approval of the repowering policy in Tamil Nadu has still not happened. The projects that we are doing, we are doing under a kind of interim approval pending the passing of the final approval through the regulatory commission.

items.statement: ~70% power sold to C&I customers in Tamil Nadu (auto, textiles, software); Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat sales to State Electricity Boards under long-term PPAs
items.quote: No, no, about 70% of our power we sell to in the C&I space, more than 70%, which is essentially industrial customers in Tamil Nadu. We have auto components. We have textiles. We have pretty much software.

items.statement: Electricity board collections improved significantly in last couple of years; prompt payments across country
items.quote: Although to give them credit in the last couple of years payments from the electricity boards has also been quite prompt. We used to face issues, and the industry also has not been facing issues on collections from electricity boards across the country.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic transactions for step change; conversations reopened after US market improvement; targeting deal by year-end; listed status creates MTM challenges for PE partners
items.quote: We are working very hard on some strategic transactions, so we hope to have something for you by the time we come to our, should we say, annual results. Beyond that, I don't think we can say.

items.statement: Significant action (dividend or acquisition) promised before end of FY27; excess cash INR 110-120 cr available for distribution once repowering complete and El Nino risk passes
items.quote: I think you will see some significant action from us before the end of this fiscal.

items.statement: Promoters supportive but no commitment to open market buying; management evaluating all options for value creation
items.quote: Well, we are looking at all the options.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds (Aug 2024) fully deployed for 24.6 MW solar; no fresh equity raise planned unless asset identified
items.quote: Whatever money we raised was primarily for new capacity, which is the solar capacity that we added. And some of the surplus from that has been used also for the wind, adding the wind to this thing.

items.statement: Wind generation dependent on monsoon/El Nino; Q3/Q4 historically weak; Tamil Nadu bureaucratic delays for grid connectivity; solar curtailment risk in afternoon
items.quote: At the end of the day, we are dependent on the environment and the monsoon. So, we have to have a substantial cushion so that even if we have a bad wind year, we are still very comfortable in our coverage to the bankers.

items.statement: Future growth wind-focused; solar expansion limited to hybrid with wind repowering due to grid curtailment and surplus solar capacity
items.quote: Therefore, we may not expand significantly our solar capacity except to the extent of hybrid within our wind repowering packages. Future growth will continue to be more wind-focused.

items.statement: Croatia 10 MW asset (51% stake, ~5 MW effective) generating cash; not material; no sale planned due to high transaction cost relative to size
items.quote: Cash accruals we have 51% of a 10 megawatt asset, so it is about effectively 5 megawatts of capacity that we own there. So, it is not material either way.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; team executing projects smoothly; active in wind power generators association for lobbying
items.quote: See, as a company, we are very active in the associations also. The wind power generators association. So, we lobby not just as OGPL, but we also lobby as an association.

items.statement: Land bank 1,000+ acres non-core (some pledged); avg value ~INR 5 lakh/acre; monetising selectively where bank permits and real estate value exceeds renewable value
items.quote: See, we have close to 1,000 acres of land which is not, but there are some parts maybe usable for future expansions, or some will be monetizable. But at that current pricing, wherever it is low, we expect that prices will go up.

items.statement: Expects growth in FY27 over FY26 and higher profitability; consolidated EBITDA roughly consistent with FY26
items.quote: we are looking at growth for the full year FY27 over FY26, and the profitability should be robust and higher than FY26 as well. This is going to be a mix of operating income performance as well as other income performance. But when we look at it on a consolidated basis, EBITDA should be roughly consistent with last year.

items.statement: Anticipates margin reversion in H2 FY27, Q4 better than Q3, driven by export and aftermarket mix
items.quote: we do anticipate a reversion to our mean, which would mean that the performance in Q3 and Q4 would be substantially better, Q4 more than Q3.

items.statement: Record quarterly order booking of ₹7.64 billion in Q2 FY27, up 17.2% YoY; exports 48% of bookings
items.quote: On the order booking front, we recorded our highest-ever quarterly order booking of ₹7.64 billion in the second quarter as compared to ₹6.52 billion in the second quarter of FY26, a growth of 17.2%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 order booking up 12.2% to ₹13.33 billion; exports 56% of bookings vs 42% YoY
items.quote: For the half year as well, our order booking was up 12.2% at ₹13.33 billion, and this is a reflection of strong international performance across the North American, European, Southeast Asian, and Turkish markets.

items.statement: Closing order book at ₹24.53 billion, up 10.5% YoY; exports 59.2% of book vs 50% YoY
items.quote: The closing order book stands at 10.5% higher than at the same point of the previous financial year, giving us confidence in the growth in the coming quarters, and this stands at ₹24.53 billion.

items.statement: Aftermarket closing order book more than doubled YoY to ₹6.39 billion, now 26% of total vs 14%
items.quote: The aftermarket business as well continued its strong momentum with the closing order book more than doubling to 105.4%, which is on a year-on-year basis, which is ₹6.39 billion on the back of contract wins in thermal, renewable, combined cycle, utility, as well as certain niche segments of geothermal and other value addition services that we provide.

items.statement: Gas turbine refurbishment contracts with potential $80-90 million over 4-5 years; only billable portion recognized each year
items.quote: the potential of these businesses in our international gas turbine contracts could be up to between $80 million to $90 million, this would play out over a 4 to 5 year period, and we would account for only that aspect of what can be billed in the current financial year from those contracts in that financial year

items.statement: Domestic market growing but market share declined in larger turbine segment (40-50 MW) due to competitor strength in steel sector
items.quote: Our principal competition is with the largest steam turbine manufacturer globally, who has an Indian operation. The competitive nature has not changed. The intensity is the same as it has been. It's just when demand comes up in certain market segments, the market share and historic installed base is different, and so therefore, the intensity varies from where demand comes from quarter to quarter.

items.statement: Enquiry book flat overall; US up substantially on data center, combined cycle, energy storage; Central South America down; Southeast Asia, Europe, India flat
items.quote: broadly, the number is about flat in terms of the Enquiry book. The US market has gone up quite substantially in terms of the Enquiry visibility, which is again split between data center combined cycle operations as well as other industrials. And what we are finding as a very new segment in the US is novel energy storage projects, carbon capture.

items.statement: Strong electrification theme driving demand: EVs, data centers, industrial power, high commodity prices
items.quote: Overall, the market for electrification is extremely robust, with newer market segments of electric vehicles and transportation, as well as data centers, adding to the entire requirement for electrification. The industrial requirement for power remains equally robust with high commodity prices.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 17.5% vs 26.3% YoY; PBT margin 15.4% vs 24.6%; PAT margin 10.4% vs 17.8%
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter was ₹858 million at a margin of 17.5% against the 26.3% of the previous quarter of the previous year. Profit before tax was down 39.2% at ₹757 million at a margin of 15.4% against 24.6% in the previous year. And profit after tax was down 41.7% at ₹533 million at a margin of 10.4%.

items.statement: Margin decline driven by domestic/export mix and product/aftermarket mix; H2 margins expected healthier with export/aftermarket contribution
items.quote: All of this has led to a decline in our reported EBITDA margins, PBT margins, and PAT margins, driven by the mix between domestic and export, as well as the mix between the product sales as well as aftermarket, both of which have been lower in the current quarter as well as the half year compared with the previous year.

items.statement: NTPC strategic order at low/negative margin; 15% billing left split equally Q3/Q4; no further margin impact expected
items.quote: That particular order, which constitutes a part of our domestic product billing for the current quarter, will diminish in the quarters to come. The amount of billing left on that order is approximately 15% of the order value, and it will be spread equally between Q3 and Q4 and will not impact margins, as we will have a significantly larger contribution of exports and aftermarket to the billing in

items.statement: R&D and personnel growth continues; advanced platforms being launched with better cost structure to improve margins in coming quarters
items.quote: Our new product and new technology developments also give us confidence that over the medium term, we will be able to strengthen our product portfolio to be able to be more diversified in a product stream to be able to cater to various different applications and solutions which our customers demand.

items.statement: Combined cycle gas turbine segment entry with 50 MW steam turbine order (150 MW plant); boiler feedwater pump drive turbine for supercritical thermal plants
items.quote: It's 50 MW capacity, and on a 3:1 basis, that would mean that it's a 150 MW gas turbine power plant, which would be in front of this steam turbine requirement. That requirement places us very well.

items.statement: Export share of revenue fell to 30% in Q2 from 55% YoY; domestic grew 51.8% to ₹3.4B; aftermarket revenue declined 16.7% to ₹1.48B
items.quote: For the second quarter, revenue from operations stood at ₹4.91 billion, 3% lower year-on-year, as strong domestic growth of 51.8% to ₹3.4 billion was offset by a 46.6% decline in export revenue to ₹1.51 billion. Export constituted 30% of revenue against 55% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Product revenue grew 4.4% to ₹3.43B; aftermarket declined 16.7% to ₹1.48B; H1 domestic sales up 40%, exports down 24%
items.quote: Product revenue grew 4.4% to ₹3.43 billion, while the aftermarket revenue declined to 16.7% to ₹1.48 billion.

items.statement: Marquee orders in combined cycle gas turbine and boiler feedwater pump segments; NTPC strategic order for long-duration energy storage to commission in Q4
items.quote: During the quarter, we made inroads in the combined cycle gas turbine segment, as well as boiler feedwater pump segment for thermal power plants. These are both marquee orders and it places the company well for future orders in this space.

items.statement: US subsidiary focused on aftermarket services for large installed base; may do packaging if tariffs justify; product supply from India for now
items.quote: The US market has possibly the largest capital stock of any country in the world, and so we want to cater to the requirements that they have for servicing aftermarket for their installed bases there. Will we do packaging? We have the flexibility to do packaging. It's a question that, would we respond to any tariffs and potential tariffs? We have the potential to do so.

items.statement: Middle East enquiry pipeline dipped in H1 due to war; expected to recover in Q3/Q4 as threat reduces
items.quote: In case of Middle East, due to the war-like situation in the H1, we saw some dip, but with the war threat coming down, we hope the Enquiry pipeline will increase in Q3, Q4.

items.statement: Solution-oriented approach may increase working capital intensity due to larger scope and different payment terms; financial discipline to be maintained
items.quote: It will naturally be a little bit more working capital-intensive because the scope is larger and therefore the payment terms will be different. As we go down, we have to ensure that if we do go this route, that we keep the financial discipline that is necessary.

items.statement: R&D and business personnel growth continues robustly
items.quote: Overall, our research and development and growth of the business in terms of personnel continues to be robust.

items.statement: Order booking run rate ₹7-8B/quarter seen as reasonable steady state for FY28; not driven by lumpy orders
items.quote: No, they're not lumpy large orders. This is regular. You have two, three factors that you have to keep in mind. One is that our Enquiry book suggests growth, and so therefore, we're responding to the market, and our market share remains reasonably consistent, and so we participate to that extent.

items.statement: Commodity price increases seen in Q1 expected to normalize by Q4; warranty/contingency accounting conservative; tax refunds not yet recognized
items.quote: There were some disruptions in commodity price increases that we saw in Q1, which will get normalized by the time we get to Q4, which will provide better visibility for FY28. We follow a conservative principle on accounting for warranty and other contingencies.

items.statement: Small gas turbine development for thrust applications (not power gen); multi-year product cycle; aims to leverage refurbishment business
items.quote: The gas turbine development on the product side is not for power generation. It will be more for the thrust application. We will come up with more clarity as we go down the path, but it is a multi-year product development cycle. It positions Triveni as an OEM, which we aim to benefit and leverage from our refurbishment business.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of approximately INR7,500 crores; long-term EBITDA margin objective remains approximately 20%
items.quote: For FY28, we are targeting a revenue of approximately INR7,500 crores. We will review and reaffirm this outlook towards the end of Q4. Our long-term EBITDA margin objective remains approximately 20%.

items.statement: No specific revenue guidance for FY27; previous 75% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin targets will not be met due to strategy shift
items.quote: We would refrain from providing specific revenue guidance for FY27 at this stage. However, Q2 has been a sequential improvement over Q1, and we expect this momentum to continue through H2 and into FY28.

items.statement: Q2 consolidated EBITDA margin suppressed at ~17% due to commodity inflation and non-recognition of Wind World O&M income; would have been ~20% if recognized
items.quote: Had they been recognized in the P&L, the consolidated EBITDA margins would have been ~ 20%. The margin profile would substantially improve going forward as we start consolidating the O&M portfolio of Wind World in Inox Green's books starting Q3 FY27.

items.statement: Wind World O&M portfolio currently at 25-30% EBITDA margin; target to reach 40%+ within 3-4 quarters through cost optimization and value-added services
items.quote: In terms of Wind World, the margins which we expect currently is in the range of broadly 25%-30% odd. With the value additions which we will do, that margins can go up to a 40% odd.

items.statement: Next-gen 4.X wind turbine platform prototype installed, commercial launch targeted by end FY27; Rohika facility ready for 4.X blades; expanding transformer capacity to 8-20 MVA and larger; adding inverters, unit substations, electronic cont
items.quote: Progress on our next-generation 4.X wind turbine platform is going well. The prototype has been installed, commissioning is expected shortly, and commercial launch is targeted by the end of financial year 2027.

items.statement: Inox Green O&M portfolio at ~12.5 GWp as of September 2026 (10.4 GW wind, 2.1 GWp solar) including 4.5 GW Wind World; additional ~2 GW wind O&M acquisition expected by March 2027
items.quote: As of September 2026, our O&M portfolio stood at approximately 12.5 GWp, comprising ~ 10.4 GW of wind and 2.1 GWp of solar assets. This includes the 4.5 GW Wind World India O&M portfolio, and additionally, approximately 2 GW wind O&M portfolio investment expected to be completed by March 2027.

items.statement: NCLT-approved acquisition of Wind World India's ~4.5 GW O&M portfolio completed in Q2; Inox Green owns 75%; line-by-line consolidation from Q3 FY27; second ~2 GW acquisition expected by Q4 FY27 subject to approvals
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the NCLT-approved acquisition of Wind World India's approximately 4.5 gigawatt O&M portfolio has progressed to completion of the payment and transfer process during the quarter.

items.statement: Inox Green raised INR300 crores via QIP in October primarily to fund Wind World O&M acquisition payment
items.quote: In October, Inox Green successfully raised INR300 crores through QIP, primarily to part-fund the acquisition of Wind World India's approximately 4.5 GW O&M portfolio and broaden our institutional investor base.

items.statement: Debtor levels stable vs March 2026 despite H1 revenue growth; working capital days elevated due to H2 seasonality (70% annual revenue) and inventory build for H2 deliveries; expect inventory to moderate by March 2027
items.quote: An important development is that our debtor levels have remained broadly stable compared with March 2026, despite revenue growth during H1, meaning that collections have been at par with sales.

items.statement: Target to reduce debtor days below 150 by end of FY28 through shift to equipment supply and strategic turnkey projects
items.quote: With our changed focus towards equipment supply and strategic turnkey projects, we are on a downward trajectory in terms of debtor days. We expect the debtor days to fall below 150 days by the end of FY28.

items.statement: Commodity and raw material price inflation due to West Asia war created temporary cost headwinds; fresh bids being priced dynamically to reflect current environment
items.quote: We have seen an impact on margins this quarter, largely due to commodity and raw material price inflation on account of the West Asia war, creating temporary cost headwinds across the supply chain.

items.statement: No significant pricing pressure seen despite new entrants like Adani Wind; limited players vs huge demand; contracts have pass-through mechanisms; wind becoming more attractive vs solar without storage
items.quote: No, not that much, because we still see that in wind we are very limited player and the demand is huge. From that perspective, as I explained earlier, with respect to our order book and as well Inox Wind Limited and as the kind of potential we see. I think we all have everyone its own niche

items.statement: India wind capacity additions: 3.2 GW in H1 FY27 vs 6.05 GW full FY26; MNRE expects 7.5-8 GW in FY27; structural growth phase with 8-10 GW annual additions near-medium term; power demand up 15% YoY in Q2
items.quote: As per the MNRE, approximately 7.5 gigawatt to 8 gigawatt of wind capacity addition is expected to take place in India in FY27. We believe India is entering a structurally stronger growth phase for wind energy, with annual additions potentially reaching 8 gigawatt to 10 gigawatt for the near to medium term.

items.statement: Inox Green machine availability averaged ~96.2% for wind portfolio in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Machine availability for our wind portfolio averaged at approximately 96.2%.

items.statement: Wind World O&M portfolio did INR580 crores revenue in FY26; expected to increase from contracted escalation, price revisions, overhauling services; post-integration EBITDA margins upwards of 45%
items.quote: Wind World did an annual revenue of INR580 crores in FY26. It is expected to increase further on account of annual contracted escalation, one-time upward price revisions in certain contracts, providing overhauling/major maintenance services, etc.

items.statement: Inox Green EBITDA nearly equals PBT (asset-light, minimal depreciation/finance cost); no cash tax for couple of years due to deferred tax assets; significant operating cash flows expected from next year
items.quote: It may be noted that the EBITDA in Inox Green is nearly equivalent to PBT due to the business being asset-light, hardly any depreciation and financial cost. While there would be deferred tax, cash tax is not expected to be there for another couple of years due to deferred tax assets on the balance sheet.

items.statement: Inox Wind virtually debt-free as of March; currently minuscule debt at 0.1-0.2x; objective sustainable growth with strong balance sheet
items.quote: If you look at our balance sheet as of March, we are virtually debt-free. Currently, we have minuscule debt, which is probably 0.1 or 0.2, and we are very, very clear.

items.statement: Strategic realignment to increase equipment supply share to ~75% of third-party order book from current 61%; reducing turnkey exposure to improve earnings quality, reduce working capital intensity, strengthen cash generation
items.quote: Our medium-term objective remains to increase equipment supply share to approximately 75% of the third-party order book, thereby improving earnings quality, reducing working capital intensity, and strengthening cash generation.

items.statement: IRSL (demerged power evacuation business) filed information memorandum for independent listing; listing subject to regulatory approvals, expected in upcoming quarter or so
items.quote: Pursuant to the demerger of the power evacuation infrastructure business from Inox Green into IRSL, the latter is progressing towards its independent listing. The information memorandum has been filed with stock exchanges, with listing subject to regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Strategy shift involves near-term trade-offs: foregoing some business opportunities, recalibrating short-term growth trajectory, letting go of some revenues in FY27 to ensure long-term balance sheet strength
items.quote: The transition has involved certain near-term trade-offs, including foregoing some business opportunities and recalibrating our short-term growth trajectory. However, we believe prioritizing quality of business over the quantum of growth was the right decision for the long-term interest of the company and its shareholders.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR 600 crores maintained with 10% growth target
items.quote: So, see, for the year, definitely we have set target of 600 CR and still we maintain that. So, it will be anything, definitely it has to be brought over the previous year and how much maybe in the single digit or double digit. So, we targeted 10% growth.

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 FY27 revenue expected at INR 170-180 crores per quarter to meet FY27 target
items.quote: So, that is the target. We have this target set up and let us see how the market supports. And so we have production facility also ready and we can do this, but depending upon the market system, but we are hopeful that we should be near to this.

items.statement: Export revenue expected at minimum INR 75 crores per quarter in H2 FY27
items.quote: For exports, yes. For exports, yes. You know, 75 per quarter is the bare minimum we can expect. It should be better than that.

items.statement: INR 20 crores capex planned for FY27 with further investments in H1 FY28
items.quote: Yes, it might be, yes, INR 20 CR for the FY '27. And then further in first half FY '28 also, there would be some further investments.

items.statement: Sanand capacity being increased by 1.5x with three additional lines to reach INR 100 crores turnover target
items.quote: We are almost increasing it. Almost doubling it. Not entirely doubling it. Yes, but 1, 1.5x increasing it.

items.statement: Third phase construction commenced at Chandipur facility adding 50,000 sq ft for garments and footwear
items.quote: On the capacity front, we commence the third phase of construction at our Chandipur facility in West Bengal. This expansion will add approximately 50,000 square feet of floor area to support our growing garments and footwear operations.

items.statement: Healthy order book and robust inquiry pipeline supporting optimism for coming quarters
items.quote: Further, we remain optimistic about our business prospects, supported by a healthy order book and a robust inquiry pipeline.

items.statement: Export demand bottomed out with order booking improving; EU FTA and US trade deals expected to help
items.quote: However, now we see the order booking getting better and healthier than before and I think India and European Union both are excited about the new free trade agreement that we are going to sign hopefully soon and that is also a factor that is playing to this improvement.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 23% YoY in Q2 FY27 and 18% YoY in H1 FY27 despite price volatility
items.quote: during the quarter, domestic revenue grew by 23% year-on-year to INR 69 crores, building on the momentum witnessed in Q1 FY '27. International revenue stood at INR 74 crores. For the first half of the financial year, domestic revenue increased 18% year-on-year to INR 130

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 350 bps YoY to 10.61% driven by lower raw material costs and better realizations
items.quote: EBITDA increased significantly by 54% year-on-year to INR 15 crores, with EBITDA margins expanding by 350 basis points to 10.61%. This improvement was primarily driven by lower raw material costs, better unit sales realizations and savings in employee manufacturing, operational and administrative expenses.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 93 bps YoY to 11.43% despite 3% revenue decline
items.quote: Despite the moderation in revenue, EBITDA grew 5% year-on-year to INR 29 crores, with EBITDA margins improving by 93 basis points to 11.43%. This improvement reflects better cost management and operating efficiencies with savings in material costs and improved sales realizations helping offset the increase in employee, manufacturing, marketing, operational and administrative expenses.

items.statement: Management targets return to 13-14% EBITDA margins over time as volumes absorb fixed costs from new capacity
items.quote: I think it should take time because one is definitely the raw material prices, but there is also, we need to have better sales realizations. Also, we have added a lot of land, building, plant machinery. So, the depreciation is also higher than what we are used to. So, it won't happen very quickly but eventually, yes, definitely we would like to reach there.

items.statement: Raw material prices have smoothened and become more predictable; price revisions for export customers expected in 2027
items.quote: We are better off than what we were in, let's say, when we started the year. Raw material prices have smoothened and are more predictable at this point and I think now going ahead with all this petro-based products should get better. So, but definitely we have, coming into 2027, we will have a revision in prices for a lot of our customers.

items.statement: Export pricing fixed for annual periods with lag in passing cost changes; cannot make customers uncompetitive
items.quote: That is something that for especially the export market and where we have larger order books, a lot of times the prices are fixed usually for a year, depending obviously on the product category as well. And unless some situations like what we experienced happens, we are unable to change the price so easily.

items.statement: Sanand facility currently mostly domestic sales with some exports; targeting both markets for same products
items.quote: Yes, mostly it is, as of now, it is mostly sold in domestic market, but we have some exports also from there for the same product. And in future also, it should be adding up. So, we are targeting both export as well as domestic sales for the same product.

items.statement: BIS license obtained for PU Dip Gloves (first company); end-customer awareness programs and reseller recognition program driving cross-sell
items.quote: So, for example, PU Dip Gloves, we are the first company to get a BIS license to sell those gloves. So, that is on the regulatory part, that is something that we are doing across our product category. Secondly, we are doing extensive end customer awareness program where we are reaching out to end customers, shipping out samples to them, educating, making them aware about the product categories tha

items.statement: Opening new accounts in Europe, US and other geographies; promoting new products to existing and new customers
items.quote: We are opening new accounts in all geographies including Europe and U.S., and we are promoting our new products as well.

items.statement: Logistical issues in Q1-Q2 FY27 from supplier and customer ends; situation improving for Q3
items.quote: Q1 and Q2 had logistical issues as well. A lot of times both ends, you know, from our suppliers' end, there were logistical issues of us getting materials on time and from our customers' end, they were not able to lift goods because of food congestion or lack of container space availability. So, we got impacted definitely with that. The situation is improving now. So, that has also helped in Q2. I

items.statement: Sanand facility achieved INR 13 crores revenue in H1 FY27; targeting INR 25 crores in H2 for full year INR 40 crores target
items.quote: So, for Sanand, we had, so productivity there is picking up now and because initially, we had a lot of beginning problem we had with the employees also. And so, now it is more on track. And for the first half, we could do the turnover of INR 13 crores, but going forward, we see that for the next half, it should be minimum INR 25 crores. So, we are targeting INR 40 crores turnover for the first yea

items.statement: Capex funded through internal accruals only; no additional borrowing planned
items.quote: Yeah, yeah. No additional borrowing, no borrowing. In the past also we never borrowed, so it is through internal accruals only. But some CAPEX is lined up, so that we will take care from internal accruals only.

items.statement: Current infrastructure supports INR 1,000 crores revenue without proportionate incremental capex
items.quote: The current manufacturing infrastructure provides the visibility to support revenues of approximately INR 1,000 crores without proportionate incremental capital investment.

items.statement: Received Eastern India Best Employer Award 2026 for people management and employee engagement
items.quote: We are also pleased to share that the company received the Eastern India Best Employer Award 2026, recognizing our continued efforts towards people management, employee engagement and organizational growth.

items.statement: BIS enforcement weaker for gloves vs footwear/helmets; company creating customer awareness about BIS standards
items.quote: Yes, definitely it is not as strong as it is in, let's say, footwear or head protection, helmets particularly. It is much newer standard and it is not a lot of awareness till now. But see, we cannot just rely on BIS if they do their job that we'll be able to promote our products. We are also making the customers and the users informed about what is BIS and why should they look for it and things li

items.statement: Export market penetration takes 3-5 years due to fixed supply chains; gestation periods extended by uncertainty
items.quote: For an OEM business, the timeframe usually that we say that the market will grow and everything, it is usually a three to five-year timeframe, nothing less than that, because the market takes time, the customers take time. They already have a supply chain, and the supply chain is changing. Maybe the countries are changing, products are changing, or even in the same product, we have to ensure that

items.statement: All products sold under own brand; no job work in domestic market
items.quote: So, we sell all under our own brand. We do not do job work.

items.statement: Sequential EBITDA margin impact in Q2 due to lower unit sales realizations offset by higher volumes
items.quote: On a sequential basis, EBITDA margins were impacted by lower unit sales realizations, although higher sales volumes helped improve cost absorption and offset some of the pressure.

items.statement: International revenue INR 74 crores in Q2 FY27 and INR 123 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: International revenue stood at INR 74 crores. For the first half of the financial year, domestic revenue increased 18% year-on-year to INR 130 crores, while international revenue stood at INR 123 crores.

items.statement: Dr. Amrut Naik joined as CEO of pharmaceutical business with 27 years commercial experience in overseas markets
items.quote: Dr. Amrut Naik, who has joined Alkem Labs as Chief Executive Officer. Dr. Naik brings extensive industry experience and will work closely with the leadership team to further strengthen execution and advance the group's strategic priorities.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20-21% for FY27 despite H1 above range due to Occlutech dilution and Enzene ramp uncertainty
items.quote: No, I don't think so, chief, because see, now you got Occlutech, which diluted our margin by 80 basis points this quarter, and we really don't know how Enzene would also pick up and how fast.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 22.5%, up 11.3% YoY; core pharma business EBITDA ~26% in Q2 but quarterally high
items.quote: EBITDA was INR1,025 crores, resulted in a EBITDA margin of 22.5%, a growth of 11.3% year-on-year.

items.statement: R&D expense guidance maintained at 4-4.5% of revenue; Q2 higher due to RLD ordering lumpiness
items.quote: Our guidance is close to 4%-4.5%, and that we are maintaining. R&D is always lumpy, and we have ordered some RLD in this quarter, and that is why you are seeing the jump.

items.statement: US business: volume growth >10% offset by ~16% price erosion (mainly Sacubitril/Valsartan) and 3% new launch contribution; constant currency -3%
items.quote: U.S., obviously, we saw a volume expansion of over 10%. However, the price erosion was to an extent of about 16%, which was partially offset by new product launches to an extent of 3%.

items.statement: US FY27 growth guided at mid-single digit in constant currency; H2 slightly better than H1 but new approvals stalled by Daman OAI
items.quote: Therefore, the year is going to look like a single digit, somewhere mid-single digit growth for the year. That is the expectation.

items.statement: Tolvaptan launched in US in September; ramp-up slow due to REMS program; not expected to meaningfully scale in next two quarters
items.quote: Tolvaptan, obviously we have aspirations, but then there are also challenges around the REMS issue, and therefore we may not be able to meaningfully scale up that product.

items.statement: Daman facility remediation responses submitted to US FDA; awaiting re-audit; 8 products due for launch from Daman delayed
items.quote: We have submitted everything. All our responses has already been sent to the U.S. FDA. We are, in fact, waiting for their counter responses in terms of how and when they will come for a re-audit.

items.statement: Mandva API facility US FDA inspection concluded with zero 483 observations
items.quote: Separately, the U.S. FDA inspection of our Mandva API facility concluded with no 483s.

items.statement: Non-US international business grew 58% YoY (22.3% overall international); LATAM (Colombia, Mexico), Chile, Australia key drivers
items.quote: Non-U.S., obviously, our Latin America engine continues to do well, Colombia, Mexico having the key drivers in this particular quarter. Chile is a strong business for us. Australia has continued to do well.

items.statement: India FY27 growth expected ~11% overall (vs 9-10% analyst estimate); chronic focus therapies driving outperformance
items.quote: I think we will end up by around close to 11% of India growth overall.

items.statement: Chronic portfolio focus: anti-diabetic (semaglutide #1 volume), cardiovascular, neuropsychiatry, dermatology, respiratory, VMN; chronic currently 24-25% of India sales vs industry 65/35 split
items.quote: Today, we are at about 24%- 25%, from an IQVIA standpoint, compared to the industry, which is at about 65/35. Obviously, going forward, chronic, gaining market share in chronic is going to be very, very critical.

items.statement: FY27 reported EBITDA margin expected ~20.4% (flat vs FY26) due to Enzene/Occlutech drag; pharma core margin improvement aspiration 100 bps YoY
items.quote: So, FY 2026 was 20.4%. Amrut Naik: So, it may be marginal. We may be at best on par with respect to last year

items.statement: Occlutech acquisition added INR 1,100 crore identifiable intangibles (10-year amortization) and INR 700 crore goodwill; PPA depreciation INR 28 crore/quarter
items.quote: We have added identifiable intangibles of close to INR 1,100 crore, and that will be amortized over a period of 10 years, and there is a goodwill of close to INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Enzene revenue target 2x in 4 years; MedTech revenue target 3x in 5-6 years; both prioritized for growth over near-term profitability
items.quote: Enzene would become double in size in four years' time, roughly, in revenue. Therefore, EBITDA would also start breaking even in a year and a half to two, maximum. And MedTech, similarly, would also come out of the EBITDA in a year's time. And more importantly, on growth, I think they will be 3x what they are in

items.statement: Enzene US facility partially operational; H2 busier than H1 with CDMO business; not fully utilized yet
items.quote: It is not completely sitting idle. It is partially standing. What I mean is, it has some business and H2 will be far busier than H1.

items.statement: Denosumab BLA delayed due to analytical queries; refiling soon; EU Xgeva biosimilar approved but not meaningful; different commercial partner needed
items.quote: What is getting delayed is basically some analytical queries we had, not infrastructure or anything like that. It is basically regulatory queries. Sandeep Kumar: Okay. Is there any timeline? Sandeep Singh: We will have to kind of refile this

items.statement: Net cash position INR 4,900 crore+ as of Q2 FY27
items.quote: Net profit saw a degrowth of 11.7%, and net cash stood at INR4,900 crores plus.

items.statement: India chronic therapies outperformance: multivitamins 1.2x, anti-diabetic 1.5x, cardiac 1.1x, urology 1.1x, respiratory 1.6x, neuro/CNS 1.1x, derma 1.6x vs IPM
items.quote: We have outperformed IPM in eight key focus therapies. In multivitamins by ~1.2x, anti-diabetic again ~1.5x, cardiac by 1.1x. Urology, again on a low base, we are 1.1x, Respiratory by 1.6x, Neuro CNS by 1.1x & Derma by 1.6x.

items.statement: Semaglutide injectable #1 in volume share in India (not yet value); VMN portfolio #1 per IQVIA
items.quote: In VMN now we are number one, as per the latest reported IQVIA. Semaglutide injectable, we are number one in volumes, again, to be clear, not in value yet.

items.statement: US price erosion of 16% driven mainly by single product (Sacubitril/Valsartan); now in base
items.quote: I think it's because of only one product, sir. It's because of Sacuval.

items.statement: Daman OAI status stalling new US approvals; 3 important product launches delayed; top priority for resolution
items.quote: Going forward, obviously, three important products that we had lined up for launch, that approval has been delayed, and that is really impacting us.

items.statement: Occlutech gross margins 80%; US launch expected 2028 for major ramp-up; 2-year timeline
items.quote: The gross margins of Occlutech are 80%, so I think it is a good business. The big delta would be in U.S. whenever we launch our products in U.S. Right now, we are present in U.S., but in a very, very insignificant way. Once Occlutech launches products, and we think that will be in 2028, you will see a major ramp-up.

items.statement: Occlutech acquisition added borrowing; interest cost included in consolidated finance cost from Q2
items.quote: Even in the finance cost, because there is a borrowing, the Occlutech, so interest cost is also added in a consolidated result, and that will remain in the subsequent quarter.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 11.5% to 12.5%

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target 13.5% to 14.5% in 2-3 years

items.statement: FY27 ending debt reduction target INR50-60 crores in H2
items.quote: we expect that we reduce our working capital by INR50 crores to INR60 crores

items.quote: Gross profit grew 4.5% year-on-year to INR171 crores with a gross profit margin of 31.8%

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.2%, H1 FY27 11.5%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA stood at INR61 crores with a margin of 11.2%

items.quote: we have already taken 2 price hikes unlike any other companies, and it constituted to around 4%, 4.5% overall, distributed amongst the 2 price hikes that we have taken. So another would be somewhere to the tune of 2% to 3% kind of price hike

items.quote: Currently, as per market, it is around this level only, INR68,000 to INR72,000

items.quote: Quick commerce recorded growth of 58.5% in value and 52.4% in volume terms, with its contribution to overall revenue increasing from 4% in Q2 FY26 to 5.4% in Q2 FY27

items.statement: Export business grew 57% value, 45.5% volume in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our export business also delivered a strong performance during the quarter with value growth of 57% and volume growth of 45.5%

items.statement: Eastern region grew 25.6% value, 16.3% volume; North grew 14.6% value, 6.2% volume in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The Eastern region delivered 25.6% growth in terms of value and 16.3% volume growth this quarter. North, our largest region registered 14.6% value growth and 6.2% volume growth

items.statement: No share buyback planned; focus on debt reduction and dividend

items.quote: So the competition is still intense in the market. We thought that it would get better. But yes, it has gotten a bit better, but not there yet. It would take another couple of quarters maybe to settle down

items.quote: The moderation in gross margin was primarily driven by higher cotton prices, a key raw material for the company. We expect cotton prices to remain elevated in the near term, and we endeavor to pass on the cost increase through price hikes

items.statement: Advertising spend capped at INR100 crores annually; H1 FY27 ad spend 6.5% of revenue
items.quote: Advertisement expenses stood at 6.5% of revenue in H1. With annual advertising expenditure capped at INR100 crores, we remain focused on strengthening brand visibility while achieving greater efficiency in advertisement spend as revenue scales

items.statement: Lakshya project rollout slowed to avoid market share loss during disruption; will resume when conditions favourable
items.quote: Because whenever you implement this project in a new state, what happens is the market gets disrupted for nearly 5 to 6 months minimum. So we don't really want to lose that market share because of this particular project, and we want to implement this when the s

items.statement: Q2 FY27 order intake Rs 4,120.8 crore; H1 FY27 order intake Rs 9,217.3 crore
items.quote: we secured orders worth Rs 4,120.8 crores during Q2FY27, taking our H1FY27 order intake to Rs 9,217.3 crores

items.statement: Order backlog Rs 33,335.4 crore at end of Q2 FY27

items.statement: Majority of capex projects targeted for completion by end of next year; new large power transformer facility targeted for 2028
items.quote: Majority of these projects are targeted for completion by the end of next year, progressively adding capacity across our portfolio. In parallel, our new large power transformer facility, which we just announced and started, is targeted for 2028, further strengthening our long-term manufacturing capabilities.

items.statement: Capex program spans transformers, high voltage products, grid automation; new large power transformer facility started, targeted for 2028
items.quote: Our capex program spans several strategic projects across transformers, high voltage products, and grid automation. These investments are aim at strengthening manufacturing readiness to capture the opportunities emerging from the continued expansion and modernization of the grid.

items.statement: 1150 kV transformer design, manufacture, and testing fully localized in India; 800 kV VSC technology ready
items.quote: Just for information, we are the first one to complete the 1150 kV transformer design, manufacture, and fully tested in India. Both the big components, 1150 kV transformer, and the switchgear, hybrid switchgear, and as well as the automation is fully localized in India.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin 16.5% in Q2 FY27 despite product mix and supply-chain pressures
items.quote: Despite the product mix executed during the quarter, continued supply-chain pressures and raw- material price escalation, we maintained a healthy double-digit operational EBITDA margin of 16.5% in Q2 FY27, demonstrating the resilience of our operations and continued execution discipline.

items.statement: Strong order momentum across transmission, industries, data centers, and exports; service orders grew 77.1% YoY
items.quote: Order growth in the domestic market excluding HVDC orders during Q2FY27 was driven by strong momentum across transmission, industries, and data center.

items.statement: Export orders grew 41% YoY in Q2 FY27; exports typically 25-30% of revenue
items.quote: Our export business also maintained healthy momentum. The export orders in Q2 FY27 grew 41% YoY, with wins spanning Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe, and the USA, (including TenneT Order).

items.statement: Order mix: products 60%, projects 34%, services 7%; sectoral mix: utilities 52%, industries 24%, transport & infra 23%
items.quote: Looking at the order mix, products remained the largest component at 60%, while the project share increased to 34% from 19% a year earlier. Service represented approximately 7% of orders. The sectoral mix became more balanced compared with the utilities-heavy mix last year. Utilities accounted for 52%, industries for 24%, and transport and infrastructure 23%.

items.statement: Material cost 61.7% in Q2 FY27, varies with product mix; expected to normalize as exports and services increase
items.quote: Our material cost, if you see, is 61.7%. which is moving based on the product mix that we have executed.

items.quote: You are correct. We have reported Rs 91 crores vs Rs 874 crores last year. This is majorly because of the movement of the large HVDC projects. That is sitting in the contract assets. As and when the invoicing happens, it will be recouping the cash.

items.statement: Notional forex loss of Rs 88.1 crore in Q2 FY27; hedging policy followed, contracts hedged upon signing
items.quote: It is also important to highlight that PBT and PAT for the quarter include the impact of a Rs 88.1 crore notional forex exchange loss. As this is non-operational in nature, it is excluded from EBITDA.

items.quote: In our view, the next 12 to 24 months, at least four to five projects are coming in. One project is already approved, NCT. The recent technology, first time is approved, 800 kV VSC technology. We are fully ready with that technology. That has been approved.

items.statement: Grid-to-rack solutions launched for data centers; will be manufactured in India when orders received
items.quote: Grid-to-rack solutions we have already launched. We are discussing with the customers. Whenever we have those orders, grid-to-rack will be manufactured in India.

items.statement: Export margins 3-4% higher than domestic on overall basis
items.quote: Overall basis, yes. Some products may vary here and there, but overall basis, yes. 3% - 4% difference will be there.

items.statement: Battery energy storage addressable scope ~40% of project value (excluding batteries)

items.statement: No foreseen slowdown in data center demand in India and APAC; commissioning schedules clearly defined
items.quote: Recently, I was attending the data center conference in Singapore and every stakeholder whom I met, they were all talking. Those plans are solid plans. They are on the ground. items.statement: HVDC market share ~50%; 1150 kV AC and 1200 kV AC readiness gives competitive advantage
items.quote: But for HVDC, we have 50% market share. Many other things like a 1200 kV AC, the addressable market will be also much higher in that. From a readiness standpoint, we are ready.

items.quote: That is the reason we are investing in more feet on the ground. We are also investing in productization of our service offerings to our customers. We are investing in the digital offerings to our customers.

items.statement: Cabinet approvals for PM-DHARA, Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (~Rs 1.86 lakh crore including 50 GWh battery storage); 1150 kV AC system approved
items.quote: The recent cabinet approvals, including PM-DHARA, the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III, represent another step in this direction, with around Rs 1.86 lakh crores of investments moving forward, including investment in 50 GWh of battery energy storage.

items.statement: FY27 services revenue guidance INR 2,650-2,750 crores, total revenue INR 2,750-2,850 crores, EBITDA margin 27%, capex INR 100-125 crores

items.quote: Our currency in circulation is at a record high of about INR43.5 lakh crores, which is 13.5% on a year -on-year basis. It's the fastest growth in five years, and it's about 3x the level of FY 2015.

items.quote: Three structural drivers sit behind this margin: price revision, productivity from the route optimization, and automation in our internal operations and business mix, with the higher share of the tech and payments and of the fixed-price contracts in our revenue.

items.statement: H1 order wins INR 700 crores; market share held at 60% in ATM cash management and 38% in retail cash solutions; pipeline active with RFPs for branch surveillance, ATM software, recyclers

items.quote: Net capex in H1 was INR 50 crores, and we estimate FY27 capex at INR100 crores-INR125 crores against INR351 crores last year. That is about half of our long -term average and well below our depreciation charge.

items.quote: Statutory minimum wages have risen by 6% to as much as 60% across key states, and fuel cost is up by 8%. These are statutory and external cost increases on contracts, which in many cases were priced several years back.

items.quote: Operating cash flow for H1 was INR177 crores, or 51% of EBITDA, compared to an outflow of INR117 crores in the first half of the last year. Our collections were weighted towards the second half.

items.quote: As we have guided that our risk cost is close to 3.5%-4.5%, which was earlier 6%, and we are within that limit only. This year, this H1 also, we are around 4% of that and which was provided.

items.quote: The pipeline remains robust with approximately 5 gigawatt of potential tenders from NTPC, Indian Oil Corporation, and SECI over the next four to five months, apart from ongoing negotiations. We also expect recurring opportunities from Inox Clean Energy over the coming years.

items.statement: India wind capacity additions: 1.8 GW in Q2 FY27, 3.2 GW in H1 FY27 vs 6.05 GW full FY26; MNRE expects 7.5-8 GW in FY27; structural growth phase with annual additions potentially reaching 8-10 GW near to medium term

items.statement: Inox Green EBITDA nearly equivalent to PBT due to asset-light model; minimal depreciation and finance cost; deferred tax assets mean no cash tax for couple of years; significant operating cash flows expected from next year post acquisitions
