items.quote: If you look at our balance sheet as of March, we are virtually debt-free. Currently, we have minuscule debt, which is probably 0.1 or 0.2, and we are very, very clear. Our objective is sustainable growth with qualitative cash flows and a very strong balance sheet.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20% to 25% over FY26 reaffirmed; expect to end FY27 financially profitable
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our earlier FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20% to 25% over FY26 and expect to end the year financially profitable.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 4.2% for FY27 and 4.5%-4.6% for FY28
items.quote: This year we will probably end up around 4.2%. Next year we are looking at closer to 4.5%, 4.6% as the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Strong festive demand across all segments with double-digit growth in Onam and October
items.quote: If we specifically look at October, since last year the GST base did kick in October, we've seen a double-digit growth on all segments, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, as well as the luxury segment and the electric two-wheeler segment.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 3.7% in Q2 FY27 from 3.2% YoY; each segment improved margins by about 1%
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved to 3.7% from 3.2% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Revenue grew 36% YoY to INR2,089 crores in Q2 FY27; H1 FY27 revenue up 40% to INR3,984 crores
items.quote: At the consolidated level, revenue from operations grew approximately 36% Y-o-Y to INR2,089 crores in Q2 FY27, while H1 FY27 revenue increased approximately 40% to INR3,984 crores.

items.statement: New Maruti Service Center at Karukachal and Tata Motors Commercial Vehicle Center at Kayamkulam commenced operations in Kerala
items.quote: During the quarter, we commenced operations at the new Maruti Service Center at Karukachal and the Tata Motors Commercial Vehicle Center at Kayamkulam, both in Keralam.

items.statement: BharatBenz Punjab and Maruti Telangana acquisitions integration largely complete; businesses delivering healthy growth
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that the integration of these businesses has progressed very well. Our initial focus was on stabilizing operations, integrating systems and processes, strengthening teams, and improving customer engagement.

items.statement: Discounting levels significantly lower compared to corresponding period last year reflecting favorable demand and improved pricing discipline
items.quote: Importantly, discounting levels were significantly lower compared with the corresponding period last year, reflecting a more favorable demand environment and improved pricing discipline.

items.statement: Premium and luxury vehicle growth contributed to higher income growth and improved sales mix; JLR and Audi strengthening luxury portfolio
items.quote: While volumes grew across categories, relatively strong growth in premium and luxury vehicles contributed to a higher income growth and an improved sales mix.
While reported volume growth remained moderated, service income grew at a healthier pace, supported by better realization and a higher contribution from high-value service jobs.

items.statement: New vehicle inventory days at 41 days vs 44 days YoY; inventory built up strategically for festive season; expect normalization in coming months
items.quote: Nevertheless, the new vehicle inventory days stood at approximately 41 days compared with 44 days in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Sequential increase in borrowing due to festive inventory build-up; CRISIL reaffirmed A/Stable long-term and A1 short-term ratings
items.quote: CRISIL reaffirmed the credit ratings of Popular Vehicles and Services and its subsidiary Popular Mega Motors at CRISIL A/Stable for long-term facilities and CRISIL A1 for short-term facilities.

items.statement: Promoter family settlement concluded; Mr. John Paul stepped away effective Oct 1, 2026; shareholding to be transferred to continuing promoters by Dec 29
items.quote: Our promoter family recently concluded an amicable family settlement under which Mr. John Paul has stepped away from the company businesses effective October 1, 2026 to pursue independent opportunities.

items.statement: IRDAI draft insurance commission regulations discussed with OEMs and FADA; compensation expected via vehicle margins or other revenue streams
items.quote: Both OEMs and FADA have taken this up with the insurance regulator, the IRDAI, and there's a continuous conversation going on both in terms of what would be the impact, and especially given that unlike health or others or life insurances, the auto dealer actually participates in repairing the vehicle.

items.statement: No threat to FY28 margin guidance of 4.5% from insurance commission changes; confident of compensation from OEMs/IRDAI
items.quote: But the reason is that there are more than 4,000 to 5,000 passenger vehicle dealers, and all the dealers have raised this issue with both the IRDAI as well as with the OEMs

items.statement: Passenger vehicle service volumes up 5% YoY to 196,652 units; service income up 22% to INR181 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Coming to passenger vehicle services, volume increased approximately 5% year-on-year to 196,652 units in Q2 FY27, while service income grew approximately 22% to INR181 crores.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle new volumes up 27% YoY to 3,549 units; CV service volumes up 9% to 54,906 units in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Moving to commercial vehicles, new vehicle volumes stood at 3,549 units in Q2 FY27, up 27% year-on-year, while total income increased 29% to INR581 crores.

items.statement: EV new volumes up 115% YoY to 3,685 units; EV service volumes up 59% to 15,792 units in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Coming to electric vehicles, new vehicle volumes increased 115% year-on-year to 3,685 units in Q2 FY27, while total income grew 124% to INR63 crores.

items.statement: Cash PAT grew 56% YoY to INR43.6 crores in Q2 FY27; H1 FY27 cash PAT up 84% to INR84.5 crores
items.quote: Coming to cash PAT, it stood at approximately INR43.6 crores in quarter 2 FY27 compared with INR28 crores in quarter 2 FY26, reflecting a growth of approximately 56% year-on-year.

items.statement: Yanik B2B e-commerce marketplace launched with 13,000+ verified spare parts; 3-4 sellers and 600+ workshops onboarded; no profit contribution expected in FY27
items.quote: FY27, we don't expect any profit contribution from Yanik. We've just started. We have onboarded approximately three to four sellers on the platform and about 600-odd workshops and mechanics.

items.statement: BKT tyre distribution commenced; no contribution expected in FY27; higher contribution expected next year as BKT scales production
items.quote: BKT Tyres has also just started the operation, so this year there wouldn't be any contribution. Next year, as BKT scales up their production, we're expecting a much higher contribution from both the two-wheeler and the four-wheeler passenger vehicles.

items.statement: Passenger traffic at TFS-managed airports declined 2.2% in H1 FY27 and 4.8% in Q2 FY27 YoY due to West Asia crisis and domestic capacity rationalization.
items.quote: Passenger traffic at TFS-managed airports declined 2.2% in the first half of the year, with the fall in passenger numbers becoming more pronounced during quarter 2, when traffic fell 4.8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Management expects gradual improvement in H2 FY27 supported by seasonal strength, winter schedules, and potential fuel price moderation.
items.quote: As we enter H2, we expect improvement to be gradual rather than immediate. However, there are some encouraging indicators. The second half of the year is seasonally a stronger period for travel, and the winter schedules announced by some airlines point towards a progressive restoration of capacity.

items.statement: System-wide sales grew 18.8% YoY to INR8.65 billion in Q2 FY27 and 18.4% YoY to INR17.1 billion in H1 FY27.
items.quote: System-wide sales increased 18.8% year-on-year in quarter 2 to INR8.65 billion and grew 18.4% year-on-year during the first half of the year to INR17.1 billion.

items.statement: System-wide like-for-like sales grew 3.5% in Q2 FY27 and 2.2% in H1 FY27; net contract gains were 11.1% in Q2 and 13.5% in H1.
items.quote: System-wide like-for-like sales grew 3.5% in Q2 and 2.2% in H1, while net contract gains were 11.1% in Q2 and 13.5% in H1.

items.statement: Consolidated like-for-like sales grew 6.6% in Q2 FY27 and 5.3% in H1 FY27; net contract gains were 11% in Q2 and 15.7% in H1.
items.quote: Here, the performance of the existing portfolio was stronger, with like-for-like sales growth of 6.6% in Q2 and 5.3% in H1. Net contract gains in our consolidated numbers stood at 11% in Q2 and 15.7% in H1.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin (ex-lounge aggregation) was 80.7% in Q2 FY27 and 80.8% in H1 FY27, within guided range.
items.quote: Excluding this, the gross margin was 80.7% and 80.8% for Q2 and H1 respectively. This is well within our guided range, reflecting continued discipline despite an inflationary cost environment in which we operate.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 37.1% in Q2 FY27 vs 38% YoY and 36.4% in H1 FY27, impacted by new unit ramp-up costs.
items.quote: At the operating level, consolidated EBITDA stood at INR1.6 billion in Q2, up 16.8% year-on-year, with an EBITDA margin of 37.1% compared with 38% last year. For the first half, EBITDA grew 13.8% Y-o-Y, with an EBITDA margin of 36.4%.

items.statement: Opened over 70 travel QSR outlets in last 12 months; expanded airport presence from 18 to 22 airports and outlet count from 501 to 570.
items.quote: Over the last 12 months, we have mobilized more than 70 travel QSR outlets. Our presence has increased from 18 airports to 22 airports, while our overall outlet count has expanded from 501 to 570 outlets.

items.statement: GMR Hospitality JV secured Delhi T3 travel QSR concession for ~50 outlets (up from 32); Semolina Kitchens JV expanded from 115 to 154 outlets including Navi Mumbai Airport.
items.quote: GMR Hospitality Limited, our joint venture with GMR Airports, has recently secured the travel QSR concession for Terminal 3 at Delhi Airport. The concession covers nearly 50 travel QSR outlets, a significant step up from the 32 outlets we operated earlier in that terminal and further strengthens our presence across the Delhi Airport ecosystem. Semolina Kitchens, our joint venture with Adani Airpor

items.statement: GHL commenced operations at Bhogapuram Airport with 6 travel QSR outlets; additional outlets under fit-out.
items.quote: During the quarter, GHL, GMR Hospitality Limited, also commenced operations at Bhogapuram Airport. We started with six travel QSR outlets, with additional outlets under fit-out.

items.statement: Focus on menu, product mix, premiumization with festive/regional offerings (Onam Sadya Thali, Ganesh Chaturthi specials) and new brands like Foo, Brijwasi, Gordon Ramsay Street Pizza, Wagamama.
items.quote: Across our network, we have continued to work on the menu, product mix, and premiumization while ensuring that the proposition remains relevant across different passenger segments and price points, including through festive and regional offerings such as the Onam Sadya Thali and our Ganesh Chaturthi specials.

items.statement: Blended price increases ~5% (range 3-8% across categories) to offset food inflation ~7.5%; long-term supply contracts and volume buying protect margins.
items.quote: Those we can therefore support in terms of pricing, no need to pass those on fully to consumers, and therefore, those metrics and those efforts at the back-end, we can play out, which I mentioned earlier to your question that 5% say price, Obviously, that's blended across lounges, F&B. Some places, some categories may take 3, some it may take 7-8, but say it blends out to about 5% is what we looke

items.statement: Lounge business: premium card segment growing >50% with unlimited access; mass card segment growing 8-15% with spend-based access restrictions.
items.quote: And actually, there, the banks on the flipside have given more access. So you're seeing many more cards with unlimited lounge access coming in. So, in reality, actually, the lounge business, I mean, evident by how busy when you go as in a traveler, but the lounge business actually is trading very strong.

items.statement: Lounge competition described as business-as-usual; EATS platform strengthens direct bank relationships and enables customized offerings.
items.quote: On the lounges piece, as in any business, I think competition has always been there. Difficult to say it's more or less because it's always been there, and we have a particular product, we are market leaders. We focus on what we deliver. So, I think in that sense, it's business as usual means you're dealing with competition.

items.statement: International expansion focused on lounge opportunities in APAC and Middle East; subsidiaries set up in Dubai and Indonesia; Kyra Lounge Hong Kong won Asia's Leading Airport Lounge 2026 for second year.
items.quote: We are looking at further opportunities in APAC and the Middle East particularly. We set up subsidiaries in Dubai and in Indonesia for those very things, and we are actually building up. We have teams, we are building up those teams even further because with the success we are seeing in that segment and with the skill set we have developed on lounges over more than a decade, we believe we are in a

items.statement: Receivables normalized to 45-52 days outstanding in H1 FY27 after EATS platform ramp-up; QSR business has negative working capital (>50% of business).
items.quote: If you recollect back, when we kick-started the EATS platform, our debtors had shot up. As I had commented at that time also, as the business stabilizes and comes into a running state, we will hover around the 45 to 52 days outstanding on the debtor side, and that is where we have now reached at H1, and that will be the steady state of TFS.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with consolidated cash balance of ~INR10.3 billion as of September 30, 2026.
items.quote: Turning to the balance sheet, we continue to remain debt-free, with consolidated cash balance of approximately INR10.3 billion as of September 30, 2026.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; cash generation and INR10.3B balance fund expansion in highways and international markets.
items.quote: We will require capital for future expansion of the projects that we have to deliver within India and also outside India. So, at this moment, we keep on exploring new opportunities as they come by. The yardstick always for our capital allocation will be the return metrics for our shareholders, and that will be how we will go about deploying the capital.

items.statement: Dividend announced in August 2026 and paid post September 30; reflected in other financial liabilities increase.
items.quote: It is predominantly the dividend payable which was paid subsequently, which is part of that liability. As you are aware, we had announced the dividend in August, and it was paid subsequently post September 30.

items.statement: Indian passenger traffic expected to grow at 7-8% CAGR over next decade driven by rising incomes, travel propensity, low penetration, and airport/airline capacity expansion.
items.quote: Indian passenger traffic is expected to grow at a 7%-8% CAGR over the next decade, materially ahead of global growth, driven by rising disposable incomes, increasing travel propensity, and low air travel penetration, alongside continued expansion in airport and airline capacity.

items.statement: Near-term risk from prolonged West Asia crisis, higher airfares, airline capacity rationalization, and elevated food inflation (~7.5%).
items.quote: The aviation environment has remained challenging, and the situation has evolved through the first two quarters. Passenger traffic at TFS-managed airports declined 2.2% in the first half of the year, with the fall in passenger numbers becoming more pronounced during quarter 2, when traffic fell 4.8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Chennai and Kolkata airports not in current 11-airport privatization pipeline; TFS operates them directly and will bid for renewals (historical renewal rate 92-94%).
items.quote: Chennai and Kolkata, I think generally, probably because of events on the ground, there's an expectation at some point those may get privatized, but it's not part of the current 11 airports from anything we've seen or any sort of announcement by the government as well.

items.statement: EATS platform enables direct bank/card partnerships, QR code/web-based access, customized experiences per card tier, and foundation for ancillary passenger services (F&B promos, meet & greet).
items.quote: EATS, I think what it does is it straightaway gives you the opportunity. One, it improves the starting of the customer experience. They come, it is immediate, you are live checking your transaction. You can do it not only through the EDC machine now, you can do it online on a web platform. It is a very QR code generation. All of that has been able to play out with that solution in place.

items.statement: Highway QSR opportunity viewed as long-term (decade) play on expressways; focusing on large landlords (road developers, oil marketing companies) for scalable, capital-efficient model.
items.quote: Now, again, like I have always clearly mentioned, this is not a short-term opportunity. We see this as being a clear long-term opportunity as roads are being built, investment is being done by the government in a big way. That takes time to play out. Consumer trends will come in, traffic will go more, and as all of that plays out. Therefore, we see it as a long-term opportunity, as a decade-long o

items.statement: Adjusted PAT (ex-provision write-backs) was ~INR1 billion in Q2 FY27 (+2.7% YoY) and ~INR2.2 billion in H1 FY27 (+13.8% YoY).
items.quote: Excluding this, PAT in Q2 and H1 will be INR1 billion and INR2.2 billion, respectively, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 2.7% and 13.8%.

items.statement: Interest cost increase due to finance lease component for Delhi T1/T2 mobilized units; expected to stabilize as revenue ramps.
items.quote: Purva, that pertains to the finance lease component, which is pertaining to the units that we have mobilized at Delhi, T1 and T2. It is the impact of that. It will stabilize as we continue adding fresh units and the revenue starts kicking in much stronger.

items.statement: FY27 AUM target >INR2,000 crores (~25% YoY growth), NII growth 35-40%, PAT growth 35-40%
items.quote: For FY27, we expect to close this year with AUM of more than INR2,000 crores, representing a growth of around 25% and over 2026, with net interest income growth of around 35% to 40% and profit after tax growth of around 35% to 40%.

items.statement: NIM improved to 11.28% in H1 FY27 from 10.88% YoY; portfolio yield 21.59%, cost of borrowing 10.59%
items.quote: Our net interest margin improved to 11.28% in H1 financial year '27 compared with 10.88% in the corresponding period last year. Our average portfolio yield stood at 21.59%, while our average cost of borrowing declined to 10.59%.

items.statement: Branches mature in 7-9 months; 45 new branches now maturing and supporting incremental AUM growth
items.quote: A key priority now is improving branch level productivity with branches typically reaching break-even within 7 to 9 months. The branches opened over the past 12 to 24 months are matured now and support incremental AUM growth and operating leverage.

items.statement: Promoter holds ~60-61%; open to infusing more capital and to dilution via preferential/FPO when leverage reaches 4.5-4.75x
items.quote: See promoter is having almost 60%, 61% shareholding overall right now. And company and the as this NBFC is a capital oriented business, so as and when capital required, promoter is ready to get funds and infuse funds and to raise fund from the market.

items.statement: Up Money DA exposure: INR26 cr transaction, INR19 cr defaulted; 90% provided (INR6 cr added in H1); 10% (INR1.9 cr) remaining; no other similar exposures
items.quote: total INR19 crores was the total quantum, sir. We have made a 90% provision. Now, 10% is only left, that is 1.90. And the, so 1.90 is only left, and rest all we have done payment. Paras: No, but how much money has been actually recovered in cash so far? Management: No. So, we have done a transaction of this, this transaction was of around INR26 crores. So from, INR26 crores INR19 crores got defaul

items.statement: Launching revolving credit lines for MSME working capital needs; secured MSME 81% of AUM; vehicle finance ~2-3% unsecured
items.quote: Building on this franchisee, we are also preparing to launch a new product line under which we will offer credit lines to our customers. Many of our MSME borrowers have recurring working capital needs, and a revolving credit facilities let them draw and repay funds as their business require.

items.statement: CRAR 22.95% (Tier 1 22.54%); would be ~27% if liquidity in FDs not bonds; debt-equity 3.31x
items.quote: Our net worth stood at INR499 crores, while our capital adequacy ratio was 22.95%, including Tier 1 capital adequacy of 22.54%. Our gross debt-equity ratio stood at 3.31 times compared with 2.87 times in March '26.

items.statement: Entire portfolio on fixed interest rate; rate hikes passed only to subsequent disbursements
items.quote: So, firstly, our entire portfolio is on fixed rate of interest. Secondly, in case of any rate increases, then definitely, we will be passing on subsequent disbursements only. That is the only option that we are having then.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR70-80 crores, representing ~60% CAGR growth, with H1 already achieving 45% of target
items.quote: as per our business model works, the Q3 and Q4 are usually better than Q1 and So, to reach that guideline number that we have given, that is around 60% CAGR growth, we are optimistic that a higher of 70s will be met, and if the good pipeline that we are looking at right now cooperates with our expectation, and then with that, we are hopeful that we will even try to reach early 80 -- INR80 crores.

items.statement: Sustainable PAT margin target of ~14% with scope for improvement as integration benefits materialize
items.quote: our focus is on improving employee utilization and project execution effectively. So, by default, that pricing discipline and the overall business mix, that margin is approximately 14%, and we believe there's a scope to improve this and as the benefits of our investment and integration initiatives, that can be improved.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of over 20% for FY27, not less than current 20.8%
items.quote: I think somewhere we can target around -- over 20, not less than that. That is what we are having expectations for. So, that is achievable. That's all I can say for now.

items.statement: Order book of INR14 crores at H1 end, with historical monthly order inflow of INR5-6 crores expected to improve
items.quote: Our last year trend was anywhere between INR5 crores to INR6 crores keeps adding month-on-month basis, and we see that being improved going forward with the better pipeline that we see.

items.statement: Major investments for FY27 already completed, no major investments planned for remainder of financial year
items.quote: whatever major investments we were looking forward to add into this year, we have already made a major part of it. So we are not planning to have any major investments going forward, at least in this financial year.

items.statement: Nashik delivery center has 40 employees with plans to add more staff due to strong client feedback and proven capabilities
items.quote: Right now, there are almost 40 people working from that location, and we are looking forward to add more people in Nashik than the other locations because of their proven capabilities to us.

items.statement: Architecture and design services contributed ~17% of H1 revenue, with Edward Farr Architects adding INR5 crores revenue
items.quote: Architecture and related design services represented approximately 17% of our H1 revenue and early indication on how our business mix is changing.

items.statement: Edward Farr Architects contributed INR5 crores revenue in H1 FY27
items.quote: our acquired company, EFA, that is Edward Farr Architects, has contributed in H1 around INR5 crores in revenue.

items.statement: 95 active customers in H1 FY27, including 28 new customer additions targeted for vertical growth
items.quote: So far, we have almost 95 customers that were giving work to us for this first half of this year. That comprises of almost 28 new customers that have been added in this first half.

items.statement: DSO currently 77 days, target to reduce to 45-50 days; working capital gap driven by GST credits and income tax payments
items.quote: So, around 45 days credit, we are expecting to be kept on DSO basis. So, currently it is 77 days around. We will get it controlled to 45 to 50 days.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR1.2 crores vs EBITDA INR7.1 crores, gap due to working capital absorption; focus on receivables collection to normalize
items.quote: Actually, our focus is more on collecting the receivables' part. So, that gap also gets reduced in upcoming periods.

items.statement: Net worth INR43.91 crores, cash balance INR20.17 crores, debt-to-equity 0.15x as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, our net worth stood at INR43.91 crores, cash and cash balance is stood at INR20.17 crores, and our debt-to-equity ratio is 0.15x.

items.statement: Warrants issued to prepare for potential large MEP acquisition (5-6x previous deal size)
items.quote: we even issued the warrants and the primary objectives for that was to prepare ourselves for the potential acquisition significantly larger than the previous ones, approximately 5 times to 6 times in scale

items.statement: Global headcount 305 (25 in US, 280 in India across Pune, Latur, Nashik); senior US leadership added in Q2
items.quote: our total group-level headcount, I would say globally, stands at almost 305 people. And among those, almost 25 people are sitting in the US and remaining 280 are operating from India.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR34.2 crores (+104.6% YoY), EBITDA INR7 crores (+134.8%), PAT INR5 crores (+157.7%), EBITDA margin 20.8% (+270bps), PAT margin 14.6% (+300bps)
items.quote: Consolidated revenue from operations more than doubled to approximately INR34.2 crores, representing growth of 104.6% over H1 last year. EBITDA increased by approximately 134.8% and Profit after tax grew by approximately 157.7%. Importantly, our H1 EBITDA margin improved by 270 basis points to 20.8% and our PAT margin improved to 14.6%.

items.statement: US accounts for ~80% of H1 revenue, Australia 10%, Europe/UK 10%; focus remains on North American market
items.quote: our current business concentration is 80% in USA and then 10% for Australia and then 10% for Europe, UK and nearby countries. So, that is how our focus is going on -- going forward and that's going to increase in almost same line of percentage.

items.statement: Quarterly results vary due to project cycles; Q2 profitability moderated due to investments ahead of revenue conversion; integration of acquired businesses still in progress
items.quote: Quarterly results can vary in a project-based business, which is why we also examine half-yearly and annual trends. At the same time, we will remain accountable for quarterly execution.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit year-on-year revenue growth for FY27 and is bullish on revenue, but did not give a specific EBITDA margin target.
items.quote: We are very bullish on the revenue growth. We will definitely surpass earlier numbers. And now the challenging part for the company is how to sustain and increase the bottom line, which we are working out with different measures, so very positive on it and growth-wise, we definitely see a double-digit growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Management expects positive EBITDA trend in next two quarters if crude oil sustains below USD 80-85 per barrel.
items.quote: In the next 2 quarters, we are very bullish considering the crude levels are maintaining the same levels currently, it's USD92 used to be USD70 to UDS80 a barrel, like sustaining less than USD80-odd or USD85, it will be great for the industry, and we can see great growth in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA was Rs. 34 million with 1.2% margin; H1 FY27 EBITDA was Rs. 196 million with 3.8% margin, moderated due to fluctuating prices.
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2 FY27 was Rs. 34 million with an EBITDA margin of 1.2%. For H1 FY27, the EBITDA reached Rs. 196 million with a margin of 3.8%, the moderation in the profitability was mainly on account of fluctuating prices.

items.statement: Warehousing and transportation verticals are expected to deliver double-digit margins.
items.quote: We have recruited a strong team, especially for the warehousing, and we see a margin of, like, double-digit margin in terms of warehousing. And coming back to the transportation, we may increase furthermore fleets and the deployment of fleets would be in different areas. And the margins would be again double-digit in terms of the transportation.

items.statement: Sea Export revenue grew 344% YoY in Q2 FY27, contribution rose to 42% from 12% in Q2 FY26.
items.quote: Revenue from this segment grew 344.4% year-on-year, with its contribution to total revenue increasing around 42% from 12% in Q2 FY2026.

items.statement: Air Import and Air Export revenues increased 68.9% and 420% YoY respectively in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Air Import and Air Export revenues increased by 68.9% and 420% year-on-year, respectively.

items.statement: Top 5 customer contribution reduced to 33% from 41% YoY, reflecting diversification efforts.
items.quote: The contribution from our top five customers reduced to around 33% of revenue compared to 41% in Q2 FY2026. We are working to broaden our customer base and increase business from existing accounts across its sea freight, air freight and transportation offerings.

items.statement: Container deployment planned to begin in Q3 FY27; capex program to be completed during 2027 using IPO proceeds.
items.quote: Following addition of trailers during Q1 FY2027, the deployment of containers is planned to begin in Q3 FY2027. We intend to complete our planned capital expenditure program during 2027, using the IPO proceeds as outlined earlier.

items.statement: Promoter provided Rs. 60 crore interest-free loan with tenure up to 5 years, repayable based on cash flow situation.
items.quote: Yes, it is Rs. 60 crores and the tenure what we have fixed is up till 5 years. I mean this is an interest-free loan, and it can be partially or fully withdrawn back based on the cash flow situation of the company.

items.statement: Incorporated wholly owned subsidiary Glottis Logistics SDN. BHD. in Malaysia to expand freight forwarding and logistics support services.
items.quote: We also took a step towards expanding our international presence with the incorporation of our wholly owned subsidiary, Glottis Logistics SDN. BHD., in Malaysia. The subsidiary has been established to expand our freight forwarding and logistics support services.

items.statement: Industry facing pricing pressure from high freight levels; shipping lines not offering long-term contracts due to crude and charter hire volatility; all business moving on spot basis.
items.quote: Long-term contracts are not getting fulfilled by any of the shipping lines in the recent past because of the high volatility on the crude as well as the availability of the charter. The vessel charter hires are also highly fluctuated. Like, crude, vessel charter hires are also highly fluctuating. The shipping lines are not willing to sign any long-term contracts which is the situation now, everyth

items.statement: TEUs handled in Q2 FY27 were 21,375 vs 21,972 in Q2 FY26 and 21,841 in Q1 FY27; H1 FY27 TEUs 43,216 vs 47,032 in H1 FY26.
items.quote: TEUs handled during Q2 FY27 were 21,375 compared to 21,972 in Q2 FY26 and 21,841 in Q1 FY27. For the first half of FY2027, TEUs handled was 43,216 compared to 47,032 in H1 FY26.

items.statement: US tariff policies and sanctions creating uncertainty for power transmission and automobile export segments.
items.quote: Most of the customers which have concentrated is like MNCs who have got offices in both locations and some of the verticals we have been targeting is, for example, one is like in power transmission and all those things. This in spite of all the tariff level or the different kind of tariff between the countries, I think this had a huge impact as far as growth in particular sector. These are especia

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth aspiration of 70-80%
items.quote: For FY27, we had earlier outlined a growth aspiration of 70-80%, driven by the core Zappfresh business, seafood expansion, Meevaa and our growing retail network.

items.statement: Meevaa FY27 revenue contribution target 10-15%
items.quote: We had earlier outlined an aspiration for Meevaa to contribute 10-15% of FY27 revenue, supported by product innovation, wider distribution and deeper customer engagement.

items.statement: Meevaa break-even expected in FY27 within 8-9 months of operations
items.quote: As we have said from the start, for FY27 overall we expect Meevaa to break even. In H1, we had only a few months of operations in our books.

items.statement: Medium-term channel mix target 50:50 B2B:B2C
items.quote: To give you a perspective on the longer term, at a steady state we would look at a 50:50 mix between B2B and B2C.

items.statement: Meevaa facility peak revenue potential Rs 120-140 crore in immediate coming financial year
items.quote: The facility that we have acquired can generate revenue of around 120-140 crore.

items.statement: Ready-to-eat capacity can support Rs 600-700 crore revenue profile
items.quote: Once we add more automation and capacity enhancements on the same land parcel, we can look at a 600-700 crore revenue profile.

items.statement: Winter season supports stronger fresh meat consumption in H2 FY27
items.quote: The winter season typically supports stronger fresh meat consumption across our key markets, particularly chicken and mutton.

items.statement: E-commerce and quick-commerce revenue grew 3.7x in August vs July, then 8.8% sequentially in September
items.quote: Revenue from our e-commerce and quick-commerce channels grew 3.7 times in August compared with July, followed by a further 8.8% sequential increase in September.

items.statement: Standalone PAT margin maintained at 6% same as FY26; consolidated dropped to 4% due to Avyom subsidiary
items.quote: If you look at our standalone margins, they are very similar to FY26. At the bottom line, which is PAT, the standalone margin is the same 6% as in FY26. On a consolidated basis, it drops to 4%.

items.statement: Neighbourhood meat retailer partner stores expanded from 100 to 200, targeting 300-400
items.quote: From approximately 100 partner stores at the end of FY26, our network expanded to 200 stores as of September 2026, progressing towards our ambition of 300-400 stores.

items.statement: Meevaa facility acquired for ~Rs 35 crore; 5 acres land with 1 acre built up
items.quote: We have five acres of land there, of which only one acre is built up right now

items.statement: No price hikes planned; annual pricing review only; pricing managed at backend
items.quote: We do not change pricing either; we do an annual pricing review. We do not plan to change prices, and everything remains largely under control.

items.statement: Channel mix shifted to 84% B2B/HoReCa, 16% B2C in H1 FY27 from 68%/32% in FY26
items.quote: During H1 FY27, the mix shifted to 84% B2B and HoReCa and 16% B2C, reflecting the faster growth of our institutional business.

items.statement: Category mix: chicken 55%, goat 20%, fish/seafood 25% of H1 FY27 revenue
items.quote: From a category perspective, chicken continues to provide a strong volume foundation, contributing 55% of H1 FY27 revenue, followed by goat meat at 20% and fish and seafood at 25%.

items.statement: Vegetarian 7%, non-vegetarian 93% of consolidated revenue; Meevaa launched with 12 vegetarian products
items.quote: We have also expanded into vegetarian heat-and-eat products, with vegetarian and non-vegetarian categories contributing 7% and 93% of consolidated revenue, respectively.

items.statement: Meevaa domestic distribution expanded to Amazon, Amazon Now, Blinkit; quick-commerce revenue growing rapidly
items.quote: Since then, we have expanded distribution beyond the Zappfresh website and app to Amazon, Amazon Now and, more recently, Blinkit in October, strengthening our presence across e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms.

items.statement: Exports 70-80% of Meevaa revenue in H1 FY27; domestic share growing
items.quote: As | said, 70-80% in H1 would be exports, and the remainder is domestic

items.statement: Receivable days increased to 73 from 60 due to higher B2B mix (60-90 day credit terms)
items.quote: On receivables, as you mentioned, the days have increased to 73, which reflects the credit period of 60 to 90 days that we allow B2B customers.

items.statement: No new long-term debt planned; consolidating existing debt to improve interest coverage
items.quote: No, we are not planning for that. We will be consolidating some debt to improve interest coverage, but that is about it.

items.statement: Advertising cost per order declined ~60% during Meevaa launch period
items.quote: Importantly, advertising cost per order declined by approximately 60% during this period.

items.statement: Monsoon campaign reached ~65 lakh people; 11:11 campaign drove 362% increase in online orders
items.quote: Our monsoon campaign, "Baarish Waali Craving? Meevaa Hai Na", reached approximately 65 lakh people, while our 11:11 campaign, celebrating Zappfresh's 11th year, contributed to a 362% increase in online orders over June.

items.statement: Revenue guidance FY27 INR450 cr, FY28 INR600-700 cr, FY29 ~INR1,000 cr; PAT margin target 10-11%
items.quote: earlier you had given guidance of INR450 crores for FY26, then FY27 INR600 crores to INR700 crores -- sorry, FY27 INR450 crores, FY28 INR600 crores to INR700 crores, and FY29 around INR1,000 crores. Is this guidance still on track?

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20-22% for new electrical products (VCB, RMU, PCVCB)
items.quote: Almost EBITDA margin we are targeting 20% to 22%, the rest will depend on the order size and the order's valuation.

items.statement: Order book INR145 cr as of 31 Oct; pipeline ~INR120 cr (FRP/SMC INR30 cr, FRP INR20 cr, VCB/panels INR50-60 cr, tarpaulin INR10 cr)
items.quote: As of 31st October, our order book stood at INR145 crores, and our focus now is exuding the orders we have in hand.

items.statement: October revenue ~INR90 cr confirmed; H2 seasonally stronger post-monsoon
items.quote: Sir, basically I summed up all your order books and your revenue in H1. So, basically I came to know that you may have delivered something around INR90 crores in October. Am I right? Neel Shah: Yes.

items.statement: H1 FY26 total income ~INR218 cr (+94% YoY); revenue from operations up 10% vs H2 FY26
items.quote: total income over H1 FY26 ratio about 94% year-on-year to INR218 crores. EBITDA grow about 55% to INR27.7 crores, and net profit increased 76% to INR20 crores, EBITDA margin for the half was 12.69%, and we also saw the growth of process six months with revenue from operations up 10% compared with the second half of FY26.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 12.69%; margins pressured by resin/copper price volatility; expect improvement in H2 with month-to-month pricing and stable rates
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the half was 12.69%, and we also saw the growth of process six months with revenue from operations up 10% compared with the second half of FY26.

items.statement: Resin 20-30% of SMC/FRP raw material; copper 25-40% of electrical raw material; exploring hedging and IEEMI price-pass-through
items.quote: Basically, resin in our SMC and FRP is used almost 20% to 30%, which depends on the products. And copper in ours is around 25% to 40%, depending on the product range, it will vary.

items.statement: Target revenue split: electrical ~50%, SMC ~30%, FRP ~20%; electrical growing faster due to data-center/utility demand
items.quote: Basically, electrical, SMC, and FRP -- electrical will be around almost 50%, SMC will be around 30%, and we will target 20% from FRP.

items.statement: New Nashik plant 60,000 sq ft operational in ~1 month; existing plant retained for approved products; new plant for VCB, RMU, 33 kV isolators
items.quote: In Nashik, we have almost a new plant's development of around 60,000 square feet in hand, whose working will almost come in a month.

items.statement: New Nashik capacity incremental revenue INR200-300 cr at 80% utilisation; combined Nashik target INR300-400 cr electrical revenue next year
items.quote: If there is full utilization, then that is much better, even if we consider 80%, then we can target around INR200 crores to INR300 crores from there.

items.statement: Additional ~INR30 cr capex needed for 66/120 kV product range, lab upgrades
items.quote: Almost we are thinking that if our new -- whatever new product range we are developing for that, almost another around INR30 crores will be required extra, because we have to go into that product range and plus into that range of 66, 120.

items.statement: 33 kV metering cubicles approval final stage; PCVCB panel launch targeted; Ring Main Unit launch targeted June 2027
items.quote: Approvals for our 33 kV metering cubicles are in the final stage of processing. We are preparing our launch PCVCB panel, and we have targeted June 2027 for launching our Ring Main Unit.

items.statement: PCVCB revenue target INR40-50 cr in FY28; EBITDA margin 20-22%
items.quote: Next year, we are targeting INR40 crores to INR50 crores, PCVCB.

items.statement: Transformer entry: 31 MVA plant in planning; fundraising update in 15 days; start with 11/33 kV distribution transformers, later 66 kV+
items.quote: Right now we are establishing a plant of 31 MVA plant. That is currently going on. So that is currently in planning on how fundraising and all that should be planned out. Proper update on that will come in the next 15 days.

items.statement: Transformer business EBITDA margin ~20-22% at 11/33 kV; higher at 66/120 kV
items.quote: Yes, it's a little bit better. As you go better in range, go into 66, 120, even better margins will keep getting made. Right now, we are focusing on 11, 33, so a basic margin of 20% or 22% EBITDA is where the business regularly runs.

items.statement: MSEDCL vendor approval for 11/33 kV isolators; targeting BESCOM, Gujarat, other state utilities; railway approvals expected Feb-Mar, defence tenders this year
items.quote: Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company approved us as a vendor for 11 kV and 33 kV isolators. The approval gives us an opportunity to do more business with a major state utility.

items.statement: First FRP export shipment to Oman; Germany slowed due to freight cost volatility; focus shifting to Middle East & Africa
items.quote: We also made our first export shipment of these products to Oman. The shipment was an important step for us, and it gives us a starting point to build relationships with customers overseas.

items.statement: Germany shipments paused due to transport cost fluctuations; focus on Middle East/Africa for quicker delivery and safety
items.quote: Basically, product approvals have come in, but right now regarding shipments and all, because of some fluctuations in rates, we did not continue with further orders. The reason was just that the transport cost was fluctuating.

items.statement: SMC utilisation low last 6 months due to rate/material volatility; FRP at 100%; electrical running well
items.quote: Right now, basically in SMC, in the last 6 months, utilization has been very low. The reason is that due to material fluctuation and rate fluctuation, we were taking orders accordingly. FRP was running at our total 100% utilization.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative but improving vs last year; target positive by next Diwali
items.quote: Compared to last year, we have also improved a bit. Yes, we haven't done it so impactfully, but the target is that by next Diwali our cash flow also comes into positive impact.

items.statement: Adopting month-to-month orders with price variation clauses; holding max 2-3 months stock to manage rate volatility
items.quote: we are taking orders and setting up accordingly, that we will also maintain a maximum of 2 or 3 months of stock, plus we are basically taking care that rates do not impact us that much.

items.statement: CTPT indoor market ~INR12,000 cr; outdoor CT Maharashtra ~INR1,200 cr; targeting out-of-state expansion
items.quote: Indoor itself will have a business area of around INR12,000 crores market, which is used for every equipment plus counting, LT CTPT. items.statement: Currently focused on 11/33 kV in Maharashtra/MSEDCL; not yet competing broadly; higher kV (66/120) less crowded
items.quote: Competitive intensity, right now whatever our production is going, it is mostly going to MSEDCL and a little bit to private parties, because right now we will have to increase our range.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility (resin, copper) impacted H1 margins; mitigating via monthly pricing, hedging, IEEMI pass-through
items.quote: Earlier, the resin and all those things we used were petroleum-based. So many times, whatever the order was -- because we had already locked in the order book from April onwards, so due to that, the impact of fluctuations in it was higher.

items.statement: Management expects 70-80% of the Rs. 229 crore order book to be executed in H2 FY27
items.quote: We can expect conversion up to 70% to 80% of the order book.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs. 229 crores as of 30th September
items.quote: And on the 30th of September, if you see our order book, we have a total order book of Rs. 229 crores.

items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at Rs. 9.52 %compared to Rs. 13.01 %in the corresponding period last year.

items.quote: until the execution of this particular project is completed in the second half of FY27 and the first half of FY28, you will see pressure on the overall margins

items.quote: we have successfully utilized the IPO proceeds of Rs. 39.56 crores as on September 30, 2026 in line with our stated objectives. This includes Rs. 29.85 crores allocated towards the Himmat Nagar solar project

items.value: Rs. 8.50 crores unsecured loan, Rs. 5 crores cash credit, Rs. 2.58 crores term loan
items.quote: We raised Rs 8.50 crores through unsecured loan, enhanced our cash rate limit to Rs. 5 crores and secured new term loan of Rs. 2.58 crores for Rashtrapati Bhawan project.

items.quote: Since there is increasing trade receivable, there is increasing trade payables as well. So, basically, it is a working capital arrangement for funding our project of 65 MW.

items.quote: we are having 15 MW to 16 MW running our IPP project. Along with that, we have capital work in progress of almost 10 MW to 11 MW.

items.quote: So, we have about 19.5 lakh units in it. 19 lakh to 19.5 lakh units come from it. So, you can see that here, in a simple fixed-panel system, it is 15 lakh to 16 lakh units, whereas here it is 19 lakh to 19.5 lakh units.

items.quote: For example, in our group, there is Uma group, Apollo group, Pragna group, there are many groups, Gayatri Ispat is there. We have worked on all of them.

items.quote: We are installing a 1 MW rooftop solar project at India's Rashtrapati Bhawan. In fact, the project is currently under progress. The project will be commissioned in the coming months.

items.statement: Unique solar park turnkey model with land acquisition, substation connectivity, tracker technology, and 25-year O&M creates competitive moat in Gujarat
items.quote: this model is done by very few people in Gujarat. And we were the only one in this area. So, we delivered such a product that people wanted it, and we entered there at the right time.

items.quote: GRC has made a policy draft in Gujarat, which has not been finalized yet. So as soon as it is finalized, we will directly introduce BESS.

items.quote: normally these projects work at 25:75 ratio. So 25% of the funding is done from own accruals and 75% of the funding for the project is done from bank finance.

items.statement: O&M handled in-house by dedicated team with SOPs; not offered to third-party asset owners
items.quote: We have created a special department. We have built a good team. And we have made a special SOP everywhere. According to that SOP, we do not go to do O&M for anyone. We only do O&M for our own customers.

items.statement: No current plans for asset monetization or strategic partnerships to unlock capital from RESCO portfolio
items.quote: No, sir. No, sir. At present, no.

items.quote: As far as certain figures that you are demanding futuristic, that we cannot comment right now.

items.statement: Management expects to protect service EBITDA on an absolute value basis next year, with margin percentage potentially higher, but no exact numbers given pending final regulations.
items.quote: we see that we should be able to protect next year our service EBITDA on an absolute value basis. So, on a percentage, it could be higher, but on an absolute value basis, we will be able to protect the service EBITDA.

items.statement: Cash balance expected to be slightly higher than INR 740 crores by March 31 due to working capital movements, refunds, and tax utilization.
items.quote: we should actually end the financial year with a slightly higher cash balance as at March 31. So, we'll end the year with a fairly strong cash position as of March 31.

items.statement: Platform premium grew 52% YoY to INR 2,419 crores in H1 FY27, driven by Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets.
items.quote: Platform premium for us grew by about 52% to INR 2,419 crores. Major portion, as we know, the premium came from Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets.

items.quote: In Q2, premium grew 55% to INR 1,214 crores. This was due to strong adoption of our Turtlefin platform.

items.quote: And there was an improvement in adjusted EBITDA margin. It improved from minus 17% last year in H1 to minus 7%.

items.quote: We acquire assets at 6%-7%, or whatever that is, but we have baked in that we should be able to push it and keep our guidance to 10%.

items.statement: AI infrastructure demand structural not cyclical; hyperscaler capex accelerating (Meta compute initiative, Google-Blackstone Crux.ai); US to add 100+ GW capacity; four largest hyperscalers investing $725-750 billion in 2026
items.quote: In general, any rollback in my mind is not expected. It is about creating differentiated experiences for 6 billion users across the world. Once we get used to how we operate, we will not roll back.

items.statement: Deepening relationships with strategic hyperscalers; expanding to newer hyperscalers and geographies; enterprise diversification across tech, healthcare, financial services, industrial, retail
items.quote: Our focus this year is to get into deeper engagements with newer hyperscalers that we have been working. We start smaller and start to get into larger projects.

items.statement: Not visa-dependent; H-1B/L-visa changes will not impact growth or hiring plans; local US company with limited visa exposure
items.quote: Black Box is a local company, and Black Box is neither a visa-dependent. When I say visa-dependent, it means more than 50% of your workforce is visa-dependent, but like most IT service companies, we're definitely not visa-dependent, and there are very limited H-1B visas for us.

items.statement: Contract mix includes fixed price, T&M, and cost-plus; overall blend delivers stated gross margins; change orders for scope changes on fixed price
items.quote: There are all kinds of contracts. There are some scope for fixed price. As long as the customer is able to give us a fixed scope, we can deliver a fixed price, a fixed margin. If there are any changes, we will get into a change order.

items.statement: Order backlog tenure currently ~18 months; expected to increase to 20-22 months by FY27 end and plateau around 24 months as large multi-year data center contracts ramp
items.quote: What will happen is that with securing of these larger orders, probably this 18 months backlog tenure will become probably 20-22 months, and ultimately it can go, let's say, in next one year time to 24 months also.

items.statement: Receivables coming down; first payment on large projects hits at 90-105 days vs 60-day terms causing initial cash conversion lag; regular cycle expected by Q4
items.quote: Because what happens is that when you start these large projects, there are teething, let us say, issues and all those things, while the customer payment term is 60 days, but the first payment hits only in 90 to 105 days.

items.statement: Interest cost stable; inorganic acquisitions may add modest debt but EBITDA flow-through to PAT expected to improve net margins to 6-6.5% in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: The interest cost is a factor of little bit on the organic, on the inorganic side, what we do, because inorganic side, if we get, let's say, the good opportunity and all those things, little bit of debt comes in on that, then probably the interest cost will be plus-minus little bit of the number.

items.statement: No slowdown seen in order backlog or pipeline despite US political changes; hyperscalers increasing capex each earnings call; structural AI demand shift
items.quote: We are not seeing anything slowing down in our current order backlog that is up for execution. In fact, on the contrary, in many of the places, we are seeing uptake and speed-up being happening.

items.statement: Large hyperscaler projects services-led (96-98%); enterprise includes managed services, T&M, and partner-led projects with CommScope/Cisco/Juniper; blended gross margin consistent ~30%
items.quote: For large projects, for hyperscalers, we do not make supplies, except, as Deepak said, 2%, 3%, 4% of supplies of, that is inconsequential. It is largely a services-led business.

items.statement: US key growth engine with 35-country global presence; serving hyperscalers in Europe and LATAM; India as GCC and development center
items.quote: We operate in all the significant markets. We recently expanded our presence in LATAM through an acquisition, so collectively we are stronger.

items.statement: Global IT spending to exceed $7 trillion in 2027 per Gartner; $1.36 trillion data center spending; Black Box positioned in largest market
items.quote: According to Gartner's October publication, global IT spending is expected to exceed $7 trillion for the first time in 2027, with AI-related investments accelerating across the technology stack, including approximately $1.36 trillion in data center spending.

items.statement: JLR FY27 EBIT guidance revised to 2-3% range with cash outflow of GBP 1.25 billion
items.quote: so we will have to change our FY27 guidance, now expecting EBIT in the 2% to 3% range and cash outflow of circa GBP 1.25 billion.

items.statement: JLR targets double-digit EBITDA and cash generation in FY28, aims to return to net cash by end of FY30
items.value: double-digit EBITDA; net cash by FY30
items.quote: we are targeting double-digit EBITDA and cash generation in FY28 and aim to return to net cash by the end of FY30 as these amazing new product launches start to drive through.

items.statement: Domestic business FY27 capex guided at 6-7% of revenue
items.quote: it will be between 6% to 7% of the revenue.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt expected to close FY27 around Rs. 47,000 Cr from current Rs. 51,000 Cr
items.quote: We expect to close the year lower at around Rs. 47,000 Cr as some of that unwinds.

items.statement: EV production to increase from 16,000 to 20,000 units per month in next 2-3 months
items.quote: the effort is that in the next two to three months, we increase our production from roughly 16,000, which has been for the last two to three months, we now move towards the 20,000 level

items.statement: TMPV EV penetration expected at 25%+ next year from current 23%
items.quote: We expect to grow both in ICE and EV. So, it would be around 25% or slightly above that.

items.statement: PLI accruals run rate of at least Rs. 530 Cr per quarter expected for H2
items.quote: we believe that at least that's the minimum run rate we are going to maintain towards H2.

items.statement: JLR VME spend may increase slightly in H2 FY27 then decline in FY28 as new BEVs enter mix
items.quote: it may go up a little bit more, and then during the course of the next financial year, as those vehicles start to become significant in our mix, it will go back down again.

items.statement: Domestic industry volumes grew 29% YoY to 1.36 million units in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The passenger vehicle industry continued its strong momentum during the quarter with volumes at 1.36 million units, growing by approximately 29% year-on-year.

items.statement: TMPV Q2 volumes up 40% YoY to ~2 lakh units, market share 14.3%; October retail up 10% YoY to 75,000 units
items.quote: We delivered our highest-ever quarterly volume of about 2 lakh units, representing 40% year-on-year growth. This enabled us to consolidate our position as the number-two player in the industry with a domestic market share of 14.3%.

items.statement: EV demand ahead of capacity with 10 days inventory vs 27-28 days overall; 30% of bookings and 40-45% of pending bookings are EVs
items.quote: We have only 10 days of inventory for EVs, whereas overall our inventories are around 27 to 28 days. This includes the transit inventory of about six to seven days. So, definitely, in EV, we have huge pending bookings and significantly low inventory.

items.statement: JLR China wholesales down 45% YoY in Q2 and 36% YTD; market declining at alarming speed
items.quote: Our wholesales were down 45% year-over-year in that quarter and 36% down year-to-date. There's no reason to assume that MENA won't ultimately recover. The same cannot be said about China, and I'll give more detail on that later on.

items.statement: JLR MENA demand and logistics struggling due to conflict
items.quote: MENA demand and logistics continues to struggle as a result of the conflict

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 6.2%, EBIT margin 1.1% in Q2; sequential EBIT margin fell from 2.4% to 1.1% due to adverse JLR mix and commodity pressures
items.quote: Sequentially, EBIT margins moved from 2.4% to 1.1% as adverse mix at JLR and continuing commodity pressures in India weighed on margins.

items.statement: Domestic business profitability flattish sequentially; commodity pressures elevated in Q3 with steel, rubber, copper increases and FX resets
items.quote: We expect commodity pressures to remain elevated in Q3 with further increases in steel, rubber, and copper and the periodic FX resets that we expect to come through.

items.statement: Year-to-date calibrated price increases and cost actions offset ~40% of commodity increase; balance absorbed
items.quote: Year-to-date our calibrated price increases, cost actions have offset roughly 40% of the commodity increase, while we have absorbed the balance.

items.statement: JLR managing material cost inflation through ex-works cost reduction mission; copper, aluminum, petrochemicals rising
items.quote: Copper prices, aluminum prices, petrochemicals, plastics, etc., are going up. We have had an ex-works cost reduction mission live for some time, and it is starting to be able to offset some of those.

items.statement: JLR committed to GBP 1.7bn cost savings over two years; GBP 400m annual savings from voluntary redundancy of ~4,000 salaried staff
items.quote: We are underway in all of our missions to reset our breakevens to 300,000 units. But we also need to build greater resilience and to free our people up from outdated systems and processes and bring them into a world of AI. So, in relation to growth in particular, I've got three charts. The first one is the next. Next chart, please.

items.statement: Aeris demand ahead of capacity; sold 4,000 units in first month, expanding capacity to 5,000+
items.quote: Demand has been ahead of our current capacity with Aeris selling over 4,000 units in its first month actually limited by its production. We are now expanding the capacity in response to the strong demand.

items.statement: Sierra sold over 70,000 units this year; working to scale capacity further
items.quote: We have sold over 70,000 units of Sierra this year and now working to scale capacity further to meet the demand.

items.statement: Punch.ev is most popular EV in market, first to cross 5,000 units in a month
items.quote: The Punch.ev has further strengthened the brand, finding a clear sweet spot with EV customers. It is now the most popular EV in the market and the first EV to cross 5,000 units in a month.

items.statement: Range Rover BEV has nearly 5,000 orders before launch
items.quote: Even without seeing the car or driving it, we have nearly 5,000 orders.

items.statement: H1 consolidated capex Rs. 2,700 Cr; expect higher run rate over next 18-24 months for next phase of capacity builds
items.quote: H1 Capex was Rs. 2,700 Cr. We are running at roughly similar levels as last year, but we do expect to run higher over the next 18 to 24 months as the next phase of capacity builds gap of space.

items.statement: JLR H1 investment GBP 1.76bn; H2 expected marginally below H1, then declining further next year
items.quote: The total for the first half of the year was GBP 1.76 billion, and we're expecting H2 to be marginally below this, and then it will decline a little bit further into next year.

items.statement: JLR invested GBP 11.5bn of GBP 15-18bn five-year program; five vehicles launching in next 18 months
items.quote: We announced a while ago, we have an investment program of GBP 15 to GBP 18 million -- billion, sorry, over five years. And we've invested GBP 11.5 billion of that already.

items.statement: Aeris capacity constrained at 4,000/month; expanding to 5,000+ based on demand
items.quote: First month, we supplied about 4,000 numbers. We are trying to now increase it to 5,000, and we have to increase it more basis the demand that we are seeing.

items.statement: Average 1.7% price increase across ICE and EV portfolio over three hikes in April, July, September
items.quote: across the ICE and EV portfolio on average, we have taken about 1.7% price increase across three hikes in April, July and September.

items.statement: Price hike confirmed for Q4, potentially one in Q3; slightly higher than previous hikes
items.quote: Price hikes, yes, it is going to happen in Q4, slightly higher than what we have been taking. We will also watch after assessing the full impact of what commodity will hit us in Q3. We might consider a price increase in this quarter also. One price increase in Q3 and maybe another in Q4. But for sure in Q4, this is what we have, we can reconfirm, but also potentially one in Q3.

items.statement: Alternate powertrains >50% of domestic volumes; EV penetration 23%, CNG growing
items.quote: Alternate powertrains now account for more than half of volumes with EV penetration at 23%.

items.statement: EV revenue >1/3 of total domestic revenue at 23% volume penetration
items.quote: For revenue, this would be now greater than a third of the overall revenue for EV.

items.statement: JLR mix deterioration: China and MENA decline, Discovery push reduced Range Rover/Defender share
items.quote: China going down, MENA going down, and then balancing into other regions has a net negative effect for us. Secondly, we had a big push on discovery in the quarter. And even though Range Rover and Defender were up versus the first quarter, their percentage of our total was down.

items.statement: Punch highest selling model in India in Q2; Nexon among top 5 in H1
items.quote: In particular, Punch emerged as the highest selling model in India during the quarter while Nexon was among the top five models in H1 FY27.

items.statement: EV market share rose to 43% despite rising competition; industry EV volumes up 70% YoY
items.quote: Our EV market share rose to 43% despite rising competition reinforcing our market leadership while significantly scaling the segment.

items.statement: Chinese OEM exports up nearly 4 million units YoY, ~10% of global ex-China/US market; JLR defending IP
items.quote: Exports are up nearly 4 million units year-over-year, and that increase alone is circa 10% of the total global car market, if you exclude China exporting them, and the U.S., which is protected.

items.statement: CAFE III policy notified, reinforcing shift to greener powertrains
items.quote: The regulatory environment also continues to reinforce the shift towards greener powertrains, most notably through the recently notified CAFE III policy.

items.statement: H1 free cash flow positive ~Rs. 2,000 Cr aided by favorable working capital and PLI receipt
items.quote: H1 free cash f low was positive at about Rs. 2,000 Cr, aided by favorable working capital and receipt of last year's PLI cash release.

items.statement: JLR H1 cash outflow GBP 1.5bn including negative seasonal working capital; expect recovery in Q4
items.quote: With the effect of working capital included, our H1 cash outflow was GBP 1.5 billion.

items.statement: JLR voluntary redundancy program: ~3,000 of 4,000 targeted salaried staff to leave by end-November, rest next year
items.quote: As of today, we expect around 3,000 colleagues to leave us this financial year, and the majority of those will leave at the end of November, i.e. 17 days' time.

items.statement: China market structural decline risk; JLR not overreacting but will remain invested for technology innovation
items.quote: the market itself has declined by 30%, then it's probably cyclical, structural, those are things we just need to read correctly. And we just want to take our time to get that right.

items.statement: JLR H1 EBIT 2%, PBT GBP 115m; Q2 EBIT margin impacted by volume/mix
items.quote: Year-to-date, at the bottom of the page, for the first half of the year, our EBIT was 2%, and PBT was GBP 115 million, with cash outflows similar to last year.

items.statement: Domestic industry greener powertrain share ~33% (EV 8%, CNG 25%)
items.quote: This takes the combined share of greener powertrains that is, EV and CNG, to around one-third of industry volumes.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 10-15% revenue CAGR with sustainable EBITDA margins of 10-12%
items.quote: Over the medium term, we remain committed to our objective of delivering 10% to 15% revenue CAGR with sustainable EBITDA margins of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Next three years top-line CAGR of 10-12% and EBITDA of 10-12%
items.quote: So translate it to numbers, probably we want to grow in next three years at a CAGR of 10% to 12% top line and probably about 10% to 12% EBITDA.

items.statement: Cement Roofing Q2 volumes up ~20%, turnover up 34% YoY; H1 volumes up 14% with significant margins
items.quote: Cement Roofing- Quarter 2 volumes increased by approximately 20%, while turnover grew 34% year-on-year. For H1 FY27, volumes increased by 14% with significant margins.

items.statement: V-Next boards volumes up ~9% and turnover up 13% for H1 FY27; panels volumes up 55% and turnover up 56% YoY in Q2
items.value: boards volumes +9%, turnover +13%; panels volumes +55%, turnover +56%
items.quote: Boards volumes increased by approximately 9% and turnover by 13% for H1 FY27, while maintaining healthy high-double-digit margins despite lower exports to GCC markets due to Middle East war situation. Panels continue to be our fastest-growing division with quarter 2 volumes increasing by 55% and turnover growing by 56% year-on-year.

items.statement: Synthetic Yarn capacity utilization increased to 92% from 89%; Q2 revenue grew 16% YoY; segment PBIT improved to ~INR5 cr from INR2 cr
items.quote: The capacity utilization increased to 92% from 89%, while quarter 2 revenue grew by 16% year-on-year. Segment profit before interest and tax improved to approximately INR5 crores from INR2 crores, reflecting better operating efficiencies and cost optimization.

items.statement: Fibre cement boards margins at 14-15%; roofing sheet margins improved with price increases
items.quote: Our margins in fibre cement boards is good. We are having about 14% to 15% margin. While I said the Roofing Sheet business is a seasonal product. However, we have increased the prices and the margins were improved.

items.statement: Tonk fibre cement and calcium silicate board facility progressing as planned; construction chemical project at Tumkur targeted for completion in January 2027
items.quote: The proposed fiber cement boards and calcium silicate board facility at Tonk is progressing as planned, while construction chemical project at Tumkur is targeted for completion in January 2027.

items.statement: Tonk facility expected operational by December 2027 into 2028
items.quote: 2027 December into '28 yes.

items.statement: Wood pulp sourced from France, Russia, New Zealand; alternative supply chains created; no near-term import issues expected
items.quote: We have no issues with the supply. We have alternative supply chain right now. We get our wood pulp from France and Russia, New Zealand. So we've created good channels and not just put all the eggs in one basket.

items.statement: V-Next competitive advantages: product quality, designer/premium boards with many designs, larger distribution channel; pricing similar to competitors with small differences across states
items.quote: quality perceived to be better than others. And our distribution channel is larger than other competitors.
