Ramakrishna Pendyala: In some states, the competitors have a little higher pricing and then some states,

items.statement: BIS introduction on metal roofing sheets reduced China imports and increased local procurement costs, benefiting cement roofing demand
items.quote: And also the substitute products like metal sheet prices have gone up because of BIS introduction, China imports have come down and the local procurement cost also have gone up and the prices finally gone up for the metal roofing sheets.

items.statement: Cash generated from operations increased to ~INR70 cr from INR55 cr in corresponding period last year
items.quote: While cash generated from operations increased to approximately INR70 crores from INR55 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: ATUM integrated solar roofing: 40-50% space saving vs traditional solar roof with similar power generation; installed capacity 30 MW/annum
items.quote: we have a long-term energy generation and recurring savings. Also, the life cycle cost is much reduced with improved return on investments because right now, what we are looking for is educating people on saying that there is a 40% to 50% saving in the space compared to a traditional solar roof which generates almost the same power

items.statement: No plans for own retail stores; will expand dealer base across states for fibre cement boards
items.quote: See we don't see any specific retail channel or retail stores. However, our company is there in the industry since more than 40 years. So we have large distribution say across India. So with the expansion of the dealers base, probably specific to different states, we will be able to achieve it, but we don't have any plans to open our own retail stores.

items.statement: No expansion plans for Synthetic Yarn division; focusing on efficiency and profitability improvement at current capacity
items.quote: So right now, we have no plans on any expansion with regards to textile division. So we're right now using our maximum capacities. We are optimizing on our cost and also our operations are tightened.

items.statement: Cement roofing not phasing out; limited new industry capacity being added; substitute price increases supporting demand
items.quote: Right now, no. Right now, even though there is very limited new capacity is being added across this roofing industry, it's a very volume-based division. So, I would not say that it's going to phase out. But while it lasts, we want to make the most out of it. Ramakrishna Pendyala: And as we mentioned earlier, substitute product prices have gone up. So at the moment, we don't see any de-growth in th

items.statement: Construction chemicals entry rationale: offer compound building material solutions alongside allied products in building space
items.quote: , like a lot of companies are offering the allied products in the building space. So we also would like to come into this construction chemicals and then give it as a compound building material solutions.

items.statement: ATUM patents granted in US, South Africa, and recently Europe; exploring international opportunities but not yet materialized
items.quote: About patent, yes, we have in U.S., we have in South Africa. And recently, we have got the patent in Europe as well. So we are exploring the opportunities in other countries, too, but did not get materialized as of now.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at approximately 30% year-on-year
items.quote: For FY27, management is maintaining its revenue growth guidance of approximately 30%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin outlook of 26% to 27% for full year
items.quote: On margins, management has discussed a broad 26% to 27% range for FY27.

items.statement: Board approved additional 3,250 tons capacity with INR31 crores investment, total expansion now 11,750 tons for INR151 crores
items.quote: In addition, the Board today further approved additional capacity of approximately 3,250 tons with an estimated investment of INR31 crores. Upon completion, our total manufacturing capacity would increase by 11,750 tons from the existing 29,000 tons to 40,750 tons with a total investment of INR151 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan of INR60 crores, with INR19 crores spent in H1 and INR40 crores expected in H2
items.quote: So current year, we will be investing maybe about INR60 crores by 31 March '27.

items.statement: Targeting commissioning of new foundry around 1 April 2028, with efforts to complete earlier
items.quote: Management is currently targeting commissioning of the new foundry around 1 April 2028, while making efforts to complete the project earlier, if feasible.

items.statement: Existing capacity utilization expected around 60% for FY27
items.quote: Management currently expects utilization of the existing capacity to be broadly around 60% during FY27.

items.statement: Executable order book at approximately INR145 crores, equivalent to around 3 months of sales
items.quote: Our executable order book stood at approximately INR145 crores, equivalent to around 3 months of sales.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 24.5%, down 387 bps year-on-year due to product development, manpower investment and raw material pass-through timing
items.quote: The EBITDA margin stood at 24.5% compared with 28.3% in Q2 FY26, a slight moderation of 387 basis points.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 margins expected under pressure due to pass-through timing mismatch from September input cost increase
items.quote: We expect margins to remain under some pressure in Q3 due to the timing of our price pass-through mechanism.

items.statement: Raw material cost increased INR2 crores in Q2 from first week of September, to be passed through in Q4
items.quote: So just to give you a very macro number, our raw material cost was INR2 crores higher compared to Q1, and which happened only from the first week of September in the current year.

items.statement: Natural gas prices increased nearly 100% from February levels, impact to be recovered through price corrections in Q4
items.quote: The natural gas has gone through the roof, almost increased 100% compared to February prices.

items.statement: Export-domestic mix expected to remain 50/50 plus/minus 5% over long term, H2 FY27 exports may slightly exceed domestic
items.quote: Over a longer term, if you see the past 5 years and forward 5 years, this exports will be 50% plus/minus 5% and domestic will be 50% plus/minus 5%.

items.statement: Demand driven by elevated commodity prices boosting mining, earthmoving, construction, railroad; China Plus One tailwinds; customer willingness to develop more parts
items.quote: What we have been hearing from our customers is that the commodity prices are likely to be staying at elevated levels. A, so with that, there will be more investments into mining, earthmoving industry, together with construction and railroad.

items.statement: Sales on ex-works basis since last 5 years, logistics costs borne by customers, no pass-through mechanism needed
items.quote: Now, since the last 5 years, all Steelcast sales are on an ex-works basis. The logistics is taken care of by the customer.

items.statement: Debt-free for third consecutive year, free reserves approximately INR120 crores invested in FDs, mutual funds, secured bonds
items.quote: The company has remained debt free for the third consecutive year. Our free reserves were approximately INR120 crores.

items.statement: Committed to consistent annual dividend payout of 20%
items.quote: We remain committed to balancing shareholder returns with the capital requirements of the business while maintaining a consistent annual payout of 20%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 ROCE 28.8%, ROE 21.9%, broadly stable year-on-year
items.quote: Our return on capital employed for H1 FY27 stood at 28.8% compared with 28.6% for FY26. Our return on equity for H1 FY27 was 21.9%, broadly stable compared with 22.0% in FY26.

items.statement: CNC machine orders worth INR35 crores placed in September, deliveries scheduled January 2027 to January 2028
items.quote: We have placed orders for different types of CNC machines, with deliveries scheduled between January 2027 and January 2028. These orders, amounting to approximately ₹35 crore, were placed in September.

items.statement: Additional 6 MW solar capacity targeted for commissioning by March 31, 2028 to meet 80% captive consumption for existing facility
items.quote: To achieve this, we need an additional 6 MW of solar capacity. Our team is currently scouting for suitable land for the project, which we intend to commission by March 31, 2028.

items.statement: New facility requires 15 MW renewable power for 80% captive generation, land acquisition in progress
items.quote: For our new facility, we need to install 15 megawatts of renewable power on the basis of 80% captive generation.

items.statement: GET products currently 1.5% of sales, targeting 6% by FY29; defense no longer focus area, railways targeting 5% by FY29
items.quote: GETs currently is only about 1.5% of sales. And that is why we did not include it in the management commentary. But our longer-term plan, say, by FY29, from the current 1.5%, we will go up to about 6% of our total sales.

items.statement: Tariffs revised 2-3 times since April 2025, currently around 12-15% range, customers absorbing increases, no demand impact so far
items.quote: But it should be around 12% to 15% range.

items.statement: Margin pressure in Q3 from pass-through timing mismatch: passing on July-August cost reductions while absorbing September cost increases
items.quote: Accordingly, Q3 is expected to carry both the pass-through of the earlier cost reduction and the temporary absorption of the more recent cost increase.

items.statement: Recruited and training additional employees in advance of foundry expansion, deliberate investment for workforce readiness
items.quote: Second, employee expenses increased as we recruited and began training additional employees in advance of the upcoming foundry expansion.

items.statement: Physical purchase orders typically 3-4 months visibility, rolling 12-month forecasts from customers, no multi-year firm order book
items.quote: At any point in time, physical purchase orders generally represent around 3 to 4 months of sales, while the balance is based on customer forecasts and their rolling production plans.

items.statement: Existing customers willing to develop more parts with Steelcast vs competition, supporting expansion decision
items.quote: Fourth is the existing customers are willing to make us develop more parts compared to the competition.

items.statement: Product development expenditure INR1 crore higher in Q2 vs Q1 for trials, experiments, rework across 111 parts over 3-year rollout
items.quote: First, we incurred approximately INR1 crores of additional expenditure during the quarter on new product development, including trials, experiments and rework.

items.statement: 55 new parts under development, 32 developed, 15 commercialized in FY27 across 3-year product development program
items.quote: At the time of presentation during the period April to September '26, 55 new parts are under development in various stages of sampling, tooling and customer qualification, and 32 new parts have been developed and 15 out of them have been commercialized during FY27 and moved towards revenue generation.

items.statement: Renewable energy portfolio planned at 13.3 MW: 9.5 MW commissioned, 2.4 MW hybrid and 1.4 MW solar under commissioning by Dec 31, 2026
items.quote: Our renewable energy portfolio is planned at 13.3 megawatts, comprising 9.5 megawatts of already commissioned and a further 2.4 megawatts of hybrid power plant and 1.4 megawatts of solar power plant, which are under commissioning.

items.statement: Renewable energy plants targeted to generate annual power cost savings of approximately INR4.5 crores
items.quote: These 2 plants are targeted for commissioning by 31 December '26 and are expected to generate annual power cost savings of approximately INR4.5 crores.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin target of 25% over 2-3 year horizon
items.quote: And also on a longer-term basis, I'm talking about a 2- to 3-year horizon, 25% will be a sustainable number.

items.statement: Historically second half better than first half, expecting improved volumes in Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.quote: As we speak now and with improved volumes in Q3 and Q4 for FY27, we expect growth of 30% compared to FY26.

items.statement: FY27 targets: 15% revenue growth, ~20% EBITDA margin, ~100% cash conversion
items.value: 15% revenue growth, ~20% EBITDA margin, ~100% cash conversion
items.quote: On our outlook for FY27, we remain confident of achieving our financial targets of 15% revenue growth, operating EBITDA margins of around 20%, and cash conversion of approximately 100%.

items.statement: Domestic wire rope volumes up 14% YoY in Q2 to 12,700 MT despite monsoon
items.quote: Demand for wire ropes has remained healthy across key applications, and we recorded volumes of 12,700 metric ton in Q2, despite the monsoon season, an increase of 14% from the same period last year.

items.statement: Middle East wire rope volumes down ~30% YoY in H1 due to geopolitical uncertainty and freight costs
items.quote: In the Middle East, as Shreya mentioned, our volumes, we were expecting growth with our expansion in Saudi Arabia. We were expecting to grow there significantly. items.statement: Domestic PTA capacity coming online: GAIL 1.25M tons Mangalore plant commissioned 5 Nov, IOCL Paradip commissioning started Sep, will reduce import dependence
items.quote: Indian Oil mechanically completed its Paradip PX-PTA Complex in September and has commenced commissioning activities. Subsequently, GAIL announced the commissioning of its 1.25 million tons per annum Mangalore PTA plant on 5th November. As production stabilizes, these facilities should improve domestic availability and reduce exposure to import-related supply disruptions.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA per kg improved to INR9.79 from INR8.67 in Q1 FY27 (13% sequential) and INR8.77 in Q2 FY26 (11.6% YoY)
items.quote: In Q2 FY '27, this increased to INR9.79 per kg from INR8.67 in Q1 FY '27, an improvement of 13% compared with INR8.77 in Q2 FY '26, an increase of 11.6%.

items.statement: Steam project expected to generate INR60-65 crore EBITDA gains from mid-Q4 FY27
items.quote: That the stated INR60 crores to INR65 crores of EBITDA gains that is -- that will be reducing the conversion cost. So that will be coming from the fourth quarter -- mid of the fourth quarter? Madhu Sudhan Bhageria: Correct

items.statement: EU FTA and domestic PTA capacity to strengthen polyester value chain and export demand
items.quote: India's textile exporters are gaining better market access while additional domestic PTA capacity is moving into production. These developments should strengthen the polyester value chain through greater exports opportunity and more reliable raw material availability.

items.statement: Plan for two 150,000 ton Ecosis plants (India and Vietnam) by Q1 CY2029
items.quote: We plan to do much more, which I have already stated, I think, in some of the conversations that we plan to put 2 plants of 150,000 tons, one in India, one in Vietnam. And they should be commissioned by first quarter of calendar year 2029.

items.statement: Additional Ecosis capacity expansions to take 18-24 months after current plant commissioning
items.quote: The new capacities will take anywhere from 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Crude oil volatility and geopolitical uncertainty to continue influencing buying decisions
items.quote: Looking ahead, crude oil volatility and geopolitical uncertainty will continue to influence buying decisions.

items.statement: Bangladesh textile exports may become uncompetitive post EU FTA as they import yarn/fabrics from China while India has full value chain
items.quote: They buy a lot of fabrics and yarns from China and then do the job work and send it. So they were thriving on the basically custom duty difference, which goes away, I think it will be difficult for them to sustain that kind of export.

items.statement: Exchange fluctuation loss INR4.79 crore in Q2 FY27 includes working capital and capital forex impact
items.quote: Exchange fluctuation net, that line is there in the profitability. Like last quarter, it was INR4.79 crores. This includes both...

items.statement: Management does not provide formal guidance but expects strong H2 performance based on current trends and sales system contribution rising to 45%
items.quote: we don't give any future guidance. But see, last few quarters have been encouraging and the current trends, even in the running quarter is giving us good numbers.

items.statement: Volume growth of 14.6% in Q2 FY27 and 18.1% in H1 FY27, significantly outpacing industry volume growth of ~1% in H1
items.quote: industry without OBL in H1 would have grown volumes by about 1%-odd, if I remember right. While for H1, Orient Bell has improved volumes by about 18%-odd.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 380 bps YoY to 9.8% in Q2 FY27 and 430 bps to 9.3% in H1 FY27; double-digit EBITDA margin expected in H2
items.quote: EBITDA for Q2 FY27 stood at INR22.4 crores with EBITDA margin of 9.8%, reflecting an expansion of 380 basis points.

items.statement: Average selling price increased to INR333 in Q2 from INR320-321 in Q1; held prices despite Morbi price cuts; gas cost at INR60 blended vs Morbi's INR83
items.quote: quarter 2 was INR333, quarter 1 was about INR320, INR321. So we are kind of holding on to the gains which were there.

items.statement: GVT salience increased from ~20% in FY22-23 to 45% currently; ceramic-to-GVT conversion of 1.2 msqm completed in Oct'26
items.quote: in last 4, 5 years, I think '22, '23, our GVT salience was around 20%, which is currently at 45%.

items.statement: Capacity utilization reached 75% in Q2; Dora plant utilization at 88-89%; 1.2 msqm ceramic-to-GVT conversion completed Oct'26
items.quote: We continue to witness an improvement with utilization levels reaching 75% in Q2.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR20 crores including maintenance; ceramic-to-GVT conversion completed; future capex likely greenfield/brownfield not further conversions
items.quote: for the current financial year, we'll be spending on an overall basis, including the maintenance capex, somewhere around INR20-odd crores.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 18 days from 20 days in Mar'26; DSO reduced from 48 to 43 days vs Q4 FY26; debtor levels down 5% despite 41% revenue growth
items.quote: Our working capital cycle improved to 18 days compared to 20 days in March '26.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet with healthy cash balance and liquid investments; adhesive business 80% cash-and-carry
items.quote: the company continues to maintain debt-free position, supported by healthy cash balance and liquid investments.

items.statement: Project-to-retail ratio constant at 80-20; walked away from some large projects due to margin/credit terms; compensated with mid/small projects
items.quote: our ratio of projects, Apurva, to retail has been constant. We continue to be in that 80-20 ratio.

items.statement: Gained market share with 18% volume growth vs industry ~1%; Morbi price volatility creates opportunity; 30-40% Morbi units closed
items.quote: if we have grown in H1 at 18% volume and, say, 40% top line versus 24%, 25% top line for the industry, there is an improvement in market share.

items.statement: Blended gas cost ~INR60/MSM similar to Q1; Morbi propane cost rose from INR67 to INR83 (20% increase); all facilities now powered by green energy
items.quote: On an overall basis, our blended gas cost is similar to Q1. It is around INR60-odd.

items.statement: Sales system contribution to retail improved from ~30% to 45%; adhesive business (Masterbond) grew 36% QoQ to INR3.2 cr from 4 manufacturing locations
items.quote: The contribution of our sales system to the overall retail is constantly increasing. It was around 30%-odd last year, which has improved to 45%

items.statement: Promoter Mr. Daga maintains separation of ownership and management; professional management led by CEO Aditya Gupta
items.quote: He strongly believes in keeping ownership and management separate. That's been his style forever to leave it to a professional manager.

items.statement: Expects gold loan AUM growth of 25%-30% for FY27
items.quote: We expect gold loan growth of 25% to 30% this year, supported by branch expansion and digital channels, and governed by the same appraisal and loan-to-value and custody standards.

items.statement: Targets ROA of 3.5%-4% and ROE of 15%-18%
items.quote: We told ROA to be somewhere between 3.5% to 4% and ROE between 15% to 18%. We stick to that.

items.statement: Expects cost of borrowing to increase 25-30 bps by Q4 FY27 exit
items.quote: From an overall Q4 exit, you could probably expect my cost of borrowing to go up more towards the 9% handle. And that is in line with what was communicated in the Q1 call as well. So, that is what we are holding to, that in terms of the exit cost of borrowing will probably increase by about 25 to 30 basis points.

items.statement: Plans to add 500 branches by March 2027; 100 opened in H1, 250 more in progress
items.quote: We plan to add around 500 branches by March 2027 to our existing consolidated network of 5,375 branches.

items.statement: Another 250 branches under construction, expected to open in a couple of months
items.quote: Even though we have opened nearly 100 branches so far, another 250 branches, the work is in the full swing, and we expect that to be opened in another couple of months.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM at INR73,303 crores, up 5.3% QoQ and 60.1% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, consolidated Assets Under Management stood at INR73,303 crores, up by 60.1% year-on-year, and up by 5.3% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM at INR60,640 crores, up 6.4% QoQ and 92.5% YoY
items.quote: Gold loan continues to be our key growth driver with an AUM of INR60,640 crores, up 6.4% quarter-on-quarter and 92.5% year-on-year, supported by strong customer demand.

items.statement: Added 3.15 lakh new gold loan customers; total customers at 27.2 lakh, up 2.9% QoQ and 11.7% YoY
items.quote: Strong momentum in customer acquisition continued, and we were able to add 3.15 lakh new customers. Our outstanding number of customers was 27.2 lakh, an increase of 2.9% quarter-on-quarter and 11.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross yield on EMI and bullet loans combined expected at 17.5%-18.5%
items.quote: The gross yield on the EMI and the bullet payment combined will remain somewhere around 17.5%-18.5%. That is the expectation. Yield will remain somewhere within that range.

items.statement: Expects gold loan yields to settle around 17%-18% in three years
items.quote: I expect that to be somewhere in the range of in three years, maybe around 17% in three years. But all depends on the borrowing cost, how it is going to be, the borrowing cost, the policy. Accordingly, then that can be changed also. It can be even 18%, even more also.

items.statement: Standalone GNPA at 1.79%, NNPA at 1.24%, PCR at 31.3% as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: As on September 30, 2026, standalone gross non-performing assets stood at 1.79%, net non-performing assets at 1.24%, and the provision coverage ratio at 31.3%.

items.statement: Stage 2 spike attributed to new EMI/short-tenor products; early reads show customers regularizing; expects normalization in couple of quarters
items.quote: It is largely behavioral, right? in April, you had this change to regulations that came into effect, and you had a set of new products that were launched, which were the shorter tenor and the EMI-based products. These products are something that the customers have never experienced before. They are used to the traditional one-year consumption kind of loan, which is traditionally a bullet payment,

items.statement: Vehicle Finance GNPA at 16.9% vs 13.4% QoQ; AUM down 15.3% QoQ and 46.5% YoY; business paused, reassessment in April 2028
items.quote: In vehicle finance, we have reported an AUM of INR2,169 crores, which is down sequentially 15.3% and about 46.5% year-on-year. Focus is on collections with GNPA standing at 16.9% versus 13.4% the prior quarter.

items.statement: MSME GNPA at 6.4% vs 5.9% QoQ; AUM at INR3,361 crores
items.quote: Loans to MSME and allied business, the AUM was at INR3,361 crores with a disbursement of INR238 crores versus INR191 crores disbursed in the prior quarter. GNPA in quarter two was at 6.4% versus 5.9% in the prior quarter.

items.statement: Home Finance AUM at INR1,814 crores, down 1.7% QoQ and 4.5% YoY
items.quote: The home loan business had a total book of INR1,814 crores, marginally declined quarter-on-quarter by about 1.7% and down 4.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gold price per gram at INR13,526 in Q2
items.quote: Gold price is on this quarter two is INR13,526.

items.statement: Auction amount INR100 crores in Q2; INR115 crores in H1
items.quote: Auction amount is nearly INR100 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Online gold loan (OGL) constitutes 91% of total gold loan book
items.quote: Online gold loan book constitutes about 91% of the total gold loan book.

items.statement: CEO resigned on personal grounds; new CEO to join Jan 1, 2027; CTO resigned due to travel; new CTO candidates being finalized; no other attrition from new recruits
items.quote: Regarding the operational aspect of CEO, the earlier CEO has resigned on personal ground, etcetera,. New CEO is expected to take charge. The recruitment is already over, and he is expected to take charge from 1st of January. The CTO also resigned due to frequent travel between Mumbai and Other than that, from the new recruitment, there is no attrition. There is great stability with regard to new r

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 22.36% vs regulatory 15%; liquidity adequate with diversified funding
items.quote: Our capital adequacy stood at 22.3% as of September 30th, 2026, compared with the applicable regulatory requirements of 15%. Our liquidity position remains adequate, supported by available cash and liquid assets, committed and unutilized fund lines, and access to diversified funding channels.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR1 per share for Q2
items.quote: Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT before OCI and minority interest at INR701 crores, up 20% QoQ and 223% YoY
items.quote: For Q2, consolidated PAT before OCI and minority interest was INR701 crores, which is up 20% sequentially and 223% year-on-year.

items.statement: Standalone PAT before OCI at INR665 crores, up 20% QoQ and 77% YoY
items.quote: For the quarter, our standalone PAT before OCI and minority interest was INR665 crores, which is up 20% sequentially and up 77% year-on-year.

items.statement: Asirvad CRAR at 29.2% as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Asirvad CRAR as at September 30th stood at 29.2%.

items.statement: Consolidated net worth at INR17,289 crores; book value per share INR184.2
items.quote: Consolidated net worth stood at INR17,289 crores as at September 30th, 2026, with book value per share at INR184.2.

items.statement: Outlook shaped by inflation, interest rates, funding costs, monsoon, rural demand, commodity prices, borrower repayment capacity
items.quote: At the same time, the outlook will be shaped by inflation, interest rates, and funding costs, monsoon conditions and rural demand, oil and other global commodity prices, and the ability of the borrowers to sustain repayment capacity.

items.statement: Reclassified ARC loss of INR14 crores to provisions in Q2
items.quote: That is about INR14 crores. It is a very small amount.

items.statement: Commission business revenue expected around INR115 crores for FY27 with EBITDA around INR18.5 crores
items.quote: Our commission business is around INR115 crores for this financial year with an EBITDA of around INR18.5 crores.

items.statement: Television business expected to contribute INR125-175 crores annually
items.quote: We expect television business to contribute around INR125 crores to INR175 crores each year because that's where the television content is moving along.

items.statement: Conservative estimate of INR150-175 crores per year from OTT commission order book of INR350 crores
items.quote: Safe bet is, I think INR150-odd crores should -- on a conservative basis, I believe out of this INR350 crores, each year, we should be able to get INR150 crores to INR175 crores from commission segment of the OTT.

items.statement: Digital B2C segment expected to turn cash positive by year-end FY27
items.quote: At the same time, we should be conscious of how much cash we are burning. And it's a growing segment. We believe it will take 1.5 years to -- but this year-end, we will be positive in terms of cash because there is a lag in cost and the revenue which comes in.

items.statement: Order book for OTT commission shows could grow to INR500 crores in 6-8 months
items.quote: I strongly feel that this can be a INR500 crores business in a 6 to 8 months' time. This is not the revenue, this is an order book, yes.

items.statement: Digital B2B order book currently exceeds INR350 crores with leading OTT platforms
items.quote: Our order book with leading platforms provides good revenue visibility for the content business with the digital B2B order book currently exceeding INR350 crores.

items.statement: 5-year pipeline (FY27-31) includes 30+ movies, 15+ TV shows, 25+ OTT series, 500+ micro dramas, 10+ YouTube shows
items.quote: Our 5-year pipeline for 27 to 31 covers over 30-plus movies, more than 15-plus television shows and over 25 OTT series with more than 500 micro dramas and over 10 YouTube shows.

items.statement: H1 FY27 PBT margin of 17-18% considered sustainable going forward
items.quote: But on an half yearly basis, 17% to 18% PBT is a number which I think is a good number, and we believe we can manage and hold on to this as we go forward.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 PBT margin around 24-25% driven by Bhooth Bangla spillover
items.quote: So as we spoke last quarter number when we released, we have clearly mentioned that there is a spillover of Bhooth Bangla coming in this quarter. And Bhooth Bangla had a very successful run at the box office.

items.statement: Micro drama market in India estimated at USD300 million in 2025, could reach USD4.5 billion by 2030 per Lumikai
items.quote: India is at the start of the same curve. Our micro drama market has about USD300 million in 2025 and Lumikai estimates that it could reach USD4.5 billion by 2030.

items.statement: China micro drama market crossed CNY100 billion in 2025 with 800+ million viewers
items.quote: In 2025, according to China's broadcasting regulator, the market crossed CNY100 billion, nearly double the year before with more than 800 million viewers.

items.statement: Three monetization models for micro dramas: own platform (Kutingg), co-ownership with platforms, and commissioned production
items.quote: So micro drama, we have 2 form of models. Basically, either you own fully and use it on your platform or you co-own and co-share with the other platform. And third is you just do a commissioned shows produce for them and then they take the risk and reward.

items.statement: YouTube partnership: 5 premium original shows, 200 episodes, INR200 crores MG deal, IP retained by Balaji
items.quote: We have got INR200 crores commissioned from YouTube. The IP remains with us. They help us in tech. They help us in performance marketing. They help us in so many ways.

items.statement: Film presales model delivers 80-90% production cost recovery before release across last 6 movies
items.quote: Our calibrated presales model has delivered average recovery of approximately 80% to 90% of production costs before release across the previous 6 movies.

items.statement: Film slate: 4-6 films per year, average production budget INR60-75 crores
items.quote: This gives us confidence to build a steady slate of 4 to 6 films a year with an average production in the range of INR60 crores to INR75 crores and to invest in franchises and IP that supports sequels.

items.statement: Long-term creative partnership with Netflix; Lock Upp Season 1 was #1 non-English unscripted show globally, renewed for Season 2 within 6 months
items.quote: Our first release under this partnership, Lock Upp became a global breakout. It was the number 1 non-English unscripted show in the world on Netflix, ranked in the top 10 in 12 countries and drove the highest new sign-ups for Netflix India. It has renewed for a second season within 6 months.

items.statement: Shows in development with Amazon and Hotstar; new deals signed with Netflix, YouTube, Amazon and Hotstar
items.quote: We have inked and signed new deals with Netflix and YouTube and Amazon and Hotstar. So there are many things which is in the pipeline.

items.statement: In-house AI team set up for content development, production efficiency, multi-language adaptation
items.quote: We have set up our own in-house AI team, and we will keep strengthening it and investing into it.

items.statement: Cash reserves of approximately INR200 crores provide flexibility for content pipeline and production
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we continue to maintain healthy liquidity position with cash reserves of approximately INR200 crores.

items.statement: Company maintains debt-free balance sheet
items.quote: In short, this has been a quarter of strong profitability on a debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: YouTube and Meta combined subscriber base exceeds 21 million; added 6.5 lakh YouTube subscribers in few months
items.quote: Our combined YouTube and Meta subscriber base was also reported at more than 21 million.

items.statement: Library of 53 films and 200+ web series plus 3 decades of TV content; library monetization is EBITDA-accretive with zero P&L cost
items.quote: Balaji owns the IP of around 53 films and approximately 200-plus web series on top of 3 decades of television when every platform wants more content, a library you own is not an archive, it's an inventory.

items.statement: Film Bhooth Bangla crossed INR240 crores worldwide box office; Vvan recorded over INR90 crores worldwide gross
items.quote: Bhooth Bangla crossed INR240 crores in worldwide box office collection and become our highest grossing film revenue. Vvan followed with its theatrical release in September and recorded worldwide gross collection of over INR90 crores.

items.statement: 4 films under production: Ragini 3, Hero Ki Horroin, Heer Ranjha, Obsessive Lover; Heer Ranjha has Imtiaz Ali as creative director
items.quote: We currently have 4 movies under production, including Ragini 3, Hero Ki Horroin, Heer Ranjha and Obsessive Lover. Heer Ranjha has Imtiaz Ali as a creative director.

items.statement: Lock Upp Season 2 production accelerated for February release due to Season 1 success
items.quote: But going by the success of first Lock Upp, Netflix has proposed that we bring the second season faster. So we are going ahead with Lock Upp 2 in February itself.

items.statement: OTT commissioned shows have slightly lower yield percentage than TV shows due to TV's long-running format and marginal costing benefits
items.quote: See, when you look at OTT-led platforms, it will have a slightly lower yield in terms of percentage as compared to TV shows because TV shows also has a long-running format and marginal costing comes into picture, and we continue to get a better yield.

items.statement: Micro drama investment trajectory not yet taken off; industry cautious on investment levels
items.quote: We believe the investment into the content of micro drama has not taken off, but we are well positioned. The moment we see this trajectory going up, we will be the best person to take this business.

items.statement: Theatrical release windows limited to 52 Fridays per year with premium slots taken by A-listers, IPL, vacations, exams
items.quote: So there are only 52 weeks in a calendar for theatrical release, correct? 52 Fridays, if I say so. Out of which the premium ones or the most lucrative ones are taken away by the A-listers.

items.statement: Balaji 3.0 strategy: integrated content studio across films, TV, digital, YouTube, micro dramas with IP creation and ownership at center
items.quote: At its core, Balaji 3.0 brings together our capabilities across films, television and digital under an integrated content studio model with IP creation, ownership and monetization at the center of our strategy.

items.statement: Merged all digital and Marinating Films into Balaji Telefilms creating one integrated production engine, team, pipeline and cost structure
items.quote: By merging all digital and Marinating Films into Balaji Telefilms, we created one integrated production engine, one team, one pipeline and one cost structure serving every screen.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,300-1,350 crores and EBITDA margin 26-28%
items.quote: We have guided for FY27, we are guiding a top-line growth of 15% approximately. Somewhere between INR1,300 to INR1,350 is our targeted number. We are guiding for an EBITDA margin, a steady state EBITDA margin, somewhere between 26%-28%, where we hope to stabilize.

items.statement: Target to be near debt-free in next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: Our target is to be near debt-free in the next one year, one and a half years.

items.statement: Consolidated order book target of INR5,500-5,600 crores in FY28
items.quote: With this order book, we are hopeful to reach consolidated order book of approximately INR5,500 crore-INR5,600 crores in FY28.

items.statement: JV ARC revenue guidance of INR3,600 crores plus for FY27
items.quote: we are confident of meeting the revenue guidance given in the beginning of the year, INR3,600 crores plus for the joint venture company.

items.statement: Long-term turnover target of INR2,000 crores in FY29 ±100 and INR2,000-3,000 crores thereafter
items.quote: We are guiding to a path towards INR2,000 crores in turnover in FY29, ±100, and INR2,000 to INR3,000 crores in a few years thereafter.

items.statement: ASTL cumulative revenue target INR2,250-2,500 crores over next four years, annual revenue INR800-900 crores by FY31
items.quote: Our plan, in likely case, touch wood, is about INR2,250 crore-INR2,500 crores of cumulative revenue over the next four years. With annual revenue, I would expect it to reach around INR800 crore-INR900 crores by FY31, based on our current visibility.

items.statement: Standalone order book INR3,937 crores, consolidated INR4,708 crores as of 30 Sep 2026
items.quote: As of 30th September 2026, our standalone order book stood at INR3,937 crores, while our consolidated order book stood at INR4,708 crores, including service orders of INR251 crores, which are typically more accretive to margins.

items.statement: Incremental order inflows in Q2 FY27 of INR2,036 crores, largely defense orders
items.quote: The incremental order inflows during Q2 FY27 stood at INR2,036 crores, largely driven by defense orders.

items.statement: Landmark Uttam AAAU order from HAL valued at INR1,844 crores
items.quote: a key highlight during this period was securing a landmark order for the Uttam AAAU, valued at INR1,844 crores order from HAL.

items.statement: Visibility to book INR200 crores more orders in FY27, with INR600 crores concluded and expected by next month
items.quote: We have a clear visibility to book INR200 crores more worth of orders in FY27, in which we have concluded INR600 crores orders and expecting those orders by next month.

items.statement: JV ARC order book INR913 crores with INR500+ crores pipeline expected in next two quarters
items.quote: Our JV company, ARC Limited, has a bright prospect to grow in strategic and tactical communication segment, and bagged worth of INR413 orders and booked the sales of INR334 crores in the first half of the year. With the order book of INR913 crores and the more than INR500 crores orders in pipeline expected in next two quarters, we are confident of meeting the revenue guidance given in the beginnin

items.statement: ASTL order book around INR900 crores with weather inquiry pipeline of INR2,000 crores
items.quote: We hold an order book of around INR900 crores in this business and a weather inquiry pipeline of around INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 27.4%, PAT margin 13%, highest ever in absolute and margin terms
items.quote: H1 2027 has been a strong first half of the year for Astra, with revenue of INR437 crores, EBITDA of INR120 crores at a margin of 27.4%, and PAT of INR57 crores at a margin of 13%. Our EBITDA and PAT are the highest of yearly numbers we have ever reported, both in absolute terms as well as margins.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by favorable product mix from domestic defense production orders
items.quote: This performance was driven by a favorable product mix led by execution of domestic defense production orders, along with better control of operating expenses.

items.statement: Comfortable guiding steady-state EBITDA margin 26-28% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: I think over the next two to three years, it's a comfortable assumption to make, right? But as you very rightly said, this time there were a lot of production orders, so we were able to capture a higher EBITDA margin. But we are comfortable guiding in a state of 26%-28%, where we believe that we will be able to deliver without upsetting the apple cart.

items.statement: Inventory buildup for Q1 FY28 deliveries and component stockpiling due to geopolitical lead time increases
items.quote: We have already specified, right, that we are going to be INR1,300-INR1,350 the year end, which implies that our next two quarters will actually have a lot of deliveries to be made, which is the reason why inventory buildup is what you are seeing.

items.statement: Target cash conversion cycle of 350 days by year end, currently 360-370 days
items.quote: We are working towards to maintain around 360 to 370. This is what our target is to make it. Maybe in future, as we go into the systems more, I think probably it may go further down. So right now, our target is to bring it down to around 350 by the end of the year.

items.statement: Free cash flow target INR250-350 crores for FY27, similar to INR300+ crores last year
items.quote: I think last year we did in excess of INR300 crores. Manish Maheshwari: Correct. Management: Somewhere between INR250 to INR350 should be the target, I guess

items.statement: Target zero working capital limits (CC limits) by year end, working towards debt-free on working capital
items.quote: More or less, by year end, we are expecting CC limits, working capital limits going to be zero. That is our target area. We are working towards a debt-free on the working capital.

items.statement: Three own IP-owned products launched by Diwali: counter-drone system with D4 radar, bird detection radar, low-level lightweight radar (40-50 km range)
items.quote: Just as important is what we are now selling. I promised you that by Diwali, Astra will have three products of our own. We have kept the promise. We have a complete counter-drone system. The backbone for that is our D4 radar. We have an Astra-designed, Astra-branded bird detection radar, and we have a low-level lightweight radar with a range of about 40-50 km.

items.statement: Developing electronic mines with potential >$750M annual demand
items.quote: When we feed in the features of our electronic mines, it's amongst the best in these electronic mines, which we are developing, India is developing, by the way. I think that number itself comes in excess of $750 million annually.

items.statement: Counter-drone TOT from DRDO given to 7 companies; Astra and BEL only ones making product
items.quote: Yes, actually, in fact, the earlier TOT was given to seven companies apart from BEL, but only as of today, apart from BEL, we are the only company who's been making the product with the TOT from DRDO.

items.statement: Uttam AAAU radar delivery schedule: 2 units by March 2027, 12 units by March 2028, then 25 units annually in FY29, scaling to 33-34
items.quote: HAL wanted us to deliver about four numbers by March 2027, which in fact we mentioned even in the beginning, in fact, while signing the contract, since that we will try to make it. items.statement: Sukhoi-30 program orders expected around calendar year 2029
items.quote: Let's say, to answer his question, I think calendar year 2029 is when you should be looking at these orders.

items.statement: Export leads from US and Europe for MMIC portfolio, potential business in next couple of years

items.statement: ASTL targeting global space supply chains, conversations with global players underway
items.quote: Few conversations with global players are already underway, and we will talk about that as something tangible materializes.

items.statement: Defense production target INR3 lakh crores annually and exports INR50,000 crores by 2029 per government policy
items.quote: Coupled with national targets aiming at INR3 lakh crores in annual defense production and INR50,000 crores in defense exports by 2029, this industry is positioned for sustained structural expansion.

items.statement: Indian space economy target $44 billion by 2033 from $8 billion currently

items.statement: Astra supplies 30-40% of ISRO remote sensing payload hardware and 25-35% of communication payload hardware

items.statement: Defence Procurement Manual and draft Defence Acquisition Procedure introduce up to 60% local content mandates and 75% capital acquisition budget for domestic industry
items.quote: Furthermore, government reforms such as updated Defence Procurement Manual, DPM, the draft Defence Acquisition Procedure, introducing up to 60% local content mandates, and the earmarking of 75% of capital acquisition budgets for domestic industry provide long-term structural clarity.

items.statement: Demerger of space/meteorology business into Astra Space Technologies Limited (ASTL); shareholders get 1 ASTL share per Astra share at no cost

items.statement: Ground-based SDR manpack missed first Army procurement phase due to software bug in final trial; ready for next phase

That is how actually we missed that initial first phase of that particular procurement.

items.statement: Dr. M.V. Reddy took charge as Managing Director on 1 Oct 2026; S.G. Reddy moved to lead ASTL
items.quote: This is my first earning call as the managing director, having taken charge on 1st October 2026. Before I begin, I would like to thank Mr. S.G. Reddy, who had led this company for years and is now taking forward our space business through Astra Space Technologies Limited, the demerging entity.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin of 5-8% under normalized non-inflationary conditions
items.quote: We expect EBITDA of 5 to 8 percentage.

items.statement: Solar adoption is very good across India with installations picking up after grid-related slowdown in first two quarters
items.quote: No, solar adoption is very good all across India. It is only there was a slowdown during the first two quarters because some grid issue and all, but afterwards I think it is again picking up.

items.statement: EBITDA improved to INR 3 crore in Q2 FY27 from a loss of INR 2 crore in Q1, margins expanded 519 bps sequentially to 2.93%

items.statement: CSS turnaround driven by volume growth across all customers, discontinuation of non-performing customers, and TCM initiatives
items.quote: The CSS business showed a good improvement in revenue across all the verticals and all the customers. In addition to that, we had discontinued a few non-performing customers, which helped to improve the margin in this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Material costs expected to stabilize with improved procurement and rupee stabilization, though subject to market volatility
items.quote: Material price and cost, we expect this to stabilize, but still there is a volatility. There may be volatility if there is any more chance of disturbance due to the war or whatever. So otherwise, we are well prepared and we have negotiated and improved our procurement costs and everything.

items.statement: EMS order book confidential; two new customers added with prototypes completed and firm orders received for execution in coming quarters
items.quote: So, as I mentioned, we have added two customers where we have done the proto and everything is done. So, the final orders have come. So, we are going to execute it in the coming months and the coming quarters.

items.statement: EMS new customers from industrial engineering, power electronics, and consumer electronics sectors

items.statement: Cost optimization via digitization, AI adoption, discretionary spend control, and field support efficiency under TCM project
items.quote: We are taking multiple actions or initiatives. Like, one is digitization, AI adoption, then controlling the discretionary spends and improving the efficiency of field support services where fixed cost is involved.

items.statement: New strategic director appointed to provide strategic guidance for company growth

items.quote: As I mentioned, we don't make forward-looking statement. And Q3 and Q4 being immediate quarters, we don't want to give any specific guidance on that. items.statement: Revised FY27 production guidance: iron ore mining 2.5 mt (from 3.4 mt), iron ore pellet 3.5 mt (from 4.4 mt); other segments on track
items.value: iron ore mining 2.5 mt, pellet 3.5 mt

items.statement: Margins expected to recover from Q4 FY27 with regulatory permission for overburden dumping and beneficiation plant commissioning
items.quote: Margins are expected to recover from Q4 '27, with expected receipt of regulatory permission for use of additional land for dumping of overburden and commissioning of beneficiation plant, enabling the higher iron ore production from captive mines and use of captive iron ore for pellet production.

items.statement: INR100 cr capex approved for 50 EV dumpers across iron ore mines and plant operations to improve cost efficiency and reduce fuel dependence
items.quote: Taking forward our sustainability agenda, the company has approved a capex of INR100 crores for deployment of 50 numbers of EV dumper across our iron ore mines and plant operations, aimed at improving cost efficiency, reducing dependence on conventional fuel and rising fuel cost.

items.quote: The way I look at it, Sanjesh, is that over the next few quarters, you will likely see a 10% ARPU increase. Our sense is that we will be able to maintain this momentum organically over the next few quarters as well.

items.statement: Marketing costs to remain at current elevated levels for remainder of FY27
items.quote: Such campaigns are a sustained effort and thus we expect the marketing cost to remain at these levels for the remainder of FY27.

items.statement: Network rollout pace guided at 3,000-3,500 unique 4G towers per month
items.quote: As stated earlier, our capex trajectory and network rollout continues to progress in line with our guided roll-out pace of 3,000 to 3,500 unique 4G towers per month.

items.statement: Q2FY27 capex Rs 3,946 Cr, more than double Q1 run-rate; H1FY27 capex nearly Rs 6,000 Cr
items.quote: During the second quarter, our capex increased to Rs. 3,946 Crore, more than twice the run-rate of Q1FY27, taking our H1FY27 capex to nearly Rs. 6,000 Crore.

items.statement: Placed capex orders worth over Rs 13,200 Cr against three-year guidance of Rs 45,000 Cr
items.quote: We have also placed capex orders worth over Rs. 13,200 Crore against our three-year capex guidance of Rs. 45,000 Crore.

items.statement: Added nearly 9,000 new broadband towers in Q2FY27; total unique broadband tower count close to 214,000
items.quote: I am delighted to share that we have added nearly 9,000 new broadband towers bringing the total unique broadband tower count close to 214,000.

items.statement: 5G services now available in 400 Indian cities and towns; 4G population coverage increased to 88%
items.quote: Our 5G services are now available in 400 Indian cities and towns, and our 4G population coverage has increased to 88%.

items.statement: On track to conclude 4G network rollout by FY28 to gain coverage parity with peers in 17 key circles
items.quote: We remain on track to conclude our 4G network rollout by FY28 to gain coverage parity with our peers in 17 key circles.

items.statement: Added 1.3 million subscribers in Q2FY27; customer base increased to 194.4 million
items.quote: We also continued to build subscriber momentum, with our customer base increasing to 194.4 million from 193.1 million in the previous quarter.

items.statement: 4G and 5G subscriber base increased to 131.0 million from 127.8 million in Q2FY26
items.quote: Our 4G and 5G subscriber base increased to 131.0 million from 127.8 million in Q2FY26.

items.statement: Prepaid net subscriber churn reduced significantly from 1.5 million in Q1FY27 to 0.6 million in Q2FY27
items.quote: I am pleased to report that our sequential net subscriber churn for prepaid has reduced significantly from 1.5 million in Q1FY27 to 0.6 million this quarter.

items.statement: Postpaid subscriber base including M2M now stands at 33.9 million; highest sequential growth since FY24
items.quote: We also recorded the highest sequential postpaid subscriber growth since FY24 with subscriber base including M2M now standing at 33.9 million.

items.statement: Revenue grew 6.2% YoY to Rs 11,884 Cr; Cash EBITDA grew 11.2% YoY to Rs 2,498 Cr with margin 21.0%
items.quote: Our revenue for Q2FY27 improved by 6.2% year-on-year to Rs. 11,884 Crore and grew by 1.7% sequentially. Cash EBITDA increased by 11.2% year-on-year to Rs. 2,498 Crore, while our Cash EBITDA margin was 21.0%

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable YoY at 41.9%; sequentially subdued due to personnel costs and higher marketing expenses
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was stable on a YoY basis at 41.9%. On a sequential basis, the margin was slightly subdued due to phasing of personnel costs and higher marketing expenses associated with brand refresh initiatives in Q2FY27.

items.statement: Customer ARPU grew 9.7% YoY to Rs 198; sequential growth moderated due to seasonality and segmental interventions
items.quote: Our Customer ARPU stood at Rs. 198, representing a healthy growth of 9.7% YoY. Customer ARPU continues to improve sequentially, though the organic growth was moderated compared to prior quarters, primarily due to seasonality characteristics of the second quarter and segmental interventions deployed to support them.

items.statement: Expect ARPU growth trend of previous quarters to resume from next quarter as premiumisation trajectory remains intact
items.quote: We expect the ARPU growth trend of previous quarters to resume from next quarter as the underlying customer engagement and premiumisation trajectory remains intact.

items.statement: Launched industry-first free international roaming on key plans across postpaid and prepaid
items.quote: In end of September this year, we launched an industry-first initiative by making international roaming free on our key plans across both postpaid and prepaid.

items.statement: Launched India's first prepaid family plan enabling data sharing among family members across country
items.quote: In another industry-first initiative, we also launched India's first prepaid family plan, enabling customers to share data among family members across country.

items.statement: Introduced Rs 200 Vi Movies & TV prepaid pack with 20 OTT platforms and extended Spotify Premium to select prepaid plans
items.quote: During the quarter, we introduced the Rs. 200 Vi Movies & TV prepaid pack, offering content across 20 OTT platforms along with data benefits. We also extended Spotify Premium to select prepaid plans.

items.statement: Unveiled refreshed brand identity with Shah Rukh Khan as brand ambassador; Vi's distinctive dot moved to top
items.quote: Alongside these propositions, we unveiled our refreshed brand identity and welcomed Shah Rukh Khan as our brand ambassador. Vi's distinctive dot has moved to the top, reflecting the brand's upward momentum and its ambition to deliver a stronger network and a more rewarding customer experience.

items.statement: Enterprise segment Vi Business positioned as key growth engine; strategy to move beyond connectivity to IoT, cloud, digital infrastructure
items.quote: We see our enterprise segment, Vi Business, as a key growth engine. Our enterprise strategy is to move beyond traditional connectivity towards a broader portfolio of IoT, connectivity, cloud and intelligent digital infrastructure.

items.statement: Partnership with AWS to evolve from connectivity provider to digital transformation partner for enterprises
items.quote: Our partnership with AWS is an important step in our evolution from a connectivity provider to a broader digital transformation partner for enterprises.

items.statement: Launched iD+ for verified business calling and Vi Business WhatsApp with AI-powered chatbots and Meta support
items.quote: During the quarter, we also launched many innovative propositions for our enterprise customers including iD+ for verified business calling to let subscribers see a verified brand name and the reason for the call before answering. Next, we launched Vi Business WhatsApp, an enterprise-grade WhatsApp solution, with AI-powered chatbots, voice calling and premier Meta support.

items.statement: Deployed dedicated full-stack private network at Hindalco's Baphlimali Bauxite Mine in Odisha; multi-year managed services engagement
items.quote: Another important development during the quarter was our collaboration with Hindalco Industries. Vi Business deployed a dedicated, full-stack private network at Baphlimali Bauxite Mine in Odisha. This multi-year managed-services engagement covers spectrum, core, RAN and managed services and demonstrates the potential for private networks to enable digital transformation in industrial environments.

items.statement: Secured total funding over Rs 10,500 Cr till H1FY27 including warrants, fund & non-fund based facilities; over Rs 4,000 Cr incremental bank funding arranged in Q2FY27
items.quote: We have secured a total funding of over Rs. 10,500 Crore till H1FY27 including warrants, fund & non-fund based facilities of which over Rs. 4,000 Crore of incremental bank funding was arranged in Q2FY27.

items.statement: Engaged with three bank cohorts: public sector consortium led by SBI, Indian private banks, and ECB through foreign banks
items.quote: As guided earlier, we are engaged with banks for funding across the three cohorts: a public sector bank consortium led by SBI, Indian private banks, and ECB funding through foreign banks.

items.statement: Public sector bank consortium process progressing well but taking longer than anticipated; confident of closure
items.quote: On the public sector bank consortium front, the process continues to progress well. While the involvement of multiple lenders has resulted in the overall process taking longer than we had earlier anticipated, we remain confident in our engagement with the consortium.

items.statement: Bank debt stood at Rs 943 Cr as of Sep 30, 2026; free cash and bank balance at Rs 5,470 Cr; legacy bank debt fully repaid as of today
items.quote: Our bank debt stood at Rs. 943 Crore as of September 30, 2026. The free cash and bank balance stood at Rs. 5,470 Crore as of September 30, 2026. As of today, our legacy bank debt has been fully repaid.

items.statement: Paid spectrum dues of over Rs 4,300 Cr due in Oct 2026; paid over Rs 6,000 Cr against ~Rs 7,000 Cr FY27 spectrum obligations
items.quote: I would like to highlight that, alongside more than doubling our quarterly capex, we have also paid spectrum dues of over Rs. 4,300 Crore which were due in October 2026. With this, we have paid over Rs. 6,000 Crore against approximately Rs. 7,000 Crore spectrum obligations due in FY27.

items.statement: Welcomed Manoj Murali as new Chief Operating Officer to leadership team
items.quote: Before I move to the developments in this quarter, I would like to welcome Manoj Murali to the leadership team as the new Chief Operating Officer.

items.statement: Overall data usage increased 27.1% YoY to 93.6 petabyte per day from 73.6 petabyte per day in Q2FY26
items.quote: Our customers continue to engage with us deeply with overall data usage increasing by 27.1% year-on-year to 93.6 petabyte per day, compared with 73.6 petabyte per day in Q2FY26.

items.statement: Churn increased 0.2% QoQ in Q2FY27 but improved 0.5% YoY over Q2FY26; churn substantially lower in circles with network rollout
items.quote: Yes inQ2FY27, we've got a churn which has increased by 0.2%. But if you really look at a churn year on year over the Q2FY26, we've made an improvement of 0.5% as far as the base churn is concerned.

items.statement: Spectrum due for renewal in eight circles in Dec 2026; represented to DoT for continuation; services will not be disrupted
items.quote: On the second one, on the spectrum, which is due in the month of December, there are eight circles where the spectrum is due. As you rightly pointed out, the auction dates are not there, but as the normal norm is that till the time the auctions are not there, we continue. We have already represented ourselves to the Department of Telecommunications of our interest in continuing with that. So, we'l

items.statement: Implemented TRAI-mandated voice-only plan at Rs 185; initial days show minimal disruption and some upside migration to Rs 199 plan
items.quote: On the first question, yes, we have as per the TRAI mandate, we've made the changes of INR 185. At this stage, it's too early to make any assumptions, but our sense in the initial days is minimal disruption. We will continue to watch this space to observe how the consumer behaviour changes, and then we'll look at this.

items.statement: Adverse impact of Rs 462 Cr in exceptional items due to mark-to-market treasury assets; remeasurement each quarter until shares liquidated
items.quote: Additionally, an adverse impact of Rs. 462 Crore was recorded in exceptional items on account of due to adverse impact of mark-to-market treasury assets. which translated into a higher reported loss for the quarter. As explained previously, this remeasurement of fair value will be undertaken each quarter with the resulting impact recognised under exceptional items until the shares are liquidated.

items.statement: Network cost increased Rs 99 Cr QoQ; will continue to increase with rollout but managed through cost-saving measures
items.quote: Just check the numbers, but we have seen an INR 99 Crores increase quarter-on-quarter in the network cost line.

items.statement: Full-year double-digit volume growth guidance maintained despite H1 at 5.5%
items.quote: Given that, our guidance for the full financial year remains intact, and the targets that we are gunning for internally remains intact as well. There is no change in the outlook as far as the volume growth targets are concerned.

items.statement: Festive season shift from Q2 to Q3 deferred primary billing; July-August primary growth ~2x quarter average
items.quote: It is almost 2x what we have achieved for the quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 20.8% in Q2, within planned 19%-21% range; expected to stay in range for H2
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 20.8% as against 21.7% last year. Cotton and crude-led raw materials remained elevated, and the price increase only partially cushioned this pressure. The margin stayed healthy and within our planned range of 19%-21%.

items.statement: 2.5% price hike in May 2026 fully effective in Q2; further hikes possible if input inflation persists
items.quote: We'll have to wait an d watch. I think in the commentary that V.S. Ganesh made, what we will try and balance out is our targeted EBITDA range versus being affordable and accessible to consumers. It's almost a wait and watch to see when we need to effect the price increase

items.statement: Raw material inflation ~6.5-7% YoY in Q2, driven by cotton and crude-based materials; persists at similar levels
items.quote: The input cost purely from a raw material point of view seems to be inflated to the tune of 6.5%-7%, which of course has been offset by price increase to the tune of 2.5%, which was effected in Q2.

items.statement: Athleisure/outerwear and women's innerwear growing faster than men's innerwear YTD and expected in H2
items.quote: Athleisure or outerwear as a business, as well as women's innerwear as a business, will be a notch above men's innerwear in terms of growth rates.

items.statement: Odisha and K.R. Pete Phase 2 plants at ~40% of target capacity; peak utilization expected by end of FY28
items.quote: As of now, we are operating at about 40% of where we want to be, or not where we want to be, where we can get to as far as these two plants are concerned. I would imagine by end of next financial year is where we will be hitting peak capacity utilization.

items.statement: Inventory days 74.0 at end Q2 vs 74.8 at start FY27; net working capital days improved to 51.3 from 55.9
items.quote: Inventory days stood at 74.0 at the end of Q2, as against 74.8 at the beginning of current financial year. Net working capital days improved to 51.3 days from 55.9 days at the beginning of the current financial year.

items.statement: FEMA non-compliance identified FY26; compounding application filed May 2026; RBI directed post-facto approval from DPIIT; amount involved INR 48 crore cumulative over 12 years; penalty up to 0.75% (INR 4-5 mn) per precedents; no operational
items.quote: We identified it last year, and we had filed for the compounding application with RBI in May 2026. RBI had to come back with our status of our application by October, which they did, but yes, they asked us to approach the government for post-facto approval of the past non-compliance. We are now in the process of approaching DPIIT to take care of the earlier past issue.

items.statement: Order fulfillment rate dropped to 96-97% from 98-99% in men's innerwear and women's outerwear due to SKU-level demand spikes and new plant ramp-up; ~3-4% primary order loss; improving toward 97-98%
items.quote: from a supply and order fulfillment point of view, we've historically operated at a 98%-99%. That has dropped to about 96% to 97%, and that's largely in men's innerwear and women's outerwear, like you've indicated. There has been about 3%-4% order loss that we've experienced at a primary level

items.statement: Competitive intensity subdued in Q1-Q2 vs last three years; high consumer offers and discounting seen during festive season in Oct-Nov
items.quote: As far as quarter one and quarter two is concerned, I think the competitive intensity has been subdued. We've seen a high level of consumer offers and discounting during the festive season, which was largely in October and November.

items.statement: Sales volume 59.8 mn pieces in Q2 (+5.5% YoY), 121.7 mn in H1 (+5.6%); sales value INR 14,396.1 mn in Q2 (+11.5%), INR 28,600.6 mn in H1 (+9.7%)
items.quote: Sales volume was 59.8 million pieces, which is a growth of 5.5% over Q2 last year. Sales value was INR 14,396.1 million, up 11.5%.

items.statement: Headcount optimal in H1; will increase in H2 with Odisha and K.R. Pete ramp-up; Karnataka wage hike for garmenting workforce effective April, support staff hike sub judice
items.quote: Going forward, the headcount will go up as we ramp up Odisha operations as well as K.R. Pete two operations. So, what you have seen in H1 is more the ramp-up phase, which will have to accelerate a lot more in H2.

items.statement: No explicit operating or free cash flow numbers disclosed; working capital improvement noted
items.quote: Net working capital days improved to 51.3 days from 55.9 days at the beginning of the current financial year.

items.statement: Auditors commented on FEMA matter in FY26 annual report and current quarter; no qualification or resignation
items.quote: The auditors have given their comments as to this matter, both in annual report of FY 2026 as well as in this quarter.

items.statement: Speedo brand shifted to third-party franchising model for online sales to comply with FDI restrictions on imported goods
items.quote: Speedo is no more a company-to-consumer direct business. It is through a third-party franchising.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 15% YoY, implying ~INR6,500 crores top line
items.quote: We had given a guidance of having a growth of around 15% on the last year's top line. Currently also, if you see the Q2, we were able to achieve 15%. Though Q1 was not that great, we had a flattish top line. Currently, we stand at 8%. So with the H2 that we are seeing, that it should ramp up, and we are quite confident that we should be able to achieve the 15% growth that we are targeted.

items.statement: Order book at INR22,711 crores as of Sep 30, 2026 with metro 7%, elevated corridors 47%, road tunnels 19%, others 26%
items.quote: Our order book as on 30th September, '26 stands at INR22,711 crores. The order book includes metro projects contributing 7%, elevated corridors contributing 47%, road tunnels contributing to 19%, and others contributing to 26%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 order inflow of INR5,540 crores; H2 FY27 target of INR3,000-5,000 crores additional for full year INR8,000-10,000 crores
items.quote: So, as of now, the company has already bagged orders of INR5,540 crores as of H1. We are quite confident that we should be able to bag orders close to around INR8,000 crores-INR10,000 crores in the coming H2. So, totaling to INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores is what I want to say.

items.statement: Strong pipeline of INR50,000-100,000 crores projects planned in Maharashtra alone over next 10-12 months
items.quote: More than around INR50,000 crores to INR100,000 crores worth of projects are planned only in Maharashtra alone. So, it's like we are seeing a lot of traction in the order book that's going to be seen over the period of next 10 to 12 months.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR30,000 crores over next 6 months including INR10,000 crores elevated corridors/roads/flyovers, INR15,000 crores metros, INR5,000 crores building works
items.quote: Though we have already submitted bids worth around INR3,000 crores, which are being submitted. There are around INR30,000 crores worth of projects which we are expecting to bid in less than six months' time, which includes elevated corridors and elevated corridors, roads, flyovers worth around INR10,000 crores. Metros would be around INR15,000 crores, and building works around INR5,000.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR150 crores for FY27 and FY28; INR80 crores spent in H1 FY27
items.quote: The capex INR80 crores that we have done, and for full year INR150 odd crores previously we said, this year and next year, so that will remain broadly the same? Kamal Gupta: Yes, it will broadly the same. You are right, Shravan

items.statement: Mobilization advance INR627 crores, unbilled revenue INR572 crores, security deposit INR490 crores as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: The current mobilization advance balance as of today is around INR627 crores. Shravan Shah: Okay. Nilesh Sharma: Unbilled is INR572 crores. And security deposit is around INR490 crores

items.statement: GMLR project: 1 TBM >300m drilled, 2nd TBM started 8m; target completion before end 2029 (1 year ahead of delayed schedule)
items.quote: For GMLR, we are running, I mean, as if you look at the original time period, which was five years for the project, and the land for the project was handed over to us around two years later. We have ramped up the progress, and we are able to see that, you know, with instead of two years delay, we should be able to complete it in less than one year before time. So, around before end of '29, we will

items.statement: Chennai project: 70-75% foundation complete, 2,900 precast segments cast; target completion Dec 2028/Jan 2029
items.quote: For Chennai, we have almost completed 70%, 75% of the foundation work, and we have casted precast segments of around 2,900 numbers. We expect it to complete it by December '28 or January '29. The work is going smoothly.

items.statement: Vadhavan project: mobilization started, service road excavation underway; revenue expected from Dec 2026/Jan 2027
items.quote: Vadhavan project we already mobilized, started mobilizing. The work for service road has already started there, the excavation and the ground clearing. The survey has been done. The work is taking shape now there. Should not be any issue in Vadhavan. We will start seeing revenues from this Jan, December, Jan from there.

items.statement: Worli-Sewri connector and Sewri-Navi Mumbai Airport projects to complete in calendar 2027; Metro Line 2B extension to Bandra also completing FY27
items.quote: the projects which will be completed this year, will be, yes, this year means like I am talking about March, this '27, sorry, yes, '27, in the year calendar '27. One is your connectivity from Worli to new airport, so that means the Worli-Sewri connector will be done. Then from Sewri to Navi Mumbai Airport, that will be completed. These two projects will be for sure done in this calendar year FY27.

items.statement: Labor shortage exists but manageable; mitigating via mechanization, pre-casting, automation; good paymaster attracts labor
items.quote: As rightly pointed out by you, labor shortage is there. It is not that it is not there. Because there are so many works simultaneously going on, there are some labor shortages. We are like, in this quarter also what we have done, we had faced some issues, but we can manage because as J. Kumar, we focus more and more to see where the labor requirement goes down by mechanizing the work and using mor

items.statement: SFIO matter is old SEBI issue; all documents submitted; cleared by SEBI; cooperating fully with SFIO; no concern
items.quote: It is the old matter which was earlier raised by SEBI, and all the matters have been clarified. All the documents has been submitted long back. It was cleared by SEBI, and similar reply is what we are expecting from SFIO also. It is a matter of procedure, and we are cooperating fully with the department, and there is nothing that we need to be worried about.

items.statement: Delhi Metro order cancelled due to project scope change; fresh limited tender expected in 10-15 days for same bidders
items.quote: Delhi Metro, they have canceled the order. It did not get converted into order book because there is some change in the project that they are doing, and because of which the project cost is also likely to go up. In another next 10 to 15 days' time, they should come up with the fresh tender. Varun Aggarwal: Okay, understood. Nalin Gupta: It will be only restricted to the number of bidders who had b

items.statement: Vizag monetization progressing well; layout approval pending; good money received in Q2; expect to exceed targets in next 2 quarters
items.quote: Yes, Vizag the monetization is going well. We are just waiting for one approval from the local government about some layout approvals. A lot of deals are already finalized. We have received good money in this quarter, and going forward in this coming two quarters, I think, we will be much above the targeted projections.

items.statement: Revenue target for FY27 remains INR 1,000 crores plus/minus 4-5%
items.quote: INR1,000 crores revenue is always on target. Any of the commentary we have been through, plus/minus 4%, 5% is a difference. Otherwise, still, the target is still INR1,000 crores for FY27.

items.statement: SSG target for FY27 remains 4-5% despite 1% in H1
items.quote: 4% to 5% SSG has always been communicated and it is on the target.

items.statement: Internal target to double revenue to INR 2,000 crores in next 4-5 years
items.quote: So internally, we have a target to achieve INR1,000 crores by FY27 and next 4 to 5 years, trying to make it double, 5 years you can say.

items.statement: Q2 sales impacted by festive calendar shift; expect recovery in Q3 wedding season
items.quote: Our sales are down in Q2 more than in Q1 because there is shift in the festive calendar. There was additional Hindu month in July due to which weddings were not there. And Durga Puja sale also shifted from September to October.

items.statement: Festive sales show like-to-like positive growth; wedding season pending
items.quote: Yes. Festive sale is rise in growth. Yes, there is L2L positive in festive sales.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth down 2% in Q2; aim to cover in H2
items.quote: SSG is down by minus 2% in Q2, but we hope we will cover the negative SSG in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: No major consumption slowdown on ground; negative sentiment due to calendar shift
items.quote: But in real, there is not much negativity in the market.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 28% from 27.2%
items.quote: EBITDA margins for H1 FY27 improved to 28% as compared to 27.2% in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 23.2%
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27 stood at 23.2%.

items.statement: Gross margin not expected to contract despite slight cotton price increase
items.quote: No, we don't see any contraction in gross margin.

items.statement: Added 80,000 sq ft in H1; plan to add 55,000 sq ft in Q3
items.quote: We have added 80,000 square feet in Q1, Q2, but we aspire to add at least 55,000 square feet in Q3 only.

items.statement: Total 690 stores covering 9.89 lakh sq ft retail area
items.quote: On the operational front, we continue to scale efficiency with a total of 690 stores across the country, covering a total retail area nearing 1 million, that is 9.89 lakhs square feet.

items.statement: Opened 23 stores in Q2; 70% family stores, rest gender-dedicated
items.quote: So, we opened, like, 23 stores in Q2, right? So, 70% stores are the family stores and rest are only men's and ladies and kids.

items.statement: Kids wear contributes 3-4% of sales; growing but small
items.quote: A total contributing sale to kid's wear is around 3% to 4% only. But we expect it to grow.

items.statement: Online sales contribution approximately 5.5% in Q2; margins not improved
items.quote: Out of my total sales this quarter, approximately 5.5% is my online sales quarter.

items.statement: Slight cotton price increase to be absorbed in cost; gross margins protected
items.quote: There is a very slight increase in the cotton prices. So, we plan to, like, add it in the cost. So gross margins won't be impacted due to the increase in raw material prices.

items.statement: Inventory high at Sep 30 due to winter/wedding stock; to release in Q3-Q4
items.quote: Because as on 30th September, the procurement for winter season as well as wedding season and other has been secured. So that should be released in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Short-term borrowing of INR 27 crores for working capital due to winter procurement
items.quote: Working capital, sir. It's a utilization of my working capital limit due to additional procurement, you can say, for the winter.
