items.statement: No long-term or capex loans on balance sheet
items.quote: We have never had a long-term loan, any capex loan will never be in the part of balance sheet.

items.statement: Lease accounting estimate changed to 6-year norm; PAT up ~INR 3 crores
items.quote: PAT for this has been increased approximately INR3 crores by the change in accounting estimate.

items.statement: INR 15 crore loan to be cleared by February; on track
items.quote: It will be cleared off in time.

items.statement: Exports only to Nepal; no plans for Bangladesh exports
items.quote: No, we are only exporting to Nepal. We are not exporting to Bangladesh, and there are no such immediate plans to export to Bangladesh.

items.statement: Small portion of production sourced from Bangladesh; factories stable
items.quote: We have a very small portion of our production sourced through Bangladesh. And the factories we are sourcing from are stable. They are not unstable due to the situation in Bangladesh.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 11% to INR 370.5 crores; PAT grew 9% to INR 23.4 crores
items.quote: Revenue from operations for H1 FY27 grew by 11% to INR370.5 crores as compared to INR334.7 crores in H1 FY26. EBITDA for H1 FY27 grew by 14% to INR103.8 crores as compared to INR91.9 crores in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 9% to INR 191.7 crores; PAT grew 4% to INR 7 crores
items.quote: Our revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 grew by 9% to INR191.7 crores as compared to INR176 crores in Q2 FY26. EBITDA for Q2 FY27 grew by 5% to INR44.4 crores as compared to INR42.1 crores in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Festive calendar shift hurt sentiment; real demand not negative
items.quote: So many brands and many companies reported negative SSG in the Q2. And despite knowing that there is a shift in the festive calendar, sentiments are down because once sales get down, despite knowing everything, sentiments got hurt.

items.statement: Overall order book stands at approximately INR 5,850 crore after recent wins
items.quote: With these wins, our overall order book increased and now stands at approximately INR 5,850 crore.

items.statement: Wagon order book is approximately INR 3,600 crore, close to 10,000 wagons
items.quote: The wagon order book today is approximately about INR 3,600 crore.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 8,000-10,000 crore by FY30 maintained
items.quote: The guidance was for FY30, not for FY29, and we are very confident that we will definitely get there.

items.statement: Targeting BESS order book of approximately INR 1,000 crore by end of FY27
items.quote: We are targeting BESS order book of approximately INR 1,000 crore by end of FY27.

items.statement: Jupiter Electric Mobility expected to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY27 and profitable by FY28
items.quote: Jupiter Electric Mobility expected to turn EBITDA positive in Q3 FY27 and profitable by FY28.

items.statement: EBITDA margins to return to FY26 levels over next few quarters, strong margins expected in FY28
items.quote: Going forward, you will start seeing an improvements in EBITDA margins. We are quite confident that a large chunks of the order book will come in next year. The impact of this will start becoming visible in FY28.

items.statement: Wheel plant total capex INR 2,500 crore; equity infusion INR 900 crore done, debt limit INR 1,600 crore with INR 1,100 crore utilized
items.quote: So the total capex was, I think, INR 2,500 crore, where we have infused the equity which was needed to be infused. Total equity infusion was about INR 900 crore, which has been infused. And now, INR 1,600 is the total limit, which we have taken from the bank and INR 1,100 has been utilized.

items.statement: Axle line commissioning by middle of next year, wheel line operational by end of next financial year
items.quote: Axle line is going to get commissioned in the middle of next year.

items.statement: Wagon production to reach peak levels of 600-800 wagons per month
items.quote: In terms of number guidance, what I can tell you is that we will be touching our peak productions, which we were doing earlier. So, it will be anything in the range of 600-800 wagons per month.

items.statement: Secured INR 1,140 crore order from Ministry of Railways for 2,583 BOXNHL and BOXNS wagons
items.quote: This includes an order for INR 1,140 crore from Ministry of Railways, which is an order for 2,583 BOXNHL and BOXNS wagons.

items.statement: Private sector orders worth INR 450 crore from GATX India, Chetak International, and Balmer Lawrie for ACT2 and BFNS wagons
items.quote: On the private side, we have secured orders worth INR 450 crore from GATX India, Chetak International, and Balmer Lawrie and Company, for supply of ACT2 automotive carrier wagons and BFNS 22.9-tonne payload wagons.

items.statement: Signed MOU with PESA Poland for passenger rail vehicle development, manufacturing, and deployment
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we have signed an MOU in October with PESA, Poland's largest train and metro manufacturer, to explore cooperation in passenger rail vehicle development, manufacturing, and deployment across regional intercity and urban transport markets.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Lucchini RS for integrated railwheel manufacturing platform with 25% stake allotted for INR 290 crore investment
items.quote: As part of the engagement and arrangement, Lucchini RS, along with SIMEST, an Italian government financial institute, has been allotted a combined 25% stake in JTRWF against the investment of approximately INR 290 crore.

items.statement: JEM Energy BESS order book exceeds 500 MW valued at INR 500 crore plus; secured 100 MW standalone BESS project in West Bengal worth INR 400 crore
items.quote: Together with earlier wins, JEM Energy order book now exceeds 500 megawatts, valued at INR 500 crore plus.

items.statement: Brake business revenue expected to double in FY28 from FY27 levels
items.quote: I think we expect in FY28, the numbers from FY27 to double.

items.statement: Stone India brake facility to produce 700-800 brake systems per month for freight market by beginning next year
items.quote: By beginning next year, we will be producing close to about 700 - 800 brake systems every month from that facility for the freight market.

items.statement: Defense manufacturing is separate JV under holding structure, no Jupiter Wagons investment, focused on export market with technology transfer for ammunition shells up to 181mm
items.quote: First of all, the defense business is not related to Jupiter Wagons. It is a standalone business under a holding structure. There is no investment of Jupiter Wagons in that business.

items.statement: JEM Energy finalized technology partner for battery cell manufacturing, targeting high-voltage high-capacity cells, announcement shortly
items.quote: We have already finalized the technology. You will see an announcement very shortly. So, by, I think, FY29, Jupiter can say that we are truly Make in India energy storage company.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 772 crore, EBITDA INR 94 crore at 12% margin, PAT INR 46 crore
items.quote: we delivered a healthy sequential improvement in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue rising to INR 772 crore from INR 671 crore in Q1 FY27. EBITDA stood at INR 94 crore, translating into a margin of 12%, while PAT was INR 46 crore.

items.statement: Expect huge order inflows in coming year with broad-based growth across sector
items.quote: I can definitely tell you that we expect huge order inflows to come in the coming year, and the market demand is going to pick up significantly.

items.statement: Being very selective on BESS order book focusing on profitable growth and C&I segment
items.quote: We are very, very selective on our order books. We are focused on the C&I segment. You will see a huge growth momentum in the sector, and our order books will continue to grow. But we are very, very focused on profitable growth.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR2,900-3,000 crores with H2 split equally at INR725-750 crores per quarter; initial FY28 guidance of INR3,400-3,500 crores with high likelihood of upward revision
items.quote: We revised our final guidance for FY27, our final guidance to INR2,900 crores-INR3,000 crores, and H2 sales will be more or less distributed equally between Q3 and Q4, between INR725 crores-INR750 crores per quarter. For next year, we give an initial conservative guidance of INR3,400 crores, INR3,500 crores, with a very, very high likelihood of upward revision.

items.statement: H1 order booking INR23.19 billion: INR20.88B generator, INR1.7B railway, INR0.16B spares, INR0.45B Turkey; Q2 order inflow INR8.24B up 57% QoQ and 70% YoY; 92% exports
items.quote: Order booking for the manufacturing segment is INR23.19 billion, out of which INR20.88 billion is the generator business, INR1.7 billion is the railway business, spares and aftermarket is INR0.16 billion, and INR0.45 billion is the Turkey business. Order inflow statistics. Order inflow for the quarter is INR8.24 billion, an increase of 57% on a Q-o-Q basis. An increase from the previous year is ab

items.statement: Pricing stable with price variation clauses linked to raw material costs; margins protected as prices adjust per formula; no drastic price increases expected
items.quote: The pricing is stable at the moment, right? Pricing is not going to go up drastically. Pricing will go up to the extent of the as per the price variation formulas that we have based on raw materials, right? So if raw material prices go up, our prices will go up. Raw material prices go down, our prices will go down to the extent that the raw materials will go down. So, our margins will be protected

items.statement: Started booking orders from Siemens Energy for two-pole generators on build-to-print basis from gas turbine group (not TI group); project construction begun with Bhoomi Puja Nov 19; forecasts and commitments as per plan
items.quote: We have mentioned in various forums earlier about the scale of the investment, and the construction of the project has begun. We have the Bhoomi Puja, which is scheduled for next week on November 19. It's going to be in full swing after that. We have ordered most of the major equipment, and the project is in full swing. The forecast and the commitments from Siemens side is as per plan

items.statement: Average generator size 92MW in Q2; produced ~400 units in Q2 vs 320 in Q1; cumulative units sold ~8,770; demand-driven order intake increase
items.quote: M.N. Varalakshmi: 92 megawatt. Nikhil Kumar: Yes. But we have more demand. We are producing more units. We have more capacity. That was the whole purpose of undertaking the capacity expansion, to produce more generators, and that is what we are doing.

items.statement: Strong cash position INR4.19B including customer advances and preferential share issue money
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong cash position of INR4.19 billion, including customer advances and the preferential share issue money.

items.statement: Hydro segment growing with largest ever vertical and horizontal run-of-river orders in Nepal; major markets Nepal and Vietnam; Q3 already received big hydro orders; margins similar to gas turbine business
items.quote: We have seen a good number of orders from Nepal market. Today, even though we are selling all over the world these hydro generators, the two major markets are Nepal and Vietnam. This business is going to grow. We have a huge pipeline of inquiries, and in Q3 also, we have already received some big orders. This segment is the one, definitely it is a growing segment for us. This trend is

items.statement: Only three global large gas turbine OEMs (GE, Siemens, Mitsubishi); tied up with Siemens Energy; competitors unlikely to engage due to exclusivity; happy with Siemens relationship and focused on growing it
items.quote: First of all, there are three people in the world who make these large turbine, gas turbines, okay? There is GE, there is Siemens, and there is Mitsubishi. So, when we have tied up with one of them, the others are not going to come to us and we are happy with the party we are tied up with. We are happy with the party we are tied up with. We are working with a world-class company, and we are happy

items.statement: SoftBank canceling GE Vernova turbine reservations does not change underlying market dynamics; one player's oversized bet not indicative of broader demand
items.quote: One player in the market has taken an oversized bet about something, that doesn't change the underlying part of the market. From my point of view, you've seen the commentary coming out of GE Vernova also, who's a customer for them, they have made their comments, and I think you should read those comments and take that also into perspective.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR1,030 crores, EBITDA margin 14%, beating guidance
items.quote: As guided to the market, revenue from operations in Q2 FY27 stood at INR1,030 crores, broadly stable versus the previous quarter and above the INR1,000 crores mark for the consecutive quarter.

items.statement: FY28 volume growth guidance 7% or outgrowing market, EBITDA margin 13%
items.quote: For FY 28 atleast, We still remain committed, we still confirm our guidance of around 7% or outgrowing the market growth in volumes, and we still stand at 13% EBITDA.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA INR144 crores, margin 14%, up 332 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR144 crores with an EBITDA margin of 14%, improved by 332 basis points year-on-year, beating the guidance.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA INR291 crores, margin 14.2%, up 353 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 increased by 36% to INR291 crores, while EBITDA margin expanded by 353 basis points to 14.2%.

items.statement: Largest coke oven order in history received post quarter end, covers silica lines for 18 months
items.quote: subsequent to the quarter end, we received our largest coke oven order in our history to cover our silica production lines for the next 18 months.

items.statement: Silica line completely booked for more than a year, will improve Rajgangpur plant utilization
items.quote: Most importantly, what is to be noted is that this will improve the capacity utilization of our Rajgangpur plant. Let's say that the silica line is completely booked for more than a year.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex INR34 crores vs guided INR150 crores; focus on equipment reliability, technology transfers, compliance
items.quote: the capex outflow that you just spoke about, the capex is on two, three areas that we've been working on. One, of course, improving the reliability of the equipments that we have, because upgrades of these equipment's are extremely important.

items.statement: Chiraipani quartzite mine (40,000 tons/year) commenced operations; Bhikampali mine on track for next quarter start
items.quote: The Chiraipani mines with an annual capacity of 40,000 tons, we have already commenced our operations. The other mine, which is Bhikampali in Odisha, we remain on track with respect to the startup of that mine, and very hopeful next quarter we should be able to start that mine.

items.statement: Plan to be fully captive on quartzite by next financial year
items.quote: Yes, we are planning by the next financial year, we should be fully on our own resources.

items.statement: Quartzite mine expected to give 3%-3.5% EBITDA improvement for full year
items.quote: And structurally, this should be able to give us close to 3%-3.5% delta in terms of EBITDA going forward for the entire year.

items.statement: Sharp cost increases in bauxite, fused magnesia, DBM; freight and energy costs also up
items.quote: Yes, it's unfortunately bauxite, fused magnesia and DBM. These are the three places. Let me put it like this. Everywhere there is an increase, but these are the three that have sharply shot up.

items.statement: Flow control mix improved 3 bps QoQ; higher realization masks material cost increase
items.quote: Let's say that from historical perspective, we have improved by 3 basis points on a quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Stepped away from low-margin cement orders; chose value over volume
items.quote: This quarter is slight bit of an anomaly, if I must say so, because we chose to step away from some of the low-margin orders.

items.statement: Added two new steel sector customers in Q2; improved position with existing base
items.quote: But yes, there are two customers in steel sector that we have added in this quarter, which are new to our account. Our position among our existing base of the customers has also improved.

items.statement: Refractory capacity overhang to persist until India absorbs 300M ton steel capacity; Chinese competition in coke ovens a concern
items.quote: So this capacity overhang will continue to be there for a while before India starts absorbing that capacity overhang in the refractory industry.

items.statement: Working capital intensity 38% in H1 due to inventory build-up for silica orders and raw material resilience; operating cash flow INR99 crores
items.quote: Working capital intensity increased to 38%, primarily due to inventory build-up to ensure raw material availability and supply chain resilience, and most importantly, to serve our future strong order book as such, and especially in the silica.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR456 crores at Sep 2026; net cash to EBITDA 0.25x
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR456 crores at the end of September 2026. Net cash to EBITDA remained healthy at approximately 0.25x, providing significant financial flexibility.

items.statement: India crude steel production grew 2.8% in H1; refractory industry grew at similar rate; company outperformed via flow control
items.quote: If I really look into the entire story of H1 in the country, while the steel demand grew close to 7.2%, the crude steel production only grew to the rate of 2.8%.

items.statement: CBAM makes Europe exports uncompetitive; North America not viable; Middle East/Africa only export opportunity but Chinese competition intense
items.quote: When you talk about Europe, due to the introduction of CBAM, it becomes highly uncompetitive for us to export there, despite we are getting a lot of technology from Europe to India.

items.statement: MINPRO JV with Khemka Refractories signed August 2026; first invoicing done; volumes to scale up
items.quote: We have now started our first invoicing from MINPRO, this joint venture, and in the coming quarter, we are looking to expand.

items.statement: Technology transfer of MGG bricks from Dalian to Rajgangpur plant ramping up
items.quote: one of the technology transfers that is now ramping up in India is going to be MGG bricks. It's the technology that we're doing a transfer from Dalian plant to our Rajgangpur plant.

items.statement: Focus on coal gasifiers, glass, aluminum as industrial growth engines; glass centre of competency being built
items.quote: Some of the key focus areas for the management in coming quarters are going to be establishing a strong foothold in coal gasifiers, which is a big opportunity in India.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 1,000 crores expected to be reached sooner than FY28
items.quote: Our earlier aspiration was to achieve approximately INR1,000 crores in revenue by FY28, supported by our stated target of 30% to 35% revenue CAGR between FY25 and FY29.

items.statement: PAT margin target of 7% by FY28
items.quote: So, with regard to profitability, definitely the target or benchmark which we took with regard to profitability also that, we are targeting to reach to a level of 7% by FY28.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 25-30% YoY expected after reaching INR 1,000 crore milestone
items.quote: And definitely we are expecting a growth of 20 to -- 25% to 30% year-on-year thereafter.

items.statement: Long-term revenue CAGR of 20-25% over five-year horizon
items.quote: And definitely, I mean, as we said that in the next two-to-three-year term, we expect at CAGR of 25% to 30%, and in the longer run, we expect a growth of around 20% to 25% at a time horizon of five years, kind of.

items.statement: No major capex planned for textile business; incremental capex directed to FMCG segment
items.quote: So as of now, we don't have much, much plan with regard to investment or capacity addition for the textile business. Whatever new facilities or new investment we will be doing will be mainly for the FMCG segment.

items.statement: Aggregate installed capacity for FMCG and intermediates at ~20,840 tons/month after Roorkee soap line commissioning
items.quote: Following the commissioning of the additional soap production line in Roorkee in Q1, our aggregate installed capacity for FMCG and FMCG intermediates stand at approximately 20,840 tons per month.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 50-55% for FMCG, 80-85% for textile
items.quote: So currently, we are almost utilizing our current capacity at a pace of - - at a rate of around 50%-55%, and we expect that this utilization will get better in the coming time.

items.statement: Roorkee additional soap line (1,700 MT) expected to generate revenue by Q4 FY27
items.quote: So, we are in discussion with various customers for the soap line at Roorkee also. With one or two customers, we are at a very final stage. So probably by Q4 of this year, we will have the additional revenue for those lines also.

items.statement: B2B model with 1-month firm and 2-month tentative customer planning; no traditional order book
items.quote: So, our business model is we have to be B2B segment, right? So, business is not the open orders or order book kind of a thing. We have planning from the customers for 1-month firm and 2-month tentative. That way it works.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 8.73%, PAT margin 6.03%; sequential improvement from lower raw material cost ratio (74.37% vs 75.6%)
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 8.73% compared with 8.81% in Q1 FY27 and 9.65% in Q2 FY26, while the PAT margin was 6.03% compared with 5.44% in Q1 FY27 and 5.75% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: FMCG segment result margin improved to 9.27% in Q2 FY27 from 8.15% in Q1 FY27 and 6.34% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: On a segment basis, our FMCG, FMCG Intermediate, and edible business reported a revenue of INR240.92 crores in Q2 FY27, a growth of 154.28% year-on-year with the segment result of INR22.32 crores and a segment result margin of 9.27% compared with 6.34% in Q2 FY26 and 8.15% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Textile segment loss of INR 0.97 crores in Q2 FY27 due to machine installation downtime and high input costs; expected to improve as costs stabilize
items.quote: Our textile segment reported a revenue of INR24.25 crores in Q2 FY27, 7.53% lower year-on-year, and a segment loss of INR0.97 crores as a higher input cost, dyes and chemicals continue to weigh on processing margins.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve as raw material price volatility settles and capacity utilization increases
items.quote: In the coming quarters we are hopeful that once this price volatility in the raw material prices will get settled, definitely the EBITDA margin will get improved. And we are more bullish on the utilization of our capacity.

items.statement: Crude-linked inputs (LABSA, palm-linked) volatile; soap noodles prices softened mid-2026; brokerages expect FMCG gross margin pressure in H2
items.quote: On the cost side, crude-linked inputs such as LABSA and palm-linked material stayed volatile after the sharp increase earlier in the year. Even as soap noodles prices were softened in mid-2026 amid subdued demand, and several brokerages expect FMCG gross margins to remain under some pressure into the second half.

items.statement: Textile input costs (cotton, yarn, dyes, chemicals) elevated; festive demand providing some support
items.quote: In textile industry, participants continue to report higher cotton, yarn, dyed, and chemical costs, with festive demand providing some support.

items.statement: FMCG value growth improved to 8.6% in Jul-Sep 2026 (rural 10.6%, urban 5.8%); urban demand strengthening through quarter
items.quote: Looking at the industry in the quarter, the data from Bizom suggests that FMCG value growth improved to 8.6% in July to September 2026 from 6.8% in the previous quarter, with rural markets growing at about 10.6% and urban at about 5.8%, and urban demand strengthening through the quarter.

items.statement: Diwali season mixed: normal for some businesses, very good for edibles
items.quote: So Diwali season was again, it's mixed up, because we have a different set of businesses. So for one of the business it was normal, but for one of the business, for edible segment it was very good. So it is mixed. It is mixed kind of.

items.statement: FMCG, intermediates, edibles ~90.7% of H1 FY27 revenue (90.9% in Q2); up from ~83% in FY26
items.quote: FMCG, FMCG intermediates, and edible together accounted for approximately 90.7% of our revenue in half year FY27, approximately 90.9% in quarter two FY27, with textile contributing the balance. This compares with approximately 90.6% in Q1 FY27 and an FMCG-led mix of approximately 83% for FY26.

items.statement: Primary growth drivers identified as soap section and edible business
items.quote: So, we see the primary growth driver is going to be the soap section and the edible business for us.

items.statement: Edibles expansion includes biscuit manufacturing facility under evaluation
items.quote: And we are also looking at diversifying the product portfolio also, like adding up the biscuit manufacturing facility or some of the other products which we are looking at.

items.statement: Revenue from group company RCM ~44% in Q2 FY27, ~42.5% YTD
items.quote: So, in the overall revenue, the revenue from RCM is around 44% kind of for last quarter. And YTD, I can say it's around 42%, 42.5%.

items.statement: Serving 200+ customers across categories; long-term relationships with brands like Godrej, Wipro, ITC
items.quote: The combination of these facilities enable us to serve a broad customer base of more than 200 customers across multiple product categories, while improving proximity to market and supply chain responsiveness.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing model with high switching costs; customers stay for years once qualified
items.quote: So as I mentioned that, we since we are catering to all the brands and we are doing the contract manufacturing majorly, that is our focus area. So I mean there it's not a short-term relationship which you have. So once you onboard any of these brands So they stay with you.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating cash flow INR 18 crores vs PAT INR 31 crores; funds deployed in edible commodity inventory for bulk buying
items.quote: During this first half, our funds mostly deployed for the inventory side because a few of the products wherein we are dealing in the edible segment are seasonal or commodity-based, and we do have the benefit of pricing, we go for bulk buying for those commodities.

items.statement: Working capital optimization focus; cash conversion expected to improve in coming quarters as seasonal inventory releases
items.quote: So yes, definitely, in the coming quarters, the cash from operations will improve as we are working on the working capital front also. So, in next -- we currently also we are at a good amount of capacity utilization. But in the coming period we will improve the working capital.

items.statement: No debt in FMCG business; textile debt to be repaid; no fresh loans foreseen
items.quote: With regard to debt, there are certain debts which we have taken for the textile business. For the FMCG business, we don't have any such kind of a debt with us, right? And we are planning to repay that also in a coming period kind of a time, and we don't foresee a fresh loan as of now for current business.

items.statement: No further fundraise planned; expansions to be funded through internal accruals
items.quote: No, no. So as of now, we don't have any plan for another fundraise. And the pace at which we are going, we, we are hopeful that whatever expansion we will be doing, that we can do through our internal approvals only.

items.statement: No inorganic growth plans currently; management continuously evaluating opportunities
items.quote: As of now, we don't have any plan in hand for any inorganic growth kind of a thing. But, management is continuously looking for the opportunity, and as and when there will be any lucrative opportunity comes we will definitely go for it if it is worth doing.

items.statement: Edibles revenue grew 63.71% sequentially in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Sequentially, edibles revenue grew at 63.71%, while revenue from home care and detergent and from Guwahati noodle section was lower, which together with the modest moderation at Roorkee explained the quarter-on-quarter dip in consolidated revenue.

items.statement: Input cost volatility (crude-linked, palm-linked, textile dyes/chemicals) remains near-term risk; expected to normalize progressively
items.quote: While the input cost environment may remain volatile in the near term, we expect margins to normalize progressively as cost stabilize and as the capacity added decent ramp-up.

items.statement: Competitive market and raw material price volatility cited as ongoing challenges
items.quote: At the same time, the market remains competitive and input cost can be volatile. For us, this reinforces the importance of execution, maintaining product quality, improving manufacturing efficiency, managing procurement and inventory carefully, and developing products and customer relationships that support repeat business.

items.statement: Management expects current ~12% EBITDA margin to sustain for next 2-4 quarters; no margin improvement guided
items.quote: For now, safely, it can be assumed that these margins will stay at this level for KP Energy. And they are not bad once the scale is there and the environment has changed for EPC, and we have to always be looking at the reality. We don't want to guide you wrong.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio will not exceed 2x going forward, even after completing the 202 MW IPP portfolio
items.quote: We have guided in KP 3.0 that we will not exceed debt to equity of 2 in future, even after this IPP.

items.statement: Order book as of 30 Sep 2026 stands at ~1.64 GW with estimated value of ~INR 1,940 crores
items.quote: Our order book as on 30th September '26 stands at approximately 1.64 gigawatts and with an estimated value of around INR1,940 crores, giving us a strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Bidding for ~1 GW of tenders; at 70% strike rate could materialize ~700 MW worth INR 7,000-8,000 crores within 3-6 months
items.quote: We have already got our hands full with the current execution cycle, and we are already bidding for almost 1 gigawatt of tenders, which are available, which may materialize even if I consider a 70% of a strike rate, 700 megawatts has not gone anywhere, which will materialize soon enough.

items.statement: Gross margin ~19% in Q2 FY27, broadly in line with Q1 FY27; EBITDA margin ~12% guided to sustain
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter approximately stood at 19%, broadly in line with the Q1 FY27. The operating environment as prevalent in the Q1 FY27 has continued through the quarter, and our margins have remained consistent with that trend.

items.statement: No large IPP capex plans beyond existing 202 MW under development; focus on EPC with limited balance sheet capex
items.quote: So you are right, there is no large IPP plans for KP Energy other than what we already have about 250 megawatts, right? Shabana Belim: 202. Kapil Kriplani: Yes, 202. And then we will not have much of further

items.statement: IPP portfolio: 48.5 MW operational, 202 MW under development; no further IPP capacity additions planned
items.quote: Our IPP portfolio stood at 48.5 megawatts operational with an additional 202 megawatts under development. As this capacity comes online, it will add recurring revenues alongside our core EPC business.

items.statement: Margin pressure from ROW cost escalation, labor volatility, raw material (steel) price volatility, and project-specific scope mix; no single component dominates
items.quote: So these are the major factors which contribute to the cost escalation. Going forward, market takes its own call and eventually, it will balance out in terms of the economic factors as well.

items.statement: Revenue mix in Q2: Infrastructure development INR 527 cr (82% YoY growth), O&M INR 3.2 cr, Sale of Power INR 8.41 cr; group vs external revenue ~50-50 in Q2 vs 80-85% group in Q1
items.quote: So quarter 2, this is 50-50, you can say so, this quarter. We have improved from the last quarter where it was almost 80, 85.

items.statement: Depreciation INR 9.27 cr and finance cost INR 17.11 cr in Q2 FY27; debt-to-equity guided not to exceed 2x
items.quote: Depreciation and finance costs stood at approximately INR9.27 crores and INR17.11 crores, respectively, in line with the expanded scale of our operations.

items.statement: Statutory auditor changed from MAAK & Associates to MSKC & Associates LLP (BDO Network) effective Q2 FY27
items.quote: MSKC & Associates LLP, a member firm of the BDO Network, 1 of the 6 largest audit and accounting networks in this world, has been appointed as statutory auditors of the company, succeeding MAAK & Associates effective from Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Related-party transactions with KP Group entities will continue at arm's length and in ordinary course of business; Q2 revenue split ~50-50 group vs external
items.quote: As a part of this integrated platform, KP Energy will continue to receive wind BOP contracts from related entities within the KP Group. Such related party transactions will be continued to be undertaken at arm's length and in ordinary course of business.

items.statement: Margin compression risk from ROW rate changes, labor availability/volatility, steel price volatility, geopolitical factors (Hormuz effect); guided to persist 2-4 quarters
items.quote: The ROW rate has changed substantially from where it was. So can I go and change that? It's not possible, right? I am a player which and I have to operate within the way the things operate around me in the industry.

items.statement: IPP portfolio (48.5 MW operational, 202 MW under development) to add recurring revenues; depreciation benefit to support cash profits
items.quote: As this capacity comes online, it will add recurring revenues alongside our core EPC business and the associated depreciation benefit will continue to support our cash profits.

items.statement: Whole-Time Director Affan Faruk Patel absent due to emergency; leadership represented by CFO Shabana Belim, Group CFO Kapil Kriplani, Vice Chairman Sunil Maheshwari, Executive Director Rajesh Shrivastava
items.quote: At the outset, I would like to express that Mr. Affan Faruk Patel could not join us due to certain emergency requirements and I share this forum with our Group CFO, Mr. Kapil Kriplani; our Vice Chairman, Mr. Sunil Maheshwari; and our Executive Director, Mr. Rajesh Shrivastava.

items.statement: Management expects to exceed the earlier FY27 revenue target of INR800 crores and continue overachieving guidance as done for the last 10 years
items.quote: Yes, definitely. As I had mentioned earlier, and in my previous earnings calls as well, that as our brands are building traction, as our business is expanding, we have kind of overachieved our target.

items.statement: A CFO is being trained internally and will join in a few months; internal audit team and audit checks have been appointed
items.quote: As I have mentioned earlier, we are in the midst of training a CFO, and the world will have the news of a CFO joining in a few months. The person has already joined the company over the last three, four years, and they are extensively training.

items.statement: Pet Care, mobility, mass market cosmetics growing 65-80% on small bases; vintage business growing 15-25% on higher base; all seven verticals contributing
items.quote: Our Pet Care is growing at almost 70%, 80%. Our mobility is growing at 65% to 70%. Mass market cosmetics is growing at almost 65%, 70%. They are at a small basis, they are growing. Our vintage business is also growing at 15% to 25% year- on- year, and that is coming at a higher base.

items.statement: New age businesses have intrinsically higher profitability; blended EBITDA margin trend improving and expected to keep improving due to new age products and operational efficiencies
items.quote: If you see the trend, it's improving, then it's going to keep on improving because of our new age products which are coming through. Definitely, if EBITDA improves, then our bottom line improves as well.

items.statement: Existing business growing 15-20% annually for next 7-8 years; new age business growing 65-70% year-on-year with potential for triple-digit growth when adding territories
items.quote: The existing businesses are on an annual growth rate of 15% to 20% on a year-to-year basis, and that will be so for the next seven to eight years based on what we are doing and where we are heading. In terms of the new age business, that will continue to grow at around 65% to 70% year-on-year.

items.statement: ARR for Pet Care, mobility and vintage business all tracking above projections; overall ARR expected to outperform earlier numbers by 15-20% this year
items.quote: The ARR for the Pet Care is in line with our projection, what we had mentioned earlier. The mobility is also in line with our projections. In fact, it will overachieve both. In terms of our vintage business, the ARR also is better.

items.statement: Invested 26% stake in Vetcare, a 4-decade pet retail pioneer supplying to national parks, zoos and Vantara; profitable no-burn model; will invest further over time
items.quote: That company is probably doing, is one of the pioneers in pet retail in the country. It is doing pet retail for almost four decades. That is more than, I would say, many, many other pet retailers were not even born when this company was doing pet retail.

items.statement: CAT (dermaceutics/hormonal) launch in 60-90 days around January 2027; anti-aging line rollout across metros in 6-18 months; hormonal products nationwide; target 80-90% counter coverage in one year
items.quote: CAT, as I said, we are launching in about 60 days, 60 to 90 days from now. Practically around January 2027. That is what I had mentioned earlier as well. Daulcél is our anti-aging line, and our hormonal line is also in the launch phase right now.

items.statement: Moats include 15-16 year licensing timelines, largest diagnostic dataset, 11-year nutraceutical research with clinical trials, deep vet/groomer/breeder ecosystem built over time; very difficult to replicate
items.quote: To get our licenses will take them 15, 16 years, irrespective of how well-funded they are and how well-connected they are in terms of bureaucracy or legacy. To give you a small example, our diagnostic center, we started a year and a half ago. We are the first ones in the country.

items.statement: Growth prospects strong across pharma, Pet Care, mobility, nutrition for next 3-4 years; current ARR per division (INR60-100 crores) small relative to industry size
items.quote: For not just the next fiscal year, for the next three years, four years, we can expect the same growth as we have been doing in our divisions. For pharma industry outlook, people tell me, that there is a war, what will happen? Irrespective of the bombs falling, people have to take their heart pills.

items.statement: Wagr pet platform not just e-commerce but full ecosystem; 45-person team working 18-19 hours daily; building for 5-6 year horizon where 'anything to do with Pet Care, you will Wagr it'
items.quote: Wagr is not just an e-commerce platform. People are saying, when will the sales start? It is not just a place where people buy products. It is a place where you are going to go for all your pet needs.

items.statement: Main growth inflection expected in next 18-24 months as brands penetrate and ecosystem dots connect; current numbers just first floor of building
items.quote: Our growth has not yet started -- Our growth will happen in the next 18 to 24 months. That is when you will see the actual growth of what we are building over the last decade and a half, two decades.

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 order inflow guidance of INR10,000-12,000 crores
items.quote: Based on the opportunities available to us and our bidding strategy, we reiterate our FY27 order inflow guidance of INR10,000 crores to INR12,000 crores.

items.statement: Confident of delivering 30-40% revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: On this basis, we remain confident in our ability to deliver the revenue growth that we had guided for, which is about 30%, 40% from last year.

items.statement: Target to reduce consolidated debt by INR600-800 crores in FY27
items.quote: We remain committed to our target of reducing debt by INR600 crores to INR800 crores during FY27, and you will start seeing this reduction in debt at length from quarter three onwards as execution ramps up.

items.statement: Aim to become net debt-free on standalone basis by FY28
items.quote: Second, we continue to work towards becoming net debt-free on a standalone basis by FY28.

items.statement: Standalone capex to remain flat or below INR100 crores in FY27
items.quote: Third, standalone capital expenditure will remain flat or below INR100 crores for FY27, which is entirely towards replacement requirements.

items.statement: Target to close FY27 at approximately 120 working capital days
items.quote: Our targets remain to close the FY27 at approximately 120 working capital days.

items.statement: Order book at INR33,081 crores as of September 30, 2026 across 12 verticals
items.quote: Our order book stood at INR33,081 crores as of September 30th, 2026, spread across 12 business verticals.

items.statement: Fresh order inflow of INR7,589 crores in H1 FY27; added INR1,300 crores more as of call date
items.quote: During this quarter, we secured fresh orders worth approximately INR7,321 crores across BOT, EPC, and HAM. This takes our fresh order inflow for the first half to approximately INR7,589 crores. I am also happy to report that as of today, we have further added about INR1,300 crores of new orders.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR3.30 lakh crores; bids worth INR23,000 crores submitted awaiting opening
items.quote: In addition to this, bids worth INR23,000 crores have been submitted, and we are awaiting their opening, while our overall bid pipeline stands at approximately INR3.30 lakh crores.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreements with Alpha Alternatives for Mekhali transmission (EV INR2,914 cr) and 1,363 MW solar portfolio (EV INR6,829 cr)
items.quote: We signed definite agreements with Alpha Alternatives for this project at an enterprise value of approximately INR2,914 crores against a project cost of approximately INR2,171 crores. The second transaction relates to our 1,363 MW solar portfolio in Madhya Pradesh. We signed definitive agreements at an enterprise value of approximately INR6,829 crores, compared with the project cost of approximate

items.statement: Alpha to co-invest 49% equity during construction (INR820 cr); will acquire DBL's 51% stake post-commissioning; DBL retains EPC work worth over INR7,300 cr
items.quote: First of all, Alpha Alternatives will co-invest 49% as per equity during the construction phase. That means out of the combined equity requirement for the two projects of INR1,680 crores, around INR820 crores will be funded by Alpha Alternatives, and the remaining INR850 crores will be funded by DBL. Secondly, Alpha Alternatives will acquire our remaining 51% stake once the projects are commission

items.statement: Entry into oil & gas infrastructure via LPG pipeline opportunity combining EPC with regulated long-term asset ownership
items.quote: The third important development is our entry into the oil and gas infrastructure segment. This is an important addition to our portfolio. It again combines, it gives us the opportunity to combine our EPC capabilities with the ownership of a long-term infrastructure asset that has a regulated revenue model.

items.statement: Standalone capex flat or below INR100 crores in FY27 for replacement only
items.quote: Third, standalone capital expenditure will remain flat or below INR100 crores for FY27, which is entirely towards replacement requirements. Our existing equipment base is largely paid for, and we do not envisage any significant fresh standalone capex.

items.statement: Long-term target of 57 million tons annual coal production by FY29 unchanged
items.quote: Looking beyond the current year, our target of achieving annual coal production of approximately 57 million tons by FY29 remains unchanged, led by the ramp-up of Siarmal and Pachhwara.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 10.4% in Q2 FY27 and 10.3% in H1 FY27; guided 10-10.5% for full year
items.quote: Yes, 10%-10.5% margin will remain the same.

items.statement: Mining SPVs contributed 25% EBITDA margin in H1 FY27
items.quote: The mining SPVs contributed revenue of INR795 crores during first half FY27 at EBITDA margin of 25%.

items.statement: Crude oil volatility keeping diesel and bitumen prices elevated; price adjustment mechanism on MDO contracts provides relief; fuel cost increases passed through with lag
items.quote: On the cost front, crude oil remains volatile amid the situation in West Asia, keeping diesel and bitumen prices elevated. The extension of the price adjustment mechanism on our MDO contracts provides some relief, while fuel-related cost increases are passed through, though with a lag.

items.statement: Road sector muted but NHAI floated over INR1 lakh crore orders; competition intense in smaller packages with irrational bidding
items.quote: On the road sector, there is muted activity, but from a lower base, we think the opportunity to grow is furthermore because the NHAI has already floated about over INR1 lakh crores worth of orders. While we welcome this, we remain disciplined in our approach. Competition in the road EPC space continues to be intense, particularly in the smaller packages, where bidding prices are, in our view, not

items.statement: Opportunity expanding in transmission, renewables, railways, water, oil & gas infrastructure with significant government investment
items.quote: At the same time, the opportunity beyond roads continues to expand. Transmission, renewable energy, railways, water, oil, and gas infrastructure are receiving significant government attention and investment.

items.statement: Working capital higher in H1; expected to ease in H2 as execution improves and collections progress
items.quote: As is typical for our business, working capital requirements are higher in the first half of the year. We are expecting working capital to ease in the second half of the execution, in the second half as execution improves and collections progress.

items.statement: Mining business expected to generate INR1,000 crores annual operating cash flow by FY29 at 57 mtpa production
items.quote: At that level of production, we expect the mining business to generate annual operating cash flow of approximately INR1,000 crores, with contractual escalation providing additional support over time.

items.statement: Mining and InvIT holdings together expected to generate ~INR1,300 crores annual cash flow without new EPC orders
items.quote: Over the next few years, our mining operations and InvIT holdings together expected to generate approximately INR1,300 crores of annual cash flow without even factoring any new EPC orders.

items.statement: Pachhwara production impacted by Punjab power plant strike; dispatches resumed September; confident of 7 mt target
items.quote: Coal production is lesser at 1.98 million ton. That includes, there was a strike at the power plant level in Punjab. The dispatches were lower. Everything started again from September. We are again here also, we will achieve 7 million ton by the year end. There will be no gap in physical performance or financial performance.

items.statement: Four HAM projects to be transferred to Anantam InvIT next quarter; remaining in FY28 pending NHAI approvals
items.quote: During the next quarter, we expect to transfer four HAM projects to Anantam Highways Trust. The remaining assets are expected to be transferred in FY28 and are awaiting the NHAI approvals.

items.statement: Alpha transaction expected to return ~INR1,900 crores (mix of cash and units) against INR850 crores equity investment
items.quote: We will be investing about INR850 crores of equity, somewhere in that ballpark figure that I mentioned. Again, is that we will be getting a return of about INR1,900 crores back. This is a mix of cash and units that will come. That is the transaction with Alpha. Again, INR850, about INR1,900-odd crores of capital will come back to the company.

items.statement: No new execution risks identified beyond usual business risks
items.quote: Sir, the risks in the business remain as they always were. There is no new risk that I can kind of think of right now.

items.statement: LPG pipeline project execution to start in 6-8 months due to land acquisition requirements
items.quote: It will take around six months or eight months from now because a lot of land acquisition is involved and there are so many different type of requirement in that project.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated revenue above INR225 crore and on a pessimistic basis INR250+ crore for FY27, with EBITDA margin improvement of 50-100 bps
items.quote: We are confident to reach at least above the INR225 crores and on a pessimistic basis INR250 plus crores on a consolidated basis in terms of top line.

items.statement: Indian plant expected to generate INR100 crore revenue in first year, INR125-150 crore in second year with EBITDA margin 8.5-9% and PAT 6.5-7%
items.quote: we will clock INR100 crores as a revenue in Indian from the Indian manufacturing facility which we are going to establish, followed by INR125 crores to INR150 crores in the second financial year, with the EBITDA margin nearly to 8.5% to 9% and PAT nearly to 6.5% to 7%.

items.statement: Board approved export-oriented manufacturing facility and product development center in India near Vadodara; acquiring 190,000 sq ft land
items.quote: A major development I would like to share has been the Board approval of a proposal to establish an export-oriented manufacturing facility and product development center in India. We are exploring and we are in focus of acquiring industrial land near Vadodara to manufacture advanced and high-performance lubricants.

items.statement: Grease manufacturing facility at Kenya plant to be commissioned in Q3 FY27; Tanzania warehousing and distribution targeted by end of FY27
items.quote: We plan to commission a grease manufacturing facility at our Kenya plant during the third quarter of FY27. We are also exploring expansion in Tanzania, beginning with the warehousing and distribution operations followed by manufacturing at an appropriate stage.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 7.74% vs 10.18% in H1 FY26; decline due to base oil volatility and higher logistics costs from Middle East tensions
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 7.74% compared with 10.18% in H1 FY26. The major operations is due to the ongoing geopolitical tension, particularly in the Middle East, which resulted into the volatility in base oils and higher logistic and distribution cost, which has impacted our margins.

items.statement: Landed cost of raw materials increased 50-60% on average due to Middle East war; significant cost passed to customers without losing major deals
items.quote: this has almost increased nearly to 50 to 60% on an average. We also have significantly passed on this cost to our customers, without losing any major deal and we have kept our customer base intact

items.statement: Specialty lubricants contribute 22-25% of revenue; share expected to increase with dedicated Indian facility for high-end and specialty lubricants
items.quote: So, the specialty lubricants, must be contributing nearly 22% to 25% in the range. Specialty lubricant and but going forward, that share will get increased comparatively because we have a dedicated manufacturing facility in India for which we are right now in process of acquiring the land.

items.statement: Specialty lubricants carry ~50% higher margins than conventional lubricants (ballpark estimate)
items.quote: At least you will get a 50% nearly to 50% margins, more margins as compared to conventional lubricants.

items.statement: Acquiring 40% stake in Quebec Petroleum Resources Limited, an Indian public lubricant manufacturer distributing across India
items.quote: we have already stepped in to the Indian market by acquiring the significant stake, that is 40% stake. We are in process of acquiring a 40% stake in Quebec Petroleum Resources Limited, which is the Indian public limited company into the lubricant manufacturing.

items.statement: Onboarded major customers from China including big retail names; expanding distribution in Southeast Asia
items.quote: Recently we have also onboarded some of the major customers from China, with the big names in terms of major retailing, some good names from the China market, we have already entered into the deal.

items.statement: Consolidated borrowings ~INR51 crore in H1 FY27; finance cost up ~60% YoY due to higher borrowings to fund revenue growth, mainly from UAE banking limits
items.quote: if you see the increase or the growth in the borrowing is coupled with our top line. Our top line has also increased comparatively. And to fund the increase in the top line, we have acquired some finances from the UAE and Kenya. Major increase came from UAE wherein we got good amount of deals from the new customers and which we got funded through the banking limits.

items.statement: Expect government capital and interest subsidies for Indian plant to reduce finance cost burden
items.quote: when we are going in the Indian plant, there are already the government schemes offering the capital subsidy and interest subsidy which will reduce the finance cost burden on the company for the production and manufacturing facility being set up in India.

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR118.64 crore (+39% YoY), EBITDA INR9.18 crore (+5.65% YoY), net profit INR4.10 crore
items.quote: During the H1 FY27, the consolidated revenue from operations have increased by nearly 39% and it has reached to INR118.64 crores, which was compared with the corresponding period of the previous financial year. It was nearly INR85 crores. EBITDA in the state H1 FY27 stood at INR9.18 crores, registering a growth of 5.65% over INR8.69 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR58.74 crore (+28% YoY), EBITDA INR4.60 crore, net profit INR2.05 crore
items.quote: Coming to quarterly performance, Q2 FY27, revenue from operations have increased by 28% year-on-year to INR58.74 crores. EBITDA stood at INR4.60 crores, while net profit stood at INR2.05 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Lubricant manufacturing 65% of revenue (gross margin 17-18%), petrochemical trading 35% (gross margin 11-12%), toll blending 2-4%
items.quote: In terms of lubricant manufacturing and petrochemical trading, majorly 65% comes from lubricant manufacturing and 35% on average comes from trading. In lubricant manufacturing, our gross margins are nearly to 17% to 18%, whereas in the trading we are clocking on an average 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Rising industrialization, infrastructure investments, and vehicle ownership support global lubricant demand; Middle East and East Africa remain key growth markets
items.quote: rising industrialization, infrastructure investments and increasing vehicle ownership continue to support lubricant demand globally also. The Middle East and East Africa remain important growth market, supported by construction activity, industrial expansion and also the growing demand for automotive as well as specialty lubricants.

items.statement: Management remains positive on reaching 12,000 metric tons volume target for FY27, expects 11,500-12,000 tons if no major cyclone damage
items.quote: We are still remaining positive at this time to reach the 12,000 metric tons. Maybe even if there is any bit of minor adjustments, even if we are under a little below 12,000 still confident.

items.statement: Expect EU FDA benefit by early 2027, enabling 0% tariff shrimp exports to EU by end of FY27 or start of next financial year
items.quote: We expect that we were informed that tentatively by early 2027, hopefully, we can get that benefit by early 2027, which means at least by the end of this financial year or for sure from the start of next financial year.

items.statement: US shrimp sales volumes grew 59% YoY and flat QoQ in Q2 FY27 due to stabilizing tariff rates and healthy customer demand
items.quote: Coming to our geographical mix, the shrimp sales volumes to the U.S.A. grew 59% year-on-year and remained flat quarter-on-quarter in Q2 of FY27 mainly this is supported by the improving trade visibility and the healthy customer demand.

items.statement: EU/UK volumes declined 33% YoY but recovered 46% QoQ in Q2 FY27 as logistics conditions improved
items.quote: However, volumes recovered strongly by 46% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 of FY27 as logistics conditions began to improve, although some challenges do persist where the sailing time to the European countries also has increased.

items.statement: Other markets volumes grew ~1000% YoY and 43% QoQ in Q2 FY27, mainly driven by Japan, albeit on a small base
items.quote: In the Q2 of FY27, volumes to other markets, mainly supported by Japan, as mentioned, grew approximately almost 1,000% year-on-year and 43% quarter-on-quarter, albeit on a small base.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 6.4% vs 7.2% YoY, flat EBITDA at INR18 cr due to higher farm gate prices and freight costs
items.quote: In the Q2 of FY27, net revenue grew 15% year-on-year to INR274 crores compared with INR238 crores in the Q2 of FY26. EBITDA remained flat year-on-year at INR18 crores with EBITDA margin at 6.4% compared with 7.2% in the Q2 of FY26.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 9.4% from 7.1% YoY, EBITDA up 40% to INR51 cr
items.quote: For the H1 of FY27, the net revenue grew 7% year-on-year to INR530 crores compared with INR497 crores in the H1 of FY26. EBITDA increased 40% year-on-year to INR51 crores compared with INR36 crores in H1 FY26, with EBITDA margin expanding to 9.4% from 7.1% in H1 of FY26.

items.statement: Management passed on some farm gate price increases to overseas customers but limited by global competition from Ecuador, Vietnam, Indonesia
items.quote: We have actually passed on some of the increase in farm gate prices to overseas customers to some extent. But at the same time, we all have to acknowledge that India is not the only producing country in the world.

items.statement: Farm gate prices rose 15-20% in Aug-Sep 2026, corrected significantly in Oct 2026 after cyclone-driven premature harvests
items.quote: And there were an increase of farm gate prices significantly in the months of August, September for that quarter, it extended to spill over to some period in October also. But after that, a major correction did happen in the farm gate prices in the month of October.

items.statement: Freight costs remain elevated due to longer shipping routes avoiding Middle East conflict zones and higher crude oil prices; no positive news from shipping lines
items.quote: Unfortunately, with one war after other, especially impacting the Middle East area. So, the vessels are avoiding taking those routes, and they are taking a longer route. In fact, our customers are getting their shipments also much later than what they used to get earlier and also adding up the freight cost to us.

items.statement: Focus on value-added and ready-to-eat products for higher realization and margin; first Japan RTE shipment expected Jan-Feb 2027
items.quote: And we are also seeing that in the case of the new market, which we have started -- restarted again after 20 years, that is Japan, where we are also working on ready-to-eat products with certain customers in Japan also, and we expect our first shipment to be happening in early 2027, supposed to be in January or February.

items.statement: RTE products offer better realization and margins vs commoditized RTC; expanding RTE to Asian markets including Japan
items.quote: But definitely, as you know very well, RTE is having a better value than RTC products, obviously. And it will definitely help us in growing our sales revenue with a higher realization in dollar terms, of course. And also, margin would be on a better level compared to some of the commoditized RTC products.

items.statement: Existing customers contribute major sales; adding new customers in East Europe, Japan, and targeting Russia by end of Dec 2026
items.quote: Well, obviously, the newer markets will come with newer customers, obviously, and that is we have been adding them, whether it's some of them in East Europe and in Japan. And hopefully, by end of December, we also -- we can add up to our order book for Russia also.

items.statement: EU tariffs of 4.3% on RTC and 7.2% on RTE put Apex at disadvantage vs Vietnam; EU FDA removal expected to level playing field
items.quote: It's 4.3%, which the importers, our customers do bear, 4.3% on RTC and 7.2%, I think approximately, it is on RTE, which they are bearing currently, which puts us in a difficult situation when compared to our competition in Vietnam, especially.

items.statement: US ADD provision of INR10.10 cr recognized in Q2 FY27 for contingent liability of ~INR30 cr due to rate revisions from 1.35% to 5.53%; appeal filed at US Court of International Trade
items.quote: Additionally, the company has also recognized a provision of INR10.10 crores in the Q2 of FY27 towards incremental antidumping duty liability totaling of roughly approximately around INR30 crores. This is pertaining to the earlier years, and it is actually a contingent liability.

items.statement: EU FDA expected effective early 2027, enabling 0% tariff on shrimp exports; currently 4.3% on RTC and 7.2% on RTE
items.quote: We expect that we were informed that tentatively by early 2027, hopefully, we can get that benefit by early 2027, which means at least by the end of this financial year or for sure from the start of next financial year, as informed to us, we should be able to do our exports to EU at 0% tariffs on shrimp products.

items.statement: Rupee appreciation would pressure farm gate prices first, then sale prices; focus on volume growth to offset FX impact
items.quote: So, in an appreciating, rupee appreciating scenario, like you have mentioned about INR90 supposedly or whatever it is, obviously, that will have a bearing on our farm gate prices predominantly because we will not be, the export industry would not be in a position to maintain the farm gate pricing, number one.

items.statement: US sales 62% of Q2 FY27 volumes, EU/UK 32%, other markets 6%; H1 FY27 US 66%, EU/UK 29%, others 5%
items.quote: Coming to the sales volume mix, the U.S.A. contributed 62% of our total shrimp sales in Q2 of FY27 and 66% in the H1 of FY27. The EU and the U.K. accounted for 32% in the Q2 of FY27 and 29% in the H1 of FY27, while other markets contributed 6% in the Q2 of FY27 and 5% in the H1 of FY27.

items.statement: EU shipments taking 2-3 weeks post-production due to Indian regulatory delays, stretching inventory holding period
items.quote: Currently, with regard to the EU, of course, because of certain non-tariff barriers and also certain issues within India with the regulatory bodies, it does take a very high time, a very high amount of time to actually execute a shipment post production. Now currently, it is going anywhere between 2 to 3 weeks post production to actually ship out goods to the EU.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio 0.04x as of Sep 2026; lean financial position with prudently managed debt levels
items.quote: Coming to the balance sheet, we continue to maintain a lean financial position with debt levels prudently managed and at comfortable levels, reflected in a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x as of September 2026.

items.statement: High-end product production creating capacity utilization limitations on certain lines; need to run all product types for customer needs
items.quote: And what we have seen this year is we have been doing some very high-end products also, but then that is also creating a limitations actually on the capacity utilization on certain lines which we have, which we have noticed.

items.statement: Cyclones hitting Andhra Pradesh East Coast in past 2 weeks caused farmer crop damage and premature harvests; another cyclone expected this week
items.quote: We understand over the past 2 weeks, we have been seeing impacts of different cyclones hitting the East Coast of India, especially unfortunately, the state of Andhra Pradesh is being hit definitely. And there is an expectation of another cyclone hitting later in this week.

items.statement: US 10% tariff restricting demand stability; even 5% price drop could boost volumes per customer feedback
items.quote: The other important point is definitely the tariff of 10% in the U.S.A. is obviously playing a big role because currently, even if the overall pricing to customers comes down by even by 5%, that could have a good bearing on the demand and volumes as informed to us by some of our customers in the past month.

items.statement: Total shrimp sales volumes 2,973 MT in Q2 FY27, up 14% YoY and 13% QoQ; average realization INR874/kg vs INR870/kg YoY
items.quote: Against this backdrop, our total shrimp sales volumes grew 14% year-on-year and 13% quarter-on-quarter to 2,973 metric tons in Q2 of FY27. The average shrimp realization stood at INR874 per kilo in the Q2 of FY27 compared with INR870 per kilo in Q2 of FY26.

items.statement: H1 FY27 net revenue INR530 cr (+7% YoY), EBITDA INR51 cr (+40% YoY), PAT INR24 cr (+13% YoY)
items.value: INR530 cr, INR51 cr, INR24 cr
items.quote: H1 of FY27, the net revenue grew 7% year-on-year to INR530 crores compared with INR497 crores in the H1 of FY26. EBITDA increased 40% year-on-year to INR51 crores compared with INR36 crores in H1 FY26, with EBITDA margin expanding to 9.4% from 7.1% in H1 of FY26. PAT increased by 13% year-on-year and to INR24 crores in H1 of FY27 compared with INR21 crores in the corresponding period last

items.statement: Order book and diversified markets provide good foresight on orders; confident of reaching volume targets if supply stable
items.quote: But we definitely, with the capacities which we have in place and also the order book, which is there, we will be able to look forward. We are looking forward to reach that number for sure.

items.statement: Consumer durable margin impact expected at 50-100 bps if commodities stay at H1 levels; railway margins to rebound to normalized levels from Q2 next year
items.quote: the margin pressure witnessed are temporary in nature, and in line with our earlier guidance, we continue to expect the consumer durable to have a margin impact to the tune of 50-100 basis points, considering the commodities are constant at H1 level.

items.statement: Railway division revenue growth guidance lowered to 15-20% due to delay in future project offtakes
items.quote: On the outlook, we now expect the revenue growth of about 15%-20%, lower than the earlier expectations, mainly because of delay in future project offtakes.

items.statement: Consumer durable business growth expected in line with industry at 20-22% for FY27
items.quote: If you see, on an annual basis, we are expecting industry to grow by somewhere around 20%-22%. We are in line to that.

items.statement: Full year capex guided at INR 1,800-2,000 crores; similar range expected next year
items.quote: expected capex is around INR1,800 crores-INR2,000 crores for the full year.

items.statement: Ascent Hosur expansion to start by H1 CY27; Korea Circuit to start in CY28
items.quote: our expected timeline is to start Ascent Hosur expansion by H1 calendar year '27, and Korea Circuit will start in calendar year '28.

items.statement: Sidwal Faridabad greenfield facility operational and scaling up production capacity
items.quote: the greenfield facility for heating, ventilation, air conditioning, doors, and gangways in Faridabad is now operational and under the production capacity scale-up to support future growth.

items.statement: Sri City plant at 40% capacity utilization, expected to normalize by Q4
items.quote: the greenfield facility of Sri City has been up, but the capacity utilization is to a tune of 40%, while obviously the expense has been added over there. We are expecting that by quarter 4, it will be back to the normal.

items.statement: CD division Q2 operating EBITDA INR 4 crores; margins pressured by commodity prices, forex, wage revision, Sri City ramp-up
