items.statement: Aftermarket revenue up 20% YoY, Power Solutions up 33% YoY, Defence revenue up 66% YoY to ~INR400 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Domestic aftermarket revenue grew by 20% year-on-year. Revenue from the Power Solutions business increased by 33%, while Defence revenue, including that from our Defence subsidiary, grew by 66%, achieving quarterly revenue of about INR400 crores.

items.statement: Switch Mobility delivered 439 e-buses and 732 e-LCVs in H1 FY27; OHM fleet ~2,100 e-buses; OHM received order for 200+ e-trucks for cement distribution
items.quote: Mobility India delivered 439 electric buses and 732 electric LCVs during the first half of the year . Now, its order book stood at approximately 2,800 e-buses at the end of September 2026. OHM Mobility increased its operating fleet to around 2,100 electric buses and continues to progress towards its profitability objectives. OHM has also received an order of deploying over 200 trucks for cement di

items.statement: Geopolitical crisis in West Asia creating logistics, shipping, freight cost and transit time challenges for GCC operations
items.quote: The continuing crisis in West Asia continued to create significant logistics and operating challenges, particularly in relation to shipping availability, freight costs, transit times, and operations connected with our Ras Al Khaimah facility.

items.statement: Commodity inflation (steel, natural rubber, forex, fuel, conversion costs) pressuring margins; Q3 FY27 also expected to be bad for inflation
items.quote: Right now, it seems that quarter three would also be a bad quarter in terms of inflation. We are already seeing some signs of that, especially on the steel side and natural rubber side.

items.statement: Demand remains robust across all segments and key end markets
items.quote: Demand continues to be robust in all the segments across our key end markets, and we have sustained order execution supporting year-over-year revenue growth.

items.statement: Expect demand across key end markets to remain resilient; geopolitical uncertainty and commodity inflation to persist near term
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect demand across our key end markets to remain resilient. Persistent geopolitical uncertainty, plus commodity and inflationary pressures, are expected to continue in the near term.

items.statement: Phased pricing actions underway but lag order execution; cost increases hitting faster than price realization
items.quote: We continue to review our pricing and work very closely with our customers. One of the things that we have mentioned in the past is we are executing orders today that we have had in the pipeline for a while, and any price changes that we will make, they will take some lag for us to start realizing those prices.

items.statement: Prolonged geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain challenges creating inflationary pressures on commodity and input costs
items.quote: Amidst all of this, the prolonged geopolitical uncertainty and evolving supply chain challenges have continued to create inflationary pressures on commodity and input costs, affecting our profitability.

items.statement: Aggressively increasing QSK60 capacity with suppliers to meet global data center demand; lead times not disclosed
items.quote: We're seeing really robust demand across the world for this product. For data center demand is not just unique to India. From a Cummins perspective, we continue to work aggressively on increasing our capacity, but it's not just the capacity of the manufacturing plants. A lot of the capacity that's required is also with our suppliers, so we're working closely with our suppliers to be able

items.statement: Robust order intake and pipeline for data centers; order book strong but pricing lags due to contracted prices
items.quote: We continue to have a robust order intake, and we're excited about that. What that means, though, is that there will always be a lag versus the pricing that we have.

items.statement: Industrial sub-segment sales: construction INR131 cr, rail INR117 cr, compressor INR54 cr, mining INR49 cr, marine INR27 cr
items.quote: So, we had 131 crores in construction, rail 117 crores, compressor 54 crores, mining 49, marine 27, and the rest is defense, oil and gas, and parts.

items.statement: Approach across LHP, MHP, HHP segments based on deep customer engagement, technology, execution and service support; no specific competitive intensity disclosed
items.quote: Our approach is pretty similar across the board, right? We think that the capabilities that we have at Cummins allow us to be successful in both of those segments. So, it always starts with deep customer engagement and understanding what their needs are.

items.statement: Launched CPCB IV+ compliant 125 kVA genset; focused on cleaner power solutions aligned with evolving regulatory requirements
items.quote: We recently launched the QSK60-powered G34 and G37 genset solutions at the bauma CONEXPO INDIA 2026 and showcased our CPCB IV+ compliant 125 kVA generator set, along with a host of aftermarket solutions, highlighting our focus on cleaner power solutions aligned with India's evolving regulatory requirements.

items.statement: No major changes to capex philosophy; continue investing in sustenance, growth, facilities and safety
items.quote: From a capex perspective, I would say not major changes, right, in our philosophy. We continue to invest in sustenance, we continue to invest in growth, in our facilities, in safety.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty, commodity inflation, supply chain constraints, and pricing-cost timing mismatch are key near-term risks
items.quote: Persistent geopolitical uncertainty, plus commodity and inflationary pressures, are expected to continue in the near term. We are remaining focused on appropriate pricing actions, driving cost discipline, operational efficiency, supply chain resilience, and delivering for our customers.

items.statement: Dahej nitric acid and Gopalpur TAN projects expected to commence operations in Q4 FY27
items.quote: We expect Dahej and Gopalpur TAN project expected to commence operations in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex incurred approximately Rs 774 crores
items.quote: During the first half, we incurred approximate Rs. 774 crores of capex, reflecting steady progress on our strategic investment.

items.statement: No major growth capex beyond CCPL project; only maintenance capex planned for next year
items.quote: At this point of time, we don't have major capex projects visible, barring the CCPL which we have already announced. That's a project which is going on and will be getting completed in next few quarters. Apart from that, no major growth projects what we have with capex aligned.

items.statement: Dahej nitric acid project and Gopalpur TAN project approximately 98% complete
items.quote: On project execution, I'm pleased to report that both our projects are now in the final stage of completions. The Dahej nitric acid project and Gopalpur TAN projects are approximately 98% complete.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN plant expected to reach 75% utilization within weeks of commercial production start
items.quote: From the day we start the production, we will go up to 75% utilization in couple of weeks itself. That's the plan at this point of time.

items.statement: New plants expected to ramp to 85% quickly after Q4 and cross 95% in following year
items.quote: The new plants, we do see a quick ramp-up of those facility, like 75% in Q4 itself we are seeing, and then this ramp-up will be pretty fast, going to 85% immediately after that, and then crossing 95% in year after that.

items.statement: Dahej project adds ~300,000 tons nitric acid capacity, more than doubling current ~250,000 tons annual sales
items.quote: The Dahej project will be adding almost 300,000 tons of nitric acid. Currently, we sell around 240,000 tons, 250,000 tons nitric acid per year. So our sale of nitric acid is more than doubling.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN adds ~380,000 tons capacity, 60-70% increase over current ~560,000 tons sales
items.quote: Similarly, in TAN business, we have a capacity of currently around five or we sell around 550,000 tons, 560,000 tons. We are adding a capacity of almost around 380,000 tons more. That's 60% to 70% additional capacity which is getting added.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 22.5% from 15.5% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA was Rs. 750 crores, up 62% YoY, while EBITDA margin expanded to 22.5% compared to 15.5% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Management expects improved margin trajectory to continue in a range, not exactly 22%
items.quote: Not exactly 22%, but in a good range, it should be sustainable in a range.

items.statement: H2 typically stronger for mining chemicals as mining and infrastructure activity picks up post-monsoon
items.quote: In mining chemicals, typically the H2 is a stronger period, as mining and infrastructure activity picks up after the monsoon slowdown.

items.statement: Crop nutrition faces near-term headwinds from El Niño, raw material inflation, high industry inventory
items.quote: In crop nutrition, we do face a near term headwind emerging from El Niño effect, somewhere some raw material inflation, and some high industry inventory.

items.statement: Eastern region and Singrauli account for 55% of India's ammonium nitrate demand with higher growth rates
items.quote: From a total explosives and ammonium nitrate demand point of view, the eastern region of India and the adjoining Singrauli region in Madhya Pradesh combined, they account for 55% of the total country's demand.

items.statement: IPA realizations remain strong supported by favorable mix and higher pharma grade sales
items.quote: Importantly, realizations remain strong, supported by a favorable mix and higher pharma grade sales.

items.statement: Nitric acid pricing seeing early decent recovery
items.quote: We are also seeing an early decent recovery on the nitric acid pricing.

items.statement: Ammonia price changes passed through to market with time lag, maintaining overall profitability
items.quote: Ammonia prices do come and go, but the way we have seen the business is we are able to pass on ammonia prices to the market and able to maintain the overall profitability to a larger extent with some time gap.

items.statement: B2C mining chemicals revenue share increased to 16% from 14% YoY, improving realization and customer engagement
items.quote: The encouraging trend is continued growth of our B2C business. B2C contributes around 16% of the segment revenue compared to 14% a year ago.

items.statement: Croptek and specialty fertilizers contribute 28% of crop nutrition revenue
items.quote: Croptek and specialty fertilizers contributes about 28% of the crop nutrition's revenue during the quarter.

items.statement: Growing pharma grade IPA acceptance in pharmaceutical and healthcare applications
items.quote: We are seeing growing acceptance in pharmaceutical, healthcare, and other niche applications.

items.statement: Crop nutrition inventory buildup entirely due to Rabi season preparation and soft Kharif monsoon
items.quote: No, it is majorly, in fact, entirely it is a Crop Nutrition Business which is carrying an excess inventory, and the reason is already spoken. It is a buildup for Rabi season as well as the monsoon was soft in the Kharif season.

items.statement: Crop nutrition inventory liquidation expected to start in Rabi season
items.quote: No, we are entering into Rabi season liquidation, so this will start seeing an impact on the inventory.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 4,743 crores, net debt-to-EBITDA at comfortable 1.5x
items.quote: Net debt stood at Rs. 4,743 crores, and our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio remained comfortable at around 1.5x.

items.statement: Project capex funded 55-60% through term loans; depreciation on new plants ~Rs 180-200 crores annually on 25-year basis
items.quote: The plants are capitalized on 25 years basis. You can compute Rs. 4,600 crores on a 25-year terms. Broadly, that will be the depreciation around Rs. 180 crores to Rs. 200 crores kind of a depreciation we see on these plants.

items.statement: Chardham Chemicals manufacturing facility in Wardha, Maharashtra being revamped; commercial production expected H2 FY28
items.quote: Chardham manufacturing facility we have in Nagpur. That is true. Currently, we are revamping the entire facility, bringing up to our site and standard. We expect commercial production to start in, or we'll have a contribution will start coming from FY28. We expect this to be towards H2 FY28.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 6,590 crores up 16% YoY, EBITDA Rs 1,595 crores up 63% YoY, PAT Rs 884 crores up 93% YoY
items.quote: On similar lines, the company delivered a record H1 with consolidated revenue growing 16% YoY to Rs. 6,590 crores, operating EBITDA surging 63% YoY to Rs. 1,595 crores, and PAT rising 93% to Rs. 884 crores.

items.statement: Government removed ammonium nitrate export ban completely in October
items.quote: The Government of India has been quite kind. They have understood the situation, and the export ban has been removed as of October this year. Last month, completely.

items.statement: Recent subsidy announcement confirms government support for reasonable farmer prices and industry returns
items.quote: However, the current subsidy announcement that came in just last week, once again, we confirm the government's good support to make sure that not only reasonable prices are maintained for the farmers, but reasonable returns are also available to the industry.

items.statement: Gopalpur plant will serve existing Taloja customers in eastern region, reducing their import dependence
items.quote: And just to add to Tarun, these are not the new customers. They are the customers which we are already serving from our Taloja plant for their requirement across the countries. So, same customer. Now, our Gopalpur plants will help them to, in our domestic supply, near to their end customer.

items.statement: Demerger/IPO discussions ongoing internally; no concrete decision or timeline yet
items.quote: We are in discussion internally at management level. Just give us some more time. We will be concluding our discussion and we will inform everybody way forward how and when we are planning to do that. We will come back to you.

items.statement: Industry occupancy up 1-3% and ARR up 8-10% YoY in Q2; domestic air traffic contracted but hotel demand buoyant
items.quote: Q2 industry performance was positive both for occupancy and ARR. Occupancy was higher by 1 to 3% versus prior year and ARR grew by a healthy 8 to 10% versus last year.

items.statement: Foreign bookings reviving; expect good trend for coming quarters
items.quote: We continue to see encouraging signs of revival in foreign bookings and therefore we'll expect to see a good trend for the coming quarters.

items.statement: EIH RGI increased from 121% to 130% in Q2; 13 of 15 hotels ranked 1st or 2nd in STR benchmarking
items.quote: EIH hotels improved on MPI as well as ARI versus the competition resulting Q2FY27 Result Webinar Transcript 3 Internal in a very healthy RGI increase from 121% to 130%. 13 out of our 15 hotels are ranked 1st and 2nd in STR benchmarking

items.statement: Oberoi brand RevPAR grew 20.9% vs luxury segment 18.2% in Q2
items.quote: The luxury segment saw a growth of 18.2%, while Oberoi hotels saw a growth of 20.9% in Q2.

items.statement: Trident brand RevPAR grew 14.8% vs upper upscale segment 10.1% in Q2
items.quote: For Q2 this segment saw a growth of 10.1%, while Trident hotels had a healthy growth of 14.8%.

items.statement: Renovation impact: Oberoi Mumbai 34 keys, Trident Nariman Point 135 keys, Trident BKC 80 keys closed in Q2; Bangalore 18 keys ongoing
items.quote: Oberoi - MD & CEO, EIH Limited: Trident Nariman Point was 135 keys, that's all come back. Oberoi Mumbai was 34 keys which have all come back. Trident Bandra Kurla was 80 keys. Those were the numbers. Mr. Vineet Kapur - CFO, EIH Limited: And Bangalore is 18

items.statement: Consolidated RevPAR grew 18.3% YoY driven by ARR; occupancy fell slightly from 72% to 71% due to renovation
items.quote: Overall RevPAR grew by 18.3% versus last year mainly due to ARR growth, which compensated for a slight fall in occupancy from 72% to 71%.

items.statement: MICE share of room nights rose from 12% to 16% YoY; direct segment share fell from 48% to 45%
items.quote: Though except as a percentage share of MICE business grew year-over-year from 12% to 16%, while as a percentage the direct segment dropped from 48% to 45%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue up 16%, EBITDA up 19%, PAT up 21% YoY in Q2; positive drop-through
items.quote: Revenue growth was at 16%, while EBITDA grew at 19% and also resulted in a healthy growth of PAT at 21%. So, most of the expenses were in line with the revenue growth which also resulted in a postive drop through on the P&L for the quarter.

items.statement: Standalone revenue and EBITDA both grew 16% YoY in Q2
items.quote: This brings me to the standalone performance which also shows a strong growth in both revenue and EBITDA. Revenue and EBITDA grew by 16% in Q2.

items.statement: Capex mainly for Hyderabad land acquisition, Oberoi Grand renovation, Mumbai unit renovations
items.quote: capital expenditure was mainly related to land acquisition of Hyderabad, spending on Oberoi Grand, Q2FY27 Result Webinar Transcript 5 Internal as well as project expense for renovation at our Mumbai units, supported by a very healthy generation of cash from operations

items.statement: Owned pipeline: ~1,100 keys by 2030 including 7.63 lakh sq ft commercial in Bangalore; Managed pipeline: ~1,900 keys by 2031
items.quote: By 2030, we will add almost 1100 keys to our owned hotels portfolio, which also includes a commercial space at Bangalore of roughly 7.63 lakhs square feet. The managed hotels, we will add 1893, almost 1900 keys to the pipeline by 2031.

items.statement: Hyderabad land: freehold, just under 10 acres for 300-key Trident hotel
items.quote: So, this is a freehold land and we'll be constructing a Trident Hotel there with 300 keys.

items.statement: Oberoi Grand renovation well underway; heritage building, rooms being enlarged, inventory reducing, full public area renovation
items.quote: On the Grand, it's a historic building. And when we renovate it, our endeavor is to ensure that we maintain the heritage character of the building. What is happening there, is rooms are being made larger, room inventories coming down. And of course, it's a complete renovation of public areas including beverage.

items.statement: Bangalore Hebbal project: 1.7 million sq ft, two hotels plus commercial and retail; larger capex than renovations
items.quote: The bigger projects, of course, is Bangalore, which is 1.7 million square feet. They're two hotels and commercial space plus in retail.

items.statement: No large renovations planned in Q3/Q4; room renovations done in summer months
items.quote: We don't do renovations to the extent that we can avoid them in Q3 and Q4. So, room renovations are done during the summer months.

items.statement: Healthy foreign bookings growth in Q2; expect healthier growth in Q3; geopolitical situation a factor
items.quote: I would say in Q2, we saw an increase in our foreign bookings. And we still continue to see a much more healthier growth in Q3. That's what I would suggest at this moment.

items.statement: OFS revenue ₹150 crore in Q2, up ~20% YoY
items.quote: So, the OFS revenue was ₹150 crores in Q2, where we saw almost a healthy growth of 20% versus last year.

items.statement: Mauritius Q2 significantly better after UK travel ban lifted in early Q2; occupancy ~67%, strong ARR
items.quote: Mauritius, we've seen significantly better results in Q2. And there were some travel restrictions from the UK to Mauritius. When they were lifted, we again saw improved performance and that's reflected in the Q2 results.

items.statement: Oberoi Rajgarh Palace doing better than expected in first full season; Q3 EBITDA positive expected
items.quote: The hotel is certainly in Q3 will be EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar expansion in planning stage; not an EIH hotel
items.quote: On Bhubaneswar, there is plans to expand on the number of keys by adding more rooms, adding more space, but we'll be doing that in due course. That work has not started yet. It's still in the planning stages

items.statement: Positive on Q3 and Q4 if no unknown global events; objective to drive rates
items.quote: The market is strong and we're positive about Q3 and Q4 if there are no unknown events that happen globally. So, fingers crossed and it should be a good Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Finance cost elevated in Q2 due to one-time lease settlement for Oberoi Delhi; will normalize
items.quote: Well, that resulted in because of a settlement we had for our lease cost in Oberoi, Delhi, where we had to pay for some settlement. Where there was an increase in the lease rental and we had to pay for some settlement for prior periods. So, that is the one-timer impact which came in for Q2.

items.statement: Acquisitions always an option if suitable opportunity found; brownfield preferred for faster market entry
items.quote: As far as the cash we are holding and the possibility of acquisitions, we are always open to all options and if we find a suitable opportunity, we will absolutely look at that. Acquisitions bring many advantages, particularly if it is a brownfield or already an operating hotel because you can come to market much more quickly.

items.statement: Government order mostly completed with small residual tail flowing into next quarter
items.quote: So, government order is more or less over.

items.statement: Full-year government order of Rs 67 crore rolling into Q3 with part completed in prior quarters

items.statement: Monthly funnel of 35,000+ OPD patients and 5,500 discharges to drive app engagement and continuity
items.quote: we have a funnel of 35,000 plus OPD patients every month, plus about 5,500 discharges, which is for this quarter and it will go on increasing as we increase

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR40 cr (+35% QoQ); H1 revenue INR70.19 cr, EBITDA INR9.21 cr (13.1%), PAT INR1.9 cr

items.quote: For H1 '25, the revenue was INR70.19 crores, and EBITDA approx- INR9.21 crores, at 13.1% margin and the profit after tax is INR1.9 crores

items.statement: Equity INR63.96 cr; net debt ~INR28.5 cr (0.45x equity) as of 30 Sep 2026
items.value: INR63.96 cr equity; INR28.5 cr net debt

items.statement: H2 FY2027 average EBITDA margins expected in mid-teens with revenue growth momentum continuing
items.quote: Overall, we expect that in second half of this year, revenue growth momentum will continue, and we expect margins to improve on a quarter-on-quarter basis with H2 average margins to be in mid-teen.

items.statement: FY2027 capex guided at Rs.1,800-1,900 Crores; FY2028 capex to reduce substantially to around Rs.1,000 Crores
items.quote: So, in capex for FY2027 we expect capex of around Rs.1,800 to Rs.1,900 Crores while next year the capex will reduce substantially to around Rs.1,000 Crores.

items.statement: Ruby-Fill capacity doubling with $67M capex (CAD 94.5M, govt support CAD 23.8M), expected online H2 FY2029, targeting >20% ROCE at peak utilization
items.quote: As we announced that capex is 94.5 million Canadian dollars, of which the Government of Canada has kindly agreed to provide support of 23.8 million. We expect the capacity to come online in the back half of FY2029, and we expect a peak utilization to generate an ROCE of more than 20% on that investment.

items.statement: Spokane Line 3 at ~$20M quarterly revenue in Q2 from 13 tech transfer programs; peak revenue $80-90M expected 1.5-2 years faster than McKinsey model
items.quote: In terms of Q2, we reported that we saw approximately $20 million in revenue coming specifically from Line 3 and again, this is coming from the 13 plus projects and 5 plus customers that we have currently doing tech transfer programs.

items.statement: Spokane Line 4 build-out complete, media fills done, tech transfers of 1-2 projects expected by Q4 FY2027; 23 active RFPs for Line 4 capacity
items.quote: We have a major qualification step that we just completed this quarter, specifically media fills for our filling line on Line 4, and we are still on track to start tech transfers, tech transfers of a project or two by the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2027.

items.statement: Six new PET radiopharmacy sites: cyclotrons deployed at 5, 3 in final qualification, 2 mid-qualification, 1 cyclotron delivering; first sites online Q3 FY2028, 2-3 sites that quarter, rest in following two quarters
items.quote: We expect the first of the sites to come online in Q3 FY2028. We expect two to three sites to come online in that quarter and then we expect the other three sites to come online in the following two quarters.

items.statement: Radiopharma: Ruby-Fill growing ~35% YoY (Q2 30% annualized); signed distribution contract for leading PET product for new PET radiopharmacies
items.quote: As we look at Ruby, we have been projecting for a while that we are seeing roughly 35% year-over-year growth, and Q2 was 30% annualized again.

items.statement: Sterile Injectables: Signed Master Services Agreement with large pharma customer for one of largest global oncology products; 13 tech transfer programs ongoing on Line 3
items.quote: We signed Master Services Agreement with one of large pharma customers for one of largest global oncology products. We continue to get traction with tech transfer of new products on Line 3 with 13 tech transfer programs currently ongoing.

items.statement: H1 FY2027 EBITDA margins declined YoY due to unavailable high-margin SPECT products, negligible third-party revenue, higher opex including Montreal remediation costs
items.quote: For both Q2 and H1 of this year, our EBITDA margins declined year-on-year, primarily due to the unavailability of high-margin SPECT radiopharma products in the radiopharma business. Additionally, margins were impacted by negligible third-party revenues and higher operating expenses, including incremental remediation costs that we are incurring in our CMO Montreal facility.

items.statement: Radiopharma margins to improve in H2 as SPECT supplies stabilize from Montreal, inching toward 40% margin as SPECT normalizes; Ruby-Fill margins lower than portfolio but improving Q-o-Q
items.quote: But in H2, given that we are expecting SPECT should come back on track, particularly in Q4, that will help us improve in margins of radiopharma business. And we should be inching towards that 40% margin as the SPECT product supply is normalized.

items.statement: Sterile Injectables: Short-term margin pressure until Line 3 costs fully absorbed; margin improvement expected FY2028 as commercialization ramps; significant margin improvement FY2029
items.quote: FY2028 will be a mix of tech transfer plus commercial revenues. So, margins will improve gradually. But as commercial production happens significantly in FY2029, that is when you can expect a significant improvement in margins.

items.statement: Generics: Margin improvement expected H2 FY2027 on new product launches in Q3/Q4; long-term target 15-17% EBITDA margin reaffirmed
items.quote: On a longer-term basis, we had guided to doubling of revenue and 15% to 17% EBITDA margin in our investor meeting that we had last year in February, we continue to stand by that.

items.statement: Net debt target ~Rs.4,000 Crores by end FY2027; not expected to increase in FY2028 with lower capex and improving cash flows; net debt zero vision for 2030 maintained
items.quote: End of this year we are looking at a net debt of closer to Rs.4,000 Crores that is what we are looking at and next year, as I said, we will have significantly lower capex and if things go as plan we do not expect net debt to go up from that number.

items.statement: Successfully raised non-convertible debentures of Rs.800 Crores
items.quote: Finally we successfully raised non-convertible debentures of Rs. 800 Crores.

items.statement: Montreal facility loss >Rs.80 Crores in Q2 (remediation + opex); H1 loss ~Rs.157 Crores; cumulative loss since OAI ~Rs.357 Crores; H2 burn expected lower than H1
items.quote: So, in first half, we lost around Rs.157 odd Crores in Montreal and before that there was further loss of around Rs.200 Crores. So that is roughly the loss that we have incurred till date on Montreal.

items.statement: Spokane sterile injectables facility received VAI (Voluntary Action Indicated) status; first product approval on Line 3 without pre-approval inspection
items.quote: We received a VAI, (Voluntary Action Indicated) status again for our Spokane facility, and on top of that, we actually had our first product approval on Line 3 without a pre-approval inspection.

items.statement: MIBG pivotal registration trial OPTIMUM completed; blinded independent review on track; NDA filing expected Q4 FY2027 or early next quarter
items.quote: The blinded independent review is progressing well, and we are on track to file our NDA in Q4 of 2027 or very early in the following quarter.

items.statement: Generics growth driven by new product launches (6-8 per year, low competition focus) and maintaining/gaining share in existing products; 13 ANDAs approved since April 2024
items.quote: We continue to maintain the guidance that we have given that we will continue to launch between six to eight products each year and we continue to go with that.

items.statement: API business stable at current run rate with pricing pressure; potential improvement in FY2028 if solvent prices improve; CRAMS traction with one off-patent custom manufacturing deal and discussions with another big pharma
items.quote: So, if the situation remains as is, then we expect that API business will be stable at this run rate, but now that situation seems to be improving especially on the solvent prices side, then if that happens then FY2028 should be better for us.

items.statement: Sterile Injectables Line 3 peak revenue $80-90M expected 1.5-2 years faster than McKinsey model; Line 4 same peak revenue timeline targeted
items.quote: We are reaching peak revenue attainment of that $80 to 90 million, one and a half to two years quicker than the McKinsey models actually estimated. And we continue to stand by that projection.

items.statement: Montreal facility under OAI warning letter; remediation costs decreasing Q-o-Q by more than low-double digits; passed 90-day threshold, moving to steadier state
items.quote: We are passed that 90-day threshold, and I expect to start decreasing some of the costs associated with remediation as we now move into what I would expect is a steadier state of OAI.

items.statement: New radiopharma product approvals expected to follow 1 CRL baseline with 10-month approval timeframe (13-14 months total); guidance builds this in
items.quote: The way we think about that in terms of market standards, we should expect a one CRL sort of approval and so our guide there is we should expect one CRL on a 10-month approval time frame. We are talking about a 13, 14 months total time for approval. That is the way we expect to perform.

items.statement: Strong demand for US isolator capacity in sterile injectables; geopolitical uncertainties and market consolidation driving customer preference for US capacity; customers demanding high-quality standards
items.quote: We are seeing an increase in demand specifically for US isolator capacity, and fortunately, we can meet that demand.

items.statement: Drug discovery business seeing increased RFPs and better-than-industry win rate; revenue ramp-up expected significantly in FY2028 with green shoots from Q4
items.quote: There is increase in the number of RFPs that we are submitting and in fact, our win rate is much better than the industry. Now it is a question of converting some of that wins into real revenues and that is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Signed distribution contract for leading PET product for new PET radiopharmacies; signed deal with one of largest PET providers with committed volume deliverables
items.quote: We signed a distribution contract for a leading PET product for our new PET radiopharmacies.

items.statement: Sterile Injectables: 5+ customers and 13+ projects on Line 3; 23 active RFPs for Line 4 capacity; 51 live customer meetings at CPHI for Line 3 and Line 4
items.quote: We have 23 active proposals right now with customers for Line 4 capacity buys.

items.statement: API pricing pressure continues due to geopolitical scenario; solvent prices improving could benefit FY2028
items.quote: The API business, the pricing pressure still continues given the geopolitical scenario. So, if the situation remains as is, then we expect that API business will be stable at this run rate.

items.statement: Montreal remediation costs to decrease substantially Q-o-Q by more than low-double digits; cost optimization planned for FY2028 as production normalizes
items.quote: That remediation cost should decrease substantially, let us say by more than low-double digits Q-o-Q and we should start to see some normalization there.

items.quote: We presented clinical data of 12 patients for our novel molecule - JBI-802 at SOHO annual meet.

items.quote: From the management today, we have Mr. Priyavrat Bhartia, Managing Director; Mr. Arjun Bhartia, Joint Managing Director; Mr. Harsher Singh, CEO, Jubilant Radiopharma; Mr. Chris Preti, CEO, CDMO Sterile Injectables; Dr. Jaidev Rajpal, CEO, Generics Business and Mr. Ashish Mukkirwar, CFO Jubilant Pharmova.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 branded alcobev growth to be much stronger than H1, with significant year-on-year growth for FY27 overall
items.quote: As we said, we are growing. And we see H2 be much, much better in growth what we have grown in H1. So our growth story will continue. Overall, we should see a significant growth over the FY26 and FY27.

items.statement: Indri single malt volume guided to grow 20-22% year-on-year over next 3-4 years to reach 5 lakh cases target
items.quote: We are growing we gave a guidance that Indri should, from the base that we have created, which is fairly large, grow 20% to 22% year-on-year and which will take us to that number that the magic figure that we are talking about, in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Expect to achieve 70% capacity utilization at Chhattisgarh and 70-75% at Indri distillery by H2 FY27

items.quote: As we have entered Q3, we have seen quite an increase in demand pickup. And we envision that, that should carry on all the way through to the coming new year and the winter season.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressure from weather-related crop issues expected to ease in 6-8 months with new crop arriving in December
items.quote: These pressures are due to the weather pattern, some droughts in the South, some corn crop failing, some rice also getting marginally hit. So therefore, these will now with the new crop coming in December, should ease out for the next 6 to 8 months.

items.statement: Net realized value evens out globally despite different duty structures; US 3-tier system adds ~25% each at importer, distributor, retailer levels

The distributor will charge you about 25% and the retailer between 25% and 35%. So ultimately, it's the government duties, it's taxes or it's the margins by retailers and distributors. Ultimately, the net realized value that the company gets, even

items.quote: Yes, we do. And last year, IWSR named Indri largest Indian single malt for the second year consecutively. I don't want to give a number because everybody doesn't disclose their figures. But we are internally, our numbers say that we should be 40% of the market share.

items.statement: Sugar business demerger regulatory process underway; will communicate next material milestone via stock exchanges

items.statement: Expect double-digit revenue growth from Q4 FY27 onwards after price increases absorbed by trade
items.quote: We are definitely hopeful that now what price increase we have taken, it has been adjusted by the trade. Q4 onwards, there will definitely be a double-digit growth coming in.

items.statement: Retail channel to remain fastest growing for next 2-3 years, followed by e-commerce and modern trade, then general trade
items.quote: What we are seeing is that retail is the fastest currently growing channel for us, followed by e-commerce and modern trade, then comes general trade. I think this trend will continue for next two to three years.

items.statement: Mass category Hawaii slippers facing volume dip due to price sensitivity, but value growth continues
items.quote: As you have rightly said, there is some pressure in the mass category, which is Hawaii. There is a volume dip also. But because we have changed our portfolio mix in the other categories, that is why we are able to grow in other categories.

items.statement: Sports and sneaker footwear growing in double digits for Relaxo and overall market
items.quote: Plus, there is a good growth what we are seeing in s ports and sneaker footwear. There we have grown in double digit. So that market is growing, not only for us, but as whole the market is growing for sports and

items.statement: EBITDA margin under pressure due to raw material volatility from West Asia conflict and higher labour costs from minimum wage revision
items.quote: Maintaining profitability was challenging during the period. This was mainly due to raw material prices volatility arising from the continued conflict in West Asia, along with higher labour cost from statutory minimum wages revision.

items.statement: Margins to remain under pressure unless war situation settles; cost increases partly absorbed, partly passed on
items.quote: The increase in cost and the wage impact is being partly absorbed by us and is partly passed on to the prices. Margins are going to be under pressure. In future also, I am not seeing that unless the war situation is going to gets settled, the margins are going to be further under pressure.

items.statement: Open footwear portfolio price increase of 15-18%, closed footwear (Sparx) price increase of 6-7%
items.quote: As you know, we have talked earlier also that open footwear is around 80% of contribution to our total sales, and we have taken around 15%-18% price increase in open portfolio. Now, we talk about closed portfolio here, we have Sparx shoes in which we have taken roughly around 6%-7% price increase.

items.statement: Price increases taken across all categories gradually with 150 new articles launched to calibrate impact
items.quote: This time, we have gradually taken the price increase, not just immediately pass ed on all the price increase. We have launched around 150 new articles. So we are trying to change the product mix so that the consumer does not get hit because of too much of price increase

items.statement: Rubber prices at INR 300/kg, highest ever, remain volatile due to West Asia conflict
items.quote: For example, rubber, which has cost INR 300 kg, that is the highe st ever. It is very volatile. It is very difficult to say how will Q3 turn

items.quote: As you know, we have talked earlier also that open footwear is around 80% of contribution to our total sales, and we have taken around 15%-18% price increase in open portfolio.

items.statement: No significant capex needed for closed footwear growth as existing capacities sufficient
items.quote: No, no, we do not think a lot of capex is required. We already have good capacities with us, so capex is not required that much to grow this category.

items.statement: Production capacity recalibrated from 10.5 to 9 due to product mix shift to complex premium articles requiring more machine time per pair
items.quote: You know, it is not that we have reduced the capacity, it is only the product mix that has changed. We are launching more and more premium products which are complex, so it will require more of utilization of our machinery. We have not reduced our capacity.

items.statement: Joint venture Relaxo Kenafric Footwears Limited with Kenafric Group, INR 70 cr total investment, Relaxo 51% stake (INR 35.7 cr), manufacturing in Kenya for East Africa

items.statement: Kenya JV facility targeting 50,000 pairs/day capacity, operations starting Q1 FY28 (FY2027-28)
items.quote: Capacity we are eyeing at around 50,000 pairs per day. We are going to start around financial year 2027-2028 first quarter.

items.statement: JV to manufacture Hawaii slippers and gumboots locally in Kenya for East Africa, leveraging duty-free access under regional pact
items.quote: Whatever we are going to produce there, whether it is range of Hawaii slippers and some gumboots which have good local demand. Those products we are going to manufacture in Kenya, and we will be selling to various countries of Africa.

items.statement: Working capital days increased 10 days YoY to 144 days due to lower-than-expected volume growth and 15-20% price inflation impact on inventory valuation
items.quote: If you talk in terms of days, i t has increased by 10 days, from 134 days to 144 days. Primarily because we expected the volume growth will be there, but we could not achieve that. That is one of the reasons that you can see the inventory days have increased by 10 days

items.statement: BIS quality standards cover only 10% of industry; 90% exempt unorganized players reducing costs and creating unhealthy competition; Chinese imports rerouted via Bangladesh duty-free
items.quote: Regarding the China matter, the government has put on quality control standards, and that has only affected 10% of the industry. 90% is still exempt out of it, and rather it has affected our performance a bit because we have to comply with all those quality standards and keep our articles above those specifications.

items.statement: Sales team split into Sparx division and Hawaii/Flite division from 1st April 2026; separate distributors appointed for Sparx
items.quote: In general trade, we have divided the team into two parts. One is Sparx and the other one is the Hawaii and Flite division. This is the big thing what we have done to give more focus towards the closed and the Sparx portfolio. We are appointing distributors also in this category separately.

items.statement: Consultants engaged to guide shift from mass to premium; exclusive articles launched for e-commerce and retail
items.quote: Plus, regarding the consultant, we are always in touch with the people who guide us how to make a shift from mass to premium articles. Plus, we are launching exclusive articles in e-commerce, and in our retail shop also.

items.statement: Retail channel revenue growth 23% in H1 FY27; 51 reimagined stores delivering stronger performance
items.quote: Plus, we are getting at least 23% growth in revenue from the retail channel. So, definitely we are very optimistic about this channel and the growth happening here.

items.statement: ASP growth ~23% in Q2 FY27 driven by pricing actions across categories
items.quote: When I look at the ASP growth of 23%, I am presuming it is largely pricing and very little mix. Please correct me if I am wrong.

items.statement: Raw material volatility and war situation make Q3 FY27 margins unpredictable; rubber at all-time high
items.quote: It is still volatile, because some of the material are still going up. For example, rubber, which has cost INR 300 kg, that is the highe st ever. It is very volatile. It is very difficult to say how will Q3 turn out. Same thing as you know, war scenario, which can erupt any time

items.statement: BIS exemption for 90% of industry (MSMEs) creates uneven playing field; government unlikely to remove exemption as 90% benefit
items.quote: 90% people are exempted, so they have no interest. The government does not want to hear from the 10% of the people. When 90% of people are benefitting, w hy will they want that it should go

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 material-adjusted revenue growth guidance of 12% to 15% YoY
items.quote: Looking ahead, we reiterate our guidance of 12% to 15% material adjusted growth of FY27.

items.statement: Expects FY27 alloy-adjusted EBITDA margin around 12% and targets 1% YoY margin improvement thereafter

When we look for the adjusted alloy, 12% definitely we are going to hit in this year also. After this, there is expectation at least that I say around 1% minimum growth improvement in the margins year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Targets 14-15% EBITDA margin by FY30
items.quote: Kashish Shah: Great. So, we can achieve 14% to 15% in FY30? Vimal Gupta: Yes. Yes, exactly.

items.statement: Executable order book stands at Rs 6,700 crore as of 30 September covering FY27 to FY32
items.quote: Alicon's executable order book stands at about Rs. 6,700 crore as on 30th September, covering the period from FY'26-'27 up to FY'31-'32.

items.statement: Q2 added 8 parts from 3 customers with peak annual revenue of Rs 270 crore and lifetime ~Rs 1,000 crore over 6 years
items.quote: Around 95% of the business is from the passenger vehicle and 5% is from the non-auto. Yearly sales realization will be around Rs. 270 crore at the peak with these businesses. Annual. Over a period of, say, six years, this will give us roughly around Rs. 1,000 crore.

items.statement: ~30 new part numbers expected to start production in next 1 year
items.quote: As of now, I can tell you that around 25-to-30-part numbers are going to be newly going to SOP, from now until next one year of time.

items.quote: The industry comparison in our highlights show automotive market growth of around 19% in Q2 on Y-o-Y basis. Adjusting for the alloy price inflation, Alicon has grown by 24% Y-o-Y in Q2.

items.statement: Expects ~15% tonnage growth for full FY27

items.statement: Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA Rs 65.3 crore, up 14% YoY and 18% QoQ; EBITDA margin 10% (12.1% alloy-adjusted)

items.statement: H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA Rs 120.6 crore, up 11% YoY; EBITDA margin 9.8%

items.statement: 100% of raw material price inflation passed through to customers

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex ~Rs 70 crore (incl. Rs 40 crore leasing) against full-year plan of ~Rs 150 crore

items.statement: Semiconductor project: customer requested quotation for several 100 metric tons after technical collaboration
items.quote: Following several months of intensive technical collaboration between Carbogen Amcis Switzerland and DCAL India on a semiconductor project, the customer has finally requested quotation for an initial volume of several 100 metric tons.

items.statement: Vitamin D analogs (Calcifediol) high-margin; Halal certification at Veenendaal for Asian markets
items.quote: Also, strong VDA, vitamin D & analogues, sales with high margin, especially Calcifediol. Halal certification will be obtained in Veenendaal to access new markets, especially in the Asian environment.

items.statement: EDQM certificate of suitability granted; new US DMF and letter of authorization submitted
items.quote: Following the recent certificate of suitability granted by EDQM, DCAL has continued its regulatory filing across several countries, and it has recently submitted a new U.S. Drug Master File and the letter of authorization to support the new drug application.

items.statement: CHF 200M ECB drawdown nearing completion; first tranche ~$50M expected before Christmas or January
items.quote: We will look at least close to about 50 million as the first drawdown.

items.statement: Quarterly interest cost expected to fall to INR 20-25 crores from ~INR 40 crores after ECB deployment
items.quote: I think the quarterly interest should be coming down to around INR 20 to 25 crores.

items.statement: NCDs raised at ~10% mainly for refinancing existing NCDs and maintenance capex
items.quote: Well, the NCD is largely raised for refinancing some of the existing NCDs. So that's the major purpose as well as for certain maintenance CapEx that we need to do in India.

items.statement: H1 working capital: receivables down, payables down INR 237 crores (includes Japanese customer advance deployment), inventories up for unshipped production
items.quote: On the other side, we also saw the decrease in the trade payables. So, overall, from a working capital perspective, yes, that has shortened it. But on the other side, we also saw an increase in the inventories. So, the increase in the inventories is largely representative of the production that was done for the orders, but for which the shipments have yet not happened.

items.statement: Consolidated cash balance ~INR 1,000 crores; net debt ~$165M
items.quote: On the cash position itself, if you see, we are sitting on a cash balance of close to about 1,000 crores. On the flip side, there is also borrowings, which has also increased a bit as compared to the cash position. So, overall, from a net debt perspective, we are still sitting comfortably at close to about 165 million of net debt at a consolidated level.

items.statement: French facility Q2 revenue CHF 1M; EBITDA negative CHF 1.73M
items.quote: So, the French facility, we did a revenue of about CHF 1 million in the quarter. And we've had a negative EBITDA of roughly about CHF 1.73 million.

items.statement: Bavla FY28 full-year revenue target INR 400-450 crores
items.quote: I would say in the next financial year, for the full year, we should expect a revenue which will be in excess of INR 400 crores to INR 450 crores.

items.statement: Tech transfer pipeline annualized revenue potential ~CHF 25-30M
items.quote: So, my assumption is something around CHF 25 to 30 million.

items.statement: Biotech funding delays caused H1 revenue shortfall; AI investment diverted venture capital
items.quote: What we had seen is that some of the funding which was expected to come in was actually diverted to AI companies because of the now actually a bubble which has been created. But that funding got diverted to AI because of which these companies were not able to progress the molecule in the manner that was expected out of them.

items.statement: Revenue recognition lumpy; dependent on customer delivery schedules and regulatory filing changes
items.quote: It all depends upon when exactly the customer requires those quantities, what is the stock position, how the molecule has picked up, etc. So, overall, when I mentioned that over the medium term, what I meant was that maybe for the current financial year, the numbers might not look that great as compared to what we were expecting.
