So the regulator asked for comments and suggestions. And our association FADA has made a very strong representation on what needs to change in those draft regulations.

items.statement: New car inventory at ~35 days vs industry ~45 days; absolute inventory value higher due to price hikes and strong demand; expected to normalize in 2 months.
items.quote: If you look at the FADA announcement, they have said that the industry inventory is nearly 45 days. We are at around 35 days. So our sales has also gone up. So in absolute numbers in rupee terms, it looks higher. But this should normalize in the next 2 months or so.

items.statement: Gross borrowings rose to INR 144.5 crore; free cash flow to be used for debt repayment; inventory-driven OCF dip seasonal.
items.quote: So we will be repaying our debt with the free cash flow.

items.statement: Aftersales per-service revenue hit record INR 30,300+ in Q2; aftersales revenue grew 11% YoY despite Gujarat flood impact on 4 workshops.
items.quote: Our per service revenue has kept on rising and has reached a record INR30,000 plus this quarter per service.

items.statement: Aftersales EBITDA margin ~18% (40% gross, 18% EBITDA) normalized; Q2 margin 17.6% impacted by workshop transition overlap costs.
items.quote: We have said that the business is approximately 18% margin business, 40% gross, 18% EBITDA. This is what we in our business kind of talk about.

items.statement: OEM price hikes expected in January 2026; inventory gains from price increases hard to quantify but not unusual.
items.quote: The prices will again go up, Vijay, in the month of January. So this is something which is an ongoing thing within the industry. But we are confident about keeping our margins where it is as far as sales is concerned.

items.statement: Gujarat floods in August disrupted 4 workshops (Honda, Volkswagen, MG) for over a month impacting service volumes.
items.quote: Nearly four of our workshops were impacted because of rains and they were not operating for maybe some workshops for over a month different brands, Honda, Volkswagen, MG and all that.

items.statement: Pre-owned car partnership with OLX structured to be capital efficient and profitable; no meaningful capital deployment until model proven.
items.quote: It is going to be a very small kind of a capital over a year. And till we get the model right, there is no meaningful capital that will happen.

items.statement: IRDAI motor insurance regulation changes could impact insurance commission revenue; industry hopes for glide path similar to insurers.
items.quote: That is the hope of a lot of people in the industry, not only auto dealers, but also insurance brokers and agents and all that because there has been a glide path given to the insurance companies to meet the expense of management. So why should there be no glide path for the other matters.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 7.6% within guided 7.5%-7.8% range; Q3 growth at least 25% YoY and Q4 at least 20% YoY
items.period: H1 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: When you look at EBITDA for the H1, it is 7.6%. When you look at PAT, it is 3.7%. Every company has a legacy; every company has a future. We request that you have the faith in the management team because we are working for the shareholders only, whether public shareholders or large shareholders.

items.statement: Long-term vision of INR 20,000 crores revenue, 8% EBITDA margin and ~15% stud ratio by 2030
items.value: INR 20,000 crores revenue; 8% EBITDA margin; 15% stud ratio
items.quote: We have mentioned our vision for 2030, with a INR20,000 crores top line and 8% margin. Also, a stud ratio of 15%.

items.statement: Q2 retail revenue growth ~29%, same-store sales growth 19% in value; H1 sales crossed INR 5,000 crores; TTM sales exceeded INR 10,000 crores
items.value: 29% retail revenue growth; 19% SSSG; INR 5,000 crores H1 sales; INR 10,000 crores TTM sales
items.quote: If we look at the retail revenue growth that we have seen for Q2, which has been around 29%, the same-store sales growth continues to be strong at 19% in terms of value. The best part is that our H1 sales crossing ₹5,000 crore have also enabled us to achieve another significant milestone with TTM sales exceeding INR10,000 crores for the last 12 months.

items.statement: Dhanteras period (Oct 1-Nov 11) revenue growth 25%-26%, turnover crossed INR 2,400 crores; SSSG ~17%, diamond jewellery sales growth ~26%
items.quote: Now I will come to the numbers that we have seen in the last 41 days. So, the revenue growth that we have seen from 1st of October to 11th of November has been around 25% to 26%, and we have crossed around INR 2,400 crores of our turnover.

items.statement: Consumers preferring lighter weight jewellery, average weight range 10%-12% lower than last year; 9-carat and 14-carat demand rising
items.quote: We have seen that with the upcoming wedding season that is going to go on for November, December, January, February, the demand with this current gold prices being extremely attractive to the consumers, I can see that the footfall at the store continues to remain strong.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 4.4% due to old gold exchange (>51% of business), festive inventory build for franchisees, aggressive discounts/schemes, and 40%-50% hedging in falling gold price phase; H1 EBITDA margin 7.6%
items.quote: Another aspect that we must keep in mind for the Q2, we have seen that the EBITDA numbers have been a little on the downward trend. That is because of three, four reasons. One is that on the appeal of our honourable Prime Minister, as an industry and as a company, we have largely driven the old gold exchange program in a big way, and the percentage share of old gold as a total business that we hav

items.statement: Old gold exchange hampers margin by 20-40 bps (0.2%-0.4%) due to handling cost, melting losses, opportunity loss
items.quote: Madam, by the old gold exchange buyback, it hampers the margin by around anything between 20 to 40 bps, which is 0.2% to 0.4%, because of the cost of handling it. There are certain melting losses, and there is a little bit of opportunity loss also.

items.statement: Customs duty gain INR 16 crores in Q1 and INR 30 crores in Q2, total INR 46 crores in H1 (~90 bps of H1 EBITDA)
items.quote: We had stated a custom duty gain of around INR16 crores in Q1, and based upon the other competitive pressure, you must have heard about the market where people are doing a lot of discounts; we still had a custom duty gain of around INR30 crores in Q2. So, a total of INR46 crores, in H1, which is ~90 basis points in H1 EBITDA.

items.statement: 14 new stores opened in H1, 10 more in Oct-Nov, total 24 stores YTD vs FY27 target of 18-20; 3-4 more planned in next 3-4 months
items.quote: Retail expansion has been one of our key pillars, and within the target that we had, that for the whole year we will be doing 18 - 20 stores, I am extremely happy to announce that by the half yearly itself, we have achieved 14 new store openings.

items.statement: Inventory grew ~INR 200 crores vs March 2026 pertaining to 7 COCO stores
items.quote: Inventory grew by around INR200 crores versus March 26, which pertains to 7 COCO stores.

items.statement: Aggressive discounts, schemes and offers in Q2 to ensure growth created margin pressure; Flexi Gold and MariGold schemes driving customer acquisition
items.quote: The third thing that we have seen is that in Q2, with the overall market sentiments and the way the consumers were behaving, we have been aggressive with our discounts, schemes, and offers to ensure that we continue to grow, and that has helped us to grow.

items.statement: Hedging at ~40%-50% currently, guided by board policy; intent to increase to 65%-70% once gold prices stabilise
items.quote: No, ma'am. There is a hedging policy guided by the board, and there is a balance between price risk, the liquidity management. 50% is something that we shall continue to sustain, though our endeavour is to take it more than 50% towards 65%-70% over a period of time, once the gold prices stabilise.

items.statement: Launched titanium jewellery with gold and diamonds; Everlite brand with Wamiqa Gabbi for lightweight everyday wear; Melorra collaboration for new-age designs and omnichannel
items.quote: I would like to take this opportunity to mention that we are the first company in India to have launched titanium jewellery with gold and diamonds integrated to it, which is an international trend.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds (LGD) in 9-carat, 14-carat gold or silver seen as another segment to offer customers; stud ratio target 15%+
items.quote: This is just a share of thought that when we say that we want to take the stud ratio towards 15% and above, one thing that is happening, and we must think about it as a part of the business and all of you as analysts, that with the gold price at these current levels, what we have seen, and I want to reiterate, and I keep mentioning it in various platforms, is the demand for nine-carat, 14-carat je

items.statement: Festive period new customer acquisition +30% across markets; typical mix 40%-45% new customers, 55%-60% repeat buyers
items.quote: I also must mention, sir, using this opportunity, that during this festive season, we have seen there has been a 30% increase in terms of new customer acquisition by us as well across the markets.

items.statement: Unorganised sector driving competitive pressure through discounting aided by high duty; organised players focused on brand building and design innovation
items.quote: I will say it in two lines. It is the unorganized segment that is driving this competitive pressure. Among the organized players, we are keeping our focus on the long-term brand building and driving the growth through new store openings.

items.statement: Customer advances (Flexi Gold, MariGold) ~INR 700-800 crores on balance sheet
items.quote: If you kindly look at the balance sheet, you will find a figure of ~INR700 crores to INR800 crores, which comes from the customer, which is presented as SY and Customer Advance in our financial statements.

items.statement: Operating cash flow optically negative due to shift from gold metal loans to cash credit; would not look negative if borrowing was via GML
items.quote: Operating cash flow, if you look at, operating cash flow optically looks negative, but this was primarily on account of the gold metal loan. Had we taken our borrowing by way of a gold metal loan, this operating cash flow would not have looked negative.

items.statement: Raised commercial paper (CP) funds to support future growth; became second jewellery company in India to explore alternative funding sources
items.quote: We are very happy to say that we have become the second jewellery company in India which has explored alternative sources of funding for our future growth. As we are moving towards our cherished short-term vision of 2 billion, we will have to open this opportunity. We raised CP funds to support our future growth.

items.statement: Sustainable growth model: 10%-12% same-store sales growth + 4%-5% new store additions = ~15%-16% sustainable growth in stable gold price scenario
items.quote: No, see, we have in our business model with a flat gold price have always considered about 10%-12% same-store sales growth and about 4%-5% new stores that keep getting added. So, around 15%-16% is the sustainable growth rate that we have always been modelling in our thoughts and in our business, if there is full stability.

items.statement: H1 PAT INR 188 crores, ~22% growth; H1 PAT margin 3.7% vs guided 4%-4.5%
items.quote: But the main season, which is the Dhanteras season in Q3 and Q4, is still in hand, and we are confident that this short-term divergent trend which you are seeing in Q2, in terms of EBITDA, will be corrected in Q3. With that, and if you look at PAT level for H1, it has grown from INR153 crores to INR188 crores, almost 22% growth.

items.statement: Other income INR 99.9 crores net in Q2 primarily from hedging gains to protect cash flow from Flexi Gold/MariGold offers; described as one-off; regular FD/securities income ~INR 35-40 crores/year
items.quote: The other income pertains to the hedging position which we have taken to protect the cash flow and liquidity management. As you said, we had to take this position to protect the cash flow as we give a lot of offers to the customer through our MariGold scheme and Flexi Gold scheme ahead of And the

items.statement: Net hedging impact across Q1 and Q2 ~INR 18 crores (Q1 in other expenses, Q2 in other income)
items.quote: In statutory accounts, there were other expenses in quarter one, which was once again due to the hedge position. A part of that changed in quarter two, and there was other income. So, other expense and other income, you have to see from the accounts. So, there is net impact of around INR18 crores due to this hedging position in quarter one and quarter two.

items.statement: Promoter stake not decreased; 8,000 shares sold by employee part of personal cash flow planning, not insider trading
items.quote: not the correct way to look at it. In India, there are 6,000 companies. Many employees get the stock. If an employee sells the share, that cannot indicate that he is expecting a bad result. Employees have cash to expect. I am not speaking for others. But employees also have their cash flow planning, and they also have to manage their

items.statement: Old gold exchange program driven by Prime Minister's appeal; company supports national interest despite 20-40 bps margin impact
items.quote: However, again, I want to reinstate, madam, that we should not discourage old gold exchange in considering the current economic condition of our nation, and we have to support the vision of our honourable Prime Minister. That is why we are trying to drive it and promote it amongst our consumer base at the cost of that little bit of loss.

items.statement: HR cost increase Y-o-Y due to increments and new hiring for expansion; fixed costs based on annualised March 2026 base
items.quote: There is a small increase in the HR cost if we look Y-o-Y for quarter two last year versus quarter two this year. Primarily, we look at all the fixed costs as a base of year and month. Let's say March 26, if we take the HR cost into 12 months and then apply increment, then this variation is not there.

items.statement: Melorra collaboration for design innovation, lightweight/studded jewellery, new generation customer acquisition, and omnichannel; to operate as flanker brand/subsidiary
items.quote: There are two parts to it. One is that in terms of the design innovation and the focus on lightweight jewellery and studded jewellery. And the second is to have certain steps to acquire the new generation customers for the future. This is strategically that we want to utilize the collaboration with Melorra and also focusing on omnichannel while we are all taking our own digital and e-commerce init

items.statement: East India ~80% of revenue (West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha); pan-India expansion focus on North, West, Central, limited South
items.quote: As you understand, our market leadership is in the East. All other players, they are not East leader. Our East revenue is 80%. When we say East, West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha.

items.statement: Average sales per store potential to nearly double over next 3-4 years; growth from INR 10,000 crores to INR 20,000 crores from new stores (25-70 in 2-3 years) and existing store maturation
items.quote: The current average sales per store have the potential to nearly double over the next three to four years. The further growth from INR 10,000 crores to INR20,000 crores, a part of it will come from new stores. Let's say, 25 stores in two or three years, let's say, 70. A major part of the growth will come from existing stores with a huge potential.

items.statement: Targeting 20%+ revenue growth across both segments in FY27 and doubling operational PBT to ~Rs 200 crore
items.quote: Backed by an all-time high business development pipeline of Rs. 8,200 crores and a very steady conversion rate, we are targeting 20%+ revenue growth across both the segments in FY27.

items.statement: Aiming for 4% PBT margin by Q4 FY28
items.quote: We are committed to 4% PBT that we had earlier mentioned, and we should be reaching that in the last quarter of FY28.

items.statement: ISCS EBITDA margin target of 10.5-11% to support 4% PBT goal
items.quote: As I said, for us to reach a 4% PBT margin, we need at least 150-200 basis points margin improvement in the ISCS actually.

items.statement: GFS EBITDA margin aspiration of 4.5-5% by FY28
items.quote: In fact, we are only looking at further improving the margins from 3.9% where it is to 4.5% to 5%.

items.statement: Business development pipeline at Rs 8,200 crore, up from Rs 7,500 crore in Q1
items.quote: Our business development pipeline stands at Rs. 8,200 crore, up from Rs. 7,500 crores at the end of quarter one.

items.statement: New business revenue exceeded Rs 500 crore for third consecutive quarter (Rs 523 crore in Q2)
items.quote: In Q2, our new business contributed Rs. 523 crores of revenue across both the segments, both from new logos as well as expanding from existing customers.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 60 bps YoY to 7.3% in Q2
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA in Q2 FY27 grew by 50.2% year-on-year, with margin expanding by 60 basis points to 7.3%.

items.statement: ISCS EBITDA margin improved 50 bps YoY to 9.2% in Q2
items.quote: ISCS EBITDA margin improved to 9.2% in Q2 FY27, as against 8.7% in Q2 FY26 and 8.1% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: GFS EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% in Q2 from 2.2% YoY
items.quote: GFS EBITDA in Q2 FY27 was Rs. 47 crores at 3.9% margin, up from Rs. 15 crores at 2.2% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Gross debt increased Rs 140 crore primarily to fund working capital for GFS volume growth
items.quote: Gross debt increased by Rs. 140 crore, primarily towards funding the additional working capital to drive the significant volume growth in the GFS segment.

items.statement: Generated Rs 234 crore cash in current year, reinvested in business
items.quote: In terms of cash flow, if you really look at the current year, right, we have generated almost Rs. 234 crores of cash, which is what we have been able to reinvest in the business.

items.statement: Strong cadence monitoring DSO and DPO days; working capital investment phase due to growth
items.quote: We have a very, very strong cadence in terms of ensuring that our DSO days, our DPO days are well under control.

items.statement: ALA MENA JV formed, achieved EN 9120:2018 certification; TVS holds 51%, ALA 49%
items.quote: This JV has been formed, and the JV has achieved EN 9120:2018 warehouse certification, a very important step to develop supply chain solutions for customers in India's aerospace and defense sectors.

items.statement: Sankyu MOU signed; Sankyu intends to acquire 0.5% equity subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: As a part of the MOU, Sankyu has also expressed its intention to acquire 0.5% equity in TVS SCS, which is subject to regulatory approvals, and the regulatory approvals have already been filed.

items.statement: 100 Fortune 500 customers; large customer base reduces receivable risk
items.quote: We actually do a lot of business with Fortune 500 customers, right? 100 of our customers are there from the Fortune 500.

items.statement: Two-thirds of GFS growth driven by volumes, not rates; structural changes in lanes, supplier base, regional empowerment
items.quote: Almost two-third of the growth is built out of volumes and not rates, which means that because of the way we are able to offer customized solutions to our customers, we have won a lot of customers.

items.statement: ISCS growth in rest of world driven by better capacity utilization and new capacity additions as needed
items.quote: ISCS growth of 21% in the rest of the world is built on better utilization of our capacity, and we are also building capacity as and when wherever it is required.

items.statement: India Ratings reaffirmed IND AA rating, revised outlook from stable to positive in July
items.quote: On the credit rating front, India Ratings reaffirmed our issuer ratings at IND AA in July and also revised the outlook from stable to positive.

items.statement: Ramanan joined as Strategy and Transformation Head; Preethi appointed General Counsel
items.quote: Ramanan has joined us as Strategy and Transformation Head, who is going to lead several initiatives that we have been working on the TVS SCS four-pillar framework. Preethi is now the General Counsel of the company.

items.statement: Forex gains/losses not forecastable; actively hedged but impacted by geopolitical currency moves
items.quote: Unfortunately, we will not be able to do that. But we actively manage our forex risk, Kunal, in terms of hedging the risk and other things.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 7,022 crore (+34% YoY); EBITDA Rs 500 crore (+42% YoY); PBT Rs 82.7 crore (+91% YoY)
items.value: Revenue Rs 7,022 cr; EBITDA Rs 500 cr; PBT Rs 82.7 cr
items.quote: On a half-yearly basis, revenue grew 33.6% to Rs. 7,022 crore. EBITDA grew 42.2% to Rs. 500 crore, and PBT grew by 91.4% to Rs. 82.7 crore.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 3,687 crore (+38.5% YoY); PBT Rs 50.6 crore (+107% YoY); PAT Rs 36.5 crore (+124% YoY)
items.quote: I am very pleased to report our highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs. 3,687 crores, a year-on-year growth of 38%. Our PBT doubled to Rs. 50.6 crores from Rs. 24.4 crores in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Material costs up YoY in line with revenue; sequentially down due to business mix change
items.quote: Material-related cost went up from Rs. 446 crores to Rs. 630 crores in Q2 FY27 on a year-on-year basis, in line with the revenue growth. Sequentially, it was down from Rs. 666 crores in Q1 FY27 due to the change in the business mix.

items.statement: Freight costs up significantly due to GFS volume growth
items.quote: Freight, clearing, forwarding, and handling expenses in Q2 FY27 was Rs. 1,287 crores in Q2 FY27 compared to Rs. 727 crores in Q2 FY26 and Rs. 991 crores in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Effective tax rate ~30%, expected to remain stable
items.quote: The effective tax rate is about 30%, and it will be stable.

items.statement: ISCS growth aspiration of high double-digits to mid-teens in FY28
items.quote: Going forward in FY28, at this stage, I would not like to make a forecast, but definitely high double digits, mid-teens or high teens is something that we would aspire for the ISCS segment in FY28.

items.statement: GFS growth >20% achievable for next two quarters; 70-80% growth not sustainable
items.quote: We may not be able to achieve 70%-80% kind of a growth, but as I mentioned, greater than 20% growth definitely achievable for the next two quarters.

items.statement: Operational PBT FY26 base ~Rs 97 crore (excluding InvIT gain and exceptional items)
items.quote: Operational was close to about Rs. 97 crores last year.

items.statement: EEI segment full-year FY27 guidance maintained at 20-25% top-line growth, INR140-150 crore adjusted EBITDA and INR95-100 crore PAT
items.quote: We remain committed to our earlier guidelines of targeting 20% to 25% growth in the EEI segment, which we have already delivered or over-performed on that segment in FY27, subject to evolving market environment.

items.statement: Lumel Alucast (HPDC) guided to breakeven EBITDA (+/-1-2%) and PAT loss of INR10-15 crore for FY27
items.quote: We expected HPDC, that is High-Pressure Die Casting business, Lumel Alucast to remain a drag to bottom line while maintaining a breakeven EBITDA. This is also our commitment to get it close to plus/minus 1% of at the EBITDA, 1% to 2% of the EBITDA. The business is likely to report a PAT level loss between INR10 crores to INR15 crores by year-end.

items.statement: EEI segment FY28 top-line growth guidance expected to be similar at 20-25%
items.quote: So that's again, we will announce those after end of maybe in the last quarter. But more or less, the guidelines will be similar. So 20% to 25% on the top line is what we will commit.

items.statement: EEI adjusted EBITDA margin expected to close FY27 at 20-22% due to product mix shift toward solar and EMS
items.quote: I would say 20% to 22% is where we should be closing the year for EEI.

items.statement: Lumel Alucast at operating breakeven in H1 FY27; target double-digit EBITDA margin over time
items.quote: Though profitability remains an area requiring close attention, we remain at operating level breakeven in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Strong order book across all EEI geographies; no dip seen except seasonal European slowdown in Dec-Jan
items.quote: And at the moment, our all EEI segments, whether it is in India or Lumel in Poland or USA, U.K., China, we are having healthy order book, and we are doing good. So there is no particular dip we can see.

items.statement: Long-term demand outlook constructive driven by electrification, data centers, renewables and grid modernization
items.quote: The long-term demand outlook remains constructive. The global electricity demand is expected to grow substantially, driven by industrial electrification, electric mobility, cooling requirements and rapid expansion of data centers.

items.statement: Nashik capacity expansion largely commissioned; incremental capex of INR10-20 crore per year for SMT lines and automation
items.quote: 1 is the big capital allocation of building those 2 buildings is almost done, and there will be some incremental capital allocation in terms of, as we start using more and more space there adding new SMT lines, etcetera, maybe about INR10 crores a year, INR10 crores to INR20 crores a year we can do year after year.

items.statement: New solar inverter production line commissioned with capacity of 400 units/day (~12,000/month) on single-shift basis
items.quote: We have commissioned a new production line with a capacity of 400 inverter units per day that translates into about 12,000 a month, providing a manufacturing base to support growth and as the demand develops.

items.statement: EEI margin dilution from growing solar inverter (10-15% contribution margin) and EMS businesses vs traditional 50-60% margin products
items.quote: For example, contribution level margins for some products may be 50%, 60%, which we sell traditionally. And some products could be like the solar inverters will be 10%, 15% because that's the market, that's the price at which these products are being sold and EMS will be around the same.

items.statement: Commodity cost inflation (copper, polycarbonate, PCB, silver, steel) pressuring gross margins; pass-through to customers delayed by contract terms
items.quote: Also, the cost of commodities are, I mean, you guys are in the market, you must be tracking all the cost of commodities like polycarbonate material, which is used for housing of all our products, and you have got copper, which is used in all the current transformers and a lot of those things. Then PCB material, silver, a lot of those commodity materials have been steadily going on, and we also try

items.statement: US business grew 100% despite absorbing part of tariff costs to retain customers
items.quote: Now it's growing very well. But in between, they booked very heavy duties. Even now they've not removed, although they removed the 100% duty which they imposed on India. But we didn't want to lose the market. So there was a very conscious decision to support that business and to support those customers. Some part, the customers paid, some part we absorbed.

items.statement: Lumel Alucast has RFQs and customer programs at commercial negotiation stage adding EUR2-3 million annual turnover
items.quote: A few of them have come closer to signing up now. So that is like adding annual turnover of EUR2 million to EUR3 million, which will take away our headache of bothering about making losses from next year onwards.

items.statement: International EEI growth: Lumel Poland +24.8% YoY to INR1,338M (39% of EEI EBITDA); US 2x, UK +38%, China +25% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Lumel SA in Poland delivered, which is the EEI business delivered a strong performance in H1 FY27 and achieved a revenue growth of 24.8% year-on-year, reaching INR1,338 million. It delivered adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.9%, almost 22% despite a relatively subdued European industrial environment and contributed INR293 million, almost INR300 million. That is 39.1% of overall EEI adjusted EBITDA, alm

items.statement: Consolidated net cash and equivalents of INR1,698 million as of 30 Sep 2026; net debt-free
items.quote: On the consolidated level, we remain net debt-free with a strong balance sheet. The net cash and cash equivalents as on 30th September 2026 stands at INR1,698 million.

items.statement: Actively evaluating inorganic growth opportunities with strategic fit; will announce if material
items.quote: But we are also potentially looking at some inorganic growth opportunities also. So they could be there, but we will not want to just add numbers to our sales. It has to have a strategic significance for our business.

items.statement: Promoter denies stake sale rumors; share price moved from INR850 to ~INR600 on speculative reports
items.quote: People are really making money and you see where they took the share and what it is today. So I think people have a vested interest in what they are doing. I don't want to comment on that. But when something happens, I assure you, I will be the first 1 to come and inform you if something ever happens.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (West Asia) increasing energy, freight, insurance costs and input material availability/pricing
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions, particularly around West Asia have increased volatility in energy, freight and insurance costs and affected the availability and pricing of certain input materials.

items.statement: Electronic component supply constraints: longer lead times and availability issues due to geopolitical choke points
items.quote: the geopolitics has really decreased the availability of electronic components. So it's a small problem. We are fighting. Delivery times have gone up. Availability itself is a problem.

items.statement: EEI segment H1 FY27 revenue INR3,255M (+29.3% YoY), adjusted EBITDA INR750M (+29.9% YoY), PAT INR497M (+32.2% YoY)
items.value: INR3,255M revenue; INR750M adj EBITDA; INR497M PAT
items.quote: During H1 FY27, EEI contributed 79.2%. That's almost 80% of consolidated revenue. This is also our focused effort to improve more sales on EEI. And this is achieving INR3,255 million, up by almost 30%, to be precise, 29.3% year-on-year. So the EEI growth is 29.3% year-on-year. And the adjusted EBITDA was INR750 million, up by 29.9%. That's almost 30%, while PAT increased from 32.2% to INR497 milli

items.statement: Lumel Alucast H1 FY27 revenue INR855M (-36.6% YoY), adjusted EBITDA -INR32M, at operating breakeven
items.quote: At Lumel Alucast, we continue to execute the transformation plan with discipline as communicated earlier. Our strategy is to prioritize profitable business rather than pursue volume and do not provide sustainable returns. The revenue declined by 36.6%. That's why at a consolidated level, you find only ~6.5% growth, but this was deliberate and reached INR855 million in H1 FY27, on track to our annu

items.statement: Solar inverter portfolio expanding: 1-5kW iUNO launched, 3-phase iNEO up to 12kW, development underway up to 50kW and hybrid inverter solutions
items.quote: Further, the 3-phase iNEO range with the models up to 12 kilowatts have broadened our offering. Development of products up to 50 kilowatts and hybrid inverter solution is underway, positioning us to address a wider range of residential and commercial applications, including integrated solar and battery systems.

items.statement: Focus on working capital discipline, inventory planning, and cash discipline amid supply chain volatility

items.quote: We have signed multiple marquee names, including R Systems, Kerala Fibre Optic Network, Vivo Mobiles, Amar Ujala, Jubilant Pharmova, APAC Financial, Vikram Solar, SBM Bank, RPG Enterprises, amongst others.

The entire load is now managed by just three people, where earlier 15 people were used, freeing up significant bandwidth and resource cost.

items.statement: Achieved positive operating cash flow at standalone and consolidated level in Q2 FY27
items.quote: On the operating cash flow, I am very happy to announce that we have achieved a positive operating cash flow, not only at a standalone basis, but also at a consolidated basis for Q2 FY27.

items.statement: 25% of customer base in major metros comes from smaller cities; luxury buyers prefer shopping in major metros for wider choice
items.quote: Close to 25% of our customer base is coming from smaller cities and towns. This is something that we have experienced over time.

items.statement: Proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries into Stanley Lifestyles Limited to simplify structure and improve coordination
items.quote: We are progressing with the proposed amalgamation of our subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries into Stanley Lifestyles Limited. The objective is to create a simpler and more integrated corporate structure.

items.statement: Ex-company secretary arrested and confessed to financial fraud; Rs 2.83 crore exceptional charge taken; potential recovery in Q3
items.quote: Good news to the shareholders is we were able to arrest the ex-company secretary who was involved in this financial fraud, and he has confessed to the police, and we are in the process of recovering that. Whatever the charge you have taken, there is a potential to get reversed in the Q3.

items.statement: Cash position strong at ~Rs 170 crore after large-format store investments; disciplined capital allocation maintained
items.quote: Our cash position remains strong even after the significant investments we have made in our large-format store openings. We have been selective about where we commit capital and have managed our cash carefully as we expand.

items.statement: No current share buyback plans despite cash reserves and stock at all-time low; management will consider
items.quote: currently we do not explore that. Of course, we will consider this, and we do explore this, and we will get this buyback done.

items.statement: Imports declined 6% YoY in H1; strategic sourcing under best-cost country model and localization underway
items.quote: Our imports declined by 6% year-on-year during the half year. At the same time, we are reviewing our brand and retail architecture to ensure that our store formats are aligned with the markets and the customer segments they serve.

items.statement: Order book robust at Rs 60 crore but invoicing delayed due to project handovers; conversion cycles extended
items.quote: Order book position has definitely improved, but the time taken for completion of the invoicing is slightly delayed because the project handovers are there.

items.statement: First international store opened in Colombo, Sri Lanka via partnership with Singer Sri Lanka PLC
items.quote: we entered our first international market with the opening of Stanley Boutique in Colombo, Sri Lanka. This has undertaken through a strategic partnership with Singer Sri Lanka PLC

items.statement: ~800 furniture retailers in India, ~80% depend on imports for leather sofas/recliners; QCO inclusion could shift demand to domestic suppliers like Stanley
items.quote: most of our competitors, if you look at the pan-India space, close to about 800 retailers of furniture, out of which almost 80% of them mostly depend on imports for these kind of products, especially leather sofas and recliners.

items.statement: Residential project handover delays across country affecting furniture purchase timing; RERA delays creating pipeline backlog
items.quote: there have been massive delays if you really look at RERA and understand. There has been a lot of delays in project handovers across the country. A lot of projects that are sold are still in the pipeline, and there are delays

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 13% to 15% for FY27
items.quote: We expect our revenues to grow between 13% to 15% for the entire year and are on track to achieve a INR1,000 crores mark by the end of financial year '28.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 10% to 11% for H2 FY27
items.quote: Over the next two quarters, on an average, we believe we will be delivering around a 10% EBITDA margin, anywhere between 10% to 11% is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach INR1,000 crores revenue by FY28
items.quote: We aspire to reach the INR1,000 crores revenue milestone by FY28.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% from 10.3% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins improved to 11.9% from 10.3% in the previous quarter, while PAT grew 21.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 11.2%
items.quote: For the first half, EBITDA stood at INR497.98 million, with a margin of 11.2%.

items.statement: Completed 1.58 million trips in Q2 FY27, up 15% year-on-year
items.quote: We completed approximately 1.58 million trips during the quarter, up 15% year-on-year, and close to 7% sequentially.

items.statement: H1 FY27 trips crossed 3 million, up 21% year-on-year
items.quote: For the first half of the year, we crossed 3 million trips, representing growth of almost 21% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Fleet size at approximately 20,500 vehicles as of September 30, 2026, up 12% year-on-year
items.quote: Our owned and vendor-operated vehicle network approximately 20,500 vehicles as of September 30, 2026, up about 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: EV fleet increased to 475 vehicles from 460 at end of Q1
items.quote: Within this broader supply ecosystem, our EV fleet on the network increased to 475 compared with 460 at the end of Q1.

items.statement: Vehicle capex planned in INR35 crores to INR45 crores range
items.quote: Our vehicle capex would remain in the INR35 crores to INR45 crores range as per our plans currently, with the large part being -- it would encompass all kinds of vehicles from economy to luxury to EVs, depending on the requirements of the clients as they develop over a period of time and our need to replace older vehicles.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex at INR273.90 million, largely towards vehicles
items.quote: Capital expenditure for the first half stood at INR273.90 million, largely towards vehicles.

items.statement: ETS contributed 58% of revenue, CCR contributed 42% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In terms of our business mix, ETS contributed 58% of revenue, while CCR contributed 42%.

items.statement: Management expects steady-state mix with 1-2% quarterly variation
items.quote: We think this is a steady-state mix with one or two percent up and down, which would keep happening quarter to quarter.

items.statement: Onboarded 72 new clients in Q2 FY27, active client base at 1,538, up 10% sequentially
items.quote: We had another healthy quarter on customer acquisition. We onboarded 72 new clients, compared with 67 clients in Q2 last year and 61 in Q1. Our active client base stood at 1,538 enterprise organizations during the quarter, up almost 10% sequentially.

items.statement: 50% of revenue from customers associated for more than five years
items.quote: Around 50% of our revenue continues to come from customers who have been associated with ECOS for more than five years.

items.statement: Cost of service improved to 74.2% of revenue from 75.1% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Coming to our cost structure, our cost of service stood at 74.2% of the revenue during the quarter, compared with 75.1% in Q1 FY27, reflecting an improvement over 100 basis points

items.statement: Employee costs reduced to 10% of revenue from 11.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: As a percentage of revenue, employee costs reduced to approximately 10% from 11.2% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Trade receivables at INR1,114.56 million, representing 46 days of revenue
items.quote: Trade receivable stood at INR1,114.56 million as of September 30, 2026, comparing with INR1,070.21 million as of March 31, 2026. This represents approximately 46 days of revenue.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations for H1 FY27 at INR109.52 million, working capital requirements increasing
items.quote: Cash flow from operations for the first quarter stood at INR109.52 million, with working capital requirements increasing alongside growth in the business.

items.statement: Cash and investments at INR1,256.11 million including INR243 million mutual fund redemption initiated
items.quote: Our cash and investment stood at INR1,256.11 million, which includes a mutual fund amounting to INR243 million from which the redemption request was initiated.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with net worth of INR2,826.69 million
items.quote: We remain debt-free, with a net worth of INR2,826.69 million as of September 30, 2026.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR2.38 per equity share for FY26 approved at AGM
items.quote: As a part of our capital allocation approach, the final dividend of INR2.38 per equity share for FY26 was approved by shareholders at Annual General Meeting held on September 21, 2026.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high in ETS segment, especially large contracts; competitors bidding at loss-making prices
items.quote: Yes, especially in the ETS segment, what we are seeing is that competitive intensity, as you call it, is still there, especially in the larger contracts, where if you go last time, we had said that we're going to set certain pricing thresholds below which we will not go. And if other competitors are willing to look at a loss, just to built a top line, so it's their strategy.

items.statement: Vendor supply may shrink due to unsustainable pricing by competitors squeezing fleet owners
items.quote: No, absolutely. I think you just hit the nail on the head right there. And this is how cycles play out. So, a highly competitive intensity like this would be followed by unsustainable business model at the last mile, which is the unit economic basis, and which would be followed by lesser investments by -- in the supply chain into cars, and which would again then result in a lower supply.

items.statement: AI adoption started 3-4 months ago with 8-10 projects running, Microsoft Dynamics ERP deployed last month
items.quote: We started that journey around 3 or 4 months back. And we have been -- so we have an AI champion highly qualified within the organization who is going department-by- department and reviewing all processes, automating them, whatever is feasible to be automated, linking them to a lot of things to our core ERP. ECOS (INDIA) Mobility and Also, of course, we have just deployed our new Microsoft Dynamic

items.statement: B2C app launched in beta testing on Android and Apple Play Store
items.quote: We have also, with the technology, we have launched our B2C app. I would encourage everybody to go and check it out and test it out. It's in the beta testing stage listed on Android and the Apple Play Store.

items.statement: Operating footprint expanded to 160 cities, adding 9 new cities in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We ended Q2 with a presence across 160 cities in India, adding nine new cities.

items.statement: Employee count stable over last 6 months after 33% increase in FY26
items.quote: But if you look at the last 6 months, we have not seen any much of an increase in our employee count.

items.statement: Trip volume growth of 15% YoY in Q2 FY27 and 21% YoY in H1 FY27
items.quote: We completed approximately 1.58 million trips during the quarter, up 15% year-on-year, and close to 7% sequentially. For the first half of the year, we crossed 3 million trips, representing growth of almost 21% over the same period last year.

items.statement: Maintains mid-teens revenue growth guidance with stable EBITDA margins
items.quote: As of now, no revision in guidance. We continue to maintain our guidance of mid-teens revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Targets aerospace and defense to contribute upwards of 10% of revenues in medium term
items.quote: In the medium- term, we are looking at upwards of 10% of revenues contributing from aerospace and defense, and that is the target that we are aiming for.

items.statement: Aims to reach high teens ROCE over next couple of years
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain focused on further improving our ROCE with an ambition to reach high teens over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Won maiden order from ecosystem of largest American smartphone manufacturer for precision tooling and fixtures
items.quote: Perhaps the most exciting development this quarter has been our entry into the ecosystem of one of the largest American smartphone manufacturers with our maiden order for precision tooling and fixtures.

items.statement: New Dharwad facility for commercial vehicle OEM to supply complete chassis assemblies, peak revenue INR 1,500-2,000 million annually
items.quote: At peak capacity, we expect this facility to generate annual revenues of INR 1,500-2,000 million.

items.statement: New Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar facility for three-wheeler body and chassis assemblies, peak revenue INR 1,000-1,200 million annually
items.quote: At peak capacity, we expect this facility to contribute approximately INR1,000-1,200 million in annual revenue.

items.statement: New sheet metal order from largest European passenger vehicle OEM for India operations at Pune facility
items.quote: The second is a new sheet metal order from one of the largest European passenger vehicle OEMs for its India operations. This program will be serviced from our Pune facility.

items.statement: Onboarded sixth OEM customer in proprietary suspension business, supplies commenced Q3 FY27
items.quote: First, we've onboarded our sixth OEM customer in this segment, one of the largest premium two-wheeler manufacturers based in South India, and supplies to them have already commenced as of Q3 FY27.

items.statement: Secured additional suspension orders from fast-growing South India two and three-wheeler OEM for two models, production Q4 FY27
items.quote: Second, we've secured additional orders from a fast-growing two and three-wheeler OEM in South India, covering two of their models. We've scaled up our capabilities to support these programs, and production is expected to commence in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Working with all top 10 two-wheeler OEMs and 12 of top 15 passenger and commercial vehicle OEMs
items.quote: For example, in the two-wheeler OEM space, we're working with all of the top 10 two-wheeler OEMs, and in the passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle OEM space, we're working with, I think, 12 out of the top 15 passenger and commercial vehicle OEMs.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 12.0% in Q2 FY27, manufacturing EBITDA margin at 13.5%
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR3,306 million, with margin at 12.0%. Last quarter, we had indicated that the worst of the cost pressures were behind us, and we are pleased to report a return to stable margins this quarter.

items.statement: Trading business margins under pressure but cost pressures largely behind, expect normalcy in next few quarters
items.quote: Trading business margins are seeing a bit of pressure. We do feel that the cost pressures seem to be largely behind us, and we expect some return to normalcy over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Expects continued reduction in capital expenditure as percentage of revenue to drive ROCE improvement
items.quote: First, a continued reduction in capital expenditure as a percentage of revenue.

items.statement: Dharwad facility ramp-up slated for Q1 FY28 for commercial vehicle chassis assemblies
items.quote: Firstly, we are pleased to announce a new manufacturing facility in Dharwad for one of India's leading commercial vehicle OEMs, with ramp-up slated for Q1 FY28.

items.statement: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar facility for three-wheeler body manufacturing, production ramp-up from Q1 FY28
items.quote: For this program, we are establishing a new manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. Our teams have developed and set up the complete production line in record time, and we expect production to ramp up from Q1 FY28.

items.statement: AS9100 certification received for one India facility, enabling aerospace manufacturing ramp-up over next few quarters
items.quote: I am also happy to announce that for one of our facilities, we have already got the AS9100 certification, which is a very important certification when it comes to manufacturing of aerospace components. We feel after this certification, it is only a matter of time before our India manufacturing for this particular OEM also ramps up over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Entered consumer electronics with CNC fixtures for American smartphone manufacturer ecosystem, discussions ongoing for MLB and FATP fixtures
items.quote: We are already in discussion for additional categories, including MLB, which is main logic board fixtures, and FATP, which is Final Assembly, Testing, and Packaging fixtures.

items.statement: Licensed technology from Yamato Co Ltd for air filters, oil filters, and resin air intake manifolds for automotive and industrial OEMs
items.quote: Under the agreement, Yamato has granted exclusive rights to manufacture and sell three product lines in India, including air filters, oil filters, and resin air intake manifolds for both automotive and industrial equipment OEMs.

items.statement: Merger with Badve Auto Components applied to NCLT, expected completion end of Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28
items.quote: We have applied to the NCLT for that. I think based on our experience and based on precedences we've seen with other listed companies, we see a timeline of anywhere between six to eight months for this merger to be consummated, and we expect it to happen maybe at the fag end of Q4 FY27 or at Q1 FY28.

items.statement: ROCE improved 60 bps to 15.3% excluding unutilized QIP proceeds of INR 12,000 million
items.quote: Lastly, during the quarter, we were also able to improve our ROCE by 60 basis points from 14.7% last year to 15.3%, excluding the unutilized portion of our QIP proceeds, which we expect to deploy over the coming few quarters.

items.statement: Exports contributed 4.8% of manufacturing revenue in Q2 FY27 (INR 1,117 million) and 4.6% in H1 FY27 (INR 2,112 million)
items.quote: Exports contributed 4.8% of our manufacturing revenue in Q2 FY27, that is INR 1,117 million.

items.statement: Consumer electronics fixtures are highly recurring, changing with every model and variant every few months
items.quote: No, these are highly recurring, so they change with every model and every variant of every model as well. In fact, there is a change that happens every few months, not even every year.

items.statement: Aerospace growth to be mix of organic and inorganic, using hub-and-spoke model with UK/Europe hub and India cost base
items.quote: We intend to use a hub-and-spoke model, with the hub, of course, being the UK and Europe, where we have the complete R&D and marketing, and then India being the best cost base for us, where we can utilize India's superior and strong engineering base, our very frugal labor costs, as well as the overall ecosystem that we have when it comes to metal forming.

items.statement: Trading business share intentionally declining, focus remains on manufacturing business growth
items.quote: That is definitely intentional. I think our focus definitely remains on the manufacturing business. I think the trading business is playing quite well into our manufacturing business with the insights we're getting into commodity prices. But I think it's fair to say that the manufacturing business's share will continue to grow going forward.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guided at INR225-230 crores due to new facility delay
items.quote: Around INR225 crores to INR230 crores.

items.statement: FY28-29 full capacity revenue guided at INR550 crores
items.quote: But in 2028-'29, you will see the full impact of the new capacity. That means we'll be in the range of INR550 crores.

items.statement: New facility revenue contribution guided at INR300-350 crores annually
items.quote: New facility would be between INR300 crores to INR350 crores.

items.statement: FY27 new facility revenue guided at INR25-40 crores
items.quote: This year will be very optimum, maybe 25 to 40 -- between INR25 crores to INR40 crores depending on how fast we can start.

items.statement: Target INR1,000 crores turnover by 2030
items.quote: But we have a target that in another 3 years' time, we should be able to achieve INR1,000 crores. That is my target, by 2030.

items.statement: Capex remains at INR130 crores for new facility
items.quote: Capex remains same at that place only.

items.statement: Investment of INR100.49 crores in new manufacturing facilities and production lines
items.quote: First, expanding our technological capabilities with an investment of INR100.49 crores in the new manufacturing facilities and production lines along with enhanced automation to drive operational efficiency and cost competitiveness.

items.statement: New facility adds 13,109 metric tons/year plastic food containers and 7,696 metric tons/year paper products
items.quote: Our plant capacity after expansion includes an additional 13,109 metric tons per year of plastic food containers through both injection as well as thermoforming processes, taking our total food container capacity to 21,095 metric tons per year, along with a new paper products capacity of 7,696 metric tons per year.

items.statement: Injection molding to start January 2027, thermoforming and paper products by April 2027
items.quote: The new facility, we are planning to start injection molding by January, and gradually start the second one, starting is thermoforming and then the paper products. So we hope to complete process setting and start production by this April 2027 in all the three divisions.

items.statement: Full capacity utilization expected by September-October 2027 (H2 FY28)
items.quote: We, let's say, start in '27, we will take about 5 to 6 months time to stabilize the total production capacity. So by September, October, you can expect that we'll be full in stream.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 18-19% despite raw material cost increase
items.quote: See, in absolute numbers they have gone down, in percentage maybe there is a squeeze of 1% or 2%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain 18-19% at full capacity (INR550 crores revenue)
items.quote: If it touches 19%, it is a bonus for us. On the most optimistic side, I put always 18%.

items.statement: Absolute EBITDA of INR95-100 crores expected to remain intact regardless of raw material prices at full capacity
items.quote: That 90, 95 figure or even up to 100 figure does not change whether the raw material prices go up or down.

items.statement: Selling prices increased ~35% (from INR200 to INR260-270) as raw material rose from INR100 to INR160
items.quote: See, basically before the Gulf War, Middle East War, the raw material prices were around INR100. Today it is ruling around INR160. So there's an increase of INR60. So let's say, earlier we were selling at INR200, today we are selling at INR260 to INR270. So there is about 35% jump in the pricing.

items.statement: Pricing passes through both ways - increases and decreases with raw material costs
items.quote: Yes, Aniket, it's both ways. It doesn't work only one way, it is both ways. Aniket Nikumb: Right? Lalit Agrawal: When increasing, it is increasing. When going down, it will also go down

items.statement: Multi-sourced raw materials to reduce single-supplier dependency amid Gulf region issues
items.quote: We have not faced any raw material -- of course there was a shortage, but we planned it so well by importing and by multiplying our resources for the supplying. So instead of depending on one source, we multiplied the resources so that if one is not available, we have from the second source, if second is not available, we have from the third source or fourth source.

items.statement: Entering paper cups and paper food containers to offer full paper packaging range to existing customers
items.quote: In the paper we will be making both paper cups as well as paper food container, food packaging products. So it will be entire gamut of paper packaging including paper cups.

items.statement: Adding in-mold labeling (IML) capability for value addition and margin improvement
items.quote: Like in the new project, we'll be going for in-mold labeling, so that can increase the margin per piece. So that way we have to keep -- like we are importing a lot of printing machines where we can do value-added service to our customers, good quality printing.

items.statement: Same customer base and channel for thermoforming and paper products as existing injection products
items.quote: Same customer. Actually, it also goes for food packaging, but they are not competing products to injection. Like, the thermoforming products can go for the fruit packaging, for bakery packaging, then for the namkeen packaging, also for food meal trays packaging, where injection becomes little expensive.

items.statement: Target export share increase from 26% to 35%, with focus on Europe and North America
items.quote: Our target is increase the export base to around 35%. Like in the food segment, if you talk about thin wall food container, we export almost 50%.

items.statement: Major export markets: Europe, USA, Australia; new inquiries from Canada and Mexico
items.quote: Isha, we already export to most of the developed countries like Europe, entire Europe, we are exporting, USA, and Australia. Now, the major thrust will come mostly from Europe and when we expand the capacity, because these are the two areas where we find major market possibilities or opportunities.

items.statement: Term loan to be INR55 crores (INR5 crores existing + INR50 crores new) repayable over 7 years at 8-8.5%
items.quote: That is very comfortable because our current term loan is almost negligible. So, having a term loan of only -- let's say, today we are sitting -- by end of the year we'll be sitting at only INR5 crores term loan from the existing loans, plus another INR50 crores term loan from the banks. So total term loan will be INR55 crores, repayable over next 7 years.

items.statement: Working capital liability at INR80 crores; cost of working capital debt 0.2-0.25% lower than term loan
items.quote: See, total liability, if you look at it, it's mainly for the working capital. Today working capital liability is standing around INR80 crores.

items.statement: No current plans for further capital raise
items.quote: Right now we have no plan. We have not made any plan. But if it is there then we will have to look into the facts and figures. Until now we have not planned anything.

items.statement: FY29 PAT guided at INR50-55 crores on INR550 crores revenue with 18% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So we can expect PAT between anywhere between INR50 to INR55 crores when the full revenue is realized.

items.statement: Depreciation to increase from INR7 crores to INR17-18 crores annually after new facility
items.quote: Existing depreciation is about INR7 crores per year. And when we implement this project then there will be addition of about INR10 to INR11 crores in depreciation, so about INR17 crores to INR18 crores depreciation.

items.statement: Return on capital presumed not below 15% at steady state
items.quote: But I presume, it will not be below 15%.

items.statement: Project delayed 6 months due to elections, government machinery slowdown, and severe monsoon (30% excess rain in West Bengal)
items.quote: See, the delay was mainly because of first it started delay because of the election, SIR process, and then after election the government machinery, they stopped, almost non-functional. And then came the monsoon, and this time in West Bengal monsoon was very severe, and there was excess rain of 30% in West Bengal as compared to minus 12% deficit in all over India.

items.statement: Raw material prices stabilizing after October; may cause marginal revenue reduction but not affect absolute profitability
items.quote: Now the prices are almost stabilized, like in October. In fact, October activity is always low because the festival season, we lose a lot of production because of the holidays in Calcutta. We have Diwali holidays, but that was in November this time, Puja holiday. But now the prices of raw material has started coming down a little bit. So there will be in the revenue terms, there may be a marginal

items.statement: Plan to migrate from SME to main board listing after 3-year requirement (post July 2028)
items.quote: Yes, of course. After 3 years, when it is finished, then we can plan for the listing on the main board.

items.statement: Subsidiaries Glen Realty (dormant) and Glen Paper Products (trading activity started) retained for future use
items.quote: Eventually we implemented in the existing project, so we will see whether we can do any further activity in Glen Paper Products. We already started some trading activity in Glen Paper Products, but GRPL, Glen Realty, is practically dormant right now. So whatever infrastructure development for our group, we want to put into the Glen Realty.

items.statement: India solar capacity must triple to 509 GW by FY36; PM Surya Ghar added 7 GW in H1 FY27; data center capacity to grow 4x to 6 GW by 2029
items.quote: The Central Electricity Authority expects peak power demand to rise from 289 GW to 459 GW by FY36. To meet this, India's solar capacity must roughly triple from about 170 GW today to 509 GW.

items.statement: Q2 order inflow 1.7 GW, more than double Q1; key accounts 1.3 GW, mid-market 400 MW; closing order book 8.2 GW after removing 1 GW US orders
items.quote: Order flow at 1.7 GW was more than double the previous quarter. Our key accounts business brought in 1.3 GW, and our mid-market segment, which was set up two quarters ago, added 400 MW.

items.statement: Closing order book stands at 8.2 GW after removing 1 GW of US export orders due to Section 232 duties
items.quote: As a result, 1 GW of U.S. export orders, which we were carrying in our order book, is no longer viable. We have removed these orders, and our closing order book stands at 8.2

items.statement: EBITDA per watt rose 37% QoQ from INR1.25 to INR1.71 driven by richer mix; distribution share rose to 44% of volume
items.quote: EBITDA per watt rose 37% sequentially from INR1.25 per watt peak to INR1.71 per watt.

items.statement: Four levers for margin recovery: mix improvement, cost optimization, capacity utilization, and backward integration starting with captive cells
items.quote: We see four levers for our margin recovery. One, the mix. This has started to deliver and will deepen as distribution scales further. Second, the cost. Optimization across sourcing, logistics, and raw material yields, together with tighter inventory cycles, will deliver larger savings as volume grows.

items.statement: 9 GW TOPCon Plus cell facility on schedule; first cell out in December, sequential commissioning over 3 months, project COD March 2027; project cost INR4,500 crores
items.quote: Our 9 GW TOPCon Plus cell facility remains on schedule. We expect first cell out in December, after which the lines will be commissioned in a sequential manner over the following three months, with project COD in March 2027.

items.statement: 9 GW wafer and ingot project estimated at INR5,600 crores; serious investment starts next fiscal targeting ALMM List-III timeline; commissioning mid-FY29
items.quote: For the wafer and ingot, the present estimate for the 9 GW stands at about INR5,600 crores, within about INR620 crores per GW.

items.statement: BESS Phase 1: 7.5 GWh assembly plant equipment shipping this quarter; commercial operations Q1 FY28; cell manufacturing by 2029-30; estimated INR3,600 crores
items.quote: For the BESS 7.5 GWh, we have made an estimate for about INR3,600 crores to spend over the commissioning dates, which Sameer-ji and Arun-ji explained to us.

items.statement: Module production similar to sales at 591 MW in Q2; all four facilities fully ramped; utilization to improve significantly in Q3-Q4 with scheduled deliveries
items.quote: Similar to the sales.

items.statement: Cell line commissioning in phases: first cell out December, sequential commissioning till March, full ramp-up 4-6 months after March; full 9 GW operational by Q2 FY28
items.quote: Our first cell out will happen in December, and the lines will then get sequentially commissioned till March. Then over the next few months, sequential ramping up will happen. That ramping up typically takes four to six months, and in that timeframe, we should be fully ready for commercial production in all the lines.

items.statement: Crude oil below $90 easing freight and logistics costs; inventory from previous quarters prevented production issues in Q2
items.quote: Crude has now luckily come down to sub-90 levels. This did affect our freight and the logistics movement in Q2 to some extent.

items.statement: ALMM List-II extension for C&I clarity came July 18, delaying decisions into Q3; C&I exempt from DCR till December; ALMM List-III timeline drives wafer ingot commissioning
items.quote: Clarity on the ALMM List-II extension for C&I came only on July 18. This delayed customers' decisions and moved C&I offtake into Q3.

items.statement: US Section 232 circular August 6 introduced minimum import price and 15% ad valorem duty with enforcement deadline December 4, making 1 GW US export orders non-viable
items.quote: The U.S. Section 232 circular of August 6 introduced a minimum import price and an additional 15% ad valorem duty with an enforcement deadline of 4th December.

items.statement: Other current assets rose from INR360 crores to INR620 crores due to capex vendor advances and DCR supplier deposits; expected to convert to recovery in Q3-Q4
items.quote: On the increase in current assets, I can only assign one reason was advances being paid for the ongoing capex vendors. Also, as we move more towards DCR, the deposits and advances to DCR suppliers also come into the picture.

items.statement: Gross debt INR632 crores, net debt INR547 crores, net debt-to-equity 0.17; Gangaikondan project funded 1/3 equity, 2/3 debt; INR3,800 crores planned infusion in H2
items.quote: At the end of Q2, gross debt stands at INR632 crores and net at INR547 crores, thereby retaining the net debt-to-equity ratio at 0.17.

items.statement: H2 volumes substantially higher than H1 as 8.2 GW order book converts; EBITDA per watt to hold at Q2 levels (~INR1.71); FY28 margins to lift meaningfully with captive cells
items.quote: For H2, we expect EBITDA per watt peak to hold at around current levels, with volumes substantially higher than what we did in H1, as the order book converts.

items.statement: 60-70% of 8.2 GW order book to execute over next 12-18 months; order book primarily non-DCR currently
items.quote: Based on the visibility we have at this point of time, 60%-70% of this order book will get executed over the next 12-18 months.

items.statement: Q3 volume expected around 1 GW; H2 offtake normalizing for both IPP and C&I customers
items.quote: That would be a fair estimate to make.

items.statement: Distribution volume grew 80% QoQ from 145 MW to 259 MW; DCR volume grew 71% QoQ; distributor network expanded to 133 from 119
items.quote: Our distribution volume rose about 80% from 145 MW to 259 MW, backed by DCR growth, and we expect this momentum to continue over the next few quarters.

items.statement: IPP customers deferred offtake due to land and evacuation constraints; situation normalizing with offtake resuming in Q3
items.quote: Our IPP customers deferred offtake of existing orders because of evacuation, land availability, and other constraints they were facing.

items.statement: India added 8.9 GW solar in Q2 FY27, down 25% from 12 GW in Q1; installed base 171 GW; utility ground-mounted additions fell 31%
items.quote: India added 8.9 GW of solar capacity in Q2, down by 25% from 12 GW in Q1, taking the installed base to 171 GW as on the close of the quarter.

items.statement: Captive cell margins expected to almost double from current DCR margins using procured cells
items.quote: But yes, with our own captive cells coming in, margins will almost double from the present DCR margins of the procured cells.

items.statement: Chinese export curbs on wafer ingot equipment monitored; cell line not impacted; alternative non-Chinese technical consultant appointed to mitigate ramp-up risk
items.quote: As far as wafer ingot is concerned, we are watching this and monitoring the developments. Based on the final outcome of those developments, we will take our decisions.

items.statement: Safeguard duty receivable INR150 crores withheld by customer; consultants hopeful of resolution sooner; will update on progress
items.quote: With regard to the specific question on the safeguard duty for INR150 crores, that is something which we have been following up. Consultants and our advisors are hopeful of closing that sooner.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 18% YoY to INR2,641 crores; volume rose 3% to 1,596 MW; realization up 15% from richer mix and higher DCR share
items.quote: For H1 2027, revenue grew 18% year-on-year to INR2,641 crores, while volume rose 3% to 1,596 MW. The difference is realization.

items.statement: FY27 capex spent INR1,700 crores till date; FY28 major spending INR3,800 crores for cell plant; FY28-29 for wafer ingot and BESS
items.quote: FY27, up till now, we have spent about INR1,700 crores. The major spending in FY28 will happen towards the cell plant capex for about INR3,800.

items.statement: BESS assembly plant equipment undergoing factory acceptance tests; shipping this quarter; stabilization next quarter; commercial operations Q1 FY28
items.quote: As we speak now, our equipment is undergoing factory acceptance tests at the OEM premises, and the equipment will be shipped in this quarter to our plant in Chennai.

items.statement: DCR segment currently limited to channel and PM Surya Ghar due to procured cell constraints; C&I DCR demand expected to ramp up significantly post-December exemption expiry
items.quote: The DCR segment we are primarily catering is channel and PM Surya Ghar, because we are currently procuring the DCR cells, and the quantum and the pricing allows us limited participation.

items.statement: Large module capacity buildup while non-DCR market narrowing ahead of ALMM List-II transition; price competition weighing on industry margins
items.quote: FY27 has seen a large buildup of module manufacturing capacity, while the module-only non-DCR market is narrowing ahead of the transition of ALMM List-II. The resulting price competition has weighed on margins across the industry.

items.statement: ALMM List-II enlistment inspection planned Q4 FY27 after sequential commissioning begins; result in 30-40 days
items.quote: This has been planned in Q4 of fiscal 27, once sequential commissioning of our lines begin. We expect the enlistment inspection to happen, and then it takes 30 to 40 days for the list result to come in.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 9.12% YoY to INR11.29 crores in H1 FY27
items.quote: Revenue from operations for H1 FY27 stood at INR11.29 crores compared with INR10.34 crores in the corresponding period last year and a growth of 9.12%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 25.01% in H1 FY27; net profit margin 14.75%
items.quote: EBITDA for the period stood at INR2.99 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.01%. Net profit stood at INR1.77 crores with a net profit margin of 14.75%.

items.statement: Provision of INR44 lakhs for a pending legal case and higher depreciation reduced net profit margin
items.quote: One is, obviously, we have prudently taken a provisional amount of INR44 lakhs against an open-end legal point which was included in the disclosures in the note as well, which has reduced the net profit for the company.

items.statement: Received work orders worth INR1.87 crores from HDFC Bank and two new orders from HARTRON
items.quote: On the order front, we received work orders worth INR1.87 crores from HDFC Bank for MIS projects along with 2 new work orders from HARTRON, Haryana.

items.statement: Company does not publish consolidated order book; guidance would be a board decision
items.quote: We do not currently publish or disclose the consolidated order book, if you are referring to that. For internal purposes, we definitely track the confirmed work orders and those are disclosed or announced to all the investors together through a press release.

items.statement: Incorporated Austere Next Private Limited (51% holding) for IT services, set up wholly owned subsidiary Austere Systems LLC in Delaware, USA, and became partner in Neural Nexis AI LLP
items.quote: To broaden our growth platform, we incorporated Austere Next Private Limited with a holding of 51% for IT services, set up a wholly owned subsidiary, Austere Systems LLC, in Delaware, USA, for IT consulting, and become a partner in Neural Nexis AI LLP to build AI-led services.

items.statement: 80-90% of revenue comes from services; products delivered as SaaS within service milestones
items.quote: So to answer your question, so whatever product we are, building, so that we deliver to our clients and services mode only as a SaaS model. So to answer your question, 80 to 90% of our revenue comes from services only.

items.statement: Retaining 80-90% of old clients for repetitive business; revenue split 40-60 between government and corporate
items.quote: if you talk about the repetitive business, mostly we are retaining 80% to 90% of our old clients in getting the repetitive business from them.

items.statement: Trade receivables grew ~6% YoY vs 9% revenue growth; milestone-based payments with regular follow-up on overdue invoices
items.quote: You can notice we have the absolute, even though the absolute receivables balance still remain elevated, but its growth is reducing with compared to the revenue growth if you look at the previous half year, which is why the trade receivables increased by approximately 6% year-on-year, but compared with the revenue growth of 9%.

items.statement: Operating cash flow positive in H1 FY27; focus on improving collection efficiency and operating expense discipline
items.quote: if you notice, this time also cash flow from operating activities has been positive in this half-yearly, and this is really, this reflects better cash generation from business operations, and we continue to focus on improving collection efficiency and maintaining discipline over operating expenses as the business grows.

items.statement: Company is cash-rich and debt-free; using IPO proceeds for growth instead of raising fresh funds
items.quote: So, we already have the IPO proceeds with us. And as you can see, we are a cash-rich and debt-free company. So we are focusing on utilizing those funds, rather than raising any funds -- further funds.

items.statement: No plans for fundraising; utilizing IPO proceeds parked in short-term deposits
items.quote: No, no. So, yes. So, we already have the IPO proceeds with us. And as you can see, we are a cash-rich and debt-free company. So we are focusing on utilizing those funds, rather than raising any funds -- further funds.

items.statement: Expanded overseas with US subsidiary in Delaware and active sales in US and European markets; pipeline described as strong
items.quote: Yes, we are like as I mentioned that we are entering into the overseas market. We, we recently opened up our office in Delaware US also. And our sales team has been active there in the US market and the European market.

items.statement: Urban digital governance (Dial 11-UrbanSphere) identified as strongest growth opportunity; targeting 660 municipal corporations in India
items.quote: It's basically the urban digital governance.

items.statement: Maintains specific margin range; uses AI to reduce delivery time on repetitive work and improve margins
items.quote: We are using the AI platform for that, which definitely -- which automatically increases the margin for the organization.

items.statement: Upskilling resources for AI capabilities; setting up AI lab in Gurugram premises
items.quote: We are in the middle of setting up the AI lab in our Gurugram premises and definitely then we will start getting the results as a part of growth.

items.statement: Differentiates by solving customer problems with focused AI implementation rather than pushing technology; client-centric approach drives retention
items.quote: So the main advantage, if I have to say, is basically we are not pushing what we have. Rather than that, what we normally do is understanding a customer problem, figuring it out what they need, and aligning that with the existing technologies or with the existing frameworks which they have available with them.

items.statement: Government payment cycles can face administrative delays due to officer transfers and bureaucracy shifts
items.quote: But generally, the projects which we are bidding, we are bidding on the project where the deliveries are aligned with the milestones and we are getting the payments on time, as per the defined milestone. So we are not getting the things delayed from our end. But something which is beyond our challenge is like the administrative delays, the reason behind the lift and shift of the government or the

items.statement: Other income increased to INR68.27 lakhs mainly from interest on IPO proceeds parked in short-term deposits; not fully recurring as proceeds will be deployed
items.quote: So, the major portion for the other income increase is the interest, that has been earned on the IPO proceeds that was parked in the short-term deposits. It is not going to be, like the whole portion, it is not going to be a recurring income given we are going to be investing those proceeds, in the growth opportunities.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR500 crores and above for FY27 remains intact
items.quote: Our revenue guidance of INR500 crores and above remains intact.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR750 crores for FY28 with PAT margin 10-12%
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are also providing revenue guidance of INR750 crores for FY28, while maintaining our focus on PAT margin in the range of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: PAT margin remained within 10-12% guidance range at 11.4% in H1 FY27
items.quote: PAT margins stood at 11.4%, remaining within our communicated guidance range of 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 20-30% within 6 months to 1 year
items.quote: Our anticipation is to obviously increase our PAT margins and the expected or target EBITDA margin would be between 20% to 30%.

items.statement: Combined order book including KIN acquisition stands at INR610 crores as of November 15, 2026
items.quote: As of November 15, 2026, our combined order book, including the order book acquired through KIN, stands at INR610 crores.
