items.statement: Planning to execute INR280 crores in balance of FY27 and targeting fresh order inflows of INR450 crores
items.quote: For the balance of FY27, we are planning to execute INR280 crores of orders. In addition, we are targeting fresh order inflows of INR450 crores over the coming months.

items.statement: Expect to close FY27 with unexecuted order book of INR750-800 crores
items.quote: Taking this into account, we expect to close FY27 with an unexecuted order book of INR750 crores to INR800 crores approximately.

items.statement: Acquired KIN Railway Equipment for INR41 crores cash plus GST with INR180 crores order book and 2 lakh sq ft facility
items.quote: We have completed the acquisition for a cash consideration of INR41 crores plus applicable GST. The acquired business brings with it an established manufacturing facility, technical qualifications, certifications, customer relationships, and an existing order book of approximately INR180 crores.

items.statement: Secured Vande Bharat sleeper interior design contract worth INR34.85 crores with BLUE Engineering as consortium lead
items.quote: In October, Airfloa, as a lead member of the consortium with Italy-based BLUE Engineering S.r.l., secured a contract from ICF Chennai for the interior design of the Vande Bharat sleeper trainset and associated development work. The contract is valued at INR34.85 crores, inclusive of GST, and is scheduled to be completed within 12 months from the issuance of LoA.

items.statement: MoU with KTK Group for platform screen door projects in India
items.quote: The second important development is our memorandum of understanding with KTK Group Company Limited to jointly pursue eligible platform screen door projects in India.

items.statement: KIN acquisition provides 2 lakh sq ft manufacturing facility to be rebranded as international business facility
items.quote: More importantly, the acquisition provides us with an established manufacturing facility of more than INR2 lakhs square feet and an operational base in Coimbatore, which we intend to rebrand as our international business facility.

items.statement: Debtor days stable, inventory days declined by 19 days vs March 2026
items.quote: Despite the significant increase in revenue, debtor days have remained broadly stable while inventory days have declined by 19 days compared to March 2026.

items.statement: 78.2% of receivables within 180 days, targeting reduction in debtor days within 6 months
items.quote: Yes, 80%, approximately 78.2% is within 180 days.

items.statement: Targeting positive operating cash flow in FY28
items.quote: Secondly coming to positive cash flow is concerned for sure our goal is to make it in the year 27-28 so that is our major focus apart from the business perspective.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity comfortable at 0.5x, cash and bank balances INR17.3 crores as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: While borrowings have increased to support the scale of operations, our net debt-to-equity ratio remains comfortable at 0.5x.

items.statement: Current borrowings sufficient for INR750 crore revenue target, may need additional INR100 crores in next 2 years
items.quote: In the next 2 years, I would say we will be going for another INR100 crores of borrowing, sir, apart from what we are having.

items.statement: Borrowing cost approximately 8.25-8.5%
items.quote: When it comes to the interest rate, then it is approximately between 8.25% and 8.5%.

items.statement: No equity raise envisaged for next 6-7 months unless large defense orders materialize
items.quote: So, in that particular case, definitely we may raise, but not at least, not I'm envisaging not for the next 6 months or 7 months or so.

items.statement: ROCE at 32.1% reflecting efficient capital utilization
items.quote: Our return on capital employed stood at 32.1%, reflecting efficient utilization of capital.

items.statement: Focusing on unmanned systems, anti-drones, autonomous technologies, precision-guided ammunition in defense
items.quote: We are majorly focusing on unmanned systems such as specialized drones, anti-drones, autonomous technologies, and precision-guided ammunitions.

items.statement: Platform screen door business worth INR1,500-2,000 crores annually in India
items.quote: Platform screen door business is approximately a INR2,000 crores business in a year. Every year there is a business growth of INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores in India.

items.statement: KIN facility approved by global OEMs Alstom, Hitachi, Siemens for export opportunities
items.quote: One of the major key strategies for the acquisition of this particular business, because this particular company has already been approved by the global platform of Alstom and other companies like Hitachi and Siemens.

items.statement: Healthy opportunity landscape across railway and metro segments including Vande Bharat, Amrit Bharat, metro rail, EMU, MEMU, refurbishment
items.quote: We continue to see opportunities across Vande Bharat, Amrit Bharat, metro rail systems, EMUs, MEMUs, refurbishment programs, and other railway modernization initiatives.

items.statement: Disciplined bidding approach, re-tendering at revised prices after aluminum cost increases
items.quote: Rather than pursuing orders at commercially unattractive prices, we engage with customers to seek appropriate price revisions and re-tendering wherever necessary. I am pleased to inform you that the re-tendering process has now been commenced and now we have started participating in these tenders at revised prices.

items.statement: Among 2-3 companies in India making both car body and interiors for rail coaches
items.quote: We are one among the company who are making the interiors as well as the exteriors for the rail coaches, unlike other companies, there are very few companies who are making the car body and the interiors together. So, we are one among the company, maybe one among the two or three companies in the entire country.

items.statement: Defense/aerospace has long gestation with qualification cycles, cannot disclose details due to sensitivity
items.quote: Certain things we cannot disclose openly since it is a defense project and it cannot be disclosed and that may come negative to us.

items.statement: JV with Big Bang Boom delayed for strategic reasons, expected to finalize within days not months
items.quote: But this JV is getting delayed for the strategical growth of both the companies because since we are now working on the defense platform. So, this is getting delayed for the benefit of both the companies, and I am very sure that this will happen in a short period of time. But it

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR1,600-1,700 crores with 5-6% PAT margin (INR80-90 crores PAT)
items.quote: Sir, so in the current year, we believe our top-line should be somewhere between INR1,600 crores to INR1,700 crores. And we are still targeting maybe like a 6% to 7% margin for the current year.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target INR3,000 crores with PAT INR200-220 crores
items.value: INR3,000 crores revenue; INR200-220 crores PAT
items.quote: Next year we are targeting, our target is to reach a top-line of about INR3,000 crores, and our PAT should be in line of about INR200 crores to INR220 crores.

items.statement: 2-3 year revenue target INR5,000 crores
items.quote: Sir, so if you ask us our target over the next 2 to 3 years is to achieve a top line of about INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR3,856 crores as of Oct 31, 2026; Solar EPC & O&M INR2,718 crores, BESS EPC INR1,138 crores (30%)
items.quote: As on October 31st, 2026, our consolidated order book stood at INR3,856 crores. Solar EPC and O&M accounted for INR2,718 crores, while BESS EPC contributed to about INR1,138 crores, representing almost 30% of the total order book.

items.statement: BESS orders of 582 MW AC and 1.3 GWh DC from RRUVNL, GUVNL, NTPC
items.quote: We have BESS orders aggregating 582 megawatt AC and about 1.3 megawatt-hour from -- sorry, 1.3 gigawatt-hour DC from customers including RRUVNL, GUVNL, and NTPC.

items.statement: Two NTPC orders where L1 totalling INR1,271 crores; LOA expected Nov/Dec 2026
items.quote: After that also, we have one more order from NTPC, and we have had two order wins. The total order value is about INR1,271 crores. We have still not received the LOA for this, but we were L1 in both these orders.

items.statement: Fully automated BESS manufacturing facility commissioned with KUKA robotics; ~1 GW capacity covered by orders in hand
items.quote: Our fully automated BESS manufacturing facility has been commissioned, marking an important milestone in strengthening our energy storage manufacturing capabilities. Equipped with advanced automation, KUKA robotics, the facility provides with an integrated platform to support our BESS EPC requirements and cater to external customers. Approximately 1 gigawatt of its manufacturing capacity is covere

items.statement: 1.5 GW module manufacturing facility in Roorkee operational and ALMM listed; 5 GW junction box line commenced operations
items.quote: On the solar side, our 1.5 gigawatt module manufacturing facility in Roorkee is operational, ALMM listed, while our 5 gigawatt junction box manufacturing line has also commenced operations.

items.statement: 2.4 GW solar cell manufacturing JV at Narmadapuram, MP targeted for commercial production June 2027; first equity tranche INR26.8 crores paid Oct 30, 2026
items.quote: Our next step in this journey is the 2.4 gigawatt solar cell manufacturing facility being developed through a joint venture at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh. The project is targeted for commercial production in June 2027. The first tranche of equity contribution of approximately INR26.8 crores was made on October 30th, 2026, following the quarter end.

items.statement: Data center EPC JV with overseas player targeted by end of 2026
items.quote: First is that we are going to increasingly look at data center EPC which is a very high margin business. And we are already discussing with an overseas player for a joint venture for India. So, we are hoping to do that by the end of this year and start targeting Indian customers in the data center business.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin 5.9% in Q2, 8.3% in H1; guided 6-7% EBITDA margin for FY27
items.quote: For Q2 FY27, our revenue from operation stood at INR244 crores, compared to INR137.9 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, registering a year-on-year growth of approximately 77%. Our EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR15.2 crores compared to INR18.1 crores in Q2 FY26, with an EBITDA margin of 5.9%.

items.statement: BESS IPP projects targeting minimum 16% IRR; NTPC BESS project targeting ~10% PAT margin
items.quote: We are targeting a minimum IRR of around 16% for those projects. The NTPC project that we have on BESS should also be substantially profitable, close to about as we close them, should be around 10% PAT margin.

items.statement: Solar cell manufacturing projected 15-20% margins going forward
items.quote: I would project a 15% -- 18% to 20% margin going forward in this business and that's a reasonable margin considering the cost that is incurred and the kind of complex operations that are done to convert a wafer into cell.

items.statement: Raw material costs (copper, aluminum, steel) easing; copper and aluminum coming down; lithium carbonate fell from 200,000 to 90,000 Yuan/ton
items.quote: Sir, 6 months back the lithium carbonate, battery grade lithium carbonate was selling at around 200,000 Yuan per ton, which has now substantially reduced and come down to about 90,000 Yuan per ton. So, the BESS raw material prices have been very, very volatile.

items.statement: PSU contracts are fixed price with no pass-through; private contracts have pass-through and some renegotiated for better prices
items.quote: And second, sir on the pass-through, so these are public contracts. All government contracts don't have a pass-through. Our private contracts do have a pass-through, and we have renegotiated some of them to get better prices. But on the PSU contracts, we really can't get a pass-through because that's how the tenders are structured.

items.statement: Residential BESS launched 1/2/5 kWh packs with good B2B/B2C inquiries; C&I segment installed first 125/261 kWh project with repeat inquiries
items.quote: In the first residential segment, Solarworld has recently launched its 1, 2 and 5-kilowatt hour battery packs. We are seeing very good inquiries B2B and B2C both on these products. Second is the C&I segment. We have already installed our first C&I project for a restaurant, which was a 125/261-kilowatt hour project. And we are getting repeat inquiries and a lot of new inquiries.

items.statement: Major PSU customers: NTPC, SJVN, SECI, RRUVNL, GUVNL; private developers for BESS
items.quote: So, so, in Solarworld, most of our revenue comes from PSU companies like NTPC, SJVN, SECI, which are some of the largest developers in India.

items.statement: BESS expected to contribute ~50% of revenue next year (INR1,500-1,800 cr); solar EPC ~30-40%
items.quote: So, when I say solar EPC, that would include my solar EPC, my module manufacturing line, and solar cell manufacturing line bundled into one. And when I say BESS EPC, it will include my BESS EPC work and the BESS factory.

items.statement: Solar cell JV to internally consume 70-80% capacity; 1.5 GW module plant to convert cells to panels
items.quote: Second, in terms of internal consumption between the two JV partners, I think we would expect to internally consume about 70% to 80% of the capacity. The balance capacity maybe 15% to 20%, we will look to sell to external customers. Solarworld already runs a 1.5 gigawatt of solar manufacturing plant. So, we will convert about 1.5 gigawatt from cell to solar panels internally.

items.statement: BESS manufacturing facility commissioned with ~1 GW capacity covered by orders
items.quote: Approximately 1 gigawatt of its manufacturing capacity is covered by orders in hand.

items.statement: Solar cell JV 2.4 GW TOPCon facility targeted June 2027 commercial production
items.quote: The project is targeted for commercial production in June 2027.

items.statement: Delayed procurement due to LOA timing (4-5 months after L1) caused raw material price exposure; H1 revenue INR412 cr vs full year guidance INR1,600-1,700 cr
items.quote: The delay was on the part of NTPC. When we submit a bid, we have to keep the bid live for a period of about 180 days. So, we can start buying the raw material and reducing our risk only after LOA is given because if the board of NTPC decides not to issue an LOA, then that raw material cannot -- we cannot use that raw material anywhere and we cannot get the drawings approved.

items.statement: Net worth INR862 crores, debt-to-equity 0.46x as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, as of September 30, '26, the company's net worth stood at INR862 crores with a debt debt-to-equity ratio of 0.46x.

items.statement: Chinese export restrictions on solar cell manufacturing equipment; pre-approval now required; mitigating via German equipment suppliers
items.quote: And we are also evaluating how to mitigate that risk. At present neither the suppliers or the buyers have any clarity on what is going to happen. The restrictions have not been imposed, but an pre-approval is currently required for export of any equipment. So, we are trying to expedite those equipment and get them out as quickly as possible.

items.statement: Solar EPC slowdown expected for 12 months due to grid connectivity issues and duck curve; margins may not sustain at current high levels
items.quote: I feel the slowdown is going to remain for another 12 months till the grid connectivity issues are resolved and a substantial number of BESS projects are installed, so that the duck curve in the electricity consumption, which is basically, very little consumption during the day and very high shortage in the evening is addressed.

items.statement: Submitted bids ~INR20,000 crores, largely PSU including BESS order from NTPC REL
items.quote: Sir, it is largely PSU and a big part of that is BESS order from NTPC REL.

items.statement: Hedging forex on LCs for imported raw materials; limited direct hedging for copper, steel, aluminum as buying processed goods (transformers, trackers from GameChange)
items.quote: Sir, so we do hedge whatever forex we have outstanding in terms of LCs for raw material that are coming from outside India. In terms of copper, steel, and aluminium, there is not really much hedging we can do because we are not direct consumers of copper, steel or aluminium. We buy processed goods.

items.statement: Solar module market oversupplied (~200 GW capacity vs ~50 GW execution); margins thin; not aiming to be major manufacturer like Waaree/Vikram
items.quote: Sir, so solar cell in terms of solar module I would say at present the business is not very profitable for anybody in India because you can see that there's about 200 gigawatt of capacity that has come in and India is likely to execute somewhere around 50 gigawatt. So that that kind of spreads the margins too thin, because the competition has gone up significantly.

items.statement: Management focused on execution discipline across EPC projects, BESS orders, manufacturing launch, and solar cell project commissioning
items.quote: As move -- as we move into the second half of the year, our attention will be on execution. We have a substantial portfolio of ongoing EPC projects, secured BESS orders to deliver, a manufacturing line ready for product launch, and the solar cell project progressing towards its targeted commissioning.

items.statement: Targets INR500 crore annualized EBITDA by CY2027; expects to be on track in normal environment
items.quote: we have, you know, provided guidance earlier of reaching to a INR500 crores consistent annualized EBITDA, you know, in the future

items.statement: Expects mid-single-digit volume growth of 6-7% for both LCL and FCL, outgrowing market
items.quote: So, I think we can target mid-single-digit numbers 6% to 7% kind of growth on volume terms for both LCL and FCL.

items.statement: LCL volume declined 5.7% YoY, FCL declined 12% YoY, air declined 10% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: For Q2 FY27, on a year-on-year basis, LCL volume declined 5.7%, FCL volume declined by 12%, and air volume declined by 10%.

items.statement: Sequentially LCL volume grew 2.9%, FCL 1.3%, air 16% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis, LCL volume increased 2.9%, FCL volume increased 1.3%, while air volume increased 16%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 2.8% in Q2 FY27 from 1.1% YoY and 0.9% QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 2.8% compared to 1.1% in the corresponding quarter last year and 0.9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA rose to INR122 crore in Q2 FY27 from INR37 crore YoY and INR33 crore QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for the last quarter increased to INR122 crores compared to INR37 crores in Q2 FY26 and INR33 crores in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: 20-30% of profit gains from industry freight tailwinds, 70% from business initiatives
items.quote: potentially 20%-30% of the gains are contributed by the industry tailwind, 70% is coming in from the business initiatives.

items.statement: Staff and admin costs flat YoY and QoQ; reduced ~8% in dollar terms last year
items.quote: Most encouragingly, staff and admin costs remained largely flat, Q-On-Q and year-on-year, with the company's focus on cost.

items.statement: Intent to keep SG&A flat in absolute terms; automation and consolidation to offset inflation
items.quote: Our strategy is to keep that flat because there's a downward pressure by using all the tools, technology, consolidation, and there's an upward pressure in terms of the inflationary adjustments

items.statement: No significant capex; depreciation mainly goodwill amortization; no new acquisitions planned
items.quote: We do not really have any significant capex. Most of the depreciation line items are around goodwill amortization and non-cash items.

items.statement: Business is cash-generating; net debt flat at INR587 crore despite revenue expansion
items.quote: Net debt stood at INR587 crores as of September 30, 26, compared to INR571 crores at the end of June 26.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents increased to INR412 crore from INR374 crore at start of year
items.quote: Encouragingly, cash and cash equivalents increased to INR412 crores from INR374 crores at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: DSO around 46-47 days; receivables up due to higher volumes and freight rates
items.quote: our DSO is around about sort of 46-47 days. The receivables have increased in purely in correspondence to the increased volume and the increased freight rate environment

items.statement: Bad debt provisions elevated from historical Middle East closures; expect normalization by Dec quarter
items.quote: The current level of bad debt in the P&L is not is not reflecting the true bad debt loss position of the business and we expect this level of bad debt provision to be finalized by the by the December quarter end

items.statement: Net interest-bearing debt to continue declining as business generates cash
items.quote: On the interest, as the business generates cash, the net interest-bearing debt should also continue to come down, and therefore that number should also continue to go down.

items.statement: Effective tax rates to lower as loss-making geographies turn profitable; cash tax lower than reported due to loss carryforwards
items.quote: effective tax rates should be lower, and also, like I mentioned earlier, the actual cash tax payout would be lower than the reported numbers given that we'd be using some of the losses in the last couple of years.

items.statement: Focus on high-yield products, exiting loss-making boxes, better trade lane management
items.quote: on improving gross profit with better trade lane management, focus on high yield products, getting out of loss-making boxes

items.statement: ECU360 platform, Topaz global OS, single data lake, integrated HRMS/payroll/finance enabling automation and cost optimization
items.quote: We have one data lake which captures all the data and information from across all the systems. We work with one global operating system called Topaz which is in developed in-house with an IT firm.

items.statement: Technology stack creates moat vs smaller single-country players reliant on agent partners
items.quote: they have typically a singular presence in a one single country or at best in a couple of countries in a region. So, they naturally depend on 60-odd different countries served through agent partners working on different systems

items.statement: Planning change of financial year to Jan-Dec calendar; may have shorter year ending Dec 2026
items.quote: we expect to you know go through the entire required approvals and other processes and we might then have a shorter year ending December 2026

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty and West Asia crisis create volatility; freight rates may soften if crisis ends in 2-3 months
items.quote: if compounded with an end to the West Asia crisis over the next two-three months, potentially in another three months post that, the situation could normalize.

items.statement: Near-term EBITDA may fluctuate over next 1-2 quarters as freight tailwinds fade; sustainable performance expected beyond 3 quarters
items.quote: there could be a bit of an up and down over the next one or two quarters. But like I said, so you assume you take away a part of the industry tailwinds and then build the organic path

items.statement: Gross profit per unit of volume (yield) is key KPI; Q2 FY27 gross profit INR837 crore, up 21% YoY and 14% QoQ
items.quote: Gross profit increased to INR837 crores, up 21% compared to the same quarter last year and 14% higher than Q1 FY27.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR7,842 crore (+17% YoY), gross profit INR1,570 crore (+11%), EBITDA INR155 crore vs INR6 crore, PAT INR4 crore vs loss INR117 crore
items.quote: Looking at the first half of the year, consolidated revenue grew 17% year-on-year to INR7,842 crores while gross profit increased 11% to INR1,570 crores. EBITDA improved significantly to INR155 crores compared to INR6 crores in H1 FY26. Profit after tax for H1 FY27 stood at INR4 crores against a loss of INR117 crores in the prior period.

items.statement: SG&A reduced ~8% in dollar terms last year; European payrolls in euros limit further reduction
items.quote: if I look at, for an instance, you know, the staff costs on in say dollar terms and you know the admin costs, I would say we were roughly about almost 8% lower than previous year.

items.statement: No new acquisitions planned; depreciation from past goodwill amortization only
items.quote: We do not foresee any new acquisitions in near future, and therefore the depreciation number should only go downwards.

items.statement: Costs in dollars/euros appreciated vs rupee; actual local-currency payouts reduced
items.quote: a lot of our payouts are across the world in dollars, euros, and other currencies which have actually appreciated against the Indian rupee, and therefore in actual payout terms in local currencies we have actually reduced the cost of doing business across the world.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR100-120 crores, 80% for retail footprint including jumbo stores
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect to incur a capital expenditure of around INR100 crores to INR120 crores in FY27 and nearly 80% of this investment will be directed towards expanding our retail footprint, particularly through the rollout of our jumbo store.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex cash outflow INR60-65 crores, COCO stores INR25-30 crores
items.quote: In H1'27, we have invested around INR60-65 crores, in terms of the cash outflow, primarily consisting of the -- our retail stores, some investment into the jumbo store, some automation-related changes and the network expansion related general upgrade.

items.statement: Added 41 COCO stores in Q2 FY27, 68 in H1 FY27, total 205 stores across 137 cities as of Sep 30
items.quote: We continue to expand our company-owned, company-operated store count during the first half, adding 41 stores in Q2 and 68 stores in H1 of FY27. This takes our network to 205 stores as of September 30 across 137 cities compared with 165 stores across 100 cities as of 30th June.

items.statement: Jumbo store in Bengaluru targeting launch in Q2 FY28, capex >INR50 crores per store
items.quote: Construction of the first store in Bengaluru is progressing, and we are targeting its launch in Q2 FY28 as per the earlier plan.

items.statement: Festive sales started Oct 8 vs Sep 22 last year, shifting demand from Q2 to Q3; October trends positive
items.quote: On the demand front this year, our festive sale events began in the second week of October compared with the last week of September last year. This resulted in a portion of the festive demand shifting from quarter 2 to quarter 3.

items.statement: Festive sale decent but not spectacular; consumer spending on discretionary products moderate
items.quote: In general, overall festive sale of 30 to 33 days has been decent, but not the spectacular thing that we expect some years, given the consumer demand and consumer spending on discretionary products has been moderate and has seen ups and downs this year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin 53.9% vs 57.7% YoY; EBITDA margin 11.1%; operating EBITDA margin 6.7%
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR243 crores, up 12% year-on-year with gross margin at 53.9% in quarter 2 of FY27 compared with 57.7% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Price hikes ~10-11% since war started; absolute gross margin per unit maintained despite 40% RM cost increase
items.quote: Our price hike on an average is around 10% to 11% before the war started versus what we are operating currently. And in terms of the recovery, we are able to recover absolute increase in the RM prices.

items.statement: No further price hikes planned unless unforeseen crude spikes; RM prices remain 30-60% above pre-war levels
items.quote: However, we don't believe that we want to do any more additional price hikes because we've always been treading the fine line between growth and destroying volume growth -- value growth versus destroying volume growth.

items.statement: RM availability eased; secured supply from multiple plants and geographies
items.quote: That, one, seems to have eased out. And, two, we have utilized the relationship strength over the last 11 years and managed to get access from different plants and different geographies to ensure that the engine keeps running.

items.statement: Mattresses 61.8% revenue, +21.4% YoY; Furniture 30.1%, +24.9% YoY; Furnishings 8.1%, improving
items.quote: Mattresses contributed 61.8% of revenue, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 21.4%. As our mainstay category, we expect steady growth, supported by our expanding omnichannel presence, a good portfolio of products and improving retail conversions.

items.statement: Furniture growth recovered to 25% after production issues resolved; Furnishings leadership gap filled, growth normalizing
items.quote: Furniture has come back to a 25% growth rate, which is higher than Mattress, which has always been the case over the last 2 years, except for last 2 quarters.

items.statement: Own channels 70% of Q2 revenue vs 60.2% YoY, growing 39.4% YoY; 32% revenue from repeat customers
items.quote: Our own channels comprising our website and COCO stores contributed 70% of Q2 FY27 revenue compared with 60.2% in Q2 FY26, with revenue from these channels growing at nearly 39.4% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Average cart ~2 products; cross-selling strong across categories
items.quote: Another encouraging aspect is cross-selling across categories with an average cart carrying close to nearly 2 products.

items.statement: Inventory buildup 3-4 months visibility for festive season; includes RM and finished goods
items.quote: And to answer your question in a more simple manner, we have about 3 to 4 months of visibility at any point in time so that we are not scrambling for it and worrying about inventory for the next month.

items.statement: Rent expense guided INR90-92 crores for FY27 vs INR84 crores last year; includes warehouses and offices
items.quote: And our rent expense would be ranging anywhere between INR90 crores to INR92 crores. That's what the current number we are tracking to.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth mid-teens for mature stores
items.quote: Secondly, on the like-for-like same-store sales growth, we have been able to deliver mid-teens level growth on the stores that have been in existence.

items.statement: Mattress volume growth mid-teens, value growth higher due to price hikes
items.quote: But for the mattress business for July, August, if you just take it, the volume has been in the mid-teens, and value has been higher than that because of the price hikes.

items.statement: A&P spend guided 7-8% of revenue for FY27; Q2 at 5.2%, H1 ~6%
items.quote: Our advertisement and marketing investments for the quarter stood at 5.2% of the revenue from operations.

items.statement: Cash pile ~INR400 crores pre-IPO + INR377 crores IPO proceeds + cash generation; deployment over 2 years for factory, acquisitions, jumbo stores
items.quote: So you're right, we had somewhere around INR400 crores of cash balance before IPO, and we raised about INR377 crores. And then as a cash-generating company, we have added to that pile.

items.statement: Furnishings leadership gap (6-9 months) filled; category growth normalizing from July-Sept
items.quote: The only reason here also was that the lack of the Head of the Furnishing category, who moved out of the company and became an entrepreneur. This was about 6 -- 8, 9 months ago, and there was a vacuum in the leadership.

items.statement: Net store additions will exceed 80 target for FY27; front-loaded in H1 for H2 maturity
items.quote: Even if we do moderate it, we will land up at a higher number of net store opening compared to the target of 80 that we had provided at the beginning of the financial year.

items.statement: Tracking well towards annual operating plan; Q2 growth rate ballpark expected to continue
items.quote: We won't be able to provide a very specific percentage on revenue and margin, but happy to share that we are tracking well towards the annual operating plan that we had shared with the Board and got approvals.

items.statement: Deferred tax unwinding to continue for next couple of quarters into FY28; deferred tax ~20-25%
items.quote: Yes, yes. So, Harish, it will pan out for the next couple of quarters as well. Only 2 quarters have passed by wherein we have unwinded. It will continue in the next year as well.

items.statement: Brought forward losses expected to be fully exhausted by Q2 or Q3 FY28
items.quote: We anticipate that it will be FY28, either the second or the third quarter, by then, we should be able to fully exhaust our brought forward losses.

items.statement: COCO model differs from franchise EBOs; faster payback (<1 year) due to multi-category, trained staff, aligned incentives
items.quote: We -- all of our COCO stores are obviously EBOs, but every one of them is staffed by Wakefit employees who are trained rigorously, who have incentives aligned for higher sales.

items.statement: FY26 full year capex ~INR30 crores; H1 FY27 INR60-65 crores
items.quote: As compared to last year, I think we invested around INR30 crores in the capex for the full year.

items.statement: Store mix: 110 mega stores, 95 mini stores as of Sep 30; last year 139 stores with only 30 mini
items.quote: Out of 205 stores as on 30th September, around 110 stores are the mega stores and 95 stores are the mini stores.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin expanded to 6.7% in Q2 from 5.3% YoY; H1 7.9% vs 6.7%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the half year stood at INR67.3 crores, registering a growth of 39% with the operating EBITDA margin expanding to 7.9% from 6.7% in the H1 of FY26.

items.statement: Polyol and TDI prices elevated; geopolitical disruption in West Asia impacting availability and logistics
items.quote: On the cost front, the operating environment remains challenging with crude-linked raw materials, particularly polyol and TDI, continuing to remain elevated.

items.statement: Mattress volume split ~50-50 between H1 and H2 in FY26 (915k units)
items.quote: Yes. So it was around 50%. You can say 50-50 between the H1 and H2, 2%-3% here and there.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue grew ~20% YoY despite uneven rainfall and El Nino impact on Kharif season
items.quote: The company recorded approximately 20% revenue growth in Q2 FY27, navigating industry headwinds while sustaining its growth momentum.

items.statement: Expects margins to normalize back to normal levels in Q4 FY27 after continued pressure in Q3
items.quote: So we see that another quarter or so, we see that it could be, where there could be certain pressures further. But I think in the Q4, we could see that the margins again coming up back to the normal levels.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin contracted to 13.2% from higher raw material costs, supply challenges, and lower high-margin product mix
items.quote: In Q2 FY27, the EBITDA margin stood at 13. 2%. Overall, the profitability during the quarter was primarily impacted by higher raw material procurement costs, supply-related challenges, and a lower contribution from high er margin products.

items.statement: 40-45% of raw materials imported from China; backward integration plant set up to reduce import reliance and improve margins
items.quote: So almost 40% to 45% of our total raw material requirement is imported. It is imported from China. And as you know, we have already set up a plant for backward integration.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven mainly by higher realizations due to raw material price increases, with some volume growth
items.quote: Growth across our key products was mainly driven by increased realizations, which was also because of the increase in the pricing of raw materials.

items.statement: ~50% of margin pressure from raw material costs, 20-30% from supply chain issues, 20% from lower high-margin product sales
items.quote: We can say almost 50% of the margin pressu re was because of th e raw material cost. Remaining 20%-30% was because of the supply chain related issues or cost and remaining 20% being the other factors of the high margin products, etcetera.

items.statement: R&D investment at ~2.5% of revenue; plans to increase investment next year for new products and backward integration
items.quote: Yes. So the current level of investment in R&D is around 2.5% of the revenue. And we plan to increase it going forward considerin g the type of products and the backward integration plans that we have.

items.statement: Exports currently 20% of revenue; targets 25% in 3 years with growth in Latin America and Southeast Asia
items.quote: So currently exports is almost 20% of our total business. And we see that going forward in the 3 years' time, this could go up to 25% with -- as the growth is also being planned for the domestic business.

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary established 3 years ago; building registration portfolio and admin office; expects sizable business in 2-3 years
items.quote: 2 years-3 years timeline, we see that we will be doing sizable business in this geography once you have acquired decent number of registrations with a good enough variability in the portfolio that we have to offer to that market.

items.statement: Focus on patented formulations and differentiated combinations; recently launched patented insecticide for Rabi season
items.quote: We have also recently launched one of our insecticide -- patented insecticide, which is helping us in this Rabi time.

items.statement: Domestic demand subdued in Aug-Sep due to dry weather; focus shifted to inventory liquidation at farmer level
items.quote: August, September being very dry, the entire placement or the inventory that was there in the market, the entire focus was more towards liquidation.

items.statement: Normalized other income ~INR 20 million; H1 increase due to land parcel sale and forex gains
items.quote: So typically the other income would be in the range of say 20 million or so. Other than, so that would be the normalized one. The one as you rightly mentioned is the additional that is because of the sale of fixed asset. A land parcel was sold.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve sequentially in coming quarters driven by Rabi product pipeline and Q4 pre-placement period
items.quote: Yes, the EBITDA margins should improve sequentially in the coming quarters considering the kind of products that we have planned for Rabi and the Q4 being the pre-placement period that is there.

items.statement: Farmers delaying sowing and switching to less water-intensive crops due to rainfall deficit; agrochemical spend delayed until crop survival visibility improves
items.quote: This weather pattern, the change of the weather pattern has impacted the farmers in a way that they are delaying their sowing to some extent in order to get more visibility in terms of how they can have an arbitrage or how they can have a risk assurance about their crop. So they are trying to delay their sowing. Number two, we have seen that there are some 5%-10% changes in the crops also in that

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth through FY27
items.quote: Despite the near-term challenges, we remain confident about our growth outlook and continue to expect double-digit revenue growth through financial year 2027.

items.statement: Cummins DG set order book at INR1,950 crore as of October 2026
items.quote: Coming to the order book, our Cummins Power DG set business had an order book of INR1,950 crores as of October 2026, providing healthy visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Data center orders account for INR1,200 crore of order book
items.quote: Of this, data center-related orders accounted for approximately INR1,200 crore, supported by a strong pipeline of opportunities in other segments, including manufacturing, real estate, rental, and others like infrastructure.

items.statement: Data center segment witnessing strong demand with operators expanding capacities
items.quote: Now, from a demand perspective, the data center segment is currently witnessing strong demand, with operators looking to expand their capacities to meet growing requirements.

items.statement: Medium and high horsepower segments see strong traction; low horsepower moderate
items.quote: The medium and high horsepower segments continue to see strong traction driven by demand from data centers, manufacturing, real estate, and rental, while demand in the low horsepower segments remains moderate.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.2%, PAT margin 8.4%; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.4%, PAT margin 8.3%
items.quote: During quarter two FY27, we recorded a revenue of INR847 crores with an EBITDA margin of 15.2% and a PAT margin of 8.4%. For the first half of FY27, revenue stood at INR1,628 crores with an EBITDA margin of 14.4% and a PAT margin of 8.3%.

items.statement: Steady-state genset margin ~9% consolidated; wind IPP blended ~62%, new projects 82-85%; EPC ~10%
items.quote: Margin, current year, we already mentioned that this is impacted. Because of that, Q1 was an impacted quarter. But steady state margin on a normal scenario, as we have disclosed in FY26, so genset margin would be considered as a consolidated basis about 9%. And wind IPP business would be close to, on a blended basis, including new and old, would be between 60%-65%, on average 62%, and the EPC abou

items.statement: Fresh steel price hikes from October 2026; copper and aluminum also up; calibrated price hikes planned in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Since the beginning of this Q3 FY27, we have witnessed a fresh increase in steel prices, with domestic steel producers announcing further price hikes through October. Effectively, earlier price increases have not fully offset the sharp rise in input costs.

items.statement: Current pricing covers RM inflation as of today; will monitor daily and revise if needed
items.quote: Yes. We've made more revisions in the past six months than we probably have over the past, like, three to four years, just because of the volatility. The current pricings do cover up, but again, it's hard to say because of the volatility.

items.statement: Long-term ambition to reach 1 GW renewable capacity; adding 100-150 MW per year
items.quote: First, basically, going forward, our little bit ambition is to make the company up to 1 GW to plan in the wind and the renewable sector. And every year, we will be keep adding 100-150 MW of the renewable energy projects.

items.statement: 50 MW GUVNL project at INR3.51/kWh tariff under 25-year PPA
items.quote: specifically about this 50 MW project, it carries a tariff of INR3.51 per KWH under a 25-years power purchase agreement.

items.statement: Wind IPP new projects EBITDA margin 82-85%; blended rising to 72-73% with additions
items.quote: Currently, we have our old projects and the new projects. Blended average EBITDA is, you can say, 62%-65%. But the new projects are having the EBITDA margin of about 82%-85%. So that's the EBITDA margins for the new projects. So, going forward, as soon as we will be adding more capacities, so our EBITDA margins will also be increasing side, maybe 72%, 73% with the addition of old and new projects.

items.statement: Manufacturing, real estate, rental growing robustly ex-data center; infrastructure moderate
items.quote: In ex-data center, or even with data center, I would say manufacturing still continues to be our highest contributor as a segment. So, Manufacturing, real estate, and rental are all growing very robustly, very steadily. So, that is on the ex-data center side.

items.statement: No major new competitors in HHP; LHP more competitive due to more players
items.quote: In terms of competition, we are not experiencing anything that we have not experienced in the past couple of years. So, we say that competition is still what we have dealt with no major new competitors entering the space from our view.

items.statement: Wind project execution timeline 24 months post-PPA; historically completed early
items.quote: So generally, a tender, we have 24 months timelines after signing of the PPA to execute the projects. And basically, Powerica has the history that we execute the projects before the timelines.

items.statement: Strategic inventory optimization and bulk purchasing based on market intelligence
items.quote: Yes, to put it simply, strategic optimization of inventory in terms of purchase timing, because of industry market intelligence that we keep track on, and as well as bulk purchasing as and when possible for the orders that we have in place.

items.statement: Joint venture agreement signed with GE Vernova for joint project development
items.quote: Apart from that, we are also developing the joint venture partnership with GE, which we have signed the agreement with them. Soon, some announcement will be there for these GE projects also, which we will be doing jointly.

items.statement: Wind business at zero debt post-IPO; will take 70% debt for 250 MW expansion
items.quote: So, right now, we are at a, you can say, practically at a zero debt post-IPO for our 330 MW of the wind business. First step is to make it double the capacity, which we will be achieving in the next two and a half years time, to make from 330-638 MW, which we already secured the bids. That will be the first phase of the execution, and we will be taking 70% of the debt for this project, to make som

items.statement: Data center ~20% of H1 genset revenue; other segments 80% with regular order flow
items.quote: H1, we can say that it is about 20% on approximate basis. Execution, what it is going to contribute in terms of H2, it's very difficult because we might say that we can execute all, but it is about the acceptance at the respective project site.

items.statement: EPC order book 600 MW for other companies; 450 MW already executed
items.quote: Already 450 MW of EPC we have done for the other customers, and already we have about, you can say, 600 MW of EPC for other companies in our hand. That we are executing.

items.statement: Reaffirmed 50% revenue growth target for FY27 despite 24% H1 growth
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering at least 50% growth in 2027.

items.statement: Targets full-year EBITDA margin near 25% on blended basis for FY27
items.quote: With these factors playing out, we remain confident of recovering our EBITDA margin closer to 25% on a blended basis for the full financial year 2027.

items.statement: Expects H2 EBITDA margin of 23-25% to bring full-year average closer to 25%
items.quote: Yes. That is how the average will work out. If my H1 is weak and H2 is similar to the previous year, there could be a difference of 1 - 2 points, perhaps because I am not a mature brand.

items.statement: Committed to maintaining full-year PAT and EBITDA in line with previous year within 1-2% range
items.quote: I am hoping, and I am already committed, that my full-year PAT and EBITDA will be maintained in line with the previous year. There may be a difference of 1% - 2% or 1 - 2 points in either direction, but it will not be a huge change.

items.statement: Aflairza brand expected to achieve 2x revenue and 3x profit vs prior year; FY27 revenue target Rs 20 crore, PAT Rs 3-3.5 crore
items.quote: Yes. I am hoping to close Aflairza at 20 crore for this financial year, with a PAT of around 3 - 3.5 crore.

items.statement: Will raise stake in Aflairza from 33% to 51% by January 2027; brand to remain independent for 2-3 years
items.quote: We will do that within January. We will complete it in January 2027 along with the acquisition.

items.statement: Expanded product portfolio from 350 to ~400 SKUs; plans to add ~100 SKUs in H2 reaching ~500 SKUs
items.quote: We will add around 100 SKUs in H2, taking Recode to around 500 SKUs.

items.statement: Opened dark stores in Odisha and Jammu; expanding PAN India across Tier 1-4 cities
items.quote: Recently, I opened a dark store in Odisha, and from there we are catering to Bhubaneswar, Sambalpur, Cuttack, and the surrounding smaller cities. In addition, I am doing very well in Uttar Pradesh. In the next 5 to 10 days, I will open a new dark store in Jammu.

items.statement: Nykaa presence strengthened to 34 touchpoints; enabled 60-minute delivery via Nykaa Now across 7 major cities
items.quote: On the operational front, we have expanded our product portfolio from 350 to around 400 SKUs, strengthened our Nykaa presence to 34 touchpoints, and enabled 60-minute delivery through Nykaa Now across 7 major cities.

items.statement: Diwali period was record-breaking; post-Diwali muted but last 3 days returned to same pace across all channels
items.quote: Yes. Up to Diwali, it was very, very, very excellent and record-breaking for us. After Diwali, because of the short holiday, it became somewhat muted, but over the last 3 days it has returned to the same pace.

items.statement: No borrowings needed; ample funds for next 1-2 years
items.quote: Not at all. I have ample money for the future, for the next 1 - 2 years.

items.statement: Face and eye categories drive revenue; 10 of 60 eye products viral, 50 face products performing well; no single-SKU dependency
items.quote: In terms of revenue, I am in color cosmetics, and everything is focused on the face and eyes. For example, I have 60 eye products. 10 of them are viral, and the other 50 are performing well. Similarly, in the face category, 50 products are performing well and the others are average.

items.statement: Paid dividend of 25 paise per share (~Rs 26 lakh) in FY27
items.quote: We paid 25 paise, so I think it would be around 27 - 28 lakh... Mr. Dhiraj Bansal: Yes, around 26

items.statement: Advertising spend 99.5% on Meta, 0.5% on Google; color cosmetics not search-driven
items.quote: I spend 99.95%, or 99.5%, on Meta and 0.5% on Google. A color cosmetics brand does not work on Google. No one is going to search for best lipstick in India.

items.statement: Expect 35-40% revenue increase in Q1 FY27 from new metal packaging facility
items.quote: And we are seeing almost 35%-40% hike in our revenue in the Q1 of 2027 from that.

items.statement: Spent Rs 9.18 crore on new plant and machinery in H1 FY27
items.quote: In these 6 months, we spent about Rs. 9.18 crores on new plant, machinery and buildings.

items.statement: New plant 75-80% complete, expected operational by March 2027
items.quote: As I told, new facility is going to be completed. It is almost 75%-80% complete. And it is going to be ready to utilize by March ‘27.

items.statement: In talks with Latin America and UK clients for IML projects occupying 4-6 machines year-round
items.quote: We are in talks with the clients from Latin America as well as the United Kingdom for the IML projects which are going to run almost whole year 365 days. They are going to occupy almost 4 to 6 machines.

items.statement: IML segment profit grew 39% due to smart raw material buying and stable selling prices
items.quote: More importantly, the profits from this business went up by 39%, from Rs. 4.15 crores to Rs. 5.78 crores.

items.statement: Passing all raw material price hikes to IML customers without bearing any cost
items.quote: Whatever the material gaining price hike is having, we are passing it out to the customer only. We are not bearing it at all.

items.statement: End Caps sales down 7% YoY due to Iran war disrupting Middle East demand
items.quote: Sales of the End Caps, were Rs. 8.79 crores, about 7% lower than last year. Profits from the business fell about 19%, from Rs. 3.5 crores to Rs. 2.47 crores.

items.statement: Launched filling machine business with Rs 14 lakh first sales; planning metal packaging with two-piece DRD cans first in India
items.quote: Our new filling machine business earned its first sales, about Rs. 14 lakhs. It is small today, but it helps us serve IML customers better and keeps them closer to us.

items.statement: Receivables increased from Rs 8 crore to Rs 13 crore in H1 FY27 due to Diwali season sales
items.value: Rs. 8 crores to about Rs. 13 crores
items.quote: The amount customers owe us went up to about Rs. 8 crores to about Rs. 13 crores in the last 6months.

items.statement: Debt reduced from Rs 24.13 crore to Rs 20.74 crore; debt-to-equity improved from 0.79 to 0.31
items.quote: We have reduced our loans from Rs. 24.13 crores to Rs. 20.74 crores. Our debt is now low. For every one rupee of our own money, we now have only about 31 paise of loans.

items.statement: IPO issued 37.488 lakh shares at Rs 97 raising Rs 36.30 crore; listed on BSE SME on 6 Aug 2026
items.quote: Through our IPO, we issued 37,48,800 new shares at Rs. 97 each, raising about Rs. 36.30 crores.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute 55-60% of revenue; key IML clients include ITC, Vadilal, Havmor, Sheetal Ice Cream
items.quote: The revenue of our top 10 customers is almost 55%-60%.

items.statement: Net profit margin improved to 13.5% from 11% YoY in H1 FY27
items.quote: Out of every Rs. 100 sales, we now keep about Rs.13.50 as net profit, compared with about Rs. 11 last year.

items.statement: End Caps business dependent on Middle East geopolitical situation; recovery expected when Iran war settles
items.quote: Because of the war involving the Iran demand, sales for the final products in which our End Caps are used, when our customers sell less, they buy fewer caps.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR1,018 crores as of September 30, 2026 across 30 ongoing projects
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, we had 30 ongoing projects with an aggregate contract value of INR1,987 crores, compared with 23 projects as of June 30, 2026. Our order book stood at INR1,018 crores as of September 30, 2026, providing a healthy base for future execution.

items.statement: Management expects order book to reach around INR2,000 crores by year-end FY27
items.quote: As far as order inflows are concerned, based on our experience and the visibility we have today, we believe that an order book in the range of around INR2,000 crores by the year end is a reasonably expected expectation under normal circumstances.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III Kerala project accounts for INR741 crores of order book with INR260 crores AMC portion
items.quote: So the BharatNet project is almost INR741 crores of our order book and out of which INR260 crores is AMC. So AMC is an ongoing work. And the EPC work for that, the right of way needs to be -- is awaited and once it is received the construction work will be started.

items.statement: Right of way approvals pending for BharatNet Kerala EPC portion; execution to commence upon receipt
items.quote: Execution of the business and balance portion will begin as a right of way approvals are not received as of date. We are in regular discussion with the Department of Telecommunications and are hopeful of receiving these approvals soon.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 19.64% in H1 FY27 expected to be sustained; dependent on approvals and clearances
items.quote: So, the margins are expected to be sustained in this at this level and factors to look out for would be you know, the right-of-way approvals that come from the government and all.

items.statement: Revenue growth CAGR expected to continue; confident of maintaining growth momentum from last 3-4 years
items.quote: And on the revenue, while I cannot suggest any guidance on the revenue number for the FY27, we are confident on continuing with the growth momentum that we have set in the last 3-4 years. We are confident of maintaining our revenue growth CAGR.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR175.06 crores allocated: INR115 crores working capital, INR15.4 crores machinery; INR70.3 crores utilized by September 30
items.quote: So, the IPO money received was around INR175.06 crores, of which INR20.5 crores were earmarked towards the issue expenses. The rest of the money was planned to be allocated towards working capital first, INR115 crores, and purchase of machinery, INR15.4 crores.

items.statement: HDD machines being purchased for existing work and expansion into new states
items.quote: These are HDD machines, and we have given the complete details in the RHP. These machines will be used towards our existing work as well as for expansion opportunities in other states where we are currently not available.

items.statement: Trade receivables reduced from INR156 crores to INR142 crores; unbilled revenue from INR76 crores to INR59 crores; receivable days improved from 237 to 192
items.quote: So, if you see, on the working capital side, our trade receivables have reduced from March number from INR156 crores to INR142 crores, and unbilled has reduced from INR76 crores to INR59 crores. That shows how much collection we have done during the current period.

items.statement: Telecom 81.23%, sewerage 14.65%, railway signalling 2.49%, gas pipeline 1.63% of order book
items.quote: on our order book, the telecom is currently our largest vertical, accounting for 81.23% of the total order book, followed by sewerage at 14.65%, railway signaling at 2.49% and gas pipelines at 1.63

items.statement: Company bid for INR3,000 crores tenders with 9.3% clearance; LOI awaited for INR125 crores; targeting INR2,000+ crores order book by March end
items.quote: We have bid for almost INR3,000 crores of tender and we have got clearance for almost 9.3%. We have got clear. Almost the LOI is awaited for INR125 crores in this month only, right? And we are aggressively now after getting fund from the public, we are aggressively marketing with -- tendering with a very cautious mode to get the revenue as well as our bottom line also. So, we are hopeful to achiev

items.statement: Will not bid below internal margin threshold; focus on profitable growth over order book expansion at any cost
items.quote: We will continue to bid selectively on our terms, looking at our execution capabilities, our experience in complex projects, the terrain and technical requirements, and the expected returns and acceptable margins. We will not go below our internal margin threshold merely to add to the order book.

items.statement: Entered renewable energy via MoU with GEIE for JVVNL rooftop solar INR44.3 crores (8,000 systems); initially supply role, targeting turnkey 100MW projects
items.quote: We have also taken steps towards entering the renewable energy segment through an MoU with GEIE for the supply of materials under JVVNL rooftop solar projects valued at INR44.3 crores. The project covers 8,000 rooftop solar system in Dausa, Rajasthan.

items.statement: Secured INR12.81 crores contract from North East Frontier Railway for 143km optical fiber cable backbone
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured a contract worth INR12.81 crores from a North East Frontier Railway for the development of the optical fiber cable backbone, spanning 143 kilometers.

items.statement: Business momentum expected to strengthen in Q3 and be particularly strong in Q4 FY27 as approvals received and execution progresses
items.quote: As execution progresses across our key projects and the required approvals are received, we expect business momentum to strengthen in Q3 and be particularly strong in Q4 of FY27.

items.statement: Collected INR73 crores from previous year receivables during H1 FY27
items.quote: And since the revenue was recognised in the second half of the last year and it will be collected, or rather, it is in the process of being collected. During the first half year, till date, we have collected about INR73 crores from the previous year.

items.statement: Experienced manpower and in-house machinery combination supporting execution capabilities
items.quote: Our focus remains on executing all these projects in a timely manner, maintaining operating efficiency, and ensuring financial discipline through our combination of experienced manpower and in-house machinery.

items.statement: Monsoon impacts Q2 execution; trenching work stops during rainy season causing sequential revenue decline
items.quote: So, EPC business per se is more heavily dependent on the second -- on the second half of the year and one more factor that happens in the quarter 2 is the monsoons that hit the country. So, a lot of areas where we're working, where we have these projects, work gets pending, work doesn't get completed because of the monsoon.

items.statement: Revenue heavily skewed to H2 historically; H1 FY26 revenue INR6.51 crores vs full year INR241 crores
items.quote: Ma'am, just going by the historical trend, because if you see in the numbers that we disclosed for the last fiscal, the revenue till H1 of FY26 was INR 6.51 crores, while the overall annual revenue was around INR241 crores. So, this shows that the revenue is skewed towards the second half of the year.

items.statement: Promoter Chairman Sanjay Kumar Sarraf expressed 100% confidence in achieving FY26 EPS level of INR6.91 in FY27
items.quote: 100%. Right. Carry on, Mayank.

items.statement: Successfully listed on BSE and NSE; IPO proceeds earmarked for capex on machinery and working capital
items.quote: Another significant milestone during the period was our successful listing on the BSE and NSE. The proceeds from the fresh issue are earmarked towards capital expenditure on machinery and meeting the working capital requirements of the business.

items.statement: Bidding market highly competitive with margins under pressure; company bidding selectively on own terms
items.quote: On bidding, the market has become highly competitive and bidding margins are under pressure. As far as our company is concerned, we have a clear understanding of the projects we want to pursue based on our experience.

items.statement: Working with government departments, PSUs, and private organizations across 10 states and 2 union territories
items.quote: We have built a presence across 10 states and two union territories, working with government departments, public sector undertakings, and private sector organizations.

items.statement: Execution track record of 365 projects over 21 years with in-house engineering, machinery, and specialized expertise
items.quote: Over the years, we have executed 365 projects, supported by in-house engineering capabilities, own machineries, and equipment, and specialized expertise in areas such as trenchless technology and optical fiber splicing, and other turnkey projects.

items.statement: L1 bidder on several sewerage, gas, and railway orders pending LOA receipt
items.quote: We have further won a few orders across sewerage, gas and railways where we are L1 bidders, however, pending receipt of LOA, the same are not being discussed or disclosed.

items.statement: Key milestones for investors to track: order book size, upcoming projects, and execution
items.quote: The milestones that you should track, would be on our order book size, on the upcoming projects and our execution.

items.statement: Measurement and certification delays, site handovers, land availability, and coordination with government agencies affect margins
items.quote: So, these are the factors that we need to look at in the future. So, the right of way permissions, local clearances, land availabilities, site handovers, coordination with the government agencies, the measurement and certification delays, these things one should look out for.

items.statement: Receivable days improved from 237 to 192; focus on milestone billing and collection efficiency
items.quote: And our receivable days have also reduced from 237 in March to 192 currently. So, this is how our working capital gap will be controlled.

items.statement: Only 28% of sewerage currently treated in India; 72% untreated; 95 crore people urbanizing by 2050 in Tier 2/3 cities
items.quote: So, in the Indian context, the treatment gap is very wide in terms of sewerage. So, only 28% of the sewerage is currently treated and 72% remains untreated right now.

items.statement: Railway signalling aligned with telecom expertise; exploring renewable energy and adjacent segments selectively
items.quote: Railway signaling is already one of them because it is very much aligned to our telecom expertise that we have. We will be very selective and we will go where our execution skills, the equipment, and the relationship carry over.

items.statement: Management committed to transparent disclosures and regular investor forums; focused on operational execution over share price
items.quote: Sir, we remain committed to an open dialogue through transparent disclosures and regular investor forums. Our true measure of success would lie in the operational execution of our work.

items.statement: Target to double revenue by FY28 from FY26 base
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain firmly on the track of achieving our target of 750 stores by FY28 and doubling our revenue over the next two years from FY26 base.

items.statement: SSG growth guidance of 35% for FY27
items.quote: In terms of SSG growth, this year we have given a guidance of SSG growth of around 35% for this year.

items.statement: Target 30% network penetration for Mobile Exchange Wala by FY29
items.quote: We are targeting approximately 30% network penetration by FY29.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to reduce by 50% in H2 FY27 or next year
items.quote: Our interest costs were anywhere ranging at 0.6x-0.7x. We can expect it coming down by 50%, 0.3x, 0.4x in next H2 or maybe one year going forward.

items.statement: Capex of ~INR20 crore each for FY27 and FY28 at INR15 lakh per store
items.quote: So whatever new stores we will open, you can consider it 15x120 is around INR20-odd crores of capex for FY27 and similar for FY28.

items.statement: Plan to enter one new state per year, starting with Chhattisgarh in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Maybe this year, no plans for new states, but again, next year, every year we will add on one new state. I think we have given the guidelines of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, I think states wherein with phase manner we will enter the states. Every year we will enter into one state.

items.statement: Festive season encouraging with premium smartphone upgrades and financing
items.quote: Turning to the demand environment, the festive season has been encouraging, supported by premium smartphone upgrade, attractive financing opportunities, and improving consumer aspiration.

items.statement: Industry volumes dropped ~15% below INR15K segment, but ASP rose >30% driving value growth
items.quote: This has resulted into roughly a 15% drop in volume. Whatever volume have been dropped, all dropped below the 15,000 category.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 71 bps to 12.7% in Q2 FY27 and 61 bps to 12.7% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 71 basis points to 12.7%. EBITDA grew 99% year-on-year to INR52.4 crore, with EBITDA margin improving by 35 basis points to 5.6%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 35 bps to 5.6% in Q2 FY27, stable at 5.6% in H1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA grew 99% year-on-year to INR52.4 crore, with EBITDA margin improving by 35 basis points to 5.6%.

items.statement: PAT margin improved from 2.5% to 3% in H1 FY27
items.quote: From last year, 2.5% of PAT, we have already moved to a 3% of PAT.

items.statement: Added 38 stores in Q2 FY27, total network 574 stores across 228 cities and 5 states
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, we added 38 stores, taking our network to 574 stores across 228 cities and five states, spanning approximately 2.8 lakh sq ft of retail space.

items.statement: Mobile Exchange Wala expanded to 108 stores from 71 in FY26, contributing 7.3% of Q2 revenue
items.quote: Mobile Exchange Wala expanded its presence to over 108 stores compared to 71 stores in FY26. This shop-in-shop model enables us to expand this business by leveraging our existing retail infrastructure while providing an additional revenue stream and supporting store-level productivity.

items.statement: COFO model contributed 73% of Q2 revenue, FOFO 16%, FOCO 11%
items.quote: In terms of our operating format, COFO model contributed to 73% in Q2 revenue, followed by FOFO at 16% and FOCO at 11%, highlighting the significant contribution of our franchise-led operating model.

items.statement: Average selling price including GST rose ~33% to INR34,050 in H1 FY27 from INR25,513 in H1 FY26
items.quote: Our average selling price, including GST, increased approximately INR34,050 in H1 FY27 from INR25,513 H1 FY26, which is roughly a 33% jump.

items.statement: Pre-owned devices contributed 7.3% of Q2 revenue vs 6.5% in Q1, accessories & protection 5%, TVs & laptops 1.7%
items.quote: Pre-owned devices contributed to 7.3% of our revenue in Q2 FY27, compared with 6.5% in the last quarter.

items.statement: Mobile phones 86% of Q2 revenue, Samsung and Apple together 50% of mobile revenue
items.quote: In terms of product mix, mobile phone contributes 86% of Q2 revenue, followed by pre-owned devices at 7.3%, accessories and protection at 5%, and TVs and laptops at 1.7%.

items.statement: Over 60% repeat customers tracked for mature stores (>3 years) across mobile, pre-owned, accessories
items.quote: Equally important, over 60% of our customers are repeated buyers. This is something we value deeply because for us, retail is ultimately about relationship and trust.

items.statement: Nearly 70% of sales supported by consumer financing
items.quote: With nearly 70% of our sales supported by consumer financing, we are making premium device more accessible to wider customer base, particularly in smaller towns and emerging markets.

items.statement: E-commerce share in electronics declining sharply; quick commerce not a threat due to need for look-and-feel, data transfer, exchange, warranty
items.quote: Sir, first of all, if you are reading the articles continuously, e-commerce is in a continuous decline in electronic business. As the average selling prices of products are increasing, people want to have a look and feel, and even the rising contribution of finance attracts the customer towards shops.

items.statement: Inventory days to range 46-50 days going forward, not below historical levels due to new store growth
items.quote: Not below this 46- 50 days, I think. This is the bare minimum that we require because we need to keep five weeks of inventory at the store level and roughly one and a half to two weeks at the hub level.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity fell from 0.9x to 0.4x post IPO; expected to stay at 0.3-0.4x
items.quote: And if you have seen already, our debt-to-equity from a 0.9x has come down to 0.4x. So, we can continue to be at 0.3x, 0.4x in upcoming days.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR360 crore; INR200+ crore in escrow for new store expansion, balance to working capital
items.quote: Because if you see our IPO proceedings of INR360 crore, I think majority of that is towards the new expansion. So, INR200+ crores is being booked into now the escrow account for all the new expansion.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth 46% in Q2 FY27 and 38% in H1 FY27
items.quote: One of the most encouraging aspect of our performance was the strong same-store sales growth, which stood at 46% in Q2 FY27 and 38% overall in H1 FY27, reflecting robust organic momentum and improving productivity across our existing retail network.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue growth: metros 118%, urban 58%, rural 69% YoY
items.quote: Our growth has also been broad-based across consumer markets with H1 FY27 revenue increase 118% in metros, 58% in urban market, and 69% in rural market.

items.statement: Non-Maharashtra revenue contribution increased to 8% in Q2 FY27 from 6% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Revenue contribution from market outside Maharashtra increased to 8% in Q2 FY27 from 6% in the corresponding quarter last year, reflecting the gradual shift of geographical footprint.

items.statement: Gross margin gain 50% from OEM margin increase, 50% from lower discounting in H1
items.quote: I think, sir, you can consider it to be 50%/50%, around 30 basis points, 40 basis points coming from some OEM increase in margin, and around a 20, 30 basis points coming due to lesser discounting.

items.statement: Apple volume demand muted in H2 FY27 due to price hikes and delayed new launch; premium Pro series demand strong
items.quote: H2, there has been some decline. The decline is there in volume, not in value. Apple already increased their prices in September end. We do not see much of a drop in terms of value in Apple because the prices have already increased by 15%- 20%.

items.statement: H2 FY27 capacity utilization target 75-80% and value-added mix 70-75%
items.quote: our priority number one is to ramp up our utilization, which currently stands at 65%, and we want to take it to 75% to 80-odd percent capacity utilization. The second would be to increase our value-added mix. Which currently stands at about 65-odd percent. We want to take it to 70%-75-odd percent.

items.statement: Quarterly utilization trajectory: Q3 ~70%, Q4 ~75%, Q1 FY28 ~80%
items.period: Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27, Q1 FY28
items.quote: Overall, if you ask me, quarter 3 would be at about 70% and quarter 4 would be 75% and then quarter 1 would be at 80%-odd, which is the maximum level that, in our industry, that is optimum level that one can achieve.

items.statement: Target net working capital days 45-50 days
items.quote: It will be between 45 to 50 days.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin 7-8% now, targeting double-digit once utilization hits 80% by Q1 FY28
items.quote: So I would say, what we are doing right now is absolutely the bottom case scenario for us, this 7% to 8% EBITDA is very much doable over a much longer term also. Of course, our target is always to improve, so we would be -- we all -- we are targeting, double-digit EBITDA, but that will only happen once our capacity utilization becomes 80%. So by mostly quarter 1 of next financial year, we'll be in

items.quote: we are doing additional capex of another galvanizing line which will be our 5th galvanizing line which will have a higher rated capacity of about 24,000 tons per annum. Which will be operational in Q4 of FY28

items.statement: Nut & bolt manufacturing and solar structures to start production by Q4 FY27
items.quote: these solar structures will come into production by quarter 4 of this financial year. And also we've introduced manufacturing for our nut and bolts.

items.statement: Total capacity ~200,000 tpa by end FY27 after added galvanizing line and solar structures; FY28 ~225,000 tpa excluding nut & bolt
items.quote: the nut and bolt will be around 2.25 lakh tons. Management: It will be 200,000 tons. Yes. Abhijit Periwal: For FY28, since you are saying that there is an addition of the line. Management: Yes. So what happens is basically, like, there is one black product and then there is galvanized product. So our black capacity will not increase, but our value-added product capacity will increase. So if you as

items.statement: Margin drivers: value-added mix 57.5%, utilization 65.5%, fixed cost absorption
items.quote: The margin expansion structure, note one, it is driven by mainly 3 factors: our higher share of value-added product, which is 57.5%, our better capacity utilization, which is at 65.46%, and the operating period as our fixed costs are getting absorbed on higher volume.

items.statement: Optimistic on demand from Jal Jeevan Mission, Amrut, Smart Cities, freight corridors, bullet train; industry 7-8% CAGR to $24bn by 2036
items.quote: On the demand side, we remain very optimistic as government has pushed, launched various schemes which are pushing our growth, which is like Jal Jeevan Mission, Amrut scheme, Smart Cities project, dedicated freight corridors, the bullet train projects, and there are many more projects which the government has already launched. The Indian pipes and tube industry is also expected to grow at about 7%

items.statement: Re-roller model passes steel price changes with ~2-week lag; EBITDA/ton rises with utilization and mix
items.quote: So actually, we are basically re-rollers, so we are not impacted by the steel price in the sense that if the steel prices goes up, we sort of pass that on in the market. It's just about, 2 weeks of lag that we have to take into account. So if the steel prices goes up, we pass on that cost. If the steel prices goes down, we sort of correct the prices of our products.

items.statement: IPO raised INR99.89 crore; INR71-72 crore used for debt repayment; debt/equity improved to 0.48x from 1.2x FY26 and 2.1x FY24; cash INR38.47 crore at Sep-26
items.quote: during FY27 we have raised INR99.89 crores via IPO, fresh issue. We have utilized INR71 crores of proceeds to the repayment of borrowing as on the date we have committed so far. As a result, our debt-to-equity has improved dramatically to 0.48 in H1 FY27 from 1.2x in FY26 and 2.1x in FY24. Our cash position stands at INR38.47 crores as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: IPO fresh issue INR99.89 crore completed
items.quote: during FY27 we have raised INR99.89 crores via IPO, fresh issue.

items.statement: Promoters belong to Jindal family (related to Naveen Jindal family)
items.quote: Yes, we are from the same family. Yes.

items.quote: When you ask about order book, what, what in our industry normally is that there is no order book position as such because we are not into the government projects. You know, wherein we take a big tender or something like that. So it's basically on a day-to-day basis. items.quote: So yes so operating cash flow negative reason was just we have piled up the inventory and we have increased our receivables from INR42 crores from last year INR33 crores. items.quote: we've added a metal beam crash barrier line. We've achieved commercial operation as well, which takes our total capacity to 48,000 tons from 24,000 tons.
