items.statement: Management expects FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ and EBITDA margin higher than FY26
items.quote: we foresee more or less the same kind of growth. And the year we are thinking that we should be 20% plus in terms of revenue and EBITDA percentage will definitely be higher than the last year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% range for FY27
items.quote: On the margins. So I think the margins are going to be at EBITDA margins, you can say approximately 14%-15& in that range.

items.statement: Lifetime order book of INR 4,000 crores across 5-8 year lifecycles, with INR 500-600 crores annual revenue potential
items.quote: approximately we can say about INR4,000 crores are the projects which are in the lifecy cle. So, we have one project which range from 5 years to about 8 years. Approximately INR4,000 crores is the life-time revenue of those

items.statement: INR 100-150 crores of orders to start in FY27, full ramp-up of INR 500-600 crores annual revenue by FY28
items.quote: it could be about INR 100 crores to INR150 crores of orders which will start within this year, and some of the orders will start next year. But overall annual size will be about -- and when it's a ramp-up, it's approximately INR500 crores to INR600 crores.

items.statement: Capex of INR 125-150 crores annually plus INR 200 crores from IPO proceeds over 2-3 years, mainly for Gears & Transmission, STP JV, and Bike Powertrain
items.quote: Our objects of the IPO, as per the objects of the IPO, we are using INR 200 crores of the IPO proceeds in the capex investment over the next 2 years, this ye ar plus next 2 years. Other than that, there would be approximately INR150 crores of capex more maintaining the same average

items.statement: Bengaluru EV facility capex ~50% of INR 350 crores growth capex, revenue of INR 60-80 crores in FY28 and INR 200 crores+ in FY29
items.quote: next year in 2027-'28, we can say that approximately INR 60 crores to INR80 crores of revenue we may do from this facility. And at 2028-'29, we have very good visibility, approximately we can say about INR200 crores plus/minus 10%, overall.

items.statement: Debt reduced from INR 410 crores to INR 220 crores after INR 190 crores repayment; debt-to-equity improved from 0.89x to 0.21x
items.quote: We have repaid INR 190 crores of our loan, which were at approximately, INR 410. Now the loans stand at about INR 220 crores.

items.statement: Quarterly interest cost to fall from INR 8-9 crores to INR 1.5-2 crores after debt repayment
items.quote: the existing -- now going forward, the interest cost will come significantly down to between INR1.5 crores to INR2 crores per quarter.

items.statement: Gears & Transmission at 70-75% utilization, Bike Powertrain at low utilization with room to grow, Alloy & Metallics at 70-75%
items.quote: and T ransmission, they operate at about, close to 70% to 75% capacity utilization levels. Bike Powertrain, there is a lot of room. We have done the capex. Now is the time to reap the benefits. So, they are at a fairly low -capacity utilization level

items.statement: EV/hybrid revenue share rose to 26% in Q2 FY27 from 20% YoY; Powertrain Solutions now 52% of revenue vs 20% five years ago
items.quote: EV and hybrid applications increased their contribution to total -- in the total revenues to 26% in Q2 FY27, compared to 20% in the corresponding quarter last year

items.statement: System-level products yield 18-25% EBITDA vs 6-8% for components; ROCE significantly higher for systems

items.statement: Blue business EBITDA margin sustainable at 13-15% long term

items.statement: Q3 FY27 expected to be significantly better than Q3 FY26 despite seasonal softness

items.statement: H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1 FY27 for AZO and API businesses
items.quote: We do expect H2 FY '27 to be better than H1 FY '27.

items.quote: Yes. I think that on a group level basis, consolidated basis, what you said, 10%-11% should be definitely sustainable. However, that would not be our internal aim. We would internally aim for a group-level EBITDA sustainability to be around 13%.

items.quote: We are now just waiting for them. What we had given them is based on their average or routine timelines, we have completed everything a few months back, and we are hopeful even earlier than that we get the approval. Definitely by March we are expecting.

items.quote: So, we are hopeful that in the next 2 years we would breach that INR 1,000 crore mark.

items.statement: AZO plant utilization at 70-75% in Q2 FY27

items.quote: Our facility is utilized at Chhatra only around 40%, so there is a lot of room for improvement utilization over there, and we are working towards that to see how we improve our utilization levels.

items.statement: Q3 typically sees softness as export customers tighten inventories
items.quote: I think the 3rd quarter typically sees some softness in demand since key export customers would like to tighten inventories towards the end of the calendar year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 13.25% vs 9% YoY, 7.18% QoQ; H1 FY27 15.15% vs 8.45% YoY

items.statement: Blue business Q2 margin clean, no inventory gains, absorbed raw material volatility
items.quote: Q2 is a cleaner quarter. It does not carry any such benefits. It absorbed volatility in raw material prices and still delivered a margin well above anything we reported through FY '26.

items.statement: Raw material prices on uptrend due to geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: So the trend of raw material prices has been on the up move, which you have seen because of the war and uncertainties of war and various other circumstances geopolitically.

items.statement: Chinese AZO suppliers recently increased prices, creating opportunity for Indian players
items.quote: But currently we are seeing an increase given by Chinese suppliers, which is not really very common for them to do. Even in increases, they usually absorb it and keep the same price.

items.statement: API Q2 pricing pressure due to customer and product mix changes, not absolute price drop
items.quote: So, what you observe in Q2 compared to Q1, which is a reduction in overall pricing, may not be reflecting the absolute picture.

items.statement: Supply chain reliability during disruptions strengthened relationships with global Blue customers
items.quote: We were one of the few suppliers who throughout was able to deliver efficiently and was able to maintain production irrespective of what is going on in the market. That helps streng then our customer ties, which will obviously help us long

items.statement: China Plus One not yet played out in AZO; Chinese dominate 70-75% global supply
items.quote: There the Chinese players dominate the global market with about 70%-75% of global supply. Blue, exactly the opposite, India dominates with about 75% or 70% of global blue supply.

items.statement: Gross borrowings reduced by ~INR 49 crore in H1 FY27; targeting <1x EBITDA total debt
items.quote: Strong cash generation in the first half has allowed us to reduce gross borrowings by about INR 49 crores. Deleveraging has been a stated priority since borrowing INR 200 crore, and the pace has been faster than we expected.

items.statement: Expect total debt substantially below 1x EBITDA and net debt to net worth 0.15-0.20x
items.quote: As we deleverage and move towards '27, we would be substantially below 1x EBITDA in terms of total debt, that is long-term and short-term debt combined. And we would be probably about 0.15x to 0.20x net worth to debt.

items.statement: Just-in-time inventory management with ~2 weeks raw material stock
items.quote: So we do work on just-in-time inventory. So we do try and keep inventory levels lower than raw material inventory levels at about two weeks also.

items.statement: AZO large customer approvals pipeline building despite competitive Chinese pricing
items.quote: We have seen large customer approvals, but the pipeline continues to build and we continue to push towards that.

items.statement: Blue H1 volume 4,691 tons vs 4,190 tons YoY; Q2 2,357 tons vs 1,748 tons YoY
items.quote: So in our Blue business we have H1 volume is 4,691 tons against the 4,190 tons previous year. And for the current quarter, we have a volume of 2,357 against 1,748 tons in last year Q2.

items.statement: AZO H1 volume 915 tons vs 907 tons YoY; Q2 546 tons vs 497 tons YoY

items.quote: I think neither us nor pigment giant like Sudarshan can really answer that even for next week. I think a lot of it is basically dependent on external factors.

items.statement: Targets 30%+ compounded growth over next 5 years
items.quote: Our priorities for the next 5 years are simple enough to state in one line each, 30% plus compounded growth, AI embedded across the value chain, not bolted on to it and the conversion of this platform into sustained profit and cash flow.

items.statement: Targets 13% revenue contribution from JITO branded medicine by FY29-30
items.quote: Under the revised model, we are targeting 13% revenue contribution from JITO branded medicine in financial year '29, '30.

items.quote: So in the year '29,'30, it will be INR4,900 crores instead of INR6,000 crores that we have shared earlier the estimate that you please note.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to exceed 5-6% target due to JITO margin contribution
items.quote: No, no, it will be more. So the EBITDA, we are estimating instead of 5% to 6% because the brand JITO will give more gross margin.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 80 bps YoY to 8.3% in Q2 FY27

items.statement: Gross margin grew 77% YoY vs 59% revenue growth, compounding faster than top line
items.quote: Gross margin grew 77% year-on-year, while revenue grew 59%. So this margin is compounding faster than the top line revenue numbers.

items.statement: Operating expenditure fell 160 bps YoY to 10.8% of revenue in Q2 FY27

items.quote: 2% of gross margin expansion, 2% of operating cost reduction through scale, and we are done.

items.quote: We have invested INR7 crores into Noida. We have upgraded our Kolkata warehouse and have put up capital in signing up with the state government for new warehouse.

We have upgraded to our Guwahati warehouse, which can also service to next 3 ye

items.quote: If you were to deploy your treasury into high value, receivables, government institutions, large hospitals, bulk buyers, we would earn around 15% annualized. That is roughly INR50 crores a year.

items.quote: We serve roughly 80,000 retail pharmacies through RetailerShakti. If you walk into most of them, you will find a paper register or at best, a decade-old desktop billing package that nobody has updated and nobody fully uses.

items.statement: Believes India medicine distribution will consolidate to <100 national distributors; aims to be one of the few remaining

In every developed market, the player has collapsed into fewer than 100 national distributors. We believe India will follow, and we intend to be one of the few that remain.

items.statement: Merger application filed with stock exchange; awaiting SEBI observation letter expected by end of December 2025; NCLT filing within 15 days of SEBI approval, 4-6 month process
items.quote: We have filed to the stock exchange, and that application is pending for SEBI observation letter. So we are waiting for SEBI's observation letter. We hope that by the end of December, we must be getting SEBI's observation.

items.statement: AI development organized around value chain: intelligent counselling, consultation validation, personalized wellness, smart health records, back-end automation; consumer AI launch targeted Oct-Nov 2026
items.quote: For next year, around October, November, we should be ready to launch.

items.statement: Fulfillment centers run AI-led picking, sorting, routing enabling 90% orders within 24 hours; new centers on same automated stack reducing marginal cost
items.quote: Our fulfillment centers run AI-led picking, sorting and routing. That is what allows 90% of orders to be delivered within 24 hours, while manpower cost per order continues to fall. The new centers coming up are being commissioned on the same automated stack. So the marginal cost of adding a location keeps reducing rather than repeating.

items.statement: NBFC/bank credit partnerships exist but adoption slow due to KYC/documentation hurdles; retailers habituated to informal credit
items.quote: We have already partnered with 2 national bank. items.statement: Management expects margins to continue improving driven by efficiency gains and AI solutions
items.quote: I am sure that with the kind of efficiency with which we are improving, plus the AI solutions which are helping us for improvement of the delivery, the margin should improve.

items.statement: September production hit record 40,000 chimneys; order position for Dec-Mar at same level
items.quote: In the month of September, we have done 40,000 chimneys from both the plants, which is a new record. The previous one was 32,000. And the order position for December, January, February, March looks to be at the same level.

items.statement: CapEx of about INR 10 crores for capacity enhancement funded by term loans
items.quote: We have already given on exchange about 6, 7 months, 8 months back that we are in the process of enhancing our capacity and we will have a CapEx of about INR 10 crores. So, bank loans have come and it is being utilized there.

items.statement: BLDC motor production to start May 2027; PCB lines by Oct-Dec 2027
items.quote: The production of BLDC motors is expected to start in May next year. And by October-December, we are targeting to start producing PCB lines also.

items.statement: New automated glass plant (40,000 sq ft) targeted for production by April-May 2028
items.quote: We hope that the plant, glass plant should be available for production by April-May 2028.

items.statement: Target 45,000-50,000 chimneys/month by end FY27; 40,000/month regular after new premises shift
items.quote: We are targeting about 45,000, 50,000 numbers. By the close of this financial year, we should at least achieve 45,000, 50,000. 40,000 we have already achieved once. So, once achieved, it can be made practice also. Once our shifting at the new premises is complete, we hope from both the plants, we should be doing 40,000 on a regular basis.

items.statement: Non-chimney revenue share to rise from ~10% to 20-25% in FY28, then 30-35% long-term
items.quote: We hope this 90:10 ratio should come down to 75-80/20-25, in the next financial year. Subsequently, the target is 60%, 65% of chimneys and 30%, 35% from other categories.

items.statement: LC limits enhanced from INR 25 cr to INR 63-64 cr; INR 30 cr LC from ICICI added recently
items.quote: We have got INR 65 crores, INR 64 crores LC limit, enhancement from the bank, sir. Earlier, we had INR 25 crores. Now, we have INR 63 crores, INR 64 crores of LC limits available with us. Recently, we have taken INR 30 crores LC limit from ICICI bank.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings up from INR 33 cr to INR 40 cr; long-term from INR 19 cr to INR 22 cr for capacity CapEx
items.quote: So definitely long-term has grown because we have taken term loans from the bank for enhancing the capacity.

items.statement: Export focus to increase in 7-8 months; targeting 3-4 exhibitions in FY28; first exports in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: We think that in the next 7, 8 months, our concentration and focus will increase for exports. In the next financial year, we will participate in 3, 4 exhibitions. And very shortly, in the next 1, 1.5 years, you will see that we have started exporting some products to other countries.

items.statement: Chimney production H1 FY27: 157,000 units vs 134,000 YoY
items.quote: As far as the production of chimneys is concerned, the total quantum in H1 FY27 is 1,57,000 numbers as against about 134,000 in the previous year.

items.statement: September monthly production record 40,000 chimneys vs previous 32,000
items.quote: In the month of September, we have done 40,000 chimneys from both the plants, which is a new record. The previous one was 32,000.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions: 3 container delays of 10-15 days in last 3-4 months cost ~10,000 chimneys
items.quote: Containers reached 10, 15 days late 3 times. Otherwise, we could have done 10,000 chimneys more.

items.statement: China supply chain risk due to AI-driven facility diversion; mitigating via JV for BLDC/PCB in India
items.quote: The dependence upon China for these products have grown multidimensional. We have to keep a lot of stocks because of a lot of supply chain issues we are facing, which is attributed to China using a lot of their facilities for development of AI. Hence, this was a decision taken by the management about a year back that we would be manufacturing these critical components in India.

items.statement: Panchkula plant maturity advantage; no new plants planned in East/West to focus on existing two
items.quote: I want us to do maximum production increase from Panchkula, because this plant has matured a lot. Labour, officers and managers have matured a lot. And after the Hyderabad plant, we understood how difficult it is to train and prepare people.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth for next 2-3 years, split roughly 50-50 between existing and new customers
items.quote: So, we are expecting about two-digit growth for the next 2-3 years consistently. Of which, if you see, this growth will be a combination of existing as well as new customers and new market segments.

items.statement: Targets blended EBITDA margin of 17.5%-18% by end of FY27 or early H1 FY28
items.period: end of this year or maybe the early half of the next year
items.quote: We expect the blended EBITDA by the end of this year or maybe the early half of the next year to be at 17.5%-18% EBITDA level.

items.statement: Jaipur plant expected to reach break-even utilization above 75% by end of Q3 FY27 or Q4 FY27
items.period: end of this quarter and next quarter
items.quote: Right now, the capacity utilization of that plant is somewhere around 65%, which we expect to go to break-even, above 75% by the end of this quarter and next quarter.

items.statement: Jaipur plant expected to contribute ₹9-10 crores revenue in FY27 and ₹15-17 crores in FY28
items.value: ₹9 - ₹10 crores in this Financial Year and then, maybe another double-digit growth in the next financial year, which will be somewhere around ₹15 - ₹17 crores
items.quote: Topline-wise, it will be contributing around ₹9 - ₹10 crores in this Financial Year and then, maybe another double-digit growth in the next financial year, which will be somewhere around ₹15 - ₹17 crores.

items.statement: EV segment expected to contribute 15%-16% of revenue by FY28
items.quote: EV segment for FY28 will be somewhere around 15%-16%.

items.statement: FY27 expansion plan largely completed; few machines already ordered to be added this year; next 2-year expansion plan to be released by end of Q3 FY27
items.quote: FY27 expansion is more or less already done. Already, because we have to work around 3-4 quarters in advance in terms of ordering of new machines, selection, ordering, testing, trials of machines and everything.

items.statement: Blended capacity utilization across plants at ~65%; Pune >75%, Jaipur ~55% (earlier stated 65%)
items.quote: So, as Sachin mentioned earlier, Jaipur is currently standing at around 55% utilization. And at Pune, we are about more than 75% utilization. So, if you say blended, it would be around 65%.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 gross margin improved to 54.3% from 47.2% YoY; H1 FY27 gross margin 51.9% vs 45.6% YoY
items.quote: More importantly, gross profit margins improved significantly to 54.3% from 47.2% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.1% vs 11.3% in Q1 FY27 (sequential improvement of 382 bps); H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 13.2% vs 17.3% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin also improved significantly to 15.1% from 11.3% in the previous quarter, representing a sequential improvement of 382 basis points.

items.statement: Added >100 new products in last 2 years and entered 2 new market categories; started working on Defence segment this year
items.quote: We have added more products; if you see in the last 2 years, more than 100 different new products. And category-wise also, if you say market segment or category, we have added two more categories in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Inventory at >141 days; target to reduce to ≤121 days or <100 days by end of FY27 (reduction of 25-30 days)
items.quote: Currently, we are carrying a huge inventory of more than 141 business days. So, that is our first target: to come down to at least 121 or less than 100 days.

items.statement: Auto component industry projected to reach $200B by 2030 with 7-8% annual growth; tractor volumes +1-4% in FY27; construction/mining equipment +8-10% in FY27
items.quote: India's auto-component industry is projected to reach about $200 billion by 2030, with domestic component sales expected to grow around 7%-8% annually up to FY30.

items.statement: EV-agnostic product portfolio focused on transmission, gearboxes, hydraulic systems; EV entry since 2016 among earliest Indian MSMEs
items.quote: Since 2016, we are in an EV segment and we are one of the earliest entrants in the EV segment, if you see, as far as Indian MSMEs are concerned, few of the earliest entrants.

items.statement: Working on international market opportunities but declined to comment specifics
items.quote: Currently, we would like to refrain from giving any comment on this. But yes, we are working on some areas.

items.statement: Growth driven ~50% from existing customers (including new products for them) and ~50% from new customers and segments
items.quote: So, we are expecting about two-digit growth for the next 2-3 years consistently. Of which, if you see, this growth will be a combination of existing as well as new customers and new market segments. And so, this will be, if you say, around 50%-50% from both sides roughly.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue ₹25.16 cr (+16.4% YoY), gross profit ₹13.67 cr (+33.8% YoY), EBITDA ₹3.8 cr, PAT ₹56 lakh vs loss of ₹5 lakh in Q1 FY27
items.quote: the revenue from operations stood at ₹25.16 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of around 16.4% compared to ₹21.6 crores in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue ₹50.6 cr (+21.4% YoY), gross profit ₹26.28 cr (+38.2% YoY), EBITDA ₹6.68 cr, gross margin 51.9% (+630 bps YoY)
items.quote: Revenue from operations stood at ₹50.6 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 21.4% compared with ₹41 crores in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Management expects H2 EBITDA margins of 9%-10% and full-year PAT margin of 5%-6%
items.quote: We are quite confident that H2, while doing, as everything is in place, we should be in the range of similar numbers which we kind of have discussed over the last call, which is about 9%-10% kind of numbers going to be there.

items.statement: Management declines to give formal FY27 revenue guidance but expects growth to continue
items.quote: I don't want to probably refrain any sort of guidance. To be honest, it is still too early for us. But as we mentioned over last call also, we will be continuing to see the similar kind of growth on top of the module sales, which will be additional.

items.statement: Total order book stands at Rs. 720.9 crores (Rs. 461.1 crores EPC, Rs. 259.8 crores module supply)
items.quote: Our total order book stands at Rs. 720.9 crores. Of this, Rs. 461.1 crores is EPC and Rs. 259.8 crores is module supply.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 8.3% vs 14% YoY; gross margin 21.6% vs 44.4% YoY due to mix shift to EPC and module sales and plant underutilization
items.quote: Gross margin was Rs. 21.6 against 44.4% in H1 FY '26. As Ankit explained, this reflects the change in mix towards EPC and module sales, both of which are materially lower gross margin than residential installation.

items.statement: Segment gross margins: Residential 35%-37%, C&I Government 25%, Manufacturing 14%-15%
items.quote: For the Residential segment, it ranges about 35%-37%. For C&I Government segment, it is about 25%. For Manufacturing, its range is about 14%-15%.

items.statement: Kits business targets 15%-18% gross margin and 10%-12% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So, wherein we are being able to make about 15%-18% of gross margin and at EBITDA level, we kind of foresee that it will be about 10%-12% of EBITDA margin.

items.statement: 1.23 GW automated module line at Miroli commissioned March 2026, ALMM-I listed July 2026
items.quote: Our 1.23 GW automated module line at Miroli, Ahmedabad was commissioned in March 2026. It makes TOPCon and PERC bifacial modules up to 725 Wp in the G12 format. The facility was enlisted on ALMM-I list in July 2026.

items.statement: Plant utilization ~75%-80% in September after ALMM listing; H1 carried 6 months fixed costs vs 2-2.5 months manufacturing revenue
items.quote: If you want to see, say, for September or so, our utilization will be about 75%-80%.

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar scheme: 50 lakh households, 14.8 GW capacity, Rs. 28,000 crores subsidy released; FY27 budget allocation Rs. 22,000 crores vs Rs. 17,000 crores FY26
items.quote: As per MNRE release of 4th August 2026, PM Surya Ghar has benefitted 50 lakh households with 14.8 GW of rooftop capacity emissions and Rs. 28,000 crores of subsidy released directly to the households. The Union Budget has allocated Rs. 22,000 crores to the scheme for FY '27, against a revised Rs. 17,000 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: Two 50 MW ground-mount EPC contracts from Mahagenco (Maharashtra DISCOM) worth Rs. 188.5 cr and Rs. 186.5 cr; payment milestones 10-12, collection 15-30 days post-milestone
items.quote: So, these are basically the contracts from Maharashtra State Government DISCOM which is Mahagenco which we need to execute. As such, the payment terms are linked to the execution phase by phase. There are multiple milestones which need to be achieved and after each of the milestone achievement, the payment gets basically disposed after each of the milestone achievement.

items.statement: Residential brand ranked #2 in India under PM Surya Ghar with 11,400+ installations and 4.8/5 rating; Solar Square (#1) did Rs. 340-350 cr revenue FY25 with cash burn
items.quote: Solarium is now a registered brand on PM Surya Ghar national portal with over 11,400 installations recorded and a rating of 4.8 out of 5. Any installer fitting our Kit can record Solarium brand against each installation. Recently at Bharat RE Summit, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and International Solar Alliance awarded us the Urja Chakra for the second position in India for residential

items.statement: H1 revenue mix: C&I/Govt EPC 47.6%, Manufacturing 36.5%, Residential 12.1%, Product sales 3.7%; Institutional (EPC+Manufacturing) 84.1%
items.quote: By segment, C&I and Government projects contributed Rs. 147.9 Cr, contributing 47.6% of revenue. Manufacturing sales were Rs. 113.4 Cr, contributing 36.5%. Residential was Rs. 37.6 crores, contributing 12.1%. Product sales, which include modules and inverter sold, were Rs. 11.6 Cr, contributing 3.7%. Institutional work, meaning EPC, manufacturing together accounted for 84.1% of revenue.

items.statement: Kits revenue Rs. 4.5-5 cr in Aug 15-Sep 30 period, reported under Residential segment
items.quote: Practically, it is August-mid we started and between August-mid to 30th September, we did about Rs. 4.5-Rs. 5 crores kind of revenue from Kits. And it fits into the residential business at this point in time.

items.statement: GST on modules, inverters, BOS cut from 12% to 5% effective Sep 25 lowers household installation cost
items.quote: The GST cut on modules, inverters, and balance of systems from 12% to 5% effective September 25 has also lowered the installation costs for the households.

items.statement: DCR cell supply secured; domestic cell capacity increased from 20 GW to 42 GW in 6 months; ALMM-II implementation extended to Dec 31, 2026
items.quote: Over the last 6 months' time, the overall cell supply has increased quite significantly. While we are speaking, it is to the tune of 50 GW plus. And over the next 6-9 months, the expectation is that the way companies are coming up with the cell lines, those dark times will be behind us or maybe the kind of supply demand gap which we were seeing 6 months back, we don't foresee that to be in place.

items.statement: Trade receivables rose to Rs. 281.9 cr from Rs. 152 cr (Mar); inventory down to Rs. 40.7 cr from Rs. 99.7 cr; majority of receivables from recent 2 months; bringing receivables down is H2 priority
items.quote: On the working capital front, trade receivables rose to Rs. 281.9 Cr from Rs. 152 Cr in March. Inverters came down to Rs. 40.7 Cr from Rs. 99.7 Cr as modules were dispatched into EPC and external orders. Bringing receivables down is our priority for the second half.

items.statement: Total borrowing Rs. 189.1 cr (LT Rs. 73.6 cr, ST Rs. 115.5 cr); cash Rs. 35.6 cr; finance cost Rs. 8.3 cr vs Rs. 4.4 cr YoY; no further borrowing increase expected
items.quote: Now coming to total borrowing first, Rs. 189.1 Cr comprising Rs. 73.6 Cr for the long-term loans and Rs. 115.5 Cr for the short-term loans. Cash and bank balances were Rs. 35.6 Cr. On the working capital front, trade receivables rose to Rs. 281.9 Cr from Rs. 152 Cr in March. Inverters came down to Rs. 40.7 Cr from Rs. 99.7 Cr as modules were dispatched into EPC and external orders. Bringing receiv

items.statement: Finance cost expected to remain at similar levels; no further increase foreseen as working capital peaks seen
items.quote: Not really. And most of the borrowing has already been in place given I think as Ankit has already mentioned that the overall plant is up and running. The ALMM is in place. We have seen the peaks into the working capital side. So, we don't foresee any sort of further increase into the finance cost as such. It should remain in the similar lines as we have seen over the last couple of months.

items.statement: No equity raise planned currently; may consider for next growth phase if execution confidence builds
items.quote: As of now, further equity raise is not on the cards currently, but if we continue to see such kind of, if we will be able to execute these contracts, means the overall contracts order book which we have in hand and we have good set of numbers, we have been able to place a good set of confidence in the overall execution of the order book and whatever we are kind of discussing over the last couple o

items.quote: Yes, that 217 GW is a nameplate capacity, like we have 1.1 to 3 GW as capacity registered. And that capacity includes three product names. One is M10 550 Wp and another is M10-R, G12-R and G12. So, right now, we are manufacturing G12 which is the highest Watt Peak available. And M10 which contributes almost 35% of the rated capacity in the ALMM list is about to get excluded as the supply chain has

items.quote: So, luckily all the complete order book is pertaining to non-DCR cells which is imported cells only. So, the order book is largely for the orders which are being allowed to use non-DCR cells even after 31st of December. So, even if the supply doesn't happen ti

items.quote: As collections come in, we are expecting cash flow to be improved and the finance cost as a share of revenue to come down.

items.quote: Yes, this understanding is absolutely correct which the contracts have been subcontracted with decent margins being already kind of accrued, not in the books, but kind of secured for us while subcontracting these to the other players. items.statement: DRDO licensed solar thermal tech for heating shelters in cold conditions till Jan 2036
items.quote: Separately, DRDO has certified our absorption of its solar thermal technology for heating shelters in the cold conditions. The license runs till January 2036.

items.statement: Gujarat state subsidy ~Rs. 28,000 on top of central Rs. 65,000-70,000; launched zero-cost residential solar in Gujarat
items.quote: Gujarat has introduced, Gujarat State Government has introduced a state subsidy, right, of about, I think, Rs. 28,000 on top of whatever Rs. 65,000-Rs. 70,000 of central subsidy. items.quote: our medium-term growth expectations remain in the range of 20% to 25%. We expect our EBITDA-level margins to remain between 30% to 35% and PAT margins to be approximately around 20% over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: H2 FY27 revenue expected at INR60-65 crores
items.quote: Approximately, yeah. Definitely.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR20-25 crores for FY27 towards diagnostic equipment and center development
items.quote: we have planned capital expenditure of INR20 crores to INR25 crores for FY27, primarily towards diagnostic equipment and center development.

items.statement: Cumulative capital commitment of INR30 crores for Dwarka facility and PPP projects
items.quote: Both the project in, cumulative INR30 crores.

items.statement: Dwarka Diagnostic Center with CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray targeting commissioning by end of November subject to PCPNDT approval
items.quote: We are targeting commissioning by the end of November, subject to the necessary PCPNDT approval.

items.statement: 3 PPP projects in pipeline covering CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray with site preparation and machine orders completed, MoU signings pending
items.quote: We currently have 3 PPP projects in the pipeline covering CT, MRI, ultrasound, and X-ray services, with site preparation and machine orders completed and MoU signings pending.

items.statement: CT scan facility established through RG Stone collaboration in Faridabad, MRI capacity expanding at Tilaknagar, genome sequencing lab infrastructure under development
items.quote: We have established a CT scan facility through our RG Stone collaboration in Faridabad, with MRI capacity expanding at Tilaknagar and dedicated laboratory infrastructure for genome sequencing under development.

items.quote: after Dwarka we have two more centers planned.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target 30-35% as upfront investments absorbed and business mix evolves
items.quote: our medium-term expectation remains to normalize our EBITDA level within the range of 30% to 35%.

items.value: INR64 crores receivables, -INR6.2 crores operating cash flow
items.quote: approximately INR64 crores of September 2026 compared to INR49.9 crores at the end of FY26. Consequently, cash flow from the operating activities was negative INR6.2 crores during the first half of FY27

items.statement: ~INR15-16 crores of receivables pending >6 months (including INR15 crores legacy COVID government dues); received INR7 crores in early November; expect clarity on regular receivables by Dec end
items.quote: I think I would say it is INR15 crores to INR16 crores more, I would say, pending for more than 6 months.

items.statement: Targeting cash flow neutrality by end of FY27 through accelerated collections and improved cash conversion cycle
items.quote: We are working towards achieving cash flow neutrality by the end of FY27.

items.statement: Finance cost declined 74% YoY to INR0.33 crores in H1 FY27; fully repaid 2 loans; net debt-to-equity -0.1x at Sep 2026 vs -0.3x at Mar 2026
items.value: INR0.33 crores finance cost, -0.1x net debt/equity
items.quote: Finance cost declined by 74% YoY to INR0.33 crores during H1 FY27 compared to INR1.3 crores in H1 FY26. We have also fully repaid 2 loans during the period. Our net-to-debt equity ratio stood at negative 0.1x as of September 2026 compared to negative 0.3x at the end of FY26.

items.statement: ROCE 18.5%, ROE 14.2% in H1 FY27
items.quote: Return on capital employed stood at 18.5%. While return on equity was 14.2%.

items.statement: Avoid aggressive bidding in government tenders; bid only if feasible based on L1 study
items.quote: We do our study and if it is feasible, then only we bid. We don't go into aggressive bidding like 48%, 52%, etcetera, what others are bidding.

items.statement: Pathology growing through B2B partnerships; expanding genome testing capacity as advanced pathology
items.quote: In pathology, we've been increasing our business through our B2B partnerships. And also we are increasing, the genome testing capacity in our lab, which is advanced pathology.

items.statement: B2C is upfront payment; B2B hospital tie-ups have 30-45 day payment cycle; government and subcontracted receivables have longer cycles
items.quote: B2C is the upfront payment. Regarding the B2B, where we have done the tie-up with the private institutions, the hospitals, there we have provided 30 days to 40 days of the time.

items.statement: Long-term loans/advances increase due to capital advances for Dwarka facility; short-term advances to regular vendors
items.quote: Long-term loans and advances that you have seen the upside is regarding the capital advances that we have provided for our Dwarka facilities. And the short-term loan advances goes towards the regular vendors that we have provided.

items.statement: Dwarka center expected to generate INR5-6 crores annual revenue in initial year; breakeven within first year, optimal performance by year 2
items.quote: The center is expected to generate annual revenue of approximately INR5 crores to INR6 crores in its initial year.

items.statement: Dwarka center breakeven within first year, optimal performance after 2 years
items.quote: We will achieve breakeven within the first 1 year. And, in the next year onwards, we will be like after 2 years, we'll be at optimal performance

items.statement: Secured new orders aggregating INR55.55 crores in Q2 FY27 from government departments and institutions
items.quote: During Q2 FY27, we secured new orders aggregating INR55.55 crores from various government departments and institutions.

items.statement: Received INR11.9 crores work order from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company for 250 security personnel for 2 years
items.quote: These included INR11.9 crores work order from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Limited for the deployment of approximately 250 security personnel across various locations in West Bengal for a 2-year period.

items.statement: Secured INR7.93 crores work order from Odisha Rural Development and Marketing Society for DDU-GKY skill development training of 1,200 rural youth
items.quote: We also secured an INR7.93 crores work order from Odisha Rural Development and Marketing Society under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana, DDU-GKY, for skill development training and placement of 1,200 rural youth in Odisha.

items.statement: Received two work orders aggregating INR34.22 crores from Building Construction Department Patna for 5-year housekeeping and maintenance contracts
items.quote: Additionally, we received 2 work orders aggregating INR34.22 crores from the Building Construction Department, Patna, for housekeeping, operation, and maintenance services at residential premises in Gardanibagh. items.statement: Secured INR1.5 crores work order from Government of West Bengal for DDU-GKY training of 210 rural youth with placement for 150
items.quote: We also secured a INR1.5 crores work order from the Government of West Bengal for training 210 rural youth and facilitating placements for 150 youth under the DDU-GKY scheme.

items.quote: The subsidiary secured a INR6.24 crores work order from CRM Enterprise Business Private Limited for the deployment of automatic number plate recognition systems and surveillance systems across 9 police districts and 1 commissionerate, along with body-worn cameras and night vision binoculars.

items.statement: Secured two CCTV surveillance work orders from West Bengal Police Housing and Infrastructure Development Corporation valued at INR53.15 lakhs and INR33.31 lakhs
