items.statement: Jindal Pioneer rig refurbishment completed in UAE; awaiting Strait of Hormuz reopening to mobilize to India for 3-year ONGC contract
items.quote: One of the rigs that we own was undergoing refurbishment in UAE, and that exercise has been completed. However, we are awaiting reopening of the Strait of Hormuz so that we can bring the rig from Middle East to India and commence operations with ONGC, as this rig already has a contract for next 3 years.

items.statement: One rig rehired at ~$55,700/day; two more rigs expected to be rehired with ONGC contracts in current month
items.quote: The second operational update is that we have received a contract for one of our rigs which is about to be rehired at a rate of approximately $55,700 Jindal Drilling & Industries Limited 16 November 2026 per day. We have 2 more rigs expected to be rehired in the next few months, for which we are expecting contract from ONGC in the current month itself

items.statement: ONGC capex cycle in India has started, reflected in increased tender activity and new contract awards
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that the capex cycle ONGC in India has started because we are seeing that reflected in number of tenders that are being issued.

items.statement: Net cash improved from INR128 crore (31 Mar 26) to INR295 crore (30 Sep 26); expected to improve further
items.quote: Net cash position has improved from INR128 crores as on 31st March '26 to INR295 crores as on 30th September '26. Going forward, we expect the net cash position to improve even further as we have a good order book and cash flows are strong.

items.statement: Priority for cash deployment is rig refurbishments and potential JV rig acquisition; no mention of dividend increase or buyback
items.quote: Sir, the first plan is to do the refurbishment of the 3 rigs which will go off hire and then get onto a new contract. That is where some cash will be utilized. In addition to that, we are also planning to buy the rig from one of our joint venture entities.

items.statement: Swarnagiri production reached 40-45 kg/month; target 90 kg/quarter minimum; 450+ kg possible in FY27; 1,000 kg/annum with new approvals; long-term 2 tons/annum
items.quote: Going forward, with the new approvals that are coming in, we will increase the production at least a thousand kilos per annum. And the long term, once all the resources are identified, it could produce around two tons per annum.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan processing 30,000 tons ROM/semi-processed material this quarter; tailings processing for 2-5 years; underground mining later could double 700-750 kg projection
items.quote: Once the proper circuit is commissioned, we will get into the leaching of the tailings. I think that is as we have always been telling our shareholders, the idea is we start with the processing of tailings for the next two to five years.

items.statement: Finland drilling 1,000-1,500 meters planned; target 800 tpd plant; potential 700-800 kg gold/year at 3 g/t average grade
items.quote: And if you actually take 3 grams as the average that is fed into this plant, we will be looking at around anywhere around two to two-and-a-half kilos of gold per day. So that will take it to almost like 700, 800 kilos of gold from this project.

items.statement: Bhalukona mining lease application planned H1 FY27; 3,000 tpd plant envisioned; 4 Mt at 0.24% NiEq delineated so far
items.quote: We are also planning to launch the mining application by the first half of 2027 that is the plan. So we are moving very aggressively on this project.

items.statement: Spain tungsten project: zero royalty, export concentrates allowed, 25% corporate tax; mining application planned after more drilling
items.quote: Spain has no royalty on tungsten. Zero royalty is paid on the tungsten produced in this country. That makes a lot of sense to be part of this and Spain has a policy where you can export the concentrates.

items.statement: Mozambique lithium-tantalum: commercial production possible in 2028; royalty <3%; 1,500-2,000 m drilling planned
items.quote: Among all these exploration projects, we strongly believe Mozambique is one project which can go into the commercial operations very soon. Very soon means not next couple of months, but at least in 2028, this could get into the commercial production.

items.statement: Swarnagiri H1 FY27: 50% PAT margin, 70% EBITDA margin; standalone profit Rs 80 Cr on revenue Rs 160 Cr; Deccan share Rs 20.57 Cr
items.quote: So that effectively shows 50% profit after tax and Deccan share of profit is around 20.57 Crores. Again, I do not have to tell the same thing again and again, but these are the kind of numbers which I have always been projecting in a gold mining operation.

items.statement: Swarnagiri inventory 133 kg doré+bullion valued at Rs 134 Cr (production cost basis); 109 kg bullion sold in H1 FY27; festive season sales in Oct-Nov to reflect in Q3
items.quote: And there is a large amount of inventory that is about 133 kilos of doré plus bullion that is available as inventory. And of course, the inventory has been kept because at the end of September, we are heading towards a festive season.

items.statement: Rs 137 Cr raised via preferential issue (Aug board meeting, Sep EGM); BSE approval received recently; funds for Finland gold, Bhalukona nickel-copper, Spain tungsten, Mozambique lithium projects
items.quote: We have raised about Rs.137 Crores, which is, I think, in the month of August we had the board meeting and then EGM we had in September. It took a lot of time for the BSE to give the approvals to us and that approval has come very, very recently.

items.statement: Finland royalty 2.5% vs India ~5% (auction up to 60%); corporate tax 20% vs India higher. Spain tungsten zero royalty, 25% tax, concentrate export allowed. Mozambique lithium royalty <3%
items.quote: Financially, if you look at it, the royalty rate in Finland is 2.5%. You just compare that one with the royalty rate in India, which is close to 5%. And if the mines are auctioned in this country, the royalties could go up to 60%.

items.statement: Ganajur Supreme Court hearing 1 Dec 2024 (postponed from 17 Nov); Court to hear batch of 8-9 connected matters holistically; Deccan is intervener; strong case with seamless RP-PL-ML transition, state recommendation 2010, MoM approvals 2015
items.quote: And this matter is now posted for hearing on 1st of December. Again, it was the request of Union of India. They asked for the postponement and Supreme Court judges have agreed for it and it is on the top of the board.

items.statement: Swarnagiri gold recovery 90-95% in circuit; grade 1.4-1.5 g/t; 135 kg produced in Q2 FY27 vs 89 kg in Q1
items.quote: And the second one is the gold recovery. I think this is kudos to our team. The 90% to 95% recovery in the gold circuit is quite a significant thing.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan resource: 4.5 t in-situ at 1.69 g/t + 1.09 t stockpiles = 5.67 t total; underground target +3 t at 2.5-3 g/t
items.quote: And within that one, there is a resource that is what the in-situ resource is that is about 4.5 tons at an average grade of 1.69 grams per ton. And we have stockpiles. That includes tailings as well as low-grade stockpiles, which contains about 1.09 tons of gold.

items.statement: Ganajur: 9 t gold resource, open-pit grade 3.8 g/t vs Swarnagiri 1.4 g/t; 1,000 tpd could yield 1 t/year
items.quote: This project we have already identified or proved about 9 tons of gold and the open-pit average grade is around 3.8 grams per ton.

items.statement: Bhalukona: 1.3 km mineralized zone, 15 holes, 4 Mt at 0.24% NiEq delineated; targeting G2/G1 resource for mining lease
items.quote: Very conservatively, we have taken the estimate as of now 0.24% of nickel equivalent and about 4 million tons of economic ore has been already delineated.

items.statement: Spain tungsten: 5,400 m drilling, every hole intersected economic W-Sn mineralization; 2.3 Mt resource in small area; Maria license antimony 1,000 ppm
items.quote: And every completed hole has intersected potentially economic tungsten and tin mineralization.

items.statement: Mozambique: 150 sq km, multiple pegmatites; Inchocha artisanal Li production; regolith tantalum potential; graphite project: 94% recovery, flaky graphite, 5 mm flakes, simple flotation
items.quote: And the beneficiation test has also been carried out. It has about 94% recovery, and it is a flaky graphite. That is what is required for the battery makers.

items.statement: Rs 137 Cr preferential issue completed (Aug board, Sep EGM); BSE approval received; funds collection in progress for exploration projects
items.quote: We have raised about Rs.137 Crores, which is, I think, in the month of August we had the board meeting and then EGM we had in September.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan first doré consignment 1.2 kg sent to government refinery as test; National Bank settlement process underway; Swarnagiri sells bullion directly to jewelers
items.quote: Now, the amount of gold in that, how much we are going to get, and more importantly, this consignment we have sent to see how the whole circle of, like it will go to a refinery and the refinery will process and then bullion is sold to the national bank.

items.statement: Ganajur legal timeline uncertain; Supreme Court batch hearing may take time; BSE approval delay delayed Finland/Mozambique drilling; Kyrgyzstan winter operations may affect commissioning
items.quote: Yes, it is a government, it is a court matter. It could take time, but I think we are on the strong footing as far as our case is concerned.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY27 loss Rs 9.28 Cr despite standalone profit; management to address reasons in Q&A
items.quote: Despite the improvement in the standalone profitability and the significant profit contribution from the associate company, consolidated results continue to show a loss of Rs.9.28 Crores for the first half during 2026-27.

items.statement: Portfolio: Gold (Swarnagiri, Altyn-Tor, Finland, Tanzania, Ganajur) + Critical Minerals (Bhalukona Ni-Cu-PGE, Spain W-Sn, Mozambique Li-Ta, Graphite); targeting battery metals (Li, Ni, Graphite) and defense (W)
items.quote: So, Deccan Gold is no longer just an exploring for resources, but it is building a global mining business. I think this quarter has provided that kind of platform and confidence to us as well.

items.statement: Swarnagiri: sells refined 24K bullion to jewelers; Kyrgyzstan: doré to government refinery → National Bank (mandatory); Finland/Spain/Mozambique: plan to export concentrates to India for downstream processing
items.quote: In Swarnagiri, we have our own refinery. So the doré bar is taken into the refinery and it is refined and we sell it to the jewelers. Whereas in Kyrgyzstan, that is not allowed. Actually, there is only one refinery that is available.

items.statement: Secured critical mineral portfolio 5 years ago despite stiff competition; first-mover in battery metals (Li, Ni, Graphite) and tungsten for defense; limited competition in Europe for Finland/Spain projects
items.quote: And we secured a large portfolio of assets in spite of facing stiff competition overseas without the assets. So, I think these are the three things this quarter has clearly validated, and it is a big achievement for Deccan Gold Mines.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan: doré refined locally, sold to National Bank in local currency; Finland/Spain/Mozambique: plan to export concentrates to India for price advantage and downstream processing
items.quote: And the corporate tax is around 25%, which is also very competitive compared to India. So, it makes a lot of business sense and it also provides a possibility of bringing those metals to India.

items.statement: Honorable Indian Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan attended Altyn-Tor inauguration; engaged experienced senior counsel for Ganajur Supreme Court case
items.quote: And the inauguration was also in fact attended by our Honorable Indian Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, that is whom we can see on the far left in the picture and dore was shown to him.

items.statement: Due diligence on three new projects: Finland gold (45 sq km, 6 t Au + 9 t Ag, expandable), Brownfield gold near Terek (3.3 t Au C1/C2, potential >10 t), Graphite (1 km explored, 10 km potential, 94% recovery, flaky graphite)
items.quote: Two are gold project, one is a graphite project. Let me start with the gold project. It is in Finland of course. It is 45 square kilometers of the granted tenement. There are two clusters. It has about six tons of gold at various stages of development plus nine tons of silver also in one deposit.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan corporate structure: Avelum Partners (subsidiary) revenue share with Kyrgyzaltyn (govt) - 17% govt / 83% Avelum; Deccan 60% of Avelum = 49% revenue; Hira Group 26%, Medetbek 14%
items.quote: We have a company called Avelum Partners, which is a revenue sharing arrangement with the government company that is Kyrgyzaltyn. Kyrgyzaltyn is like an Indian public sector company that is like an NMDC, if I take an example.

items.statement: Targets 450-500 kg gold production from Jonnagiri in FY25, up from earlier 600 kg guidance
items.quote: So we would be reaching anywhere between 450 to 500, if not more. Because if you see the previous quarter and this quarter there is significant jump. So we will be in my view we would be reaching close to 500 kilos and we have always been telling this could be anywhere between 500 to 600 kilos in the first year and then it will be enhanced later.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan production guidance deferred pending 15-20 days of winter operations testing
items.quote: As I said, explained previously during my presentation, give us another 15 days' time and see how the plant is functioning during this winter time and then I will be more confident in giving those numbers and guidance value.

items.statement: Expects Kyrgyzstan PAT margins of 30-35% with maximum 40%
items.quote: In Kyrgyzstan, which we have always been maintaining, that the PAT margins are going to be anywhere around 30% to 35%, and the maximum being 40%.

items.statement: Jonnagiri EBITDA margins may decline from 70% to 65-67% if gold prices remain at current levels
items.quote: So our numbers, the 70% EBITDA may come down a little bit to 65, 67, in that range. That is what I foresee if these prices continue to be like this.

items.statement: Ganajur project could achieve EBITDA margins of 70-80% due to high grade and low opex
items.quote: Maybe the EBITDA margins upwards of 70, close to 75, or even 80 is possible, of course, depending on the gold price.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan winter operations test underway; 15-20 days needed to assess 180 kg annual target feasibility
items.quote: Currently, we are going to run with the actually ore, it is not with tailings. So within next 15 days we will have a clear idea how much we are going to produce in this, particularly during the winter.

items.statement: PLI scheme for critical minerals may provide 20-30% of capital requirement for downstream processing
items.quote: My understanding it is only my understanding, it is not on the paper at least 20% to 30% of the required capital they could provide.

items.statement: Exploring offtake arrangements with downstream players for nickel, lithium, tungsten to fund critical mineral projects instead of equity dilution
items.quote: In fact, a couple of people, they have already approached us in terms of like having a nickel offtake for nickel or for lithium and also for tungsten. So, in fact, we are talking to them. Now, in case if we, that is one other route which we believe can fund these projects, particularly the critical mineral projects

items.statement: Deccan Gold lent Rs 276 crore to Kyrgyzstan subsidiary at 15% interest; eliminated in consolidation
items.quote: You must be aware that Deccan Gold has lent about 276 Crores to Kyrgyzstan at a rate of 15% interest. Those interests are recognized in Deccan's standalone books.

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan stockpile grade 0.99 g/t (combined low-grade 0.78 g/t and tailings 1.29 g/t); in-situ pit grade 1.69 g/t
items.quote: is an average grade if I remember of the stockpiles which includes two that is tailings as well as low grade stockpiles. Low grade stockpiles have an average grade of 0.8 grams per ton or 0.78 and the tailings have a grade of about 1.9. So, it is a combined grade that is shown as 0.99 and in situ resources, if you show in this presentation, that is from the ore that is coming as 1.69 from the pit

items.statement: Consolidated losses narrowing due to Swarnagiri contribution; other projects pre-revenue
items.quote: The consolidated losses, you know, significantly narrowed down during this quarter, and we hope that it will continue in ensuing quarters also.

items.statement: Expects 60% revenue from gold over next 5 years; critical minerals value addition requires downstream processing
items.quote: I still believe 60% of our revenues will come from gold. It is primarily because the lot of critical minerals, the value addition comes from the downstream.

items.statement: Copper concentrate from Bhalukona pilot could be sold to Indian copper refineries
items.quote: Do not go for the bigger one immediately, but a pilot scale operation, which can start producing a smaller amount of the concentrate and start selling the concentrate to the refineries in India. There are copper refineries in this country, obviously, won by all big players.

items.statement: First mover advantage in Indian nickel mining strengthens PLI scheme eligibility
items.quote: I personally feel there is a lot of advantage because we are one of the first players who are developing this kind of nickel mine in this country. So we stand a good chance.

items.statement: Planning analyst meets before December 15th to improve institutional visibility
items.quote: We will again go back to the analysts and conduct some meets in this quarter itself before December 15th. We are contemplating to do it.

items.statement: Winter operations at Kyrgyzstan untested; 15-20 days needed to validate plant performance
items.quote: This is the first time this entire plant is being operated during winter. So, it is not that we are not going to face any challenges, but we would like to see and you have to give me that much of time, at least another 15, 20 days, how this is going to happen.

items.statement: Monthly production disclosure planned for Kyrgyzstan; will request Swarnagiri for monthly data
items.quote: monthly production, particularly from Altyn-Tor, we will announce. There is no doubt about it. And in terms of Swarnagiri project, it is actually quarterly reports that we get from them. That is what we have been presenting. We will make an effort definitely to talk to them and then get the monthly production from

items.statement: Feed sales for FY27 estimated around 5,80,000 MT
items.quote: It is estimated that the feed sales during FY27 would be around 5,80,000 MT.

items.statement: Shrimp feed consumption for FY27 likely around 10 lakh MT vs 9 lakh MT in FY26
items.quote: As far as the shrimp feed consumption is concerned, as in this earlier estimate of 11-12 lakh for the year FY27 is likely to be around 10 lakh MT as against about 9 lakh MT in FY26.

items.statement: Fish meal price increased to INR 199/kg in Q2 FY27 from INR 153/kg in Q1 FY27 and INR 98/kg in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The prices of fish meal increased in Q2 FY27 to INR 199 per kg from INR 153 per kg in Q1 FY27 and increased from INR 98 per kg in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Soya bean meal price increased to INR 67/kg in Q2 FY27 from INR 58/kg in Q1 FY27 and INR 43/kg in Q2 FY26
items.quote: In case of soya bean meal, their prices increased to INR 67 per kg in Q2 FY26 from 58 in Q1 FY27 and increased from INR 43 in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Wheat flour price increased to INR 32/kg in Q2 FY27 from INR 28/kg in Q1 FY27, decreased from INR 33/kg in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The wheat flour price increased to INR 32 per kg in Q2 FY27 from INR 28 per kg in Q1 FY27 and decreased from INR 33 per kg in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Current purchase prices: fish meal INR 210/kg, soya bean meal INR 80/kg, wheat flour INR 36/kg
items.quote: The present purchase price of fish meal is INR 210 per kg, soya bean meal is INR 80 per kg and wheat flour is INR 36 per kg.

items.statement: Feed price hike of INR 8/kg taken in October, around 8% increase
items.quote: In October, we have taken a hike of another INR 8 in the month of October.

items.statement: PBT margin on total income at 6.03% in Q2 FY27 vs 7.03% in Q1 FY27 and 15.05% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The PBT stood at 6.03% on total income during Q2 FY27 as compared to about 7.03% during Q1 FY27 and 15.05% during Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Management acknowledges currently at lowest margin in business cycle
items.quote: I would say that we are at the lowest margin now, actually.

items.statement: Farmers continuing culture due to comfortable farm gate prices; restocking in November expected to improve feed consumption in Q3 and Q4
items.quote: But since the farm gate prices are comfortable, stable now, the farmers are still continuing to have the positive profitability and they are continuing to continue the culture. And of course, there were some shortcomings because of the flights and all, early harvest. But then farmers are again restocking now in the month of November. And we expect that in the current quarter and also in the first

items.statement: Early harvest due to cyclones led to restocking; feed consumption expected to be higher in Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027)
items.quote: the farmers have taken to stop now, they may continue for under, say, maybe 60 to 90 days, depending upon growth and other subject to other conditions that no more cyclones and no more diseases, etc. So, with that, the consumption of feed also is likely to be more in the first three months of 2027, which happens to be at Q4

items.statement: Antidumping duty revised to 5.53%, countervailing duty 5.77%, Section 301 tariff 10%; total ~21% import duties into US
items.quote: So currently, the export duties, like, especially for USDA, so the company is paying antidumping duty at the rate of 5.53%, countervailing duty at the rate of 5.77% and Section 301 tariff at the rate of 10%. So overall, the company is paying around 21% in terms of import duties into U. S.

items.statement: Company appealed antidumping duty revision, provision made; expects duty may reduce in next review
items.quote: So, we felt that it came out higher than it should have on consultation with a lawyer and everything. So, we did put an appeal, but we made a provision for that. So that said, yes, it is surprising that it went up. But the good point is that it's retrospective, so we hope that it goes down in the next review.

items.statement: Represented to government for quota restrictions on fish meal exports to ensure domestic availability; also requested short-term soya bean meal import permission
items.quote: So, the Aquaculture Feed Manufacturers Association have represented to the government to bring in some sort of a controlling mechanism because the availability of fish meal for shrimp culture in India is inadequate. So, because there's big chunk of this is being exported outside the country. So, we have made a representation and some quota restrictions like so much should be available for the Indi

items.statement: Land purchased near Hyderabad for pet food plant; land conversion and consent for establishment approvals obtained; construction to commence
items.quote: As informed earlier, the company has purchased land near Hyderabad for establishing a state-of-the-art pet food manufacturing facility and completed land conversion from agriculture to non-agriculture. The company also obtained the requisite consent for establishment approvals from the concerned government authorities and now planning to commence the construction activity.

items.statement: US largest export market at 33%; China 21%, EU 17%, Southeast Asia 11%, Japan 5%, Middle East 3%, others 10%
items.quote: USA was the largest importer with 33% of frozen shrimp, followed by China 21%, European Union 17%, Southeast Asia 11%, Japan 5%, Middle East 3%, and all other countries put together 10%.

items.statement: Focusing on value-added products and diversifying to Japan, EU, Middle East, Korea to reduce US dependence; achieving significant success
items.quote: The company has been focusing on value added products and also diversify into other markets such as Japan, EU, Middle East, and Korea to reduce dependence on U. S. Market. The company has been achieving significant success in this direction.

items.statement: China has lower margin profile vs US; other markets vary by customer profile; US not necessarily most lucrative due to duties
items.quote: So generally, since you mentioned with China, China has its own processing factories. So, they produce their own shrimp, Indian companies just supply them raw material. So generally, lower margin profile compared to the U.S. And compared to other markets, it really depends, cannot say specifically that this particular market has higher margin. It usually depends on the customer profile in each mar

items.statement: El Nino impact on fish meal and soya bean supply likely to continue till March-April; prices expected to remain challenging rest of year
items.quote: Overall, we see that the March, April till that El Nino effect is likely to be there, and this may have an impact on the natural products such as vegetable crops and also the fish meal. If the prices are likely to be a little challenging for the rest of the year, we may not expect a big reduction in the prices.

items.statement: Cyclones, floods, disease reduced shrimp production; exports revised down from 19,000 MT to 17,500 MT for FY27
items.quote: However, basing on the overall performance in the first half year and forecast for the rest of the year, it is expected that the exports in FY27 would be around 17,500 MT. The decrease in exports is anticipated due to reduced production of shrimp on account of impact of cyclones, floods, and disease in some areas.

items.statement: Cash surplus used for working capital to build raw material inventory amid price volatility; funds kept in short deposits and mutual funds; no distribution planned
items.quote: What has happened in the last few last month, number of times the prices negotiations were made with the government and discussions with the farmers and all, lot of fluctuations were there. And during that time, the raw material prices were going up, and we have to hold lot of inventory for raw material inventory for the purpose of production for the current and the next early first crop also beca

items.statement: PetCare Q2 FY27 sales INR 202 lakh vs INR 180 lakh in Q1 FY27; growth in cat and dog food segments
items.quote: Q2 FY2627, sales increased to INR 202 lakh as compared to INR 180 lakhs in Q1 FY2627 reflecting continued growth in both cat food and dog food segment.

items.statement: US Supreme Court ruled reciprocal tariffs not legal; refund mechanism exists but bank account entries not yet liquidated; no timeline for refund
items.quote: Yes. So, the U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that the reciprocal tariffs, were not legal. So, there is a refund mechanism. So, we did open our bank account, but the entries have not been liquidated yet. That means that the tariffs have not been refunded yet. So, you know with regulatory, we don't know exactly the time lines. They haven't mentioned so. So right now, we haven't received a bulk of the p

items.statement: Fish feed project delayed due to low-cost competition and profitability concerns; evaluating which fish feed type is more profitable
items.quote: Yes. See, it's very difficult because low-cost fish feed is available in India in plenty. There are number of, maybe I would say, feed mill and it is something like a backyard fish feed facility almost everyone will have. So, with that the sustainability and profitability of the Fish Feed Project is in a big question. So that's why we are not able to take a firm decision to go ahead on that, and w

items.statement: JMD states current fish meal INR 210/kg, soya bean meal INR 90/kg, wheat flour INR 36/kg are exorbitant; urges government intervention
items.quote: Then the present prices of fish meal at INR 210 per kg, soya bean meal at INR 90 per kg, and wheat flour at INR 36 per kg are exorbitant, and the cost of production of feed increases steeply.

items.statement: Feed division EBITDA per kg around INR 3 in Q2; management cannot predict if it will reach INR 5 given raw material volatility and off-season
items.quote: Under the profitability, again, the raw material prices may play a major role. And also, this is not the peak season for the aquaculture. So, it all depends. So, we cannot say, like, whether it'll be five or three or two.

items.statement: Revised FY27 consolidated revenue guidance INR 205-210 crore and EBITDA INR 10-12 crore
items.quote: FY '27, the revised consolidated revenue probably will do about between INR 205 crores to INR 210 crores. And revised consolidated EBITDA will be about INR 10 crores to INR 12 crores.

items.statement: FY28 consolidated revenue target INR 280 crore and EBITDA INR 35 crore
items.quote: FY '28, this could go up to about INR 280 crore, and revised EBITDA could be about INR 60 crores. No, capsule business would be say 230. Plus here consolidated EBITDA, EBITDA would be, we are saying the cash income, roughly about INR 35 crores.

items.statement: API business FY27 revenue revised to INR 12-15 crore from earlier INR 70-80 crore
items.quote: Therefore, this INR 70 crore to INR 80 crore of revenue that we had forecast is going to take a dip, and we are now forecasting something about INR 12 crores to INR 15 crores.

items.statement: API subsidiary cash breakeven expected FY28, revenue breakeven FY29
items.quote: Cash breakeven we are expecting in FY '28 itself and revenue breakeven in FY '29.

items.statement: API subsidiary cash breakeven revenue level INR 120 crore
items.quote: I would say cash breakeven would be in the range of about INR 120 crores top line revenue.

items.statement: Long-term API target INR 250 crore revenue with 20% EBITDA margin by FY29-30
items.quote: Our target is that in FY '29 or FY '30, I would rather say, about INR 250 crores of top-line revenue with about 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Gelatin capsule demand firm; added new customers including Mankind Pharma and passed Zydus Lifesciences audit
items.quote: Demand for gelatin capsules remained firm, and we added several new customers in the quarter. Mankind Pharma came on board, and we successfully completed an audit by Zydus Lifesciences.

items.statement: US demand for HPMC capsules still absent; converted HPMC lines to gelatin to protect utilization
items.quote: With the U.S. demand still absent, that will not happen. We chose to protect utilization and profitability rather than hold capacity idle for a market that has not returned.

items.statement: Capsule business EBITDA margin 14-16%, can go to 17%; consolidated EBITDA margin 4-5% in FY27
items.quote: On consolidated basis, the EBITDA margins in our capsule business are in the range of 16% at the moment, 14% to 16%, which can go up to 17% as well. Whereas an API business, it is on negative side now at the moment. So consolidated basis, we are doing roughly around in terms of percentage, it would be like about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: COPP filings for 7 products; 4 validations done, rest by December; all filings complete by March 2027
items.quote: Certificate of Pharmaceutical Products, COPP, filings for 7 products. Validation has been completed for 4. Remaining filings are scheduled for December. Remaining validations are scheduled for December, and we expect the process of all filings to be complete by March 27.

items.statement: Pipeline of 16 molecules for US DMF and European CEP; 8 filings in FY28, 8 in FY29; US FDA audit expected Q1 FY29
items.quote: Regulated markets, we have planned a pipeline of 16 molecules for US DMF and European CEP filing. At the moment, we have projected that we will file 8 in FY '28, another 8 in FY '29. We expect a US FDA audit to be conducted by Q1 of FY '29.

items.statement: Building contract manufacturing pipeline for Tumkur facility; new contract signed, discussions ongoing for fermentation and synthesis blocks
items.quote: We are building a broader contract manufacturing pipeline to make full use of our Tumkur facility. We are taking on a contract with a new organization, and discussions with a few other parties are going on.

items.statement: May need additional capex for sterile API block; seeking equity infusion and concessional debt (BIRAC, DBT, foreign institutions)
items.quote: We are planning to put up, say, sterile block, which would require some more CAPEX, and to sustain the cash burn in maybe another 12 to 14 months. Maybe for that period we think that this CAPEX, and we will be doing some fresh equity as well.

items.statement: Second HPMC line being converted to gelatin; will add volumes in H2 FY27
items.quote: The second HPMC line is now being converted and should add volumes in the second half.

items.statement: Expect gelatin prices to rise due to coal/oil prices; will pass increases to customers as done previously
items.quote: We expect gelatin prices to rise as international coal and oil prices increase. Raw material costs may go up in the coming quarters. We have passed such increases on to the customers in the previous quarters. And expect to do so again.

items.statement: European API prices 30-40% higher than Indian; US prices 60-70% higher than Indian
items.quote: Europe prices are at least about, I would say, 30% to 40% higher than the Indian price, and European prices are at least about 60% to 70% higher than the Indian price.

items.statement: Added Mankind Pharma; completed Zydus Lifesciences audit; expect Zydus business in coming quarters
items.quote: Mankind Pharma came on board, and we successfully completed an audit by Zydus Lifesciences. We expect business with Zydus to begin in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Warrants and shares issued to promoters to shore up working capital and fund inorganic acquisition opportunities
items.quote: The warrant and stocks have been issued to promoters. It is just to shore up the working capital and also to look forward for any kind of inorganic acquisition opportunities that may arise.

items.statement: API subsidiary seeking equity infusion and concessional debt (BIRAC, DBT, foreign institutions) for sterile block and cash burn
items.quote: We are talking to Government of India. We have applied for BIRAC and DBT funding. We are also talking to some government institutions in foreign countries where concessional rate of debt could be raised and equity could be brought in.

items.statement: Considering merger with parent to unlock tax losses and GST credits; also evaluated demerger of subsidiary
items.quote: We will consider it at Board level and then make a suitable decision.

items.statement: H1 FY27 operating cash flow INR 7.18 crore; capex INR 3.76 crore; net financing outflow INR 3.20 crore
items.quote: We generated INR 7.18 crores of cash from operations in the half. Capital expenditure was INR 3.76 crores and net financing outflows were INR 3.20 crores.

items.statement: Management expects margin improvement to continue as revenue mix shifts and operational discipline persists
items.quote: And I expect that to continue to exist in the future as we continue to progress.

items.statement: Total EBITDA margin expanded 339 bps QoQ to 13.1% in Q2 FY27 driven by lower operating costs and revenue mix shift
items.quote: Total EBITDA, which includes other income, increased 36.5% to Rs. 158.8 crores QoQ. Total EBITDA margin improved by 339 basis points sequentially to 13.1%.

items.statement: Continuing business delivered high single-digit comparable growth with newer engagements ramping up
items.quote: On a comparable basis, the continuing business delivered high single-digit growth, with newer engagements ramping up, and we continue to improve our delivery efficiency.

items.statement: Pipeline at historically strong levels with shift toward larger, technology-led transformation mandates
items.quote: Our pipeline is at historically strong levels, but it's not simply its size. It is the nature of the work. We are increasingly participating in large pursuits, more technology-led transformation programs, and mandates that bring together multiple HGS capabilities.

items.statement: Added 27 new logos in Q1 FY27 after 79 in FY26; top client 4.6% of revenue, top 10 at 26.1%
items.quote: And just as a recollection, as we said in FY26, was our best year of new signings, adding 79 new logos across BPM and digital and HR operations, which has set us up for a better FY27. And Q1 we have added an additional 27 new logos.

items.statement: Capex measured at Rs. 81.9 crores in H1 FY27; depreciation outpacing additions
items.quote: CAPEX was measured and the cash outflow for the half year was driven by financing interest, lease and borrowing repayments and dividends.

items.statement: Established HGS MENA IT Consulting LLC in Dubai to build technology and consulting capability
items.quote: In Q1 we have incorporated as HGS, MENA IT Consulting, LLC in Dubai to build technology and consulting capability.

items.statement: Operating expenses reduced Rs. 29 crores QoQ while revenue increased Rs. 26 crores, showing delivery efficiency
items.quote: From a cost and efficiency perspective, operating expenses came down to Rs. 1,055.7 crores from Rs. 1,084.9 crores in Q1. A reduction of about Rs. 29 crores while revenue went up by Rs. 26 crores.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting toward multi-tower, technology-led deals; CX Services 54%, Digital and Media 46%
items.quote: There is a shift towards multi-tower outcome-based deals. And the broad delivery footprints across India, Philippines, and the West is what allows us to price and deliver those deals competitively.

items.statement: DSO increased to 68 days in Q2 FY27 from 61 days in Q2 FY26; trade receivables down to Rs. 800.1 crores from Rs. 871.8 crores in March
items.quote: DSO is at 68 days in Q2 FY27. as against 61 days in Q2 of FY26. As I just read in the balance sheet, the receivables have come down to Rs. 800.1 crores from Rs. 871.8 crores in March.

items.statement: Operating cash flow positive at Rs. 108.4 crores in H1 FY27 despite pre-tax loss
items.quote: Cash from operating activities was an inflow of Rs. 108.4 crores in H1 and for the full year FY26 it was an inflow of Rs. 412.6 crores. Operations are generating cash in both the periods.

items.statement: Total borrowings increased to Rs. 1,406 crores from Rs. 1,294 crores in March 2026
items.quote: Total borrowings are at Rs. 1,406 crores between both non-current and current against Rs. 1,294 crores in March.

items.statement: Dividend of Rs. 20.2 crores paid in H1 FY27 following final dividend recommended at June results
items.quote: Financing outflow was Rs. 169.5 crores, interest paid Rs. 84 crores and lease liabilities and borrowings at Rs. 65.3 crores and dividend paid of Rs. 20.2 crores.

items.statement: Broadband revenue up 8% YoY in H1 FY27 on 6% subscriber growth; >100 Mbps pack share rose to 13.5% from 10.4%
items.quote: Broadband, as you know, is pretty much a sunrise industry. And as digital inclusion increases, broadband proliferation will continue to grow significantly because, even as you know, with over 300 million households, barely just over 50 million households are connected with wired broadband. So, we have already seen traction of about 8% growth in revenues in H1 of this year.

items.statement: Project Ganga operationalized 16 networks with 200 paying customers; target 8,000-10,000 digital service providers in 2 years connecting 20 lakh households
items.quote: As of date, we have trained over 1,221 applicants, and we have got over 4,000 applicants as of today. And 355 of these trained applicants have filed their application with CM YUVA for securing their loan, as you know, it's an interest-free, collateral-free loan from the government of Uttar Pradesh in its endeavor to ensure digital inclusion and social transformation, of creating a new breed of ent

items.statement: DTV business faces structural decline and subscriber churn globally; broadband growth and cost optimization are key offsets
items.quote: The challenge, there is no doubt, is that the media business continues to face profitability pressures because traditional digital cable TV is, in fact, a declining industry globally, not just in India. Experiencing a much broader shift, if you look at it just you yourself as consumers move towards online streaming, a reality where every single industry player is facing significant subscriber chur

items.statement: Management clarified RPTs are disclosed per accounting standards; denied existence of quasi-RPTs
items.quote: Just to continue on what Venk said and also just to clarify, there are RPTs, but there is nothing like a quasi-RPT. So, whatever is required in line with accounting standards, we are disclosing that as RPT transactions.

items.statement: Uneven rainfall and drought-like conditions impacted agricultural activity and farmer purchasing decisions in H1 FY27.
items.quote: The uneven distribution of rainfall and drought-like conditions in certain regions have impacted the seed industry, with their effects visible across both revenue and profitability.

items.statement: June 2026 rainfall was 35% below normal per IMD, with uneven distribution affecting crop patterns and farmer sentiment.
items.quote: According to the India Meteorological Department, rainfall during June '26 was 35% below normal, while others reported a deficit of 16%.

items.statement: Paddy emerged as largest crop contributor at 37% of sales; cotton contributed 26%, Bajra 13%, maize 6% in H1 FY27.
items.quote: Paddy emerged as our largest contributor, accounting for approximately 37% of overall sales, while Bajra contributed around 13%, followed by maize at 6% to the total sales.

items.statement: Cotton sales volumes declined 2.29% YoY to 1.06 million packets in H1 FY27 due to unfavorable weather.
items.quote: Sales volumes stood at approximately 1.06 million packets, reflecting a decline of 2.29% YoY.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 11.4% from 14.4% YoY in H1 FY27 due to crop mix and higher trade schemes.
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR 410 million compared with INR 461 million in the corresponding period for the last year, with EBITDA margins at approximately 11.4% compared with 14.4% last year.

items.statement: Additional INR 5 crore trade schemes given to maintain top line impacted EBITDA in H1 FY27.
items.quote: This year, being a specific year wherein there were market liquidity areas and there were issues because of the war and some of the things actually affecting all over, if you go through our quarterly, you will find that we have given at least INR 5 crores additional to the market for ensuring the top line.

items.statement: Excess cotton seed inventory to be liquidated over next 2-3 years; no quality issues expected.
items.quote: We have already initiated measures to rationalize cotton production and expect to gradually liquidate the excess inventory over the next two to three years. We do not expect any quality issues in the cotton seed, which is sturdy in nature.

items.statement: Net cash flow from operating activities was negative in H1 FY27 due to higher receivables and inventory.
items.quote: Consequently, net cash flow from the operating activities stood at negative at the end of first half.

items.statement: Interest cost rose by INR 3.5-4 crore due to higher working capital borrowings for stock buildup; blended cost ~9%.
items.quote: But because of the stock buildup, we needed more funds. So, we have taken more money from the banking channel, working capital. Hence, the rise in the interest overall. That is another thing which has beaten my net profit margin or net profit, not margin. Almost about INR 3.5-4 crore has gone more as interest only.

items.statement: Cotton volumes expected to grow 20-30% next year driven by higher cotton prices (INR 9,500-10,500 vs INR 7,500).
items.quote: Next year, cotton, we are expecting to grow by 20-30%, because the commercial prices are very good. If you see last year, it was around INR 7,500, and now it is going in between for INR 9,500-10,500.

items.statement: Corn (maize) acreage expected to grow at least 20% in 2027-28 over 2026-27 due to higher commercial prices.
items.quote: And this year again in 2027-28, we are expecting at least 20% growth over 2026-27 in corn next year.

items.statement: Targeting INR 100 crore net profit at ~14% net margin, likely achievable around INR 750 crore revenue.
items.quote: But as I made it a statement earlier, that as long as the top line is growing, the bottom line will automatically follow. If not today, then tomorrow. But we agree with you that we are also desirous of making that figure. Let's work towards it.

items.statement: Trade scheme payout expected to normalize to 26-28% next year from higher levels this year, saving ~4% margin.
items.quote: Next year, they'll come down to around 26%, 27%, 28%. We save 4% there also. So, the bottom line rises.

items.statement: Illegal BT cotton estimated at 20-25% of total market sales, concentrated in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana.
items.quote: In legal, there are no data, but there are estimates of 25%. 20-25% of the total sales is accounted by this illegal BT sales. The majority is, let's say, happening in Gujarat and also in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana.

items.statement: Uzbekistan JV (90% owned) clocked INR 15 crore revenue in FY26; INR 9 crore in H1 FY27 consolidated.
items.quote: Uzbekistan, in March, we clocked the INR 15 crore top line, and that was given in the consolidated results. If you go through the consolidated results of H1, you'll find INR 9 crore of sales attributed in the consolidated results to Uzbekistan.

items.statement: Uzbekistan JV Bt cotton soft launch targeted for 2028; local variety conversion agreement signed with government.
items.quote: Nath Bio-Genes Central Asia has signed agreement with the government of Uzbekistan to convert their local varieties into a Bt-GT versions, and we are on the way to it. Our first soft launch will be on 2028.

items.statement: Key climate-resilient hybrids: Cotton (Sanket, Rana), Paddy (Tata, Tata Gold, Gurukripa), Pearl Millet (Super Surprise), Mustard hybrid for production next season.
items.quote: We have our well-performing hybrids in cotton called Sanket and Rana. Sanket is one unique hybrid which has passed a high rainfall year and as well as drought year. And in both the places, it has been performing very well. It's one of the most climate-resilient hybrids.

items.statement: Network strengthening via big distributor appointments and manpower hiring focused on corn, hybrid paddy, Bajra markets.
items.quote: So, network strengthening is our main thrust activity, number one. Number two is, we are already strengthening across India our manpower. If you see our new hirings, we are concentrating, focusing more on corn markets and even hybrid paddy and Bajra markets.

items.statement: Cotton MSP increased ~7% for 2026-27 season; commodity prices up 30-40% YoY supporting farmer purchasing power.
items.quote: The minimum support price for cotton for the year 2026-27 season has been increased by approximately 7%, which can provide support to farmer realization. Commodity prices are all-time high, reflecting an increase of 30-40% over last year.

items.statement: Exports minimal (<INR 10 crore/year) to Egypt, Sudan; not a focus for top line growth.
items.quote: As regards exports, we have always maintained that our exports are minimal, to the extent of not more than INR 5-7 crores or INR 8 crores every year, less than INR 10 crores in any case.

items.statement: El Nino conditions expected to strengthen through winter; soil moisture and water availability will shape Rabi sowings.
items.quote: The monsoon entered below normal and El Nino conditions are expected to strengthen through the winter. So, soil moisture and water availability will shape sowings going ahead.

items.statement: New hirings focused on corn, hybrid paddy, and Bajra markets to support diversification.
items.quote: Number two is, we are already strengthening across India our manpower. If you see our new hirings, we are concentrating, focusing more on corn markets and even hybrid paddy and Bajra markets.

items.statement: Targets INR1,000 crores revenue by FY30 with 90% from dairy and 10% from other categories led by RTE/RTC exports
items.quote: You have given an ambitious target of INR1,000 crores in revenue by FY30 alongside doubling your manufacturing facility.

items.statement: INR10 crores capex underway for next summer demand including new machinery and 3D shaped product capacity
items.quote: We are doing in capex in the range of around INR10 crores for us to meet the demand for next summer.

items.statement: Next larger expansion to be funded by mix of debt and equity; current expansion funded by internal capital and debt
items.quote: The next expansion will be a bigger expansion in order to meet our next target, and that will be a mix of debt and equity.

items.statement: RTE/RTC plant currently at 40% utilization, expected to reach 100% in 2 years with space for rapid machinery addition
items.quote: Currently, we are utilizing about 40% of the capacity, and in 2 years of time frame, we will be at 100% utilization of our ready-to-eat, ready-to-cook plant.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 39.8% in Q2 FY27 from 35.1% in Q2 FY26; focus on procurement, efficiency, mix and pricing
items.quote: Gross margin in Q2 FY27 improved to 39.8% compared with 35.1% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Over 80% of milk price increase passed to consumers via price or quantity revision; paneer demand boosted by analog paneer ban
items.quote: Ultimately, we have about more than 80% of the price gap being carried forward to the consumer, either in the form of price revision or else quantity revision.

items.statement: Export margins better than domestic; increasing export share expected to lift overall margins
items.quote: It gives a better margin in comparison to the domestic business.

items.statement: Winter arrived late this year reducing seasonal consumption dip; metro markets show strong ice cream demand
items.quote: Winter has been quite late, so that the change in weather has led to, you know, a lower spike in consumption.

items.statement: Revenue split 90% milk/milk products (ice cream, paneer, ghee, sweets) and 10% other categories led by RTE/RTC exports
items.quote: 90% will be dairy products, milk, and milk segment, which includes ice cream and variated dairy products such as paneer, ghee, shrikhand, and all Indian sweets.

items.statement: Samosa in RTE segment receiving strong global response; milk products and RTE are key growth drivers
items.quote: In RTE, specifically, samosa has been a very good product for us, which is receiving good response across the globe.

items.statement: 35% revenue from outside Gujarat, 65% from Gujarat; targeting deeper distribution in existing states and expansion to new states
items.quote: 35% of our revenue comes from the states other than Gujarat. 65% is the split with Gujarat.

items.statement: Exports ~5% of sales last year, growing steadily; export customers primarily Indian diaspora; separate team and processes being built
items.quote: Last year, about 5% of our sales was from the exports business, and it is growing year on year.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle 228 days in H1 FY27 vs 212 days in FY26; focus on inventory discipline, receivables and working capital efficiency
items.quote: Our cash conversion cycle was 228 days in H1 FY27, compared to 212 days in FY26.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 0.6x in H1 FY27 vs 0.3x in FY26; current ratio 2.3x
items.quote: As of H1 FY2027, our debt-equity ratio stood at 0.6x, compared with 0.3x in FY26, while our current ratio stood at 2.3x.

items.statement: Milk procurement 1.5 lakh litres/day in summer, 70-80k litres/day off-season; sourced via exclusive aggregators and BMC points near Gir region
items.quote: In summers, it goes up to 1.5 lakh liters of milk per day, whereas in the time other than summers, it goes around 70,000 to 80,000 liters of milk procurement per day.

items.statement: Renewable energy share increased from 40% to 75% in 2 years; targeting 90% via solar and wind; will factor into next expansion capex
items.quote: Earlier, if you see, 2 years ago, it was about 40%, and from that, we have reached to this stage. And moving forward, when we do the next expansion, we will keep this as a factor for us in capex as well.

items.statement: Board approved 1:2 stock split (INR10 to INR5 face value) and 5:1 bonus issue; each existing share becomes 12 shares; authorised capital raised to INR68.5 crores
items.quote: The Board has approved a subdivision of our equity shares, whereby one equity share with a face value of INR10 will be split into two equity shares with a face value of INR5 each. Following this split, to further widen our retail investor base, the Board has recommended a bonus issue in the ratio of 5:1.

items.statement: Key operating metrics to track: volume growth, revenue outside Gujarat, channel-wise contribution, capacity utilisation, repeat sales in new categories
items.quote: Key operating indicators can include the volume growth, revenue outside our core market of Gujarat state, channel-wise contribution, capacity utilization, and repeat sales in newer categories.

items.statement: Deploying 10,000 freezers nationally in FY27, >50% already done; GT market primary focus, quick commerce secondary, outlets third
items.quote: This year, we have targeted to deploy about 10,000 freezers across the country and more than 50% of deployment has been already done.

items.statement: Super stockist model minimises risk; logistics cost squeezes margins in distant states; plan child plants in high-revenue states to protect margins
items.quote: Once we received a considerable amount of revenue from an individual state, then we'll set up a child plant over there itself, from where the high value or high-volume products can be catered directly from the local state itself.

items.statement: Premiumisation via higher milk fat (8-10% vs 5%) and new 3D shaped products; premium products priced above INR30 pass cost increases directly to consumers
items.quote: Supposedly, earlier the product was available of 5% milk fat, we are trying to give a product of 8% or 10% milk fat in the product itself.

items.statement: Government ban on analog paneer boosted demand for pure milk paneer, aiding placement and consumption
items.quote: Overall, what has happened recently is the government has banned analog paneer. So as a result, what happened is the demand and consumption for the paneer made from pure milk has increased.

items.statement: R&D team working on protein-enriched products using whey from paneer; machinery additions being finalised
items.quote: Our team is in working in bringing this new products into our product range, and but that will be going through the existing distribution mode only.

items.statement: Launched 4 new products in Q2 FY27: Jumbo Mango Dolly, Jumbo Chocobar, Red Velvet and Pista Kunafa candies
items.quote: During the quarter we launched four new products. Two were premiumization of existing product range such as Jumbo Mango Dolly and Jumbo Chocobar and two new SKUs and new flavors that was in the Red Velvet and Pista Kunafa candy segment.

items.statement: Standalone double-digit EBITDA margin targeted for FY27
items.quote: So with respect to the guidance level, I think we have said that we'll at standalone level, we'll be doing around double-digit EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 9-10% for FY27
items.quote: We'll continue to maintain 9% to 10% on consolidated level for FY27.

items.statement: Indian steel production growing healthily; domestic demand resilient
items.quote: During H1FY27, India's crude steel production continued to register healthy growth while finished steel consumption grew at a fa ster pace, reflecting healthy underlying domestic demand

items.statement: USA steel production up 6% YoY YTD October 2026
items.quote: USA steel production growth is robust, 6% growth year-on-year at 75 million metric ton YTD October '26 compared with the corresponding previous period.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin declined to 43.9% in Q2 FY27 from 45.2% YoY due to higher input costs
items.quote: Gross margin for Quarter 2 FY27 stood at 43.9% compared with 45.2% in corresponding quarter last year. The decline was primarily attributable to higher raw material and input cost.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved marginally to 48.9% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Gross margin for Quarter 2 FY27 stood at 48.9% compared with 48.6% in Quarter 2 FY26, indicating a marginal improvement.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 10.8% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for Quarter 2 FY27 stood at approximately INR35 crores compared with INR37 crores in Quarter 2 FY26, while EBITDA margin st ood at 10.8

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 9.2% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for Quarter 2 FY27 increased to approximately INR51 crores, registering a grow th of around 28% year-on-year, with EBITDA margin improving to 9.2

items.statement: Export revenue grew 40% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Export revenue has shown a sharp surge in and grew by 40% year-on-year, increasing operational efficiency and visibility help us form an optimistic view going forward.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 5% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: The do mestic business continued to demonstrate a strong momentum, delivering 5% year-on-year growth in Q2 FY27

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR40-50 crores for FY27
items.quote: We'll be doing around, around INR40 crores to INR50 crores of capex.

items.statement: India capacity utilization at 60-70%
items.quote: It is around 60% to 70%.

items.statement: New tap hole clay plant in Tianjin, China with 2,000 MT capacity and INR20-25 crore revenue potential
items.quote: The facility has an installed capacity of 2,000 metric tons per annum and is designed to manufacture pitch-free, tar-free tap hole clay for blast furnac e applications. The plant is strategically positioned to serve customers across the region and is expected to unlock annual revenue potential of approximately INR20 crores to INR25 crores at full utilization

items.statement: Small capacity additions underway for existing product lines
items.quote: Yes, in some area we are going with some small capacity addition with existing product line.

items.statement: Debottlenecking for a couple of product lines; ample capacity otherwise
items.quote: I think we mentioned for a couple of product lines we are working on debottlenecking. Otherwise, we have ample capacity.

items.statement: Raw material prices (alumina, resin bonded material, magnesia) increasing due to war; customer support for price increases
items.quote: Again, because of this war and all the alumin a and the resin bonded ma terial and magnesia all are increasing and as mentioned by Rawal-ji and Manoj-ji, that customer is supporting us in getting the price increases on account of this

items.statement: Pricing contracts negotiated periodically; bespoke products built into costing
items.quote: So pricing, generally all the contracts what we have with the customers, you can split it in 2 parts. Like in India, most of them management and service contracts or refractory management contracts. So those are negotiated periodically, a nd then with the cost pressures, we have to approach the customers to get the increases

items.statement: Export growth driven by Middle East, Turkey and Asia; Europe subdued
items.quote: I think as Rawal-ji said that we are working with Middle East, Asia, it's contributing a larger portion, and we are good with Europe also as of now, with some pressure from there off because of this economies. So, our export is equally ev enly distributed but has a upper hand on Middle East and Turkey and Asia

items.statement: European business returned to positive segment result in Q2
items.quote: During Q2, the European business returned to a positive segment result compared with a loss in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: US operations delivered strong revenue growth and significant profitability improvement
items.quote: Our American business record ed strong revenue growth during the quarter, accompanied by a significant improvement in segment profitability

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved significantly in H1FY27 due to better receivables, inventory control and working capital discipline
items.quote: Operating cash flows have improved significantly compared with the previous year, supported by better management of receivables, improved inventory control and greater discipline in working capital utilization.

items.statement: Consolidated cash flow increased by ~INR68 crores in H1FY27 vs ~INR8 crores YoY
items.quote: Further talking about consolidated cash flow, cash flow shown a drastic improvement, increased by approximately IN R68 crores during H1FY27 compared with approximately INR8 crores in corresponding pe riod last year

items.statement: JV with Marvel International Group and Marvel Refractories (Anshan) terminated effective Oct 14, 2026; investment impaired by INR1.69 crores
items.quote: As a part of our ongoing portfolio and strategic review, the company has mutually agreed to terminate the joint venture arrangement with Marvels International Group Company Limited and Marvel Refractories (Anshan) Company Limited effective October 14th, 2026.

items.statement: Voluntary liquidation of Hofmann Ceramic Czech Republic completed July 1, 2026
items.quote: The voluntary liquidation of Hofmann Ceramic in Czech Republic was completed with effect from July 1st, 2026, as part of our ongoing efforts to rationalize the group structure.

items.statement: Sheffield Refractories technology transfer Phase 1 complete; Phase 2 equipment ordered for delivery by Dec 2026 and Feb-Mar 2027; revenue expected FY28
items.quote: We have already do ne the marketing and sales pitch jointly from 2 experts from Sheffield Refractor ies who are in India and our technical team, we've done the presentations everywhere and received a very positive response from all the customers and hopefully, this financial I mean, not this year, but in next year, that is '27-'28, we should be able to see growth in this area on a very good positi

items.statement: Continuing diversification into non-ferrous industry despite Marvel JV termination
items.quote: We are still into diversification. We are still catering to the non-ferrous industry. But this particular product, we will have to further evaluate it. But other products, we are still catering to them.

items.statement: Standalone total income INR325 crores in Q2 FY27, up 13% YoY
items.quote: Total income for Quarter 2 FY27 stood at approximately INR325 crores, registering growth of around 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated total income INR555 crores in Q2 FY27, up 13% YoY
items.quote: Total income for Quarter 2 FY27 stood at approximately INR555 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of around 13%.

items.statement: Standalone PAT INR18 crores in Q2 FY27, up 23% YoY
items.quote: PAT for Quarter 2 FY27 stood at approximately INR18 crores, registering a growth of 23% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT INR26 crores in Q2 FY27, up 103% YoY
items.quote: PAT for Quarter 2 FY27 increased significantly to approximately INR26 crores compared with approximately INR13 crores in corresponding quarter last year, registering a growth of around 103%.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, trade issues, supply chain constraints and elevated input costs persist
items.quote: The industry continues to navigate challenges arising from geopolitical developments, trade- related uncertainties, supply chain constraint s and elevated input costs

items.statement: Global supply chain disruptions and freight cost increases causing challenges; actively mitigating with customers
items.quote: During the period as we all know, the global supply chain disruptions and freight cost increases compounded by increased lead times are causing much grief to one and all, and we are not insulated from the same, and we are taking every effort to mitigate the same as much as possible with active discussions and cooperation from our customers.

items.statement: Mature projects concluded causing sequential revenue decline; enterprise pipeline traction with customer discussions, evaluation and onboarding underway
items.quote: While some mature projects concluded during the period, resulting in lower sequential revenue, we made steady progress in product development, commercialization initiatives and customers onboarding.

items.statement: Expect enterprise engagements to contribute progressively as they move into production deployment
items.quote: We expect these engagements to contribute progressively as they move into the production deployment.

In October it received APR Design Recognition for Recyclability from Association of Plastic Recyclers in the United States. Together with the CIPET Certification we already held in India, RecTech™ is now independently validated across India, Europe and United States.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on PET films erased 5% cost gap; RecTech™ film now marginally cheaper than PET-PE with better performance and full recyclability certification

In fact, RecTech™ film is marginally cheaper than PET-PE film, delivering better performance and at the same time fully certified as recyclable.

items.statement: Converting division has ~4-5% global market share, presence in ~90 countries; focusing on spares/service revenue from installed base
items.quote: in the converting business, we have 4%-5% global market share. So, is there any opportunity to increase this further and are we taking any efforts for that? Thank you. Rajashekar Venkat: Yes, there is a lot of efforts and strategies. items.statement: Trade receivables aging reduced from Rs. 20 cr to Rs. 12 cr; most overdue amounts recovered with clear plan for remainder
items.quote: Most of that has been received because currently our total aging is close to Rs. 12 crores. So, most of the debt that you see has been recovered and whatever is remainder even in this, we have clear plans to recover from the market.

items.statement: All backlog orders secured with advances; no order cancellations, only delivery deferrals confirmed for H2
items.quote: We don't have any orders which are cancelled while there has been delayed delivery demand from customers and we definitely have advances secured against all the orders. Without advances, we don't even log the orders in the system.

items.quote: We have one 9-layer plant scheduled for dispatch in H2. We also have one plant which is already ready and awaiting customer clearance for dispatch. We have additional 3 more plants in the pipeline which would come under manufacturing and dispatch in H2.

items.statement: Packaging division targets 30-40% domestic growth for FY27; expects segment growth despite US headwinds driven by domestic and ROW
items.quote: Yes, it does. As I mentioned, we have a strong pipeline and it continues to remain strong for us. The shortfall in H1 in execution was again mainly two reasons. One is the US, which continues to have persistent headwinds and leading to the shortfall. And the domestic market has come back strong.

items.statement: RecTech™ global opportunity: 1% conversion of PET-PE to RecTech™ equals ~USD 3 billion material purchase value for FMCGs
items.quote: Even if we consider even just 1% of PET-PE getting converted to RecTech™ globally, the value of that material in terms of purchase cost to FMCG companies close to USD3 billion.

items.quote: And in case if there is a price variation, for example, if raw material prices goes up, then yes, it has a direct impact on the end customers' pricing as well of the equipment that they buy from us. items.quote: We have created a call center that is running on AI, which is routing that if you have to place an order in Gurugram or Delhi, which outlet's number you need, it is one number of ours which is centralized and running through AI. So, the growth study we did after our IPO, we have increased our sales from 11% to 15%-16% today.

items.statement: Aggregators (Zomato, Swiggy) support new 'Maa Ka Khana' brand with zero advertising cost for 3-6 months; live cooking differentiates from frozen competitors
items.quote: The aggregator has made a settlement with us that wherever you will bring this brand, there will be no advertising cost for us on that, they will just give us linger on for 3 to 6 months that you expand it, so we will set up 15 to 20 outlets, 15 to 18 outlets in Delhi NCR as soon as possible.

items.statement: Daily orders per mature outlet ~1,000; AOV ~INR 350-400; KPT 15-20 minutes

items.quote: Each person owns five kitchens and tackles the entire kitchen work for five to six kitchens, and we reach a conclusion at 6:00 PM. And in that conclusion, we also have how much of our dairy was consumed, how much our vegetable cost was.

items.statement: Expansion to Punjab, Agra, Jaipur planned but sequenced after achieving INR 1 crore daily in Delhi-NCR to protect margins and supply chain
items.quote: I will proceed in the same way as the rabbit and tortoise story. Since 2013, I have been operating this way, and I will continue to do so. This is a race between the rabbit and the tortoise, and I am following the same.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 revenue target of INR400 crores despite slower ramp-up
items.quote: I think we should not revise this target. I mean and it should be possible to achieve it the way the things are getting scaled up and the way we are trying to address this inventory issue, small, small component as I mentioned.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA to turn positive in Q3 or Q4 FY27
items.quote: We should see this very well in the fourth quarter. I think if the gods support us, I think third quarter itself you might see this positive happening.

items.statement: Received new order of approximately INR275 crores from Indian Railways
items.quote: And I am sure you would have seen, approximately INR275 crores order that we just received, I think about two days ago.

items.statement: Order visibility of INR1,000 to INR1,200 crores for locomotive propulsion systems
items.quote: You mentioned about INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores. Yes, we will -- we should do this kind of turnover very naturally next year from the locomotive propulsion system as a product.

items.statement: Unit 2 factory expected to be fully operational by 15th December 2026
items.quote: Now the second one, the second factory, which we call this as Unit 2 is under execution as of now and we hope that by 15th of December or third week of December, we will have that factory also fully built and fully prepared to produce and supply propulsion systems from that unit as well.

items.statement: Unit 3 at Gwalior 10-acre land allocated, execution to start January-February 2027
items.quote: And finally, we are allocated a land of 10 acres at Gwalior MP IIDC industrial area. A formal ceremony is scheduled on tomorrow, that will be chaired by the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh and there we shall receive our letter of intent for allotment letter, you can say, for the 10-acre land which is taken to execute our propulsion system and new projects that we foresee in that particular place.

items.statement: Unit 2 capacity of 50 propulsion systems per month, plans to run at 40 per month for stability
items.quote: If you leave aside Unit 3, even at Unit 2 level, we will have a capacity to do 50 propulsion systems per month, but we will not utilize to do more than 40 propulsion systems as such so that we remain very very stable in terms of producing this thing.

items.statement: MEMU/EMU propulsion system prototype expected Q2-Q3 CY2027, followed by RDSO trials
items.quote: The development or the prototype development, the first propulsion system of the MEMU trains is expected about second quarter or third quarter of the calendar year next, 2027. And after which the trials or the prototype testing as a regular practice will start by RDSO or Indian Railways after that.

items.statement: Automatic fault locator for rail electrification under TOT with South Korean company, prototype testing imminent
items.quote: One very important product in this category is automatic fault locator, which locates the faults in electrical lines and automatically convey this to the concerned division. So these automatic fault locators are being or basically planned to be manufactured in TOT, transfer of technology agreement with a South Korean company. The systems are ready and the products are offered for prototype testing

items.statement: Component costs decreasing with volume scale-up; value engineering to further reduce propulsion system cost
items.quote: And now we are coming into ambitious base, we are ordering bigger quantity. You will see a significant price reduction of the components or raw materials. And further, this is not going to end. There will be a lot of value engineering which are pending, which will again reduce the price of the overall propulsion system.

items.statement: Raw material price fluctuations passed through via IEEE-based formula in Indian Railways purchase orders
items.quote: There is a very beautiful formula which is orchestrated by Indian Railways and they have used this formula from an association called IEEE, which will very clearly define the impact on the propulsion system by increase or decrease of these important commodities. So if, in say, for instance, we receive an order at INR1 crores price for propulsion system, if there is an increase in copper and raw ma

items.statement: Indian Railways payment terms: payment received within ~15 days of supply
items.quote: The payment terms of Indian Railways is very clear and it remains very consistent. So, generally by historically, if you see, we have received the payment terms in line with what they have mentioned on the purchase order. When we supply, the equipment reaches them and tentatively within 15 days' time we receive the payment.

items.statement: IGBTs and capacitors supply secured with 2-3 suppliers, bulk POs placed; minor components still stabilizing
items.quote: we have established good relations with a very renowned companies on this side and not only one, but two to three companies were finalized, shortlisted and to use basically. So these -- this was very clear and the order, purchase orders, the bulk purchase orders, looking at the schedules and the orders that are received were based on these suppliers well in advance. Now at least these two commodit

So, that doesn't mean that the qualification has happened. But however, we with open arms, we welcome them to come to this lobby because Indian Railways now needs indigenized suppliers to strengthen our ecosystem so that we are not dependent, we are not fully dependent o

items.statement: Automatic fault locator addressable market ~INR1.25 crores per set (substation + mid-point units); scales with route km, doubling, new lines, freight corridors
items.quote: Going by the current prices, prevailing prices, you can roughly say something like INR1.25 crores per set. This will constitute one set, one at substation, and all of these things. And then you can calculate the route kilometers of the railways, the line track which is there and further the one which are getting doubled and the new lines being planned and the freight corridors.

items.statement: Maintenance revenue 3-5% of purchase order value, recurring annually as per contract terms
items.quote: Okay, generally it varies between 3% to 5% of the total value of the purchase order And you keep getting year over year, as the way it is specified in the purchase order as a maintenance part, because these are not proprietary products, So they are limited to those suppliers who have actually supplied those or installed those in the trains or locomotives.

items.statement: Refurbishment market potential equals new locomotive market (1,500-1,600 units/year) as 15,000-16,000 loco fleet ages

So that year itself you will get another 1,500 locomotives, propulsion system standards or orders published for rehabilitation part. So that is why I'm s
