items.quote: I would say PAT will remain dynamic and you will see continuous improvement in PAT for next two quarters. Why? Because first of all, when we were developing our propulsion system and obviously we produced only one or two propulsion systems. One was used for prototype testing and by Indian Railways other one was for our reference, but we bought the components in the form of primary packaging quanti

items.statement: Supply chain irregularities in early ramp-up due to long lead times (up to 6 months) for imported electronic components; largely resolved now
items.quote: The actual, big-scale ordering started happening after the listing happened and that was late August, this quarter 2. So we ordered very, very wide variety of parts on mostly the international suppliers. These are all electronic components generally not being manufactured in India, wherein the delivery times became very, very high, went up to something like 6 months also in some of the cases. So,

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 1,393 crore as of 30 September 2026
items.quote: With this addition, our total order book stands at approximately Rs. 1,393 crores as on 30th September, which provides a strong revenue visibility for the coming years.

items.statement: Bids under pipeline worth Rs 870 crore await results
items.quote: Currently, we also have bids under pipeline for an amount of Rs. 870 crores for which the result is yet awaited.

items.statement: Expect 60-70% of Delhi Jal Board project revenue in FY27 and FY28 combined
items.quote: So, if you are talking about both of the financial years, then I would say 60% of the work will be completed within the next balance financial year and the next financial year. 60% to 70% I would say.

items.statement: Tendering environment strong with multiple government schemes launching bids
items.quote: So, the tendering environment is such that the existing schemes of Namami Gange and AMRUT 2.0, they are launching their bid separately. And new projects are coming in under Swachh Bharat Mission and Urban Challenge Fund.

items.statement: Margins flat in Q2 due to rainy season slowing execution while overheads constant
items.quote: And for the first question, I think it was about the margins being a little flat. So that also links it to the rainy season itself because our overheads and all of our staffing expenses are constant, but the execution going on at the ground is little less than what we expect.

items.statement: Receivables cycle typically 120 days; government payments delayed by fund allocation process
items.quote: Yes. It is usually 120 days. And sometimes with the West Asia crisis, it was delayed a little bit, but usually it's around 4.5 months.

items.statement: Interest-free mobilization advance of Rs 95 crore expected from Bihar project
items.quote: In Bihar also it was Rs. 750 crores there we are going to get interest free mobilization. We have submitted bank guarantees and all so around Rs. 95 crores we will get the interest-free mobilization from Bihar.

items.statement: Security and retention release of Rs 15 crore from completed projects aiding cash flow
items.quote: And additionally, the past projects which we have successfully executed, and we are commissioning and handing over to the government, we are also releasing the security and retention amount. So, they have released around Rs. 15 crores of security and retention amount.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used for working capital to execute large project pipeline
items.quote: The money raised from the fresh issue is being used for the purposes we have already disclosed in the offer documents, including utilizing it for the working capital required for the execution of this large quantum of projects that we have procured.

items.statement: Qualified to execute individual contracts up to Rs 400-500 crore
items.quote: So, we are working in these six states at the moment and we are qualified to execute large value contracts up to the value of Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 500 crores we can qualify individually.

items.statement: Revenue growth 27.8% YoY in H1 FY27; EBITDA growth 41% YoY
items.quote: Now for the full first half comparison, the revenue stood at Rs. 192.98 crores compared to Rs. 151.98 crores in H1 of last financial year. So that is a growth of 27.82%. The EBITDA grew almost 41% to Rs. 37.91 crores from Rs. 26.89 crores.

items.statement: Expect higher revenue in Q3 and Q4 as Rs 1,100 crore of new projects enter execution phase
items.quote: So, the execution will only pick up on those projects, the Rs. 1,100 crores project that in the Q1 and Q2 have started on. So that you will definitely see in Q3, Q4 for increase in operation and revenue.

items.statement: Order book predominantly wastewater treatment projects sized Rs 250-300 crore each
items.quote: And if we are talking about currently executing, then the majority of the order book out of the Rs. 1,393 crores, it is basically all wastewater projects. And the range of those projects is around the range of Rs. 250 crores-Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Delhi Jal Board awarded Rs 196.47 crore sewer line project in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter ended September 2026, we received a letter of award from the Delhi Jal Board for a project worth approximately Rs. 196 crores 47 lakhs.

items.statement: Projects funded by AMRUT 2.0, Namami Gange, Swachh Bharat Mission, Urban Challenge Fund and Asian Development Bank
items.quote: We have worked under the programs like AMRUT Mission, Namami Gange, Swachh Bharat Mission, Urban Challenge Fund. These are the new projects of Central Government's Swachh Bharat Mission and Urban Challenge Fund and state deposited work by the development authorities in metro cities and all projects funded by the institutions like the Asian Development Bank.

items.statement: Targets full-year FY27 revenue over INR5,000 crores with profitability sustained at current levels
items.quote: Skyways is definitely looking forward and targeting a revenue of over INR5,000 crores for this full year. While we want to make sure we go towards this vision, this mission, we want to make sure that our profitability is also sustained at the current levels.

items.statement: Expects sustained volume growth of 25-30% year-on-year over next 4-5 years
items.quote: We feel over the next 4 to 5 years we will continue to see a very sustained volume growth of 25% to 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: Air cargo volumes grew 27% YoY in Q2 FY27, growing at nearly 3x industry pace
items.quote: Air cargo volumes have grown significantly by 27% in this quarter for us and we have seen a solid double-digit growth also in the other verticals of logistics for the group.

items.statement: Indian export market grew ~8% in Q2 while Skyways grew 3x that rate
items.quote: The Indian export market grew roughly around 8% in this quarter, while Skyways grew 3x of this.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 4.46% in Q2 FY27, up from prior year; PAT margin 2.53% in Q2, up 43 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA in Q2, operating EBITDA, stood at INR58.47 crores, which is up 96% year-on-year, and an EBITDA margin of 4.46%.

items.statement: Expects gradual EBITDA margin improvement over 1-2 years as international offices reach breakeven
items.quote: Gradual process will continue and as more and more scale and more and more geographies will get added, eventually the international offices margins is better than the India export margin per se. And once the breakeven is achieved, even in the geographies that we are targeting, we can reasonably expect an improvement in the overall EBITDA margins over a period of 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 90.3% YoY to INR2,527.9 crores across all service lines
items.quote: These numbers have added up and given us a very solid H1 for FY27, whereby revenues for this H1 have grown 90.3% to INR2,527.9 crores

items.statement: Asset-light ethos; invests only where backed by customer demand; recently completed cold chain facility in Delhi (200,000 cu ft) and warehouse in Birmingham, UK
items.quote: So we've just recently concluding our cold chain facility here in Delhi, which will enable us to get about 200,000 cubic feet of cold chain capacity for the healthcare sector as well as the food and vegetable sector. And also we've recently operationalized one in Birmingham, UK

items.statement: Air freight yields may vary 5-10% quarterly due to fuel surcharges; no sharp shift expected in next couple of quarters
items.quote: So we are not expecting to have any kind of a sharp decrease or increase in these rates because if the normalcy of general freight rates other than the fuel is does not see a very big shift in very quick time.

items.statement: Non-air businesses (ocean, express, trucking, customs brokerage) grew ~80% YoY in H1 to INR566 crores
items.quote: Our non-air businesses, which have also seen a significant growth, delivered a strong momentum for us, with H1 revenue growing from INR315 crores to INR566 crores over the last H1.

items.statement: Customer base stable at 9,500+ with no customer losses reported
items.quote: Our customer base also is continuing to be stabilized at 9,500 plus levels, and no loss of customers have been reported in the portfolio.

items.statement: Gross debtor realization improved to 62.77 days in H1 FY27 from 75.19 days in FY26
items.quote: The gross debtors realization period has also improved to 62.77 days vis-à-vis 75.19 days if we compare the H1 to the FY26, which shows good collections and the credit selection of the customers with the top customers and the collection cycle improving in the current period, H1.

items.statement: Gross debt-to-equity reduced to 0.58 as of 30 Sep 2026
items.quote: Our gross debt-to-equity has reduced to 0.58 as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: IPO proceeds being effectively utilized; ROCE ~23% annualized showing capital deployed well
items.quote: We are currently operating at an annualized ROCE of approximately 23%. Even though this is one of the best in the industry, but this is not our destination.

items.statement: Brace Port acquired 76% in Sageroute Logistics with planned capital infusion; Avito Global Freight setting up Abu Dhabi Free Zone subsidiary
items.quote: Sageroute Logistics, which specializes in the road freight business and focusing on the renewable sector, which is done through our subsidiary Brace Port. As Brace Port, which is our subsidiary, has acquired 76% in Sageroute Logistics with the planned capital infusion to support its operation.

items.statement: Board declared second interim dividend of INR0.40 per share (4% of face value) for Q2; record date 20 Nov 2026
items.quote: I'm also pleased to announce or share that our board has declared a second interim dividend of INR0.40 per equity share, which is 4% of the face value of INR10 each, for the second quarter. The record date is scheduled on Friday the 20th November 2026.

items.statement: Headcount grew ~15% while revenue grew 90% YoY; revenue per employee improved ~67%
items.quote: So as we talk about the 90% growth year-on-year and there has been a kind of a 15% growth in the, headcount. So the overall effective increase has been around 67% and that is where the revenue per employee has improved.

items.statement: Air cargo volumes: 27,629 tons in Q2 FY27 (+27% YoY); 51,115 tons in H1 FY27 (+25.2% YoY)
items.quote: Volumes, if you talk about the Q2, were 27,629 tons, which were up 27% year-on-year basis, and 51,115 tons in H1, which is up 25.2%.

items.statement: Ocean volumes: 9,165 TEUs in Q2 FY27 (+15.9% YoY); 17,187 TEUs in H1 FY27 (+16.7% YoY)
items.quote: Volumes in the ocean segment stood at 9,165 TEUs in Q2 which is up 15.9%, and 17,187 TEUs in H1, which is up 16.7%.

items.statement: Express shipments: 72,197 in Q2 FY27 (+8.4% YoY); 1,34,967 in H1 FY27 (+17.7% YoY)
items.quote: We handled 72,197 shipments in Q2 FY27, which is up 8.4%, and 1,34,967 shipments in H1, which is up 17.7%.

items.statement: ASAP platform in final testing; launch expected early Q4 FY27; 15-20% of overall bookings currently digital; Express 95-96% digital
items.quote: Our tech platform ASAP is -- now it's in very final stages of testing, and across all aspects, we are making sure that this works perfectly well. And we are looking forward to launching this in the early part of Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Online platform improves efficiency 15-20% overall; digital penetration growing each quarter
items.quote: So once the online platform is there, the efficiency obviously improves by 15% to 20% on an overall basis for all of us.

items.statement: India-UK FTA in place expected to boost India-UK trade lane volumes
items.quote: With the India-UK FTA now in place, we are confident that this step will further boost our business volumes, not just on India-UK trade lane but also for global customers seeking logistics solutions in UK.

items.statement: Imports currently 5-6% of business; targeting significant growth over 4-5 years; new Asian offices to drive import volumes
items.quote: So currently our import is roughly around 5% to 6% of our business, and which we expect to keep growing year on year. And we are targeting to have a very, very decent part of our business in the next 4 or 5 years coming in from imports

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions separate strong players; Skyways maintained volume growth during March-April capacity crunch via carrier contracts and technology
items.quote: Well, these geopolitical issues actually separate the haves from the have-nots. And if you look at how we have performed even in the difficult period of March and April when there was a considerable amount of capacity decrease across the world, our volumes still grew.

items.statement: Ocean capacity expected to remain range-bound for 2-3 quarters; normalization depends on Middle East shipping routes reopening
items.quote: So I think that the ocean capacities will remain pretty range-bound over the next two to three quarters. We don't really see too much of change happening there.

items.statement: Targets PAT margin of 10-11% for FY28-29
items.quote: PAT margin would be between 10% to 11%. We are projecting for higher PAT margin. But the deliverable is around 10% to 11% of PAT margin.

items.statement: New Liwaspur facility capex INR72.58 cr; 80-85% to be spent in FY27 if GRAP lifted, else 50-60%
items.quote: The proposed facility will be spread across approximately 1.07 lakhs square feet with an estimated investment of around INR72.58 crores.

items.statement: Power transformer capacity to rise from 1,350 MVA to 3,250-4,000 MVA; enable up to 100 MVA and 220 kV class in 2-3 years
items.quote: Our existing power transformer manufacturing capacities of approximately 1,350 MVA is expected to increase to around 3,250 to 4,000 MVA per annum following the expansion.

items.statement: Order book INR427 cr as of Sep 2026; 85-90% private/EPC; ~10% fixed price, rest variable with 1-month lag
items.quote: Our order book stood at approximately INR427 crores as of September 2026, with 85% to 90% contribution by the private sector customers and EPC companies.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 6.8%, PAT margin 4.1% hit by raw material cost spikes and lag in pass-through
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR8.2 crores with a margin of 6.8% impact by the higher price of key raw materials, including aluminium, copper, steel and transformer oil, along with the time lag in passing on these cost increases.

items.statement: Transformer oil price doubled from INR68 to INR148/litre due to Hormuz closure; copper, aluminium, steel also up; 70-65% orders on PV clause with 1-month lag
items.quote: Today, the price has increased from INR68 to INR148 per litre, which is more than double. So, in that, what happens is that since some orders are fixed rates, some are on variable rates, we were not able to pass on the 100% cost increase because it was the initial stage.

items.statement: H2 FY27 demand seen shifting to 250-1,000 kVA copper transformers (70-75% copper, 25-30% aluminium); new RDSS orders expected in FY28
items.quote: Now, what is running at present, within that, we are doing copper transformers majorly in the second half and the demand that is going to be there in the coming time, in the second half, what I am feeling is that it is going to be from 250 kVA onwards, up to 1,000 kVA.

items.statement: Phasing out aluminium distribution transformers below 200 kVA; focusing on higher capacity copper units, IDT up to 30 MVA, power transformers up to 40 MVA at new plant
items.quote: Regarding the new facility we are setting up, as I mentioned, we are building the infrastructure to support up to the 400 kV class; however, our immediate target for the next 3 years to 4 years is to reach the 220 kV class.

items.statement: Trade receivables down 29% in H1 FY27; B2G payments on time since MSME law; B2B secured via LC/BG; no collection issues
items.quote: Additionally, trade receivable declined by 29% during the period, reflecting an improvement in collections and working capital management.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.14x; net worth INR195 cr; avg bank facility utilisation ~30% over last 10 years; interest cost only INR1 cr on INR363 cr revenue
items.quote: The company maintained a healthy capital structure with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.14x and net worth of INR195 crores.

items.statement: IPO fresh issue INR120.47 cr; INR31.72 cr utilized by Sep 30 (26.3%): INR16.71 cr working capital, INR11.16 cr offer expenses, INR3.6 cr capex, INR25.41 lakh general corporate
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, the company has utilized INR31.72 crores out of the total fresh issue IPO proceeds of INR120.47 crores, representing approximately 26.3% utilization.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue INR121.1 cr; FY26 revenue INR363 cr; current facility at ~100% utilisation, peak ~INR363 cr +/-5%; new plant targets INR1,500 cr in 4-5 years
items.quote: Within the current facility, we believe that we generated a revenue of INR363 crores last year. Plus or minus around this, you can assume that we will be able to reach only 4%-5%.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 3-4 years until INR1,500 cr revenue; small capex from internal accruals only
items.quote: No major capex is planned for the coming 3 years to 4 years.

items.statement: New Liwaspur facility (1.07 lakh sq ft) targeted operational in FY27; will relieve space constraint that capped revenue at INR363 cr
items.quote: The factory should be completed and put into production within the current financial year.

items.statement: Order inflow steady; additional INR46 cr orders booked after Sep 30; total executable order book ~INR550 cr including H1 execution
items.quote: Furthermore -- as Modi ji just noted we have secured additional orders worth around 46 crores over the last few days, which are not yet reflected in the September 30th order book.

items.statement: Operating across 17 states; supplies to remote regions (Leh-Ladakh, NE borders); EPC clients with 5-10 year relationships; preferred despite distance due to commitment and 5-year guarantee service
items.quote: Today, we are successfully operating across 17 states in India. From our base in Sonipat, we supply to regions as far-flung as the borders of Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Nepal, and even as far as Leh-Ladakh.

items.statement: Competition always present; differentiation via execution commitment, pan-India service, 5-year guarantee support; not reliant on regional freight advantage
items.quote: Clients, specifically our EPC customers choose us because of their long-standing experience with Raksan, having worked with us for 5, 8, 9, or even 10 years.

items.statement: MSME law ensures timely B2G payments for 8-10 years; no payment delays from government departments
items.quote: Regarding B2G payments, ever since the MSME law was introduced, the situation has changed. About 8 to 9 years ago, payments from government departments used to be delayed, but that is no longer the case; payments are now received on time.

items.statement: GRAP restrictions in Delhi NCR may delay new plant construction; if not lifted, only 50-60% capex deployed in FY27 vs 80-85% if lifted
items.quote: But if this GRAP is not lifted, because construction activity is totally stopped in the Delhi NCR, so we are hopeful that if we have completed everything or all the machinery is installed, then we will do 100% capex this year. Otherwise, some part might be more or less 50% to 60% of the funds we have raised for capex, that will be invested in this financial year only.

items.statement: Historical proforma growth ~23%; forward growth target late teens to 20%
items.quote: historically, we basically have grown at about 23 odd percent if you look at proforma growth. Go forward, the intention is that you basically be between late teens to 20, so to speak, from a growth perspective.

items.statement: H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1 FY27
items.quote: what we can definitely mention is that H2 will be better than H1.

items.statement: Definitive agreements for 2,450 beds at O.P. Jindal Global University; total capacity ~10,500 beds
items.quote: Post-second quarter, we also executed, I am pleased to say, definitive agreements for the acquisition of additional 2,450 beds at O.P. Jindal Global University, taking our total capacity in the campus to approximately 10,500 beds.

items.statement: O.P. Jindal acquisition consideration Rs 1,350 crore over 9 years with Rs 150 crore upfront
items.quote: The total consideration is Rs 1,350 crores payable over nine years, including an upfront payment of Rs 150 crores.

items.statement: Pre-construction started for 1,800+ bed PPP project at IIT Madras; Ministry of Finance approved viability gap funding
items.quote: we have commenced pre-construction activities for the development of an 1,800+ bed student accommodation at IIT Madras under the PPP model, and we have just received the approval from the Ministry of Finance for the release of the viability gap funding for this project.

items.statement: Greenfield/brownfield pipeline: 6 projects, Rs 646 crore total cost, Rs 350 crore pending capex, delivery FY28-FY30 at 10-12% entry yield
items.quote: the identified projects represent an estimated total project cost of around Rs 646 crore, with pending capex of around Rs 350 crore. This will come at an entry yield on cost of around 10%-12%.

items.statement: Portfolio: 20,000+ owned/managed beds, 2,100 under development, 58,000+ managed beds across 23 institutions, 18 K-12 campuses
items.quote: As of September 30th, our portfolio comprised approximately 20,000+ owned and managed beds. items.statement: Contractual same-store growth 5-6% embedded; achieved 7-9% in select assets
items.quote: Firstly, we have contractually embedded same-store growth from our existing assets, anywhere from 5%-6%. In fact, we have already achieved 7%-9% in select assets already.

items.statement: IPO proceeds Rs 750 crore fully utilized for debt repayment; INR debt cost reduced ~30 bps to 8.9% as of Nov 1
items.quote: I am happy to clarify that as we speak, the entire Rs 750 crores from the IPO proceeds, which was earmarked for debt repayment, has fully been utilized. Furthermore, as of November 1st, we have been able to further reduce the cost of debt of our existing INR debt by around 30 bps points to around 8.9%.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs 2,100 crore: Rs 1,100 crore for K-12 acquisitions, Rs 750 crore debt repayment, Rs 128 crore other acquisitions
items.quote: We have raised Rs 2,100 crore, of which Rs 1,100 crores has been deployed for K-12 acquisitions, Rs 750 crores has been deployed for debt repayment, and about Rs 128 crores for the other acquisitions, which Narasimha just spoke about.

items.statement: Acquisition pipeline: 10 deals across segments; 4 in diligence stage expected to close within 6 months
items.quote: Of the 10 assets that you are currently seeing within the pipeline, 4 of them are currently in the diligence stage, and we expect that we would be able to get them closed within the next six months' timeframe.

items.statement: Occupancy ~95% in owned/managed student accommodation portfolio
items.quote: We cater to a student capacity in excess of 107,000, with approximately 95% occupancy in our owned and managed student accommodation portfolio.

items.statement: Q2 margins impacted by Rs 2 crore IPO expenses, Rs 5 crore higher employee expense, Rs 6 crore share-based compensation
items.quote: This quarter, margins were also impacted by certain IPO-related expenses of around Rs 2 crore, which had to be routed through the P&L. Furthermore, we saw higher employee expense of around Rs 5 crores and share-based compensation expenses of around Rs 6 crore.

items.statement: Negative working capital cycle at portfolio level; contractual escalations and minimum revenue guarantees provide cash flow visibility
items.quote: Additionally, this business is a negative working capital cycle at a portfolio level, while our exclusivity provides continuity to our institutional relationships.

items.statement: Portfolio split ~55/45 student accommodation vs K-12; expect tilt toward student accommodation for operating leverage and value-added services
items.quote: Currently, our business, as you know, is split roughly between 55/45 on the student accommodation and K-12 side. We are seeing probably the portfolio will be a little bit more growing towards the student accommodation side.

items.statement: TAM $9 billion: $5 billion K-12 (13,000 schools, 1.5M students), $4 billion student accommodation (3M beds, 2M students); <1% market share
items.quote: Based on our analysis, our opportunity set here is about 13,000 schools, representing 1.5 million students. On the student accommodation side, our TAM is nearly 3 million beds, which is represented by the top private-ranked, private, unaided institutions of scale. So, if you look at it, we are targeting about approximately 20 lakh students, and the sharply defined TAM is a $9 billion revenue marke

items.statement: Greenfield pipeline: 6 projects, Rs 650 crore capex, Rs 300 crore spent, Rs 350 crore pending, 10-12% entry yield on cost
items.quote: we have six projects which are going to be scheduled to deliver between FY28 and FY30. This involves a capex of about Rs 650 crore, and Rs 300 crores is already spent, and Rs 350 crores more to go. Here, our economics are like an entry yield to cost will be more like 10%-12%.

items.statement: Four acquisition deals in diligence expected to close in 6 months; sufficient to deliver high teens to 20% EBITDA growth
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. They would be enough.

items.statement: H2 FY27 expected to be much better than H1; 60-65% of revenue typically comes in second half
items.quote: Yes, it will be much better because 3 - 4 months of the first half fall within the rainy season, during which there is no pipe or micro-irrigation work.

items.statement: New capacity revenue contribution of 135-150 crores expected mainly in FY28-29, some in FY27-28
items.quote: To some extent, we will be able to achieve the expected revenue of 135 - 150 crores in FY 28 - 29.

items.statement: Combined turnover target estimated at 250-300 crores once new products reach full commercial production
items.quote: Yes, that should be the estimate. It should reach that level, sir.

items.statement: H1 PAT margin 3%; H2 margins historically 4.5-5% due to better capacity utilization and pricing power
items.quote: Therefore, in the second half, we normally operate at a margin of 4.5% - 5%. If you look at our historical performance, our margin has generally been between 4% and 5%.

items.statement: New three-layer drum technology with 30% recycled middle layer to lower cost by 30% and increase margins vs older single-layer tech
items.quote: The middle portion will consist of recyclable material, and the cost will be lower by 30%. Therefore, our profit can increase, and this technology is not available with everyone.

items.statement: Installed capacity 26,500 MT; expanding by ~10,000 MT to 36,500 MT (4,000 MT honeycomb, 2,000 MT PP corrugated, 1,500 MT 210L drums, 500 MT 60L drums, 1,500 MT pallets)
items.quote: Our installed capacity so far is 26,500 MT, which will increase to 36,500 MT after the expansion. Of the additional 10,000 MT being added, approximately 4,000 tons will come from honeycomb sheets.

items.statement: New machines expected delivery by March 2027; trial production April-May 2027; commercial production FY27-28; full swing FY28-29
items.quote: We expect to complete the installation of the new machines and start production by March 2027. Either trial production or commercial production will start by March 2027.

items.statement: Strong repeat demand from infrastructure (Adani, Tata, Gujarat Govt) for cable ducting; turning down orders due to capacity constraints
items.quote: There is so much cable work that it is difficult to describe. These are all repeat orders.

items.statement: Drum demand very high in Vapi chemical zone (15,000 SMEs); customers following up for production start; metal drums being replaced by polymer
items.quote: We have such a large requirement for drums in the nearby areas that people are already following up with us and asking when we will start production.

items.statement: Gas distribution pipes (MDPE) large opportunity: thousands of km orders from Gujarat Gas, Mahanagar Gas; registration process ongoing 2-4 months
items.quote: Once it begins, a very large quantity of pipeline will be required because the orders are for thousands of kilometers.

items.statement: Portfolio: HDPE pipes, fittings, sheets, corrugated sheets, DWC pipes, drip irrigation, MDPE gas pipes, drums (3-layer), honeycomb sheets, bubble guard, pallets
items.quote: We have pipes, sheets, DWC pipes, and packaging sheets. We are certified and ISO certified, and we have BIS certificates for all our products.

items.statement: ~60-70% direct customers; key accounts: Torrent Power (largest), Amul Dairy, Gujarat Gas, Mahanagar Gas, chemical majors in Vapi (UPL, Aarti, Pidilite, etc.)
items.quote: Torrent Power is our largest customer. Wherever it lays cables inside pipes, it uses our pipes.

items.statement: EPR mandate: 30% recycled content current year, 40% next year, 60% thereafter; metal drums banned for exports; government pushing piped gas over cylinders
items.quote: The government has now made it compulsory to use 30% reprocessed material, meaning material next to virgin material available in the market. This requirement is 30% for the current year, 40% for the next year, and 60% thereafter.

items.statement: Term loan repayment made in October from IPO proceeds; interest savings to add to profits; may approach bankers for working capital
items.quote: The only term-loan repayment was also made in October. Therefore, every contribution we have made toward our performance so far has been through our own internal funds, bank funds, or internal accruals.

items.statement: IPO proceeds received October 2026; used for machine orders, margins, term loan repayment; Phase 2 capex funded from IPO
items.quote: The IPO proceeds came to us in October, and only the installation and ordering of machines have started so far. The only term-loan repayment was also made in October.

items.statement: Indian plastic fittings industry growing at 10.4%; global plastic pipes 6.46%; protective packaging 5.19%; polymer production 13.37%
items.quote: The Indian plastic fittings industry is growing at 10.4%. Global plastic pipes are growing at 6.46%, global protective packaging at 5.19%, and polymer production at 13.37%.

items.statement: Capacity utilization limited to 70-75% due to changeover times and rainy season; new product market acceptance only after physical availability
items.quote: Customers generally do not place orders until the product is physically available. Our marketing team has already started moving through the market and is promoting that we are going to manufacture these products.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps over next 12-18 months from current ~13.25% average
items.quote: We believe that realistically speaking with the expansion of capacity, we can look at a margin expansion of maybe 100 to 150 basis points.

items.statement: Management targets export revenue to at least double from current 5-6% of total revenue within 18-24 months
items.quote: We believe that in the next 18 months to 24 months, from 6%, we should be able to go at least double of our total revenue from exports.

items.statement: Management aims to increase value-added product contribution from ~5% to 15% of total revenue
items.quote: So, we look at increasing that to 15%.

items.statement: Capacity expansion of 87,301 MTPA planned using IPO proceeds, to be completed by FY28 end
items.quote: As planned in the DRHP and IPO proceeds, we will be completing this expansion to 87,000 tons by FY28 end.

items.statement: Current capacity 44,340 MTPA; Q2 FY27 added ~9,000 MTPA; targeting ~55,000 MTPA by FY27 end
items.quote: So, you will see that by FY27 end, we will increase the capacity from 44,000 tons to somewhere close to 55,000 tons.

items.statement: New capacity typically takes 12-18 months to reach 70-75% utilization
items.quote: We believe that we will be able to achieve that looking at the current market scenario as well as opportunities that lie in front of us.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by manufacturing; trading revenue reduced from INR 58 cr to INR 55 cr in H1
items.quote: So, last year, we did a trading in H1 of INR58 crores and this year, it has been reduced to INR55 crores.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA grew 41.47% to INR 33.57 cr; PAT grew 51% to INR 20.77 cr; sustainable EBITDA margin seen at 13-13.5%
items.quote: We have been able to sustain an EBITDA margin of 13%, 13.5% even in our annual financials last year.

items.statement: Focusing on MAH-grafted specialty adhesive compounds for multi-layer films and pipes as value-added products
items.quote: Currently we are focusing on developing our adhesive range of compounds which are MAH-packed specialty compounds which have applications in various different multi-layer films and multi-layer pipes.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute ~55% of revenue; no single customer >8% of manufacturing revenue
items.quote: Our top 10 customers contribute almost 55%. And if you take out our trading revenue on a manufacturing side, no customer contributes more than 8% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Export revenue currently 5-6% of total; trials ongoing in Tunisia, Nigeria, Poland, Romania, Algeria, Turkey, Indonesia
items.quote: Currently, our export revenue is between 5% to 6% of our total revenue on the manufacturing side.

items.statement: Inventory buildup at Q2 end is seasonal due to monsoon impact on infrastructure sector; expected to normalize by December/March
items.quote: Typically, what we have seen is that in the Q2 end, the inventory would always go up because of various factors which are related to the infrastructure industries.

items.statement: Compounding industry asset turnover at peak utilization typically 8x-10x
items.quote: So, peak utilization, typically, the compounding industry has asset turnover of around 8x to 10x.

items.statement: Power cable consumption growing 15-16% annually over next 5-7 years driving XLPE capacity expansion
items.quote: So, there is a 15% to 16% growth in the power cable consumption, which has been slated over the next 5 years to 7 years.

items.statement: EPC approvals are product approvals for pipe coating projects, not entry into EPC contracting business
items.quote: So, basically, no, we are not entering any EPC project or taking any EPC contracts. So, all of our infrastructure projects are dependent on various approvals by various authorities who approve our product.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin temporarily rose to 15% due to price spike from West Asia crisis fallout
items.quote: And in Q1 this year, it was a little bit further increased to 15% due to the current jump in prices because of the fallout of the West Asia crisis.

items.statement: Revenue not dependent on single large orders; widely dissipated across B2B customer base in telecom, power, oil & gas, water infrastructure
items.quote: So, we are looking at continuous orders and adding customer base. That being said, our revenue growth or revenue are widely dissipated and not dependent on any single large orders.

items.statement: Targets INR 10,000 crores revenue by 2030 and aims to reach around 6% EBITDA margin as soon as possible
items.quote: To me, it is clear that we want to reach our EUR 1 billion revenue in 2030.

items.statement: Expects US entity integration by early 2028 after balance sheet readiness
items.quote: I think the U.S.; we feel that 2028 beginning will be the right timing.

items.statement: Order backlog has doubled compared to 18 months ago
items.quote: That is a given due to the workload and the backlog we have addressed and acquired, which is double from the one we had 18 months ago.

items.statement: Q3 standalone EBITDA loss of INR 12 crores due to early-stage project execution
items.quote: At the standalone level, the company recorded an EBITDA loss of INR12 crores during the quarter, reflecting the current operation performance of the business.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated EBITDA loss of INR 35.7 crores
items.quote: At the consolidated level, EBITDA for Q3 stood at a loss of INR35.7 crores, and net profit for Q3 was INR11.1 crores.

items.statement: Registered workshop in Zhangjiagang, China near Shanghai to strengthen metal business presence
items.quote: In China, however, we have registered a workshop in Zhangjiagang, near Shanghai, to strengthen our presence and support our metal business, including key equipment-related activities.

items.statement: Recruited over 100 people in Indian operations since September 2025 with plans to add more by end of 2026
items.quote: Since September 25, our Indian operations has recruited more than 100 people, with plans to add further personnel by end year 2026.

items.statement: China operations recruited over 30 employees with additional recruitment planned
items.quote: Our China operations have also recruited more than 30 employees, with additional recruitment planned before the end of the year.

items.statement: Board strengthened with appointments of Praveen Kadle, Shekhar Kashalikar, and Jan Lueder; Vivek Bhide stepped down
items.quote: I am pleased to welcome Praveen Kadle, who will join the board, and Shekhar Kashalikar, who joins us as a non-independent director. I also extend a warm welcome to Jan Lueder, who joins us as an independent director.

items.statement: Investigating all options to raise funds and bring capital/equity for acquisitions and technology expansion
items.quote: We are investigating all options to raise funds and to bring capital and equity into the company so that we can further expand through acquisition.

items.statement: Allotted 35,185 CCPS to John Cockerill SA after BSE and RBI approvals; US entity acquisition deferred to 2028
items.quote: The company received the requisite approval from BSE Limited and Reserve Bank of India. Subsequently, the company allotted 35,185 non-cumulative, non-voting, 0.001% compulsory convertible preference shares, or called CCPS, to John Cockerill SA.

items.statement: Renewing JVD licensing agreement with ArcelorMittal for two-cell technology; VAMA Phase III project announced in China
items.quote: John Cockerill is renewing its commitment towards ArcelorMittal right now on JVD technology and expanding our licensing agreement for the two-cell JVD technology, which is the next level of development of the technology.

items.statement: Volteron technology pilot planned for 2027; discussions ongoing with several customers
items.quote: We have big ambition on Volteron next year, and we would like to build our first pilot in 2027. Right now, we are discussing exploring this opportunity with several customers.

items.statement: World Steel forecasts ~8% steel demand growth in India for 2026 and 2027; electrical steel contract with JSW Vijayanagar Metallics
items.quote: India remains particularly attractive with world steel forecasting steel demand growth of approximately 8% in both '26 and '27.

items.statement: Signed MoU with Government of Maharashtra on September 2 for green iron and green steel cooperation in Gadchiroli
items.quote: The MoU signed on September 2 of this year covers cooperation exploring advanced technology for green iron and green steel and supporting Maharashtra, particularly Gadchiroli, as a green steel manufacturing hub.

items.statement: Recognized exceptional income of INR 53.6 crores (INR 47.1 crores after tax) from sale of Andheri land and building
items.quote: Additionally, during Q3, the company also recognized an exceptional income of INR53.6 crores, which is INR47.1 crores after tax, arising from the sales of its Andheri land and building.

items.statement: Q3 standalone revenue INR 174.4 crores, up ~80% YoY; 9M revenue INR 523.6 crores, more than doubled YoY
items.quote: Revenue from operations for Q3 was approximately INR174.4 crores, compared with approximately INR97 crores in Q3 from last year, representing robust year-on-year growth of approximately 80%.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated revenue INR 316 crores, up ~22% YoY; 9M consolidated revenue INR 959 crores, up ~31% YoY
items.quote: For Q3, consolidated revenue from operation was INR316 crores, compared with INR259 crores in Q3 from last year. This is representing a growth year-on-year of around 22%.

items.statement: Project execution profitability timing uncertain; projects from 2026 expected to recognize revenue in 2027-2028
items.quote: The percentage of completion will start to recognize revenue, I would say, '27, '28 for what we have acquired as project in '26.

items.statement: Allotted 35,185 CCPS to promoter John Cockerill SA as part of Project Vulcan restructuring
items.quote: Subsequently, the company allotted 35,185 non-cumulative, non-voting, 0.001% compulsory convertible preference shares, or called CCPS, to John Cockerill SA.

items.statement: Aspires to reach INR 2,000 crores revenue and INR 400 crores EBITDA in next 4-5 years including JV
items.value: INR 2,000 crores revenue and INR 400 crores EBITDA
items.quote: And we are aiming for about INR 2,000 crores revenue and about INR 400 crores EBITDA in the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to scale 10x in sales and EBITDA over 10 years versus last financial year
items.quote: we would scale up to becoming 10x in sales and EBITDA in 10 years' time.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 10.8% vs 11.2% in Q1 FY27 due to higher power and fuel costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in the current quarter Q2 is 10.8% vis-a-vis 11.2% in the Q1.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 11% in line with Q1 and Q2
items.quote: And the EBITDA margin in H1 is 11%, which is more or less in line with the Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals margins suffered due to high raw material costs and tactical volume-driven growth at lower margins
items.quote: But if you look at our percentage margins, they came down. And some of our fundamental businesses, which were, for example, in the oil and gas sector, which we wanted to do quite well. And some of our materials, which used materials like propylene oxide, you see, I've also mentioned propylene oxide, lauryl alcohol, phenol, etc. The cost became very high.

items.statement: Specialty Materials expected to deliver steady growth near to long term; Performance Chemicals to be key growth pillar
items.quote: The Specialty Materials is expected to deliver steady growth. It has been a consistent business for us for the near term as well as for the longer term in the foreseeable future. For the near term to midterm as well as the long term, Performance Chemicals will be an important pillar to drive growth

items.statement: End markets like personal care, textiles, pharma, coatings growing faster than GDP in India
items.quote: India is a growing market, fast-growing market and will continue to remain a fast-growing market for the next 10 years. You agree, I agree. And when there is increase in income, the first thing that people spend is on discretionary spend.

items.statement: New Performance Chemicals business volume grew ~90% YoY and ~74% QoQ in Q2 FY27
items.quote: And in terms of volume growth, that performance chemicals business compared to same quarter of last year has grown by about 90%. And compared to previous quarter, volume growth in that separate small division for which we do not separately now report as a detailed result is about 74%.

items.statement: CWIP of INR 114 crores across 14-15 projects; most to complete by Dec'26-Jan'27, some by Jun'27
items.quote: CWIP of INR 114 crores, there are, say, about 14-15 capexes, which is going on, which Mr. Rupark has already told regarding the capacity enhancement in amine manufacturing and some other capexes. That is all on the completion stage, some of the capex, which will be completed by June '27, while most of the capexes will be completed by December'26-January '27.

items.statement: New Specialty Unit running at healthy occupancy; some areas at full capacity with debottlenecking investments underway
items.quote: I think we have a very healthy occupacity of our new specialty unit. In some areas, actually, we are running full. We are doing small debottlenecking investments to continue to get those volumes up.

items.statement: Glycol margins under pressure as export prices linked to US ethanol prices while costs rose; glycol ethers benefited from expensive crude-based imports
items.quote: glycol margins were under pressure interestingly because a number of the glycol that we sell to niche customers are exported. And their prices are linked to prices of U.S.-based imported ethanol. So while the crude prices went up and people thought MEG was in short supply and people will make more money in MEG, our margins were actually under pressure because prices were linked to ethanol.

items.statement: Key raw materials: ethanol (largest), coal for energy, propylene oxide, lauryl alcohol, phenol
items.quote: Our single biggest RM is ethanol, which we discussed and then our RM other than that big RM is coal, which is for energy. And 3 other RMs I named. I named propylene oxide, lauryl alcohol and phenol.

items.statement: ~45% of sales from exports; freight volatility impacts export competitiveness but domestic alternatives benefit when import freight rises
items.quote: nearly 45% of sales coming through exports. So if you could explain, is there any impact related to freight and approval things? And secondly, how do you look at the mix change over the next 3 to 5 years in terms of exports?

items.statement: Long-term debt allocated to India Glycols INR 450 crores with ~INR 125 crores annual repayment; working capital limit INR 300 crores
items.quote: Regarding the debt, which has been allocated to India Glycols, the total long-term debt allocated to India Glycols is INR 450 crores and out of which is repayable every year is about INR 125 crores.

items.statement: Working capital CC limit of INR 300 crores allocated plus non-fund-based limits for BGs and LCs
items.quote: Relating to the working capital limits, yes, we have allocated the working capital limit out of the total limits which company was having. So now the India Glycols will be having about a working capital CC limit of INR 300 crores and some non-fund-based limit for the bank guarantees and the LCs.

items.statement: Bio-based Specialty Materials revenue share shifted from 55% to 52% in H1 FY27 supporting specialty-led portfolio
items.quote: Broadly, we've had an improvement in mix in bio-based specialty materials, where revenue increased from 55% to 52%, supporting the shift towards a more specialty-led portfolio.

items.statement: Collaborative projects and strategic partnerships with end consumers (personal care, crop care) and global players (BASF, Dow) expanding
items.quote: many of our projects are collaborative projects or strategic partnerships. So that was how the company looks like in a slightly more focused manner after the demerger.

items.statement: Ethanol sourcing from IGL Spirits at arm's length; will import if cheaper; pipeline supply across border is cost-effective
items.quote: Now as far as the choice of buying is concerned, the choice of doing the appropriate buying for this business is with IGL Chemicals, which means that if manufactured ethanol is more expensive and imported ethanol is cheaper, I can definitely buy and I will continue to buy imported ethanol.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA INR 113 crores including JV share; standalone EBITDA INR 79 crores; PAT INR 56 crores, EPS INR 8.40
items.quote: So INR 113 crores, including JV, but I will talk only about India Glycols -- so it is about INR 79 crores. And whatever INR 200 crores we can target, that target is including the JV.

items.statement: Demerger completed into three listed entities: India Glycols (Chemicals), IGL Spirits (Potable Spirits + Ethanol), Ennature Biopharma (APIs, Nutraceuticals, Biopolymers)
items.quote: So there are 3 businesses which have been listed now. One is IGL Spirits Limited. To refresh your memory, of course, IGL Spirits Limited has Potable spirits, which includes IMFL as well as Country Liquor. But it also now has the biofuels business as ethanol.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility (crude prices, freight, trade policy) creates unpredictable operating environment; tactical measures taken this year
items.quote: Everyday morning, when I look at the television, the world seems to have changed. That is how volatile it is, especially given our friend, Mr. Trump. So it is very difficult to predict for 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Employee cost reduced due to lower Chairman salary allocation and commission; quarterly run-rate ~INR 17-17.5 crores
items.quote: Relating to the employee cost, which Saket-ji, you have mentioned, actually, what has happened is the cost has come down because of the reduction in the salary of the Chairman, which will be allocated into companies. So accordingly, the commission has also reduced.

items.statement: Targets FY27 revenue of INR 1,300 crore and 5-6% EBITDA margin
items.quote: if you see if we are right on the right track of achieving the 1300 crore revenue target.

items.statement: Expects to recover EBITDA margin to 5-6% in next two quarters of FY27
items.quote: we are very positive about our EBITDA margin, and in the next two quarters, we expect to cover up the EBITDA margin and be at par with the last year of 5-6%.

items.statement: Nakoda PET chips plant expected operational by Q2 FY28 adding INR 1,200 crore annual revenue and INR 70 crore EBITDA
items.quote: It is expected to be operationalized by Q2 of FY 28. This strengthens our backward integration, gives us better control on raw material and supply, and is expected to add around 1200 crores of annual turnover, and 70 crores of EBITDA.

items.statement: 12 MW solar plant commissioning by December 2026 to save INR 23-25 crore power cost annually from FY27-28
items.quote: our solar project of 12 megawatt is expected to be commissioned by December 2026, which will take our renewable energy to about 50-55% of our total consumption. This will help to increase our revenue by 23-25 crores, by saving power cost.

items.statement: Value-added yarn expansion expected to add INR 300 crore annual revenue and improve margins
items.quote: This is expected to end around 300 crores of annual revenue and improve our margins.

items.statement: Expects strong demand in remaining months of FY27 due to wedding season and lower crude prices
items.quote: For the rest of this year, we expect demand to improve with the wedding season, and especially the crude, the crude prices have gone down. So, our raw material is expected to go down, and we are expecting better margins.

items.statement: Sees very good demand in coming months as war is over and prices are reasonable
items.quote: As the, what you can say as the war is over and the prices are getting reasonable, we are expecting a very good demand in the coming, remaining months of this year.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 2.53% from 5.39% due to spread over material cost narrowing to 17.1% from 23%
items.quote: EBITDA margins, including other income, was INR 9.22 crores in Q2 against the 14 crore in the last year, with the margin of 2.53 basis against the 5.39 basis. The lower margin is mainly because of the spread over material cost narrowed to 17.1% from the 23%.

items.statement: Margin moderation due to high crude and raw material price volatility with time lag in passing on costs
items.quote: The key reasons for decrease in the margins is purely because of high volatility in the market due to the high crude prices and raw material prices, and also supplementary prices. We were able to increase our finished prices also with the raw material prices, but there is always a time lag, and due to that, the margins were... had gone down.

items.statement: Targets 5-6% EBITDA margin on FY27 revenue of INR 1,300 crore
items.quote: In the current year, we are expect... we are, targeting to achieve the 5% to 6% EBITDA margin on this turnover.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 sales volume 23,000 tons; Q2 FY27 sales volume 29,000 tons (combined yarn, PET chips, all categories)
items.quote: in the first quarter, our sales, stood at approximately 23,000 tons. And in the quarter two, our sales in, quantity has gone up to 29,000 tons.

items.statement: Plant running at 95-98% utilisation; added 40 TPD FDY capacity taking total to 160 TPD
items.quote: Our plant is running at an optimum capacity of 95 to 98% utilization, and we are... we have added 40 tons per day of FDY capacity, taking it from 120 to 160 tons per day.

items.statement: Nakoda subsidiary has 1.4 lakh ton per annum bottle-grade PET chips plant in Surat expected operational by Q2 FY28
items.quote: Nakoda through our subsidiary Sumeet specialty chips we have acquired will have a capacity of 1.4 lakh ton per annum, bottle-grade PET chips plant in Surat. It is expected to be operationalized by Q2 of FY 28.

items.statement: 12 MW solar plant cost ~INR 40 crore funded from pre-rights issue term loan; no additional debt raised
items.quote: a 12 megawatt solar plant, which is... Yeah, getting commissioned right now. Has a cost of approximately 40 CR.

items.statement: Funds from rights issue (INR 194.9 crore) allocated: INR 100 crore working capital, INR 85.9 crore Nakoda asset integration, INR 9 crore debt repayment
items.quote: Our right issue shows completed in Q1 FY27, and the net proceeds of 194.9 crores are used for working capital of are used as follows, working capital of 100 CR, Nakoda asset integration of 85.9 CR, and debt repayment of 9CR.

items.statement: Stopped cash discounts to agents/customers after working capital improved, leading to 42% receivables increase
items.quote: After our working capital became healthy, we have stopped those discounts, and that is why the receivables have gone up. But the receivables are still in line with the industry standards.

items.statement: Power cost for H1 FY27 (April-September 2026) was INR 39 crore excluding fuel cost
items.quote: For the current year, from April to August-September 2026, our power cost was 39 CR, which is apart... apart from the fuel cost and anything, this is only power cost.

items.statement: Shifting up to 50% capacity to value-added yarns (dope-dyed, bright, cationic, BSY) for better prices and margins
items.quote: still in process of moving up to 50% of our capital capacity into value-added yarn, such as Dope - dyed yarn, Bright Yarn, catonic yarn, BSY yarn, which will fetch better Date & Time: 20th Novemeber,2026 |3:30 PM prices and, importantly, better

items.statement: PET chips and FDY to drive 30%+ revenue growth in FY27, not DTY/POY
items.quote: plus 30%, PET chips and FDY, not DTY POY. The PO and DTY are the same, we have increased our production in FDY, and so we expect FDY and PET chips to drive the plus 30%. revenue growth.

items.statement: B2B textile-based customers; value-added yarns (dope-dyed, bright, cationic) used in textile applications
items.quote: So, the target customers and industries, we are B2B. So, yes, our target customers and industries are business owners only who, takes our raw material and convert it to further, finished products. We are textile-based, so our customers are also textile-based.

items.statement: Bottle-grade PET chips has ~50% import dependence (China); Nakoda capacity 400 TPD is only 10% of ~4,000 TPD current domestic market
items.quote: Presently, already approximately 4,000 tons is being manufactured per day for these chips, and we are only manufacturing 400 tons. That is only 1 /10th... only 10% of the market capacity.

items.statement: Receivables up 42% (INR 133 cr to INR 189 cr) due to stopping cash discounts and higher raw material prices
items.quote: See, the major cause is the... initially, when, till the last year. As our finances were not good, and we were paying high financial cost, we were giving extra discounts to our agents and customers who were cutting the cash discount and making us a payment. After our working capital became healthy, we have stopped those discounts, and that is why the receivables have gone up.

items.statement: Working capital and cash flow healthy; expects further improvement as raw material prices decline
items.quote: Our working capital and cash flow is, quite healthy presently, and, we are easily managing it. And, as the war has, come to an end, and the crude have also come down. So the Raw material prices will also come down, which will help us to manage better our working capital and cash flow.

items.statement: Borrowings down to INR 137 crore from INR 160 crore; debt-to-net-worth improved from 0.75x to 0.33x
items.quote: Borrowings came down at 137 crores, and the previous one was 160 crores. So, borrowing to the net worth improved, 0.75 times to 0.33 times

items.statement: No additional debt raised for solar plant; funded from pre-rights issue term loan by reallocating from expansion capex
items.quote: So, no additional debt has been, raised.no additional, money has been input, all the things which we were... we had planned before the right issue, and, we are continuing the same thing, only the funds have been reallocated.

items.statement: Depreciation for H1 FY27 INR 9.22 crore; expects similar INR 9.22 crore for H2 FY27
items.quote: Half yearly is... okay, yeah, 6 monthly is around 9.22, so the second 6 monthly will also be the same, approximately.

items.statement: Margin recovery dependent on raw material prices declining and market improving in remaining 4-5 months
items.quote: But the positive thing is, in the remaining 4 to 5 months, as the raw material prices have gone down, the markets are also looking positive now from here onwards, and so we are quite sure that we will be able to increase our margins and cover up the loss in the margins.

items.statement: Management expects domestic manufacturing facility to reach 75-80% capacity utilization in next 2 years
items.quote: And we expect in the next 2 years, we should be hitting 75% to 80% of our production capacity in that unit.

items.statement: New domestic manufacturing facility in Andheri East, Mumbai spans 5,360 sq ft with 100-125 kg annual capacity at ~INR7 crore capex
items.quote: We established a new manufacturing facility in Andheri East, Mumbai, spanning approximately 5,360 square feet, with installed capacity of 100 to 125 kg of jewellery annually. The facility represents a capital expenditure of approximate INR7 crores, excluding working capital.

items.statement: Domestic manufacturing facility expected to increase overall manufacturing capacity by 50-60%
items.quote: and is expected to increase overall manufacturing capacity by 50% to 60%.

items.statement: Domestic manufacturing facility has started sampling with orders worth INR1-1.5 crore sold so far
items.quote: We've already got some orders and right now it is at a very minimal range, like we've been able to sell around INR1, INR1.5 crores of jewellery.

items.statement: Plan to open 7 additional NIBHANA stores in coming quarter, taking total to 11 stores
items.quote: We already lined up another seven stores in the coming quarter. And after that, we'll be reviewing the situation of how these stores work out in metros, in Tier 2.

items.statement: Long-term vision to open around 100 NIBHANA stores in next 3-4 years
items.quote: And as a long-term vision, we have a plan to open around 100 stores in the next 3 to 4years.

items.statement: Typical NIBHANA store investment INR2-2.5 crore including INR40-50 lakh interiors, INR1.5-2 crore inventory, INR40-50 lakh security deposit
items.quote: So, in a typical store, the investment should be from INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores.

items.statement: Management sees encouraging customer response to NIBHANA stores, expects India lab-grown jewellery boom similar to US trajectory over coming decade
items.quote: But obviously, the response has been very encouraging. And we have been working in US since a long time for lab-grown jewellery. So with that experience of production and what's happening in US in the last 7-8 years in lab-grown, we expect in India that kind of boom to come in the coming decade.

items.statement: Domestic manufacturing targets retail chains in South India and Middle East retail chains' Indian operations, plus own NIBHANA stores
items.quote: So, I would not be naming any names right now, but these are all retail chains, particularly in South. We are already in touch with few of them. And also in exports, we were doing business with a couple of these retail chains who are established in Middle East also. So we already had the customers, Middle East branch working with us, now we are just extending it to the Indian market.

items.statement: Domestic manufacturing will focus on natural diamond jewellery; lab-grown jewellery production dedicated to own NIBHANA stores
items.quote: Lab-grown jewellery will be making in a special unit which is only for our stores.

items.statement: Gold hedging done by booking price with customer at order or using gold margin loan facility for exports
items.quote: some situations, we book the gold price with the customer when we get the order, so that we are hedge that way. In some cases where it is not like that, we also have Golkunda Diamonds & a facility called gold margin loans where we can pay the gold amount when we export. So we generally get hedge that way

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond jewellery margins around 20-25%, better than natural diamond; pricing largely settled after previous declines
items.quote: In terms of margin, it is definitely right now better than natural diamond in terms of the margin. It should be around 20% to 25% right now, the lab-grown margin, compared to natural diamond, which is significantly lower.

items.statement: Focus for next 2-3 years is domestic market expansion; export markets will grow organically but not focus area
items.quote: So, our focus for the next 2 to 3 years is mainly in India. Obviously, our current export markets we are catering to and organically we are growing there at a decent pace. But that's not our focus area for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Domestic manufacturing at full capacity could add 50-60% of current export revenue in couple of years
items.quote: So domestic, when it's working at 100% capacity, it should add to around 50% to 60% of the total revenue, as what we are right now, in the export market. That will take a couple of years, probably.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow due to heavy investment in new factory and retail stores over last 6-8 months
items.quote: As you know that the last 6-8 months, we have been expanding rapidly. We've been -- we have started a new factory. There's been a significant capital expenditure in the new factory. We've also opened a few stores. So there has been a significant outflow in that.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue grew 14.75% YoY to INR172.57 crore; EBITDA up 77.18% to INR18.58 crore with margin 10.74% (+378 bps); PAT up 88.76% to INR11.92 crore with margin 6.89% (+270 bps)

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue INR87.35 crore (+7.92% YoY); EBITDA INR9.94 crore (+84.62%); PAT INR6.78 crore (+113.23%)
items.quote: Coming to our quarterly performance, Q2 FY27 revenue stood at INR87.35 crores, registering 7.92% year-on-year growth. EBITDA increased by 84.62% to INR9.94 crores, while PAT grew by 113.23% to INR6.78 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR6,000-6,500 crores and EBITDA margin guidance of 18%
items.quote: we are committed to maintaining our EBITDA margin guidance of 18% for FY27, and we remain focused on delivering our FY27 revenue guidance of INR6,000 crores-INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: FY28 revenue guidance of around INR7,000 crores
items.quote: We are confident that the next financial year we are giving a guidance of around INR7,000 crores.

items.quote: We expect it to exceed INR300 crores in this financial year itself.

items.statement: Export business expected to reach INR500 crores in next three to four years
items.quote: As I have given the guidance earlier also, the next three to four years, we are confident that our export business will be to the tune of INR500 crores.

items.statement: Working capital days expected to improve by 50-75 days in FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: We remain confident of improving working capital days by 50 to 75 days in FY27 compared with FY26.

items.statement: Net debt expected to peak at INR2,000 crores and decline from FY28
items.quote: We expect net debt to start reducing from FY28, as guided.

items.statement: Healthy pipeline of large tenders across several states over next 12 months
items.quote: We expect a healthy pipeline of large tenders across several states over the next 12 months and consolidation among AMISPs further expands our opportunity to supply meters to other operators.

items.quote: Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Haryana. So I am confident with Bengal, Haryana, and Tamil Nadu, with these tenders, we should play a good role in that.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 19.4%, ahead of 18% FY27 guidance despite elevated input costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 19.4%, comfortably ahead of our FY27 guidance of 18%, despite elevated input costs and seasonal execution challenges.

items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 127 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 38.3%, supported by better supplier terms and improved logistics efficiency. EBITDA stood at INR225 crores, with EBITDA margin improving by 77 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 19.8%.

items.statement: GIC platform can support 3-5 crore additional meters without fresh capital
items.quote: Our strategic platform, GIC, backed by long-term non-recourse project financing and AA- rated project SPVs, can support 3 to 5 crores additional meters without the need of fresh capital.

items.statement: Year-on-year margin moderation due to elevated raw material costs from West Asia supply disruptions and currency movements on imported components
items.quote: On year-on-year basis, margin moderated, mainly because of elevated raw material costs amid supply disruptions related to the West Asia situation and currency movements on imported components, along with the higher depreciation and finance costs as we scaled up our operations.

items.statement: Gas metering opportunity INR35,000-36,000 crores over next few years, PNGRB specs by end FY27, traction in FY28
items.quote: In India alone, this is an opportunity of about INR35,000 crores to INR36,000 crores over the next few years. We expect PNGRB to finalize smart gas meter specifications by end of FY27 and tendering for smart meter gas meters to gain meaningful traction in FY28.

items.statement: Water metering emerging as significant long-term opportunity in India and globally
items.quote: We also believe water metering will emerge as a significant long-term opportunity, both in India and globally, as utilities focus on digitization and resources optimization.

items.statement: Adani is a major customer for meters; Adani's acquisition of IntelliSmart viewed positively
items.quote: Adani is one of our major customers for meters. We are one of the largest suppliers to Adani for smart meters. So in that sense also, it is good.

items.statement: Selective bidding approach focused on return thresholds; consolidation among AMISPs expands supply opportunity

items.quote: That was basically on the terms of dividend, that the company this year has not paid any dividend and to give a benefit to our shareholders, and where promoters have not participated in the buyback.

items.statement: Chairman Ishwar Chand Agarwal passed away on 4th November 2026
items.quote: On 4th of November 2026, we lost our Chairman and Executive Director, Mr. Ishwar Chand Agarwal.

items.quote: It is about 4.1 million meters which we have installed in H1. As JK sir was saying, Q2 is seasonally weak, so about 1.8 odd million meters are installed in Q2.

items.quote: This quarter we have turned operationally cash positive, and we are very confident that we will be containing our working capital, our gross and net debt because of the cash generation phase that all our projects have now entered into.

items.statement: Uttar Pradesh installation slowdown due to local body elections; expect normal pace from April 2027

items.quote: So as of now, we cannot give some sort of guidance on the numbers and all. We are already working on that.

items.quote: So almost INR40 crores we have already tied up for the Dewas extrusion machine and another INR10 crores of similar other fabrication machines are in order. So the INR50 crores to INR60 crores is already tied up.

items.statement: Dewas facility yet to commence commercial operations; extrusion press machine in production phase, expected in 3-4 months.

items.statement: Pithampur extrusion capacity 24,000 tons per annum; foundry capacity 12,000 tons per annum.
items.quote: Our manufacturing infrastructure includes a foundry capacity of 12,000 tons per annum, an extrusion capacity of 24,000 tons per annum, along with machining and anodizing capability.

items.statement: EBITDA margin moderated to approximately 2.2% in H1 FY27 from 4.5% in H1 FY26.
items.quote: Consequently, the EBITDA margin moderated to approximately 2.2% from 4.5%.

items.statement: Focus on high value-added products in automotive, construction and solar industries.

items.quote: Our export markets include United States, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, Qatar, Israel and Australia. Export remains an important part of our manufacturing business.

items.quote: we have gone ahead and adopted in line with some of the global shipyards where they use Cobots, the collaborative robots for shipbuilding purposes, where they can operate even during curved surfaces.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue ₹1,827 crores (+9% YoY), PAT ₹172 crores (+12% YoY); H1 FY27 revenue ₹3,641 crores (+26% YoY), PAT ₹345 crores (+26% YoY)

PAT stood at INR26 crores compared to INR30 crores in H1 FY26, primarily due to higher depreciation and interest costs.

items.quote: Finally, our EBITDA guidance, which we spoke to you about last time of about INR 500 crores to INR 550 crores for FY27, I feel it is within reach.

items.statement: Target to become debt-free by FY29
items.quote: Much of this internal accrual will also go towards our debt repayment, and we reiterate our stand that by the year 2028-29, we will become a debt free company.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 17.6% in H1 FY27 from 16.5% in H1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins for Q2 and H1 are comparable at about 17.7% and 17.6%. This is a marked improvement in last year numbers of about 129 bps over last year Quarter 2, where it was 16.4%, and last year H1 was 16.5%.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 39.5% in H1 FY27 from 35.4% in H1 FY26
items.quote: The gross margins are at a healthy 39.5% for our total business in H1 FY27 as compared to about 35.4% last year.

items.statement: Biofuels EBITDA margin improved to 10.2% in H1 FY27 from 8.4% in H1 FY26
items.quote: H1 EBITDA was at about INR 71 crores, and the margin rose to 10.2% in H1 FY27 from last year 8.4%.

items.statement: Non-IMFL EBITDA margins at 23-25%
items.quote: Non-IMFL incidentally, if you if you were a part of the last time's call, I had told you that our margins on non-IMFL are also pretty encouraging in the tune of 23% to 25%.

items.statement: IMFL EBITDA margins north of 27-28%
items.quote: this part of the portfolio is predominantly from the P&A part of the IMFL segment where the margins are northwards of 27%-28%.

items.statement: IMFL volumes grew 84% and revenue up 42% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: However, the silver lining is that the IMFL volumes grew by 84% and the revenue was up by 42% in Q2, and that continues the trend from Q1.

items.statement: Non-IMFL volumes in UP dropped from 6.4M to 6.2M cases in Q2 due to higher strength mandate
items.quote: And that explains the volumes in non-IMFL in Q2 dropped from 6.4 million last year to 6.2 million this year.

items.statement: IMFL revenue share rose from 12% in Q2 FY26 to 18% in Q2 FY27, targeting 24% in Q3 and 28-30% by Q4
items.quote: If we look at Q2 last year, the contribution of the revenue from IMFL was about 12%. Q1 in the current year was at 14% and Q2 we ended at about 18%. Our outlook for Q3 stands at about 24%.

items.statement: IMFL EBITDA contribution rose from 33% to 39% in H1, targeting 50% by FY27 end
items.quote: This 25% of revenue of IMFL last year contributed to about 33% EBITDA, and the 32% IMFL revenue this year has contributed to about 39% of the EBITDA mix that we are declaring for H1.

items.statement: Potable spirits realization improved from Rs 410 to Rs 432 per case
items.quote: Realization per case has improved on potable spirits, and that is because of the increasing IMFL share. We've moved northwards from Rs. 410 per case to Rs. 432 per case.

items.statement: ENA capacity at Kashipur increasing from 30 lakh to 55 lakh litres per month by Dec/Jan
items.quote: So, at Kashipur, right now, we are manufacturing around 30 lakh litres of ENA per month, which is expected to be around 55 lakh litres per month.

items.statement: H1 capex of INR 54 crores for maintenance, tanks, machines and ENA capacity expansion
items.quote: The capex during the half is related to some maintenance of tanks and machines. There is some ENA capex also going on.

items.statement: Ethanol allocation for current ESY at 14.75 crore litres vs 10 crore litres last year, targeting 20-21 crore litres total supply
items.quote: Today the allotment of biofuel is 14.75 crore litres. Comparatively from last year it is high because last year in the initial tender we got about 10 crore litres of supply.

items.statement: Grain prices rose from Rs 21.7 to Rs 23.3/kg in Q2, expected to average Rs 26.5-27/kg in Q3
items.quote: Grain prices have moved northwards from 21.7 to 23.3 for quarter two, and we expect an average buying price in the range of about 26.5 per kg to 27 per kg in quarter three.

items.statement: Coal prices increased from Rs 5,500 to Rs 6,800, power & fuel cost to remain at Q2 level in H2
items.quote: The power & fuel cost have increased in quarter 2 on account of increase in the coal price from around the INR 5,500 to the INR 6,800. Right? And the second half will be same as compared to quarter 2.

items.statement: ENA manufacturing cost expected to rise from Rs 56 to Rs 64-65 per litre in Q3
items.quote: my per-liter manufacturing cost in Q2 was about INR 56. On account of the inflationary trend on grain prices, etcetera., I expect this to go up to about INR 64 to INR 65.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of INR 186 crores in H1 FY27 vs outflow last year
items.quote: The balance sheet is the part I'm most pleased with where the operating cash flow was INR 186 crores against an outflow last year.

items.statement: Gross borrowings reduced to INR 714 crores, debt-to-equity improved from 0.66x to 0.54x
items.quote: We repaid INR 88 crores of debt, bringing gross borrowings down to about INR 714 crores and our gross debt-to-equity improved from 0.66 times to 0.54 times.

items.statement: Entered West Bengal via expression of interest, launch slated Dec-Jan; pursuing Andhra Pradesh, Daman, Silvassa registrations
items.quote: There is an expression of interest that we participated in West Bengal, and we have come through successful in the same. The launch is slated in the months of December-January, depending upon the label registration.

items.statement: Planning entry into Rajasthan, Punjab, Himachal, Northeast; expect 1 North state entry by FY27 end
items.quote: In the list that I spoke to you about North, my gut feel says that we'll probably be able to manage one state before the end of this year.

items.statement: IMFL standalone realization at Rs 832 per case vs potable spirits blended at Rs 432
items.quote: IMFL alone as a standalone is at about INR 832. So that partially answers your question.

items.statement: Potable spirits realization projected at Rs 500 at 24% IMFL mix and Rs 550 at 30% IMFL mix
items.quote: At 24%, we expect this realization to go up to about INR 500. And at about 30%, the average realization, which is for potable spirits, should be at about INR 550.

items.statement: Biofuels margins better than peers due to strategic procurement, FCI rice allocation, molasses/pent wash power
items.quote: we will not be impacted as some of the other players in the industrial, plus we are a well-established old player in this industry. Our plants are located in the rice belts, and we also have a 30% allocation of FCI rice.

items.statement: Biofuels profitability challenged by rising grain and coal costs; maize margins lower due to price squeeze
items.quote: Our biggest concern, of course, is the fact that the costs for our inputs is rising. Grain prices have moved northwards from 21.7 to 23.3 for quarter two, and we expect an average buying price in the range of about 26.5 per kg to 27 per kg in quarter three.

items.statement: Marketing and advertising costs significantly lower than peers due to infancy stage of IMFL business
items.quote: Currently, because I am in the infancy stage of IMFL, my marketing and advertising costs are significantly lower compared to my peers.

items.statement: Management expects margins to recover when war impact lifts and regulatory costs anniversary
items.quote: I think we will be back to winning ways, not just on revenue, but on profit as well.

items.statement: Industry grew double digits for first time in long time in Q2 FY27
items.quote: In quarter 2 of '26-'27, which is July to September '26, the industry actually, for the first time in a very long time, grew double digits, which was good to see.

items.statement: Gross margins down ~420 bps YoY; PBT margin fell to 0.6% from 3.6% two years ago
items.quote: The gross margins have come down this quarter versus the previous year by about 420 basis points, which is a lot.
