items.statement: War-driven commodity inflation and currency depreciation biggest margin headwinds
items.quote: The big one is obviously the impact of the war in the Middle East, and the impact of that is basically on two very big areas. One is basically commodity inflation driven by the rise of cost in anything to do with crude oil.

items.statement: Energy efficiency regulation changes for refrigerators and ACs (nearly two-thirds of business) materially impacted gross margins
items.quote: This year, we have had the war, and then on top, the energy change on refrigerators and air conditioners, which is nearly two-thirds of our business. Therefore, that has had a material impact on the gross margins.

items.statement: 5% price increase taken on 1st November due to significant cost inflation
items.quote: First, we have taken a 5% price increase already on the 1st of November, because of the significant cost inflation that we have been experiencing.

items.statement: Launched Luxuriem 650L four-door refrigerator range in August with triple evaporator cooling and freshness detection AI
items.quote: We are really delighted, and I will share more detail on this later, to launch the Whirlpool Luxuriem range, which is the 650 liters refrigerator, premium four-door refrigerator, which has gone off to a great start.

items.statement: Front-load washing machine volume grew 30%; launched 10kg range; Bloom Wash premium top-load gained triple-digit bps share
items.quote: In front-load washing machines, we have seen a 30% volume growth, and we have also launched the 10-kilogram range, further premiumizing our portfolio.

items.statement: Semi-automatic washers: >45% of portfolio now has Dynamix technology; launched first glass-top semi-auto with Dynamix dispenser
items.quote: More than 45% of our semi-automatic business is now got the Dynamix technology.

items.statement: Direct cool refrigerator auto-defrost range grew 40% YoY; launched Stain Wash 9kg Cold model to strengthen mid-segment
items.quote: In direct cool refrigerators, we have the auto defrost range, which grew 40% year-on-year, demonstrating good consumer pull.

items.statement: Held overall volume share in refrigerators and washers (~10 bps lower YoY) despite competitive pressure and April-May price hikes
items.quote: We held share. We almost held share, because we are about 9 or 10 basis points lower versus last year in the entire refs and washers.

items.statement: No-frost refrigerator share down >50 bps due to absence in premium >500L segment until Luxuriem launch
items.quote: In no-frost refrigerators, we have more than 50 basis points decline in our market share versus year ago. The key reason for that is because we were not present in the premium segment of the refrigerators.

items.statement: Semi-automatic and front-load washer share grew double digits; top-load lost triple-digit share overall but gained triple-digit in premium segment
items.quote: Semi-automatic washers in a very competitive market, very tough market again, several players coming in. We have been able to grow our market shares by double digits. Same is the case in front-load washers, where we continue to grow our share by double digits off a smaller base.

items.statement: Invested in Luxuriem launch to enable grand August launch; manufacturing capacity for obsidian interiors constrained
items.quote: The biggest problem that I have right now is to be able to manufacture enough of these to cater to the demand for obsidian interiors.

items.statement: Net working capital as % of net revenue nearly flat; 6 of last 9 quarters flat or negative; standalone (ex-Elica) better in June and September
items.quote: This quarter is nearly flat. I would say it is more or less flat. Therefore, six out of the nine quarters, we have been keeping it at flat or below.

items.statement: Revenue grew ~14% YoY in Q2 FY27 led by April-May price hikes, premiumization, and volume share hold in growing industry
items.quote: For the quarter, your company delivered a double-digit revenue growth of circa 14%.

items.statement: Elica subsidiary revenue grew 12% and profit grew 22%
items.quote: Elica continues with a very good performance, revenue of 12% and profit of 22%.

items.statement: Commodity inflation from crude oil impacting polystyrene, MDI, polyol, polypropylene, ABS; currency depreciation increased imported component costs
items.quote: Whether it's polystyrene or whether it's MDI or polyol, polypropylene, or ABS, all of these are impacted by the price of crude oil in a very big way.

items.statement: Thanked engineering, procurement, and manufacturing teams for Luxuriem development and launch
items.quote: I just want to say a huge thank you on behalf of all our investors, shareholders, to all of the people in engineering, all of the people in procurement, and all of the people in manufacturing who made this amazing thing happen.

items.statement: Revenue grew 13.7% YoY in Q2 FY27 driven by price increases, volume growth, premiumization, and Elica double-digit growth
items.quote: In this quarter, we delivered a top line of INR1,873 crores. It came in at a growth of 13.7%.

items.statement: Price increases taken in April and May 2026 to mitigate war-led inflation, oil, currency depreciation, and energy impacts on refrigerators and air conditioners
items.quote: The first one was the price increase, which we took in the month of April and May, to mitigate the impact of the cost increases on account of the war-led inflation, oil, currency depreciation, and the energy impacts on refrigerators and air con.

items.statement: Material margins impacted by commodity cost increases, currency depreciation, and regulatory upcharges from new energy regulations; partially offset by P4G program and price increases
items.quote: Our material margins are impacted by multiple factors, and the biggest one of that has been the war-related, the commodity increases.

items.statement: EBITDA at INR 40 crores (2.1% margin), down 31% YoY; PBT before exceptional items at INR 34 crores (1.8% margin), down 28% YoY
items.quote: On the profit side, our EBITDA came in at INR40 crores at 2.1%, a decline of 31% versus last year, and a profit before tax, before exceptional items at INR34 crores, 1.8 percentage points of net sales, again declined by 28% versus last year.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA at INR 179 crores (3.9% margin), down 33% YoY; PBT at INR 173 crores (3.8% margin), down 29% YoY
items.quote: On the profit side, EBITDA is at INR179 crores at 3.9%, a drop of 33% versus last year, and a PBT at INR173 crores at 3.8%, again, a drop of about 29% versus last year.

items.statement: Premium segments growing 2-3x faster than entry segments; direct cool premium market share now higher than middle/entry; frost-free premium share half of entry but expected to grow substantially in 12-18 months
items.quote: Typically, we would be growing about 2X in premium or between 2X and 3X in premium compared to what we're doing in the entry segment.

items.statement: Luxuriem refrigerator production line at Pune plant has 400,000-500,000 unit capability, sufficient for several years of demand
items.quote: Well, we have about, call it between 400,000 and 500,000 capability, basically. But again, the reason I'm not able to give you a straight answer is because different things can come out of that line.

items.statement: Cash utilization planned for regular capacity enhancements, new product launches, factory automation, backward integration, and evaluation of inorganic margin-accretive opportunities
items.quote: Firstly, we need cash as we said, capex for our regular capacity enhancements over the next few years. Second, we need to make sure that we have cash to be able to do all the new products.

items.statement: Evaluating potential inorganic growth opportunities in India that are margin accretive, at exploratory stage with no certainty of materialization
items.quote: Further to this, and we have intimated this earlier as well, we continue to evaluate potential inorganic growth opportunities in India, which are margin accretive.

items.statement: No further updates on parent stake sale from current 39.7% holding; last update provided to NSE/BSE on September 24, 2026
items.quote: On the second question, as far as any stake sale of the parent is concerned from its current holding of 39.7%, we do not have any further updates to provide at this time.

items.statement: Buyback considered as one option among others for cash utilization; board will review all aspects and take collective decision when ready
items.quote: As we look at all the options for cash, this will certainly be one of the things that we look at. But like I said, it's right now too soon for me to come to you with an idea.

items.statement: New energy regulations effective beginning of calendar year 2026 impacting refrigerator and air conditioner business (65% of business) with regulatory upcharges
items.quote: The new energy regulations came into force at the beginning of the calendar year, impacting the ref and air con business for us, which is 65% of business.

items.statement: Elica kitchen appliances business delivering double-digit revenue growth and double-digit profit margins with profit growth higher than revenue growth
items.quote: Elica continues to deliver double-digit profit margins, and profit growth is higher than revenue growth for Elica.

items.statement: Highest-ever washer production in July 2026 driven by highest-ever front-load washer production, indicating strong demand and ability to meet it
items.quote: We had also the highest-ever washer production in July 2026, which is good because it means that there is demand as well, as well as the ability of us to meet that demand.

items.statement: Commodity costs remain way above year-ago levels despite recent declines; cycle time means cost reductions not immediately reflected in margins
items.quote: cost Whirlpool of India Limited November 19, 2026 still, they're way above what they were a year ago. It's nothing even close to irregular. It would be more like extraordinary, right

items.statement: Gross margin recovery uncertain due to ongoing geopolitical issues, commodity volatility, and competitive intensity; too soon to predict Q3/Q4 recovery
items.quote: I think gross margins, I see them till this black swan event is over, I think it is going to be challenging. And there is no point in my or anybody trying to second-guess it.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 13.7% split roughly half from pricing and half from volume and mix
items.quote: Our overall revenue growth is about 13.7% as you've seen in the slides. The broad breakup of this is, a bulk of it, roughly half of it is coming from the pricing, and the balance half is coming from the volume and mix because it's a question of both.

items.statement: AC volume increased about 60% this quarter
items.quote: The volume increase is about 60%, if I recall, on AC. That is what our growth is in this quarter.

items.statement: Margins will stay compressed this fiscal year due to commodity costs and regulatory impact
items.quote: I think in the balance of the year, as long as this war is there, and as long as the anniversary effect of the regulatory impact is there, which will be October, November, December, and January, March, I think margins will continue to stay compressed, because commodity costs have not gone down, they have only gone up.

items.statement: Price increases of roughly 5% in April, 5% in May, and 5% on November 1
items.quote: But we took roughly about a 5% price increase in April and 5% roughly in May, and now we've taken a 5% in November 1.

items.statement: Significant price promotion and new brands at entry to lower mid-end in top-load washing machines and direct cool refrigerators
items.quote: On water top load, I did tell you that there has been a significant amount of activity or action that has happened at the entry end, entry to lower mid-end, where there has been a lot of price promotion, and really significant price lowering activity from a competition point of view, and a lot of new brands coming in.

items.statement: Attrition YTD is better than last year and lower than durables average; top 12 leadership team extremely stable
items.quote: Our attrition this year at this point in time YTD is better than last year, which means it is lower than last year, right? That means the number of people who are leaving the company as a percentage is much lower than last year, and it is lower than the kind of average that we see in durables.

items.statement: Elica MD Pralhad Bhutada stepping down March 31, 2027; Whirlpool veteran Anish Ahuja to take over as CEO and MD from April 1, 2027 after 7-month handover
items.quote: coming to an end on March 31, 2027, and with very strong mutual cordial discussions, he has decided to step down as the CEO and MD of Elica from 2027 as part of the normal course of his tenure ending. We then made sure that we moved somebody from Whirlpool who was a top talent internally, who was one of the very, very strong performers, who had a very strong P&L experience managing a similar- size

items.statement: Luxuriem brand investment is reasonably significant, a few crores this quarter and coming quarter, not one or two crores
items.quote: It was obviously reasonably significant. It was not one or two crores in this quarter or in the coming quarter. It's a few crores, but I'm not going to get into the detail of that because we do not want to share so much information with the general market because it erodes our competitive advantage.

items.statement: Outsourcing capacity increasing industry-wide in washing machines and refrigerators; Whirlpool sources semi-auto washing machines with embedded tech, ACs fully outsourced, refrigerators fully in-house
items.quote: Indeed, you're right that it's not just the washing machine, the refrigerator industry, but basically the 3PL, the OEM manufacturers who can provide to companies like ours or companies which are our competition definitely is going up in terms of capacity. Also, such players are branching into different categories and segments.

items.statement: Board will review cash and share price; decision on capital allocation by end of summer 2027
items.quote: Very simply, by the end of summer, we should have a pretty good idea of what to do because we are looking at multiple options of how best to leverage value for the company and the shareholders. That is something that we will have by the end of summer 2027, and that was a promise I made a few months ago, that we would take the time to look at all options and come back, and we will do what is best f

items.statement: This is a black swan year; commodity costs up, regulatory impact through Oct-Jan; neither Oct, Nov, Dec nor Jan will be easy
items.quote: I think this year, like I said, is a challenging year. Neither October, November, December, nor January, especially October, November, December is not going to be easy because the commodity costs are still impacted.

items.statement: Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin target 5%
items.quote: That is what is our hope; we should target to reach 5% once again.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance moderated to 10% YoY from earlier 12-15%
items.quote: We had earlier projected about 12 to 15% growth of volume for this year. I think we should be moderating that down to 10% growth going forward over the next few years, looking at the way the copper prices and the market is there.

items.statement: FY30 revenue target 5,000 crores driven by 10% volume growth and price increase
items.quote: We are looking at 10% growth of volume year-on-year, and the balance is coming from price increase when we reach 5,000 crores by 2030.

items.statement: Commodity margins 2-3.5%; value-added margins 4-10% averaging 7-7.5%
items.quote: The commodity margins in our business earlier used to be around 2%, but last quarter we got good margins from China, so that went up to closer to 3%. As regards the value-added products margins, it varies from 4% to 10%, averaging roughly about 7 to 7.5%.

items.statement: Capex target 40 crores over two years; 9.45 crores spent in H1 FY27
items.quote: We have had a capex target of 40 crores spread over two years. In the first half of the first year, we have already spent 9.45 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity 35,000 tons; expansion to 45,000 tons targeted by Q4 FY28
items.quote: Our original plan of capacity expansion was in the next year 27-28. We still hold to that guidance that towards the end of next year, the capacity will be increased from 35,000 to 45,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Value-added capacity roughly 20,000-25,000 tons currently
items.quote: I would say roughly about 20,000 to 25,000 tons would be my capacity for all the value-added products put together.

items.statement: CTC conductor capacity 100-150 tons; running at ~50 tons/month
items.quote: Roughly about 100 to 150 tons is our capacity, but we are doing close to about 50 tons a month.

items.statement: Value-added share 60% in Q2 FY27; target 69% over 5 years; commodity 31% long-term
items.quote: In our earlier projection also, every year we are forecasting that our value-added products will keep going up from 60% all the way to 69% over a period of 5 years, but even at the end of 5 years, we were saying that 31% will be commodities.

items.statement: Value-added split: automotive/switchgear, transformers/motors, bus bars; bus bars serve building, trade, panel, AI
items.quote: The way we have classified is in the three categories of value-added products. Number one is automotive and switchgear, which very clearly are going for automotives and switchgears. Number two is transformers and motors, which is also, I don't think there's too much doubt in what that means. The only place where, when we say bus bars, the bus bars go right from the building industry to the trade t

items.statement: OE sales ~50% of value-added; 10% trade; rest OE
items.quote: Out of the 60% value-added products, I think roughly about 50% will be to OE; there might be 10% which goes to trade, and the rest is to OE.

items.statement: Transformer customers include Atlanta, Crompton Greaves, TMC; over 50 transformer companies served
items.quote: We have a customer base of over 50 transformer companies. The most notable ones would be Atlanta, Crompton Greaves, and TMC. These are the three main ones, and we supply them the entire range of products for the transformers.

items.statement: Value addition ~114 rupees/kg on raw material
items.quote: If you see the presentation, you would have seen that our value addition is roughly about 114 rupees a kilo on our raw material.

items.statement: 85% of copper exposure hedged on MCX; practice continues
items.quote: We have been always saying that 85% of our exposure is hedged on the MCX, and we continue to maintain the same practice.

items.statement: Scrap supply adequate for next 1-1.5 years; vertically integrated advantage
items.quote: At least in the next one to one and a half years, I do not see any major hiccup. One thing we need to understand as we go forward: the availability of scrap also keeps going up; it is only a question of whether we will be able to garner enough share for ourselves. I am quite confident with our connections and with our supply chain linkages we should not have a major issue.

items.statement: EPR launched April 1, 2026; registration live; 5-10-15% ratio over 3 years; weak enforcement expected initially
items.quote: EPR has been officially launched on April 1st of 2026. I think, the website for registration of all companies on EPR has gone live last month, and the ratio is from 5, 10, and 15% over the next three years. It is going to be a slow start. While the registration has started, I have not seen too much rush of companies registering for the EPR, both as producers as well as for people who need to fulfi

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to A- by ICRA; expected to reduce interest costs
items.quote: During this quarter, our credit rating was upgraded to A- by ICRA, which I think is a great achievement and will bring down our interest costs in the future.

items.statement: Restructuring: 1:1 share allotment from Bhagyanagar India on Oct 8, 2026; BSE/NSE in-principle approval received; SEBI approval awaited; listing targeted by Dec 2026
items.quote: For every share held of Bhagyanagar India, one additional share of Tieramet has been given, and this has been done as of 8th October 2026. In-principle approval of the listing of the share of Tieramet has been received from both BSE and NSE. Now we are awaiting an in-principle approval from SEBI, after which the formal listing process for Tieramet will start.

items.statement: Not pursuing copper clad laminates or PCM for next 1-2 years; lacks technology/expertise
items.quote: We are evaluating a lot of products in which we want to go ahead, but laminates and PCM is not there in our immediate plan of action for at least the next one or two years. That is not where we are looking at, because that technology and our expertise at that level is not really there.

items.statement: India LPG consumption grew from 26.3 MMT in FY20 to 35.04 MMT in FY26, making India the world's third largest LPG consumer.
items.quote: India is already the world's third largest LPG consumer; consumption increased from about 26.3 million metric tons in FY20 to 35.04 million metric tons in FY26.

items.statement: Company operates 68 bottling facilities, 478+ LPG tankers, 225 HCVs/LCVs, 3,400 dealers, 3,400 direct customers, 300+ industrial customers, 315+ ALDS, 52+ CNG stations, 82+ CNG cascade vehicles, 15+ cylinder manufacturing units, and 3 high-
items.quote: Our robust and integrated infrastructure comprises four time-chartered LPG vessels, 68 bottling facilities, a fleet of 478 plus LPG tankers, 225 HCVs and LCVs, a network of 3,400 dealers, and 3,400 direct customers, 300 plus industrial customers, 315 plus auto LPG dispensing stations, and 52 plus CNG retail stations, 82 plus CNG cascade vehicles, plus 15 plus LPG cylinder manufacturing units, manu

items.statement: Entered new long-term supply arrangements with industrial customers for 2-3 years on competitive pricing, adding customers like Patanjali, Parle, and Pizza Hut.
items.quote: We also entered into new long-term supply arrangements with industrial customers, with new and old customers, commitment to remain price competitive, ensuring sustained customer relationship and supply continuity.

items.statement: Working capital increased due to longer procurement cycle from US LPG imports; short-term borrowings funded advance payments to suppliers.
items.quote: The increase in LPG imports from the USA, in response to supply disruptions in the Middle East, has lengthened our procurement cycle and raised our working capital requirement. We have funded this through a short-term borrowing to keep supplies uninterrupted to our valued customers, and we expect it to ease once supply conditions in the Middle East stabilize.

items.statement: Net debt stands at ~INR820 crores; INR290 crores of other current assets are supplier advances for US imports, making effective net debt lower.
items.quote: Our debt has gone, the net debt stands at somewhere close to INR820 crores. But if you knock off that INR290 crores, so probably that, yes. You are right in saying that, yes, the numbers can be much lower.

items.statement: Other current assets jumped from INR449 crores to INR738 crores (INR298 crores increase), primarily advances to suppliers for US LPG procurement.
items.quote: If you see the balance sheet, the other current assets have moved from INR449 crores to INR738 crores, which is INR298 crores jump. I would say the larger aspect is these are advances to the supplies

items.statement: Promoters increased shareholding to over 60%, reflecting confidence in company prospects.
items.quote: Promoters increased their shareholding to over 60%, reflecting their confidence in the company's prospects.

items.statement: Over INR800 crores invested in capex over last five years; benefits now being realized.
items.quote: With over INR800 crores invested in capex over the last five years, we are now realizing the benefits of these investments made.

items.statement: 56 CNG stations already capex done; 6 more to be operational soon; targeting 100 stations in Bengaluru JV with GAIL within 3-4 quarters (by next Diwali).
items.quote: But, hopefully, within two, three quarters we will complete this target. Our next three to four quarters, we will complete this target. Sammed Vardhaman: Of 100?… Mr. Nitin Khara: Yeah 100, Because 56 is already over, and another 10 are under pipeline. So, it'll be 66. We are focusing by next Diwali; it will be over

items.statement: Management does not give formal full-year guidance but indicated H2 will be better than H1; last quarter's 10-15% QoQ growth aspiration maintained on bottom line.
items.quote: We do not give any guidance in terms of what the full-year numbers would look like, but you would have seen the growth trajectory that we have achieved in Q1 and Q2. We are almost, I would say, in terms of EBITDA, for H1, we have been trading at somewhere close to INR304 crores and with a PAT of somewhere close to INR132 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 7.2%, up 120 bps from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: EBITDA grew 93% Y-o-Y to INR161 crores from INR83 crores in Q2 FY26, with an EBITDA margin improving sequentially to 7.2% and expansion of 120 basis points over Q1 FY27.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue of INR4,644 crores nearly matched full FY26 revenue of INR4,705 crores, showing strong momentum.
items.quote: Notably, the company has almost matched its full-year FY26 revenue from operations of INR4,705 crores within the first six months of FY27, highlighting strong momentum and business performance.

items.statement: Long-term customer agreements use formula pricing linked to international LPG prices; company remains price competitive due to 30-year market experience and 169-guideline plants.
items.quote: We have signed agreements with many people based on formulas, linking them to international prices, so they will continue with the company.

items.statement: Board to internally discuss dividend increase and buyback; no timeline communicated.
items.quote: Look there are multiple factors into it. We will internally discuss, and there is a board approval which is required for the same. Currently, we cannot communicate what and when it is going to happen, but let us hope for it.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments and Middle East supply disruptions causing LPG price volatility and longer procurement cycles from US imports.
items.quote: During the quarter, the LPG industry continued to face challenges arising from the ongoing geopolitical developments and supply uncertainties in the Middle East, which resulted in volatility in international LPG prices and availability also.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth for watch components expected to exceed original 12-14% expectation
items.quote: Based on this, we believe our full year revenue growth will be higher than our original expectation of about 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Eigen medium-term revenue growth target remains 20-25% CAGR
items.quote: Our medium-term goal continues to be in the range of 20% to 25% CAGR.

items.statement: Standalone H2 FY27 growth expected to be similar to H1 FY27 (~35% YoY)
items.quote: And the second half, we believe will be something similar to the H1 of the year.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 increased to INR 70-75 crores from earlier INR 50 crores plan
items.quote: During the year, we will be spending in the range of around INR70 crores, ~75 crores for the capex.

items.statement: Watch components capacity expansion started earlier than planned FY28 timeline
items.quote: Instead of starting in FY '28, we have already started work on it, and we will be able to share more details about this in our next interaction.

items.statement: Eigen expansion includes Unit 1 space expansion, Unit 2A rack plating line commissioned, Unit 2B plot finalized for mid-FY28 operational
items.quote: We have already installed the rack plating line as a backward integration step in Unit 2A, a new facility located about 6 kilometers from our existing plant and shifted a set of other machines there, too. In addition, we have also finalized the agreement for an adjacent plot for Unit 2B in order to provide us with additional manufacturing space. This will become operational in the middle of the ne

items.statement: Watch components dials and hands grew ~30% YoY in H1 FY27 driven by volume growth from domestic and export customers
items.quote: We see a very encouraging performance during H1 of this fiscal year with revenue growth of approximately 30% Y-o-Y. The growth has been led by volume growth, both from the domestic and export customers

items.statement: Eigen precision engineering delivered close to 50% revenue growth in H1 FY27 from strong export demand and new customers
items.quote: The business has delivered close to 50% revenue growth in H1 FY '27. This performance reflects strong demand from our export customers, along with additional business opportunities from new customers.

items.statement: Packaging business Ornapac revenue grew over 30% in H1 FY27
items.quote: This business has continued to make encouraging progress with revenue growing by over 30% during H1 of this year.

items.statement: Bracelet business impacted by subdued export demand in Swiss watch industry
items.quote: The bracelet business caters to international customers and its performance during H1 FY '27 was impacted by a relatively subdued demand environment in the export segment.

items.statement: Gross margin decline due to product mix shift toward faster-growing Eigen (lower gross margin) and higher domestic sales in watch components
items.quote: Inherently, Eigen has a slightly lower gross margin than the watch component business. And as Eigen is growing faster than the watch component business, the mix -- the blended gross margin will drift downwards a bit

items.statement: Eigen new customers across battery energy storage, electronics, aerospace, defense segments in US and Europe
items.quote: We are in segments, which is not only EV, it is battery energy storage systems, electronics, aerospace, defense. And we are seeing a pretty robust pickup in demand and even new customers across these segments.

items.statement: Packaging business gaining traction with international luxury brands for local sourcing in India
items.quote: We're already seeing this kind of traction with some brands. Unfortunately, I can't name the brands, but these are international brands.

items.statement: Favre Leuba present in 35+ countries with 45+ doors outside Ethos; sales higher than expected
items.quote: In terms of number of countries, we are in excess of, I think, 35 countries. I need a little bit time to check on it. And more than 45 doors in countries other than Ethos. So almost 50% of the doors are outside Ethos.

items.statement: Overall company export share ~75%; Eigen export share slightly higher
items.quote: The sales in the export is almost 75% overall for the company. For the Eigen, it is slightly on the higher side.

items.statement: H1 FY27 growth majorly volume-driven with minimal currency impact
items.quote: In this first half, there is not much change into the currency compared to the previous year. So majorly, the growth is the volume-driven growth.

items.statement: Eigen winning programs based on manufacturability, repeatability and customer confidence, not just cost
items.quote: In most of these high complex and the technology products, it is basically the understanding of the product, how is your manufacturability and how is your repeatability. The customer confidence in those matters is more important.

items.statement: Eigen capabilities expanding: rack plating commissioned, welding, blanking, machining capabilities added incrementally
items.quote: I already mentioned rack plating. That's an important part that we do. There are different forms of welding, different forms of blanking and machining that these are incremental capabilities that allow us to expand our product base.

items.statement: Ornapac packaging achieved positive PBT in Q2 FY27; expects profitability to continue
items.quote: An important milestone during the period was achieving positive PBT in quarter 2 of FY '27. We expect the positive profitability trend to continue through the remaining quarters of the year

items.statement: Marginal debt increase for FY27 capex and higher working capital from business growth
items.quote: As in the current year, we are planning major capex. So there will be some debt addition. And as the level of the business is going up, the working capital requirement is also increasing, and there is a marginal increase in debt.

items.statement: No immediate restructuring plans; focus on growing existing businesses over fragmentation
items.quote: Right now, the businesses, they have so much potential. There's so much growth happening. There is so much excitement in what we are doing. I think right now, the focus is really to increase efficiencies, get new customers, grow the businesses. Maybe the time for restructuring will come a little later.

items.statement: Estima breakeven delayed to FY28 due to Swiss market challenges in US, UAE, China markets
items.quote: We are hoping that if everything goes right, perhaps next year will be the breakeven year.

items.statement: Bracelet business recovery dependent on Swiss watch industry revival and new customer homologation
items.quote: We expect that the customer base, we'll start to see the results of the expansion of the customer base in the next quarter -- from the next quarter onwards.

items.statement: FY2027 revenue target of Rs.200 Crores with H2 revenue expected above Rs.100 Crores
items.quote: We, I think, committed Rs.180 Crores in our last presentation, but we will cross, I think, Rs.200 Crores and margin will be good. Revenue in the first half, six months, I think we reached to 98. So in the second half, we will be having sales revenue of more than Rs.100 Crores.

items.statement: Solar MMS target of 1000 metric tons production and supply by end of FY2027
items.quote: As on date, we have produced and supplied 135 metric tons of MMS and further 200 metric tons orders are in hand. And till the end of the year, we expect 1000 metric ton production and supply of MMS structure.

items.statement: Solar MMS revenue expected between Rs.10-12 Crores by end of FY2027
items.quote: In October month itself, we supplied MMS material worth Rs.1 Crore. Now, we have an order of around 200 tons worth Rs.2 Crores and we are negotiating order worth around Rs.8 Crores to Rs.10 Crores with different clients. So, by the end of this year, we will be having a sale of solar MMS in tune of between Rs.10 to

items.statement: Capacity utilization target increase from 50% to 65-70% over next 12-18 months
items.quote: Capacity utilization is almost 50% right now. And in coming 12 to 18 months we will try to increase it to 15% to 20%. Because it is totally a labor-oriented factory where a lot of labors are involved in this.

items.statement: FY2028 priority to increase capacity utilization with revenue expectation of more than double FY2027
items.quote: The priority for FY2028 is to increase the capacity utilization because we are equipped, frankly speaking, for the bigger revenue compared to what we are expecting in 2027. In 2027, we are expecting Rs.200 Crores revenue and we are expecting more than double in coming years.

items.statement: Current order book of Rs.30 Crores with Rs.120 Crores revenue already achieved in H1 FY2027
items.quote: Order book right now we have an order book of around Rs.30 Crores and we have already done revenue of Rs.120 Crores. So, 150 has happened, still there are three to four months, we will comfortably reach 200 Crores.

items.statement: Solar MMS orders of 200 metric tons worth Rs.2 Crores in hand plus negotiation of Rs.8-10 Crores
items.quote: Now, we have an order of around 200 tons worth Rs.2 Crores and we are negotiating order worth around Rs.8 Crores to Rs.10 Crores with different clients.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve with capacity utilization; steel price stability key for margin maintenance
items.quote: Margin, I think we will maintain a little bit here and there. And if things are in our favor, like steel rates are stable, we will have more margin. If steel rate fluctuates, there are chances that we may have down or upward of 0.5% to 1% not more than that.

items.statement: Insulated panel JV gross margin 15-20%, net margin 6-7%
items.quote: The margin will be somewhere between, gross margin will be somewhere between 15% to 20%, net between 6% to 7%.

items.statement: EBITDA and profit both will increase once capacity utilization improves
items.quote: Yes, EBITDA is going to improve in future even the margins, once we start utilizing the capacity which we already built. 100% EBITDA and profit both will increase.

items.statement: Proposed insulated panel facility capex Rs.25-30 Crores through Durapuf Insutech Panels JV
items.quote: We are also evaluating a proposed continuous insulated panel manufacturing facility through Durapuf Insutech Panels Private Limited and this is a jointly owned entity with an individual partner responsible for operations. Estimated project capex is Rs.25 to Rs.30 Crores.

items.statement: Phase 5 and 6 expansion completed; adding 300-400 tons/month lightweight fabrication capacity
items.quote: With this, in phase 6, we are also adding approximately 300 to 400 tons per month of lightweight fabrication in These additions are intended to improve production flow, reduce operational bottlenecks, and enable more fabrication activity to be undertaken internally.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization ~50% without incremental capacity; ~40% with phase 5&6 capacity factored in
items.quote: Our current total, which does not yet account for incremental capacity, is at a certain level; once incremental capacity is factored in, it will decrease further, reaching around 40%.

items.statement: Rooftop solar capacity 300 kW meeting 53% of factory power consumption in Q2 FY2027
items.quote: Our installed rooftop solar capacity stands at approximately 300 kilowatts. During Q2 FY2027, rooftop solar met approximately 53% of our factory power consumption, compared with approximately 45% reported in Q1 FY2027.

items.statement: Steel price volatility impacts margins; 30% advance taken to hedge raw material cost
items.quote: For example, today I have an order of Rs.3 Crores with me. So, what I do, I purchase the maximum item of that particular order because we take around 30% advance from the client. So, we invest from our side and keep the stock.

items.statement: Steel price increase of 20% (Rs.50 to Rs.70) caused margin pressure in Q2
items.quote: What has happened this time is that the price of iron has increased by 20%. The material that we were buying for Rs.50 is now costing Rs.70. This results in a loss because I had made my calculations based on an amount of X, but when I actually go to purchase the material, I have to pay X plus the additional amount.

items.statement: Q2 FY2027 product mix: Roll forming 55%, PEB 45%, others 5%
items.quote: Roll forming products contributed approximately 55% of Q2 FY2027 product mix, while PEB accounted for the remaining 45% as presented in our investor presentation.

items.statement: Revenue structure: Fabricated structure 45%, Roll forming 50%, Others 5%
items.quote: Revenue structure, for fabricated structure is 45% of the total revenue. And roll forming is around 50% and rest is 5%.

items.statement: 91% of revenue from Gujarat; targeting Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan for expansion
items.quote: Our sales have 91% from Gujarat itself. In Gujarat province, in Gujarat state, we sell 91% of our total revenue. In Q2, while it remains an important industrial market for us, we are working to develop business relationships in other regions in a measured manner.

items.statement: Roll forming: 80% repeat customers; PEB: 90% new customers; Others: 80% new customers
items.quote: For roll forming products, we have repeat customers, a lot of repeat customers, you can say almost 80% repeat customers. But in fabricated structure, once you make your factory, then you wait for three to four years for expansion, so it is every time a new customer.

items.statement: Trade receivables reduced from Rs.350.47 lakh to Rs.162.8 lakh; inventory stable at ~Rs.1987.5 lakh
items.quote: Trade receivables reduced from 350.47 lakh to 162.8 lakh, while inventory stood at Rs.1987.5 lakh compared to Rs.1945.68 lakh at the end of March.

items.statement: No credit offered to solar MMS buyers except proven EPC contractors; 30% advance standard for projects
items.quote: First of all, we do not offer any credit. Our company is debt free. Our company is we do not have any bad debts. So, in solar structure, we keep ourselves away from the buyer who want credit. So, we do not supply material on credit.

items.statement: Proposed 50%+ stake in Durapuf Insutech Panels (trading PUF panels) for insulated panel JV; board approved, no investment yet
items.quote: First of all, we have not paid anything to anybody till date. It is just a board approval we have taken. Right. So, that is the first. Second thing is, it is an ongoing company which is doing trading of puf panel, insulated panel. Now the idea came to mind that there is a person who is experienced, there is a person who is ready to invest. So, why not to make it a subsidiary of Bansal?

items.statement: ROCE ~31% and ROE ~24% for H1 FY2027
items.quote: The historical financial highlights chart in the presentation also report return on capital employed ROCE of approximately 31% and return on equity of approximately 24% for H1 FY2027.

items.statement: Labor cost increasing due to government policies; automation reducing headcount (10 to 4 workers); robotic welding planned in 1-2 years
items.quote: Labor cost is not being reduced; it is rather increasing every day because of the government policies. Now you must have heard that PF we have to give even if the worker works for one year. Sorry, gratuity. PF amount has increased. Lot of compliances are there, so labor cost is not going to decrease. But yes, we have done automation, by which, where 10 people used to work, there now 4 people work.

items.statement: Labor availability risk during festivals (Navratri, Chhath) causes production disruption
items.quote: The labor is the only concern. See what happened? We have a lot of migrated labor; we have a lot of local labor. If Navratri comes in Gujarat, local labor disappears. If Chhat comes in Bihar, migrated labor disappears. This is the biggest challenge for us.

items.statement: Manufacturing 99.9% in-house; outsourcing only Rs.10-20 lakh out of Rs.50 Crore quarterly revenue
items.quote: Sir, this year, we cannot say zero, but it goes a little. 0.23% something like that. Very less, very less. In terms of, if I tell you turnover, out of 50 Crores, 10-20 lakhs of work would have been given out. Rest, everything is in-house.

items.statement: Insulated panel JV first year revenue target Rs.50 Crores, increasing Rs.25 Crores annually; line capacity 2000 meters/shift
items.quote: With addition of this line, our minimum revenue will increase by Rs.50 Crores in first year, minimum revenue I am telling you. And maximum we make around 2000 meter, we can make 2000 meter in one shift, so 2000 meter x 25 x 12 x 1250. We can add Rs.75 Crores in next year and the increment of Rs.25 Crores every year.

items.statement: Order inflow target of INR 450-500 crore expected in Q3 FY27
items.quote: And we are expecting orders about INR 500 crores in this financial year, somewhere, I mean, at different stages of -- in Q3, we'll be expecting around INR450 crores to INR500 crores of orders to be received.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 20% for FY27
items.quote: That is our aim -- that is our target. 20% growth, we want to get, yes, definitely.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to cross last year's 22.8% in FY27
items.quote: We'll certainly be crossing that last year figure of 22.8%. We are confident in that because the sales -- when the sales volumes increases, obviously, the margins will increase

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 2,164 crore as of 1st October 2026
items.quote: And the order book position of the company as on 1 st October 2026 stands at INR2,164 crores.

items.statement: Order book split: 35% aero, 22% space, 14% naval, 10% missile, 8% energy, balance others
items.quote: Yes. So we have 35% from aero sector, 22% from space sector, 14% from naval sector, 10% from missile sector and 8% from energy sector and balance is others.

items.statement: INR 1,000 crore capex plan approved by Board, financial sanction pending, execution over 3 years
items.quote: With respect to capex plan, yes, we have gone to Board and got approval. So we will be getting financial approval also, okay, we have announced. And we are in the process of finalizing the specifications and seeing we'll be coming back with more finer details on this once we get the financial sanction also.

items.statement: Wide Plate Mill part of INR 1,000 crore capex, strategic asset for rolling high-strength steel and aluminium plates up to 3.2m width
items.quote: Yes, what you are referring to is Wide Plate Mill, okay? And this is a very unique facility in the country where we can roll up to 3.2 meter width. And not only that -- not only these very high-strength steels can be rolled.

items.statement: 3D printing powder manufacturing facility of INR 40 crore expected to be established in 1 year after BAFA license received
items.quote: And probably in the coming 1 year, we will be able to esta blish this facility. It is something like a INR40 crores facility, and we should be able to get because we got preliminary license and our party also is working towards supplying the equipment currently

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 20%, confident of crossing FY26's 22.8% in full year
items.quote: EBITDA for the last financial year, if we look at it, it is 23% overall last financial year. And this quarter, the 6 months also, we are at 20%. And when in Q3 and Q4, we are expecting the higher amount of sal es, then obviously, it will be crossing that last year figure

items.statement: Majority fixed-price contracts under 18 months; price variation clause only for longer contracts; factoring likely inflation in pricing
items.quote: Generally, when fixing the price, we are factoring the likely inflation. As majority contracts are fixed price contracts only. If delivery period is less than 18 months, we are not allowed to have price variation formula.

items.statement: New global aerospace contracts expected to be long-term with price variation clauses, not fixed price
items.quote: So whatever we are now discussing, auditing is going on maybe last 1, 1.5 years, maybe in another 1 year, we are going to have a contract with them. So those are long-term contracts with price variation clause only.

items.statement: Raw material prices showing some cooling off after geopolitical disruptions; nickel and cobalt 100% imported
items.quote: Raw material pri ces depend on the geopolitical situation. So when supply chains are uninterrupted, I think they should cool down now in the current situation. We all have to see because the situations are dynamically changing. So now a little cooling off is being seen

items.statement: MoU with Heavy Water Board for nickel and cobalt recovery from scrap; strategic initiative for supply security, not immediate cost savings
items.quote: We had signed an MoU with Heavy Water Board under Department of Atomic Energy for recovery of nickel and cobalt from some of the scrap that we are having currently. So idea is a long-term perspective, okay?

items.statement: Revenue mix: 20% superalloys, 22% titanium alloys, 13% maraging steels, 36% special steels, balance miscellaneous; shifting focus to higher-value superalloys and titanium
items.quote: For example, we get about 20% of our revenue from super alloys, okay? And 22% from Titanium alloys and about 13% from maraging steels and special steels contribute about 36% and balance is other miscellaneous grades.

items.statement: Scrap usage 30-50% depending on customer specification; Gaganyaan requires 100% virgin; plant reverts never sold
items.quote: Normally, okay, it depends on customer requirement. Some of the customers say like Gaganyaan and all for Department of Space, they want 100% virgin because of their requirement. But for normally, we use about 30% scrap. Approximately, I'm telling you ratio of virgin metal to scrap.

items.statement: In touch with GE, Safran, CFM, Pratt & Whitney; S-400 certification received, 4-5 inquiries being processed; expect better revenue visibility in H2 FY27
items.quote: we are in touch with the companies that you have named. And with respect to S -400 certification, yes, we got in the first half o f the year, the certificate. We are getting probably to have the numbers to tell you, I think maybe in the next half, I think we'll get better figures

items.statement: AMCA development orders for specialized titanium grades under execution; production orders expected after successful qualification
items.quote: AMCA, during developmental projects, we are executing some of the Titanium orders, okay? This is basically -- when it is in design stage, some of the new materials that they want to introduce into AMCA program, they approached us because we are working on Titanium alloys.

items.statement: Spring manufacturing plant operational; no direct Vande Bharat orders yet, smaller orders in hand, certification in progress
items.quote: See, we are -- now our spring manufacturing plant is operational, and we are getting the licenses and all. Directly, we don't have any order with Vande Bharat, okay? But we are having a couple of orders with smaller orders, and we are in the process of getting certification.

items.statement: ABHED bulletproof jacket technology from IIT Delhi DRDO; processed samples, participating in tenders, no orders yet
items.quote: We have taken a technology from IIT Delhi DRDO Center of Excellence, and it is called ABHED. It is one of the lightest weight jackets. And we have already processed some jackets, and we are anticipating orders. Currently, we don't have orders for ABHED as such.

items.statement: Private players entering space sector (Jindal, Raghu Vamsi); MIDHANI maintains niche in maraging steel plates, rings, superalloys, titanium for launch vehicles; ISRO qualification takes long time
items.quote: We supply -- MIDHANI supplies material for -- for example, if you look at the GSLV currently, what is there, or PSLV, we supply for all the 4 stages or all the 3 stages of PSLV or GSLV. So we make, for example, maraging steel plates we supply. And this is the only mill that is available where you can roll maraging steel, okay?

items.statement: Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2026 draft proposes 10% price evaluation preference and 15% minimum indigenous content; will benefit domestic suppliers like MIDHANI
items.quote: Yes, that all the pressure would be on the equipment now, whoever is buying, whether Defence or aero or all those systems. The government is giving pressure to them that you have to buy from the indigenous source only. So in that case, like MIDHANI companies and many will be benefited.

items.statement: NADCAP certification for heat treatment obtained, NDT certification in progress; enables direct OEM sourcing; initial export orders expected in tens of crores
items.quote: NADCAP is a certification for process, process control. So for heat treatment we have, and we are currently in the process of getting for non-destructive testing. The advantage is that original manufacturers can directly source looking at the NADCAP certification because the processes are very established and they have been certified.

items.statement: Scrap inventory reduced from INR 392 crore to INR 353 crore in H1 FY27; INR 39 crore scrap consumed; target to maintain optimal scrap levels
items.quote: In first 6 months, like if you see that around INR39 crores worth of scrap, we have -- I mean, we reduced the scrap opening quantities. That means the scrap usage has improved, okay? So that is the one thing. And scrap values also inventory side, scrap values have come down drastically, like we started in the year at INR 392 crores and now we are at INR 353 crores something.

items.statement: Capex funding within Board powers; no government funding required for INR 1,000 crore plan
items.quote: Within the Board power only, depending on the project cost, what we are envisaging is within the permission of Board only.

items.statement: Ministry target of INR 1,600 crore revenue for FY27; working towards it
items.quote: And Ministry has given us a target of INR 1,600 crores. We are working towards it.

items.statement: Highest-ever titanium alloy production in FY26; expect to surpass in FY27; superalloy production 5-6x higher than 5 years ago
items.quote: Even last year, we declared that highest-ever Titanium alloy we have done. Even this year also, we are going to surpass that. Superalloy also, if we compare more than 5 years back and presently what we are doing, more than 5, 6x more we are doing.

items.statement: Capacity constraint: current equipment limits revenue to ~INR 1,500 crore; INR 1,000 crore capex needed over 3 years to enable growth beyond INR 2,000 crore
items.quote: Otherwise, there is a stagnation -- whatever equipment available with us, beyond this INR1,500 crores, it is not possible actually. Once those INR1,000 crores is infused and all those equipments are available, then only we can be able to think of whether it is INR2,000 crores or beyond that.

items.statement: Order execution risk: booking orders beyond current capacity leads to delays and penalties; balancing orders with available capacity to avoid liquidated damages
items.quote: So presently, we are balancing with whatever available capacity and able to supply, not getting into any LD at all. This is the way we are planning and going ahead.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book at Rs 800 crore as of call date, up from Rs 625 crore at Sep 20
items.quote: as of September 20, it was 625 crores to which we have added, so that makes it close to Rs. 800 crores of our un-executed order book as of today when we are talking

items.statement: Bidding pipeline of Rs 2,000 crore with conservative 20-25% conversion implying Rs 400-500 crore incremental orders
items.quote: Even if we consider conservatively, let's say, a 20%-25% conversion, that will also add to about close to Rs. 400 to Rs. 500 crores of orders

items.statement: Targets 25-30% year-on-year growth over next 3 years
items.quote: we are definitely expecting for the next 3 years to give growth of 25%-30% year-on-year

items.statement: Rs 1,000 crore revenue target expected to be achieved in 3 years
items.quote: the target of 1,000 crores would be achieved in 3 years

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 13.18% vs 11.72% YoY, driven by higher specialized construction mix and project payment cycles
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved from 12.10% in Q1 to 13.18 %, that is also an improvement that definitely reflects a stronger sequential revenue and improved execution momentum during this quarter

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement attributed to higher specialized construction share and project fund deployment/payment cycles
items.quote: As I mentioned, it is a combination of both. Particularly, the project requiring the deployment of funds in terms of machinery and the payments cycle. Secondly, the increase in the specialized construction activities

items.statement: Revenue mix at 35% specialized construction, 65% maintenance; order book mix at 60% specialized construction, 40% major maintenance
items.quote: Till September, we are at 35% specialized construction and 65% maintenance orders in revnue. I was talking that as far as the order book is concerned, we are currently having the order book distribution of 60% from specialized construction and 40% from the major maintenance

items.statement: Specialized construction orders typically 18-24 month execution; major maintenance orders 6-12 months
items.quote: The MMR order book generally takes about 6 to 12 months. Construction orders generally are completed from 18 months to 24 months

items.statement: Entered marine infrastructure with two projects in Andaman & Nicobar Islands; evaluating port construction and jetty development
items.quote: we have recently got an entry into the marine infrastructure development. We have got two projects in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

items.statement: Also doing rehabilitation facility project in Andhra Pradesh to build varied experience for further bidding eligibility
items.quote: we have got an opportunity in Andhra Pradesh, we are doing rehabilitation of facility in Andhra Pradesh. So, by building varied experiences, we will be eligible for further bidding

items.statement: Merger to provide complete service array under one roof, better bidding capability, cost advantages, and higher eligibility for larger tenders
items.quote: post amalgamation, what will happen is, complete array of services under one roof, better Bidding capability because of the data easily available for us, we will be in a better place in terms of cost. Because of this larger size, our eligibility criteria will also increase for the larger size of the tenders

items.statement: Road maintenance allocation in India at ~15% vs 40% international benchmark; growing network (34 km/day) and mandatory 5-7 year maintenance cycles create structural demand
items.quote: The maintenance allocation in the Indian market remains below the benchmark illustrated by the developed countries. Almost, we can say that as against 40% internationally while in India it is about 15%

items.statement: Private institutional participation (InvITs, funds) now allowed during construction phase since May 2026, driving focus on lifecycle maintenance and quality
items.quote: Earlier, the funds or the PPP participation was only allowed post-construction. In May 2026, the construction phase to the MNCs and FDIs. Now, this will also definitely increase their participation, asking for better quality roads and well-maintained roads

items.statement: All major funds operating in India are clients; largest service provider in sector with pan-India presence across 12 states and 5,700+ maintenance projects
items.quote: We stand very high, the thing that every fund that is working in India is our client. And we are the one of the preferred vendors for doing all sorts of maintenances or specialized work because of our credentials and credibility

items.statement: Only listed pure-play highway O&M specialist offering full spectrum of services; competitors offer only 1-2 services; proven track record unmatched
items.quote: Only company providing the entire spectrum of services, whatever is needed in terms of operations and maintenance. That puts us definitely from all others. There is no other company who provides the complete spectrum

items.statement: IRC and MoRTH codes mandate complete overlay and maintenance every 5-7 years for road assets
items.quote: road being the wear and tear asset, it demands, as per the IRC and morth codes, it demands a complete overlay and maintenance every 5 to 7 years

items.statement: India highway construction rate at 34 km/day vs 20 km/day in 2014; network expanded from 1 lakh km to 1.5 lakh km over past decade
items.quote: India's road infrastructure has expanded significantly over the past decades, building 20 km then back in 2014, and wherein now today we are building almost 34 km per day

items.statement: Tenders quoted on PBT basis factoring capital employed, machinery, depreciation and interest; EBITDA varies but bottom line fixed at bid stage
items.quote: Being a service provider, the quotes are based on the depending upon the capital employed, machinery required, the approximately depreciation interest calculations according to that. So, that the EBITDAs would vary. But by and large, the tenders which are quoted are ensured that we have a fixed bottom line

items.statement: Construction quality variations in greenfield projects due to terrain/substrata; initial phases may have levelling issues; maintenance role begins post-construction
items.quote: initially, when the greenfield road alignments happen, considering the terrain, substrata, it often happens that in the initial phases, there could be variations. Though it is pertaining to the construction quality, which I have no reason to comment because that is where I am not involved

items.statement: Target crash barrier production of 2,500 tons/month this year; with Haryana unit adding 1,000 tons, total target 3,500-4,000 tons/month
items.quote: Our target this year is around about 2,500 tons. Once Haryana gets established, it will add another 1,000 tons. So, we are talking about anywhere between 3,500 to 4,000 tons we should be able to do in crash barrier if the installed capacity is utilized properly.

items.statement: Haryana subsidiary production expected to start in Q1 of next financial year (6-8 months)
items.quote: Hopefully, North region will also be very beneficial, and we are expecting that we should start its production by hopefully sometime in Quarter 1 of next year. So, in around about 6 months to 8 months, we should have some production to go on from North region as well.

items.statement: New product approvals (telecom, railway, Power Grid) expected soon; revenue contribution from new products visible by next financial year
items.quote: By, by next financial year, all of this shall start to see, to make its presence in terms of the numbers. This is what, again, it is future, so very difficult to pinpoint when it will start, but we are very confident that it should start very soon.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand across products; order books healthy every month; road projects ramping up before 2029 elections
items.quote: So far the demand has been more than it's ever been. So, every month it's been healthy order books booking, and we have been hitting healthy dispatches.

items.statement: Transmission line tower demand nationwide; current orders from Chhattisgarh and MP; Power Grid approval imminent
items.quote: Current orders that we have is Chhattisgarh and MP. Once power grid comes in, the orders will start coming from everywhere.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 81% pipe, 12% highway guardrails, 6-7% towers/poles/others
items.quote: The revenue bifurcation, till now we have around about 81% that comes from pipe and 12% comes from highway guardrails. Around about 6%-7% comes from tower, pole, and other products.

items.statement: Strong order flow for crash barriers from railway; NATRAX certification test due 28th; road projects to drive future demand
items.quote: A chunk of it, a lot of it is going in railway. Secondly, this also requires a certification of NATRAX. That NATRAX certification testing is due on 28th, so that if the NATRAX comes in, then anyone from NHI, the road contractors, will be willing to buy from us.

items.statement: Haryana subsidiary (Vibhor Infra) being set up for highway guardrails, poles, transmission towers; inspections due Dec/Jan
items.quote: We are putting a subsidiary unit in Hisar, Vibhor Infra, because we are constantly getting a lot of enquiries and a lot of demands from our current distributors of highway guardrails, crash barriers, that we should open up one unit as there is demand in North India as well for highway guardrails.

items.statement: Odisha galvanizing: Tank 1 at ~2,000 tons (full); Tank 2 (13m) capacity 2,000-4,000 tons awaiting Power Grid/telecom approvals
items.value: Tank 1: ~2,000 tons full; Tank 2: 2,000-4,000 tons potential
items.quote: When we started in Jharsuguda, we had one galvanizing unit. Now we have two. Both of them are operational. One is running at almost full capacity of around 2,000 tons. So, that galvanizing tank is complete. The second galvanizing tank, which is 13 meters long, that depending on the nature of orders we get, can have an installed capacity of anywhere between 2,000 tons to 4,000 tons.

items.statement: Maharashtra and Hyderabad galvanizing tanks running at full capacity; Odisha pipe at 1,500-2,000 tons vs higher installed capacity
items.quote: The rest of the places in Maharashtra is running at its full capacity in galvanizing. All galvanizing tanks are full. Hyderabad also, both the galvanizing tanks are full. They are running at maximum capacity.

items.statement: Overall galvanizing utilization ~40-50%; focus on utilizing existing capacity before adding more
items.quote: Yes, in terms of the galvanizing, I would say. Manav Mehta: In total? Vibhor Kaushik: In total, there is a lot. So, as I said, for the pipe, we are making around 1,500 to 2,000. Our installed capacity is

items.statement: Steel and zinc prices rising month-on-month due to geopolitical factors, manufacturer breakdowns, shipping costs; increases absorbed by market
items.quote: This year has been very good in terms of the steel, and the inventories have always month-on-month given us an advantage because the price of steel has always been going higher. May that be for the geopolitical reasons of the world. Some steel manufacturers have taken some breakdowns. So, there has been some scarcity of steel.

items.statement: Applied for RDSO railway products and telecom tower certification; telecom inspection done, certification expected soon; railway may take longer
items.quote: We have applied for railway. The RDSO has a requirement of certain products that we can make for them. Also, we have applied for telecom towers. The inspection is also done. The certification should come to us very soon.

items.statement: Jindal Steel agreement (4-5+ years) for pipe supply to West, South, Northeast; comfortable relationship; declined other brand offers
items.quote: So, I would say, there is a far more dependability, dependence that they have on us. So, this is a very safe point for us that there will always be supply and orders and execution of pipe from servicing a brand.

items.statement: Export shift from Middle East to Australia; domestic demand in Maharashtra increased offsetting export decline
items.quote: Now that export has become a little less due to the conflict, but at the same time, we have opened up some other markets which we were not catering to, such as Australia. We are exporting to Australia on regular basis now.

items.statement: Inventory increases driving EBITDA growth; managing inventory balanced with sales to protect future margins
items.quote: One of the main reasons is the increase in inventory. The inventory is always been increasing this year. So, that is one of the main reasons.

items.statement: Keeping inventory in check with sales; not over-leveraging or undercutting to withstand price declines
items.quote: We are keeping inventory in check with our sale. We are not over-leveraging it, we are not undercutting it. We are trying to keep a good balance of the inventory so that in the future, even when the prices go down, we do not see a margin of a massive hit on our EBITDA levels due to that.

items.statement: Power Grid approval documents submitted and accepted; approval expected very soon after one-year wait
items.quote: All the formalities are completed. The documents are also submitted to Power Grid, and it is accepted. We just had a word with Power Grid today, and it appears to us that the documents are complete, and we shall be getting Power Grid approval very, very soon.

items.statement: No significant impact from state/central elections on pipe, guardrail, or transmission products due to vast applications and fixed deadlines
items.quote: I don't think any of the state election or even central election will have too much of impact because deadlines are always set, already set for most of these products. So, they will be delivered like that.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict minimal impact on sales; raw material cost increases (steel, zinc, shipping) passed through to market
items.quote: For us, the geopolitical conflict has almost no impact in terms of our sale. In turn, in terms of our raw material, it could, which is why I think part of the reason why the prices of steels have stayed up because of this conflict.

items.statement: Management expects hotel GTV to grow triple digits over next 4 quarters and aims to be largest hotel OTA in budget to mid-market category in 4-5 years
items.quote: our target will be to continue growing in triple digits if we can, right? But if I were to give you longer-term guidance, like 4 to 5 years, we want to be the largest hotel OTA in the budget to mid-market hotel category on a room night basis.

items.statement: Hotel gross take rate expected to edge up over next 3-4 quarters but no specific guidance given for next year
items.quote: Over the next 3 to 4 quarters, you will see them edge up for sure. But I'm not giving any guidance right now on where we'll be next year. It's just that we will be higher. That is a certainty.

items.statement: Hotel segment expected to continue investing for 2-3 years before profitability becomes priority, within guardrails of mid-single-digit EBITDA at company level
items.quote: for 2 to 3 years, we expect to continue investing in getting to a scale where we become comfortable that profitability becomes more important. But in the short to medium term, I don't see why we would want to not keep doing what we are doing, which is done for growth. Within guardrails, we've always said that we do this within guardrails.

items.statement: Hotel investment expected to remain in INR 10-12 crore range per quarter over next couple of quarters, not formal guidance
items.quote: Think of a similar range as this quarter, which is between INR 10 crores and INR 12 crores. Having said that, if the growth- if what we are seeing on the ground becomes more enticing or less enticing, either way we could move one way or the other, yes.

items.statement: Flight demand remains challenging with festive demand a shade lower than expected and capacity not yet returned
items.quote: festive demand is a shade lower than what one would have expected this time of the year, right? We are not saying there's any major negative bump. I mean, it's actually -- obviously, the season always sees some bump up, but one would have seen a higher bump up if the sales were more amenable for the consumers.

items.statement: International flight GTV grew 59% year-on-year, more encouraging than domestic
items.quote: International travel has been more encouraging, with our international flight GTV growing 59% year-on-year.

items.statement: Hotel contribution margin improved from -55% of revenue a year ago to -15% this quarter with contribution loss of INR 1.2 crores
items.quote: Contribution margin improved from minus 55% of revenue a year ago to minus 15%, with a contribution loss of INR 1.2 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Hotel segment expected to become one of highest contribution margin businesses alongside buses when settled in a couple of years
items.quote: when it becomes a settled business, it will be one of the highest -- this and buses end up being the highest contribution margin businesses for us because of the nature of this business, because of fragmented supply.

items.statement: Hotel GTV grew 2.6x Y-o-Y to INR 111 crores with 4.7 lakh room nights, 3.9x Y-o-Y growth and 50% sequential growth
items.quote: In Q2, hotel GTV reached INR111 crores, up 39% sequentially and 2.6x year-on-year. Revenue grew more than six-fold year-on-year to INR8.1 crores, and our gross take rate exceeded 12% and became the highest in our business.

items.statement: Direct hotel supply increased to over 12,000 hotels across 1,100 towns from 10,000 last quarter
items.quote: Out of the 70,000 hotels in India that we sell, we are now tied up directly with over 12,000 hotels across about 1,100 towns, up from 10,000 hotels last quarter.

items.statement: Hotel investment of INR 11 crores this quarter including INR 1 crore above contribution margin and INR 10 crores below in people and technology
items.quote: we would have spent a further 10 crore in the people and technology line for hotels, taking the total investment in hotels to slightly north of INR 11 crores this quarter.

items.statement: AI system TARA handles 43 lakh queries, resolves 94% of chat queries and 82% of calls end-to-end without human intervention
items.quote: TARA handled 43 lakh queries before and after the booking and now resolves 94% of chat queries without human intervention and 82% of customer calls end-to-end.

items.statement: Launched Smart Lock agentic AI product for flights that scans fares 24/7 and locks cheapest flight matching preferences with full premium refund if no match
items.quote: Smart Lock is an agentic AI product that finds and locks the cheapest flights based on preferences. You can tell it your route, budget, and travel preferences. It scans the airfares 24/7 and locks the first flight that fits within that budget and matches your preferences. If nothing matches by the time scanning ends, you get your full premium back in ixigo money right away.

items.statement: 94% of hotel transactions involve travel to or from Tier 2 and 3 cities, and more than 9 out of 10 trips sold by train or bus
items.quote: 94% of our transactions involve travel to or from Tier 2 and 3 cities, and more than 9 out of 10 trips we sell out by train or bus.

items.statement: ConfirmTkt now highest-rated travel app globally among apps with 100M+ downloads at 4.9 on Google Play Store
items.quote: ConfirmTkt now has a 4.9 rating on the Google Play Store. And among the apps that have a scale of over 100 million downloads, it has become the highest-rated travel app in the world that operates at this kind of scale.

items.statement: Awaiting regulatory clarity before launching fully agentic booking flow demoed at GFF conference in Mumbai
items.quote: we demoed a fully agentic booking flow complete with payments at the recently concluded GFF conference in Mumbai, and we await regulatory clarity before launching the same.

items.statement: Total cash and equivalents including FDs and mutual funds net of borrowings at INR 1,831.71 crores; operating cash flow for year INR 76.44 crores vs INR 91.55 crores last year
items.quote: On the balance sheet, the total cash and cash equivalents, including fixed deposits and mutual funds and net of borrowings, is about INR1,831.71 crores. Operating cash flow of the year was INR76.44 crores against INR91.55 crores last year.

items.statement: Will pursue selective acquisitions with strategic fit, strong team, technology or distribution synergy and reasonable pricing; will inform markets when something crystallises
items.quote: we would pursue selective acquisitions where there is a strategic fit, strong team, technology or distribution synergy and reasonable pricing. Now, as we've said before, whenever something crystallises, we will inform the markets right away.

items.statement: Consolidated Brevistay in hotel segment this quarter; part of hotel growth is inorganic
items.quote: We began consolidating Brevistay this quarter. So part of this growth is inorganic.

items.statement: GTV grew 22% Y-o-Y to INR 5,304 crores; revenue from operations grew 13% to INR 321 crores; PAT all-time high aided by Freshbus stake sale
items.quote: In Q2 FY27, we delivered resilient growth on quarterly GTV as well of INR5,304 crores, up 22% Y-o-Y, and revenue from operations of INR321 crores, up 13% Y-o-Y. Our PAT was an all-time high, aided by our partial sale of stake in Freshbus.

items.statement: Flight GTV grew 37% Y-o-Y but revenue fell 8% to INR 82.66 crores and contribution margin fell 10% to INR 35.68 crores due to 30% fare increase and capacity constraints
items.quote: GTV grew 37% on the back of higher fares, but revenue fell 8% to INR 82.66 crores, and the c ontribution margin fell 10% to INR 35.68

items.statement: Bus GTV grew 32% to INR 752.65 crores; revenue grew 24% to INR 81.04 crores; contribution margin grew 27% to INR 43.14 crores
items.quote: GTV grew 32% to INR 752.65 crores. Revenue grew 24% to INR 81.04 crores, and contribution margin grew 27% to INR 43.14 crores.

items.statement: Train passenger segments grew 7% to 2.9 crores; revenue grew 16% to INR 149.14 crores; contribution margin grew 29% to INR 47.23 crores
items.quote: Passenger segments grew -- rose about 7% year-over-year to 2.9 crores. Revenue grew 16% to INR 149.14 crores, and contribution mar gin grew 29% to INR 47.23 crores

items.statement: Flight segment remains cautious near-term with capacity not returning as expected and 30% fare increase Y-o-Y impacting bookings
items.quote: Flight remains challenging in the near term as capacity has not returned as quickly as we had expected, and we are seeing the impact of oil prices reflected in the 30% increase in fares Y-o-Y on several routes.

items.statement: AI agent disruption risk acknowledged but management believes specialist vertical agents will outperform horizontal agents due to contextual data and trust
items.quote: We do not think that it will not happen again. I mean, I think there is a reasonable chance that in every vertical, you will have specialist AI agents who can do that vertical job far better than any horizontal AI agent will, right? That's our view.

items.statement: Reduced stake in Freshbus to focus on asset-light tech and distribution platform; Freshbus remains valued commercial partner
items.quote: Reducing our stake now reflects our focus on being an asset-light tech and distribution platform. And the lessons from that investment that we learned now help us to service bus opera tors with more understanding of the unique opportunities and challenges that EV -based operator. Freshbus remains a valued commercial partner

items.statement: Targeting FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and maintaining H1 FY27 PAT margin ratio
items.quote: For FY27, we are targeting revenue growth of approximately 30 to 35%, supported by sustained growth across technical, formulation and branded products.

items.statement: Expect FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and aim to maintain or improve H1 FY27 profitability ratios
items.quote: For the revenue part, we are expecting roughly a 30 to 35% increase from last year but it will depend upon the season, weather and we can't commit to exact figure. And the PAT will, we'll try to maintain the same ratio, whatever we achieved in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Formulation expansion capex of Rs 3.75 cr spent from IPO funds; backward integration technical plant estimated at Rs 30 cr with Rs 4-5 cr spent so far
items.quote: The capex done on Dahej expansion is around Rs. 3.75 crores. It is from IPO fund. And the backward integration the cost will be around Rs. 30 crores. And we have expended around Rs. 4 to 5 crores on backward integration
