items.statement: Orders in hand sufficient to meet committed targets despite El Nino impact on monsoon
items.quote: With the orders in hand, we expect to do whatever we have committed.

items.statement: Trading margin 10-12%, B2B formulation 21-22%, branded >25%, exports >28-29%; blended gross margin ~16%
items.quote: So, the margin on trading sales is close to 10-12% and while for the B2B formulation part, it is 21-22% and brand sales are more than 25%. If you are talking about export, it will be more than 28-29%. So, the total average gross margin is close to 16%.

items.statement: Manufacturing share of revenue increased to 45% in H1 FY27 from trading 55%; target 70-75% manufacturing share in coming years
items.quote: If you see during H1, our manufacturing has gone up to 45% and the trading of technical is 55%. Ultimately, our aim is to bring the manufacturing revenue split to around 70 to 75% in the coming few years.

items.statement: Branded sales Rs 6.61 cr in H1 FY27 matching full FY26; exports low at Rs 75 lakh due to geopolitics; formulation ~Rs 83-84 cr
items.quote: And the brand sale, it is Rs. 6.61 crores. So, we have achieved the brand sale last year, it was closely Rs. 6.5 crores, but within six months, we have achieved whatever we achieved in FY26. And the export sale is a little bit low due to geopolitical reasons; it is close to 75 lakhs. And the formulation part is around Rs. 83-84 crores.

items.statement: El Nino impacted monsoon across states but diverse product mix and client base enabled good H1 performance; expect good collections due to high commodity prices
items.quote: This year has been a very difficult year for the whole industry as a whole because of the El Nino. If you see, most of the states in India, whether it was Maharashtra or the southern states, were all impacted by the El Nino, and there was no rainfall during the major season. But for Mahamaya, because of a diverse product mix and clients, we were able to do good.

items.statement: Raw material cost ~82% of revenue; technical imports (80% from China) constitute 80-90% of formulation cost; partial pass-through possible as customers aware of China price movements
items.quote: See most of our raw material purchase is technical imports. And a technical import is the active ingredient (Al) in a formulation is almost worth 80 to 90% for a formulation product. The major component of a formulation product is the active ingredient. So hence whatever we are importing the products for which we have exclusive registration, for that we need the material to be imported. And yes, t

items.statement: ~80% of technical imports sourced from China; applied for forex hedging with banks; currently price in higher forex rates as buffer
items.quote: AlImost 80% of our imports is for technical from China. And currency exposure, we have already applied for hedging with banks. But normally when we calculate we keep at a higher price. So, we consider the volatility in the Forex market. But we have applied with banks for hedging purpose.

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~150-155 days; targeting reduction of ~10 days to 140-145 days over next few quarters via better collections and inventory rotation
items.quote: Roughly if you see any agrochemical industry there is a longer working capital cycle and we are having the same experience. So, we have around 150-155 days working capital cycle. But we are working on collection and the working on the rotating of inventories and we'll try to set in next few quarters we'll try to reduce it by around 10 days, that means 140-145 days.

items.statement: Average cost of debt 8-8.75% depending on bank
items.quote: Yeah, it depends on bank to bank and it is around 8% to 8.75%.

items.statement: IPO net proceeds Rs 61.96 cr; Rs 32.72 cr utilized by Sep-26; balance Rs 29.24 cr in FDs/monitoring account; utilization timeline extended to Mar-28
items.quote: The company received net proceeds of Rs. 61.96 crores last year in FY25. Out of this amount, Rs. 32.72 crores have been utilized on or before 30th September 2026, while the balance Rs. 29.24 crores remain parked in permitted fixed deposit and the monitoring account. As per the monitoring agency report, there has been no deviation from the objective for which the IPO proceeds were raised. The timel

items.statement: Technical sales 55%, formulation+branded+exports 45% of revenue in H1 FY27
items.quote: Yeah, so the bifurcation is: it is technical sales are around 55%. And the formulation, brand and export are 45%

items.statement: 33 products have indigenous manufacturing registration granted after CIB inspection; 19 more in pipeline; targeting off-patent molecules (2026-27) for technical plant
items.quote: Already we have registration for indigenous manufacture for 33 products and 19 products are in pipeline. And these 33 products the Central Insecticide Board officials have come and inspected the manufacturing process and the emissions and the solid waste everything, and the impurities present in that, and they have taken samples also to their own laboratory and analysed after which only all these

items.statement: Patent pipeline: 4 applied (awaiting approval), 4 in pipeline, 3 in progress; filing more as formulations demonstrate better efficacy
items.quote: Number of patents, formulations, we have applied for four. Pipeline is another four and we have not yet received any final approval. These are under scrutiny and in the meantime, we are developing more formulations and once the formulation showed better efficacy and better over the existing products, we will file the patents for those molecules also, those formulations also. Another three are in p

items.statement: Office building CWIP of Rs 4.5 cr completed and capitalized in early Sep-26; R&D and pilot plant to be capitalized by Mar-27
items.quote: Apart from the IPO related capital project, there was another project, the office building, that was Rs. 4.5 crores around the cost of the building. That has been completed and we have capitalized it. Okay, we are using it as secondary office. We are taking the you know, meetings, business meeting there, an important business meeting there, just it was capitalized in the first of week of September

items.statement: Key obstacles to revenue growth are seasonal factors (monsoon, pest attack, crop choice) not order book or capacity constraints
items.quote: No, obstacles, as | told before, agrochemical is a seasonal business, it depends on a variety of factors like monsoon, pest attack, and the farmers who choose to plant which crops. So, the major obstacle would of course be the rainfall and the distribution on rainfall and in each division and states of India. No, it is not limited to our order book or limited manufacturing capacity because we have

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs.165 Crores as on September 30, 2026, including a Rs.70 Crores one-time non-recurring order
items.quote: If you see our order book, our order book stands at Rs.165 Crores as on September 30, 2026.

items.statement: One-time order of Rs.84 Crores in hand, Rs.12 Crores executed in H1 FY27
items.quote: We have one time order in hands with us, which is of around Rs.84 Crores, and out of that, Rs.12 Crores has been executed in H1

items.statement: EBITDA margin target around 25%, with plus/minus variance due to one-time orders
items.quote: 25-26% EBITDA margin around 25%. There will be plus or minus because there are more one-time order in talks, so there is a chance of it going to happen.

items.statement: New building construction to be completed by June-July 2027, shifting to complete by March 2028
items.quote: Our target is till March, but I think we will be able to complete by June-July and after that we will start shifting to our new unit.

items.statement: Capacity to increase 2-3x from current 1200 metric ton to ~3100 MTPA post expansion
items.quote: If your capacity is around 1200 metric ton, and the building we are scaling up, the new building will have 3x capacity.

items.statement: Revenue potential of Rs.400-450 Crores at full 3100 MTPA capacity utilization
items.quote: There is Rs.400-450 Crores revenue capacity approximately but it cannot be so blunt and the capacity will keep increasing.

items.statement: WONDRA B2C cleaning products revenue grew from Rs.1.7 Crores to Rs.9.1 Crores in H1 FY27, targeting break-even this year
items.quote: For WONDRA, which we have started last year, 2025-26, so that has grown significantly because in H1 the revenue was Rs.1.7 Crores now it is Rs.9.1 Crores.

items.statement: WONDRA EBITDA margin expected around 15% at scale, currently negative due to overhead absorption
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin will be around 15% . But this is basically a volume business. So, we are building capacity.

items.statement: Steel procurement via mother blocks at fixed prices, mitigating commodity volatility
items.quote: We tell the company that this block is for us and in a particular year, we will absorb everything from you. Otherwise, we will give you money. So, in this way, our steel block becomes ours.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute ~70% revenue, largest ~20%; management confident of retention due to specialized capabilities
items.quote: We have India's top 5-6 customers in pipe-fitting. We take part in all the exhibitions including domestic and overseas. So, new people come, but our existing customer has so much volume.

items.statement: Automotive order visibility till 2030 with launch schedules from major OEMs including Maruti, Mahindra, Tata, TVS, Royal Enfield
items.quote: All the OEs have given us the launch periods, which all vehicles will get launched when and how much tooling is available in those particular models and all. Those things are already given to us so that we are ready to cater to such orders.

items.statement: Among top 3 in pipe fitting moulds in India; integrated hot runner + mould capability creates competitive moat
items.quote: As you see in pipe fitting, we are among top three in India. If anyone wants to venture in the pipe fitting business, they have to come to Om Galaxy.

items.statement: IPO proceeds marginally deployed as of Sept 30, 2026 (12 days post-listing); balance to be deployed by June-July 2027
items.quote: As of 30th September, it has been deployed marginally. Our listing was done on 18th September, so in these 12 days billing of the building construction which was done has been deployed and the loan repayment was done on the same date.

items.statement: Will need debt for working capital post capex; machine loans already initiated
items.quote: No, no, sir. We will definitely need debt for the working capital.

items.statement: Auditor qualification on MSME interest provisioning; management says terms vary by vendor, no interest claims received
items.quote: So, the terms of every supplier are different. The approval processes are different. So, with respect to every term, every approval process, stage of completion, trial period, so this manufacturing has a long period for manufacturing that product.

items.statement: Inventory/WIP builds in H1 due to order book execution weighted to H2; stock levels correlate with order book progress
items.quote: In H1, we see a lot of stocks. Because in H2, there are a majority of executions.

items.statement: Order execution cycle 4-6 months; price fixed at order acceptance for that period
items.quote: Our cycle time is 4 to 6 months. So, our price is fixed for that particular period.

items.statement: Hot runner maintenance recurring revenue 10-15% of system cost annually
items.quote: If you have 15 moulds, you get 15 system if there is any damage, you get a spares business, in maintenance 10-15% cost continues.

items.statement: Current capacity fully utilized, outsourcing some work; new plant to enable 25-30 ton moulds vs current 12-15 ton
items.quote: As we said earlier, we are over 100% capacity. So, we are outsourcing some work outside currently.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target Rs.200-240 Crores excluding WONDRA (order book execution), conservative with 10-15% variance
items.quote: Your understanding is correct and plus we have not included WONDRA turnover in order book because it is recurring business.

items.statement: Pipe fitting demand cyclical but diversified across PVC, CPVC, HDPE, OPVC transitions; 2000-2500 SKUs provide breadth
items.quote: there was PVC, then CPVC then HDPE, now there is OPVC. There are many new types of fittings over a period of time. There are many new types of fittings coming in, over a period of time, now there is OPVC, so as new things come in, the order of fittings is increasing

items.statement: OMG Auto: 75% Om Galaxy, 25% Nandakumar (auto specialist); Infuse HRS: 73% Om Galaxy, 25% Jawahar, 2% Nandakumar (specialists)

items.quote: Within that 9%, about 5% was private labeling. And the balance would be other channels, which are quick commerce, exports, and food ingredients.

items.quote: We are working on a range in which every pack size would be under 50 calories and there would be multiple products. The entire idea would be you can have one pack, and it will be under 50 calories so it can be guilt free for you.

items.statement: Using structural shrinkflation (grammage reduction, packaging optimization) annually to protect margins at sub-Rs.10 price points amid rising commodity costs

items.statement: Super-stockist count stable in H1; regional distribution centers planned for West, Central, South to reduce lead times and unlock capacity-constrained demand
items.quote: Sir, in this half year itself, the number of super-stockists has been relatively stable.

items.statement: Trade receivables down from Rs.48.6 Cr (Mar-26) to Rs.37.8 Cr (Sep-26); inventory stable; trade payables up from Rs.35.4 Cr to Rs.37.1 Cr; working capital cycle improved ~20+ days
items.quote: We have already been able to bring down the working capital cycle in this current period by about 20 plus days. items.statement: Private label offers attractive working capital cycle, potentially negative cash conversion cycle; no corporate marketing/sales overheads
items.quote: Although the cash conversion cycle on this private label play is extremely good. So, what ends up being the case that in certain private labeling plays, you could even be on a negative cash conversion cycle.

items.statement: Sonipat expansion funded by debt and internal accruals; debt expected to rise slightly by FY2027 end then decline; Rs.22 Cr IPO debt repayment in process, completion in 2-4 weeks

items.statement: Active management by Kapil and Pavil Garg; strong N-1 team (GM plant ops, GM sales); active recruitment ongoing, no reduction in promoter involvement planned

items.statement: Seasonality typically 40/60 or 45/55 H1/H2; FY2027 skewed more to H2 due to Sonipat activation

items.statement: Customer audit/onboarding funnel for developed-market exports 1-6 months; plant visits can start in 1-1.5 months as products already running at Sonipat

items.statement: MNCs focus on core global portfolios; Shellz targets gap with innovative products at India-specific price points (sub-Rs.10), similar to successful domestic players in Korea, Malaysia, Thailand
items.quote: The MNCs in this sector have a very speciﬁc policy globally. And that policy is to have a core portfolio and to focus on deep penetration of that core portfolio. And that same strategy has allowed for there to be several extremely large domestic players in the same categories that we operate in, in multiple different geographies

items.statement: GST reduction on confectionery from September 2025 benefited industry; part reinvested in product improvements, balance drove margin expansion
items.quote: The major driver was reduction in GST in confectionery from September 2025, a change that beneﬁted the industry as a whole. We reinvested part of this beneﬁt in our consumers through improved products and the balance contributed signiﬁcantly to our margin expansion

items.statement: Objective: sustainable positive operating cash flow via better working capital management, disciplined inventory planning, improved collections; balance capex, working capital, operating cash generation
items.quote: Our objective is to establish a sustainable pattern of positive operating cash ﬂow through better working capital management, disciplined inventory planning and improved collections. items.quote: EMOSS Netherlands reported a revenue of INR10.8 crores in Q2, and as noted last quarter, the EV market in Europe remains difficult, and we are managing the business very cautiously.

items.statement: Cancer hospital at 65 beds; no immediate expansion planned until occupancy improves
items.quote: At present, we are not looking for, increasing number of beds, rather, we are looking for increasing the occupancy rate and the business.

items.quote: IPD patient volume grew by 13% year on year, while OPD volume increased by 25%.

items.quote: Our EBITDA margin improved significantly to 22.4% compared to 19.8% in Q2 of FY26, making our highest ever quarterly EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Management believes 22.5% EBITDA margin is sustainable

items.quote: Once this clarification is received from there this daycare treatment of this daycare patients, if settles down and this daycare is considered as daycare and it is not considered in the RPOB, then this RPOB should be around INR35,000 approximately.

items.statement: Targeting 80-90% growth in both revenue and profitability for FY27

items.quote: Idea is, in next three- four years of time, how IP revenue can contribute at least 25 to 30%, and we are poised towards it.

items.statement: Two agentic AI implementation deals won - one from UK, one from US, in implementation stage
items.quote: We have already started doing agentic AI implementation. So some two customers, one from UK, one from US, we have been. We have already got the deal, and the deal is in implementation stage.

items.statement: Muralidharan joined as Chief AI Officer from TCS where he was CTO for Cloud and CX
items.quote: Murali joins from TCS, where he was CTO at TCS. So with Murali, we are taking this agentic AI journey to next level not only on software side but also on hardware and infrastructure side.

items.statement: Board approved opening office in Dubai to cater Middle East market; partners requesting expansion there
items.quote: Already we got a board approval of opening office in Dubai to cater Dubai market. The good part is, both Dubai, US, and all these regions, our existing partners are saying that come and expand there.

items.statement: Expanding Cloud ERP partnerships beyond Acumatica to include Odoo and Microsoft Dynamics
items.quote: We partnered with last time, we talked about Acumatica as one of that, and then we are now expanding that to adding Odoo and Microsoft Dynamics and other players as well.

items.statement: CX as a service growing at 8.4% CAGR, AI as a service at 35% CAGR, Cloud ERP also growing
items.quote: Now, the trend is that both CX as a service and AI as a service is growing at a CAGR of 8.4%, 35%, and also the Cloud ERP.

items.statement: 97% customer retention across 150+ clients; own customer relationships end-to-end
items.quote: See, first of all is, we own the customer. So when I talked about 150 plus client, 97% customer retention. We own the customer, we own the relationship.

items.statement: Participated in NiCE Cognigy agentic AI platform launch in India; Murali was key speaker
items.quote: We also were a part of the launch of Cognigy agentic AI platform which was launched by NiCE India, and I was part of the speaker there and the key speaker in one of the in the opening event.

items.statement: NiCE World events in Mumbai and Delhi attracted 450+ attendees; booth saw strong interaction
items.quote: With more than 450 attendees. With more than 450 customers joined us through these events alone. Honestly, telling you that, we're really amazed how interested customers were.

items.statement: International deals driving major revenue and profitability growth; infrastructure-as-a-service expected to contribute significantly in coming quarters
items.quote: The growth in revenue as well as on profitability side is credited majorly from international deals. And as we expand more, there is a huge potential which is expected coming from international geographies.

items.statement: Full-stack observability offering including SOC, NOC monitoring and management
items.quote: Apart from that, we also have our full stack observability, where we do monitoring, management of SOC, NOC, and other areas to keep up the product, the third part of it.

items.statement: Upgrading legacy applications like SAP onto private infrastructure on CAPEX-OPEX model
items.quote: Finally we are also, last but not least, we are also investing in upgrading applications, transforming legacy applications like SAP onto the private infrastructure on a CAPEX OPEX model.

items.statement: Gopinath Bailur elevated to Chief Operating Officer with extensive product development and delivery experience
items.quote: Elevation of Gopi as a Chief Operating officer. The idea was very clear that Gopi got a extensive experience in product development as well as in delivery, and now with customer relation also.

items.statement: Traditionally Q4 is biggest quarter; expecting to achieve 80-90% FY27 growth targets
items.quote: And traditionally Q4 has been the biggest quarter for us because of all the valid reason, industry reason and all. So we expect that the same way we will be able to turn around in next two quarters.

items.statement: ERP acquisition due diligence not satisfactory; decided not to proceed with that target
items.quote: The due diligence is not up to mark for that, and we are being very cautious about this, and I'm sharing this very transparently. So we are not going ahead with that.

items.statement: Targets 80-90% year-on-year growth for both top line and PAT in FY27
items.quote: So Devan, like I mentioned, we have bigger plans, so our idea is to look at 80-90% of growth year on year.

items.statement: Expects 35-40% of revenue from infrastructure as a service in three years
items.quote: In three years' time we expect that around 35-40% revenue should come from infrastructure as a service.

items.statement: Targets 35-40% revenue contribution from AI infrastructure in current year
items.quote: For this year, our own target is that close to around. Again, around 35-40% should be contributed from infrastructure, not infrastructure as a service.

items.statement: Aims to expand customer base from 150 to 500-600 in three to four years
items.quote: We want to expand our customer base to 500 from 150 in three to four years' time, so there are three, four new developments which has happened towards that.

items.statement: Targets 60% of revenue from international markets by FY30
items.quote: Just to summarize, and we are expecting close to 60% of revenue by FY30 coming from there.

items.statement: Order book at 680 Cr with 410 Cr remaining for execution over next three years
items.quote: Out of current order book, we have executed 280 Cr worth of order, 410 Cr still remains to be executed. This 410 is there for next three years.

items.quote: We expect this order book to increase significantly. Now, the second part to your answer is, all this order are renewable, and while we are saying this, we are getting incremental order from these customers.

items.statement: Sees no moderation in enterprise AI spending; existing customers giving incremental deals
items.quote: No, we are in a different space. That is what I would like to see. The spending which everyone is talking about on the tokens or with the hyperscalers, that is a very big play. We are in a very different space.

items.statement: Domestic gross margin 20-22%; international margins significantly higher
items.quote: For domestic, we get gross margin of 20 to 22%. Internationally it is much higher than this. Let me not comment on this, because this is something which we are staging.

items.statement: Initial investment in infrastructure business may pressure margins for first year but will become very profitable over time
items.quote: See, initial one year there will be a substantial investment also, Nikhil, expenses also which will be there, but over a period of time this will become very profitable.

items.statement: Plans to invest close to 2 million in ExaFone product development
items.quote: It is close to 2 million what we're eyeing to invest in this product.

items.statement: Launching ExaFone with NiCE and Mitel partnerships for on-prem agentic AI solution
items.quote: We are in advanced level talks with NiCE and Mitel, especially with NiCE, to make them a part of their go to market.

items.statement: Building integrated offering combining AI as a service, infrastructure as a service, and consulting
items.quote: We are not going and doing five different things, rather integrated offering. So suppose our customer is asking for infrastructure also, they are training their model, that they want GPUs, etc., so we are giving them, and we are also giving our consulting.

items.statement: Added iQor as significant US BPO customer; two more large customers with MSA signed
items.quote: One is this iQor, which I mentioned, and iQor was a significant contribution to this addition. And then there is another deal which is almost done. There are two more large customers which is done, but the contract signing is in place.

items.statement: UK customer Diligenta gave incremental consulting orders driving PAT growth
items.quote: One customer is this UK customer, which is our existing customer. The second customer is a new customer, which is from US. Now, you understand that these two customers, why the first customer, the UK customer, Diligenta, why we got this incremental value is that we are doing a lot of consulting on top of what we have already sold.

items.statement: Has 120 Cr+ recurring contract with a UK client expecting incremental additions
items.quote: So we have 120 Cr plus contract recurring contractor for. With this, we are expecting some incremental, huge incremental addition in this quarter and next quarter.

items.statement: International revenue has much higher margins than domestic 20-22%
items.quote: International revenue has more margins, this is what we have experienced last two, three deals. For domestic, we get gross margin of 20 to 22%. Internationally it is much higher than this.

items.statement: Team camping in US and Singapore for large deal closures; leadership with international experience onboard
items.quote: Team is camping there in US and Singapore and other geographies. So yes, that is how it is. So just to answer you, in short, it takes some time.

items.statement: Plans to incorporate wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai for Middle East expansion
items.quote: With this ERP acquisition, we wanted to. One thing which we're gaining was this Middle East geography, which eventually as of now is not happening. While I said that there are three more companies which we are evaluating. So we now plan to organically expand to Middle East region.

items.statement: CX industry expected to grow at 15-18% CAGR from $15B to $30B by 2030
items.quote: I shared earlier also that this industry is expected to grow at a CAGR of 15 to 18%, and currently this is around 15 billion, which will be around 30 billion by 2030.

items.statement: Strengthened leadership with Murali, Paresh, Kailash, Abhijit for international GTM and delivery
items.quote: Having more presence there is helping. Middle East, like I mentioned, through inorganic acquisition we wanted to have a presence there. But for some reason, if that is not happening, we are growing there organically. Infrastructure as a practice, we were doing in bits and pieces, but under Murali's leadership, and with Paresh also, Kailash also being there, we see a bigger play.

items.statement: Evaluated acquisition but Big Four report was not favorable; focusing on organic growth
items.quote: I mentioned in my previous call that we wanted to acquire a company. We had one of the top Big Four consulting firm, and somehow the report was not that good. So I will be very transparent in this forum that we don't want to make mistakes.

items.statement: International deals take 6-8 months closure time causing quarterly order book volatility
items.quote: These international deals, especially these deals, takes some time. It is typically six to eight months of closure time. So what I can assure you is, this quarter could be a game changer quarter.

items.statement: NiCE partnership revenue share model: Exato gets 200-300k on a $5M deal
items.quote: Suppose, a 5 million dollar deal, our part would be 200, 300k. So our entire part will be given to us, they will charge certain margin on it.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: We remain committed to the objective we shared on our last call. We're delivering around 15% to 20% growth year in year '27.

items.statement: PAT target of INR 34-35 crores for FY27
items.quote: PAT margin is expecting around INR35 crores this year. Last year, it was INR26 crores. The PAT margin will be around INR34 crores to INR35 crores this year.

items.statement: Vision 2.0 targets revenue of INR 1,250 crores and PAT around INR 120 crores by 2030
items.quote: Looking ahead, our Vision 2.0 roadmap targets revenue of INR1,250 crores, and PAT is around INR120 crores by 2030.

items.statement: Three new long-term contracts signed: liquor logistics (INR 24 cr FY27, scaling to INR 100 cr), 5-year cement contract in North East with 30 electric trucks, 5-year beverage contract worth INR 60 cr over tenure
items.quote: Together, these 3 wins take us into the new categories, deepen our position in industrial logistics and add long-term contracted revenue to the business, which is exactly the kind of growth we want to build.

items.statement: Haldiram's and Dalmia fleets started in last month of Q2; full benefit from Q3 onwards along with new liquor and beverage contracts
items.quote: Haldiram's and Dalmia fleets started running only during the last month of Q2. So, the full benefit, along with the new liquor and beverage contracts will come in Q3 and onwards.

items.statement: Haldiram's and beverage contracts combined expected to generate INR 28-32 crores annual revenue with better margins due to alternative fuel
items.quote: Yes, yes, total revenue from these 2 contracts will be around INR30 crores -- INR28 crores to INR32 crores, approximately. And these are better margins because one contract is 100% electric and one is on CNG.

items.statement: Plan to add 200-250 electric vehicles by March 2027 using mix of owned and leased models
items.quote: We are trying to add around 200, 250 vehicles of electric in this year, March '27. And this will give us good revenue as well as the profit also. And we are using the mix, owned and leased, both model we are working.

items.statement: Charging station cost ~INR 1 crore each; need 4-5 chargers at origin and destination for Dalmia electric fleet
items.quote: We have put the charging stations, where the cost is around INR1 crore per charging station. We need to put around 4 to 5 chargers at origin location and 4 to 5 chargers in the destination location.

items.statement: Standalone PBT margin improved 220 bps to 6.7%, PAT margin improved 120 bps to 4.7% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Standalone PBT margin improved to 6.7% from 4.5%, an expansion of 220 basis points. PAT margin increased to 4.7% from 3.5%, an improvement of 120 basis points.

items.statement: Target 10% PAT margin by 2030 as operating leverage improves and vehicle EMIs get paid off
items.quote: So next 4 years, we will reach INR1,250 crores. And today, we are at margins of around 4% to 5%. But we get the leverage when we have increased the business, so our expenses will not increase in the same ratio. So that is why we have mentioned about the 10% margin.

items.statement: 75-80% of business has fuel surcharge mechanism; diesel cost pass-through with 10-15 day lag; 40-45% of cost is diesel passed to customer
items.quote: So around 75% to 80% business, which is corporate clients, is already under the mechanism of decrease or increase in the prices. Our prices are increased according to a formula. Say, around 40% to 45% is the cost of the diesel, where the customer is passing on the same to us.

items.statement: Electric trucks use solar power at INR 4-5/unit vs industrial grid at INR 8-10/unit, improving margins vs diesel
items.quote: And the electricity, which we are using is solar electric. So, for example, if the industrial electricity cost is around INR8 to INR10 per unit, whereas the solar cost is around INR4 to INR5 per unit. So, we are taking the electricity from the solar system. So, our margins are better than diesel in these movements.

items.statement: Green logistics fleet includes LNG (launched Apr 2024), 55-ton electric trucks (first in India), CNG; running EVs for Tata Steel, Nestlé, LNG for ITC
items.quote: We launched our first LNG fleet in April '24. Soon later, we became the first company in India to deploy a fleet of 55-ton electric trucks. Starting with Tata Steel, we are now running electric vehicles for Nestlé and LNG for ITC.

items.statement: Liquid logistics with 96 ISO tanks moving bulk liquids mostly by rail; 400+ reefer vehicles for dairy, food, pharma; warehousing on WMS; operating on Dedicated Freight Corridor
items.quote: We move bulk liquid in our own ISO tanks, mostly by rail, which is safer, cheaper and cleaner over the long distances. Rail, cold chain and warehousing complete our offering. We already operate on Dedicated Freight Corridor. Our 400-plus reefer vehicles service dairy, food and pharma sectors, and our warehouses run on our warehouse management system.

items.statement: Entered liquor logistics with 2 signed clients, 2 in pipeline, targeting 4 clients in first year; 6-7 total liquor companies approached for raw material and finished goods movement
items.quote: Almost 2 we have signed and 2 are under pipeline. Another 2 will come up after April '27, we will go, because we want to serve 4 customers in the first year, which will give us revenue of around INR25 crores.

items.statement: Cement and steel companies under carbon reduction pressure driving long-term EV contracts; one major cement client signed, more in discussions
items.quote: The EV vehicles in the heavy-duty is making a mark because these 2 industries, cement and steel, they have carbon reduction targets to the government. So they are under tremendous pressure to achieve those numbers. So they are putting long-term contracts with us.

items.statement: Fleet of ~1,100 vehicles; ~900-1,000 vehicles to be EMI-free in next 4 years reducing interest burden
items.quote: As of now, we have a fleet of 1,100 vehicles approximately. So, out of that, next 4 years, around 900 vehicles or 1,000 vehicles will be without EMI. So, the interest burden will reduce drastically on us.

items.statement: Network: 3,000+ owned/hired vehicles, 70 branches, 7.5 lakh sq ft warehousing across India
items.quote: Today, AVG runs more than 3,000 owned and hired vehicles from 70 branches with about 7.5 lakh square feet warehousing across India.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds (INR 52 cr) used mainly for working capital (fuel, driver advances) and 25% general corporate purposes
items.quote: And majorly, the contribution we have taken through the rights issue it has been for the fuel in the working capital. So the major part is for working capital, and 25% of the proceeds is towards the general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Borrowings increased by INR 30-40 cr (not INR 189 cr); debt-to-equity comfortable vs peers; capex funded via debt (5-7 yr tenure) and equity mix
items.quote: Borrowings have not increased by INR189 crores. I think you have some wrong figure. It has increased by INR30 crores, INR40 crores only. And majorly, the contribution we have taken through the rights issue it has been for the fuel in the working capital.

items.statement: Received INR 52 crores through warrants and equity issuance in H1 FY27
items.quote: the company received around INR52 crores through warrants and equity issuance during H1

items.statement: Open to 2-3 acquisitions but valuations unreasonable (15x EBITDA/turnover); prefer organic build
items.quote: We are looking for, 2, 3 acquisitions, but people are asking for some unreasonable value. So, like for example, they ask for a valuation based on EBITDA, a multiple of turnover, or 15 times of that. With that much effort, we could build the same within our own business, so there is not much value in it.

items.statement: Electric truck range 150-160 km per charge; 50 trips/month per vehicle for Dalmia cement contract in Assam
items.quote: because our vehicle can run around 150 to 160 kilometers at one go after one charging. And charger cost is, say, around INR1 crores, but the profitability is better than diesel because we can make more trips in this vehicle.

items.statement: Khorda facility in Odisha targeted for next financial year pending customer factory establishment in the industrial area
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting it in the next financial year, because there are some developments going on in that industrial area. So once the customers, which we are targeting to cater, so once they establish their factories or the warehouses there, so definitely we will be able to create that facility for further utilization and generating more revenue from there.

items.statement: H2 traditionally stronger season; Q3-Q4 expected to deliver 15-20% growth compensating for H1 single-digit growth
items.quote: Actually, if you see the previous history, our quarter 1 and quarter 2 is always a little less compared to the quarter 3 and 4. So in quarter 3 or 4, there will be definitely growth of 15% to 20%. And we will try to compensate the previous quarter also.

items.statement: 600+ employees keeping network running round the clock
items.quote: The results were possible because of the hard work and commitment of our 600-plus employees who keep our network running round the clock.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 34-36% for FY27 and EBITDA margin of 25-26%
items.quote: We are anticipating a strong revenue growth for the whole year, as well as well aligned with our goal that we will be delivering a growth in the range of... above... definitely above 34-35%, right? That is our revenue growth goal, as well as well aligned with our EBITDA margin of 25% - 26%

items.statement: FY28 revenue growth guidance of 35-40%
items.quote: We are committed, based on the... this thing, every year we should... we are looking for a growth in the range of 35-40%.

items.statement: Long-term target of 4x revenue growth to reach Rs 500 crore by FY30 from FY26 base of Rs 125 crore
items.quote: By the end of the financial DATE: 24/11/2026 TIME: 4:00 PM (IST) year 29-30, we are expecting a 4x growth to reach and like, in last year revenue, it was 125 crores. Aligned with that, we're looking for a 4x

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin lower at 22% vs 26% in H2 FY26 due to annual salary hikes, rent, AMC/CMC and new lab costs front-loaded in Q1
items.quote: In H1 of 26-27 With the growth of H1, revenue, the profitability growth is not aligned, it is less, mainly due to one reason. As you all know, in India, the financial year start from the month of April. So, all the annual increment and, also, a lot of... Fixed expenses, like rent. And, as well as AMC, CMC, a lot of expenses happens in the April, May, June quarter.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin expected at 25-26% currently; post Rs 300-400 crore revenue margin may reach ~30% and PAT 18-20%
items.quote: After reaching up to a certain level, beyond 300 to 400 crores, normally the margin reaches to close to 30%, and PAT reaches from 18% to 20%. However, once we reach beyond 300 to 350 crores level of revenue. Otherwise, in the current scenario, we are anticipating we will continue with a margin of 25% to 26% level.

items.statement: Invested Rs 35 crore in H1 FY27 per plan including USFDA lab acquisition and Panchkula lab upgrade
items.quote: From the CAPEX part. As you... you all must have seen, we have invested close to 35 crores, and the entire 35 crores is well aligned with our plan of 2-25-26, when we had put the plan in the last financial year, review meeting.

items.statement: Plan to establish automobile lab in South India (Chennai) to serve OEMs and reduce logistics cost
items.quote: Since in automobile, the sample size are big, it is very difficult to do the transport from one part of India to another part of India, which is having a huge logistic cost. And also, it impacts the service level for that we are trying to have our presence in south part of India.

items.statement: Annuity revenue of Rs 2.5-3 crore per month; order pipeline of 2.5-3 months revenue visibility
items.quote: If we are doing a revenue of 15 to 16 crores per month now, our annuity business is close to 2.5 to 3 crores per month. Little bit more than 3 crores, as well as a pipeline of around 2.5-3 months.

items.statement: Total addressable market (TAM) of $3-3.2 billion out of $9 billion India TIC market, growing 7-10% YoY
items.quote: Though the total market is $9 billion in India, the addressable market where we are now, it's 3 - 3.2 billion, and growing at a rate of 7-10% year-over-year.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue mix: 82% testing & R&D (core), 18% CAPEX-light/OPEX model (inspection, audit, certification, lab process outsourcing)
items.quote: In the business fleet, 82% of the revenue is coming from the testing and R&D, which is our core business, and 18% of the revenue is coming from the CAPEX Lite business, or majorly OPEX model business.

items.statement: Automobile and food sectors combined contribute ~70% of revenue
items.quote: As automobile, it's one of our key business sector contributing a good amount of our revenue, if I say both automobile and food, combinedly contributing close to 70% of our revenue.

items.statement: Top 50-60 customers contribute ~55% revenue; Tata group is largest customer across multiple sectors
items.quote: Our top 50-60 customers are contributing Close to 55% revenue, which are more or less stable and the... First, our number one customer for us is Tata.

items.statement: Competes with top 10 MNCs holding 40-50% market share; differentiates on technical capability, accreditation parity, service level and India network
items.quote: If you think about the service that we are providing, it is completely depending on the technical capabilities know how and service level. Right? And the... since a lot of business is regulatory driven, then in that case, if you have the accreditation of USFDA, whether it is SGS or Qualitek Lab, it doesn't make any difference.

items.statement: Preferential issue of ~Rs 40+ crore awaiting BSE approval; funds expected first/second week of December for acquisition (cybersecurity) and South India auto lab
items.quote: It is in the process of BSE approval. So, the money, we are anticipating in the, first or second week of December. So, that utilization of the funds, we are looking for some expansion. And, we have identified one, acquisition target also which is into new area, that is cybersecurity.

items.statement: Built in-house R&D and training centre to address skilled manpower retention and accreditation pace
items.quote: We are well aligned with that. I don't consider this as a, like, threat. Rather, it is an opportunity, we converted this as an opportunity by establishing our own R&D and training centre in-house, where we continue to support and training to the people as part of our leadership and people development plan.

items.statement: Key execution risks: accreditation timelines, skilled manpower, lab utilization, government receivable delays (3-6 months)
items.quote: Sometimes working capital is a challenge, keeping in mind, the... some part of our business is coming from government, which is close to 20%. Sometimes the government payment, it takes time. But money, it comes.

items.statement: EMI/EMC equipment import cost rose sharply due to USD/INR move; outsourcing used until in-house capex viable
items.quote: Because due to the USD increase substantially. Right? And almost all the EMI/EMC equipment are imported. Right? So, just in, like, a short span, the cost has gone up substantially. Right? Which is impacting the capital, this thing.

items.statement: Implementing AI in LIMS to support global inspection order management
items.quote: We are working very close to very closely to implement AI in that module to support in the global inspection business. It is not going to be limited to only domestic business, so the AI module will work to face the order from the international market.

items.statement: Management expects revenue of around INR220 crores for FY27 and reiterates guidance of 25-30% CAGR over next 3 years based on current business
items.quote: We are seeing close to about INR220 crores, for '27. We are seeing close to about INR220 crores for '27.

items.statement: Management confirms guidance is on track and based on status quo, not dependent on NADCAP certification
items.quote: Yes, yes, we are still on track with the guidance. Yes.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR101.64 crores as of September 30, 2026
items.quote: Our order book stood at INR101.64 crores as of September 30th, 2026, which gives us a good visibility for the coming months.

items.statement: Management expects open orders of INR90-120 crores by April 1, 2027
items.quote: So we see that by April, we should be having similar set of open orders by March end. I mean, as on April 1st, we should be having close to about anywhere between INR90 crores to INR110 crores, INR120 crores worth orders, open orders.

items.statement: CERN tenders worth close to INR100 crores coming up in January
items.quote: But apart from that, there are other contracts for which we bid, and TIFR has been, supportive to us. I mean, whenever they go meet the scientists, they, they also, if you have any requirement, they, they communicate with the scientists there and then, help us out in getting to be qualified and getting to be on the bidders list. They are still supportive. It is not bypassing them in any which ways

items.statement: IPO-funded capex installation and commissioning expected to complete by end of calendar year 2026
items.quote: The funds we raised through our IPO are being deployed towards our committed capital expenditure just as we had planned. The order -- ordering and delivery processes are underway, and we expect installation and commissioning to be completed by end of calendar year 2026.

items.statement: Second SMT line being installed currently, first line installed in January 2026
items.quote: The first line was the one that was installed in this January. The production line, 1 lakh components per hour line, was the one that was installed in the month of January. And the second line is the one that is being installed now.

items.statement: Potential future capex of INR100 crores for full system manufacturing foray
items.quote: And if the -- if what we are working upon comes yields, then I think we are looking at an investment close to about INR100 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity: 7.65 lakh SMD boards, 6 lakh THT boards, 4.20 lakh product assembly units per year at 65% utilization
items.quote: On capacity, we can currently produce 7.65 lakh SMD boards and 6 lakh THT boards and 4.20 lakh product assembly units per year, and we are running at about 65% utilization.

items.statement: Two SMT lines installed, second line for high-mix low-volume, existing infrastructure sufficient for INR500 crores revenue
items.quote: So, the one line equates to whatever INR100 crores is probably is not applicable in this context. However we have two lines as of now and with existing single line, we have whatever the existing -- the declared numbers have been achieved. So as far as the reaching INR500 crores is concerned, I think the existing infrastructure is sufficient.

items.statement: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 26 bps to 14.91%, net profit margin improved 461 bps to 11.27%
items.quote: EBITDA grew 94.76% to INR15.99 crores with EBITDA margin improving by 26 basis points to 14.91%. Net profit more than tripled, growing 223.72% to INR12.09 crores compared with INR3.73 crores last year. Our net profit margin improved by 461 basis points to 11.27%.

items.statement: Obsolescence segment EBITDA margin 25-30%, outsourcing segment gross margin 30-40%
items.quote: So there after the direct expenses and all the indirect expenses, it will come around to 25% to 30%. It will fluctuate because it depends, like in a year how much of obsolescence part we supply. Based on that, it will you like, but it will be in between 25% to 30%.

items.statement: CERN orders carry at least 22% gross margin
items.quote: We have a gross margin of at least, 22% on their order, at least. I mean, that's on the, the other side.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Build-to-print ~85%, Build-to-spec (obsolescence) ~INR11 crores, targeting 20-25% BTS and 15-20% obsolescence by FY29
items.quote: So one is BTS, FY28 probably will be close to what, I think we'll beginning to -- we'll be beginning to do that in FY28. I mean I expect the RF associating to start happening, starting financial year '27-'28. I can speak of '28-'29 where I see it should be close to about 20%, 25%, and on obsolescence we'll stick to 15 anywhere between 15% to 20% and remaining will be built-to-print.

items.statement: IR seeker assemblies for Nag missiles, air defense systems, helicopter-launched missiles
items.quote: Yes, so basically IR seeker is for surface-to-air missiles, and, it was initially meant for Nag missiles, and apart from that, now it is also being used in air defense. Systems and also, helicopter-launched, missiles also.

items.statement: Analinear expected to bring INR25-30 crores orders next financial year
items.quote: See, this could mean close to about anywhere from Analinear, we see an order worth at least INR25 crores to INR30 crores.

items.statement: HAL outsourcing potential INR2,500 crores if fully converted, Merritronix targets 30% share
items.quote: And the potential for the total outsourcing contracts from there, from them should be nothing less than about, INR2,500 crores. Sorry INR2,500 crores. If all of them are converted, then it will be at least INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Cash flow currently negative due to advances paid and waiting for materials, inventory stuck for want of 1-10 parts
items.quote: See, as far as the domain is concerned, you know, even now we have, projects where, only for want of 1 or 2 parts, or at the most I think sometimes even 10 parts rest of the material is being in the -- is in the inventory. So, cash flow, we will be putting more efforts in making it positive, but as of now it is negative.

items.statement: Short-term loans and advances INR49.85 crores: supplier advances INR29 crores, capital goods advances INR14 crores, GST/prepaid INR18 lakhs
items.quote: And as far as the short-term loans and advances are concerned, advance to suppliers is INR29 crores, advance for capital goods is INR14 crores and balance with government authorities, that is GST and there's prepaid expenses, some 18 lakhs.

items.statement: NADCAP certification audit expected by January end 2027, 100% confident of clearing
items.quote: Yes, there is a progress, but yes, it is a bit slower than, expected. The audit date should be mostly, January end. So, the, the consultants could not get it, I mean, basically for December since it's, it's a vacation month, towards the end, the dates slipped into January.

items.statement: NADCAP certification will not affect FY27 guidance as guidance based on status quo
items.quote: And, apart from that, the Nadcap certification is -- I mean, as far as the guidance is concerned, the guidance was given based on status quo. mean, whatever we have now. So, it not getting in the eventuality of whatever you said, whatever, whatever has been mentioned, that if it doesn't happen, what happens to the guidance? items.quote: We have -- very recently also we have won bids close to about INR10 crores. So the order accumulation is continuous throughout the year. It is not like October has come and the tenders stopped or bids stopped.

items.quote: So as of now… Varun Sheth: Yes, Yes, we can hear you. Management: Yes, so, our, we, the total strength of the company is as of now, 100, sir, and of them about 45 are on contract. About 55, 56 employees are on rolls, and of these 56, 15 of them are engineers, 10 of them are, are on the administrative side. items.statement: H1 FY27 growth driven by timely execution, repeat orders, and new requirements as customer confidence grew; H2 momentum expected to continue
items.quote: Yes, so the reason for this growth is timely execution of orders and then customers getting back to us with, some repeat requirements and further new requirements as the confidence grew in, in their minds. And as far as, H2 is concerned we expect the momentum to continue.

items.statement: Defense electronics demand follows 60% H2 revenue pattern, peers show similar seasonality
items.quote: I sincerely hope that should happen because whatever you have mentioned is, a trend that has been seen over the years. So based on the trends of, past years. What you're saying is true, and we hope it happens.

items.statement: CERN first bid at 22% gross margin, future bids to be priced higher as competition mainly non-Indian
items.quote: First bid we had to be a bit aggressive. Aggressive meant 22%, but going forward we will be a bit more, conscious and then see. I mean, competition will be mostly from non-Indian companies going forward, so we'll, based on the situation, we will try to quote a bit more with little bit more profit.

items.statement: NADCAP certification enables access to 30+ global aerospace customers currently behind certification wall
items.quote: Now Nadcap, like you have rightly pointed out, gives us, you know, the ability, if you will, to go to a different set of customers or existing set of customers in specific different areas. items.statement: IPO funds deployed towards committed capex as planned
items.quote: The funds we raised through our IPO are being deployed towards our committed capital expenditure just as we had planned.

items.statement: Customer backward integration risk acknowledged but management not worried as they cater to different segment
items.quote: So, as of now, some of our customers, they have their own manufacturing facilities and still the same, we are getting orders from them. The reason being we are not doing what the -- whatever capacity that they have, we are catering to a different segment to them, so it will continue.

items.statement: Order updates not uploaded to exchange due to execution focus, will make it regular practice going forward
items.quote: Yes, there is no specific reason. See, these are the orders which have been coming, on regular basis, and, they were not, I mean, any order, about INR10 crores, we thought it would make, it would be worthy, uploading one with the board. Basically, we were busy executing orders. That's the only reason.
